these hustlers are scam artists. they charge me $500 to remove a wart from my foot by an np -- a procedure that took at most 15 minutes. i highly doubt the np is earning $2k an hour ($4m per year) -- so lots of "administrators" must be taking a generous cut of the cash. i complain and the business office, annoyed that i call and doing everything they can to just get me out of the way, says i can call anytime before a procedure to get a quote. they're lying because two months later, the wart is still there. before going in i try to get a quote and they refuse to give one. i go anyway, again pay the exorbitant fee only for it not to work again. how can they charge so much to fail at what they do? if i didn't deliver in my job, i'd offer to re-do it right at no cost. swedish is the worst kind of big business -- arrogant, ineffective, and unaccountable. the doctors/medical staff are fine, and clearly try. but the business office and administrative staff clearly hate working, are arrogant and condescending to customers, and are just there to line their own pockets.

i had a stroke christmas moring 2017 and went to swedish fore rehab. this is the worst rehab location i've ever seen since then. the food is  worst than the bad food you normally get in a hospital. the staff dropped me twice and the night before i checked out a nurse dropped a cot on my one unaffected  foot( she was putting it  in my room for my girlfriend to sleep onbefore we got a flight back home.)  the hospital didn't seem to be overly concerned about it once they took x-rays and said there wasn't any broken bones! they barely apologized! there was a nurse there that seemed overly concerned about seeing my penis to the point she would yell at me to see it. i don't know how long it's been since she had sex, but she seemed horny as a toad. i reported her to the head nurse on my floor, but it seemed to me all the hospital did was talk to her with no discipline. the staff is extremely slow to respond when you need help. good thing i never had a heart attack while i was there. i lost my charger for my iphone after i go there and one of the staff had one, but he blantantly refused to let me use it to charge my phone! i had to order another one thru amazon! worst hospital on the planet my advice, go anywhere, but swedish. i believe a mom and pop rehab hospital would hve been better, safer and les humliating than that horrible place!

arrived at emergency room 6:41 pm due to prednisone reaction at 8:16 pm i was still waiting to be seen in er on 2/22/20. i then decided to leave went to er desk and asked to be removed from patient roster going to another facility. not one staff member knew how to perform this service nor responded appropriately to the issue.  i assumed the desk clerk was bothered since he was texting on his phone.  i was in the facility with another woman who had even been vomiting in the area only to see her sit and the mess only cleaned up.  the final straw was listening to a male staff nurse discuss private patient information.   this facility needs to train its staff on patient privacy guidelines immediately.  i left the hospital and went to owensboro.  never saw a doctor or received medical care.  this facility isn't fit enough to see a pet let alone a human being.  i asked for written proof showing i was being removed as a patient and i definitely don't want a bill from a substandard hospital of this magnitude.

wow, some very low ratings for this hospital on yelp!  i'm actually surprised because our experience was pretty good.  from the front desk/security desk, to the floor nurses/staff, to the social workers; everyone was very friendly, helpful and accommodating.  

they were super helpful when my 85 yr old aunt and 97 yr old uncle, came to visit their son in the hospital.  they both have difficultly walking and the staff went out of the way to make sure they both had wheel chairs to bring them to my cousin's room.  truly professional and wonderful staff all around.

i have nothing negative to say, and appreciate the care and attentiveness they provided my cousin during a very difficult time.  big thanks to everyone!!

south miami hospital emergency room is now the worst around the area. in the past, it was one of the best. we have been there twice recently with serious conditions and they left us alone in the room for hours. the tests were spaced hours apart and they would not even give us a blanket. the first time the older male er doctor would not even come in the room and gave us incorrect information from the doorway. the second time, the female er dr. basically threatened my husband saying that if he left he would die. he is just fine weeks later. do not go there! doctor's er is by far the best and will treat you with compassion.

i've been seeing a doctor here for 3 years and i was in appreciation with the help and service i was getting...once i began to get seriously ill the level of care seemed to have been ignored...if a doctor is taking care of you one would expect enough care from a doctor to be proactive in were to place a patient before an illness progresses...this was not done. 

instead i was left to suffer an illness that should have not gotten as bad as it did...very upsetting...i fired this doctor because i do not trust him..he has known me for a long time and allowed me to suffer!!

i give this doctor 0 stars because of the level of care i got from this man in the later months of 3 years...khalid bashir, md a f***king failure when it came to my care....i truly believe he snickered in laugh with my suffering....if grady is not careful someone in grady's team of doctors and students might  really f**k things up....

i give the grady hospital 3/4 stars for the level of difficulty i do understand  is happening....so it be said...i know grady is trying to be better with the good they have done....

very upset with bashir a certain group of students, surgical team....

recently i visited the grady er due to difficulty breathing and a high heart rate. simply put i felt like i was suffocating and was going to die, so my wife rushed me. my heart rate stayed at around 150-160 bpm for 5 hours straight until it started to lower in the final hour. i can't say i was conscious the whole time enough to know about my full experience, but by the end, i felt like i was treated pretty fast and to the best ability of the staff there. 

ultimately, the downside of the experience was the staff's response to me. you see, the reason i showed up was due to too much alcohol followed by smoking. sober me knows i can't smoke cause it closes up my airways, drunk me thought nothing of it and that's the story. 

the staff was irritated at me from what i remember, felt like they thought very lowly of me. they also spoke ill of me while i was going in and out of consciousness due to the nature of my stay. they didn't take me seriously and my insurance wasn't even taken down. they just sent me a bill for $600 for 3 hours on an i.v. and called it a day. the whole experience was fine minus the treatment by the individuals, not to say that is how the staff acts, but that in my case the staff i was with were this way to me. 

i'd still recommend it, but just keep in mind er's are generally miserable anyways so word of the wise, always have low expectations for that mess.

i attended the bi-weekly parent support group here that paige leads here.  it has an interesting guest speaker which i found useful.  also, there is a baby weigh-in at the beginning of class.  overall, this is a wonderful group that talks about daily joys and concerns of parents with their kids.  there are also additional resources provided in class to help with common topics for both moms and dads.

if i could leave 0 stars i would. i went to the e.r. the nurses were rude in the room. when they left the room i heard them talking about me. they "forgot" to put me in a gown. when they did put me into a gown they made sure my curtains were open didn't shut the door and called out when people went past " she needs her but checked out!"they also did not come into the room when the male dr came into check me alone. i would normally not have a problem of a male dr being in a room alone however where he checked there should always be a nurse in the room!!!

i have never had a more disappointing er experience. my father is back for the second day in a row... he was promised pain meds yesterday and he didn't get them. we're back today because the pain is worse. whoever the radiologist is takes too long to read a stat chart from the er. 3 hours is too long to wait for an ultrasound report and we're now at 1.5 hours waiting for results of a ct scan... absolutely unacceptable for an er visit. seek help elsewhere.

my mother was at seton for about a month last year. what a horrible hospital, the emergency room was ok and some of the nurses and doctors are ok on floors 1-5 but over all my mom was lucky to get out of there alive. 

shifts change and one hand doesn't talk to the other, many employees have lost the compassion they need for their jobs. and some simply just don't care, when you want to speak to the doctor they screen the calls and the doctor will almost never call you back.

they will sent in a social worker to talk to you, the  doctors are obviously lower end as far as experience "they do a lot of guessing when diagnosing" then you start seeing tons of issues arising from them experimenting with different treatments. 

they need to shut that place down and those people need to take up coding or a different career.

if your family member goes up to the 6th floor, god help them. they will go through the motions but if they need any kind of actual care they will show them the door, "which believe me is the best chance your loved one has of making it to tomorrow!

i can only imagine how many people have been lost due to the incompetence of this place. if you go here and you are one of the lucky ones to survive, listen to them sit in the wheel chair as they wheel you out the front door, then turn and punch which ever scumbag is pushing your chair get up and run!!!! it's your only hope of survival...

they made an error on my emergency bill. i had to pay the full amount since i'm protecting my credit. then i asked help from cigna to help me make reach out to seton so they can explain that portion of payment they sent to seton was from my flex account. seton considered that the full payment form cigna was only from insurance, so they decided to charge me extra $900. i spoke to multiple people several times but they keep saying they will call me back. now it's been months! they're so unprofessional. i'm proceeding to filing a complaint to the county and cigna is willing to send me all documents to i need to show proof that i should be getting my refund. will never go back to this hospital!

brought my mom is a few months ago (before the coronavirus) because she couldn't regulate her temperature due to her cancer treatments. the nurse kept saying we were safer to stay home. i get it! we are surrounded by sick people but she was covered in blankets and heating pads and felt like she was going to freeze. when she finally got a room days later the nurse was more concerned about the paperwork than my mom. she asked us the same questions we already answered three times before about her medications and medical history. mom started to get chills again which is always followed by a high fever. i told her and that tylenol would do the trick. she wouldn't give it to her bc the fever hadn't spiked yet. it's just tylenol!!! she kept asking her questions but by then my mom was delirious and couldn't even say her own name! she kept saying she was fine and just tired. i begged for tylenol but they refused. they used the external temperature and it was 99. they said they will wait till it got to 100 to give her tylenol. i brought my own oral thermometer and it read 102. finally i had to call the head nurse to get help and by then her fever was 103!!!! this is the worst place! i hope that nurse gets fired!!! they had no regard for my moms well being and we will never go there again.

the emergency services here were the highlight of my experience.  i was taken directly from the ambulance to be seen with no time in the waiting room.  xrays were quickly and competently done and the er doc put on a soft cast quickly.  but, with broken bones in both feet as well as sprains and a lot of swelling, the orthopedic doctor never saw me.  they then admitted me to the hospital where there is a combination of competent, kind, professionals and dismissive, malingering.  first of all, the bell system doesn't work to connect patients to the desk;?only a light goes on over the door, so unless someone is passing by your door they won't know you need the; at least, that's what the nurses say.  one night, i got left sitting on a full bedpan for 45 minutes.  last night i tried for 2 hrs to get the pain med that  was ordered, in tears from pain.  but the worst is that after 3 days with broken bones and sprains in both feet orthopedics still hadn't seen me!

my daughter has been at the facility.  she has gotten great care from doctors, nursing staff and rehab personnel.  what she isn't getting is help from her last 2 case workers.  they have permission to share information with me as i am in california, but they have been vague and have avoided giving me information on services my daughter will need.  my daughter is low income so they have pretty much discounted her needs. i have asked if they have gotten her in touch with or helped her fill out forms for some type of welfare and was told there isn't any and she should figure it out herself.  they have hounded her to find a place to stay when she is released and told her they would probably put her in a cab and drop her off at a homeless shelter. how is that helping her to get well.  it has been sad, confusing.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Round Rock

review: i went in for a minor surgical procedure. i was very nervous, mostly because of a fear of sedation. but the staff was very understanding and took amazingly good care of me. i could not have asked for a better experience. i would have no hesitation to go back, should the need arise.

i delivered my first baby here back in november and it was the most amazing yet wildest experience of my life! everyone here is so heart warming and kind. they made me feel so comfortable and well taken care of from the moment i was admitted to the moment i went home with my baby girl! i want to give a special shout out and thanks to donna, jody, and osha! i wish i could remember all of the nurses's names because they were all so great! donna is the  coolest and she was my first nurse! she felt like family after we found out my husband graduated with her daughter. when it was time to move to a delivery room she made sure the best one was available for me! jody and osha were the storm troopers! they saw me at my worst when i was turning into the exorcist from those crazy labor pains lol but even then they were so calming, professional, and guiding my labor amazingly! dr. hernandez gave me my injection, he was so professional and quick. thanks to dr. northey, although she was not my ob, she was perfect and i'm so happy i delivered my baby with her. finally after my baby made her grand entrance, everyone i encountered during our stay were beyond amazing! oh and lily the lactation nurse! oh my god she was the sweetest and so helpful! the rooms are nice and big, the food is great, everything was awesome! i know i'll be coming here again if i am blessed with another baby in the future! thank you

this is by far one of the worst places i've ever been in my entire life the staff is unbelievably bias and rude very violent and overall very unwelcoming i was waiting to be admitted for and hour and a half mind you, this place is not busy and i am within earshot vision, the so called "staff" were gossiping about patients and other things completely irrelevant to anything work related there was an unbelievable amount of neglect, as i was hungry after dinner i asked a staff member for food and he said "no you cant have any", and that is not in the right you are not allowed to refuse a patient food, and when i had gotten food the next day and took it too my room i was eating it because, i don't feel comfortable eating in front of people a staff member came in to check on me and told me to hand my food over, i did as told not wanting to start an argument and as he was leaving he started eating it while going down the hallway. the next day i was taking a shower and i was not told dinner was done so i hadn't eating anything and when it came to visiting i said i hadn't eaten and the staff member said they'd get it, 30 minutes later i go back with no food what so ever and i say "so i still haven't gotten food yet" and they said "i forgot" so i started arguing with them and they put they're hands on me trying to get me to calm down but i wasn't having it..

over all i think you get the point im trying to make, do not send your kid here it is the absolute worst thing you'll regret doing this place is unprofessional and negligent and misrepresented as a "nice place for people to get better".

for god's sake, do not agree to admitting your child here!!!! while the food is good the care is inexcusable! they will find any reason to extend your child's stay. it's more a money making proposition than a place to get help for your teen. no matter how your teen is behaving, substance problems, or if they are having emotional issues fight tooth and nail before letting you child be put into this institution!!!! please! do not let your child enter these doors! i'm begging you! do not do it! all doors here lead to h*ll!!!!! be warned!
there are a lot of good things about clara maas.  but, twice they had the wrong medication on my mothers discharge papers and that's a serious mistake that people need to watch out for!

i had an emergency and was taken to aventura hospital . they were expedient , efficient , and took care of me. i had no family here to visit but they made me feel comfortable and the nurses constantly checked to see that i was doing well. 
i thank the ambulance drivers , emt, doctors , and nurses and the rest of the staff for all your compassionate help and professional service. i highly recommend this hospital and medical center !

ive had the occasion to visit a friend in this hospital for way too long and its a place i would never go and you shouldn't either.  the rooms always smelled like urine and or poo wheres the the cleaning staff or nursing to clean up?  the staff is clueless and a majority speak creole and like to talk about the patients and visitors they need to smarten up as i understood exactly what they were saying more than once!
i was misdiagnosed in the er. the  er doctor doctor billed me about $1500.00 for a 10 minute consultation. the better emergency room in aventura is mount sinai.

please think twice before seeking care at this institution.  the staff is in a constant state of flux and those that stay are burned out.  i've had friends that are er docs, neurosurgeons, internists and general surgeons who have worked here.  they are overwhelmed by unsympathetic leadership that is more concerned with the bottom line than staff health and patient care.  it is known locally by medical professionals as "aventorture".

i had a problem with kuakini's transportation for my mother to a rehab facility.  recommendation from social worker to be transported with a mobility van to facility.  my pickup time was 10:00 and driver never arrived.  spoke to nurses station and was told 10:30.  finally at 12:30 a helper told me 12:45.  

how inconvenient and ill responsible.  a very bad reflection on kuakini medical hospital.  my mother has to wait over 3 hours.

as i expected it's been 21 days from writing a review and bringing up issues like exposing patients and staff to harmful chemicals. i filled out the response as soon as i saw it posted with all of my contact information and nothing but silence. they quickly post something that says that they care so that it looks like they are going to address it but then nothing happens. management does not plan, think, or respond to the people in their care or to the concerns of their staff. my first review got so long that i did not list everything in like when they waxed the floors there was no warning so that they pt items like stairs that they just love to show on the videos no one could get to. for those of you thinking of anything but day use do i would not stay overnight there again and please it is not the nursing and support staff, it is the management. every single person trying to care for us was doing the best that they could with management standing in the way every step of the way and signing contracts for things like waxing the floor to the lowest bidder not caring and not putting in their rfps that they handle things safely.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Uptown

review: went today to the er because my husband wasn't feeling good .. so we get in there and honestly didn't like it .. we go into a room that had two beds but instead they gave my husband and i seats to sit on and across from us was a differently family and they are sitting as well. went in at 2pm and didn't come out almost 6pm ... they took so long to do everything . i get that the more important patients are the ones who sick/dying but wouldn't it be easier to send someone who doesn't need much attention to go home quicker ??? but anyways we were in a room and everything seemed to be falling apart .. i just didn't like it at all seemed very old this hospital needs a clean up and updated equipment.

this hospital doesn't deserve even 1 star after how i was treated with double pneumonia last week.  my 70 yr old diabetic, dialysis.heart patient also with double pneumonia was allowed to leave his room without the nurses even giving me a call. my husband said he was not getting the proper care and needed my help. i was a nurse for 26 years!  anyway he returned to er and has now been waiting for 2 days for another room.  this has become a nightmare and proves that this hospital can not deal with the catastrophe of the flu....god forbid rome ever have a real deadly attack from a natural or military attack!!!
i've spoken to all the head administration and special directors concerning the nurse allow such a sick patient to leave in the first place..  they are not acting as nurses.
i'm going up to see what i can do today or else take him to floyd.
redmond is no place to go get any care......debra smith

love the cancer institute ! that are all outstanding!  i should have reviewed sooner!  they are precise, always on time, know how to handle bad reaction to my very first chemo infusion.  can't say enough from checking in to checking out the most polite, caring group of individuals.
treated me with much respect, explained everything along my journey.  thanks to my doctor leslie martin and her entire staff i am currently ned!  ( no evidence of disease) i go every 3 months for  follow ups and what a great group!  can't say enough for the entire staff!  they got it going on!
fac_name: John Muir Health, Concord Medical Center

review: i wish i could put 0 stars. seriously don't come here unless you want to die. doctors are absolutely terrible. they don't have the time to stop in and tell you what's wrong with you. my dad stayed in the this hospital for one whole month and honestly only spoke to one doctor for five minutes during the entire stay. hospital staff is unpleasant. no bedside manner or professionalism. no one seems to care about their patients, all the workers seem like they're there for a check. my dad was non verbal and unable to communicate because he had a stroke during his first few days here, by the way, it took 8 days for the hospital staff to order a scan to find out if he had a stroke. so at that point all hope for recovery was out the window. so we told the care team that he was allergic to penicillin. the hospital staff, knowing this information simply disregarded it and had him on a penicillin drip for two days even though we asked them several times to discontinue due to his allergy. the doctors and nursing staff will go on with certain treatments and major changes in the care plans without alerting the patient or family! my dad coded and literally during cpr compressions, my dads nurse that shift stopped the code team from doing compressions to convince my mom to change my fathers code status to a dnr. right then and there while a code blue was called. this experience happened five years ago and to this day the care we received at this hospital shakes me to my core. it was incredibly traumatic, and i want to save anyone from experiencing something like this, don't go here unless you want to die from malpractice.
fac_name: John Muir Health, Concord Medical Center

review: my family and i were on vacation in merritt island and my mom had a bad fall. she had three broken bones and a dislocated ankle. the er wait was less than 10 min. the staff in the er and in the hospital were phenomenal. her surgeon was dr. brennan and he took really good care of her. the entire staff made my mom and my family feel so at ease and were so friendly. they made a bad situation feel at ease. we really appreciate the entire staff at rockledge and how hard you all work! there is no where else we would have rather ended up for her surgery.

i never post reviews but i am so upset what my mother went through here after surgery! they removed cancer and the surgeon was fine but the nurses are the important part. the nurses make sure your pain is manageable and not bring meds hours late. not to mention the one nurse, lauren, told her she already had her morning meds then said "i'm not going to argue with you" only to come back realizing she was wrong- but with no less of an attitude. i regret not being their to advocate for my mom!!!! these are mean people.

hate that hospital. ambulance took me there   and i wish i never went there. rude  and i was left in the hallway plus the nurse was not helpful there had me walk to the restroom when they knew i passed out  . never had the dr come to introduce  him to me . he just popped his head around the corner and yelled out what was my diagnosis was where everyone could hear. never will go there ever again. worst hospital ever i wish i could put zero ratings.

i had a previous injury that led to me separating my shoulder again today but the doctor was not interested in my medical history. i was told that my previous injury didn't matter cause i had just hurt it again today even though it was a hill-sachs fracture (depression on humerus head that increases chance of shoulder dislocation and separation) but i guess that had nothing to do with hurting it again from lifting only 35lbs. i was left to sit in the waiting room with my shoulder in excruciating pain. if you are not in a life or death situation do not come here, go to one of the urgent cares where they treat people correctly!

they are great at taking care of you, i will be forever grateful.  however, i know realize one of the reasons healthcare is so expensive is their administrative help is really bad.  really, really bad, make sure if you don't see a bill, call them and find out why.  i gave them all my current information and they billed 3 times to an address i had 20 years ago and they never updated, they had my phone number and never called me, and put me in collection, first time i have ever been in collection.  just be warned.

if i could give less stars i would. the first time i came here when passing a kidney stone, i waited for four hours and they didn't even have my information when i went and inquired about how long it would be. they had an addict flailing around on the floor, weren't doing anything to assist or help the scene. there was puke all over the floor and no one cleaned it up, not even a caution sign.

the second time i had to come to hurley was when i having a severe allergic reaction to pineapple. 
they didn't get me anything until i was turning purple, and my significant other screamed at them to save my life. never again will i ever go here.

i was sent to this hospital, from another hospital, to have a test done. the tech was polite & seem to know what he was doing. i did not get any paper with a diagnoses. they said,  "it was a gland that was swollen. they doubt it was anything serious, but need further testing. in 4 hospitals they couldn't tell i was having a stroke?? i have lose complete faith in all these hospitals who do not take the proper time to figure out the problem. i had so many signs of a stroke, even i knew what it was. i was given nothing to back anything up or explain what they had said. also, all of a sudden, they were rushing me out the door. i asked to give me a minute, to make sure i have everything & the answer was no! so i'm wondering what they were hiding to rush me out that fast, that my head spin.
they don't care about what doctors they hire, or what mental issues they may have. they do a great job of pretending to care when you bring it to their attention, but sadly that isn't the case.

neglected my uncle who was in the icu. they discharged him and the next day he died. they did not do anything to help my uncle but just sent him away and turned their shoulder to the whole ordeal. piss off einstein. this is a garbage hospital, if you can even call it a hospital.

i think you need to be having a heart attack or close to dying before a doctor sees you in the er. 

my son was throwing up and was in writhing stomach pain that we brought him to einstein er. he was curled up and in pain upon arrival at 10 pm. registered 15 minutes later and paid a $150 copay.  at 1:15 am, no doctor has seen hm. he's threw up green bile  2 times within those hours. we gave the bucket to the nurse for them to see. nobody seemed it was life threatening enough to constitute any attention from any doctor or nurse. i wonder, where should i have taken my son late at night if he was in that much pain but not deemed "emergency" enough by einstein er? i thought that was what er is for, isn't it?

i was transported to the hospital by ambulance with acute kidney pain. they dropped me off in the er waiting room where i passed a 5mm kidney stone because they didn't put me in a bed for 4 hours. i was throwing up and passing out in the waiting room and instead of getting help the triage nurse laughed at me and the front desk person yelled at me to go back and sit down. i passed out in the bathroom while screaming and throwing up and they all probably just thought i was a junky or something because no one cared to check. do not go to einstein!!  you will not be treated with respect or care!

the ut only portions of this place are top notch. well, they've had experience with the texas medical center in houston...etc so of course they know their stuff. 

seton however still believes 1) that people are receiving care merely out of 'charity' and 2) that this is a indigent only hospital. therefore the places they own inside the facility are really poorly run. they find ways to ignore you and otherwise avoid you.
fac_name: Dell Seton Medical Center at The University of Texas

review:
recently, i was sitting in an er room with my younger sister who had just attempted suicide, a nurse who was "sitting" mentioned to another nurse that she once sat for a man who had jumped four stories to try and end his life. that's right - in a room with a suicidal person (and her loved one) a nurse who was supposed to be looking out for the well-being of my sister, spoke about another suicide attempt. i understand desensitization happens, but that was completely unacceptable and unprofessional. if i wasn't putting the needs of my sister first, i would have made a scene. i am appalled. during the hardest day of our lives, this nurse had the audacity to speak about another suicide attempt in front of us. 
try sensitivity training or making sure only qualified social workers sit in rooms of patients who have attempted suicide. do both. do better seton. you can't change what happened in my experience, you can't fix the pain that comment amplified but do better. be better. you owe your patients and their families that much.
fac_name: Dell Seton Medical Center at The University of Texas

review:
dell seton icu unit, nurses and doctors are responsible for the death of my father.
my dad had an accident and required major surgery in the icu unit.  he survived the surgery just fine.  the doctors said full recovery.
along the way, he caught pneumonia.  this is a risk with major surgery and can result in death as i have learned.  we figured it was just something he had to get through and see how his condition improves.
the second night after he caught pneumonia when i came to visit, it was different approaching his icu room.  this time, about 6 to 8 nursing staff was with him in and out of the room.  very unusual unlike before. when i got there, there was a nurse that said "every time i get here he's doing bad.  every-time i leave he's doing good again".  my sister, who was there already told me later that that same nurse earlier got confrontational with the staff and said "yall are wasting my time, go ahead and give him the medicine." or something to that effect.  this was quite alarming and we couldnt decide to escalate this to someone or not.  
my dad got worse and in this process, got a heart attack.  doctor olsen, who i now call grimmy because he's always trying to convince us to pull the plug citing quality of life (blah..blah..blah..), asked us before heart surgery if we wanted to pull the plug if the operation doesn't go well.  why in the world would any doctor suggest this without knowing the outcome.  why not do the heart surgery first, see how he does and then decide?
dad survived heart surgery and cardiologist says his heart is very strong.  3 weeks into this thing, my dad was still on a ventilator, which is dangerous after 7-14 days, from a doctors own mouth.  they were suppose to do a trache, but did not until we pressured them and they got it scheduled.  during the inquiry into the trache, an arrogant resident doctor continually talked about "quality of life", "you should get your entire family here for a meeting with the staff", even though my dad was in relatively stable condition at the time.

however, he would not live to have the trache done. the last time i saw my dad in stable condition i had a conversation with a nurse name jennifer.  she was working on him and started talking about quality of life.  i told her it was my wishes that dad continue treatment for a few months, at least give him a chance to recover, and we see where we are and make the decision then.  she told me, older people and trama dont work well together.  i left and 3 hours later i get a call back from jennifer stating i need to get back.  my dad would be dead 1 hour later.

i asked her what happen.  when i left just a few hours before, he was fine.  she stated that "as you know, his heart was weak, and he was on the heart machine.  i told her, that is not true.  he was removed from the heart machine over a week ago and the cardiologist told us the heart was very strong, beating faster than normal, which was good.

then she said, "well, before his heart started to give out, his blood oxygen level went low and i we knew it was going to be bad.  thats when we started some procedure.".  i couldnt put 2 and 2 together at the time and did not pry any further.  i am convinced someone stopped the ventilator enough time to for my dad to be deprived of oxygen to his brain which controlled the heart.  he was stabilized before i left and its too coincidental the medical staff continually asked us about pulling the plug.  

also, pneumonia is caught by non sanitary environments especially having the mouth open all the time.

i just buried my dad and generally don't let my emotions defy common sense.  i cant speak of every hospital because going through a process like this is rare for my family.  however, if you are a senior citizen, i strongly recommend you avoid seton care like the plague.  you are automatically discriminated against and they will pressure you to pull the plug, if not 'accidentally' give you some wrong dosage leading to your death.  we had inquired about moving my dad to st.david's, but we came to the conclusion that it was too risky.  ironically, you have to get permission from the doctor that it is safe to move the patient.  the same doctor and medical staff trying to get us to agree to pull the plug.

doctor olsen, if you are reading this, you should not be practicing medicine.  i blame more my dad's death on the nursing staff, but you are so god damn quick to 'pull the plug' without giving any consideration from time to allow people to heal.

for those reading this, know this in icu... resident doctors are students.  always talk to the attendee doctor.  the resident doctor, dr.doom#2, gave us a bunch of garbage.

it should also be noted, while my dad was in critical condition, there was a young nurse (or student nurse), sitting on the sink swinging her legs just chatting away to another nurse, without a care in the world that family is in there and my dad is in critical condition.

go to st.david's.

haloperidol deaths
there were 6,598 deaths (9% of the study cohort) during the first 180 days of antipsychotic treatment - a rate of 37 per person per year of treatment. about half of these were caused by circulatory disorders (49%).feb 23, 2012

the doctors, nurses, technicians and staff at memorial hospital of gardena rock! can't say enough nice things about them. i have been to their e.r. twice in the last 20 years (most recently this past week), and my wife has been here 3 times in the last year 1/2. my wife took me to the emergency room because i kept having chest pains, tightness, palpitations and burning in my stomach, back and arms. surprisingly the waiting room was pretty empty, then again it was a wednesday morning. 

i was admitted pretty quickly into the e.r. had my vitals checked and given a bed. they did an ekg on me and i was "glad" i was having the heart palpitations right at that moment and they were pretty intense and nonstop. i figured whatever was going on, if it was heart related they should be able to see it. that's the tricky thing with heart palpitations, often times they don't always happen, so you might go to the doctors office and not be having the symptoms when they do the ekg or listen to your heart. but this time i was having the palpitations and the doctor said my results came back normal and good and that i wasn't having a heart attack.

dr. sean howse was awesome as was the ekg technician. the phlebotomist was the best i've ever had! i didn't even feel the needle prick, and that was the part i was dreading the most, because i hate needles! but he took several vials of my blood and i didn't feel a thing! even the receptionist and security guards were nice! overall it was a great experience considering where i was at. i mean, no one wants to really go to the e.r., especially me! 

after the ekg and the doctor talking to me, listening to my heart and me describing my symptoms, he told me i had gerd and gastritis. he was about to discharge me but my wife and i insisted they do all the blood tests, all the heart tests to 100% rule out that it was not my heart, since i kept having these symptoms. the doctor was like "you're fine, it's not your heart, but if it'll make you feel better i can do all the tests." we were like "yes please do all the tests." 

i also insisted on him doing an ultra-sound of my stomach and intestines, since i kept having nonstop burning in my stomach and chest area and striking pains/cramping. he agreed to do all the tests i requested. for some time now i had been agonizing over if something was wrong with my heart and since i suffer from generalized anxiety disorder it constantly gave me panic attacks. i really needed to figure out what the hell was wrong with me and try to fix it. 

so they drew several vials of my blood, gave me a chest x-ray and a stomach ultra-sound. the test results for my heart and all my blood panels came back good. no liver, kidney, thyroid or heart issues, also no infections. the doctor said "that's good news that you have no stomach infections, i was worried about that, and your pancreas is good too, which was another concern." he said "my test results came back better than his!" dr. howse was very funny and his anologies are hilarious. my wife had him on a previous visit. he takes his time talking to you, explaining what's going on and what the results and treatment options are. he didn't rush when talking to me like some doctors do, he was very patient and caring and answered all my questions. so was the ekg nurse/tech ,the phlebotomist and the lady who did my ultrasound.

there was no evidence for active cardiopulmonary disease. there was no evidence for congestive heart failure on my chest x ray. no evidence of pneunothorax (a collapsed lung), and the osseous structures are intact. he said i need to drink more water because my water levels were lower than they should be but otherwise "my tests results came back better than his." but i do have gerd, gastritis, and i have several small gallstones. the doctor said they're tiny but they're there. he prescribed me antibiotics and several meds for gerd and gastritis and recommended a follow up with a gastroenterologist.
