i am so disappointed by my experience at hss.  i saw three of the "best" doctors at hss and was referred to their pt and kept getting worse and worse.  i was referred to nyu and saw their specialists who immediately diagnosed my problem which was made profoundly worse by hss and the pt department who sees many patients at the same time.  i had surgery with another physician and got the best pt with a clinic at nyu.  be careful as it seems that they are not interested in patient care.  no one coordinated my pt with my physician and refused to provide feedback.
my uncle had 2 hip surgeries here and they did a very nice job. he was in and out promptly after the recovery room. i would recommend this place for hip surgeries.

if this is the best place in the us/world for orthopedics then orthopedic medicine is in truly sorry state. unless you have a diagnosis so easy you could make it yourself after  a couple hours of study, you're out of luck at hss. i've been there to see half a dozen different doctors, and it has been nothing but a waste of time and money (i have to drive 3 hours each way, sometimes getting a hotel room nearby for morning appointments). the doctors don't do any analysis. sure, they take mris and look at those, but they haven't done anything with those images that i couldn't learn in a matter of hours. they just look at images, and look at you, and don't do any actual analysis. if your problem doesn't fit within a tiny, strictly defined box, they all refuse to do anything else to help you. i have begged and begged for a more comprehensive analysis and they refuse to even think about what might be causing my problems. they just compare me mindlessly to some statistical norm and deem me to be or not to be a surgical candidate. after that they shove me out the door and don't want to hear from me. they don't follow up. they don't offer any path forward. they have proven they don't care even slightly about diagnosing patients with difficult to diagnose problems.  

their "social media" commissar types a boilerplate message to all negative reviews asking you to contact them. when you do, they put zero effort into remedying the situation. they have a patient advocacy group, and i have called them numerous times, but they always tell me they can do nothing for me. how is that advocacy? they don't actually care if you are dissatisfied with how you have been treated, as proven by the fact they have never put an ounce of effort into setting things right with me. 

there will be no follow up to your complaints. their doctors will do nothing to provide you more effective treatment. 

hss is all that is wrong with medicine.

whoever the idiot that answers the phone in the rheumatology department is should be written up. i called to speak to a doctor who is no longer there (i knew this prior to my call) and mentioned that to this idiot. i told him that that doctor diagnosed me with lupus in 2015 and i was under his care that year. that doctor since then left the hospital. i stopped taking the medication a few months later after realizing the symptoms were manageable. my initial call to hss rheumatology yesterday was because i wanted to get a new prescription for hydrochloroquine (which i was on years ago and in this current covid-19 scare, i feel that i should take precautions and start taking this medication again). i understood that i may have had to see the new rheumatologist and was prepared for this idiot to tell me so. i also requested a letter from the doctor explaining my diagnosis to my employer. this idiot took down my name, number, pharmacy and said that the prescription would be sent to the pharmacy. he then said "and you wanted something else-an excuse?" no, a$$hole, i didn't say i wanted an excuse. i asked for a letter. i chalked his misuse up to a possible lack of language comprehension. hours later, the prescription wasn't available at the pharmacy. no big deal. i called the idiot back the next morning and told him that the prescription wasn't there. he very coldly replied was "you were a no-show in 2016 and you weren't a patient of dr. berman and she's no longer taking new patients." i said "yes, i told you i was a patient of a doctor who is no longer there yesterday, but doesn't the hospital still have my medical records? this is hss, right?" he said "no, i'm telling you what i see here. also, the previous doctor took your records with him." it would have been courteous to have gotten a phone call back saying this instead of me having to call back inquiring about my medication.  zero customer care from this young man in the rheumatology department at hss. if you are a new patient, or a patient from long ago, go somewhere else. i was in customer service for years and would never be as cold and lack follow-through as this young man.

this review is in regard to my daughter's visit to hss pediatric radiology and based on our experience with a single individual. well, sometimes it just takes one person and one experience to make or break someone's day, and my daughter's radiologist nicole is that one person who made my day and resulted in hss getting a five star review from me today. my daughter needed a x-ray and i came in last minute on a friday. i believe the reception person had left. i walked in looking for someone who could provide me with some information while my daughter was still taking the elevator from the lobby. nicole asked me if i we lived far away. i said we did, to which she replied i understand and i want to make sure your daughter is taken care of and you don't have to come back for this on another day. while i waited for my daughter, nicole was on the phone getting the paperwork done so the moment my daughter walked in she could work on taking her x-rays. nicole, you deserve to be recognized for providing outstanding service, and you did it with compassion and kindness. thank you hss for having nicole on your staff!

my wife and i should've given a 5 star review for the first time we came to this hospital but unfortunately it was because she had a miscarriage. everyone was so helpful and caring and very sympathetic to our situation. when we thought about trying again one of the comforts we had was how comfortable we were with the staff and treatment. now a year later my wife gave birth to a healthy baby boy and from the security staff to the cafeteria personal, everyone and i mean everyone was exceptional. way above and beyond. all the nurses and doctors who tended to us were amazing. even the person taking the food orders and delivering the food was awesome and personable. couldn't ask for a better experience. i wish i had the means to give back to everyone who interacted with us. thank you so much.

2 stars because although the overall hospital stay was professional and at times friendly, the treatment received from charge nurse pearline was so egregious that it could've resulted in death. so if you can get past an enraged and unstable charge nurse, you might actually have a chance at survival. 

i took my boyfriend here last year for an infected abcess. he was admitted at 1am and taken to a shared room on the second floor. the roommate he had was extremely loud, through no fault of his own. he had heavy labored breathing and was coughing things up. the er physician told us that his next round of antibiotics would be at 6am, so we wanted to ask if it would be okay for him to go home to get some rest and come back in the morning, since he wouoldn't get a wink of sleep in that room. we realize that might sound like a silly question, but neither of us have ever been admitted to a hospital before so we don't know how it works and thought we could ask a medical professional. 
we tried to explain this to the charge nurse pearline o'connor hill (middle aged white woman with straight brown shoulder length hair and black glasses). she angrily blurted out, "the new patient!?" and when we looked at her in confusion, she asked "or you're the new patient!?". we confirmed that he had just been admitted, and pearline commanded a younger nurse to get the a.m.a. form. it was presented on the desk and he was repeatedly urged to sign it. we didn't know what the form was and pearline refused to explain it. we tried to ask again about returning for the next round of antibiotics, and she said "you want to leave the hospital and then come back to the er!?" and stared at us with furious disgust. she wouldn't listen to us or answer our questions. i realized that we would need to get away from his woman in order to seek medical care. he did like she wanted and signed the paper, at which point she commanded the younger nurse to remove his iv and cut off his hospital bracelet. we quickly went to the elevators to escape the furious charge nurse who angrily stared us down as we walked away. 

my boyfriend was exhausted after already having been at the hospital for 5 hours and just wanted to go home and get some sleep. i insisted that we return to the er doctor to ask him what to do. it felt absolutely crazy that i was having to help my sick boyfriend around the hospital building through the parking lot in the middle of the night to seek medical care! when we returned to the er, the er doctor was confused to see us, but when we explained what happened, he was shocked and appalled. he said my boyfriend wasn't even eligible for an a.m.a. form because he has sepsis, and that he would make some calls. 

while we waited, many other medical professionals were confused to see us in the er again but were shocked and apologetic after learnging what had happened. eventually shelly schwartz arrived, identifying herself as the head of nurses. we explained what happened, and asked again if he could go home to rest and return in the morning because we never got an answer to that question. she said that since he was admitted, he needed to remain under hospital care. that was fine, at which point we asked if it would be possible for him to get a quieter room. at about 3am we were taken to another room. he was hospitalized for 5 days and underwent surgery. 

we have no complaints about the care received from that point on, although the hospital visit was spent in fear of pearline o'connor hill showing up and what she might do, since she was clearly unstable and my boyfriend was in an extremely vulnerable situation. 

pearline hill's inexcusable and outrageous behavior could have resulted in my boyfriend's death. she was inexplicably furious at us and aggressively demanded he sign a form she refused to explain. who knows how many patients she's done this to, people who were alone or too sick to persist to receive medical help. my boyfriend was exhausted and confused, but thank god i was there with him to guide him back to the er to find medical help. had i not been there, he would've gone home to get some rest, gone into septic shock and died. i cannot understand why an otherwise friendly and professional hospital would employ someone that is such a clear liability and danger to patients.

i went to downtown pres when i went into labor and although i want to give 5 stars for the amazing nurse i got at 7:30 am named leah that took such good care of me and helped me as much as she could, i also want to give negative stars if that was possible for my nurse when i got admitted at 10:30 pm the night before named  angela pacheco. i couldn't believe how rude, unfriendly, and uncaring she was! if you're going to be a nurse, especially for woman in labor/having a baby, they need someone comforting in the most vulnerable time. i wish i would've asked for a new nurse or was given an explanation for anything she was saying/doing. she seemed to hate her job and is only there for the paycheck! if it wasn't for leah at the end i would never recommended this hospital, but because of her i truly recommend this place! if you get angela do yourself a favor and ask for a new nurse!
horrible place to be sick, the e.r. is horribly "busy" so they all say... hire better nurses and hire qualified staff that want to help people, not just collect a paycheck. i had to remove my own iv

i had a bad virus (cold) for over two weeks.  my cervical area (neck) was extremely painful. my friend drove me to the er at presbyterian.  this review is not about dr. skarbek.  he was wonderful, aware, and took his time with me while getting to know who i am and my lifestyle.  my complaint is with my attending nurse, caisa.  she treated me like a 90 year old woman.  for background, i am a lifelong athlete with a low resting heart rate and normal vitals.  my birth year was 1946.  i take no prescription meds for any ailment.  first, caisa asked me if i walk with a walker and i said, "heavens no".  i told her that i was gainfully employed full time as a secondary teacher, and i would need a note to take off a few days to rest.  she replied, that i must have worked at my school for a long time.  i told her "no" and "i worked there for only two years".  when she asked me questions, she interrupted me before i could respond.  i suggest that this millennial nurse should understand that some seniors may be in better shape than she.  she should improve her listening skills without interrupting, not profile patients, and learn to respect her elders. she could take a ski trip to aspen and check out the ages of the hot dog skiers. i am sick of the profiling that older people receive here in albuquerque.

recently  my daughter  stayed in icu. i witnessed  mso many mistakes. meds were not given according  to doctors orders be abuse shift change nurses were  not organized. when my daughter  was struggling  and trying  to get out of the bed and i reported  it i was told they were allowed  to move around  until  someone  finally  got around  to checking.. one nurse aid named samantha who was lazy left my daughter lying puddled up in the bottom of the bed several times and she had ard time breathing and not resting and she said to leave her like that so that she would  not be able  to get out and she would  not have to check on her at the same time. all night long she was lau6 with her friends and they even kept me awake and i was not a patient  who needed to rest because  they became  easily  agitated.  i was there for a week and saw so many things that made me sad...but there were also many more who were caring . i do not ever leave my loved ones alone e in the hospital  ever.

my dad is here due to a severe heart attack. the nurses are amazing as the doctors. 
the thing that surprised me was  how dirty the cafeteria and where the vending machines are. not only is the coffee cold but they have a horrible selection of food   they truly need a up grade or better janitors   they only get the stars for the nurses and doctors
hospital has the most friendly people that work there. the food isn't the greatest but what hospital is . the dr. and other specialist are top notch .

been waiting 2.5 hours for a nurse to help my mom. this nursing shift is unfriendly, no smiles, and feels like they are purposely ignoring us. just terrible!

and an update... they just tried tell me that they already talked to me about my mom, so now blaming me instead of good service. just awful.
fac_name: Little Company of Mary Hospital and Health Care Centers

review: trash. do not come here unless you're in an ambulance. for the 2nd time we have been sitting in the er waiting room for 8+ hours without being seen by a doctor. they take your "vitals" and that's it, you're just sitting in the waiting room with no updates what so ever. my grandma had major surgery at this hospital which is the only reason we've returned to follow up with the surgeon with our major concerns as instructed and nothing. we cannon see a doctor! i am beyond dissatisfied with this hospitals service.
fac_name: Little Company of Mary Hospital and Health Care Centers

review:
my mother was brought to this hospital after having a seizure. i was not able to get the hospital so my little sister was able to go. i tried calling up there and they had me waiting on the phone for a half an hour and then tried to say they can't talk to me about my mother over the phone, and i would have to come up thereafter i told the nurse i was unable too. i tried to ask a question and the nurse just kept trying to dismiss my question saying my mother will be fine and they will take care of anything not knowing any medical history about my mother. then the nurse started talking sarcastically
 to me on the phone that, i just hung up and left work to go speak to another nurse. all the nurses were slow and unhelpful. i suggest going to another hospital for your loved one cause this one ain't it anymore!
fac_name: Little Company of Mary Hospital and Health Care Centers

review:
i have heard some horror stories about the place, but after my wife had a devastating stroke, and spent two weeks here, i found nothing to complain about.

staff was totally compassionate and professional. they quickly did her cat scan. she had a massive hemorrhage, and they thought she would die in the emergency room. they arranged a video consult with a neurosurgeon in albuquerque, since there is none in taos. he explained there was nothing to be done as far as surgery...we could only wait and hope she would recover.

for a week, she drifted in and out of a coma as almost a dozen friends and family streamed in from around the country to be at her side. the hospital took incredible care of her, and all of us. they made us feel so comfortable, people kept referring to it as the hotel, instead of the hospital. when i complained about the fold out chair i was sleeping in, they found me a better one. staff was caring and compassionate. doctors were accessible and informative. i can't think of anything i wish they would have done that they did not do.

at the end of the first week, when most of our friends had to leave, the cafeteria manager helped arrange a thank you gathering and provided snacks at no charge. the meals there were cheap and excellent. 

after the first week, my wife came out of the coma and started to get better. they arranged for her to move to a skilled nursing facility in albuquerque. her recovery has been miraculous.  

i love our little hospital.

i am pretty amazed at some of the bad reviews here. at least two of them are from people upset that the hospital did not provide them transportation home. looks like a lot of people just don't understand that, in the er, its not first come, first serve. they treat the sickest first. we've been the the er 3 times, and found it totally professional.

if i could give zero i would. my daughter got stomach virus. the wait has been two hours and we r still waiting!!. people rude. avoid!!! they are the only hospital in town snd they know it. waiting room full of people and they just don't care. my daughter just throws up every 15 minutes. shame on any doctor who works here. we are from austin,tx and have never waited this long. they say that the rooms are full but i have gone to our hospital at home and they would line us up in the hallway and treat us there. do not retire in this town! you will likely die in the waiting room. what a nightmare.
the doctors and nurses- aside from one exceptionally rude er nurse- are great. the registration folk are across the board (pun intended) a nightmare.

worst hospital!!!
they don't know what they are doing. they have the worst er nurses. i had to call their supervisor to finally have them explain to me what was going on with my father. they got so angry that they began to completely ignore me. my father was having a stoke and they wanted to discharge him. i just hope they can get their shit together because sadly the health of others are in their hands and they don't seem to know basic information. instead of my priority being focused on my fathers health and comforting him it was focused on arguing and calling their supervisor so my father could receive medical help. i'm truly shocked on how horrible my experience was i was caused distress the whole stay.
fac_name: Dignity Health - St. Bernardine Medical Center

review: my husband was admitted for neurosurgery. we arrived a little earlier than our appointed time and were taken in shortly thereafter to do the inpatient registration paperwork. everything went smoothly and we were taken upstairs to pre-op (acu). everyone there was absolutely amazing. as usual, the surgeon was backed up on his schedule. when surgery was over, i received a call from the nurse in recovery to let me know how my husband was doing. when my husband was ready to go upstairs, the nurse called me back and advised me of the room and i went to meet him there. all the nurses and staff went above and beyond in caring for my husband.
fac_name: Dignity Health - St. Bernardine Medical Center

review: there is a serious issue with their billing department. i went to the emergency room in april of 2018, received my bill and paid the $50 co-pay in june. over a year later i receive a phone call stating i never paid the bill! thankfully i still had the email with my receipt. when i called them back to give them my confirmation number i was placed on hold. after 30 minutes of holding i was disconnected. i called back and was told it was taken care of. a month later i receive a letter stating i still owed the $50!!! my husband called to dispute this only to be told that they see the payment was received over a year ago, but the main office has not removed the charge, and that they will contact him later during the week letting us know if the main office has changed my account to show paid. what's even more crazy is the same thing happened to my sister in law, who was billed twice, and my father in law who received a bill that was for a different patient who happened to have the same name. the billing department didn't even bother to check the date of birth to verify they were billing the correct person. i'm beginning to think this whole thing is a scam to rob people. all i can say is save your receipt. you never know if you'll end up getting billed for something you paid over a year later!
fac_name: Dignity Health - St. Bernardine Medical Center

review: my wife went to the filthy emergency room for what ended up being kidney stones, after treatment the nurse discharged her and we left, she gets a bill a month later for the $50 copay, we pay it thinking that was the end of it.  but we were wrong... she gets a call 15 months later asking she call them back, where they tell her she owes the $50, she tells them she has the email and confirmation number, they put her on hold for 30 minutes, then hang up on her, she calls back and a different lady says it's taken care of.  11/15 we get a bill for the $50 that states it was going to collections and is pass due, i call them and they say they see the payment but don't understand why the "main office" hasn't taken the charge off the account, i ask if i can contact the main office and they say only they can, but they are unable to change the account to show it was paid.  she in fact confirmed it was paid but said there's nothing she can do, until her supervisor contacts the main office.  this is insane, how doesn't the main office see the payment when their "call center" sees it.  i can imagine the amount of people that have paid the amount more than once, because of their fraudulent billing practices.
fac_name: Dignity Health - St. Bernardine Medical Center

review:
on sunday, dec 1st, our daughter's friends brought her to prisma health baptist, after bringing her to urgent care, which they were not able to draw blood and test it. they were worthless. 
when they brought her to prisma health baptist emergency room, the staff was rude and so unprofessional to the group of girls, saying that they were "sorority girls". they would not test our daughter and the doctor did not believe she had mono. they did not take the girls seriously at all. this was extremely upsetting to us, since they are of age college students! they should be treated as adults and taken seriously, especially when they are sick!   we drove from summerville, sc to columbia, sc an hour and 30 minutes away. they started drawing blood and testing her when we arrived in the emergency. this is totally unacceptable and should have been done when our daughter was first in with the doctor! the doctor brought back the results and our daughter had mononucleosis. they only said that she should take motrin and extra strength tylenol every 3 hours switching off when she has a fever. they said if she has any symptoms, such as vomiting, jaundice (yellow) face and skin, dark urine, pain in abdomen to bring her back. we left and brought her back to her dorm room.  on tuesday, dec 3, our daughter's roommate called and she had all the symptoms that the emergency rooms said, so i drove up to columbia, sc and brought her to musc in charleston, sc. they admitted her into the hospital and tested her and diagnosed her with mononucleosis and cold agglutinin disease. 
we will never take our daughter back to prisma health baptist emergency room! we will always bring her to musc from now on, since they have the best doctors in the state and took the best care of her, which was so much appreciated. they were so professional and caring and updated us on our daughter's status regularly.

i was taken to the hospital's er after having a seizure. my address information was given to the admitting staff once my daughter and sister arrived. and yet, i never received the bill. all of a sudden, a negative charge for more than $6,000.00 appeared on my credit report. even when i asked to see the charges, it still took forever to receive the itemized total.

your better off dead than going to this place. 
unprofessional staff with bad behaviors. 
wouldn't recommend this hospital even to my worse enemy's.

absolutely horrible. dr. brittany glenn was rude and lacked compassion. she was dismissive to every single thing i was trying to address. i feel like i was treating terrible here and never even given a room before they just discharged me still scared and in pain. they took nothing i said seriously and did not even check for all that i was asking for. 

what a waste of time and money. i'm so disappointed in the care i received here. many young nurses (male and female) with big attitudes. they seem to talk down to everyone and i could hear them talking about stuff behind people's back. 

no way to run a hospital, much less an er where people are feeling that they are in a crisis and are looking for support. 

i've always hated coming here, but unfortunately had to go back because i needed somewhere quick and it was the closest.

even one of the nurses there apologized for dr. glenn's behavior and also thought that i was treated poorly. she said i should contact the hospital and report it. 

worst hospital i've ever been to! maybe you should read your reviews and take them more seriously and change the way you do things. i will be reporting this doctor.

i was seen by the emergency department care team on 2/11/2020. vanessa, the admitting nurse was very kind, and the triage team took my vitals, gave me a mask and sat me down in the waiting area. it was recommended that i get a chest x-ray. instead of walking to another building, i went into a nearby area of the emergency dept and received my chest x-ray. the x-ray technician was very friendly and patient with me.  while i was waiting to see doctor, director of er, lee passow chatted with me to see how i was feeling. doctor assessed my condition and the discharge nurse, jennifer handed my paperwork, she informed me that doctor wanted me to take meds and discharge nurse called in my prescription to nearby walgreens. when i went to nearby walgreens, my prescription was waiting for me!!   

due to me not feeling well, i was very impressed with corona regional medical center's emergency care team. i'm on the road to feeling well!!

it's really no surprise that this hospital has a bad reputation. everyone who lives or grew up in corona knows, that corona regional isn't the best. sure they might be trying to improve their reputation, but i believe they care more about expansion rather than care. corona regional hospital has plans to expand in the near future to increase their profit. which is scary since they will be providing more services to the community. in my experience they don't treat patients well, especially in the locked unit. patients are taken advantage of and not treated fairly. i've been to this hospital on several occasions, not by choice but rather due to logistics. if possible, i go to loma linda or a different hospital. the hospital seems to have a high turnover rate as well because staff members are overworked. listen to all the bad reviews and heed the warnings about this hospital.

i didn't get his name but he was a male nurse in labor and delivery and i honestly loved him. he was so nice and on top of his game. 1 shot he got my vein didnt even feel for the vein just saw and hit it once very awesome job!!! didnt even hurt as most do

i was so impressed by this er today. i walked in was greater by the friendliest staff. took me right back and did vitals. then i sit in waiting area not even 10 minutes and doctor calls me back. he asks we what's wrong and tells me then action plan. i get put in a room 5 minutes later. they start treatment right away. take x ray really fast. then nurse claire was amazing. she made me feel so comfortable. the only down side was they didn't have a bed for me but i still was in a comfy recliner chair. claire apologized for no bed and having to wait. i had to have a two hour iv and claire went and got me snacks. they sent me home with prescriptions and the whole process was so smooth. i would highly recommend this er.

we had a wonderful experience with labor and delivery! all of the nurses were amazing in labor and delivery as well as postpartum. they went above and beyond to make sure we were taken care of! the anesthesiologists did a great job and checked on me the next day. big shout out to lynda, gina, dominque, alex, hope, lisa, melissa, and heather, (i'm sure i'm missing more wonderful nurses, sorry)! thanks for the great experience!

honestly just had the best er experience i could have had. i've been to a few other ers in my day, so i have some experiences to compare, and this one was by far the most efficient and professional. every staff member that interacted with me was kind and communicated clearly, too. i'm glad i ended up here when i needed it! thank you to the er team here.

their er sucks my daughter was complaining of chest tightness and shortness of breath and all they did was sat her in the waiting room for so long they came and gave her inhaler she checked her lungs and said her lungs were clear and send her home and said when you feel like you can't breath at all and feel like passing out come back  i don't recommend anyone to go there....the next day i took my daughter to her primary doctor and she checked her lungs and said that her lungs have diminished sound i'm like wow....they did the same with me in the passed i was feeling dizzy and feel like passing out they said i was dehydrated and i told them no i know my body can you do mri and they said no need for mri...the next day i made and appointment with my primary doctor and she gave me the the order for mri and sue enough there was a mass under my brain ...

my recent experience was horrible, my sister was taken to er for headache, shortness of breath tingling in the arm. they assessed her and later diagnosed her with high blood pressure. she was released with high bp vitals about 2 hrs later and a major headache...  it's unreal how the staff let her go home with vitals still high.  released and given instructions to follow up with dr the following day.  she returned to dr as instructed, dr requested documentation from er visit come to find out all information documented was of another patient. the only information on the triage  paperwork was the headache! what's going on? do they not pay attention to their job? my sister could have had a major stroke or even worse! i will not go to this hospital unless i absolutely have to!!

not a good hospital.  nurses are rude and don't care for the patients.  
my brother was admitted into icu for high sugar and he's diabetic.  was released the following day and he still wasn't feeling well.  he said he felt his blood sugar was not good and when he stated this to the nurse she just gave him 2 juices and took him to the the front door and left him there.  
when he was getting released he asked the icu nurse if he could wash up before he left and he was told that they don't have sink basins to wash up. 
when i arrived to pick him up he was standing outside where he was left by the nurse. 
i've been to nice hospitals where they will wheel you out when your ride arrives and they make sure you're okay . 
this hospital sucks!!

illegally forced medication into me more than once and experienced an illegal threat to consume medication or it would happen again.

not fun, not enjoyable. illegal and the staff was informed (from myself) about it prior towards the actions being performed.

other staff members of whom had concern repaired the scenario by being kind and documenting what had occurred. those staff members would bump the review up to a 3... the food was quite delicious...

however, the bathrooms were not of the cleanest nature.

a number of staff members were amazingly blessed (kind, sweet, polite, empathetic, sympathetic, understanding & comprehending) and with other staff members the experience was illegal and not enjoyable.

point is, the protective rights/rules that were placed around me were broken and it lead towards me being forced to consume medication and that was not enjoyable.
legal medical term duress. 

different staff members and different experience.

really deserves a 1 star, however the kindness of the staff members that actually had concern does bump the rating up to a 2 star.

the reason i also wrote about the 3 star was because of the healthy food that was provided by the kind staff and because of the friends & eternal friends that i had been blessed with.

blessed to have met them and hoping they are doing okay.

unfortunately, the experience was poor. i worked in the area as a transport medic and had always good experiences with the staff at corona er. 
as i went in with my father as a patient, the experience was completely different. we waited quite some time, in a not very busy er. when we got in, my father had symptoms that most hospitals would consider doing an ekg for. none was done here. 
when brought up, the pa stella was short. i know a lot of the staff here from work, and i was extremely let down my stellas poor bedside manner. my father was treated for his pain, with not much further of an answer. i know that the er is meant for emergencies, not always diagnosis, but he wasn't even brought into a room for an actual evaluation. he never even got an actual hands on doctors assessment! wild. 
silly enough, as we waited in the waiting room, a bum with a completely nonsense complaint, that came in behind us; got a bed and a sandwich  

tip, skip this er. head to rch, where you will be treated like a human. better yet? get kaiser. 

the two stars is for the quick and appropriate treatment of my fathers pain. only thing i'd much agree with here.
the worst 4 day hospital experience ever.  i'm still too sick to write much.  i begged the paramedics not to take me there.
i am so glad they finally expanded the facility in order to accommodate more patients. the emergency room is newer and bigger.

i went in for a monogram and got the best assistance ever . the whole hospital is very clean and have fast service , only took 15 mins for everything and there is not that much waiting . better than any other hospital i have ever came too . from reservation in front the lady was so nice .

i hate to write a bad review but i had to maybe if this happened again this person has better luck .  last saturday dic 28 around 6:30/7pm i got off the bus after been in it for almost 4 hrs i am not familiar with the buses lines so i got off bell/6th and i started to walk towards ontario about 2 more miles i was just released from a hospital been treated for phneaumonia i was feeling pretty sick still the night was cold and i wasnt wearing a jacket and my feet and bones was hurting bad let along the hard time breathing , and then i start getting cramps i look around for a bathroom nothing just the hospital so i was releved and i started to walk fast towards this hosp and at soon as i got in i was ask ^ how may i help you ^  by a person at front desk so i told her that i have an emergency and i need to use the bathroom please and she ask me if i was gonna see a dr i say no and i only need to use the bathroom , she say no , i told her the i still have long way to walk and theres no other bathrooms on the way she say im sorry but no '  well you guys can imagine my walk home was a real nightmare i dont have a phone to call anyone for help .                                    i was totally in shock , i coulnt believe a hospital denied the use of the bathroom to a person in need smh.....

do your best to avoid this place, even if it means driving a little more to riverside community hospital or pomona valley. my father was taken to er, last week after an unwitnessed fall. after being admitted, his condition worsened, after being in the hospital for 7 days. i had enough of not knowing because hospital policy is the rn cannot communicate to family what the diagnosis, prognosis or treatment. the primary doctor is the only person who can inform only one (1) family member. how inefficient is this, as if an rn is incapable of such communications. his doctor was awful and talked to us, so condescending. his doctor was offended,'because i wanted to know what's going on....seriously? she was so unprofessional and accused me of "not liking" her. i responded, "really?! lady, this ain't about you! wow! let's focus on my father, please! " then she got more offended that i called her "lady"! too much bs. the quality of care solely depends on that primary doctor and the assigned rn. trust your instincts. if something does not sound right, get another opinion! advocate for yourself or your loved one!

st. vincent healthcare medical records has merged my records with someone elses.  after numerous telephone messages left with the medical records department (they never actually answer their telephone, you have to leave a message, then a week later, at 5 minutes to 5:00 p.m., they call you back, and leave a message, assuring you never actually get to connect with a person) i am left wondering why the leadership void and complete absence of professionalism, accuracy, helpfulness and civility?  i guess st. vincent healthcare's mission statement is simply a marketing device.

nfrm pond lighting was a blast of holiday time a spirit. park across the street at the mall and the cops for crossing. there was several food trucks, face painting, make decorations, a movie, santa and other activities. so it you looking to get lit this holiday season it definitely worth a look see.

note this review is only about the nfrm pond holiday lighting display.

my 90 y.o. mother and her 97 y.o. husband are residents of an assisted living facility. on sunday 2-9-20 my mother couldn`t get out of bed. my step dad called 911. she was taken to nfrm by rescue at around 8:00 am. by the time i drove from jacksonville, picked up my step dad and got to the er it was close to 11:00 am. they had sedated her in order to examine her as she has dementia and becomes agitated if her husband is not with her. upon our arrival she was sedated and sleeping. their test could not find anything wrong with her but they wanted to admit her for observation. we asked when she would be admitted and moved to a room. they told us the did not have any beds available at this time . we were concerned  and didn`t want to leave her but didn`t want to watch her sleep for hours. upon my request the er nurse gave me her cell phone # and told us to call in a couple hours and she would let us know if she was awake. i called the # at 2:00 and no answer, 3:00 same results. finally at 4:00 we just showed up. she had been moved to a different room and was basically unattended as she was waiting for a room to become available. we asked the staff if her husband would be allowed to stay with her in the room as she becomes agitated and uncooperative if separated from him. we were told by a couple er nurses that it wouldn`t be a problem and they would put a recliner in the room next to her bed. so here we are in a er room awaiting a room. one chair for us to sit on  which we gave to my step-dad while my niece and i stood. mom was still out of it. still waiting for a room to become available. a board in the room shows that some test were ordered and completed and others were pending. we asked about which test were done and the results but nursing staff was unable to give us answers. we asked which test were pending and the answer was the same. we are getting mad that we are just in a room with no idea whats going on or when a room will be available. finally about 7:00 pm they told us a room was available but it had to be cleaned. we waited and waited. finally the nurse tells us that because multiple room became available at the same time housekeeping had to clean them in the order of the vacancy so we had to wait longer for them to clean her assigned room.

i don`t remember what time we got to the room but i again asked the guy transporting her about her husband staying in the room. his response: that`s not a problem. in the process of transferring her to the bed it was discovered she had been laying in her own urine for quite awhile. i then asked her nurse about her husband staying in the room and the answer was "absolutely not". this is the women`s floor and no men were allowed to stay in the room. they said he could sleep in a recliner at the end of the hallway, in the visitors area. i asked to speak to the charge nurse and she reiterated the same thing. she didn`t get that i was upset because everyone up to this point had stated "no problem" and at the last minute she says no! major communication breakdown. this lack of communication causes us problems and get my mother and step-dad to become upset. in addition, even though they had a list of her meds it took them until the next day to admin. to her.

because they found no medical reason to treat they ordered pt to get her up and moving. i spent 2 whole days next to her bed and never saw a physical therapist. i spoke to the case manager about transferring her to a rehab facility and she stated she sent referrals to 2 places and has not heard from either. 

in the meantime my mother becomes delusional, agitated and "talking crazy" i told the nursing staff i believe my mother has a uti as i have seen this behavior before and know it can be caused by a uti. the nurse stated she was checked for a uti in the emergency room and was negative. talked to the dr. about it and she denied a uti stating my mom`s dementia along with a new environment caused her to be confused.my niece along with her father refused to accept this explanation and demanded she be tested again for a uti. guess what ? positive for a uti. antibiotic iv was administered and she is slowly recovering from the delusions.

still haven`t seen the pt. follow up with the 5th floor case manager revealed that we didn`t hear from terrace view rehab because referral was not submitted.

my mom was finally transferred to a rehab facility where she can get the help she needs. all of my family agrees that the hospital experience at nfrmc was terrible and if my mom had stayed there any longer they may have killed her. i have never been a patient in a hospital but  i have been in a bunch of them. this was the most disorganized and neglectful place i have ever been. we were angry when she was sent there by brookdale because our hospital of choice was shands.

even though this was not a good experience for us i have to say that rn kym and both of the cna`s were wonderful and took good care of my mom. kudos to them.

i had a horrible experience at nfrmc. following surgery where peter sarantos tore blood vessels during the surgery and then lied about it to cover his blunder. the next day the torn blood vessels ruptured and i suffered an internal hemorrhage. what was supposed to be same day surgery turned into 9 days in the hospital with 4 in the icu. but after the original surgery i had to deal with negligent nursing staff.  i woke up in a bare bed with a urinal and asked the nurse caring for the confused patient next to me for a blanket. she stated " i am not your nurse" and continued to ignore me for the entire 8 hours until the night shift arrived at 7pm. i had to struggle out of the bed, walk up and down the hall just to get a blanket. i got one from the housekeeper.i asked the clerk at the nurses station " who is my nurse?" she was extremely rude to me. she shouted "cant you see i'm busy" "i'm working on it". i went back to my bed  and no nurse or tech came to my bedside for 8 hours. i received no water, no food, no vital signs were taken, no pain medications. it was extremely frustrating, painful, and unsafe.

i had a miscarriage, after visiting my ob right across the parking lot from the hospital for confirmation on pregnacy, and the er dr questioned if it was just a period.  yeah, after thousands of periods i got confused as to whether this was a pregnancy. and the er dr had already called my ob so they would have confirmed it before he even asked this. if your jaw isn't dropped, you're not human (like this jerk dr). will travel an hour to a better hospital from now on. never, ever, ever will i return. what a horrific experience

this hospital is my favorite hospital!! i've been there maybe 4 times and all the times, i've had great experiences. i gave birth to my daughter here a couple years back and i love it!! my room was huge and the staff were so polite and helpful!! the only bad thing was that i left my phone on the bed and when the lady changed the sheets, she took my phone. i was so upset bc i had photos of my new born!!! they never found it, even tho it was 5 mins after they took the sheets. i did check find my iphone later that night. it appeared to be at some apt complex and i knew i would never get it back. other than that hiccup, every other time i've gone to visit someone or to go to a doc appt; i've had good service. the hospital is also super clean!!!

great overall experience. i went in for chest pain and shortness of breath and was seen right away. everyone was nice and it did not take long to be placed in a room. i wasn't in the waiting room for hours like other places. keep in mind that this was on a wednesday night. i would recommend.

professional staff with state of the art equipment and rooms. all of your medical needs are located on the houston methodist west campus. there is not only an emergency room with little to no wait, but they have 2 medical office buildings with doctors specializing in every medical need a patient could have. the hospital also specialize in cardiac care. the best in the west houston area.

i can't say enough about this wonderful hospital.  my husband went to the er and was subsequently admitted. what impressed us the most was how attentive and friendly the staff was here.  from admitting, to the er nurses and doctors, the 5th floor nurses, catheter lab staff, and even the housekeeping staff, catering staff and technician who fixed the rooms tv - every single person was kind, patient and extremely helpful.  before they left the room they always asked if there was anything else they could help us with. we never felt forgotten and the nurses always made sure we knew what to expect. we have had many stays at various hospitals and none every came any where near the level of excellent we experienced at katy methodist.

i spent 22 days between the trauma step down unit and rehabilitation unit. i was injured at home and because it was considered a trauma, i was transported to regional one. the facility is obviously old, but the service and attention to detail was fantastic. the quality of care was very good. i cannot say enough about the staff. i am home now, still recovering but feeling very grateful for my care.

review:
this hospital has turned into a wonderful place. you saved my husband's life. thank you! 
this is not the same hospital as years ago. i have never seen such an effort made to turn things around.
lone pine is a safer place to live in.

dora cruz takes such good care of my grandmother and is so nice to my family.  
we are very thankful for her help and that she is here at this hospital!!!

my sister had her baby here last week and we had a great experience thanks to l&d nurse elisa and also post partum cna dora cruz. elisa and dora were both very attentive, kind, and went out of their way to make sure our family was comfortable. they were super informative and were more than happy to answer any questions we had and assisted with any help we needed. i'm happy my sister had a great experience delivering her first baby!
nurses were all super nice especially dora, pauline, and brenda.  they took great care of my wife and new born son.  i definitely would recommend san gabriel valley medical center.

my boyfriend had to visit the emergency room for a not extremely severe  reason and we were able to get in and out within the hour. we were given excellent advice as well as reassurance that our issue was not life threatening. we left there feeling assured of the diagnosis we received and the nurses took us seriously and were veery professional.

it took me so long to write this review but here it is. about 5 years ago i went into the er because i had a really bad rash on my back and i was in alot of pain. the dr came in (young asian...can't remember his name) and asked if i knew where i was cause my issue belong in a dermatologist office and then he left the room. he was extremely rude and of i knew what it was i would of gone to where i had to go. anyways a few days go by and i seen my doctor. at first she didn't know what was causing my rash and then a few months later as it got worst she did labs and found out i had lupus. ever since then i never stepped foot in this hospital again and i continue hearing bad things about it so beware and go at your own risk.

i' m here to visit my mom, i am very happy when i walk in to this hospital to see all the staffs with a smile. awesome services! what amaze me is to watch dora cruiz a nurse who provides care of love to a lady next bed of my mom's. this hospital deserves 5 stars

i was actually assigned to this hospital by my hmo despite living in west hollywood. i broke my ankle and am currently non weight bearing on my left leg and spent a few days here under observation. everyone was so helpful and made sure i was comfortable and that my pain was well managed at all times. once i was discharged i received follow up calls to see how i was feeling and how my experience was.

yesterday i had surgery on my ankle and i was absolutely terrified as i've never had surgery before. everyone was so kind and understanding-from the nice young lady at the check in counter who took us up to the correct floor, to the phlebotomist and iv nurse who were able to find my tiny veins in one stick, to the scrub nurse and anesthesiologist who joked with me to calm my nerves. my outpatient surgery nurse susan was absolutely stellar. she was so warm and helpful and did absolutely everything she could to make my recovery as painless as possible. then today i received another call to check in on me.

i have nothing but good things to say about this hospital and will probably continue going here despite the distance because of how great the staff is!
dora is amazing  any questions you have she is so patient and teaches you on those things that you need that you dont know that you need
me encanta este hospital , todos son muy amables y profesionales en especial la enfermera dora cruz que hace su labor con mucho amor y dedication estoy bien agradecida.

my mom was having a very hard time breathing so i brought her to the e.r. 
i was helped by ted vuong who did an excellent job taking care of us and comforting my mom throughout the entire process. in addition, he was able to speak to my mom fluently in chinese which  helped so much and made everything smooth.

my baby is one week old today. i am so happy to choose this hospital for my labor. i love everyone here. i think i have had the best services since i checked into the hospital until discharged. the charge nurse at labor department, irene( yen lu; not sure that is correct spelling) is really attentive. she had checked me so often to make sure i feel comfortable. i appreciate that. my pain is well controlled from the moment my cervix started to dilate until i labored. then, for my postpartum recovery, the nurses are so great. especially, feng and meili, they are so knowledgeable. they taught me a lot of things how to  taking care of myself and my baby. those knowledge has helped me not to struggle so much with my baby. if i have another baby, i will definitely choose this hospital again. i would recommend to my friends and my family! i have a great experience here. love....

delayed review but...i delivered my baby at sgvmc back in september of 2018 and what a disaster it was!!!! we checked in to labor&delivery around lunchtime complaining of severe stomach pain. no pain from contractions, just stomach pain. it was shrugged off as 'normal labor pains'  i kept reinforcing that it  didn't feel normal. they kept brushing it off. during my epidural 13 hours later, i screamed at them that it wasn't normal. again, they brushed it off as another contraction...until seconds later when they lost my sons heartbeat. 
turns out, i was suffering from a very severe complication - placental abruption. my nurse was terrible and started screaming at the top of her lungs - in no way did she try to calm me down at all, in turn causing me to panic and go into distress. they got both of us on to the operating table within minutes - no heartbeat from the baby and an  unconscious mom. 
luckily, both of us are alive and healthy today.
fastforward to the next 4 days in the hospital....i got told i need to suffer through the pain and work through it because 'i shouldn't be needing pain meds this frequently this long after a c-section.' 
i had concerns about the latch of my baby for breastfeeding - no one ever checked, i was simply told 'look at him, he's latched and doing great!!' he in fact was not latched and was not doing great. he had lost 12% of his birthweight and nobody at the hospital cared. he had a severe lip and tongue tie, making latching very difficult. nobody at the hospital took the time to check or figure out. my poor baby was starving and  my concerns were being ignored!
i asked for formula multiple times. after being denied the formula 3 times, we finally demanded it on the 4th time. they begrudgingly gave us formula, as well as a waiver to sign agreeing to subjecting our child to the risk of cancer and obesity due to formula feeding - talk about mom shaming!!! how dare you tell me what is best for my child in this case?! my child was starving!!! 

i could go on, but you get the idea. we will never step foot back in this hospital ever again. you deserve more than what this hospital can give you!

my 84 year old mother stayed overnight for observation in sept. 2019.  san gabriel valley medical center billed medicare over $29,000.00 for 24 hours in a non-critical care bed.  the first bill she received was dated 12/30/19.  i wrote a check for her on 01/06/20.  the hospital cashed the check on 01/08/20.  she received another bill for the same stay from a collection agency, for the same amount plus interest dated 01/07/20.  "predatory billing practices" by hospitals such as san gabriel valley medical center need to be made public, that is why i am writing this yelp review.  we need to take the matter in our own hands since our elected officials seem to be doing nothing about it.  the most vulnerable such as the elderly are most threatened and we all suffer from the huge egg healthcare has laid upon our country's economy.

thank you to the entire san gabriel team. i had the best experience a patient can ask for. from nurses to the rest of the staff, i was truly blessed to be cared for by the l&d and postpartum team. thank you so much.
we've been waiting in the er for 3 hours. people keep coming in and out, and i'm still waiting. i'm being told i'm next and yet nothing is happening. ugh, i rather go to county hospital.

this place is a hole, my mother was screaming after surgery and one of the nurses told her "be quite you're going to wake up the other patients"... did not even come to her once to ask her on a scale 1-10 how bad is the pain... what the fuck is that about ? you're supposed to calm her down and keep her sedated of course she's gonna be in pain after surgery, i hope the stupid bitch that said that to her is reading this, just imagine someone telling your mother that after a mastectomy. i wish i were in the room and found her name, her position would have ended that day. i can only imagine how they treat everyone here. the rn didn't check on her once all night and after she did not offer to help her with anything. also, they're out of face masks? it just gets worse and worse. also, no offense but the asian nurse kept talking over me very loudly when i would as a question. also, she had to share a room which is very understandable, but i wanted to stay overnight and there was no chair to even rest/sit. it was was infuriating, i do not recommend this place and am happy to get my mother out!

the young asian female "practitioner" in the emergency room had a lot of attitude towards a patient and was not professional in any way. as she comes in to speak to a boy who is about 14 years old, the boy is on his phone because they have been making him wait for a while. the doctor then proceeds to start conversation with the boy and the boy is still using his phone during the first few statements. nothing wrong with that. then she proceeds to get all riled up and says "oh i will come back when you're finished because i am very busy right now. and i knew she was not in a very rushed state because when she leaves the rooms she's out there making jokes and playing around on the job. she literally does a couple things such as listening with the stethoscope, checking ears and throat and calls that busy. the boy had the beg the doctor to stay... is that right?? very unprofessional, should not even be a practitioner, doctors should be respectful at all times, her ego was just through the roof! yeah we all get it you're a doctor but becoming a doctor shouldn't increase your ego especially in a medical setting. you just made yourself look very dumb. here's some advice if you're reading this "doctor" before you start your shifts leave your attitude at your own home. you deserve to have your license revoked that ego will eventually get someone killed.

my mother had surgery here today, and i am so impressed and grateful for this hospital! firstly, my mother's doctor asked if he could pray with her before the surgery....that spoke volumes!!! our experience was nothing short of superb! the entire staff was extremely professional and exhibited optimum bed-side manners! the superstars of jhmh for our family were krista, brandy & lauren mc! thank you all for the wonderful work you do each day!

very important to know, you cannot expect too much while visiting a public hospital.
however, this place is very well-managed, it's very clean, and the facility it's nice and comfortable.

they even have a water sign for fountain.

the nurses and doctors were all very nice, energetic, and very friendly as well as knowledgeable about my situation.  every person was as helpful as they could be.  the staff was also as quick to respond as they could be making my night  out the same day instead of an overnight that most people thought my situation would happen.

i'm very surprised to see the reviews for this hospital. i have spent a lot of time here interacting with staff regarding a family member in this facility's care. i have found the staff to be nothing short of exceptional, specifically dr. hull.  they have done everything to make my family feel at ease and to seem make all efforts medically possible.

excellent hospital.  had surgery there and stayed two days.  everybody

i don't know the reason for having an online check in for the er is. arrived at our scheduled time and have been sitting here for an hour now. walk ins are getting in before we are. i guess the pain level isn't high enough. should have come in an hour earlier and been seen and gone already. 

the staff is friendly, but really?

the noisiest er i've ever been in. unfortunately, i've been in many with my mother, husband and my son. the staff was very loud, yelling to each other about what they had for dinner, what movie they were going to watch, talking on the phone loudly about how busy they were,details of other patient's conditions and more. i heard about "all the sick medicare people". supplies were loudly slammed onto counters. 
another issue is after waiting 30 minutes to register we waited over an hour for my friend to see a triage nurse. then another 2 hours before being seen by a physician's assistant. then bloodwork, iv, mess, cat scan and more. my friend never did receive an exam by a medical doctor until the next morning when he was seen by a doctor on the ward he was admitted to. 
nothing about this experience instilled confidence in this facility.

awesome care in the er! great staff!

this was an excellent trip to the er for the least traumatic reason i've ever gone to an er!

yesterday i cut my finger deep while washing dishes when a thin glass broke. it hit the tendon and it needed 5 stitches. 

in comparison to banner desert or the va in phoenix this  was a whole other world of great care and efficiency from an emergency room!

i had almost no wait time to be seen even though i was not emergent. everyone professional i encountered was professional and polite! 

the nurses all did a great job and the pa was also great. 

great job people!

this is my experience  with doctor wild. he does not listen to the patient there is something wrong, but he refuses to listen. he does not take into consideration when the patient is trying to explain their history. the patient knows their body and their history better. the doctor should take that into consideration and listen to what the patient has to say. he came out and said, "i'm sorry, you have a hard ass today". he doesn't take into consideration of the whole picture.

was admitted for a ruptured appendicitis, was able to get in very quick, at least 15 minutes of checking in. all staff were very friendly and responded quickly with urgency. kept up with my vitals every morning and night to be sure i had not gotten any infection post-surgery. bed wasn't all that great, as my back would get a little sore, but tempature of the room was good, so it wasn't hard to fall asleep. from where they put me, it was very quiet and was never woken up from unnecessary notice outside of the room. food will always be hospital food. if you expect good customer service and urgency, come to mercy gilbert.

once again, we found ourselves back at mercy gilbert, but for my mother-in-law this time. overall, the medical care was great - the doctors were skilled and personable and the nurses/nursing staff were patient and considerate. 

we came in through the ed and, as always, the care and experience was excellent! if i were rating only the ed, it would be a 5-star review. 

but! this is the 4th time i've had a loved one at this hospital and the discharge planning was either non-existent or poor, at best. this leads me to believe that this is a pattern for their social services department - that they have been led to believe this kind of service is acceptable. 

this time there, the experience with social services was poor - extremely. 

the first social worker was impatient, did not follow through and was very casual regarding finding a snf for my mother-in-law - we were overwhelmed with everything going on and she hands us pages of facilities in no particular order and tells us to "pick one" and left. we are fairly confident she did not follow up on our request to check with another facility with which we had prior experience as she blew us off when we asked if it was an option.

on the day my mother-in-law was to be discharged, the social worker poked his head in the room and said "they'll be here to pick her up between 4 and 6" and then left. that was it. he didn't tell use what facility it was, provided us no information about it or the address so that we could meet transport there. he didn't sit down with my mother-in-law to explain what was happening or what to expect. she is elderly, just broke her hip and has dementia...she needed that explanation! 

we never saw social services after that. we had more caring, personality and compassion from the surgeon (they're not known for their bedside manner) than we did from social services.  and, then, transport was over an hour late and was terrible. that is a separate issue that we will take up with that company. 

i guess that we should just be grateful that we had any discharge planning at all. and, unlike my father-in-law, she was not discharged with a broken nose from a fall sustained at this hospital because someone did not turn the bed alarm back on. 

perhaps social services did not get the "hello humankindness" (the 
"motto" of dignity health) memo or they just ignore the plaques on the walls that are reminders of that idea. but, really, social services is the department lacking humankindness?  i am confused.  

this is why another hospital remains our hospital of choice, but they were on diversion the day we went to the ed.

my mother was recently there. we had a lot of trouble with the hospitalist from alliance hospitalists group. she has a lot of complicated chronic issues which this physician did not take any of them into account. really subpar. most of the nurses were great except one that i had to report to the charge nurse. my mother was brought to this hospital in emergency but honestly it wouldn't be my first choice. everybody in the emergency room was nice but the place was filthy. girl at the emergency room window was rather unthoughtful when our mother was just brought in by paramedics she acted like it was nothing urgent. all in all a two-star stay.

i was just a patient there for 6 days. i want to commend the nursing and support staff. they were all extremely responsive, caring and helpful. it's impossible to speak highly enough of them. you were appreciated more than you could ever possibly know. hopefully, i expressed that to most of you during my stay.

atrocious is the only word that comes to mind when describing dignity healthcare on the whole and mercy gilbert is no exception. on multiple occasions have had terrible service here. both in the emergency department and in post-op care. similar experiences at the other local dignity run hospital as well. if you have the choice, drive the extra 15min to get to banner.

i have unfortunately had two accidents in the past four months that ended me up in the er. in september, i had a fall and cut my eyebrow open, requiring stitches and in december i had another fall and broke my foot. both times in this er i was treated quickly, as in 5-10 mins and i was in the back. my stitches from my first visit healed very well and the scar is barely noticeable which shows how skillful the physicians assistant is. for my broken foot, i needed surgery and was referred to a wonderful orthopedic clinic for that. the nursing staff was wonderful and attentive. falling and injuring myself sucks but if i do it again (hopefully won't!) i'll come back here! the er staff is wonderful!
