my family had to deal with select specialty hospital since mid november 2019 & just got out of there this last thursday. the main credit i give them is that my father is still alive & some of the staff was nice. though we had a lot of problems there. on christmas day he had a relapse & hasn't fully recovered from it, yet they still forced him out to a rehab center, because of insurance. if we let my dad stay there this move could've killed him.

when we first got the tour of select specialty hospital it sounded & looked great. everyone was so friendly, telling us how well my dad would be taken care of. i really felt this was great for him, at the time my dad was trapped in ohio for five weeks because he fell breaking three ribs & cracked his liver open while a guest at a convention. we were staying in a hotel, coming here would make it so we could go home.  they showed us a therapy room, & had a lot of promises for his care that i felt never happened.

once dad got there we noticed problems right away with our first visit.  the food was pushed in the room, left on a table out of his reach. he could not feed himself, so we ended up feeding him. there was nurses that would help, but there was many times we'd get there and the food would be sitting there not touched out of his reach. i got excited when he finally got to the point of feeding himself. i was there the first time & helped him as much as i he needed.  

dad started to get better, so we were doing ok.  he was talking, watching tv & even asking for his art supplies. on dec 11th, mom was first contacted being told he is being moved to a rehab center & we had to set things up. we were in shock thinking this could be a bit early, but because he was starting to show signs of getting better we didn't fight it. we started to set things up to get him to a center near home, but because dialysis was not set up it was postponed till dec 24th. we got everything set up for the christmas eve move.

on dec 24th, a half hour before his move they found that my dad's back was broken out with the hives. the move was cancelled. so we had made our plans to spend christmas there. i was the first to arrive & saw dad was sleeping with his bi-pap on. i decided to let him sleep till closer to my family got there. though the nurse was warning me that he wasn't doing good. i could see it too. the nurse was in the room a lot with me that day.

when i heard mom was heading over i tried to wake dad.  he was barely waking, acting like he did back before he got here. i was warning my family that he's very bad that day. it was our hardest christmas as he never came too & we kept saying to the nurse and other people there that it could be his co2 because that goes high & it's hard to wake him. though they had the bi-pap on him most of the time, he was not being ignored. when they were trying to hook him back up this heart monitor they were having problems, the nurse even put the connection right on a hairy area so when the guy came in to try and fix the problem he blamed where the connection was put. it was late so we headed home.

in the morning we got a call, he had a relapse and they had to put ventilation tubes into his throat. he also got a feeding tube, which he's been needing as he wasn't really eating good for anyone before this relapse. we would check in with him daily. on jan 1st, he pulled the ventilation tube from his throat. he did not fully recover before his next relapse on jan 10th. at this point they just put a bi-pap on him because he pulled the ventilation tubes out.  

there was a meeting with doctor tata sunday, he told my mom to contact my dad's normal lung doctor, she did just that. he told her to have him moved to beaumont. when she brought this to the doctor on the 13th, he said dad would not be moved for a long time!

tuesday we get a call. dad is being sent out to a rehab center on the 16th. on wed we got his dialysis set up & picked up his stuff so we'd be ready for the transfer on thursday. he's in no shape to be moved. we looked into what we could do for my dad as there was panic going through my family.  

we found that we could get him transferred to beaumont from the rehab place. though we agreed we'd only do that if we needed too. the day of the move came, and when transport got there and saw dad they questioned why he was being moved. when questioned the reply was:

"that is our call to make. not yours. he's fine" - caelin said then she left the room.

my dad was moved, had chest pains on the ride. and was having a hard time staying awake. we then found out transport for dialysis was not set up. because of his health & dialysis he was sent that night to beaumont. 

once he got there had a fever & a sore on his back. they tried a bi-pap on him for over 24 hours, but his c02 went high and his blood pressure dropped low. now my dad is in icu. their call was wrong. dad is not fine.  this was not good care of my father.

i would not go to the er for any reason unless you're gushing blood from your jugular vein. the triage nurse was totally non-empathetic to the level of pain i was in, 10-10. after an hour i asked how long before i could be seen, keep in mind my pain is excruciating, albeit not life-threatening. i was informed they were not a restaurant and they could not give me a time. all the while the girl at the desk and some nurse were yucking it up and laughing while i'm wincing in pain and can't even sit down. after 1:45 minutes i finally left. save yourself and drive the extra 15 minutes to sky ridge.

this is a sh!## hospital. er staff's cognitive abilities are equal to a russian zoo. went in with afib and rvr. they did nothing and released me after 6 hours of no treatment. still with heart rate up in the 150s. my cardiologist was pissed amd told me to go to sky ridge next time. then they charged an additional $108 because i came in at 7:30 am. insurance said this was not a normal charge and refused to cover it.

dr. knaut or however you spell it always rushes me out. no concern, no care, nothing. always says nothing is wrong but yet i go to my primary and they find something. i don't know if it is because of my insurance but he needs to be done with practicing. he's not caring and not kind.

this is my third visit here wirh my husband.  i have yet to have a good visit.  the er ignores you.  it was quicker for us to go to skyridge than to get emergency help at this hospital.  a surgery sceduled for 10:00 didn't start until 12:00.  the complaints keep going.

nurses are terrible at responding to calls they are too busy gossiping in the nurses station to come and help a bed ridden patient in need. experienced this in both maternity and acute care. less social and more work please

went into the emergency room of the castle rock with a slight fracture to my wrist. before i officially signed in i told the lady i was nervous about the money - i have insurance with a 7900.00  deductible. ... i said if i'm worried about money should i go to urgent care? she said that urgent care would send me over here... and then she said not to worry about the money. i went to their er. just to walk in the door cost me over $1,000.00! i found this out after i was x-rayed. i will also be billed for the doctor, the techs and nurses, the x-ray, the pain pills, and the splint they put on my wrist... the problem is i have no idea what it is ultimately going to cost because they don't tell you. i met someone the following week- who also had a broken wrist - she went to urgent care and paid $20 for the exact same thing i received at the castle rock er. so i was lied to and ripped off. these people are liars and criminals. they care nothing about the well being of the person walking into their er - their only concern is getting as much money from you as possible - if at all possible stay away from these crooks. they should be ashamed of themselves!
this place is dirty and disgusting. it's hard to believe people come here to seek help.

this was the first time i have been to the hospital. i was here for the woman's and children's department. the parking deck was pretty hectic and you have to exit the deck by going to the top floor. you also have to pay for parking - they take cards.
i was a new patient here. i arrived early for my appointment and the receptionists were kind. they were very thorough with labs and their questions. i waited 45 minutes in my room for my meeting with my gynecologist and the nurse came in and told me they will be another hour and a half because of emergency surgery. so, after driving a hour for this location i was not seen by a doctor unfortunately and had to head home and reschedule my appointment, which is a month from now. i get that things happen and doctors have priorities; however it was extremely disappointing. thank goodness my symptoms are manageable! i look forward to having a better experience in a month.

i'd give this place no starts if possible.  my son went last night to the er there as he was in terrible pain and thought he had a kidney stone.  he begged and begged to see a doctor while vomiting on their front desk.  no one ever saw him.  they said they had no rooms.  he didn't need a room.  he needed someone to look at him.  it might have been food poisoning as he finally felt better after throwing up there four times.

how the hell does this place not send a doctor to look at him after an hour of being in pain?????  so much for the south.  i'm in ny and trust me this wouldn't happen at my er room.  this place sucks the big one.

this hospital is the worst!!!  ridiculous wait time in the er with uninterested, unengaged staff...we couldn't get anyone to come help us while we were waiting on a doctor and my poor elderly mother peed in the bed!!! no one would make eye contact to help us. and when she was admitted to the hospital, it wasn't safe for me to leave her by herself because the staff wouldn't come when she called and she kept having to poop and pee on herself, waiting for help. furthermore, she was an extreme fall risk, and the staff disabled the bed alarm in her room and just set up a portable potty by her bedside for her to use. also, both her arms were bruised badly up and down because no one could get a decent pick line in. rather than call on a pick team to come do it professionally, they kept sticking her over and over and over and over. i've never met so many unprofessional, uncaring hospital staff in my life. i would never take someone i love and want to survive to this hospital!!!

went to aspirus to visit with lynn kern for my first obgyn appointment. this is my first pregnancy so i was excited but nervous. the nurse who greeted me was very much robot-ish. not the most friendly to start with. when i was met with lynn she stated she need to be fast because she had another  patient she was helping.. granted i was early for my appointment and this was my scheduled time with her. anyways i proceeded and didnt ask much because i'm still very new to this all. once she start the bedside ultrasound she asked if was still pregnant.. obviously i was confused but said yes. about a minute and a half rolls by and she decides this was taking too long and to send me to an ultrasound. i cried the whole way there.. finally in the ultrasound they confirmed a valid pregnancy. however i'm so upset she couldnt have taken a few extra minutes with the bedside ultrasound.. i'm now stuck with a $700 ultrasound bill that i believe was not needed at all. i'm with marshfield clinic now and much happier!
room was filthy. staff overworked. no customer relations. only good thing was our surgeon who goes other places also. check it out beforehand if you can.

was accused of only wanting drugs and shelter after being sent to their emergency room from a doctors appointment. it was extremely offensive not only because i am not a drug user, but also because i was dressed professionally (i was supposed to go into work after my doctors appointment that morning) so clearly i'm not living on the streets. the doctor that accused me of wanting drugs never came back in after my pee test came back clean, but the doctor that took over was no better. they discharged me while i was still actively showing the symptoms i came in for and shortly after leaving i lost consciousness, but refused to go back. i will be using my secondary insurance to receive care at ahn hospitals from now on.

worst service from the front counter lady at the er. i was rushing to take my brother when his fever was 105 degrees and asking for the paper work to fill it out for him. i had politely asked for the paper that we need fill out in order to check in and she very absurdly just said "first of all who are you?" and held it down and said "my brother is having an emergency can i get the paper that we need to check in?" and she decided to reply rudely with " that's not how we say it here, you're not saying it right." what if english was my second language or if i had speech impediment. this looks very bad considering she is working at a hospital. i didn't catch her name considering she was turning to the side with her name badge but it was the african-american lady with glasses.

this place is a pit, filthy & disorganized. the staff are rude & hostile. no one knows the answer to anything. my spouse has been waiting on a gurney for 2 hours for a bed. our hoc is st. jude but they were full. he will be transferred asap. choosing this dump was a huge mistake. stay away!

well besides one rude er dr me whole experience was wonderful. not even in my room yet all the staff making jokes making me feel welcome. props to su in icu. your the bomb. all of you guys. i felt like a king there. to all the icu staff. i b.v wish i could give this experience  10 star. huge rooms nice po privacy.  i hope i get dick again just to go see them. i

wow wow wow!!! 
best service ever!!! 
had my baby here 2 weeks ago and i can see why everyone on the big island recommends having their baby here. 
can't review the whole hospital but the women's center as well as the birthing family unit is amazing! so coordinated.
all my pre pregnancy was managed by the 4 midwives and the 3 obgyns here. they try to get you to meet everyone because everyone takes call and who knows what day you will be in labor. 
thank goodness we live 5min away because labor is no joke. 
akiko and dr. kong were life savers! didn't take a birthing class because i knew my birth wasn't gonna be like what they said. as soon as i arrived they pushed for me to get a epi because i wanted one and i got one within 15min of arriving. thank the lord. but this hospital is well known for having a major percentage of non anesthesia and non c section births. to each their own! 
after 12 hours in labor with 2 hours of active labor, i had round the clock service for 48hours by multiple nurses with great food! 
skin to skin contact immediately with 1 hour without any measurements or doctors. just me my hubby and our baby interrupted. we even got delayed cord clamping. they are very attentive to what you want with your birth plan. 
i hope to have another child

good for routine things:  immunizations, sinus infection, urinary tract infection, general checkups, physical therapy, etc. they also have an er.  staff is friendly, patient, and calm, the interior has beautiful hardwood floors and you can see hawaiian quilts and other displays on the walls.  like any hospital, they serve the entire community from infants to elderly, but because it is a smaller community it can have a more comfortable feeling, like you are not just a number. because it is a small community and facility, expect to have a wait. bring a snack and some water if you are the type to get hangry (hungry+angry).

sometimes chronic symptoms or conditions/diseases that need specialists take a long time to get taken care of, or to find the right treatment. you may have to wait for a specialist to come in from honolulu or for an appointment to open up on a lab's fully booked calendar, so there also isn't a lot of choice in this area as a whole.  

i would recommend going to a bigger hospital for rare and severe conditions, but in general this hospital serves a vital need in the community and i'm glad it's here.

had an er visit yesterday due to a sever allergic reaction. it was probably the shortest er visit iv ever had in my life. the doctor and nurses were extremely friendly, helpful, and thoughtful. i'm visiting the big island from the mainland for unknown amount of time and didn't bring any warm clothing on our trip. a nurses brought me multiple blankets to keep me warm and comfortable. hand down one of best er visits i've ever had.

first i must start by saying that i am  picu nurse in new york city so i was not sure what to expect when i needed to go to the emergency room here on the big island bc i thought i may have a blood clot in my leg after the long flight . to my surprise i received excellent, efficient & quick care , even better than i have received in some of the hospitals i have been back at home . dr gary goldberg was amazing , he was in to see me right away , kept checking on me & had impeccable bedside manner. he updated me on my results as they came in & luckily everything was negative. my nurse ashely was also just as terrific, attentive & kept me updated too. the us tech, x-ray tech & everyone i came in contact with was so professional that i felt the need to commend them & write a review. my standards are very high & you guys all rock , thank you for the excellent care you gave me ! mahalo! don't be fooled by the small town vibe , they really know what they r doing up in waimea!!

st. luke's is the reason that healthcare in this country has such a bad reputation. my daughter and i got the flu while on a ski vacation at tamarack and unfortunately the only thing open in the area was st lukes. we spent about 20 minutes waiting for a doctor and when he came in he spent abut 5 minutes telling us that we definitely had the flu but did no tests and gave us no medicine. we just received a bill for over $1200 after insurance for the visit, an amazing rip off. we will never use a st luke's ever again and i suggest you never attend their if you are in central idaho or any area they serve.

i rarely would dive into being happy about being in a hospital. however i really think this place deserves to be recognized. from the moment i came into the er to being admitted and being in the main hospital, i have been treated like i'm a guest at a 5 star hotel. doctors were methodical, listened, patient, and not in a hurry. the staff and nurses have been exactly the same and incredibly personable/friendly. they have gone out of their way to keep me as comfortable as possible and treat me like i was the only one that mattered. when was the last time you could say that about a hospital visit? this is a remarkable hospital and team. thank you leeza, laura, rebecca, and dr. lewis for the amazing care you've been providing me. it is truly appreciated.

happy holidays! the best place to bring your children for medical needs!  !
a safe place to be. merry christmas

it's got to be one of the dirtiest hospitals i've been in understaffed not enough rn  nurses my father stayed here different doctors all the time never knew what medication he was really on worst place i wouldn't recommend it

p.a stephens decided that having labs drawn on my son in the e.r were not important. he is 10 years old have chest pain it was hard to breath shaky dizzy yes it was slightly better since we were in the room but she didnt want labs. she said he looked fine, yes someone may look fine but until labs are drawn you wont fully known unless your a mind reader..... i used to work here very disappointed.  i work at moffitt now an we  dont asses people by assuming.  we actually get evidence to help dmfind a solution

i went for my first mammogram at memorial hospital west and was highly impressed!! check in was fast and efficient. i was personally walked to the area to wait by a nice lady. i was explained every step of the process. they had a nice changing area and even had coffee and little cookies/crackers in the waiting area. the woman who performed my mammogram was so professional. she explained everything and told me she has been doing this for 30 years. i was amazed how quickly i received my results, which revealed no cancer thankfully. i was treated very well and not like just another number. 

a friend of mine was diagnosed with breast cancer and was very impressed with the care at this hospital. her nurse was truly caring and made my friend feel as much as ease as you can in that situation.

went to the hospital because my big toe was cut badly and it needed mending. the emergency room was excellent , the doctor and nurse who helped me had really good bed side manners. my big toe was glued and
bandaged up and off i went home. thank you for the excellent care and for attending to my bleeding toe promptly. parking was easy.

came here hoping that i would be able to give birth to my daughter. after moving to miami  at 32 weeks, no obgyn would take me in because i was so late and the hospital i was affiliated with in hawaii didn't have any nearby hospitals in miami, their nearest location was in  jacksonville. however, when i felt contractions coming, i waited about 5 hours until they were more consistent and closer together and checked into the hospital. they immediately took me in, i had to do some paperwork, give them my prenatal records from hawaii, and they didn't give me a hard time at all. everyone was nice and expedient and they assured me that everything was going to be okay. i was in labor for 12 hours and they didn't rush a c-section and didn't try to transfer me anywhere. they were persistent ad supportive and the nurses made sure i was hydrated and gave me a clear liquid diet (i didn't eat  since the day before). when my daughter came they moved me to a room within hours and made sure i was comfortable the whole time. nurses and doctors were very informative and they were strict to make sure i was feeding baby on time and that  she was able to come home with me within the 2 days (she was coombs positive and had to be put on the blanket for jaundice). i love this hospital and the people in it. definitely recommend!

i was in the e.r. two days ago.  the staff was absolutely wonderful.  janelle, karen, elvie and jessica were all very pleasant, caring, considerate, used good infection control technique and i truly felt well cared for. they all deserve a 5 star rating.    this evening i called and the "nurse" by the name of seneca was arrogant, rude, condescending, uncaring and had a very nasty tone of voice.  my fiance heard the conversation and was shocked that a nurse from santa ynez cottage hospital would treat someone that way.  her tone of voice made me feel like a child who was being scolded. my discharge papers stated that if no improvement to return to e.r.  my call was to confirm that even though i have an appointment with my primary doctor on thursday that i could come back in.  she told me that i should go to marian hospital closer to my home if i felt it was an emergency. i told her that it is not an emergency but am still in severe pain and the ibuprofen was not working.   myself and my entire family always go to santa ynez cottage hospital because of the kind way that we are treated by staff.  not any more.  this person needs to find a different profession because of the way she speaks to the human race

review:
i was transferred here from cedars due to some insurance issues. the transfer required me to be open minded as this hospital is visibly older so i gave it a chance. there has been a great lack of communication between the team of people responsible for my case. at first there was uncertainty about if i could eat or not due to a procedure i was supposed to have, the only thing is i wasn't scheduled for any procedures so they had me fasting from 3pm one day until just about 3pm the next day for no reason. i had asked about it and they kept saying they would get ahold of the doctor to ask and find out more information but it took for me to call patient support for them to figure it out. i am in the hospital due to my oxygen levels dropping while ambulating which is a scary thing in itself so they were trying to figure out if i had another blood clot in my lungs that is causing it or if the hole in my heart that is the cause. i have not seen any sense of urgency to try and figure it out. every other doctor that comes in here has said something different, one will say it's a pe the other will say it's the hole. i'm on day 3 no with no definitive diagnosis and it is beyond frustrating. i could keep writing but i'm still here and getting more and more annoyed by the minute. i have encountered 2 nice nurses who did their rounds when they were supposed to but some other staff are not as great. avoid this hospital if you can!

i'll be updating this post until i leave. i'm not getting any answers. these doctors are lazy. i'm asking questions and all i'm getting is "i don't think so"when it should be answered with either yes or no. if you don't know do more research and/or consult another doctor and figure it out!

upon discharge i asked for a work note and the doctor literally said "you work at a clinic, your boss is a doctor he should know". my mind is blown. i should have said and yes i'm a nurse and the way you all operate around this hospital needs to be reported.

review:
this is regarding the kaiser south sacramento infusion center an rheumatology clinic. 
several months back, i took my sister in for her infusion. she had an anaphylactic reaction to the medication being infused. the male nurse (who transferred in from the ed)  was excellent. he knew what to do and took good care of her. this was supposed to be our last visit under the care of the rheumatologist who ordered the medication. we had, had enough of her poor practices and decided to transfer care to ros. kp.
somehow, because it was the middle of the month, she superseded the new rheumatologist we were transferring to. my sister went in for what we thought was a new medication to try (to get her disease under control). 
i dropped her off and told her i would be back after i picked the kids up from school. within minutes of me getting home, i received a phone call from my sister. she was whispering "can you come back and take me to the bathroom". i asked her to repeat it several times because i could barely hear her and i couldn't believe what she was saying. nevertheless, i rushed back, in rush hour traffic. her door was closed all but a crack. anger came over me when i saw her condition. she was horribly swollen with a bright red face. her face was so swollen her eyes looked closed.  she had a bath blanket over her chest with spit all over it. she said she felt like she had to have a bowel movement and urinate. she said that her nurse told her it that they don't take people to the bathroom. i was stunned, shocked and in disbelief. just then, her rn walks in and says " yeah, um are you the family"? i said "yes". to which she replied " yeah, so we don't take people to the bathroom so if she's going to need the bathroom when she's here one of you need to stay with her and help her to do that. this is an outpatient clinic, this is not inpatient hospital we do not transfer or take people to the bathroom". "if she is gonna be needing to use the bathroom then you're going to have to talk to her doctor and see if she can be admitted to the hospital for these infusions and then discharged when she's done". i was speechless. i looked at her probably with disgust and confusion, then looked at my sister, then looked back at her. she then went on and said "oh yeah she went into shock again we almost had to transfer her to the er". i said, she's allergic to the new medication to? the nurse replied, "her rheumatologist, wanted to try the medication again from last month. we thought that if we front-loaded her with as much steroids as we possible could that she wouldn't have a reaction. but, she did and because we had already front-loaded her with all the steroids; we couldn't give her anything but iv fluid. hence, that is why she is so swollen." i said oh, so you have her the medication that she had known anaphylaxis to. she went into anaphylaxisi again which is why she has to use the bathroom and why she is whispering (swelling in the throat). i said, and which md ordered this? the nurse said it was the md we had just transferred away from. i have since spoke to two separate providers and both agree that the massive amounts of steroid that she was given pushed her into cushing's disease.
in my opinion, the the doctor needs to be reviewed for unsafe medical practices. and the nurse should be reviewed by the nursing board and perhaps have her license suspended. regardless of if a doctor orders a medication or not, if you know it is unsafe for your patient you should not be giving it. thank god for the medical assistant that heard my sister trying to call out for help over her swollen vocal cords and alerted the medical staff team. that is a huge problem with kaiser. they want people that bsn or higher behind their name regardless of how they obtained it and what experience they may have. 
btw, i tried to file a complaint on my sister's behalf because she was too ill to do it herself and kaiser would not allow me to. i was told they have to come directly from the member or you have to be the dpoa on file to file a complaint on their behalf.

in 2009 when this hospital first opened, it was very nice.  the doctors, nurses and staff were professional and courteous.  things have changed dramatically over the years.  my mother was admitted to the hospital in 2015 after a fall on our veranda which left her with a bruised and swollen leg.  they performed an mri of her brain along with xrays. i thought an mri was a bit much but she was 78 at the time.  the doctor just discussed the bruising on the leg and never mentioned the mri results.  i didn't ask because i assumed if the mri showed anything bad, they would have told us.  boy was i wrong!  fast forward to end of 2019.  my mother had an infection that had developed in her leg so she was admitted to hospital for iv antibiotics.  by this time, she had developed vascular dementia unfortunately.  the er doctor was curious about her mental state so he went back thru her records.  that's when he told me that my mom had suffered a stroke in 2015 along with other vascular issues in a different part of the brain.  the er doctor never told us about any of this in 2015 when they did the mri.  in my opinion, the lack of information sharing on their part was medical negligence.  i could have made an appt. for my mother to see a neurologist whereby her further stroke risk could have been assessed and treated.  i will always wonder if her vascular dementia could have been postponed or prevented if she could have started medications sooner.  we'll never know.  on a separate note, i was in the er a few months ago due to ms issues.  the doctor told me that they do not have a neurologist on staff, only one on referral phone call. he also said that they do not have the ability to do an mri from the er. he followed up with a comment about st. anthony's only being a community hospital.  unbelievable!  i did phone the administration office the next day and was told that the er can order an mri but the patient has to be taken to a different part of the hospital. the scan has to be truly an emergency because of already scheduled mri appointments.  i've always been a patient of swedish in downtown seattle so perhaps i've been spoiled.  i enjoy living in gig harbor but may not stay much longer if the hospital situation doesn't improve.

my daughter has a uti, i scheduled an appointment for her to be treated on tuesday but it got canceled due to the doctor being on call, so they rescheduled for 2 hours later, then canceled that one too. 
okay, fine, i'll reschedule for wednesday even though she's in pain and it's not ideal, i just received a confirmation text that it is for thursday, and not wednesday as the receptionist said.

these people are crooked as hell. i was seen in september of 2018 while on vacation. i have insurance but was still billed $2000 and some change for my visit. as soon as i got the bill i started making payments, they sent me to collections anyway, yet they still continue to accept my monthly payments. the collection agency still continues to contact me and it has been put on my credit report even though i have cancelled checks showing that i pay every month and they cash my checks. i've disputed this with the major credit reporting agencies but have still not got anywhere with marshall medical center. i call them, i write them and never get anywhere but they still get there money. 
shiesty shiesty shiesty!! 

also, was told by the er nurse after being in the er for eight long hours, that if i left i could possibly die. umm okay, i'm pretty sure that could be a possibility for anyone correct? just curious if they tell everyone that if they leave they could possibly die or was it just me?? another way to make that money folks.

from the moment my mother was seen in the emergency room and later transferred to the icu, she was treated with compassion, professionalism and even a little humor ( which she needed).  the nurse who took care of my mom in the er kept us up to date with information and had an exceptional bedside manner. i can't thank her enough. 
i stayed with her in the icu and the wonderful care extended there as well. prior to my mom being discharged the doctor was kind enough to speak to me on the phone because i had gone home and missed when he came in to see her. i am thankful my mother is alive and so grateful to the wonderful doctors, nurses and staff who took care of her ( and me) during her stay. 

i felt it was important to remind our health care professionals the importance of treating patients with kindness because it does matter and you matter! keep paying it forward! thank you for allowing us to spend thanksgiving together because we have so much to be 
thankful for. 
carrie r.

it starts with my brother. marshall hospital is a joke. i was born there. my brother gary died there. when i first heard that he was in the emergency, i called tried to find out what what happened... the person who answered referred to my living brother as a gumbie.... i don't know what that means. but it's not good. she didn't know i was the sister. and it shouldn't matter, no one should be referred to as a gumbie. as she said, that is a common reference to people in icu. wtf!!!! 
i should have sued your ass off right then.
my brother was still alive & awake & i was pressured into a dnr. not by him... but marshall.  i was pulled aside & and told he didn't have much time. and he really didn't,  i get that. but they also said we need to make this disciion right now before dr. "sing" comes comes back. well, what does that mean? would dr. "sing " have tried harder to save my brother's life? or at least given us more time  together.

the absolute worse place to go to. went in for strep and what i thought was an abscess. got admitted and taken to the second waiting room pretty quickly (7:00pm) wasn't called to be seen by the doctor till about 10:00pm. went to the room to see the doctor and didn't see him till about 11:00pm. only saw him for less than 5min and that's the only time i saw him. asked 3 different nurses for something about the pain (never got anything until after i was discharged and that's  only because pain medicine was prescribed to me). went to the reclining area and got some blood work done and a strep test. wasn't called for a ct scan till about 12:00am. said it'd take about 15min (took almost an hour) was in the waiting area for about 2 1/2 more hours. didn't get discharged till about 2:15am. got my prescription at their pharmacy and didn't go home till 3am. i was handled by nurses the whole time only seeing the doctor once for less than 5min, never got anything for the pain i was in, never got my results for my strep (was written off as sore throat), and am currently still in the same health i was when i went in if not worse. **also noticed a nurse being extremely rude to a patient who was struggling to speak with her (clearly there was a language barrier) and made no effort to try to listen to her and spoke down to her***

came for my appointment this morning and the check in process was fast and efficient. i saw the doctor and the procedure was painless, fast, and easy! i even got a few goodies to take home :-) my surgeon is amazing and lives up to his awesome reputation! kaiser exceeds expectations and i did not feel any pain during my procedure. i was honestly scared for nothing.

staff is beyond spectacular. nurses and receptionist are friendly and helpful.

i also had a 3:00 appointment and checked in early so the other doctor was able to see me sooner.
they addressed my concern and i was out in no time living my best life.

kaiser is absolutely the best! parking was a bit busy for  10:00 am but i was able to get in and out fast.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review:
came here for my wife's surgery and was very impressed with the facilities and people. while waiting for my wife janice"sissy" came in and really eased our minds. she allowed our adult son "drive by" and say good bye before he had to leave town. she was funny and sweet; i was surprised to learn she was a volunteer.

the check in process was easy and all the nurses were extremely nice. we came here on a wednesday so we were fortunate to spend a little time at the farmers market in the patio. the music and plenty of stands with both raw produce and food.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: the way they run this place is a joke. i brought my 76 year old grandmother to urgent care to see if she had pneumonia and i her there's a wait in urgent care, but it's been over 3 hours and that's just ridiculous! there's no one in the waiting room who was here when we arrived, so, i don't know if she was lost in the system or wtf, but elderly people are more susceptible to illness and shouldn't be kept waiting for several hours. it's just sad.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review:
pediatric urgent care hours are different! please make sure your child is not sick after 430 on the weekends and after 8 on weekdays-they will refuse to see them. i don't understand how you can turn away a child that is miserable and a family that is just looking for some help. aren't urgent care doctors trained for any situation? i've been to the road side urgent care facilities many times before joining kaiser and was seen despite my children's ages. 

you really need to fix this kaiser!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: i was there a few days ago in the emergency room, i was in a lot of pain and feeling so much under the weather. from the moment i walked in till the moment i left this people were the most professional and nice team i ever met. nurses would come frequently to my room to make sure i was confortable, dr came and talk to me and he took his time to make i could be treated right away. i had some issues with my insurance so social worker came and helped me enroll for financial assistance so my visit to the er and my prescription to take was all free. thank you so much for everything
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: i had very severe bronchitis during the winter that caused me to have to see a doctor so many times... some don't seem to take the time to find out the root cause.. even had one doctor. in the er be outright rude.. listen to the patient issues and not what you think is best and the outcome will be more positive .. hopefully my experience with kaiser will be better going forward
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: kaiser wla is the best!  i've been to several emergency rooms -- ucla, cedars, st. john's due to a chronic health condition -- and by far and away, kaiser treated me like a queen.  fast service, polite staff, clean accomodations, easy parking, very efficient, great communication!  i grew up hearing horror stories about the kaiser system, but it is unfair of me to be stuck in a past iteration of it.  clearly, they have upped their game!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: this was hands down the best experience i've had at a hospital!!!! from the time i was in the er until they admitted me and i was finally discharged after 3 days. they gave me a private room!!! i've been to cedars 2 times w my daughter and they had her on a bed in a hallway for 3 hours and forgot we was there. when i arrived at kaisers er, it was a minimal wait( maybe 30 min) then they put me in a room. the er doctor did thorough test!!! x-ray, ultrasounds, ct scan, blood work, everything until she could find out what was wrong with me. she did not treat me like a second class citizen( i don't have kaiser as a insurance)she kept coming in and checking on me up until i was admitted. the social worker called my doctor to see if i should go to. once i was admitted the nurses were wonderful!! they ask me questions to get to know me and as the days went by, they greeted me with respect, dignity and compassion!!! i want to change my insurance!!!! before i was discharge social worker came in and told me they would schedule my follow up w a pcp. once i got home we found out the insurance didn't pay for a med nor the machine i needed. kaiser's case manager sent some company to bring me a machine and they made sure i had medications. again, i am not even a part of their insurance family. they treated me like family!!! it was amazing and i'm grateful  it was very clean too!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: kaiser is by far the worst hospital ever. they are under staffed and are always booked. the people working there are brain dead.  everything takes forever. they need to get there act together and hire more people. i wouldn't recommend kaiser to anyone.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: if you care about yourself or if you have loved ones- avoid this hospital and probably other kaisers, since they hire shady people as such! nurses and staff steal from patients that cannot help themselves or maybe if they can, they will do it when you're not around. had a dear friend of mine pass away here and they stole some of his stuff meanwhile he was dying of cancer, one personal item was a bose bluetooth. they would also leave him soiled in his diaper and was still not changed by the time i would arrive. very poor work ethic! once you see what is the norm of what they hire- you'll see what i'm talking about! again- if you care about yourself or others- you're better off in another hospital where they may be more selective of the individuals they hire.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: had to go in for the flu and received absolutely the best care imaginable. dr. overman, her nurse helen, and everyone made sure they checked everything, were so kind and considerate.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: i am waiting for open enrollment to go ppo.. urgent care is a 3 hour wait to see the doctor for 5-7 minutes for them to only tell you what you are feeling.  they have a serious issue in giving you time off work.. i went to the disability office in the basement to pick up my fmla paper after receiving a phone call to pick it up...i arrived and the room was packed with people sitting down filling out paperwork.. i was the only person in line waiting... a lady finished her paperwork and was the only person and stood up... the black man behind the counter said next, i walked up because i was next but he told me to wait because the lady had a clipboard  and was already here.. i said but i was in line when she was sitting down completing her paperwork and i'm here to only pick up my documents.. he refused and took the lady.. inconsiderate and very unprofessional.  he took her paperwork and went to make copies. couldn't believe it. can't wait until april 2020
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: i had my knee replacement surgery performed here. i have to say, my experience here was exceptional. the entire staff was so caring and attentive. thank you for making a pretty rough procedure as positive of a experience as it could be made.

my husband recently had spine surgery here and i have to say i was above and beyond impressed. 

-very clean waiting room with good coffee and granola bars. private rooms when your doctor comes out with surgery results. 

-amazing cafeteria. the food was delicious. i couldn't believe a hospital actually has good food. i ate there 3 times in 24 hours. my husband loved everything they fed
him. 

-nicest nurses ever. my husband's nurse julie was so sweet, accommodating, informative, and took great care of my hubby. she was awesome. 

-spacious, clean rooms with updated fixtures and very nice tiled bathrooms and direct tv with all the channels. i was so impressed. 

overall a really great experience and i am so glad he had his surgery here. we left very happy and he felt very taken care of the entire time. i wish they delivered babies here/did c-sections because i would love to have my
next baby here lol!

recently had knee replacement surgery. the staff is great! very friendly and helpful. nurses were great, especially lindsay. they answered all my questions and seemed to really care about how i was doing. this is a small hospital so the nursing staff isnt overloaded with patients. great hospital and if given the choice i will always choose to go there for future needs.
dr. sore was great!  all the people there were nice and attentive.  highly recommend if you need emergency care, like i did.  dr. sore was funny and has a great bedside manner.

the doctors are good ,the 2 stars are for the chemo side. the nuses screw around visiting in morning so the ppl who have 815 appointments dont get hooked up to chemo until 930 ish when he had 815 apt. i timed a nurse. 1 person b4 my dad, 35 mins because she talked for 25 mins about her life story as my dad sat and waited. long day for sick ppl 5 hours chemo take 6.5 because of the chatty nurses. it's not a party. come on!!

went in to the back and spine department for back pain. the dr. and radiologist i saw were nice; the dr. told me to go to physical therapy and come back in a few weeks. however, i'm giving two stars because to see the doctor for maybe 10 minutes regarding an issue that has drastically altered my quality of life for the past two months, i was charged $130 just to see the doctor and an additional $160 to get an x-ray. now i'm afraid to go back for fear i'll be charged an additional $300 even though i probably need further imaging. if the services were more pay transparent and the hospital had a better layout, i would give them more stars.

i visited st elizabeth medical center from out of town for 3 days to help my nephew through open heart surgery. the procedure went well, but i was very surprised by the state of the facilities compared to our hospitals in milwaukee. the "campus" is a nightmare, extremely hard to navigate, with no maps or user friendly signage. on a few occasions there was no one  at the "welcome" desk, and i had to pick up a phone to get help. not helpful! it was extremely confusing to get around, up and down elevators, down many halls, up and down stairs, outside to get into another building, etc. to make matters even more confusing, the elevators up/down buttons were all different. it doesn't sound like much, but when you are lost, emotional, and frustrated, and you get to the next elevator and have to think through the up down buttons it gets  pretty annoying!! the bathrooms next to the icu waiting room were dirty with no toilet paper or paper toweling on and off for most of the three days i was there. there was no kleenex in the icu waiting room, nor were there cups for the coffee station which was also very poorly maintained-unkempt with amenities absent. the parking garage elevators were filthy with fingerprints everywhere as well as garbage on the floor. the parking garage elevator was very dangerous with the doors closing so quickly there was not time to get two people through without the doors closing on the second person, and not automatically opening up again. i would hate to have seen if a child got caught! we had to pay for parking, which surprised me especially when that also was a nightmare. not only was the inside ticket payment booth broken the whole time i was there, but the outside payment booth worked inconsistently and there was never an attendant present to help. at one point i had to leave my car to look for someone to get the ticket machine to work when the car ahead of me was stuck behind the gate with cars backing up behind me!  i never appreciated our hospitals in milwaukee as much as when i left boston. we also have hospitals with large campus', but somehow they have managed to make them welcoming, staffed, and user friendly.

thank you dr. chandra for saving my husband life . i appreciate you took the time after being off for duty and coming here in an emergency and performed a big surgery for him, and  thank you all your team and all the icu department for being there in this hard situation 
thank you so much!!!

as a recent patient for 22 days in the bone marrow transplant unit, i experienced superb care across all job functions from evs to the three mds who oversaw my care. the food and food service were top-notch, too. thank you, scripps green!

dr. takata was negligent, and caused my daughter to have an abscess, because he didn't take the time to properly clean her abdominal cavity after a pelvic surgery. she could have died because of his negligence. he is also arrogant and rude, and not a nice person. avoid him.

my husband has had a knee replacement and a hip replacement here and i can say this is a very good hospital and staff! i have been in two other health systems' hospitals, and the new sharp is it's best competition. medical center also, very good care. support for patient and their caregiver

incredible staff. so nice and caring, yet professional and efficient at the same time. clean and safe environment with great guest amenities for my waiting family. administration and guest relations laid everythingout for us,  and even offers my 5 year old a coloring book. the nursing staff was delightful from start to finish. great experience during a stressful time.

after years of my doctors requesting that i give the medtronics spinal stimulator trial a go, i finally decide to do it and get everything approved only to find out that this "hospital" refuses to work with my current doctor because they aren't getting paid what they think they should be.  

now, because this "hospital" won't work with this doctor and allow him to do surgeries in their facility, there are now literally hundreds (sadly yes, the doctor's scheduling person is loosing his mind over this) of people waiting on trials and implants that will continue to wait until their approvals expire or the patients expire.  it's sad to see that profits are more important than patients at this "hospital".  i have never seen a "hospital" turn away patients because their surgeon isn't giving them a kick-back.

i had a great first impression, maybe because my mom joined. however, 5 years later i need to update this review. it's impossible to get an appointment. i will take you months and when you finally get there, you wait forever! then when you are finally seen, it's a nurse practitioner or a medschool student.  where are the actual doctors!? i've never been able to actually sit down and discuss my injury with an orthopedic surgeon! that is insane especially considering my traumatic injuries where years ago. everytime you go to the va, you have to take labs, which results in more waiting. the labs area is creepy too. oh and while you do more waiting, you will be asked for money. alot! panhandling is a huge problem at this va and i've had to grab a security guard more than once because i didn't  feel safe at this va

my advice, take a vacation day to do this.  you will be there for hours. 

the one star is for complementary valet parking for veterans. this valet crew has always been nice and address me by mam; which is well mannered. however, after i asked for my parking validation and i was told that i couldn't have it, that it was only validated for vets. i am a young looking female vet and have  been out for a few years. news flash, educate your staff that the female is the future veteran... like are you for real!!! we are here now and we demand quality care. its was extremely embarrassing when your staff demanded prof of my veteran status. come on be better! 

i will be writing our state senator next. trust & believe

this hospital is downright dangerous.

communication within this hospital to patients and between staff is a huge area of opportunity. i had a surgery on an infection on my hand. upon releasing me from the hospital i was told someone would contact me. many days later, when no one contacted me, i called the clinic and explained my story to maybe 2 dozen people, and that i have a large open wound with not enough supplies to continue dressing the wound. they told me to just see my primary care doctor in a few weeks. as it turns out, after dozens of phone calls and flagging down the borrowed surgeon from northwestern medical center for an improvised appointment, i was told that i had mrsa a contagious and dangerous infection. the hospital had no plans of telling me about this dangerous infection. the surgeon was appalled that no one followed up with me and that they would not schedule an appointment for me for weeks citing that the "clinic was closed" for nearly a half a month. veterans, unfortunately, must be very careful with their life/health at the jesse brown va medical center.

my grandmother was admitted to oakbend's jackson street campus, 3rd floor ace unit. she has been there for five days and i can't emphasize enough how caring and compassionate the nurses, physical therapists and doctors have been to me and my family. thank you, thank you, thank you for all you do and continue to do for so many!

review:
exceeded expectations!  first visit here. came about 630 am, for urgent care. i have been so impressed with the doctor and all the nursing staff- so compassionate, knowledgeable, and accommodating to my every question and need. and this dr is i think the best i've ever had. (dr shah).
i "took a chance", trying somewhere new- and i'm so glad i did! i hope others will too!

"warning" this hospital is the absolute worst. may have been good at one time, but not anymore. not sure if all they could get was the worst of the worst doctors and er staff. they will do nothing for you. not a heart monitor or oxygen meter. then they will have you sign a patient denied treatment form before they will release you. most likely to save there butts from a lawsuit. and then be prepared for a er level 2 charge. i'm taking thousands, even with insurance. ( please don't bother apologizing for the unprofessional  behavior of your staff. we have already discussed this matter several times in detail, over the phone and in writing. i'm sorry if you feel all your patients are liars. you absolutely have no care what (customers) have to say). note to any potential patients. please search for care at a non hca hospital, southside and vcu is not a hca hospital.

over thanksgiving, i was experiencing a migraine so severe i ended up at the er. i have ankylosing spondylitis which causes major flare ups around my major joints and back. sadly to say, this migraine was a result of my disease. morphine wasnt touching it. i was in such excruciating pain in my head, opening my eyes and light would cause it to go worse and me to throw up. the staff at erh was so kind, professional,  courteous to my disease and very thorough. they were doing everything possible to get me to feeling better.  i ended up staying thru thursday,  friday and mostly saturday. i just wanted to say thank you for the support and care i received from these wonderful people. iy seems all we here about any more is the negative experiences. i wanted to give a positive one.

i was on vacation and my son was having issues that we thought might be diabetes.  i went to urgent care and asked for a urine test to make sure he did not have diabetes.  the urgent care is linked to the hospital.  it was going to cost me $150.  he said we needed to go to the hospital.  we went to the hospital and i stated what we needed.  waited three hours took test everything was fine.  they said they wanted me to see a doctor.  we waited another hour in the room i talked to my son's doctor in california while waiting and he said he is fine.  left because no one would see us.  get a bill for $700 from the hospital and $512 from the doctor.  we never even saw a doctor.  $1200 bill for a five minute test.

this hospital is the worst i've come across. they have no regard for their patients or their families who are clearly having a hard enough time with someone in the hospital. they are rude, the staff does not all follow the same protocol. they dehumanize patients, making them feel trapped and like a bother. as i am sitting in the waiting room writing this, i am not being allowed back, aside from what the nurse specifically told me when i left. i wish i could give zero stars.

is it sad that i have a preferred er? well, piedmont is it. i, unfortunately, have had to go to the er a number of times (for myself and friends) over the last few years. piedmont was recommended to me and it is in network for my insurance. i find that it isn't as crazy as some of the other ers. you get into triage quickly. the time getting back to a room isn't too bad either. time to actually seeing the doctor when you are back in the room has varied. staff has mostly been quite good. one complaint- perhaps have some places to lay for folks that have medical issues with sitting or standing for long periods of time. it is indeed an er and people are going to have all kinds of issues.

terrible hospital to investigate their dangerous breast surgeons who disfigured patient.  wrote to dr. cohen, the executive of the piedmont hospital and he referred the case to dr. robert miller.  dr. miller ignored the seriousness of the injury to the cancer patient and sexual attempt by one of their breast surgeons.
there is no safe-guard of patients in this hospital.
surgeons who have been involved in this case are: dr. william a. barber and dr. john symbas.
stay away!

this review is for my dad's cardiologist, hemal parekh. she has fixed my dad's complex heart issues with care and compassion. my dad was very scared going through a necessary procedure. 

her team sat with my dad for 30 mins and explained that he needed it. the nurse was so compassionate and went ahead with the procedure that improved my dad's condition tremendously.

she has followed my dad's case very closely and even follows up on weekends when necessary.

once again i thank hemal parekh and her team for fixing my dad's heart issues.

i wish i could give 0 but here is my 1. 

so many i'll mannered and rude comments coming from the staff. upon checking in i was told that my son's sickness was just the "common cold and that parents are just bribing in these kids for the same thing" well what you know my son has an on going fever and double ear infection. so please leave your wayward comments for someone else, especially if you know we are first time parents. 

thank you for not helping out the stressed out parents who have to care for their sick child. maybe find a different profession that doesn't require human interaction or your wack a** opinions.

since this seems like a common occurrence through all kaisers, might as well reevaluate your team infrastructure and employees with proper training.

review:
the only reason this medical center has any stars is because we are forced to give at least one when reviewing. please consider this a negative star rating. 

where to start????  

i live in oakland. i know what you're thinking?  why go all the way to kaiser santa clara?  trust me, this was not by choice. after having my appointment scheduled in san francisco (my oakland kaiser is not equipped for this procedure) i was later informed that the scheduling department made an error, in order to be seen in sf i would need a referral, and that i was really scheduled  to be in santa clara by 8am. if you know, you know... traffic! 

a little about the procedure. a capsule endoscopy. not sure how many are familiar with what these require so let me give you a little background.  basically i'm swallowing a camera so they can look at my small intestines. in order for this to be successfully done i would need 1 gallon of the ever delicious gavolite (lemon windex. flavored poop juice that literally makes you pee out of your ass for hours to the point your shit is clear).  

now to the next debacle, the pharmacy (different kaiser location) received a  notification that my doctor had ordered my poo juice, shortly after i received a notification staying that it was ready for pickup. i arrive to the pharmacy, wait 30 minutes in line in a cesspool of germs to be told that it was not ready and the ready for pick up notification was sent in error. after one hour of being subjected to a number of nasties, poo juice was finally in hand. 

so let's fast forward to yesterday. i am not allowed to eat at all!  i am a big guy, eating is the most important part of my life, forgive me i have yet to eat and i am quite hangry. recap of monday, no food, drinking the delish poo juice every 15 minutes (did i mention i had to set an alarm for 2 am and start my second round this morning), and lack of sleep, by 5am i ready to hit the road, jk, i have to poop. 

anyways, get on the road around 6 from oakland and finally make it santa clara. check in at 8 as instructed. what would you know, the computer system is down. we are in the fucking heart of silicon valley and you make billions of  dollars with on-site it, what do you mean your computers went down?  they take me back, my blood pressure  is looking "awesome", computers are still down, but they tell me i will be out the door by 9:20. all i can say is, lol. 

at 9:20, nothing has happened, shocker. here's the real kicker, santa clara being the only facility that's can  handle this procedure forgot to charge the fucking battery!  are you serious??  why wasn't it on the charger, i bet your phone is charged?  get this, they have 2 batteries, one is broken, the other dead!  i mean, i really have no words. 

then they told me i could wait a few more hours so the battery can charge. i have a few issues with this: 1. took off work. 2.  fiancé took off work. 3. most important, i'm fucking starving. 4. i would have to come back again tomorrow?!?!? 

obviously i didn't have the procedure and i'm gonna go stuff my fat face while i file a grievance with member services. i'm sure that will go smoothly.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center

review:
*kaiser permanente santa clara clinic* 
i've been to the evening clinic thrice so far when skyport, where i usually go for routine health care & generally like, didn't have any appointments. each time, i've been disappointed with the quality of doctors at the clinic. granted it is just 3 different doctors so there may be some sampling bias. but i will promptly update this review if i ever visit this location again (& i hope i don't have to).

*kaiser permanente santa clara emergency room*
skyport doesn't have an er so my nearest er is also santa clara. this week when i needed to, i was hoping that their er would be different - at least as good if not better than any regular er (eg. kp oakland) - from its evening clinic. after all, they're two different buildings, adjacent but on the same campus. but i was just so disappointed. at the er, it was an experience, just as bad if not worse than some civil hospitals. first, we couldn't find parking & there was no one available at the valet. it took us 10 min to find parking, but far away. registration took us another 25 min. i was in pain but there was also another patient behind me on a wheelchair who appeared either passed-out or in deep-pain so had just put her head down & was being assisted by another kaiser helper waiting their turn. long lines & only two nurses to register & only 1 nurse to take the vitals, who was also a part-time helper if a patient needs wheelchair assistance, after. it appeared that they had no sense of urgency or emergency, sometimes even chit-chatting & laughing amongst themselves while we were still waiting in the line, in pain. in fact, most of the er medical staff including the doctors & the nurses seemed fairly junior & disorganized too. as you'll read further, all of them (from the nurses that registered to the doctors & nurses who diagnosed/treated me) were asking me the same questions all over again, yet re-typing my responses into their computer, not realizing i was in pain & frustrated, repeating the same responses. for example: 
-what brings you in today?
-when did you start feeling this way?
-on a scale of 1-10, how would you rate your pain?
-have you seen a doctor for this & when?
-is this your first time at the er for this issue?
-have you had any medication recently?
-other personal questions, already on my chart
after the registration, i was sent to the waiting room & after another 30 min, into the screening room - the first point of medical triage. in the screening room, the nurse first asked me the same bunch of questions that i had already answered during registration. she hadn't read my chart nor my earlier responses to these questions. then after about 5-10 min a doctor came by & asked most of the same questions, again, without having read my chart, but a few new too, related to my pain:
-do you have any sensitivity to light?
-do you have stiffness in your neck?
-have you been already tested for this infection? (no. but as you will read below this somehow got interpreted to yes!)
he then told me that some other doctors would examine me further and i was sent to a patient room at the back of the er. after waiting for 10-15 min another nurse came in & asked me the exact same questions all over again. the room was very cold, so i asked her for a warm blanket which she quickly got for me. 
then after about 5 min, a doctor came to see me. she asked me most of the same questions again & ordered bloodwork, saline water, & other pain medicines through an ivr. finally reading into my notes, she thought that i was already tested for this infection earlier. (remember my answer above was no.) i said no again, and she said she'd order it - she didn't. the nurse inserted an iv needle to draw out blood & then administer saline water & pain medication. but while inserting the iv needle she wasn't gentle -showed her inexperience. she inserted the needle so hard that a lot of blood spilled over the sheet & the floor below -by the way, not the cleanest i've seen in an er. instead of apologizing, she asked me:
-have you had any alcohol or use blood thinner? (no.)
she just smiled & told me that i have a lot of blood that just oozed out so quickly (ok! what!?)
i was administered the saline water & some pain medicines. after 30-min, another doctor came in. he also assumed my infection test was done but i said no yet again but he said that it didn't matter anymore!  he suggested some otc medicines, assured me that i should feel better soon & left. after about an hour i started feeling better due to the pain medicines but during that time a lot of people were walking & talking pretty loudly outside. i overheard an entire conversation of a random nurse who's soon moving in with her boyfriend (good luck, but this is an er!). then my nurse came back with my discharge papers, went over them, wished me well, & then i gladly left. at least no longer in pain. at least i'm not mad at yelp for not letting me leave them 0 stars & they get 1.

she was extremely rude to us and we also had to constantly ask her for things the patient needed, like status or even socks.
