i was in the 1st floor in the therapy department and  i tell you  i was treated like a queen . all the drs , nurses and therapist were wonderful . they were very helpful, patient and understanding. they helped me understanding and helped me learn how to walk and take care of myself after my back surgery at summerlin .  i wish  i could give them 10 stars

good service in a medical emergency. 

the security was a little lax for my taste, but, the important part is that we received the right help at the right time. the process, despite the panic of an emergency, was well choreographed. that helped me to process and stay calm. 

navigating the parking lot and door was easy too. it helps to have easy in/out when you're the mental fog of uncharted waters.

i was in there in er recently for 9 hours. i needed emergency surgery and went through every test you can imagine. however, the hospital staff and surgeon were top notch and attended to me properly. they made me feel comfortable and confident that i was in good hands. even though i was there most of the day, i never felt the need to call out for assistance as they checked in on my regularly. once the surgeon perform the needed surgery on me right there in er, i was thoroughly checked on all vitals and released within 90 minutes of the procedure completion. while i hate hospitals and have only had 5 prior experiences with ers, this was the best possible treatment i've had and i feel it was due to the quality of the hospital staff.

will start this off and say the surgeon and medical staff were awesome. 
with that said, we showed up for a scheduled surgery and was told we were not on the schedule. even though we did the phone check in the night before. so we wait in the lobby for 30+ minutes until someone get's their act together and they finally allow us to go up (now over 30 minutes late for surgery check in) oh but wait, not until they wanted a credit card payment for 10x the known and pre-authorized deductible. so, basically hostages at this point. we paid the 10x deductible (over $3000). now that it's been a month later they are nowhere to be found to issue a refund. call every day and sit on hold for 30 minutes, only to be dumped into a voicemail box that they do not return calls from. (we have left numerous messages in the past 25 days and have had zero return calls). finally today we were able to get a hold of someone with no resolution to our grossly huge over payment. horrible experience based on the billing issues alone.

had visit this hospital before for care for my husband back in 2018, it was excellent customer service from everyone at the hospital. i had a leg pain so bad that i wasn't able too move my leg at all or walk for the same reason. the ambulance took me too the emergency room, ended up in the waiting are for hours before they called me up ? doctor and assist came out writing what ever he said, he didn't check my leg he just order some xrays not and mri too see any damage inside my leg and knee !! this was since 13 of this month waited more hours for a ct , not an mri again !! finally he came out again an immobilized my leg, gave me crouches and pain pills ? he gave an order for a orthopedic specialist, since then i made my own appointment with dr fouse at desert orthopedic center , were they gave me an appointment immediately i was seen on the 18th of this month , specialist also mentioned that the brace was the worst thing for my leg situation. he also checked my leg moved it around, looked at the notes asked me questions to determined my injury. he order an mri immediately which i have an appointment today at 5pm this should been done since the 13th when i went to the emergency room at the desert springs hospital !!! i don't think i will be visiting this hospital for any other emergency for me or my family this service is very questionable now !! bad service is bad service like this one !!

my mom from out of state ended up here for a cardiac emergency through the emergency room. i was told this hospital was not good, but i must say the care she has received has been amazing. every employee has been so helpful, loving and caring. the dr's and specialists have had a great bedside manor. if i have any complaint it would that she was in the er for two days before an actual room became available. the hospital was packed so there is only so much they could do. otherwise it has been a great experience for a very difficult time.
if you can stay away from this place..they messed with my blood pressure with my sugar they wouldn't give me my medication i had to end up leaving ama

all 4 stars for peter and the rest  of the physical therapy staff my dad went in because of a broken head the surgery went well he is recovering fine only reason why its not a 5 star is because there was no communication on getting the medicine that he was on  and needed. but the  physical therapy team was outstanding

i came in with a kling on size ball on my forehead and a busted shoulder and they gave me no medication. i'm sorry but that's crap. take some tylenol is what they told me. i was mortified. the people were nice but the dr who made the decision to not medicate me is rubbish. don't go here unless you're missing a leg. then maybe they will medicate you. i'm in so much pain and they didn't care fory pain.
desert springs hospital has good people working there, god-bless them. after three days of good care after my surgery i am now home and doing great.

had my mom transferred from another facility to desert springs acute rehab. very kind, caring staff that stays on top of the care delivered to the patients. my mom was able to be discharged  home after a week as physical therapy and occupational therapy is taken very seriously. patient safety is also taken seriously. i was able to go home and sleep knowing that my mom was in very good, caring and capable hands. rooms are private, clean and well appointed. great work at this place

was admitted through the emergency room.    all staff very caring cheerful and made a nervous patient relaxed.   a  few tests and a good diagosis.    everyone on staff treated me with respect and caring.    the hospital was clean and comfortable.   although spending a night on an er bed i could have done without.    hospital was full and i was awaiting a room   when i got to my room,  it was very comfortable and i forgot about the er stretcher/bed.   i was on a limited diet but what food i could have was very good, arrived hot and tasty    they have an interesting food service they call it room service and for me it worked well.    on my discharge day,  the room service person called me to remind me that i hadn't ordered lunch   just another nice touch

i took my daughter to anna jacques er three weeks ago for a finger injury. i paid my 100 dollar co pay and this week received a 250 dollar bill from the attending doctor, who we never saw. this is the second time this has occurred  here and i am told the doctor does not work for the hospital and that he gets paid to review the case. it is very upsetting that patients are not told that the doctor bills separately and patients will end up owing much more that their co pay. this has never happened at beverly hospital. anna jacques touts itself as a community hospital but seems to forget the common courtesy of laying out their billing practices.  i was truly disgusted when i received the second bill and will never again bring anyone to anna jacques.

if i could make 2 separate reviews i would. 5stars for the pediatric icu and 0 stars for the emergency room. 

on feb 8 i took my four month old son to the er for difficultly breathing. he was having noticeable chest retractions, nostril flaring, a nasty cough, and was super lethargic. after getting checked in and into a room, he was hooked to the spo2 monitor and we waited to be seen. during the first 2 hours his o2 levels were steadily dropping, from mid to lower 90s. the nurses hardly came to check on us, and i finally asked when they put them on oxygen and she responded with "like lower 90s usually" as he's sitting at 91- we still had to ask for oxygen for him after she stated that. once the rsv test came back positive, they tried discharging us with instructions to "come back if he gets worse". i refused papers because of his chest retractions and strained breathing and the fact that he was never even physically observed. the male pa came back and looked him over and said "well i can call peds" what! how is that not standard practice for a four month old baby with breathing problems!? it took another hour to get any word on what was going on with peds, and finally the nurse came back and asked if the pa had been in to talk to us, which he hadn't, and told us we were getting admitted. within 10 minutes of our admission to peds, my sons o2 dropped to the lower 70s and he was blue. the respiratory therapist and about 4 nurses had to stabilize him before transferring him to the picu. he stayed on high flow oxygen with deep suctions to clear the rubber cement glue consistency mucus from his lungs for a week. once we were upstairs our experience was fantastic, the head doctor is amazing and informative and everyone is gentle and caring and i had confidence in the care he received. i'm extremely disappointed in the er though. for a trauma center, you'd think the protocol for an infant with breathing difficulties during rsv season would include calling pediatrics immediately upon arrival. i'm not sure what would have happened to my boy if i accepted the discharge- he may not be here today.

in response to "web c." the "business owner" who responds to bad reviews on yelp and google, i will instead stick to warning people about the awful and unprofessional nurses at this hospital instead, as i cannot imagine the rest of your staff being any better. thank you.

this being my first visit to an er anywhere, ever, i have to say i was underwhelmed.  my husband fell and hit his head. the trauma doctors did an immediate work up and then stuck him in "obs".  like another review mentioned, the nurses station looks like a panel of blank faced dolts.  our nurse wasn't particularly helpful, her tone was condescending and when i kept asking questions and didn't understand, she said "i told you what we know" and i told her i did not appreciate her condescending tone....she gave me the hand, turned around and marched away from me!  at this point i was aghast, told the other nurse that the other was a rude bitch and needs to remember she is taking of us, and needs to get an attitude adjustment we waited over 4 hours to see a doctor to tell us the results of the ct scan and i still haven't seen a doctor or know really what's going on.  so after another nurse explained as much as she could, miraculously a doctor arrived and explained everything to us.  no one told us that my husband had actually been "admitted for obs" , no one changed his soiled sheet even though i specifically asked three times, and it wasn't until 430am i was told i could go home, that he needed to stay for a few more hours for "obs".   no one told the doctors i was even there! at noon the following day we were sent home with  little information- at least in layman's terms. no care instructions. only to take tylenol.   i am online now researching a competent hospital. never going there again.

times are tough!  the er cannot afford kleenex in the rooms, a rolling table to assist nurses with all the medical items they need to do their work on you and no pillows at all.  looking for new medical providers this year

i'm literally sitting in the ed and having a panic attack because of the breathing treatment i was given....hr spiked up to almost 140 and all of the nurses and doctors are sitting!!!! i pressed the call button 3 times only to be told that i need to calm down. no, i don't especially when i've been coughing up blood. as a patient this is never how i should be treated! i am also a healthcare professional and would never treat my patients this way! i pray that o never need to step foot into this hospital ever again. instead of remodeling they should consider tearing it down or maybe simply firing the entire ed staff since retraining clearly never happens.

i underwent a pre-scheduled cervical spine surgery at gw by way of a neurosurgeon.  the pre-surgical and post-surgical treatment at gw were fantastic.  the doctors and nurses were attentive and detail-oriented.  the head nurse in charge ensured everyone did their jobs.  five stars if you require surgery or longer-term hospitalization at gw.  

now i turn to the emergency room (er) of gw university hospital.  in contrast, the er receives one star.  it was horrible.  avoid the gw er if at all possible.  the nurse assigned to me had a bad attitude.  i was experiencing severe cervical spine pain.  i asked for an injection.  the nurse claimed she had injected me with morphine, but i felt nothing.  then she disappeared for 2 to 3 hours.  no pain relief was provided.  it was chaos.  when i was discharged, there were patients waiting for a room.  they were laid out on gurneys.  peeing in their pants.  yet there were over 12 nurses joking around on their computers in the triage center of the er.  these nurses were ignoring the patients.  no one appeared to be in charge.  poorly run er.  avoid it.
i have been at the er now for almost nine hours. nine hours!  i have a terrible flu. average wait time is not an hour. and i'm still not treated.

i went there tonight because i hit my head on double pane glass wall when i fell and they didn't even see me...precedent was me was given to a woman with a broken hand; i was horrified, horrible hospital they don't know what the hell they're doing there!!!!.  

the hospital is dirty and run down and has derelicts at night, it's not a safe place to be, nor do they have good and timely care.

go to sibley hospital
excellent, expedited treatment. discharge 90 minutes later. thank you, gw hospital - er staff for taking good care of me.

don't come here to the er if you can help it. the place is under construction and it takes hours to be seen. it's full of people who come in for colds so no one takes you seriously. you can hear the nurses telling each other how dangerous and incompetently run the hospital is. to make it worse i got home and realized they had given me 2 other peoples' signed discharge papers, which i'm pretty sure is a hippa violation.

took my daughter into the er as she was having a severe allergic reaction. they rushed her through the doors and immediately started working on her.   totally pleased with the attention they gave her during this medical emergency.

this poor review is against ssm and not the people working at the hospital.  
after getting a massive bill for a er visit i have been making payments on my own $200+ a month.
today i got a call from ssm that they were going to send my account to collections if i did not make payment arrangments.  
ssm are a bunch of money grubbing suits... go anywhere else!!!!
fac_name: SSM Health St Joseph Hospital - Lake Saint Louis

review: at this time, emergency has been 10 hours and doctor spent less than 5 minutes.   still waiting for a room.  no help with bathroom.
fac_name: SSM Health St Joseph Hospital - Lake Saint Louis

review: do not come to this hospital if you can get anywhere else. you will wait forever & the people up front are extremely rude. i get this feeling they look down on certain patients and it's very annoying . and the treatment isn't much better . after waiting 2+ hours to even be seen you're usually thrown in a hall or even if in a room it takes another few hours to get anything done and another few hours for results . trust me if you can get to milton hospital it's way more worth it.

day surgery is a nightmare if your time is scheduled in the middle of the day. staffing is short and scheduled times are just a suggestion. plan on waiting and running late. oh, your blood pressure will be up due to the added anxiety. 

robin in surgical reception needs sensitivity training. i arrived to pick up my husband after a day procedure and was told by his doctor when i should arrive back to the hospital. i did as he said and i walked up to the desk when i arrived back. she was talking to another woman and abruptly stopped, looked at me, and asked "do you need something?" i explained what i stated above and she told me to take a seat and she would be with me in a minute. five minutes later she came over to me and said she is not supposed to call back and he just got out of surgery. not true! i volunteered to show her my phone with the time the doctor called me. she told me it would be about a half hour longer, which is now close to 2 hours for recovery before i could see him. the reception desk is less than welcoming in fact i received a chilly reaction given what we were going through that day.

if i were able to give no stars that would be more accurate!! i was in the er in april of 2019 and received probably the worst care i've ever had to encounter in my almost 25 years of being chronically ill. i called the very next day to submit a formal complaint which was just handled by even nastier people and swept under the rug. billing has been an absolute nightmare. claiming i owe a certain amount after both my insurances and myself has contacted them several times saying this is not true. ssh apparently only goes by the first page of an eob. i've never had any of these issues with any other ma hospital. if you value your life, sanity, and money, you should find a different establishment because between the incompetent er staff and billing department, i'm surprised they haven't faced medical malpractice lawsuits out the ass. i'd rather drive 45 minutes in an emergency to bwh or mgh than the 10 minutes it would take me to get to ssh.
"frances farmer will have her revenge on seattle" nothing more than a snake pit that needs to be shut down and it's workers arrested and jailed.
fac_name: Montgomery County Emergency Service Mental Health

review: army tricare isn't the best insurance out there but when i delivered my baby, the staff were pretty good at what they do! my baby was sunny side up. i was pushing for an hour and a half and they had to call a doctor since my body was weak and baby wasn't budging. major (dr.) tillman gave me the options of forceps and vacuum and he recommended forceps. i went with it. within 4 pushes, my baby was out! and i was expecting a bad marks on my baby's face but it was barely noticeable and went away within hours! after delivery, nurses are in and out to keep me and the baby in check. the next day, the same dr. (tillman) came to check on us again. thank you major for being extra cautious! i heard the worst outcomes from forcep deliveries but you made mine quick and didn't harm my baby!

best hospital in redding. was on a wild goose chase trying to find a lab that would draw my blood for my doctor in oregon. everyone had some sort of reason why they couldn't do it or wouldn't do it. finally came into mercy and everyone was so kind. they bent over backwards to get me into the lab. i was missing some paperwork, but instead of telling me to leave and come back with it, they tracked it down and had it faxed over. everyone was so friendly and the hospital was so clean and set up nicely. definitely coming back for any medical needs.
fac_name: General Surgery - Mercy Medical Center - Redding, CA

review: i had my daughter here horrible experience. woke up to a doctor preying over me . i guess i didnt fit there views of someone who could raise my daughter because baby daddy was not there and my girlfriend was. i'm sure this doctor is a bethel attender and you know they hate gays. got my baby taken and now fighting with the government which are even more corrupted. this place should be shit down.
fac_name: General Surgery - Mercy Medical Center - Redding, CA

review: what bad service and being a retired military man and being treated the way we were treated is not called for.  matter of fact the way everyone has been treated there is uncalled for.  making people wait for over 10 hours one day and we go back the next day and we still wait over 8 hours.  nurse was rude to us when asked how long.  human kindness is false advertisement.  i am totally disappointed in the service and the way patients are treated. build a bigger er or provide better service. we are there for the third time in 4 days. still lousy service.  i have not received a phone call about my complaint i made on friday night early saturday morning.
fac_name: General Surgery - Mercy Medical Center - Redding, CA

review: communication between nurse to nurse, physician to physician, and staff to family members is terrible and irresponsible. my father was under care here and inappropriately discharged to home which was not a safe place for him due to multiple medical issues and safety concerns (high fall risk and dementia). we spoke with multiple staff members and were never told the full extent of his injuries until after he was already discharged (neck fracture and swallow difficulties requiring a special thick liquid diet). he was discharged suddenly and late friday night which left little to no options to pick up his required medications (antibiotics included). they made no efforts to assist in this matter. my father is a military veteran and medicare eligible yet no plans were made to set him up with the resources available to him to help with physical and mental recovery. this is unsafe practice and needs to be fixed immediately. they need to do better.
fac_name: General Surgery - Mercy Medical Center - Redding, CA

review: carrier clinic is not the same since hackensack meridian took over. a family member was there is 2017 and it was a wonderful experience for him. patients could go to the dining room and play cards. go off the unit and explore the beautiful grounds. it felt happy when you went on the unit. he was there again recently and its feels sad and pathetic. patients cannot leave the unit at all.  they eat all meals on the unit. patients pace the hallway all day and it feels like an insane asylum. everything has to be approved, even a weighted blanket. thank god my son connected with a wonderful nurse.he was moved to a different unit and his room four times because he couldn't sleep with all the chaos. his experience there was traumatic. people screaming at night saying they want to die or just screaming in general. if my family member needed inpatient mental health help, i don't think i would want to send them to carrier. hackensack meridian needs to reevaluate their methods of treating patients because it could be so good. it was good. now, not so much.

my child was a patient here on the adolescent unit in the middle of october 2019 and i found the staff to be polite and very hellful both in person and ln the phone. they have grewt weekend visiting hours although i thought the 6 day stay for my child was  a little rushed

during our visit to breckenridge we went here at 3am because one of the members of our group suffered from altitude sickness, dehydration, hypokalemia, hypoxia and gastroenteritis. the hospital is located in frisco, just a 15 minute ride away from breckenridge. we were attended to quickly and all of the staff from receptionist, nurse, phlebotomist, radiology tech, respiratory therapist, and er physician dr. adler were professional and caring. we received clear discharge instructions and they also made arrangements for home oxygen that we could use for the week. copies of all the test results were given to us. because of their prompt and expert care we were able to enjoy the rest of our vacation. thank you to everyone in the er- you were all great!

this is my 7th day as a patient here & i am shocked how unclean the sections are. the er where i spent 1 day was fine. but the ncu (a "step down unit") where i spent 6 days because icu was full, was filthy.  not 1 time was the room cleaned, floor washed, dirty tray wiped down. my sheets were changed 1 time.  floor was disgusting. i'm now in another section. my sheets were changed today but have seen no type of cleaning/tray wipe down, remote wiped off. 

i am shocked & stunned how such a lack of cleanliness in this day of infections & germs is allowed. it has followed me as i've progressed through different departments. is no one responsible here?

i am from a medical background.  i fell at home and had a complete break of a bone in my arm, split right into two pieces.  an ambulance took me to bryn mawr hospital er, not my choice based on past bad experience in this er.  the pain was like nothing i'd ever experienced.  i was given a dose of iv pain medication by a compassionate ambulance crew member (narberth ambulance thank you!) they put the arm into some kind of traction in the er and the people in the bryn mawr er were not so compassionate as was the ambulance crew- they did this with no pain medication.  then they started sticking needles right into the place where my bone was split into two.  i'm embarrassed to say that i thought i was going to black out, the pain was so bad. i wished i would black out.  i was asking and asking for pain medication while a doctor or whatever he was was sticking needles into the fracture and manipulating the bones. the lidocaide he kept injecting into my arm wasn't working and was like fire inside the broken bones.   he got all irritated and said "we can't just keep giving you pain medication"  in a really nasty tone.  i couldn't tolerate anymore of the needles and this doctor moving the bones around and so he sent me home and told me to see a surgeon in the morning.  bryn mawr hospital emergency room sent me home with my arm bone in two pieces and no pain medication!  i sat up all night in agony, terrified i was going to have a fat or blood clot go to my brain.   i wasn't able to see the surgeon until about 12 noon the next day, and had to drive myself in that state of agony and shock with no pain medication.  the surgeon was compassionate, like the ambulance crew member and gave me pain medication (thank you rothman orthopedics!)  this was not my first traumatic, horrific experience in bryn mawr hospital er.   would it have killed you to cough up pain medication for a patient whose arm bone is two pieces you cold hearted monster of a doctor or pa or whatever you were!

it's called children's hospital but the thing you need to be worried about is losing your life savings to them.

my son had a 5-minute laser procedure administered by dr. anna bruckner. a no-risk laser treatment. we've had it done for years.

what did they charge for this procedure? well, dr. bruckner charged us $2,688. what?! even better, children's hospital charges us separate from that $1,102.

$3,800 for a 5-minute procedure. the system is broken, and people like dr. bruckner perpetuate this. our insurance company, aetna, saved us about 25% and my total bill is now $1,700.

for a 5-minute procedure.

make sure you get the cost of your procedure in writing before going forward with anybody here. i will never give them my money again.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review:
took my son for a consultation and it was a good experience. the doctor was knowledgeable and very good with my son. he made sure we were comfortable with everything at each step. 

parking is always a bear, but the computerized check-in process they have now is super handy.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review: i have 4 kiddos and all of them have been patients at children's at some point. the staff is attentive and willing to help. i've learned that i need to be super clear about my expectations and my child needs. we have dealt with a lot of medical issues and i feel as though the staff and our family are a team working to get the medical issues resolved. my one criticism is the dental department. i have waited in the waiting room for extensive periods of time and it is always overflowing with people. we scheduled a dental surgery and were given a price for the procedure and then were charged almost triple. that was extremely frustrating. i give the hospital 5 stars and the dental department 2 stars.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review: i brought my elderly grandfather into the emergency room because he was having severe issues breathing. mind you he's had a 5 way bypass and cancer in the previous years, and recently diagnosed with dementia as of 2 years ago. i expressed to the woman at the front that he could barely catch his breath nor even walk in the building due to being out of breath, they didn't seem concerned and told us to wait our turn. ok, totally fine we can wait not a problem in any way. 4 hours later during which my grandfather struggled to breath the entire time to the point where other patients actually expressed their concern for him to the front desk. once again we were wrote off, and i never once complained. we finally were sent back to a freezing cold waiting room where we waited for another 2 hours. at this point my grandfather is impatient and scared due to his dementia. when nurses finally came in they told us we were going to have to go back out to the waiting room where i finally said absolutely not. there's something seriously wrong, she agreed and said they would set up a chest x-ray. long story short he was admitted and his heart was failing! they kept us in the er for the night which was miserable my grandfather is completely restroom incompetent  and i was the one that had to change his diaper and clothes! we finally get a room the next day and majority of nurses yelled at my grandfather and talked so loudly in his face he was terrified. the next night was the worst i had found out the nurses were giving my 81 year old grandfather and entire vile of adavan for no reason except they didn't want to deal with him. i finally asked a nurse why he looked so out of it and she told me they had been giving it to him and it was never once discussed with me. i never left the room after this unless absolutely necessary. fast forward to 10 that evening my grandfather was out of diapers and i needed to grab some out of the car. i requested a nurse to sit with him (mind you he was completely passed out sleeping) i specifically instructed the charge nurse and my nurse to not give him anything at all while i was gone. i timed myself- 11 minutes, when i got back they had dosed him again! i specifically instructed them not too. at that point i was absolutely disgusted and completely upset. your staff needs a significant amount of training when dealing with elderly people, and especially ones suffering from dementia. there was only one nurse who didn't scare my grandfather, and he absolutely loved her. she talked calmly and quietly and he even would joke around with her. i had to ask someone to help me bath him 3 days in which i once again had to do. it was a terrible experience really. i absolutely do not recommend this hospital to anyone suffering from dementia/alzheimer's.

as difficult as it can be to have a loved one need to go to a facility.  reuben was so understanding.  all the while an addict yelled racial slurs at him and spit. others were non stop talking loudly.  one trying to outdo the others bac. the pacers the runners . the withdrawn and the agitated . he was cool as a cucumber.  professional and took all the bs they threw at him. special place in heaven for him. very kind. the world of mental healthcare providers needs more people like him.

it's has been three days now that my mom was taking from summerlin hospital and was brought here. 1st let me start with no one and i mean no one at summerlin hospital told me anything about a patient code. december 5th i had my mom taking to the hospital because i felt she could be a harm to herself, my mother is dealing with schizophrenia, multi personality dis order and since my mom has been here in north las vegas, her health issue have been rapidly worsened. the doctors here has done nothing but given my mom a bunch of pills to take and that's it. she was transferred to this place here and my experience has been even more suspicious of the quality of care here in las vegas nv. so the night my mom was transferred i made no phone calls because it was late and i wanted to allow her to get settled in. i called the next day and the person on the phone said "patients code" i'm like "what's that" . immediately the person on the other ends says if you don't have the case i can not help you. i responded with you absolutely will help me, my mom was transferred there, i don't know anything about a patient code and before i could finish my sentence the lady transferred me to another line. the gentleman that picked up with going into detail was extremely rude, unsympathetic to my issue, had no other alternative and lastly hung up the phone in my face. i then called back to again be faced with unsympatheticness, no other option then this dam code they keep asking for that i repeatedly said, no one gave me a code, and where is my mother? then a angel from having this special voice got in the phone and said "is this shalon" and i just started crying because i could hear the comfort in this woman's voice that she was about to tell me that everything was okay. samone the part time worker in in-take at this hospital save this place from going up there a causing a really ugly ugly seen. all the people before here that i encountered there need to read this hospital statement again and again and again. so i went in for a d&c, which is a fairly standard operation. no matter how i tried, i couldn't get them to put into their medical records that i'm allergic to some antibiotics--one severely. my primary care doctor told them. i believe my ob-gyn's office told them, but friday afternoon before i was to have surgery, they called me on an old phone number i haven't used for fifteen years (somehow, it still put a notice in my email), and when i called back, they had no record of these allergies. 

what they wanted (it was a nurse who didn't seem to care about putting in my drug allergies) was $4,000 upfront, or they wouldn't operate. i needed this operation to rule out cancer, so i argued them down to $1,000 upfront.

the medical information they had on me was 20 years out-of-date, including illnesses i hadn't had since my 20s. i'm almost 50. 

spooked by this horrible record-keeping, i made sure to walk in on the day of my operation with several printed copies of the medicines i was taking and the medicines i was allergic to. i gave these out to several nurses. (it was never clear to me who was a nurse and who was a med-tech. they should introduce themselves better.)

on intake, they mentioned that they gave people lavender essential oils as part of pain relief. i told them not to--that i was allergic. lavender gives me asthma. remember this....

so i gave out my sheet listing my medications and allergies to several people, but when i got into the operating room, one of the last things i remember the surgeon saying was, "so, no allergies?!" i told him then and then--they were already giving me things through my iv, that i had a severe reaction two two common antibiotics (clarithromycin and cirpo) and could not take them.

this was after telling seven people that i had these issues.

so i woke up in recovery, and there was the nurse, trying to give me lavender.

i told her to go away.

i was in pain, but only accepted an extra-strength tylenol because i was afraid that, if i was out-of-it, and they screwed up and tried to give me something that would make me sick, i wouldn't be able to stop them.

i had a forced opportunity to experience reality at bs&w-irving when i took my wife to the er a couple of days before christmas.  i was highly impressed by the care, expertise, teamwork, and professionalism of the entire team including the on-call surgeon ed clifford, md.  when we walked through the halls, staff members made eye contact, smiled, and said "hello."  when we needed to locate the cd with cat scan results we dropped off at the reception desk, the team member in charge of records made an exhaustive effort to locate it in the hospital like it contained precious images of a loved one.  and we were met with smiles from members of my wife's care team when she was cleared for release.  the image i grabbed says it all.

when i asked if they knew cindy schamp everyone gushed with how wonderful she was and the interest she showed in her people.  "we love it here" in the words of a nurse.  they were all impressed by the improvements she made -- from the new facility to the commitment to education.  the list is too long to post here.

maybe it was the christmas spirit.  and i can't promise all patients and visitors will see cindy schamp's vision come to life, but on this visit it did.  if you're curious about that vision, just google "cindy schamp grandma test" for one of her favorite stories on video, then watch a few dozen videos by googling for her name, then video.  learn  more about her winning values even if you're not ceo of a major medical facility.

review:

i will never go to this medical center again.  they show no human concern for their patients. i felt like a cash cow being milked while my wife continues to struggle with severe pain. this should have been a relatively quick imaging procedure, but now we have to have our primary care physician refer us to another facility.

please go elsewhere, your health is too important to waste valuable time and resources here.

review:
(12/28/19; better get my last 2019 reviews done!) 

being from san leandro, my family and i were happy to see this place develop over the years. today, it is an expansive hospital and healthcare facility, complete with all the kaiser fixings of a lab, pharmacy, and specialty physicians for all seasons. 

i have a history with this place. i once enjoyed a fascinating stay at the er for an injury that would make for a good story some other time. suffice it to say, this kaiser permanente has long earned my trust and confidence. 

on this particular morning, all i needed was a little blood work. i requested an elective test, and my doctor in union city obliged by ordering it for me. it required an early hour of arrival, which initially concerned me since a lot of blood work is often scheduled for the mornings (fasting glucoses, hormones, and so forth). however, when i arrived at 8:00 a.m. on this saturday morning, i was pleased to find that i was the only patient there! 

i drew a number, checked in shortly thereafter, and within a minute i was already seated -- a phlebotomist being drawn by another phlebotomist. we had a pleasant chat about venipuncture and how cold the weather was outside, and before i knew it, our work was done! best of all, i got my results that very evening. 

that'll do, kaiser san leandro. it's always a pleasure for me to visit this facility. in the highly unlikely event i were to move back to the bay area, it would be an honor to practice medicine here, or any of the other kaiser offices. nonetheless, being a patient is more than fine by me, and when i'm next in town, i know where to go for my healthcare needs. until then!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Leandro Medical Center

review:
i've come to know the local kaisers very well and the san leandro location is a favorite, especially for the pharmacy.

pharmacy
quicker and friendlier than alameda or oakland! i've been to all three and, on multiple occasions, have had so much difficulty getting medications. the shortest wait i've had for either alameda or oakland has been probably 45 minutes to 1 hour, despite no lines at either place. with san leandro, i was in and out with the same medication in less than 5 minutes.

ultrasounds
the other reason i've been here. this is where i officially found out i was having twins (biggest shock of my life) and the technician was super supportive and sweet. i've also been here for ultrasounds for my kids and the technicians they've had are also really great to work with. my kids have had multiple appointments, the most memorable being when they cried through the appointment and when one baby proceeded to laugh his head off and grab the probe, thinking that it was a toy. during every appointment, the technicians were always very patient, friendly and would talk to and soothe my babies, which was so reassuring to this mama. 

cafeteria
i've swung by the cafeteria for a cup of coffee as well. there's a starbucks at the end of the cafeteria. i usually get my simple go to--small pike's place. and to make myself feel better for the caffeine i'm inhaling, i also grab a cup of their infused water, which is so refreshing and yummy.

review:
i could not be more impressed or pleased with my experience at kaiser san leandro 1 week ago. i was admitted for a full right knee replacement surgery very early in the morning as i was asked to arrive at 6am for 8am surgery time. we had to drive over from marin county and needed to allow for any extra traffic delays. 

from the moment we went in through the emergency doors, there was something making me feel comfortable right away. the parking was so easy compared with the congestion and confusion experienced at the oakland facility where my surgeon is. from the get-go, every staff person we encountered were very helpful and so friendly. 

once we got to the surgery section, it was 100% care for the remainder of my stay that day until being discharged by 4:30 to head home. my surgical prep nurse was elizabeth, and wow, so thorough and a lot of patience with me. i knew i was in the hands of a very kind and well-prepared woman! she put me at ease and made my husband comfortable there too. 
then it was a hoot when i heard the anesthesiologist rolling down the hospital corridor on his stool and making the announcement,  "hi, i'm andy the anesthesiologist, and here to discuss how we will manage your pain" ! he carefully explained my options and cleared away my concerns about choosing a spinal. he took the time to go into my medical chart and clarify where having a spinal would be my best option and work within the parameters of my spinal stenosis issue in the lumbar region. he reviewed an mri from 2015 and said they would know how and where to administer that safely. big relief! great results on that. 

i couldn't have felt more comfortable with the 2 nurses on staff once i returned from surgery! they were ruben and destinie. i kept having difficulty recalling ruben's name but once he said, "like the sandwich, just call me mr. ruben sandwich" that finally sunk in. maybe it was the drugs! they were an awesome team!  they had their goals and kept me on track for an easy discharge. and they had such a terrific demeanor. 

of course, i got a visit from my surgeon, dr. eric eisemon, before we departed.  we first met at his office at kaiser oakland. he made me feel confident from the beginning that i would be in great hands with him doing my surgery and obviously he achieved the results he wanted! its now 1 week out and i am feeling really amazingly well and on my way to healing well! 

before i departed, i had 1 more visit from the anesthesiologist, 
dr. katragadda. he came to inquire whether he could put a catheter into my upper thigh  which would function for the next 4 days to slowly disperse a numbing med and keep me more comfy. he gave me the option and i selected it....so happy i made the decision to do so.  

as for the facility of kaiser san leandro ...i'm giving it *****.
..that's a 5-star rating!!  
1st of all: the parking
according to the 2 family members who needed to park, both said it was "super easy" and close to going into the hospital. the oakland kaiser is more like a zoo....impossible, time-consuming, and paying by the hour can get pricey. my family said it was free with excellent communication helping guide visitors where they needed to be and how to get there.

the hospital was well-laid out and organized. the best part: there was always a staff member to get help on finding where one needed to go.

but for me, i just loved that i was in a "state of the art" hospital. it was modern, so well-equipped. there was a sense of well-being there and a feeling that you were in very capable hands, not just going through the motions, but wanting one to thrive there!  the theme kaiser permanente strives for.  when my pt worker came to my home the next day for our first session, we talked a bit about my incision. i told him it seemed pretty sure that the scar that would remain would be much more minimal than the one in my left leg from the replacement surgery just 7 years ago when they used staples to close up my incision!  that old scar is not attractive at all. and then he told me that other kaiser facility still uses staples to close the wounds after surgery!  wow, san leandro seems light years ahead!!
i could not be more pleased with my decision to have had my surgery at kaiser san leandro!

review:
the two stars is for the ot and rt who are great. besides that, this place is a junk. i would find a better ltac. do not buy into the tour or the fancy way you are spoken to when you visit this place, it is in fact a nightmare.

the frustration begins with the entry process. it takes a long time to check each person in. furthermore, they ensured me to maintain patient privacy/security a password would be used, we were never asked for this password or saw it being enforced.

the doctor's here do not know what they are doing. dr. niaki is a scary one to have taking care of your loved one. he clearly had no idea how to handle a stroke patient and was using some very questionable drug methods. they have 0 interest in getting your loved one back again and more curious to make sure they are alive to be thrown into the next facility.

there are beeping noises from various monitors that are poorly attended to, this will probably drive your loved one and yourself insane. it is incredibly loud and disturbing. 

i would not even send my dog here if i had to. my suggestion is find a better ltac. i was very fortunate to be able to move my father to a nearby ltac with a superior level of care within days of realizing our mistake of chosing kindred.
fac_name: Kindred Hospital San Francisco Bay Area

review:
in just a couple weeks, this "care facility" not only reversed all of the progress my daughter made after 3 major surgeries, they returned her to the real hospital that trusted them in need of an additional, immediate surgery to fix the damage they did.

with the exception of a few nurses, patients are ignored much of the time. even when a family member goes to the nurses' station to ask for help because no one will respond to the multiple beeping call lights. they are ignored.
fac_name: Kindred Hospital San Francisco Bay Area

review:
my friend was in this hospital for weeks. the lady in the front is the most sweetest person, but how can a place neglect someone so badly?! my friend's urine tube got displaced, and despite his mom asking for help, his bedsheets weren't changed for 4 hours! 

what's worse is we let the nurse know that we're concern about him having a viral infection, but nothing was done. instead, a week and a half later, they discharged him to a rehabilitation facility. well guess what; he didn't even stay at that new place longer than a few hours because he had to be moved to an acute hospital. yes, he did have a viral infection, and kindred didn't even do anything to look into it. if only this place took better notice of patient concerns, my friend would be in a better condition than he is now.
fac_name: Kindred Hospital San Francisco Bay Area

review:
staff is good but organization of care is poor
the administration is horrible
our loves on was in a vegetative state and when the woke up which we didn't expect they didn't call us out of town for 3 days to let us know he is awake and cognoscente. we walked ito his room thinking it was his final hours and there he lays fully conscious and commutative.
they were supposed to work on removing him from a respirator slowly and they are barley making progress.no focus on his physical therapy as well
once again the administration is terrible with communication

review:
i went to the emergency at 11:30 am. i was having a hard time breathing 
they tookx-rays  and did a ekg. the er doctor said oh you only have 
a sore throat. he also told me  just spray your throat with chloraseptic and 
use cough drops.  a week later still having the same issue, so i went to a urgent care. the urgent send me to a gastroenterologist and was diagnosed 
with a hiatal hernia and gerd.  
the chloraseptic and cough drops  made my acid reflux worse.
please don't use the er doctors at this hospital.

horrible experience here. the doctors barely speak english. the nurses are rude, condescending, dis-respectable and not responsive when you need help. they tie patients to the beds and force you to be bed-ridden with the beds body-weight alarmed and some patients leave with bed-sores. the food is disgusting and un-healthy consisting of all salty canned foods. the so-called "nutritionist" barely speak english. this place is a dirty low-grade nursing home. i am younger, athletic and was there for a post-op orthopedic recovery. this place is ok if your demented and cannot complain but they will rob you blind. you're better off being homeless in kelly square.

horrible front desk staff (especially dawn!). rude, ignores you, no idea what they are doing, confused about what patients are in vs out. asks you to sign in 3 times because they lost the paperwork. do not pass through messages for the doctor to call you. just deplorable. gossiping together and ignoring the patients. also lost our hipa forms. do not go there!!

horrible unorganized emergency room with a wait time of 10 hours while i had a fever of 102.4. the man who did my blood draw calapsed my vein right in front of me. he left the tourniquet on while pulling the needle out i almost threw up. i'm a phlebotomist and that is the number one thing you don't do to a patient. crazy that they let someone this inexperienced be the person to work on someone who is so sick. never will use anything with wake forest's name on it again.
fac_name: Wake Forest Baptist Health - Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center

review: thought this hospital got better but noooooo. where do you even start, the receptionist was so rude, major attitude, she makes you sign papers and doesnt explain what the hell  you are signing, fortunately i know what those papers where, second we have been here since yesterday 7pm, it is now 5am we where suppose to be discharged an hr ago and we are still here, ohhh by the way they lost the urine sample obtained when we arrived. point of this story dont come to this  hospital, travel a little farther for better care.

this hospital has the worst post-op care of any hospital i have ever been to. i had a two level spinal fusion and i was refused any iv pain medication after my surgery. i laid in the hospital bed for two days crying and writhing in pain and they did nothing to help me. the "nurse" that discharged me slammed my foot on the ground because she was angry with me for asking for medication. i had to walk myself out of the hospital with a walker two days after my spine was realigned with hardware because she was being so rough with me. please be aware of you are having surgery here-you will receive no iv pain medication post surgery no matter your procedure. you will be given shots in your butt for pain control which does nothing! please have your surgery at the lake. there is also no icu or critical care floor if there is a complication. i have made complaints with the nursing board, ohh, and frog to investigate this facility. please do yourself a favor and choose the lake where you can get the medications you need post op. horrible horrible facility. never again will i have anything done there!

there was an er doctor there who chastised my daughter who came in the er with kidney stones. instead of giving her pain medication , he began calling her a brat and told her to apologize to a nurse  who was her "life line". he treated my daughter like garbage. he defensiveness was even 
more bizarre because nothing was a problem except for the fact that they were withholding her pain meds during this. i am going to be requesting the medical records and will make sure he is called out for this. shameful, unprofessional and not his lane.

had a definite, verified, horrible heart attack. was treated like scum and called a "homeboy" (f*ggot to a gay man). 

healthcare is abuse. i left untreated, in medical trouble and in fear.

a very disturbing aspect is isolation with no call light/assist when needed, cell signal, tv, and all other employees completely ignore kindly nurse requests.

if on any of my jobs i ignored a customer, i'd be rightly fired, in healthcare it's encouraged to do to wounded patients.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: so far so good. went to the er during my first trimester. was worried i'd be there all day but considering the severity and treatment i was out in about 3 hours which was far less than i planned. the obgyn department is also very efficient. they always have a full house but tries to honor everyone's time. i've gotten blood work and visited the pharmacy at this location its all been pretty decent. i would say to anyone skeptical abt coming over here 1.) know where you are going as far as the building and floors 2.) try to arrive early to allow for parking and walking 3.) grab a face mask to decrease your anxiety 4.) check in on your kp app and keep a your phone charged in case its a busy day. 5.) always treat ppl on the job with respect. it comes with perks.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
making an appt now typically requires a wait of 35 minute on hold. rep on phone was a jerk with an attitude when i asked him several questions. 
care is substandard with you now seeing pa's and not dr's. went for months and the pa wasn't proactive and my shoulder worsened. she didn't even request an mri after i told her about my preexistíng issues. the dr's are too conservative, unproactive and allow your concerns to linger on. never going back to this outfit next enrollment. my health needs have never been met with this organization. they don't listen to their members and disregard their requests.

review:
it was my first time here at kp south bay! the encounter with so many dr. , nurses, and staff members. dr. zane was my surgeon he very polite, informative on how process was going to take place.  he's chief over the bariatric department. i was able to pick my own surgeon and dr.zane was surgeon. dr. tim was the one who was putting the tube with cameras down my throat.

fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
mom mom had pain on her chest that radiates thru her back and left side, short of breath, the guy took her vitals, my mom went to the little room for ekg and guy inside said wait for 5 mins for the md. til now we're still waiting, it's almost an hour. mom's pain from 5/10 when we got here, now it's 9/10. are they gonna wait til their patient collapse? my mom has afib and hx of heart attack.
if only urgent care is open, atleast there, they attend to her right away because of breathing and circulation issues. this er sucks

review: i dont do reviews normally but holy hell this place is a hot mess. be prepared to wait until you drop. this place is just wowww.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
my dad is a chemo patient and he had fever over 100.6. we went to kaiser harbor city urgent care first couple days ago and the staff are super friendly, the dorctor prescribed antibiotics but unfortunately the fever did not go down after 48 hours. we decided to go to the er this time because it passed the urgent care hours. it turned out a nightmare! the staff from receptionist to er nurses didn't smile at once. the x-ray tech is friendly though. in harbor city urgent care, the receptionist gave us a heads-up the possible wait time. in here, they replied they don't know and kept my dad waiting. my dad expressed several times in the waiting room that he felt chills and fatigue and wanted to go home, all he wanted is something that can reduce his fever and safe to take during chemo. but the doctor kept him waiting and waiting. the blood test was taken and so did flu test. we went in around 1030pm and got out at 5am, almost 7 hours wait and in between the doctor shifted. the first doctor didn't carry over all the notes and my dad had to repeat everything again to the second doctor. the flu test was still not ready by 5am in the morning so we decided to leave. by 6am in the morning, i finally got a phone call from dr. nguien confirmed the flu test came back positive, which i appreciated him calling very much. few hours later, my dad's oncologist doctor called and told me he could not find any doctor notes on the system so we had to repeat everything again...

i am glad this nightmare is finally over. i understand er prioritize the worst case first, which is fine i understand. however, i was just at harbor city urgent care coupledays ago: the pharmacist sincerely apologize for the wait if you've been waiting for more than 30 minutes, but here in the er, instead of explaining, they asked my dad to sign an agreement form before he leaves the hospital without any explanation. really? 

if the staff in harbor city urgent care smiles and gives you heads up, then why can't here?! if the staff went through the same basic training, then a little care to your patient won't hurt. i assume you will not treat your parents like that but why do you think it is ok to treat other people's parents like that? 

we would never come back to this er.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: kaiser emergency department sucks ! worst than the county was here for 5hrs waiting to be called just to be placed in a bed and waited another 1hr for md. the check in desk ppl are no help  either . horrible
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: i have heard about kaiser nightmares as far as wait times. we were visiting relatives during the christmas holidays and my wife was experiencing chest pain and heart palpitations. we waited almost 5 hours in emergency to see a dr. absolute joke to run an emergency room / dept this way. i will never come to this hospital again! i'll make the 2-3hour drive to see a dr and will still come out better time wise.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
i have had several issues here. in 2018, my mom was taken in by ambulance with complications do to hemochromatosis. after three days, they told us she was in organ failure. not their fault and nothing they could have done for her. however, they made us, and her, feel like we were such a massive burden to them. they knew she was dying but still performed an unnecessary surgery, left her intubation tube in for 24 hours without explanation. she had in the previous few days had a procedure requiring an abdominal ultrasound. everyone in that department was wonderful. but following the unnecessary surgery, an intensivist took over and demanded that his ultrasound guy, jared johnson, was the only one who could do the test. she waited for hours for him. when he finally showed up, he looked me in the eyes and said (in front of her!!!) that she "wasn't a priority." 
they let her go from the time she was admitted until she died five days later without a single bite of food or sip of water. did this ultimately kill her? no. but it made her last few days on this planet absolutely miserable. and a complaint to the patient advocate got a blank stare, an asante shrug, and my assurance that they are the best and i should just be grateful for the opportunity to have my family treated like shit. they are really proud of the national award the get. i don't know who votes, but they are, in my opinion, one of the worst.

my best friend and her family were taken in by ambulance after a car accident just before valentines day 2020. she received 6 stitches to her head. she has 2 broken ribs. her dad has a broken sternum. they cut this 79-year-old man with heart issues lose after a couple of hours with a prescription to go fill on his own. they sent her packing at midnight with no pain meds at all. my daughter picked her up. they were just so darned busy! now my friend has a massive infection in that cut (it was still bleeding when she left) and her father died of his injuries three days later. but they were too busy to take the time to treat him and far too full to admit either of them. 

i don't care if i am bleeding profusely from the head, i will die in a ditch before i am admitted to rrmc.

i hardly give feedback but i must commend this hospital for employing not just intelligent medical doctors but m.d that has good relationship with her patients.  i dont know her name unfortunately but my visit was feb  10th at the dental pediatric emergency. she did an excellent job. she saw my baby had a swollen figure she was concerned as if it was her own child that really touched me. we were not familiar with the hospital as it was our first visit, she took us right to were we are to be registered to see doctor for my baby finger at the emergency. this warm reception made me love jamaica hospital. this doctor deserve an award, she was soo friendly. god bless her soul. please keep employing people like her. i can tell she love her job. the lady at the reception also  did a good job. when i told her my daughter gum bleeds  when she starts crying she ensured we were attended to very quickly. god bless her. i love jamaica hospital.

i want to thank the entire staff of nurses, medical assistants, doctors, security, and lovely volunteers at calvary for their compassionate work and professionalism during the most difficult time, the last days of one's life.

patients are treated with respect, given the utmost in comfort and medical care. family and friends visiting are treated with tender genuine compassion as well.  

the facility is kept clean and well run, tightly organized 24 hours of each day and night.  all questions and needs were addressed immediately and respectfully. 

every staff  member we met the past two weeks, was truly wonderful, thoughtful and sensitive to our needs during the last days of my mother-in-law's life.  her wishes were honored and met with utmost compassion. 

we know of calvary through those we know who have familiarity with the facility as their choice for hospice and palliative care.   we recommend calvary highly.

this message is for frank calamari.  please respond to my review and answer my question listed below: i 

my name is sheila r.  

is your staff now working from 1am to 4:30 am? attending the the patient needs or do they still go to sleep including your supervisors.    

i want my question to be answered.  i do not want to speak to barbara.  answer my question here so everyone will know what's happening at your hospice care before sending their loved ones in your care. thank you

i cannot express how grateful we are to calvery for the exceptional end of life care my mother received there. she was a long-time supporter of calvery through the years because of friends and family members relating stories of caring and compassionate staff. the medical and nursing teams were top notch, the facility was comfortable and not institutional, and visitors were treated with great compassion and kindness. my mother never had a day of discomfort or anxiety for her 2 weeks at calvery. we will continue out financial support for this important community resource.

i noticed the place is expanding so there is construction on some parts of the hospital.  this was a nice facility with two cafeterias from what i noticed.  i mean this is a hospital what can you really say either you love them for what they have done for a loved one or you hate them for not responding the way you wanted them too.  just judging by my visit it was a pleasant visit with helpful staff.

i am a 66 year old woman. i have been in many hospitals during my life and this one is by far the best. critical care unit is top notch. the doctors are all caring and kind. no matter which department i have been in for care it has all been excellent. i also use the doctors in the outpatient clinic and have found them to also give excellent care. no bad marks at all against them.

ive lived in branson for 20 years and love this hospital.  i have always had a wonderful experience with especially the doctors  and staff there.  they diagnosed my breast cancer at an early stage and spent many months there going back for treatments. they 
all have me hope and courage to undergo all of the treatments!  loved my surgeon.  doctor moll who made me feel at ease as i had to have two surgeries.  all of the chemo nurses were top notch to.  so nice.  i never had to wait  more than 10 minutes to see my oncologist. i have no clue why all the negative coments on this site.  this hospital saved my life.  i noticed most of the people who gave them were from out of town and probably out of network.  now that might be a problem.  i have many friends who use this hospital who love it too.  like i said i am a local resident.many of my friends have had surgeries there and also use their urgent care.

incomplete care. untrustworthy billing practices.financial assistance is not available even if they say it is.

i was on vacation and became very sick. it was the only er nearby and so there wasn't much choice. the wait time was easily 4 hours, and they never did any bloodwork or complete testing to see what was really wrong. i ended up at an urgent treatment center a few days later because i wasn't well. a week after the er visit i was in another state with family (because i was too sick to travel all the way home) and the practitioner there did run bloodwork and started emergency protocols for that condition. all things that could have been done out of branson er but they did not do their job completely. 
their website very clearly touts that they are not-for-profit health system, but their financial assistance isn't available for everyone they say it is. as a not-for-profit they were the least willing to work with me of any medical group i've ever dealt with, and they sent my bill to collections after having established a payment plan, a payment plan they did not follow through on their part. 
and i still had to pay all the medical bills of all care after that event, because they id not do all the testing needed to determine the cause, cost that could have been avoided and put my health in even greater jeopardy.

kootenai healths discriminatory treatment practices strike dark totalitarian undertones that places big pharma, and their bottom line above patient care.

my wife and i had our second child delivered at kootenai health. during our newborns first physical inspection the doctor discovered our child was born with ankyloglossia (tongue-tied), and at that time it was recommended that it be clipped as is routine. this is a common procedure at kootenai, and the for mayo clinic which it is a part of. 

however because we opted not to have every shot and vaccination administered kootenai refused to perform the procedure. the labor units head physician told us directly that had we accepted all the shots they have performed the procedure, and that he had done so on numerous occasions. although we asked for studies indicating our newborn was more at risk than any other child the physician told us there were none, and that no such information existed. 

despite the fact  that we were troubled by what this meant for our newborn my wife and i remained civil, and kept cool heads. as our meeting came to an end i made the attempt to shake hands with our proudly out of state physician as we parted ways he refused. in idaho that speaks volumes.

i fear that kootenai's good name no longer means what it used to; beyond that i can't help but feel terrible for many of the incredible nurses, and doctors who work there but are obviously unable to speak out in against kootenais one size fits all approach to health. it is only because of those hard working individuals that kootenai health earned two stars rather than one.

kootenai medical sucks. had a sleep study for take home cost me almost $600. the payment people told me i had months to pay off.  been getting calls from a 1 888 974 1235 , no message left. turns out to be them. i paid 250 and 117 off from that balance  in november now they have called me 2 times about my remaining balance  of 223.  wtf kootenai!!!!! there are people who owe thousands and u gonna call me about 223.00. will not go there for any reason. yes rumors are correct.  they suck!!!!!! paid balance off today so i don't get harassed by them again. please people go somewhere else!!!!!!!!!

i had a planned day surgery in late november. i have insurance. i was hounded by billing to prepay what my insurance didnt pay. i ultimately caved and paid $500. i paid december, january and now its february 20, 2020 and i get no less than 1 call every week. some as early at 7 am all for payment. i've never missed a payment. i have yet to receive my february  bill. i was told it went out yesterday but they called me?. i asked for the bill to be emailed so i could make my payment and was told they would do that. nothing! i was told it is "customary" for calls to be made until paid in full. give me a break.  it's not an issue with staff but billing. i'm  not a deadbeat quit treating me like one.

if i could give negative stars, i would.

we brought his clothing back the same evening. we were told he would be allowed to call us today during calling times. he didn't call. i called and was told that they would have him call us. when he called we were told that they didn't allow him to call earlier.

additionally we have spoken to gloria saez who is the chief clinical officer who told us that we could see our child tonight. the head nurse mary is very rude and won't allow it. supposedly there is no doctor available. she says she called the on call doctor.
