update: i had an emotional breakdown and massive panic attack. i thought i was having a heart attack. 911 was called and i had to leave for my own health. 

back again this morning, waiting. 

feel free to contact me.

the sole reason i've given three stars is because the majority of the staff are phenomenal and caring. i have the most experience with the few rns they employ since i require central line care and all blood work ordered by my primary doctor has to be done there and i've never had a problem with failure to use aseptic technique, which not all nurses ensure they follow when doing central line care even though not doing so is incredibly dangerous. however, the best care couldn't make me blind to the fact that the hospital desperately needs to be updated cosmetically and otherwise. supplies in exam rooms are stored in sterilite containers found at walmart, the en-suite bathrooms in each exam room are so small that you couldn't fit the iv pole in with you if you were getting something intravenously, and everything from the vital sign monitors to the thermometers are woefully outdated. i can't understand how this is the case when they've managed to acquire a facilities in both cushing and jenks.

i've never seen more compassion and care. my son was born there as was his wife, who is an rn in the children's hospital. my husband is currently in the icu and they saved his life. yes, parking is a problem but well worth the care. i wouldn't trust any hospital more for you or your loved ones.

i went to the er before when it was as if i was having a stroke with a lot of pain. they told my husband that i was just looking for pain meds which i have at home. my face and upper body was contorted and i couldn't talk!!!
now, i was scheduled to have surgery this afternoon. they (hospital scheduling dept) changed the time and did not call me the day before like they were supposed to and didn't call me this morning like they were supposed to do. i drove over an hour on my way to find out my surgery had to be cancelled because i wasn't there. the surgeon, the dr office scheduler, myself and whoever is in this disaster has been highly inconvenienced including my ride who took the day off. i will not be returning to this hospital even if i have to find a new surgeon.

omg!   i had a broken foot.  i called a stop in clinic and was quoted about $200.  i should have gone there.  instead, i thought i just had a sprain so i waited and when the pain got bad i went to the emergency room.  the result:

over $2,200 in bills.   all they did is have me wait around in the waiting room.  i never once saw a doctor.  i have no idea who he or she is.  instead, i got a medical assistant.   and later a nurse who "fitted" cheap floppy boot that didn't fit (they only had a very, very large size - so it was worthless).  they took 2 x rays of the foot.  that's it.... lots of wasted time and only 2 x rays.   all for 10 times what a stop by clinic quoted.   zero of this had anything to do with fixing the broken bones - they ended up healing themselves perfectly without intervention.

i learned how terrible this emergency room is.

i can't believe the unprofessional staff the er department has. my daughter in law was taken via ambulance for complications during pregnancy and i think we would have had better service at a free clinic. they are beginning to be like borrego health. nurses rolling their eyes when asked questions. not to mention she is in a gurney in a hallway. what is happening to this hospital. they put us in a bungalow where we are obligated to check if it's our turn because the security guards radio doesn't work. this place is a joke. on the bright side my sister works with the joint commission and i called her already and she is starting to make phone calls to the chief nursing officer and the hospital director.

this is a follow up review. my daughter and grandson are finally home. 
after my first, not so positive, review i received a call from maggie s., the perinatal manager. after a nice long talk i discovered that the issues i mentioned in my first review stemmed from a lack of communication and not just on the part of desert regional but also kaiser permanente. the 8 hour er wait could have easily been avoided if kp had done their part. 

i'm very grateful that desert regional has taken my concerns seriously and is making a concerted effort to make sure the problems don't happen in the future to other patients. they made sure my family was healthy before being sent home and the care they received was, once again, top notch. i would like to mention the two nursing students that helped 'babysit' while i took my daughter to the cafeteria for a break. thank you so much for being so sweet and kind. they always had a smile on their faces. that's the type of customer service needed in stressful situations.  

thanks again.

desert regional hospital employee doctors like dr. kaul neerrja who do not communicate with patients, don't provide treatment plans or support treatment for their patients wellness.  from what observed i feel very sorry for the team that works under dr kaul neerja.   when i confronted dr kaul neerja  on her poor management of my case she was very dismissive. it seems to be the only goal of dr kaul neerja and the hospital was to prolong my stay in hospital to again the highest insurance reimbursement possible.  as a patient with a high deductible that hurts the pocket book.  

since release i have talk to others who have a bad experience at desert regional hospital.  one states "james wrote a review and they went to talk to him, james told them everything that happen and they still didn't do anything to make it better".   another says "just horrible hospital unless you're in trauma... sorry"

as a mental health provider physical trauma impacted by poor care in not conducive to healing.  

with that, said i met the most amazing nurses, techs and hospital bed runner (sorry i don't know your true title).  these members of the hospital team brought me support, reassurance, smiles and many laughs.  these are the people that are in the profession for the right reason.

words will never express how amazing the ladies of the labor & delivery ward are. though i'm not a first time mom, every single rn i came into contact with was so extremely nice, knowledgeable, helpful, and so sweet. from the moment i checked into triage to the moment we checked out with our little bundle of joy. h u g e shout out to rn char who took such good care of us while i was in labor. she was beyond kind, attentive, informative, and never once left my side. char, if they notify you of this, i am forever grateful you are part of our birth story. we won't ever forget you.

i came to the emergency room on 01/21/2020.  i was admitted at 10am. at 10 am the doctor ordered iv antibiotics, they started the iv at 10pm.

that is just the beginning of the meds ups.

i lived in los angeles my whole life. i've been in and out of a lot of ers. this er takes the cake! my husband is here for a possible blood clot and they kicked me out because i wasn't a patient and there were plenty of seats. my husband is not a dr person he needs support. i think it's ridiculous you can not wait with love ones. i never experienced this in my whole life. i'm waiting in my car now while my husband is frantically texting me every 5 secs and wants to leave. you need to change your policy, some people need support and are not capable of sitting alone for 10hrs. also i live over an hour away and can not just leave and come back

we were from out of town when my daughter had an emergency case and we were brought to this hospital. my daughter was in er for 6 hrs and was admitted in pediatric department overnight. the procedures were done in a reasonable amount of time and they gave us the attention and best care possible which i was not expecting since i can see how busy they were. every staff we met were friendly and supportive. dr. h. abu-zahra, the medical residents and all the nurses assigned to my daughter were very thorough, they explained everything well and includes the family in decision making. i am very grateful and i appreciate everything they have done for my daughter.
everyone from andre in a triage to all the staff in the rapid assessment area, registration, dr.s glover and roten thank you! you were all so kind to my mom.

i would like to extend my great appreciation to rn diazoni, virna for extending her assistance during my stay at the recovery room. she is kind, attentive and she listens what we really need. quality care to rn virna for me is great care for me.

my mother doesn't handle pain medication while but she made a big scene because she was in pain from her broken leg and from an infection on her head so they gave her some earlier today her oxygen intake levels got really low and she had to be monitored heavily. the night nurse silvia has been amazing in being here and making sure she was stable. 100% review for that nurse.

i was visiting from out of town and had a medical emergency that caused me to end up in the desert regional er.  my care once i finally made it to the actual treatment area was very good.  the doctors and nurses were all very attentive and they were good diagnosticians.  excellent in fact. but getting to the treatment area was another experience entirely.  the waiting room was inadequate and the staff was over-burdened.  not enough seating, dreary atmosphere.  i was terribly ill - we waited approximately an hour to be seen which wasn't so bad, but given i was so ill it was an eternity.  i ended up spending hours in the treatment area once finally there to obtain the necessary treatment to be able to leave.  this hospital has a lot going for it, but it needs to create a better experience for patients as they come in the front door.

my daughter in law was hospitalized in the labor and delivery department for one month due to pregnancy complications. the nursing staff was absolutely amazing thru the whole time,they had so much compassion  and took great care of my daughter in law, son and grandson the whole time of her stay. job well done !! thank you jz

never take your love one here! especially our senior parents, friends anyone you truly love!! the staff: doctors, nurses and all on board are workg to make living/$$$, as we all are! but i lost the love of my life just because my baby was a senior. the lies the coverup after suing and reading my loves med records revealed how far corp america will go to make $$$$$$

horrible er experience! thursday night, i was dizzy & fell hard on my side & head brought in by paramedics. i was left at checkin at front door, a couple minutes later a woman with her husband walks in on her own. she was given a ride in a wheelchair by the nurse & i was told to walk after them! what? i came by paramedics was disorientated, dizzy & barely able to walk because of my ribs and i was told to walk! i stumbled behind them crying, shaking  & confused, told to go to triage 1/2 way down a hallway. then go sit down with a bunch of people. eventually i go & sit in a large chair & see a doctor. i'm still crying, shaking & confused. she asked me how i got there. did she mean the room or the hospital? " i said i walked, i couldn't even get out paramedics brought me there, and then i was forced by the nurse to walk to triage." after seeing the doctor i needed to go to the bathroom. i told the nurse i was freaking out because i was barefoot i was absolutely disgusted with being barefoot walking around shaking & still crying. all i wanted was to lay down to be able calm down! but, no, i was in a lot of pain, confused & hysterical. and i had to get up & go all sorts of places. then they came to take me to get an x-ray! these horrible people had me walk to get my x-ray! what the hell is wrong with this place??? the guy took off down the hallway & around the corner then he finally realized i wasn't  with him.. i was using the walls to standup right! i was in the er because i fell & hurt my head, ribs, face & hand and i was dizzy!i should have been taken by wheelchair everywhere i needed to go not walk anywhere!!!  i don't even know what to say about this experience it was so horrendous! i was traumatized by my fall at home & the er should be a place to be able to calm down because you are getting help. but my er experience was just as traumatizing as my fall! mostly what i got was nauseous because of all the up down, sit down, walk here, walk there all while being hysterical. not one member of the staff helped me put the socks on they gave me, but a very nice man in the waiting room did. i was physically unable to get them on and the staff didn't care or notice! i talked to their social media person about my review, he did apologize & said he would have the head of  the emergency department & over a month later i have not heard from anyone! they didn't give me take home notes for possible concussion nor anything about bruised ribs! what a feeble er! not helping injured people & making the dizzy holding their ribs people stagger the hallways ignoring their pain. & no take home notes for their injuries! what the hell****update for february 2020!! ****still no apology from emergency room!! i was treated like  trash!!! i could have had broken ribs & no one ever checked to see if i was alright!!! had me walking really i was staggering, holding my ribs & used the  walls to hold me up!!! disgusting how i was treated!!! shame on you desert regional! ***3 weeks ago i left a message with their complaint dept. i have heard nothing!!
excellent staff! great place with a family feel that truly does the best they can to care for patients.
fac_name: Wesley Rehabilitation Hospital, an affiliate of Encompass Health

review: best hospital i've ever been to and that says a lot considering i've been to the hospital in uc san diego. after getting no treatment at all at el centro regional medical center for having a screw 2-3 inches inside my left foot i went here and they gave me pain medication in less than 5 minutes and all the nurses were so nice and funny! they literally made me feel at home and they told me what procedure would be done so quickly! they performed surgery on my foot and all the doctors were so kind and so talented. they left the tiniest hole in my foot and cleaned it out very well. the reason i think this is such a great hospital is because they don't just try helping you physically...they care about their patients on an emotional level and they're very sympathetic.

worst hospital ever!!! the nurses are rude, and on top of that while my sister was in labor, doctors were calling to her room about how she was going to pay for her delivery because her medical didn't go through and were asking him to pay 1,800 right then and there, like why cant they ask some one to come to their room pull my brother in-law outside and talk, or talk to him about it after the baby is here, now my brother in-law and my sister who is giving birth are stressing out, and on top of that this f**king hospital is cold  my sister has 3 thick blankets on while having really strong contractions and is still freezing, even my boyfriend is cold and he doesn't get cold easily so that says something... 
i definitely would not recommend this hospital at all, make the drive to somewhere else, anything but here!

awful! most of the maternity ward staff is uneducated and rude. in the patient guide it's recommended to ask questions and to speak up if there is a problem. the nurses become hateful if you ask to much or complain, as if it's a hassle. family members are treated poorly. the actual dr. was good it's a shame he doesn't have a better supporting staff. if i could give zero 's i would. there has been action taken and hopefully changes will be made.

my husband had a total knee replacement. i found that the nurses, aides, doctors, pts, ots, maintenance,food staff, etc. we're excellent beyond other hospitals. everyone really helps you. mary, my husband's doctor's nurse, answered every question that my husband had forgotten to ask dr. stern to the point of drawing diagrams so both he and i could understand. she called us several times at home to check on my husband. she is a gem! 

they have developed a class and a booklet that you need to attend in order to have the operation for hips or knees that teaches you how prepare for the operation physically and how to set up your home, explains everything you need to know about the operation, and what needs to be done after the operation to heal well.

from the time my husband entered the hospital for surgery, the nurses and aides had bright smiling faces that put you at ease as they worked efficiently and succinctly preparing you for the operation. they also had a good sense of humor and kindly put up with my husband's jokes and gave him the time he needed. 

some of those people were: mary (nurse), an stna with the last name valentine, darryl, nate, hannah, katie, christine all nurses or stnas i believe. kristin the ot who took care of my husband, and the maintenance men and the people who deliver the food one by the name of kevin in a blue and black jacket who help me several times when i got lost. everyone was so kind and affable.

the work on my husband was fantastic as he has been puttering around at home just five days later. through i need to remind my husband that he is supposed to use his walker. also my husband had two classes before he left a day after his operation. this is a great facility in my opinion. it is number 1 to me, and if i decided to have a knee or hip operation i would only want it done at lutheran hospital in cleveland, oh!

this was a nightmare.  i came in here very sick and with chest pains and extreme high blood pressure.  trash cans overflowing, rude nurses.  i got sick and she yelled at me not to vomit again because there is no house keeping.

in massive amounts oof pain and told too bad not even tylenol   i getthat there are drug seekers but i did not visit the hospital for fun.

disgrace to the medical community.  this place is a shameful.

i wish i could give 10 stars. i managed to to pay the er a visit twice within 3 days. life of a mom of boys. my son who is 7 got hooked by a fishing hook from my older son and the amount of compassion and kindness was out of this world. i wish i could have remembered all the wonderful medical staff that attended to us on night one. ( wendy, dr. woolery etc) what was such a traumatic incident for myself, they performed miracles helping my little man feel 100%. flash forward to the next afternoon when my oldest son slipped in on river rocks in the water and sliced his forearm and tumbling into arctic water, we rushed back down into town. they made my big guy feel extremely comfortable when he was scared to death of getting stitched! the medical students that performed his sutures were awesome. both the boys are doing amazing! i am so grateful for the care that we received. hopefully we won't have to return anytime soon!

this is the worst experience i've ever had with a medical facility. i went to the clinic to get medication management and they treated me like a drug addict. they billed my insurance for $1440 for a half-hour meeting with the doctor. the doctors all have lousy grades from vitals and heathgrades, and it's no wonder. the place is filthy. the doctors are incompetent to say the least. do. not. go. here. under. any. circumstances.

elgin location. 
my husband cut his hand while working in the area.  we checked in to the er waited about 10 minutes got a room #17, it was really tiny but sufficient. the er appeared clean.  the room was semi clean, with the exception of the probe covers. they even brought a portable xray machine to the room, which was nice for the patients.  you get the results fast.  the doctor was working with an intern who she allowed to stitch my husbands finger, she sewed a vein in the stitch so it was sticking out, she said dont worry it will die.  the service was fast but not very thorough.  lets hope we do not have to come back to this location.

review:

my heart i believe that's exactly what he did. he was laughing talking to this nurse and told me i'll be in a kind of hazy state but after the iv i knew nothing until i was back in the same room they review:
from the moment the ambulance brought me here, to the exam, x-rays, being admitted, surgery, different floors based on my condition and operation prep, not a single person let us down. the nurses, doctors, pa's, surgeon, all introduced themselves, all explained what was going on, kept us informed, and demonstrated true empathy and concern. it was if i walked into a place with long lost family. this hospital managed to hire people in every field we came in contact with that had a great sense of humor and willingness to help.  if i was wealthy i would want to give them all gifts. they truly made a horrible situation of my breaking both ankles, the best it could be. way to go baylor!

i don't understand why other ratings are low. there's no doubt my bill will be a maddening surprise, but um.....welcome to any hospital. i've lived all over va and the chicago area and have never had an urgent care or er experience like this as a patient, someone bringing a patient in, or volunteering.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: another update:  still no bsw police reports as i have requested now (3) times.  i did receive a threatening letter from their collection firm harris and harris yesterday that i need to pay the balance due of $1,578.69 before 30 days or risk having this negative impact on my credit report for the next 7 years.  i received barbaric treatment from one of their in-house doctors and i have to pay for it or suffer the consequences.  their letter december 20, 2019 sends profuse apologies and thanks for the information on how to improve patient care but at the end of it all you need to pay up.  i agree with justin i. they just want your money and that's all.

review:
yet another poor review for this exact same visit over 6 months ago. you would think that due to the pies poor care/service that they would just leave us alone and go about our lives.

nope. we continue to receive a bill from physicians billing wanting another $1000 for this crappy care. our insurance informed us many months ago that we were only responsible for the copay. we were also advised to ignore the bill by our insurance. 

this agency has been notified of this. yet, they continue to send threatening bills. apparently, the $3000 already paid was not sufficient for this visit. they also do not appear to care about your well being and are much more focused on the amount of money they can squeeze out of you.

please do not make my mistake going here and avoid this facility!

this is not the first time bsw has screwed me around, but i guarantee it will be the last.

it is unacceptable that our government has not taken action to end extortion such as this that has been taking place for decades.

i would love the opportunity to provide these blood suckers with a "service" that they do not have the opportunity to see the final bill amount and send them another bill 6 months later for another $1000-$2000. that's like your contractor quoting you $2000 for your new cabinets and sending you another bill in 6 months demanding another $1000 for their "out of network" subcontractors. 

hospitals and healthcare are supposed to have our needs and best interest in mind. our system is pathetic to allow these con artists to continue to do business this way.

review: my husband was treated at the cancer center. first-day nurse was rude for chemo, didn't know the proper treatment plan. several times a tech who was not licensed administered meds. not sure if that is legal, one med was especially important to administer with warming up and she almost forgot. not sure this place is safe for anyone, most especially cancer treatment. the nursing staff is not kind or compassionate. assigned a navigator, never heard from her, she was preoccupied with being 'pretty'. not sure who to explain most of the experience was shallow and indifferent.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review:
pretty upset with my visit today. 
i had my 1st child at this hospital 2 years ago and i loved it. but i have since then moved to austin and am in town visiting family. i started to noticed my baby wasn't moving very much and was concerned. my obgyn recommended i be seen just to be sure everything was ok. 
the er front desk was friendly, and the nurse who took me to labor and delivery was sweet and made conversation. but as for my triage nurse and the dr who had finally seen me, were not very friendly. they seemed annoyed to be having to see me, even tho i wanted to be sure my baby was ok. all the dr did was ask the same questions the nurse asked me, and then left telling me to have a nice day. 
if i need to be seen for any reason again while pregnant, it will not be at this hospital.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: urgent care (not hospital review)---i have never had a more poorer experience than i had at the bswh mckinney urgent care.  is this what you call healthcare?  is this today's healthcare? is this the expectation going forward on how long you have to wait to see a provider?  i have never felt so embarrassed to be a us citizen and have to wait over three hours to be seen at a walk in urgent care center. all people beware that if you plan to see a healthcare provider at this location on a saturday then you might as well bring your lunch and dinner or go somewhere else. i think it is absolutely ridiculous to only have one nurse practitioner working at an urgent care. yup, just one and no doctor. the individual that came after me said it was their second visit in two days and they sent her away again today (like the day before) because even though the center was open they were not checking in any more patients.  mind you it wasn't even 6 o'clock and the place closes at 8.  for some people i talked to they said their insurance "requires" them to use that particular urgent care (unless i guess you want to drive to dallas). over three hour wait people!! three hours!! bswh you got my vote as the worst urgent care in the north dallas corridor.  i hope this review will bring about some sort of change.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: great caring people. especially night crew. they all were very helpful thorough nurses and doctors.  a lot of indian hospitals get a bad wrap or people only post the negative, so i'm glad to post a great experience.

took a friend to hospital for a hip replacement surgery. it turned out to be a wonderful experience for all. especially my friend she was really pleased with the nursing service the doctor that took care of her and replaced her hip and all the after services she received in the hospital thank you so much. i especially care for all the services in the cafeteria the food was excellent well-prepared always hot and fresh. i truly enjoy going to the cafeteria each time i must be in the hospital for one reason or another because they always take good care of the staff as well as all the visitors to the hospital the food is of a good variety it is also always fresh good for you but delicious it always looks good and also always homemade. they always have a good selection of items from soup to salads with hot items like sandwiches dinner is like meatloaf or chicken parm. everything is available from like 11 a.m. till 7 at night. they put on a really good breakfast each day that you can get eggs the way you like them pancakes or waffles they will make omelettes to order. they always serve regular decaf and flavored coffees as well as a good selection of teas. i sometimes go to this cafeteria just to eat even when i don't have someone in the hospital. it is very inexpensive when my friend was in the hospital i was able to eat breakfast for under $3 and her children that were with me at the time that it was two of them they had breakfast and it cost them under $10 and they had omelettes and toasts etc. is definitely worth going each time i have gone i spent less than $5 for each meal. that's a reason to have something is affordable and filling as well as fresh

the staff in the nuclear medicine department and radiology reception are phenomenal. they are truly kind and they explain every step of the testing process as it's happening. i'll definitely continue to get my diagnostic imaging done at milford.

i have gone here for various procedures.  however, kudos to the emergency dept.  overall, the wait was 10 mins to be seen.  i had a problem with this.  i was the only one sitting in the check in area.  i could barely walk to the door i was in so much pain.  these 2 nurses were sitting to the side chatting it up and never moved an inch to assist me.  the er dr was great considering they were slightly busy.  i spent no more than 6 hours here and was sent home with meds and  prescription.  i was very pleased with my visit.
this was the most horrific experience of my life i was brutally beaten and bit by a black male security guard last name anderson. no one from the hospital ever reached out their comment is a lie.

i am very pleased with the care i received here in the er!! the nurse practitioner was great as well as the other staff... i hope i never need to go back to the hospital, but i will go back to hemet er if necessary!

giving them even one star is being generous and perhaps only because the nursing staff and the one doctor i have spoken to are kind and doing their best despite a severely broken system. this hospital's issues run deep and i could go on forever, but there is a big disconnect between the telemetry floor (which is a misnomer) and the radiology department. my dad arrived via ambulance to the er department on wednesday at 7 pm. he was admitted thursday morning to the hospital. we literally got our very first report from the radiologist on sunday at 11 am, despite my father having multiple x-rays since being admitted on thursday morning. he should have had a confirmed diagnosis within one or two days....not five days later. it was one series of errors after another. we waited from friday afternoon to saturday evening for a radiology report that we would truly never receive as the final x-ray was never performed...and no one even knew it! it took me calling the house supervisor, speaking to a doctor and demanding he call radiology. they have no intenal process in place to know when something hasn't been competed as ordered?! heaven forbid you need a radiologist over the weekend, as they are only staffed from 9 am to 3 pm. i thought hospitals should funtion 24/7? global is too cheap and/ or dysfunctional to pay onrad  (their contracted afterhours radiology department) to read a report, despite all the previous blunders and the doctor specifically requesting it asap. as a result, my father has been in the hospital since wednesday night.... paying per night for their incompetence and getting increasingly exposed to numerous other potential issues. 

i will update and revise this review when the hospital administration has reached out to me and satisfactorily resolved these issues. it's a miracle that they are still accredited by the joint commission and are capable of honestly receiving medicare payments.

took my friend to er for chest pain. the receptionist was non caring to begin with. let staff know my friend had chest pain. they said we will give info to nurse. i just wanted her vitals taken. 45 min later i went up again and was told angie the nurse was given my information. as my friend seemed to be getting worse for a third time i approached the desk and stayed we have been 1 hr 15 minutes and no one has taken my friends vitals. i just wanted someone to take her blood pressure. angie the nurse just about flew over the receptionist to say " this is an emergency room the wait time is 4-6 hrs." i stated fine i just want my friends blood pressure taken. i then asked what if my friend is having a heart attack. and nurse angie stated " well she is in the best place to have one" " go sit down and i will triage you" 15 minutes later she took my friends vitals and she was immediately given an ekg referral of which she had to have two consecutively. my friend was immediately admitted. i spoke with the charge nurse and he asked me to file a complaint. i will go further by filing a grievance.
my friend was near death weak and unable to think correctly. thank god i was her advocate. the unprofessionalism and just simple meanness exacurbated the already delicate situation.
i really was appalled at the front room treatment we received.
go to urgent care if you can...
patients beware

this hospital is horrific!!! my niece had an infection due to mastitis raging through her body and all they did was give her tylenol and not even every 4 hours!!  more like 8 hours!!! then they forgot she was even there!  she was admitted on tuesday and no doctor until 9pm wednesday!!!  the nurses kept insisting she needed to pump which she did until she was bleeding!!!  what the frick??!!!  then her boyfriend was staying with her for two nights and no one said anything about it. then on thursday he came to see her and was planning to stay again and "nurse rachet" actually came in and rolled the bed out!!  crazy!!  please, if you love your family, avoid this hospital at all cost!

my father was brought in by ambulance on friday 11-29. i ran into the er upset and frantic. clearly how someone whose parent just had a massive heart attack would behave. i was asked by the security guard my father's name. i told him and he said no one was there by that name. i was confused how that could have been the case. i couldn't possibly have left the scene after the paramedics and made it to the hospital before them. the security guard said maybe but did he give them his name. i said no we didn't because he was unconscious. the guy said maybe he is in the system as a john doe. so i naturally asked well can you tell me if an 80 year old john doe arrived here with cardiac arrest in the last few minutes. the nurse at the desk behind him said "jesus" and scoffed and rolled her eyes at me. clearly not the response someone trained in this field should have. i wasn't the least bit ok with her response and got agitated. the security guard said if i don't calm down i would have to leave. i said i will calm down but this clearly isn't ok and you can't treat people like this. all i want to know is if he is here. after about 30 minutes the guard came back and said he was here and someone would speak with us shortly. another 20 minutes or so went by and a woman came to gather information. after that another person came and said that he is bed 11 and we can see him in a bit. which is hopeful right. after about 10 minutes we were called back. the man ushered us into a room with 3 chairs facing the door. no clue what us going on but it didn't feel good but they said he was in a bed so maybe it's not bad. they said a doctor will be with us shortly. after about 20-30 minutes of watching nurses walk by joking and laughing a doctor walked by. my husband got up and the doctor said how's it going to him. he said well fine i guess just wondering what's going on. the doctor said yeah i'll be with you in a minute and walked away.  finally he came in and sat down said said well he didn't make it. we shocked him with the paddles and he didn't respond. he literally just kept repeating that and offered no further insight or explanation. then he and his nurse said we will get him cleaned up so you can see him. we waited and waited and waited. finally we were called back. my dad still had the iv lines and some sort of mouth piece in. clearly he wasn't cleaned up. there was another nurse in the room going over the details with someone on the phone. i asked if they could talk about it elsewhere since it was highly distracting and desensitizing. they said well we tried to get you back quickly. i don't call nearly 30 minutes or more quickly. i asked twice why can't they make the phone call from the nurses station plus this whole time they were supposed to be cleaning him up yet he wasn't. we just had to leave since this wasn't how we wanted to see him and we couldn't get any privacy. it's really unfortunate because you don't get that time back and their lack of professionalism and courtesy robbed our family of this precious moment. when we went to leave there was no one to show us out and very little explanation of what to do from here. if all of this wasn't enough. less then an hour after leaving the hospital my grieving mother gets a call from a place called legacy. it was a mortuary. she had missed that first call which was at around 11:30 pm. not to worry because at 1:30 am they called back. the guy on the phone pretended to give a damn about what had happened. my mom told them to kiss off and to never call her again. apparently the hospital sells and/or gives your number to other places or affiliates. this way they can try to profit even more off of your loss. if there was such a thing as negative stars this place would get it. absolutely horrible from beginning to end. you should be completely ashamed of the operation you guys are running. despicable!!!

definitely a 0!!!! do not bring your loved one here!! unless you want them to die! nurses are useless and lazy! they definitely do not care about the patient's. my loved one got hospitalized here and when she pushes the call button nobody responds to her need. she's totally bed ridden and cannot feed herself or anything, they do not feed her! we've asked multiple times for them to please please keep giving her ensure as she can't eat solid food or even hold the ensure bottle and they don't even do that. if we didn't come everyday to check on her i really think besides herr illness she would starve to death! no water given to her either. they leave her unbathed don't brush her teeth comb her hair etc. they will only do this if we say something because we check on her everyday. the hospital  is old run down and so dirty. completely disgusted with how patients are treated here! once again do not bring your loved ones here please!!! hemet hospital is pathetic and unhumane. i feel sorry for the people who don't have anybody  checking on them and or who are bed ridden. get it together hemet hospital!!!! this facility disgusts me!!!!!

the doctors and nurses have cared for me many times and love their professional approach to caring for me when i was sick or needed medical care. thank you to all the medical teams for giving your all to treating in my time of need!

review:
i have a trained service dog for mobility and medical alert. while my disabilities can be invisible, it's usually not as you can see i have a major walking issue. i worked with a local service dog training organization that meets assistance dogs international standards to get him. he is legit, no amazon certificate or anything. he took 2 years of training and cost tens of thousands to train.

his mobility vest is made of leather. it doesn't fit currently (we think it shrank due to rain and not having proper care taken of it) and we're waiting on his new one to come in (takes up to 8 weeks because it had to be custom made as it's a mobility/guide vest). still, he was leashed to his collar and had a couple leash wraps that showed he was a working service dog. we even put on his working booties (they're heavier duty than what you can get at petco and meant for working dogs). we have the laws printed out and highlighted and i/my boyfriend both know how to answer the required questions.

yesterday, i had three important doctors appointments. i've waited several weeks for them (about a month) and they were supposed to be a new step in figuring out my chronic disability. they were also about a 40 minute drive to get to them. between the first appointment and the second, i thought it would be a good idea to get a printout of my medical records, as my new school was requesting them.

this meant going from the clinic side to the hospital side, where they had the hospital administration who dealt with these requests. while waiting to see someone, i noticed a bit of commotion going on but decided to focus on filling out the paperwork. i had noticed someone called the cops or security, but i was entirely oblivious to why. when i was called back i was told they would get my paperwork filed but i would need to leave as the cops has been called, so if i protested they would escort me out by force. this entire time, my dog hadn't even lifted his head from his nap, tucked beside my feet and out of the way. the administrator talking to me told me it was bs because she knew me and my dog and has seen him vested before, but they'd had five complaints about him (particularly his size) and so i'd need to go. the administrator confirmed it was due to his size/not being vested and that his behavior had been perfect.

i pulled up texas state law on my phone as well as the ada. they said it didn't matter as it was hospital policy. i left, unable to go to the rest of my appointments (missed ), obviously. they told me i wouldn't be welcome back to any of their hospitals or clinics until he was wearing his new vest (takes about 2 months to get). 

i called the head of hospital administration, michelle, to get a copy of the policy. she confirmed it and said by it saying she didn't care what i thought the law said. she refused to hear me out and kept talking over me any time i tried to say it was against the law. she also started talking about how my dog was unleashed and causing issues (wtf?!), which is completely untrue and i have several witnesses that can attest to that. even the doctor i saw earlier today told me she was afraid of dogs, especially big ones, but she was beyond impressed with how well behaved mine was. he was completely leashed and i can show you a picture of everything he was wearing yesterday.

to make this story even worse, this is the second time they've done something like this to me. the first was in the exact same department about 9 months ago. the greeter stood up as soon i walked in and screamed "get that thing the fuck out of here!" i spoke with hospital administration after that incident and they told me they had dealt with it and will provide better training for their employees and volunteers on service dogs.

sources:
ada faq on service animals (pay special attention to q1, q2, q5, q7, q8, and q14-17): https://www.ada.gov/regs2010/service_animal_qa.html
ada on service animals: https://www.ada.gov/service_animals_2010.htm
texas disability law on service dogs: https://gov.texas.gov/organization/disabilities/assistance_animals
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Temple

review: by far the worst experience i've ever had in a hospital. i drove from dallas to temple to come check up on my brother that was in an accident. when i got here the front desk had no record of him at all. i went to the one on the other side and they can send me down stairs. i went down stairs just so they can tell me "oh go talk to someone on the phone". i called the operator and she didn't know anything either! her response was "you sure he didn't change his name so he wouldn't talk to you guys!" like really?  finally i called my sister and she called other people and we managed to find out he wasn't even on the same area. they could had told me they had moved him. oh and did i tell you i was also holding a 17 lbs baby while running back and forth? yes i was upset. not only did the front desks not care but no one seems to know anything about patients. i honestly hated my experience
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Temple

review: so hold on to your boots people because descrimination still exist to this day. in what we ask people really i say? i saw an elderly man get questioned about his retirement date! and of course i am next in line only to be ask the same. she says oh but it is a standard and required question by medicare. never again. #timeisup for those that think this is right.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Temple

review:
my mom was diagnosed with cancer... she's waiting on an appointment for a nephrectomy. they told her she'd have one within a week of a biopsy. it's been weeks since her biopsy and they keep dismissing her. the receptionist laughed when we called for a follow up as if trying to get rid of cancer is funny. staff definitely needs to be retrained and doctors need to re-evaluate why they're practicing medicine if they're not going to care about their patients. 
update!!!!
my mom got her kidney taken out and the nurses made the experience horrible! my mom was in pain crying and pain meds were suppose to be given to her ever 4 hours and the nurses where giving them to her every 6-7 hours because they were "busy". she was suppose to be walking around when their help and they were too "busy" to take her but they told the doctor that they were. she was there almost a week and wouldn't shower her even though the doctor said it was fine to do. they tried to discharge her when her pain was not under control and she wasn't having bowel movements but they didn't care, they lied to the doctors about that too. the only person who was very caring and compassionate was a cna by the name of julian. my mom even cried because he was nice to her. the whole experience was traumatizing.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Temple

review: north coast used to be sagamore hills children's psychiatric hospital in the 80s. it was horrible and you didn't get to leave the locked ward. in fact, you couldn't even leave the building. you were always locked down and don't get me started on mandatory drugs! no one was trusted with pills, it was all liquid. other patients were allowed to instigate trouble and very little was done to stop it and you wonder why some of us used to stay in our rooms and lash out at staff who would try to roast us out of our rooms and on ward. this would be a nasty physical confrontation usually initiated by staff. as soon as they put their hands on you and you happen to be combative, it was a bad day for them, and i mean terrible if you happen to be a born fighter because you knew how to draw blood even with nothing but your teeth. you got dragged to the qr, which is really the quiet room, and empty concrete room that was also also locked. school was mandatory but some of us played sick. we were able to successfully stay back from school as long as we had a fever. i learned how certain peers were able to constantly stay back from school. all you had to do was stand on your bed when no one was around and hold the thermometer up to the hot ceiling where the heat came from, but don't hold it too long or they might get suspicious. the ceiling could be used to our advantage anytime we wanted to stay home and fake sick, the ceiling was also a heater vent. one time i almost got caught but thankfully i never did. i hated school anyway and i hated the disrespect i got and uncaring nature of the teachers. it was hard for kids who did nothing wrong to be locked up so bad. the only times we had access to the hallways was when we were walking in line escorted by staff to and from necessary locations elsewhere in the building. if you try to fake something needing a regular hospital, it may not work because  any ambulance ride and regular hospital could easily be used for and easy escape plan. you take the ambulance ride to the hospital and when no one's looking, just run from the hospital and wherever you want! that would've been fun but i never got that chance. then you had no comfort items, which made an already bad problem far worse. when you're coming out of a severely abusive home, having no love or nurturing even in the new places and especially no comfort items is enough to make you go mad. they punish you when you lash out over unfair conditions and then leave you locked in the qr until you calm down. at some point you break and eventually start calming down, you can't stay in there forever. i don't blame people for lashing out because such living conditions, especially for abuse survivors who did nothing wrong really don't deserve it. when you're forced to live as though you were a criminal, sagamore hills now known as north coast was really a children's prison. when you have to live like a criminal, that makes an already bad situation far worse for an innocent person who did nothing to deserve to be locked up

my initial visit to the er at chi st. luke's in sugar land was good. my nurse was considerate and attentive. the nurse who took over was also amazing! i did wait five hours due to an issue with the ultrasound tech not being in the building. the doctor i was first seen by needed to be "reminded" which side of my body was needing care immediately after i explained why i was there.

the primary reason i'm giving this er only one star has to do with the er doctor  who i saw and their billing practices.  she was despondent throughout my visit and the entire brief time she spent with me. it was like a cold wet towel on a rainy day. after learning who she was i was not too shocked to learn she wrote two books about reconsidering being in the medical field. she lives in a 700,000 home. 

her billing practices are to turn over patients within 60 days of treatment. not from the time the patient actually receives the bill and knows of the debt. i was turned over to collection for $53.20 and had only been given two weeks to pay this invoice before i received a notice stating that i would be turned over for collection for non-payment.

the medical industry will never get better in this country. the truth behind all of the issues we face when seeking medical care is greed. we have fostered a belief that monetary success is what all should seek at the expense of others and now our medical practitioners do not enter into their careers due to a love of science and caring for others but simply so that they may live in million dollar homes, take luxurious vacations, and show off all that monetary success at the expense of their patients. 

the hospital claims it has no control over the billing practices of their doctors.
fac_name: CHI St. Luke's Health-Sugar Land Hospital

review: i'm glad you offered for us to call and talk to you. you didn't do that the night you kicked my mother out in a rainstorm and send her home because we complained about the lack of nurses visiting her. she's dead now.
fac_name: CHI St. Luke's Health-Sugar Land Hospital

review: had a stroke. fortunately i knew the warning signs, and had my wife drive me to er as soon as possible. they knew we had a 3 hr. window to reverse the damage and quickly got me set up for an air ambulance to the west side and swedish hospital in seattle. they got the okay from the care team in seattle to give the critical meds now. and then sent me on my way. they did a great job. thanks!

i have been taking my daughter to this heart center since day 1, they have gone above and beyond to make her feel comfortable every time we come. they are always nice and caring to all the kids. 

they are located inside rady's to the left, right by subway.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Heart And Health Center

review: if i could give them zero stars i would they the nurses are the worst they never went in to check check on my dad they were about to give him the wrong medication when i brought my dad no wheel chair they made him walk in by himself  nurses were so rude i will never take him back and would not recommend this place to anyone the only people that weee nice and caring are the therapist nurses and staff so unprofessional!!
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Modesto

review: my experience was very positive. my first night was horrible because i was in so much pain but that was the doctors fault for not the nurses. the doctor would not pick up her messages from the exchange but in the morning boy oh boy did she get an ear full and after that i was comfortable. the food here is excellent. every meal was good. you have your own room! the nurses are so busy but i saw them quite often. the real hero's are the nursing assistants that came when you pushed the button. wow- they were so very kind, nothing was a big deal to them. i was hugged when i cried, they held my hand, they gave reassurance they cleaned up horrible messes, they were awesome. the physical, occupational, and speech therapy was great. non other place would you rehabilitation several times a day. if you wanted to work, they would work you. the gym was available to go to any time of day. they encouraged everyone to get up and get moving, which is their job! if you just want to lay around and get waited on then you need to go to a nursing home. this place is for rehab where a person wants to get better. the only down fall was there social services workers for when you going home. that lady was horrible, not helpful, snotty, rude just the worse. i made a complaint about her and also did my family. i really hope she was fired
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Modesto

review: i have been a patient there 6 times and the 5 times were awesome. the nurses, techs, dietary staff, housekeepers (wonderful) pt's were all wonderful. they always made my stay very comfortable. i never had to ever wait very long for anything. with that being said, my last stay will be my last stay. i live a 120 south of st louis so it's not like it's just around the block. i came up for post-op checkup and i had some kind of  something happen to me in the backseat of our car. we went to the er,now mind you i don't recall any of this. they put me on a stretcher and put all kinds of monitoring equipment on me. my daughter said i was thrashing around on the cart and mumbling shit no one could figure out what was going on. in fact my daughter said the nurses and doctors were rude and one of the nurses accused me of faking it. so they went a head and admitted me and i finally came to later that night. they did a good job from that point on. they never figured out what was going on. they turned my pain pump off and loaded  me down with narcotics. i was so disappointed in that place bc i had always been treated so well. so i'll never go back or recommend them ever.

my boyfriend got into a very bad car accident and we were struggling with trying to decide whether to take him to an urgent care vs er, after going to an urgent care and being refused care we went to northside. i always refered patients to northside for imaging so i figured we could try them out! they saw my boyfriend right away at the er. the pa and staff were very informative and did a full examination. i am very impressed for our first visit to an er, i am glad we came to this hospital!

the front desk staff can be a hit or miss . i would assume they are judgemental based off the weird , awkward looks they give the moment you walk in the door . feels like i'm in the 1950's . am i missing something ? is there a colored section ? if so point me to it so that i can be treated with some respect . there is no sense of urgency . i think you would literally need to run in with a bullet to the chest for them to take you seriously and get you to a room  in sensible amount of time . coming in pain , vomiting , unable to breathe ? you will be stuck like me waiting for two hours before a nurse even gathers your information.
they have a wonderful and lovely atrium level it looks like money i went walking all over this place and i must say if it looks like money must be money lol.

this hospital deserves a no star. took my mother here to have her little pinky finger check due to ulcer. her illness history are hypertension and hyponatremia, and we all are know that. we even show them the medication and dosages. in this case they don't even bother her pinky, but keep drawing her blood every four hours for 4 tubes (3-10ml size) each time, and my mom is a very tiny vietnamese female. they diagnose her with of the following: diabetic even though her blood lab results low in sugar, finger injury even though my mon bed ridden more than 5 years (she has no chance of falling or hit herself to anything), speech disorder and they order speech therapy for her even we refused because my mom doesn't speak english, but it does not work, also dementia even though my mom know and remember everything. they keep her there for 3 days and 2 nights to give her intravenous fluids and antibiotics. they discharge her with the pinky ulcer still there. 
what do you think of this?
this is a horrible experience.
worst hospital and terrible system! they could never get my appointment figured correctly! every experience dealing with  them is ridiculous  and time wasting!
worst hospital system i have ever been too. save yourself the headache and go somewhere else.

i've been waiting for two hours to see a doctor in their er.   i was told by northside urgent care, after a ct scan, to go immediately to the er because i was diagnosed with appendicitis.   i informed them of this over two hours ago and still waiting to be called back.  i thought appendicitis was an emergency?!

i realize you can't always choose an er but if you can i highly recommend going elsewhere. in my experience the on duty md has no compassion and horrific bedside manner. he made it clear that he didn't have the patience to explain things more than once and when he did explain things it was double-talk (aka incompetence). when pressed to provide a clear answer the conversation actually devolved into a cursing match. have you ever had a doctor call you an a-hole? this one will. while this doctor is an embarrassment to northside, if he must practice, then an er position is the right place for him. no need to establish rapport there - no need to be the type of person looking to maintain a good reputation that a doctor in a successful private practice needs to stay in business.

my primary care doctor suggested that i make an ultrasound appointment here. scheduling an appointment was effortless as was a reschedule for today, due to a recent snowstorm. 

i arrived promptly and was greeted by a friendly receptionist. the intake staff member was engaging and friendly. i was escorted to the waiting room and within a couple of minutes, the ultrasound technician greeted me and escorted me back. she was very pleasant and engaging as well. the ultrasound took less than 15 minutes and i was through before 9:00 (my appointment time, my check in time was 8:30). 

i highly recommend this place for imaging.
fac_name: Imaging & Radiology at St. Anthony Hospital

review:
recently my dad was taken to there emergency room with chest pains on a sunday evening. when he arrived they found he had high blood pressure but did not have a heart attack! there are 4 of us siblings and all of us showed up to check on him. we all went into the er and had a normal conversation with a 77 year old gentlemen who new everyone and exactly what was going on. they decided to hold him overnight to monitor his blood pressure so we all went home. when we returned the next morning they had given him so many drugs it was like as if he was in a coma! his eye lids would open but his eyeballs where rolled back in his head. he could not speak and really didn't make any noise. i could go on and on about the next couple days but the bottom line is that on wednesday i decided i was not going to allow them to drug him anymore. i watched over him till thursday when my brother could take over. he watched him till friday till my sister could take over. finally by saturday most of the drugs were out of his system and he was allowed to go home!  
stay far away from this place, i could go on and on and on about there mistakes and lies!!!!!

very receptive phone staff at this hospital, both the main switchboard and the emergency services. i am not in the area, and received a call that someone close to me was being taken from their work to jennersville hospital after having a medical event. i had very little information, and was in a bit of a state, understandably. thankfully, my confused and panicked phone call was answered with helpful information and patience. i was also able to convey medical information about the individual, as their job was unable to provide such information. someone was even so kind as to bring the phone to the person so i could speak with them directly, as they were put in the ambulance without their phone or any personal belongings.

this was my first time visiting the hand clinic. i was diagnosed with trigger finger. wow! this is so painful and uncomfortable. after speaking  with p.a. glick she advised i would need a cortisone  injection. she advised that the injection could work as soon as later in the day or within 3 weeks. after 2 days i was able to bend my thumb and i'm happy. i recommend this establishment. great job!

the nurses and night sitters did not follow the doctors orders to contact poa to ask permission to administer haldol drug to my grandfather. it was a prn medication but poa was never contacted. my grandfather died shortly after it was administered.
worst service ever, been sitting here over 3 hour's for ct scan, asked the nurse what's going on and all she has to say "not yet"". seriously! what kind of answer is that?

so this is 24 hours after my experience with triage at advocate hospital . simply i will state my review .we had the front desk employees state that we should escalate my wife's severity or we would sit for 8 or 9 hrs and not even been given a simple ekg ???  the doctor we finally received was excellent after a 6 hour wait but why the attitude of the non medical idiots at the front desk ? so this is the breakdown 2 hours after you arrive you get a test . then 3 hours later you'll get another test blood labs ? i am stating the obvious st .james closed and the administrations of this mega hospital are still giving this bullshit service .we pay up the nose for insurance and i felt last night i was in a third world country .

will update when they do something productive     it's been hours and she could be suffering a concussion or worse from the police brutality i witnessed her fall victim to.   sayreville police should be ashamed of themselves.

very poor triage decision making by person who you describe your symptoms to as you enter.

i described symptoms of stroke or heart attack. 
i waited for doctor after many children with flu like symptoms were taken  ahead of me . appears to be first come first serve.

after waiting 30 to 40 minutes doctor looked at me and decided i had stroke symptoms. sent me back to waiting room. i then heard announcement code stroke.er was now empty. i was diagnosed with mini stroketia. then i had tests. no room for 13 hours. very dangerous and life threatening triage.
fac_name: St John Medical Center Emergency Room

review: i'll just add my two cents to counter the one-star review. brought my wife into the er for a serious eye problem and while it was very expensive, as ers are, the care  was top notch.  my cousin also had a hip replacement here and was very happy with the entire experience.

this place is absolutely unreal.
every single person i know who has been here has had a ridiculously terrible experience. 
i was having problems breathing from being in so much pain after my wisdom teeth were removed, my oral surgeon is in santa rosa and told us to go to the er because of my issues breathing - i wish we had just gone to santa rosa. to start, the nurse was rude and condescending when asking me questions & then jabbing a thermometer into my mouth multiple times, roughly, after i told her i had gotten my wisdom teeth out two days prior. she then left without telling us the doctor would be in and we had to listen to them gossiping out at the desks for half an hour while we waited for the doctor, great. the doctor didn't give me absolutely any hint as to what may have been wrong; but instead decided to read me the riot act about how i should be "tapering off of the vicodin" (5 mg, administered twice a day) that i was on for less than 48 hours at the time. stop pushing your agenda onto other people. he told me i did not have dry sockets and guaranteed me that i was having a reaction to my meds. nobody ever addressed the fact that i was having issues breathing (other than the nurse condescendingly asking if i was having a panic attack) - had another nurse come in and take my blood pressure and then talk to me for another fifteen minutes about not taking anything but advil. went to my oral surgeon and found out within 30 seconds that i had dry sockets, which i had been told i didn't at the hospital. these people are absolute idiots, if you're not dying & able to go to another hospital do not go to this hospital 
update
update: 
this hospital has let down yet another family member! thank you for sonoma valley hospital for never ever providing quality of care, icu is the only place that has ever treated our family fairly, the skilled nursing unit is full of people who are incredibly unskilled and who do not care about the quality of care they provide! good job sonoma valley hospital, yet another disappointing visit!

update: 
had to visit again around a two months ago. i am petrified of needles and had to get blood drawn. the nurse decided that the best way to "help me get over" my fear of needles was to show me every single step of what he was doing - even as i was in tears and my boyfriend was telling me to just focus away from the needle. he took the entire piece apart from a new bag and showed me and explained every step to me and showed me all the needles. it was absolutely unacceptable. more than twice my mom and boyfriend who were in the room told him i didn't want to look, and i, completely pale and in tears asked him to stop. he wouldn't. i ended up scarring from that blood draw, as he did such a poor job, i didnt move once. it was an absolute nightmare. this hospital continues to get worse with every visit.
please do not consider sending anyone here.   it was a true nightmare that i found myself in.    no counseling.     homicidal people in with non-homicidal people.   dirty.

my daughter was admitted 48 hours ago for an over dose of ativan. she also has severe narcolepsy. since being in she has only gotten 1 of her depression meds and ativan! nothing to keep her awake so that she can participate in order to get the help she needs or even been seen by the doc who has to write for narcolepsy meds. she hasn't gotten any of her other depression meds and i get no info from any of the staff. not a good first impression! so far no stars from me

have been going to this hospital for a few years and i have never received poor service.  there are a lot of patients and it takes time for the doctors and staff to get to everyone. longer than normal wait times are going to happen there and in many other medical facilities. it doesn't mean they don't care. unexpected things can happen where the doctor may get called away or a certain patient may need a little longer care than usual. emergencies happen, delays happen.  no, i do not work for the va but i am a disabled veteran.  thank you for your time.
this place is great. he was called shortly after arriving in the er. the nurses examined him quickly and the doctor didn't take forever to see him.

two stars is about right.  and only that because there are actual doctors here.   the nurses walk around like they're in a fashion show.  i've never seen so much sashaying, slipper dragging behavior outside of someone's sunday morning bedroom.  

don't need anything.  you will wait.  and wait some more.  the staff appears to be completely unaccountable.  poor record keeping, no one knows anyones last name.   medication distribution is haphazard. 

if you have a choice, you might be better off somewhere else.  i hate to think this is a standard in our country's medical care.

i had an ms collapse  in church i wish no one had called 911.   over 30 years we've had to make visits to the er and was very satisfied.   place was near empty on a saturday at 4 pm. 
i think i was partially delirious due to low blood sugar after looking at the final blood tests.  i was treated like a pin cushion for practice three sticks in the left arm three sticks in the right before they finally brought someone that knew what they were doing. a nurse tried to supervise these green smocked techs they should practice on each other before getting near patients.  
nice doctor was going to have me transferred to kaiser i am a member and i love them.  
at 6 pm the nurse said night shift is taking over and i was given no call button.  a urine analysis had been ordered and i was given us an iv drip.   after an hour i called out with no answer and had to carry the iv bag to the bathroom with great difficulty due to my ms relapse for having no one look at me for an hour.   i had disconnected the heart monitor that was beeping constantly and no one came.   
luckily i had my phone and was able to call my son will eventually pick me up at 8 pm i was given no food and sip of water water, had money i would gladly paid for a coke or anything.   
when we got to the car my son gave me a sip of sweetened iced tea and i instantly felt much better. 
this is just my experience hope yours goes better.
my mother got superb care at this hospital.  they coordinated with her doctor at johns  hopkins and were very thorough.  nurses and other staff outstanding too!
stay away from this er!!! nurses joking at the front desk, being rude to very sick patients, people leave after long hours of not being seen! stay away from this hospital! worse customer care ever!

i've heard just about every good or bad thing about veteran hospitals. this one i will not be using. i tried for 2 months to get an eye exam. they said due to me being in bowling green they would have an optometrist in bg call me and set up an appointment within 10 days. two weeks later i contacted the optometrist they said would call me. the optometrist stated they did not have a signed contract enabling them to see veterans. i called the va back, they said they would again have a a dr. call me again in 10 days.. that was a month and a half ago! i also needed a hearing test. the va clinic in bg said that they had walk appointments on tuesdays and gave me the times. when i called nashville to double check i was told was for hearing aid repair drop off only. the next open appointment was over two months away! i'm so glad so many vets like this place, but for me i wish that this va hospital cared a little bit more for vets who have placed their lives on the line for this country.

they took amazing care of my 2 month old, the pediatric center is amazing with incredible nurses and doctors. i'm so happy with everything my son received while being admitted. they listened and cared. i would recommend the pediatric unit to anyone i know. thank you beaumont for making the medical care truly about the health care of our children and not profit. 

i had to bump down the stars even though i love the children's unit and give it 5 stars, the 4th floor center is a nightmare. it's supposed to be a step down unit from the icu but it seems like a step down from death. they are so uncaring, unprofessional, and just make the entire situation and hospital stay more demeaning.

the neurology center there 8 th floor south side is also wonderful. i guess it all depends on the unit. this is just based from my eoe

i had to have an outpatient procedure done. it took about 45 minutes for me to check in to the point where they started my anesthesia. the whole procedure took about an hour.

i was initially checked in and waited in a room, not far from the entrance. i had to be called again to be given a tag for my wrist and then put into another waiting area. i was put into a waiting room to change before they called me into another room, where i was laid down to be giving my anesthesia. 
remember sitting in the waiting room cold, since i had just had a gown on only. 
the procedure went pretty quickly. that was nothing as far as pain went, the pain when i got all the bills. they kept coming for a couple months. it's never good to have to get any surgery and be at a hospital, even if it's outpatient.

i've also had to have a cat scan done here in the past, that's done in another building. that intake and process seemed much quicker and more efficient than actual surgery.

i get that this is one of the larger hospitals in michigan. it always feels so cold, it's all about profit and the staff act so indifferent.

i really try to avoid going to the hospital, then again don't we all

the only advantage of this hospital is that it's so close to my house. there's no other closer hospital than this one.

when i originally posted this review in may, it was a positive experience.  however, what i didn't expect was the horrible billing practices that they have here. i came in for the 7 for $70 heart and vascular program and expected that when i paid for my services upon completion of the tests  i was all set.  i was wrong.  i have since received bills for all the 7 services separately and have had to constantly call them to fix their billing problem because their systems are disparate.  what is alarming is that it means that their information is not linked together for a single patient, what is also scary is that most health systems should have a single patient record.  if they can't keep track of a persons labs and know it's one person, how are they tracking their medical care?  how will the specialists administer treatment without complications because often treatments are delivered by different departments and different specialists? so does that mean that medical data disparate too?  regardless, this experience has reaffirmed why i stopped going to beaumont for services 20 years ago when they made a mistake on me.  it appears it hasn't changed at all.  the irony is that this was a heart screening and this whole process is giving me blood pressure and chest pains.

worst experience ever!!!

brought my wife to the er because she was having stomach pain. the pain level was a 10. there seems to be no since of urgency with the er staff. ask the front desk for to give me a time table when they would be able to see her. they keep telling me that they are trying and they were every busy. at the same time my wife is screaming in pain.  finally few other people spoke up and they took her in. inside, they made us wait another hour. now we are approaching 3 hours of waiting. the service was unacceptable and they treated us like just a number. very disappointed.

worst place to go for an emergency... 4 hours and counting... i've never experienced anything like this.

i've had three experiences with beaumont's er over the past twenty years. two were minor home accidents that required some suturing, and the third was a gall bladder attack that required emergency surgery. i've always been treated well there, and over the years i've observed a lot of improvements in both the physical infrastructure and the quality of care. on my last visit i showed up just before midnight on christmas day (!) when the er was very short staffed, and it did take me a while to get pain meds- points off for that. but once the necessary staff were available, i was quickly admitted and scheduled for surgery the following morning. that morning i was visited before surgery by both the surgeon and anesthesiologist, both of whom took time to explain what was going on, and to ask if i had any questions. following surgery, the nursing care i received was exemplary, and the follow-up care at the hospital was very good as well.

there is a total lack of communication between departments at beaumont. as patients get passed from one department to the next, they are given incorrect information about the time things will take.  when the "receiving" department is told the timing that the previous department indicated they blame the other department saying "they should have never said that." with the exception of the gi pa (tara karmo) who stuck to what she promised and got back with me in the 15 mins she said she would, all others failed.

my saga...

beaumont urgent care sent me to beaumont emergency due to a possible foreign object in my throat and to get my throat scoped.  i arrived around 3:00 pm in the afternoon.  at the time, there was not a line for checking, but there was a number of people waiting.  after waiting about an hour and a half, i was taken to triage where i was asked a few questions and was told by that person i would be taken to er shortly.  an hour later or so later, i was taken to er and was told they wanted to do a cat scan rather than a scope.  at that time, i was told the wait would be about an hour.  3+ hours later, i was taken for a cat scan. the cat can people said i would get the results within the hour.  4 hours later, around midnight, someone came to take me to my room  as they were admitting me ????

when i questioned this the response was "hasn't anyone talked to you?"  when the resident did talk to me, she indicated that nothing came up on the cat scan and they needed to scope my throat (which is why i was there in the first place) and all the ent people were gone by then.  i asked if i could just make an appointment for the next morning and come back for the scope and they said if i left, they wouldn't be able to get me in. so, i asked for them to confirm that if i stayed, someone would be able to do the scope first thing in the morning.  they assured me they would do it first thing in the morning.  i finally had the scope done around 1:30 pm.
around 3:30, the gi pa (tara karmo) told me that the ents did not see anything on the scope, but the scope wasn't able to see into the esophagus. the ent wanted to do a barium swallow but she didn't think the test would give the information.  to get the right information, an endoscopy would be better. but, it was too late to get that done and i would need stay another night.  i said there was no way i was going to stay another night for a "timing issue" and we needed to come up with another option.  she said she'd get back to me within 15 minutes, and she did. she had some meds prescribed for me and got me an appointment at her office a few days later.

i was a patient at southside hospital in bayshore, ny after being airlifted from another suffolk county, ny hospital. upon my admittance, i was immediately relieved to meet a staff of doctors, nurses and support staff who were truly dedicated to their work. from my bed in icu, i was greeted by the kindest and most accommodating nurses who attended to my needs without delay. their reasonable manner in handling my complicated illness provided so much comfort that my body began to finally heal. i believe it was not only because of the medical treatment but also the emotional care that i received in icu and step down that truly healed me. after a total of 9 weeks in 2 hospitals and a rehab center, i finally returned home and i am so relieved that i am alive and well. thank you dear doctors, nurses and support staff of southside hospital.
