i have just finished six weeks of outpatient rehabilitation for a bi-lateral knee replacement at the rehab services department at broward health in coral springs. 
  
everything - from the warm and compassionate greeting from joanie who answered my initial, very  nervous call - to the sessions thrice, then twice, then single weekly sessions paul mcgowen have been noteworthy for his skill, compassion, encouragement  and knowledge of various physical therapeutic exercises.

understanding that i have made years of accommodations for my fused knees prior to my surgery, paul incorporated hip and lower back exercises into my pt plan.  he gave me exercises for home and followed up each session with a progress report.  he told me what to watch for - how to correct myself.  in short - he cared.

bhcs rehab consists of an incredible group of people - and for this, the program director, ms. pomerantz should be recognized.  she has put together an incredible team.  it was not unusual for any of the other therapists - edwin, amanda, allison and monica - to stop by me (either on the table or on a machine) to cheer me on.    youlanda was always ready provide heat and ice and tell me how great i was doing.

i have been to other facilities for physical therapy.  i know what it is to be treated as a case number.  i know what it is to be viewed as an insurance claim and nothing more.  this is not the case at broward health coral springs.  my experience with paul and his colleagues has completely "etch-a-sketched" those very negative experiences from my memory. 
 
my life has changed dramatically for the best - and i owe much of it to paul mcgowan and the rehab group at bhcs.  i thank them all.

hopefully you read this before going to the er, not after like i did.  reading some of the other reviews - similar things happened to me.

on friday february 28th at about 8:30pm my daughter and i took our 18 month old grandson to the emergency room on bee ridge and cattlemen.  

1.  my daughter was holding the baby who was crying - he had been bitten on the hand by a dog.
2.  the security guard never looked up from his computer and mumbled for us to sit down - "they know you're here."  we were the only people in the er, so i'm thinking "who knows we're here?"
3.  three women were behind a desk and did not make eye contact with us - no concern for a young woman holding a crying baby.  they just talked to each other - nobody told us anything.
4.  five minutes becomes 10 minutes and nobody said anything to us.
5.  after about 10-12 minutes a door marked triage opens and some patient comes out.  the triage nurse asked us to come in.
6.  she did not wash her hands, use purell, or wear gloves.
7.  she had to do all the typing to get us into the system (i guess the other three women were busy not helping)
8.  after about 15 questions - she finally asked why we were here.  we told her he had been bitten by a dog.
9.  when she reached for his hand - he of course screamed - so she reached for an unsanitized teddy bear on her desk and gave that to him to quiet him down.
10.  she dabbed the wound clean (did not rinse it) and moved us through some double doors into another waiting room with about six chairs - again we were the only people there.
11.  about another 10-15 minutes later a nurse came in and confirmed the baby's name.  then she asked us if he had a fever?  no?  a cough?  no?  we told her he had a dog bite.  (i wonder why she hadn't read the triage report??)
12.  she asked my daughter a dozen questions which had nothing to do with the dog bite, including vaginal or c-section delivery?  i'm guessing that is a priority when treating a dog bite.
13.  another 10 - 15 minutes and a doctor came into the room.  and here's where i started to question this whole operation.  he never came closer than 10 feet from the baby - never looked at the wound, let alone cleaned it.  from 10 feet away he then described what he was going to do - he was going to order an x-ray and then give us some antibiotics - because he told us without antibiotics the risk of infection is very high.
14.  another 10-15 minutes and a guy from x-ray came and told us he had been instructed to an x-ray of the right hand.  "is this _____?"  good guess!

did you ever see the movie zootpia where she has to go to the dmv to get her license?  that's what this experience brought to my mind.  they were like the sloths but without the smile and the compassion.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=drhsktakrzc 

15.  another 30 minutes and the nurse came back asking us what was happening.  that is when i got a little frustrated and asked her why the doctor had not even looked at the wound?  why hadn't the wound been cleaned?  she seemed to think that the doctor had looked at the wound.
16.  i could go on and on...

finally the nurse came back with the prescription for the antibiotic - it was now 11 at night.  i asked her if she could call in the prescription so it would be ready when we got there.  "we don't provide that service."

this is a perfect example of an organization which is driven by procedure - and has absolutely no focus on patients.  no compassion, no coordination, no communication.  the system these people work in has crushed their humanity - and this is with an empty er.

all the while i'm thinking to myself - "omg imagine if there was a corona virus outbreak in sarasota and there were five or six puking sick people in the er waiting room?  this hospital is completely unprepared to handle anything like that."

come to find out two days later that there was a corona virus patient in the hospital that night - and i thought back to the people not washing their hands, etc. etc.  i pray that my grandson, my daughter and i were not infected.  

and hannah b. don't respond "i am so sorry to hear about your experience..."  if you gave a damn, you would go to the er yourself and see what your customers see - it isn't pretty.  if you did care, it would either be fixed, or you wouldn't be working there.

review:
original review ~ dec 2019

my experience as a patient at kaiser permanente: in 2018, i scheduled a preventive care checkup with my primary care physician, collin reed, md when it was due. his office canceled my visit less than 24 hours in advance, leaving me unable to, instead, schedule a client in my business. i rescheduled my appointment with the doctor. and again: one of dr reed's assistants canceled less than 24 hours before the appointment. concerned about the delay i chose to meet with another physician in dr. reed's office. however, i was only allotted 5 minutes for an entire yearly check-up that year. come 2019, i again scheduled my annual checkup with dr. reed. as in 2018, his office canceled with less than 24 hours notice. two more times this year i scheduled with the collin reed, my primary care physician, and those appointments as well were canceled with insufficient notice to fill the allotted time with clients in my business. in total then, dr. reed cancelled five physical checkup appointments with less than 24 hours notice during 2018/19. i consequently incurred hundreds of dollars in lost income. if i ran my affairs as dr. reed handles his appointments, i would lose my business, and certainly my clients' confidence. the strong message of these events is that kaiser does not value patients' time. if the organization invested a quarter of

the money it spends on tv advertising on customer satisfaction, kaiser might run more productively.

update jan 27, 2020:

after registering a complaint with the member services team at kaiser for the series of canceled appointments with my primary care physician, (see below) i was assigned a representative. she told me that my experience with kaiser was 'abominable' and then asked me what kaiser could do to ameliorate the situation. i suggested to be reimbursed for my out-of-pocket expenses that resulted from the series of late cancellations. she got back to me a few weeks later with the happy news that i would be reimbursed for out-of-pocket expenses and that a check would be issued.

no check arrived for those expenses and the member services representative subsequently rescinded the promise to me in an encrypted e-mail.  one might imagine that maybe kaiser's law department reversed the decision, putting the member services representative in a bind. if that was the case, i would have appreciated an explanation of this fact. as it went, the retraction of the promise of reimbursement for out-of-pocket costs was cold and without explanation. after announcement of the reversal of reimbursement, i reached out to the representative through e-mail and voice mail and there was no response. i have no insight as to what caused this reversal.

i have been dealing with kaiser for a few years now because i am a caregiver to a family member with kaiser. i wish my family member did not choose kaiser.   like most businesses, it's hard to find good customer service or service nowadays.  there are a few "gems" who work at kaiser, but there are also a bunch of duds, from nurse aides to doctors to administrators. 

here are a few examples of the recent/past negative experiences (it's getting worse):  

1.  we had a cardiologist who went mia (he was here one day, and abruptly left back to the mainland...). there's more on this cardiologist....tmi      it's not easy to see a cardiologist--problems hiring/retaining.

2.  a fiscal office who hounds family members to pay the bill for elderly family member.  no kidding--most recently, a kaiser employee "happened" to be near my family member's er room and offered to escort/follow us out of the er only to demand payment for the er visit, cat scan, etc. before we could exit with our (still) sick family member--no invoice seen, but demands $$$!!!  family member did not expect to go to the er as it was an "emergency" so $ was not transferred and was not ready for payment. soooooo they looked at others to pay the bill for our family member!   we were told blood tests will be invoiced.  the family member has never been delinquent $.    kaiser has no shame$$$ and seems to care more about $$$!!  

does kaiser hound the emtala patients? #harassment

3.  a fiscal office calls family members (goes down the next-of-kin list, power of attorney, etc.) to call to pay the invoice for a current hospital stay for a family member before leaving the hospital--kaiser likes to equate it to a doctor's visit copayment.  no invoice. see #2 $$$$$$$ 

how does one know this is a "verified" caller from kaiser asking for a credit card# over the phone?  see #4 how do i get on the "no call" list?

4. a family member with power of attorney cannot email kaiser on behalf of a family member's account, but has to "jump through hoops" to set up a (so called "verified") separate account to email kaiser on behalf of the family member.  yet, it's okay for doctors, nurses, social workers, patient coordinators to call/speak/meet with the family member with power of attorney.  yet it's okay for the fiscal office to call family member with power of attorney for payment...just not email. who's to say who we are via email, phone, or  in-person?!

5.  we were once assigned a clinic doctor so perplexed with family member's ongoing health symptoms that "hospice" was this recommended solution instead of any attempts to fix the health issues. 

6.  where can a non kaiser member file a complaint, comment or suggest improvements on behalf of a family member?  better yet, try getting someone at kaiser who cares about what you think!!!  you are at kaiser's mercy and cannot just go to another doctor, hospital, etc.--and kaiser knows this! you are just a number--pick a number.  what quality assurance?

concerns fall on deaf ears--so get the word out and yelp it or post it online. otherwise "what happens in kaiser stays in kaiser!"

7.  it's not hard to find sassy/rude nurses in ambulatory, patient care coordination, etc....  instead of practicing "health" and "wellness" --it seems as though kaiser adds to the stress of patients and (for sure) the stress of family members.  lack of communication and lack of trust does not help.

i (unwantingly) know my family member's hospital roommate's name, date of birth, medications, medical conditions, doctors, visitors, etc.

i love kaiser permanente as our health care provider! they are all in one , i can even book a few different appointments one after another on the same day at moana loa or koolau. the staff are always so nice, my primary dr. is dr mia hawkins at koolau and she is amazing! so is dr. patel & gyn dr lawrence.  our eye doctor michelle okabe in waipio is so nice & a sweetheart. my ortho is dr. santi for my knee, dr. matthews for my hand & dr. vasconcelos for sports med. dr. santi runs a great ortho dept and his assistant claudia is awesome & caring. dr. greninger in general surgery has been a surgeon since 1985, pa sara palm is young, nice & patient. the icu nurses are the best in their field. peter q. is so nice & good with his patients and their families & brian h. & luis p. are also good. i've brought my dad several times to er and they are very efficient. i've had quite a few operations as you can tell with my knowledge with the staff lol and everyone is attentive and very nice.  and believe it or not their hospital food is so good it really is!  check-in is quick & they have a self serve stand if there's a line. nice gift shop, cafeteria ok, the vending coffee is too expensive, i usually get mine at the outside stand paradise coffee stand. moa has farmers market, i think on wednesdays. the only complaint i have is that i wish they had more handicapped stalls you would think being a hospital they would. and that they revamp the kailua clinic. i would definitely recommend kaiser as you're primary health provider.

this is one review i wish i didn't have to make, but my adult daughter came down with severe abdominal pains and due to the hour i had to bring her to the er. i drove up to the er entrance and was assisted by a security staff member who made sure she got up to the check-in desk while i parked the car.

parking was a breeze and when i walked back into the er lobby, i was pleased to see that the staff was already getting her information and vitals. once they were done, she was assigned to an exam room where more questions and tests awaited her.

throughout her time in the exam room, she was visited by no less than 4 employees for administration of iv and meds, lab work, escort to x-ray, etc. everyone was extremely professional and constantly checking to see how she was holding up. we were there for at least 2.5 hours, and to be honest it felt a lot shorter.

it's experiences like these that make me proud to be a kp client.

love/hate relationship with this place. husbands eczema flared up pretty bad friday evening. (his face was super red and swollen!) we called to make an appointment with after hours but they were booked. so we opted to seek advice. first person we spoke to transferred us to a nurse, who then told us she was gonna talk to the doctor. was on hold for a bit and nurse says a doctor would call us back. guess what? no calls....


saturday morning we called again to make an appt. they asked what was wrong and whatnot and person said she was gonna send his symptoms to a doctor and a doctor would call back to make an appointment... well, we did not get any call back and at this point i was getting annoyed because my husband was miserable. i opted to take him to their damn er instead because i was tired of waiting. thankfully they weren't busy and i was finally glad he got seen and was given steroids! now i would just hate for the damn bill to come in.

the er visit would have been avoided if they just called back or made an appt. right away!

my experience with kaiser in 2019 was the worst. in the year 2020 i will be changing my insurance to hmsa. never going back to kaiser! keeping it short since my review keeps getting removed. keep your children away from kaiser. they will have your child taken away by child protective services based on their poor judgments. don't go to doctor saba russel md of kaiser moanalua emergency room. he simply has a poor judgment especially the pediatrician he works with who is a woman with a tattoo on her arm pierced nose and lips. unprofessional!!!! do not trust your kids with these kaiser moanalua doctors!!!!

the doctors and nurses are very friendly but my mom was recently admitted here which is not her first choice of hospital but due to the circumstances it was the nearest. anyhow, my family and i were told of course there is no sleeping in the icu which is understandable they told us we were welcome to "camp out" in the waiting area which they said was really nice. when we got to the waiting room i was appalled at the way this place looked and they expect  family to be comfortable. icu family members are already under enough stress  as it is but it's like kaiser said f your comfort. the waiting area was dirty and had bugs crawling everywhere, the chairs were worn. i have previously been a meme bet of kaiser and the amount of money you pay for medical is through the roof!!!! then to have to wait in a disgusting waiting room is beyond belief. i have posted pictures i wish there was a way to post video.

this review is directed towards the er only. i only gave them 1 star because i had too. i would give them negative stars if possible. my stepfather was very sick and took himself to a clinic. the clinic immediately called an ambulance to take him to the hospital. they feared he had a blood infection or septic. 

upon arrival at the hospital, the emt removed the fluid bag from his iv and said he will be hooked up right away. when you arrive in an ambulance you are supposed to be given a room immediately. the er made my stepfather wait in the waiting room for 3.5 hours! they left the iv in his arm unhooked so all the blood clotted in the tube so bad they couldn't get it out. he actually walked over to the cancer center to be able to lay down and the er nurses had no idea where he went. they lost a patient and didn't call any codes.

my mom arrived to help him and she had to walk around the hospital to look for my stepdad. the nurses didn't even attempt to look. once she found him and took him back to the er they made him go into the segregation room, where my mom had to push tables together for him to lay on and covered him up with her coat, because he was freezing. my stepdad has severe back issues so laying on anything other than a bed is excruciating. 

after 3.5 hours, they finally got him back in a bed in the er and started running an iv. he should have had one when he got there! he was extremely dehydrated and due to this, his calcium levels were critically high, threatening a heart attack or cardiac arrest. his kidney functions were also down due to the dehydration. once my stepdad was put on a regular floor he was taken care of. he stayed for 2 days and was released. he had a severe case of influenza a.

once you get to a regular floor in the hospital you can expect to be taken care of. however, the er is a joke. they don't care one bit about the patients and half of the nurses should be fired. i understand most people are just trying to get drugs. but if someone comes in there dying, maybe they should actually do their jobs.

sports med clinic review: 

i just sat in the waiting room at the hot springs for my appointment for physical therapy. after 41 minutes of waiting i could no longer wait anymore and left. i called the main office to explain what had happened. they were sympathetic and offered me the next available appointment but i had re arranged my entire day to accommodate this appointment... very unprofessional, they shouldn't have opened a second locattion where they don't have someone working the front desk in order to tell the therapist that they have someone waiting. very disappointed by this because i've seen them before and they were great but i will not support a business that operates in this fashion!

been here a number of times and feel it is really a wonderfully managed and organized health center. the 300-bed facility is built on 130-some acres of property, and replaces the old silver cross hospital that used to be in joliet. 

as you approach, the main building is the hospital center, and on its right is a separate but connected building that houses most of the testing and other diagnostic capabilities. nicely organized in keeping testing away from the busier hospital itself. we utilized the testing rooms, and felt the scheduling and organization was perfect.

have also had occasion to visit patients in the hospital and it is clean, roomy, wide-aisled, and up-to-date in almost every area (it opened in 2012). it seems that most every room is now a private one. this hospital is an anchor in will county, and is easy to get to in being right off i-355. 

never had the opportunity or need to use the emergency care facility so don't have a comment on it, but understand that it is a level ii trauma center. this is a nice addition to the area and a wonderful replacement for the old joliet facility.

yay. very nice staff all the way around. been here three days and not a single bad exchange with any staff member. from checking in to being discharged this has been the smoothest visit to any hospital around. it amazes us that there are so many negative reviews (mostly emergency room and at night though).

this place is a joke. came here by ambulance otherwise i would  have gone to loyola. i have a disease called pseudotumor cerebri. i came in with migraines and urine problems. they help with the migraine but when my bladder started acting a fool they refused. i'm in massive pain and they don't care. next time it's loyola. when i asked for a social work they told me they leave at 3. doubt that. never again will i come here.

price gouging!!!  watch your money! a single shot x-ray of a wrist cost $236 on 7/5/19.  i was just billed $641 for the same exact x-ray done on 1/24/20.  called customer service - useless.  referred to "price quotes" department for an explanation, also useless.  all they say is "i don't know" or "that's way above me."  no one knows anything so why is there a number for billing questions?  and why are you answering the phone? i was always a big fan of this place, telling everyone it was great, but not any more.  how do you increase the price of a routine, regularly scheduled x-ray 172% and not even mention it? it is shocking how unhelpful and unsympathetic these people are.

waiting 2 hours and my daughter is in pain. they say there's nothing  they can do , we have to wait. she is two months pregnant and bleeding and in pain and the check in person , nicole , says we have to wait! this is the worst experience i have ever had with a hospital. i will be contacting the hospital administrator in the morning.
wouldn't even post 1 star if it was an option. they don't know what they are doing at this hospital and my family will never forget the horrifying experience they had.

organization is terrible. they told my pregnant girlfriend that they would give us a call when they had a room available so that she could be induced. we get the call around 10:30pm that her room is ready so we get everything we need and drive over. once we got there we found ourselves sitting in the waiting room for nearly 2 hours! so there we were sitting in the waiting room with all of our stuff and my 9 month pregnant girlfriend miserable in these uncomfortable waiting chairs. next time give us a call when you actually have a room instead of making a pregnant woman sit in the waiting room for 2 hours in the middle of the night. 

update: once we finally got in and got a room the service of the nurses was great. the over all experience wasn't terrible, the only down fall was that we had to come back and fourth about 3 times before we actually got into a room. but besides that the doctors and the nurses were great and they took really good care of us. now we have a healthy baby at home. over all myself and my girlfriend are pretty satisfied with our experience.

this for profit hospital is not a choice i would recommend. i've had two admissions for possible strokes. they lost my housecoat i wore on the ambulance and take no responsibility. they show on an hourly basis why medical mistakes is the third leading cause of death in america. my meds were wrong daily. it was a circus but not a fun one.

mca is awful. if you don't have insurance they dont care about you. doctor acted like he did not care about anything i had to say. gave me zero blood work. treated me for an allergic reaction after they told me i wasn't having one. i left this hospital with no answers, throat still left like it was closing up and all they gave me was some benadryl and prescribed me a steroid that caused me to have anxiety, depression, heart palpitations and many more side effects that has caused me to go to back to the hospital (i went to somewhere instead).  they weren't concerned because my airways were clear but was not willing to get to the root of the problem.

after 6 months of pregnancy, i went in for a 8:45am appointment for my 6 month check up. after seeing this hospital for six months they suddenly decide to tell me that they don't accept my insurance .  i questioned them, and they told me they had never accepted my form of insurance. i had medicaid cooks, and suddenly they wouldn't accept it after many many visits to their doctors office with no issues . i've heard about a lot of problems with this hospital from peers. find a better hospital .
horrible go to the west side if you can. waited 4 hours just to talk to someone and it wasnt even that busy everyone was rude

my husband and i traveled to arizona to see my 88 year old aunt! she is great  but my husband contacted pneumonia and a secondary infection, so was admitted to banner del webb medical center. what a fantastic experience! john received excellent care, knowledgeable professionals, excellent  food and a private room. we were lucky this happened in the vicinity of banner del webb medical center! thank you for your kind care!

review: allow me to introduce myself as a registered nurse, board certified by the american board of quality and utilization review. i attended the care of an 86 year old alert and oriented senior who came to this emergency department for relief of pain in her prosthetic hip. she remained in the emergency room from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. during those eight hours, she was never assessed for pain, nor was she offered or administered pain medication. the physician appropriately ordered a ct scan, blood work and a urinalysis. eventually, a young female physician reported to my friend that the ct scan revealed two hematomas, typically caused by a fall / trauma. my friend had experienced neither. following the initial ct scan, the same transport person came to my friend's cubical to transport her to a repeat ct scan. there was only one ct scan ordered, and it had been done. in addition, the rn suggested a straight catheterization urinalysis. i suggested that my friend first try to provide a voided urine sample, which she did. the rn chose not to respond to my friend's call light, which was  "blinking" for quite some time.  the rn reported that the original specimen had been "misplaced". huh? then, it was found. excuse me?  my friend remained in the same position for eight hours, more than enough time for a pressure ulcer to develop. i requested water and for some sort of nourishment to be provided. finally, she was given a dry turkey sandwich that had to have been days old. it was embarassing and disgusting.  at del webb,  seniors are disposable. my counsel would be to get the hell out of that hospital ed as quickly as possible.

review: this is the absolute worst hospital ever! i brought my 12 year old daughter here because she was having stomach pain.  the nurse asked her if she was sexually active. my daughter told her no. the dumb nurse then asked my daughter if she has ever had anal sex!!!! my daughter looked at me confused and asked me what that was. she also told my daughter that the doctor would most likely have to do an inappropriate exam on her. we were both wondering why this idiotic nurse only thought that this could be a sexual problem. my daughter got nervous. the doctor came in after a very long wait and started asking my daughter questions. nothing sexual or inappropriate.  i told him what the nurse had asked and also told him what inappropriate test that the nurse said that he would do.  his face turned red and said that it wasn't something that he does and wasn't planning on doing that.  the doctor said that he couldn't figure out what was wrong with my daughter and that she should see another doctor to follow up.  they had poked her with an iv needle and we waited 30 minutes for the liquid. i asked one of the nurses how much longer it would take for the liquid and he with attitude told me that if the doctor ordered it my daughter should get it soon. we waited another 30 minutes and still no liquid. i walked out and asked another nurse when she will get the liquid because she was in pain. she also had an attitude problem and said that it should be soon. 1 hour later the idiotic nurse from the beginning walked in and i told her that what she told us wasn't true about the test and she laughed it off like a dumb b! i told her that we were still waiting for the iv and she said that she thinks that the doctor didn't order it. the doctor then came and said that he forgot and that he would order it now. ummmmm really??????? 1 hour later and no damn liquid for her iv! i told the nurse that my daughter was in pain and tired and to get the damn needle out of her arm.  we walk out and we're were told that we needed to pay $1200! for the f'ed up service??????? wow! i told her that i had insurance and she told me with the insurance it was $1200. i asked her what a cash patient would be paying and she said $900. i said then consider me a cash patient and we received the worst service. they are so lucky that i didn't sue them. i took my daughter to another doctor that was able to figure out her problem without it becoming sexual.  this hospital should be closed down. i called and complained several times and was told i should also call other departments, but anytime i called back i would be told that they never received my complaints. they supposedly had no idea that i had complained and one of the idiots told me that those were normal questions that the nurse was asking. one more thing!!! i had asked for an itemized bill and one of the charges was $250 for a pregnancy test on a child that has never had sex!

even  acknowledging my concern . she prescribed me acetaminophen codeine and muscles relaxers . i had been taking for days already with no relief!!! ( which i told her) ( and i hate taking pain pills !!! i do have a job) ...  so , i was sent home with the written rxs and still in pain !!!! i called the bcbs doctors visit line when i got home .  the dr there said there is a good change it is

thank you crystal for being so nice to us you really helped my nervousness you are awesome

my wife has known epilepsy. normally she only goes to the er if her seizure lasts for more than a certain time or doesn't respond to her rescue medication. she was taken to medical city alliance after a seizure at work. a coworker who didn't know her history took her to mca. still agitated and confused from her seizure medical city alliance made her check out against medical advice because she refused a pregnancy test, that she had no chance of being pregnant (abstinence) and no intervention/surgery was being done that required a test. another question, why would you want someone who was brought in for a seizure,because of a interaction with another medication, up walking around your hospital for the sake of a pee test. seems like a liability to me if she were to fall. if you wanted a pregnancy test that bad, why didn't you do it when you did all the blood work. it was literality for more money. if you want to run to the cvs down the road and get a cheap pee test, sure i'll have her pee on it, but not for what mca charges. when my wife said no, nurse said " okay well you will have to leave ama if you refuse the pregnancy test and handed her the paper minutes later. when you go online and read the so called "doctor's report" it states that the physician came back in to explain the risks of leaving ama. he came in once at the beginning of her visit and never came back. her nurse was the one that informed us that her lab work came back good. that report is bs. nurses were rude. hospital is dirty. never asked about medication. another time i took her for a migraine before this seizure event and they wanted a pregnancy test. she refused and said she didn't need to go, had no chance of being pregnant (abstinence)and nurse's response was "we will just load you up on fluids until you can give a sample" are you kidding me??? review:

she's amazing. she even came to visit me in recovery & gave me a hug. she has so much passion for what she does and she is right where she needs to be in life. since i progressed quickly after my epidural my doc didn't make it so the laborist on call delivered me. i  didn't catch her name but she was awesome too! on the postpartum side i'd like to thank dr. abdulla and dr. lamotte for performing a frenotomy on my baby at just hours old so it didn't effect breast feeding/latching. all the staff made sure to accommodate  us with anything we needed/ wanted. they fed my hubby each day we stayed so he never once had to leave our side and they also gave us a celebration  dinner with steak, shrimp, a baked potato, a bunt cake along with two bottles of sparking cider. the kitchen staff was amazing and so kind and all the food was on point. i have nothing negative to say about my experience. i will have all my babies here in a heartbeat. thank you for making our experience unforgettable while we welcomed our double rainbow baby into the the  world.

this review is for labor and delivery/maternity/triage

we arrived around 2am ish??? on sunday. the security helped us find a wheelchair and we were off to the second floor! the two front desk ladies were really accommodating and made it all as easy as possible for us to check in. insurance and all. i was wheeled to triage as soon as someone could come to get us and although i was in pain and it seemed as though time was going so slow, it was quicker than i thought it would be. but i was lucky enough that it wasn't busy at all that night. 

one of my biggest fears was waking my husband up in the middle of the night only to go and be told i wasn't dilated enough. so i waited until i just couldn't handle it anymore and i was 2.5 min at least in between contractions. everyone is different though so make sure to call ahead and ask to speak to a nurse. 

this isn't our normal hospital, nor have we been seen here ever so there was no record of our labs or anything. i was taken care of swiftly in triage. they were patient, kind and patient even though deep inside i felt pretty irritable being in pain. they tried to pull up some of my records but the system was down for the place i get my labs done at. they took all my test right then and there at triage. i was definitely in labor and they found me a room. 

the room was intimidating at first because all i could think of was "this is it! this is the place!" anyways, to keep this part short, i wasn't progressing and i was in so much pain so i was slowly induced and got the epidural. i pushed for a few minutes and bam. we had our baby and it was almost pain free compared to the contractions. the cramping and the stinging on the few stitches i got were far worse after the epidural was done. 

we were there long enough to see two shifts and they were both amazing. both doctors, all the nurses, even though i was getting kind of rude from not being able to eat while waiting to dilate all the way. (sorry everyone) it was amazing and i wouldn't have had the experience  anywhere else. 

recovery room, great. you get shown more than a few times on how to breastfeed your baby if you're there long enough which is nice in my opinion because i hate asking questions but they really make sure you can do it so you are a confident momma when you leave. you get the tools you need for using the restroom, and for when your baby uses the restroom. they even provided blankets and pillows for my husband and included him on everything.

i have had a number of bad run-in's with the health system here in the central coast, but i have also had some good ones so i have always held off posting anything.
my interaction this past week changed that completely though.
back story - i have been on topiramate for around 3 years, which for anyone who has never encountered this medication, is an extremely expensive medication with horrible withdrawal effects and not very fun side effects. one 30 day supply costs me around $250 since i got laid off and lost my insurance. i can't afford that and don't want to stop cold turkey so i have been trying to wean myself off since december. (i was on 400 mg).
on thursday night, i had a partial focal seizure. i was awake for the whole thing, screaming but could not stop myself, it was by far the most terrifying thing i have ever dealt with. i couldn't think straight after for the next 24 hours.
my partner called 911 and they asked me to go with them to the er because i couldn't stand without getting extremely dizzy and my blood pressure dropping.
i was in the er until 6 am, and the doctor tested me for a uti. and then told me i fainted because i have a blood pressure issue.
i would like to hit on the point again that i was in no place to advocate for myself, and neither was my partner. he didn't fully know what happened, and i couldn't think straight. i couldn't even explain it fully to my partner for 2 days. but this doctor decided, despite being told i was getting off a medication that has been known to cause seizures, and that i had a seizure like episode that i might have had a uti and blood pressure issues. (spoiler, i didn't have a uti).
he kept coming into the room to ask me "if i was ready to go yet", like i was enjoying having a nurse watch me pee when i needed to go. finally, we just left because it was obvious that he was not going to help and i was exhausted.
i am terrified to see the bill for this useless trip. i only know what kind of seizure i had from my own research. i don't know if it hurt me at all, seeing as i was awake the whole time, or if anything else happened.
that doctor doesn't care at all. it makes me sad. if i have another seizure, i'll just let it play out and hope i survive. that's all that will happen if i go to the hospital, except they will charge me money if i do.

i was the support person for my daughter's recent labor and delivery. the labor and delivery service was mostly good, but the time after the delivery was awful.
we came to the delivery room around midnight and my daughter delivered at 2:30 with an uncomplicated natural childbirth with no pain medication. the delivery was very smooth and the dr. was skilled and personable. i thought it was a wonderful delivery.

because i was my daughter's support person, i was there for the entire 31 hours after delivery. and this is my story. 

we got in the recovery room about 4 and the nurses began their protocol of patient care. my daughter was not allowed to sleep more than 2 hours at a time, plus she was caring and feeding her newborn. nurses continued to wake her up over and over for some sort of patient care, that was in my opinion mostly unnecessary. at one point a nurse came in to wake her up and ask her if she wanted a pain pill. where is the common sense in that?
i got her out of there as quick as possible because she needed rest after being exhausted by delivery. she guesses she got 3 hours of sleep in the 31 hours she was there after delivery. perhaps this is a way to get new mothers out as soon as possible?

the sad thing is many new parents don't realize how abusive this protocol is and just accept it as normal. even the lactation specialist i complained to said she had her baby at home for that exact reason. a natural, un-medicated delivery is a normal part of life. and in my opinion the hospital's patient care is abusive.

we all joke that new parents are sleep deprived, but in the hours after delivery a new mother should be allowed to sleep if baby will let them. i worry about other mothers who may have had complication. they need the rest more than anyone and i know they will be denied rest by hospital patient care. 

we asked to be left alone for a few hours for sleep. the staff agreed then just continued on with all the things they are required to do. 

we left a day early so my daughter could come home and get some rest and she has been doing that. she would have liked to stay the full time because she has another child to care for and she is a single mother, but she told me she was so exhausted, that she needed to leave. she said she couldn't keep her eyes open and i saw that every time her eyes closed she would immediately be asleep. how is a person that exhausted able to care for a newborn or even herself?

i'm sorry for anyone who delivers at a hospital especially this one.  patients are trusting your hospital with their health and a very very important part of health is rest.

review:
in feb 2019 i went to stanford for a small surgery for a hiatal hernia that started at 1:00 pm. i woke up from the surgery about 6pm in tremendous pain in my neck and shoulders.  they gave me something right away that helped me sleep, but wore off after a few hours. at 10:30pm, i woke up again in pain, i asked for more pain meds but was told i had to wait till 1am. by the time the night nurse showed up at 1:30 am, i was sobbing in pain and not able to move! at one point, they missed the vein and the pain meds created an egg sized bulge in my arm. ultimately the surgeon had me stay an extra day because my pain wasn't under control.

during the 2nd day the day nurses were wonderful, took very good care of me, they were responsive cheerful and i was always comfortable. i couldn't have asked for anything more.

however at night, it was a nightmare! the 2nd night i asked for the same pain meds as they gave me during the day, but they refused. even the charge nurse refused to give me pain meds and never called the attending. she seemed annoyed that i even asked. i had asked the night nurse  for a schedule of when i would get pain meds as i wanted to know if i had to last 1 hour in pain or 3 hours. she refused to tell me. the night nurse told me in front of the charge nurse if i was asleep, i was fine and she wouldn't wake me to give me pain meds.  the second night after surgery i went 8 hours with no pain meds at all. zero! needless to say, i crashed and ended up in severe pain the morning of the 3rd day.

when the attending dr. showed up the morning of the 3rd day, he told me if i needed any pain meds, just ask the nurse. i told him they weren't giving pain meds at night but during the day it was a different story. he checked the chart and his eyes got very big, he then made sure i was comfortable! i would have been better off going home the second day where i could have gotten care. i know it may sound like i am some kind of addict, but i actually don't like opioids and got off them as soon as i could. but they were a necessary part of being able to heal.  

if you go to have surgery, understand what the plan of care is, how the communication amongst the staff works, who is in charge of your plan of care, how to make a request if you need something and who your advocate is. i regret i didn't ask more questions. once i was in the hospital bed, i was treated like a non-person by the night nurses, an annoyance when i asked for help and dismissed when i was in pain. it was a terrifying experience to be so unable to take care of yourself and have the night nurse staff have total control of keeping you in pain or relieving your pain, and not have any recourse.

i read that women are often dismissed when they are in pain. i can sadly say that was the case for me at stanford, but only at night!

this review is for maternity care and child birth

on 26th december 2019, me and my husband were blessed with a baby girl at the stanford valley care hospital in dublin, ca. 

i was admitted to the hospital on the morning of 12/25/2019 when my water broke.

our daughter was born on 12/26/2019 in the afternoon. experience so far was good. we were discharged on 12/28/2019 in the afternoon around 1:00 pm only to return to emergency at 5:00 pm. that morning we had informed the staff that the baby is not fed almost the entire night. apart from not taking the feed, the baby was crying inconsolably all night. we called the staff multiple times, but nothing was done or taken care of. next day the lactation nurse helped us feed at about 11:00 am. the wait in the emergency room which was more that a couple of hours was very discomforting and causing more concerns. 

my concern is that we should not have been discharged, if the baby was not well. we were informed that the bilirubin levels of the baby were on the higher side. we asked the nurse what steps need to be taken for high bilirubin levels. however, the nurse said some kids have high level. all these days after the baby was born, we had been complaining that the baby is not feeding, to which the nurses and the doctors mentioned that it is normal since they are learning to latch. we had multiple times informed that the baby is constantly sleeping and not feeding. at this time, nobody provided us with the formula. when we returned to the emergency and the bilirubin test indicated that the levels are significantly very high and hence readmitted to the hospital. we learnt there that there was a misunderstanding that the baby was given the formula after birth, however that was never the case. 

we have faith in the hospital staff for discharging us, which makes us feel all is good with the mother and the baby, which was not in this case. we also noticed that the adjacent bed baby had a similar case, only thing is that they were discharged on 12/28/2019 and they came to back on 12/29/2019 morning. i believe, in such cases extending the stay and treating the baby will be better than the hassle of been discharged and then returning through emergency. 

this not only put us through a lot of discomfort and stress but also has financial implications. 

i would really appreciate if this can be looked into and not cause stress to other new parents.

!!do not bring your child here with asthma or difficulty breathing!!

team has little-to-no knowledge of pediatric pulmonology. my child has asthma that is triggered by chest colds and she had pneumonia (bad combo). 

she needed a strong steroid (which is usually the first step every time i've ever taken her to the er for asthma). instead of giving her a steroid treatment, the doctor on duty was convinced that my child needed to have a magnesium infusion. she was going to need the iv for being admitted anyway, so i consented. i was not informed of how painful these infusions are. my child was put through a painful, invasive magnesium infusion (which for some reason the whole staff was obsessed with doing) - which ended up doing absolutely nothing for my child. 

she was in constant pain from the iv, and they didn't once offer her any pain medication or any type of pain management (no heating pads, no nothing). the nurse practitioner was rude, harsh, had almost no bedside manner, and treated me like i had no clue what i was talking about. she literally said (in a sarcastic, clearly-feigning-empathy, tone) 'oooh, poor baby' to my child who was in pain and crying from the mag. treatment (which was completely unnecessary and ineffective). i've had a child with asthma for 8 years - i know what works - and the nurse practitioner treated me like an idiot and blew me off. 

i had to basically beg them to give her a steroid. they finally did, but not before telling me that she needed to be in the icu. i didn't think she needed to be in the icu (they were stating 'hospital policy' based on the fact that she needed hourly breathing treatments - which could be done in a regular room?? - not making the decision based on the severity of her asthma) - she wasn't in distress, she was calm, she just needed breathing treatments because her o2 levels were staying low. (pro tip: constant albuterol treatments will lower your o2 levels - the staff didn't seem to know this) they didn't have any available rooms in the icu (probably because their standards for admitting someone to the icu are so low), so they basically insisted we be moved via ambulance to dell children's. 

this was probably the only thing that st. david's did right. the dell team showed up - took one look at my child - and said "she doesn't need to be in the icu". when we got to dell - one of the first questions they asked was 'has she had a steroid yet' - wow, what do you know - mom knew what she was talking about! they also told me not to worry too much about her o2 levels - which st. david were obsessed with - because, as stated above, constant albuterol treatments will lower your o2. at dell they immediately took her off of oxygen, gave her additional steroids, moved her breathing treatments from every hour to every 3 hours, she was able to cough a bunch of stuff up, and we were able to go home the next day.

save yourself the trouble and stress and bring your kids to dell children's for asthma (or anything else for that matter). they have extensive pediatric pulmonology knowledge (a whole wing dedicated to it!), they treated me like a person, considered and listened to my opinions, gave a sh*t when my child was in pain, and their team made me feel so at ease after the hell that was st. david's north austin. 

i will never bring my child to another st. david's. i will always go straight to dell.

review:
this place is absolutely amazing!! must seem like a weird adjective to describe an emergency room, but it was such a positive experience. you rely on hospital staff to comfort you and make you feel better when you are
sick. the university of utah er team was incredibly patient and effective in their treatment. 

i drank 2 shots of vodka one saturday night (i never drink), and immediately went into a puking frenzy. i could not keep fluids down. i was puking non-stop every 5 minutes, it was unbelievably miserable and the nausea was intolerable. this continued for 8 hours (worst 8 hours of my life). i finally decided to go to the emergency room around 7am in the morning. the staff immediately gave me fluids and gave me some zofran. within 10 minutes my nausea was gone and i felt better. i was very cold at a certain point and two nurses brought in 3 heated blankets for me. my doctor was also incredible. i wish i remembered her name, but she had purple hair and a killer sense of humor. turns out i had a bad case of gastritis. i have an incredibly sensitive stomach and it cannot handle any alcohol. 

although i am barred from alcohol for life, i couldn't be happier with my experience at the u of u hospital. the staff was so comforting and my doctor was so genuinely concerned and sweet. i highly recommend this place if you are sick, they take great care.

i had a stomachache virus and the urgent care was not open so i was sent to the emergency part of the hospital. everything from the intake was good, once i moved to the room it went downhill from there. it was 6am and i was told nurses and doctors shifts were changing. i spoke with what seemed like ten different people and i kept having to repeat my symptoms, which was becoming alarming. 

1.) i had an emt come take my blood and start poking my arm a couple time. then she stated that my vain popped and took off, she didn't explain what that meant.

2.) then the first male nurse, while nice, came and poked my veins again. that did not go so well for me. apparently, i look over and my whole arm and sheet is covered in blood. the nurse apologized and changed the sheets. but the kicker is that he set up my iv. he left and  never set up the iv to flow. i was just sitting there for 30 mins, with an iv im my arm which wasn't flowing anything.

3.) the new nurse team comes in and fixes the issue by flowing the iv and apologizes. i explain my frustration with the two incidents from the emt and nurse and how i'm really concerned about the delivery of services. 

4.) the second nurse tries to put another bag of fluid and this time it's super painful and my arm has blood underneath the taping. i express my discomfort and he advises he would would bring me water instead. some time passed, and i was never given said water, and i was discharged. at this point i'm just tired and want to go home and rest. 

overall, i was very alarmed at the services and the process and efficiency in the delivery. i now have this big bruise on my arm to remind me of my visit to the emergency room. everyone was extremely nice and friendly, which i really appreciate, but i need professionals to be on their a game. explain to the patient what you are doing, introduce yourself and if you don't know how to draw blood then request training. don't let patients feel like test patients. and lastly, i think a little more work needs to go into coordinating staff once they've been assigned a bed. i may have gotten there when shifts were ending, but i must have spoken to 8 to 10 people and had to restate what was happening and my symptoms, which i think could have been evaded.

monday night. arrived at 7pm for extreme kidney pain. went to urgent care because the er was a 4 hour wait. urgent care sent us back to the er because they wanted to take blood - no big deal. we waited for about 3 hours until we were taken back. no rooms were available so we were given a bed in the hallway. we were assigned elizabeth, a resident, the most dry, unhelpful, unenthusiastic person i've encountered. 8 hours later still sitting in the hallway on a bed, given some morphine and liquid ibuprofen. resident says some tests come back negative, then an hour later the nurse says they're waiting on the results we already received, this happened twice. the resident comes back to tell us her shift is ending. great, can we get something for the pain before you go? her response: bye, feel better. wtf.

my callback was finally received about 6 weeks later, after i have had to make phone calls over and over, again requesting a callback.  this only happened because i got in touch with lillian martinez who heard me and cared enough to document and follow through unlike anyone else had done previously.

i want the doctors and great staff to know they have people like sandra dewars, clinical nurse specialist who are making calls on the doctors behalf and speaking down to people and being demeaning in tones. rather than making an apology that a ball was dropped somewhere they start the conversation off with excuses and then they tell me there are no notes in the system.  how

cannot speak highly enough about the emergency care that i received at this hospital.  on 07/14/16,  i arrived at this hospital by car unaware that i had suffered a fluke "plaque collapse" and had no blood flow to the right side of my heart.   i was going to die without immediate emergency medical treatment which required inserting a stent to reestablish blood flow.  

from the moment my wife pulled up to the hospital emergency entrance at which point i realized i could no longer walk on my own, the professionals at littleton adventist went into action. 

i was immediately wheeled into the hospital and surrounded by a team of professionals who determined that this previously very healthy patient was in the middle of a fluke major heart attack.  i was dying.  they stabilized me and immediately took me into an operating room where i was surrounded again by an incredible team of professionals.  a cardiac surgeon who was already at the hospital performed the procedure and i had a full recovery.  

in fact, felt great right after surgery when i once again had blood flowing to the right side of my heart.  spent the night at the hospital where everyone who interacted with me was a+ wonderful.   my surgeon told me days later on follow up that there was no residual damage at all to my heart.  he attributed that to my regularly working out for years while i attribute it more to the incredible skill of my surgeon and all of the amazing professionals at littleton adventist who worked with superb teamwork to save my life.

i feel bad giving hospitals bad reviews, but this time, it's necessary. i brought my son in with severe back pain and sciatic leg pain. we got here at 2:15. got into a room at about 3:00. a nurse came in and asked all the usual questions and said "ryan" (pa) would be in to talk to my son. one hour goes by. no one.  nothing for the pain. it's about 4pm and my son hadn't eaten anything. i went out to the nurse's station and asked if i could get something from the cafeteria for him. 'nurse one' says probably, but he needs to be seen by ryan to get the ok. i go back to his room and we wait. another hour goes by. i return to the desk and ask, "when will ryan go to my son's room?" 

nurse one - oh, he hasn't been in yet? i'll get him in there.

ten minutes later, ryan shows up, asks my son what's happening and he tells him about the severe sciatic pain and low back pain. 

ryan says, "so, what do you want us to do for you?" 

i'm shocked. he says,  well we can give you muscle relaxers. or, i guess we could do an mri." um, yeah. thanks, we'll take the mri.  and something for his pain right now? thanks....

i went to get my son something to eat and someone came in and gave him a shot of valium. valium? he's not having a panic attack... his disc is blown! 


we wait.

we wait. 5:30 a different nurse comes in and says they'll be taking him out for his mri soon - remove all metal etc. at 5:40, ryan comes back in and says, "well, its gonna be another couple hours until we can get you the mri, so if you want to go home, i can give you a prescription... you probably won't get the mri till 8 or 9."

at first, i'm like, yeah, we're going home this is bs. we'll  just go home and try to make it through the weekend. then i started to think about that.  if we went home, we'd go through the wind with him in pain. monday, try to get an appt with a surgeon. prob won't get an appt for that week. meanwhile, we still can't get an mri because we haven't seen a dr. to authorize it. weeks will go by without any help. 

so, i go back out and tell ryan we want the mri after all. he says he just cancelled it. i said reschedule.  

in less than 10 minutes, someone comes in to take my son to get the mri. really. 

i'm figuring ryan was trying to clear out the room my son is in without doing anything for him. its friday night and they need the room. 

this kind if care is what i'd expect with socialized medicine.  this is unacceptable.  i'd give a zero if i could. no attention, no urgency. they act as if severe pain shouldn't be an er visit,  make you wait long enough and maybe you'll just go home!!

this is my story, please note, this is being toned down.
went to crmc on 25 december 2019 for sever lower left side abdomen pain and unable to get my blood sugar under 250. 

i informed the admission desk, intake nurses and doctors that i got six steroid injections into my feet a few days earlier. at the time i went to crmc er my blood sugar was 287. all the above personnel told me that they don't treat blood sugar until it gets 300+. that should be have been my first clue to leave and go to another medical facility. shame on me, due to the pain i stayed. 

it gets better, the doctor ordered lab (blood) test, waited for the lab (blood) results and the doctor ordered an ct scan with contrast. i told them that the last time i had contrast, it created pain in my kidneys and i didn't want the contrast (two times). 

well, the x-ray tech, stated, your kidney lab results came in and it showed your kidneys are fine, they never orders a gfr test. again told her not to administer the contrast, she administered the contrast anyways. 

immediately thereafter, i exhibited kidney issues and on 31 december 2019 was diagnosed with stage 3b renal failure. 
12 december 2019, normal gfr and creatinine results
25 december 2019, crmc er didn't order gfr and creatinine test.
notified all crmc personnel that i came in front of, the recent steroid injections, diabetic, hypertension and the er gave me large dose of antibiotics for ten days. 
31 december 2019, diagnosed with stage 3b renal failure.

steroid injections effective blood sugar and kidney functions. being a diabetic with hypertension, contrast dye, high dose of antibiotics, steroid injections should be a clue for kidney functions issues.

when i saw my endocrinologist and nephrologist and explained the above, they were shocked why the er doctors didn't treat my high blood sugar, (they both asked me twice why they didn't treat my high blood sugar). when i told them about the contrast dye, they put their heads down and negatively turned their heads. 

hopefully crmc will take the above as a learning experience and i promise that i will never ever go back there nor will i allow any family member to go there.

i have mixed feelings about my recent hospital visit. i'll start by saying that i first presented to the ed on 12/3 for a kidney stone. my ed visit went pretty quickly and i felt well taken care of. however, my pain didn't go away and during the night of 12/6 i returned to the ed. my original ct scan had showed a 3mm kidney stone and my us at the second visit showed a 6mm stone in the same location. so i feel like something was measured incorrectly there and i likely shouldn't have been sent home to pass a stone that large. i hope that someone is considering investigating this.

in any event, they offered me admission and consultation with a urologist, which i agreed to. i do understand that with flu season and snow birds coming into town census was very high. it took a very long time for me to get assigned a bed. when i finally did get a bed it was an overflow bed. what that means is that it was a bed in a hallway with a small partition in front of it. the lights in that area didn't turn off. the bathroom was a very long walk away for a patient with a urinary tract issue. needless to say i got no sleep. no one really explained to me that i would be going to an overflow bed...i just felt like there was a general lack of communication once i left the ed and was on the floor. it took the floor nurse a long time to get pain meds for me because they were apparently ordered for ed and not the floor and that was really challenging for me. i understand that this may not be the nurses fault, but i shouldn't have to suffer while they get it sorted. someone, maybe an administrator, came by early in the morning and promised to get me a room "sometime" but that didn't really happen.

i was fortunate that urology was able to fit me into their schedule later in the day friday and i had a procedure done. everyone in surgery was amazing. they explained everything and answered questions and kept me really informed. it took a while to get me out of recovery because, according to the observation unit, someone would assign me a bed and take me out, then assign me again...so she was surprised when i actually showed up. 

my night nurse, julie, on the observation unit was amazing. she was super attentive to my needs and helped me make decisions about pain control. i wasn't as jazzed with my day nurse, hayes. it seemed like she didn't believe my pain level. i felt like dr. khan, who discharged me, also felt that way. i asked her about pain meds at home and she told me i already had them filled on tuesday and if i needed more i needed to talk to my primary care doc. the ed had given me a small prescription of pain meds that i'd been taking for 3 days, so i only had a couple left. it was saturday and i was worried about just getting through to monday. she snidely said to me, "you do understand this is only going to get better, right?" then she was gone and i never saw her again. of course i knew the pain would be getting better, but i didn't want to be in a situation where my pain wasn't controlled over the weekend and i had to visit the ed again. luckily, the urologist had ordered some pain meds for me on discharge. 

overall i would say my biggest complaint was the care didn't seem super coordinated. after the doctor said she was discharging me hayes said she'd get the paperwork ready so i called my husband. after we'd sat there for quite a while i asked her about a couple things and then she's like, "oh, are you ready to go home?" like she was surprised by this? i thought we'd been waiting on her to bring us discharge papers. the discharge papers were 43 pages of notes about my condition and medication, but very little useful info regarding my actual stay. i guess i thought i might have gotten a care summary or something so that when i talked to my pcp i could speak to everything that had occurred.

first and foremost, nothing but the utmost respect for all of the nurses and dr. tsai in the labor and delivery ward. they were pro's and honoring of the birth process. 

however... things took an abrupt and horrifying turn after our baby was born when the hospital pediatrician began the initial examination of our son and made several alarming observations and "diagnoses" that were not accurate. the false observations included:

1. a supposed heart murmur that warranted a 48 hour extended hospital stay.  4 additional heart auscultations by 2 different doctors and 2 nurses did not pick up any said murmur.

2. a supposed mild spinal bifida - non-union or closure of bones near the sacrum/buttocks (that was actually just a cute butt)  

3. supposed extremely low body weight and size- our boy was actually 6 lb 6oz and 19 inches long. just a small little guy.

4. said he felt hot and might have an infection. for the post birth examination, babies are placed under a heat lamp that if you are standing close by to it, feels like a nice warm outdoor heat lamp. i was watching his skin turn pink from the heat.... to be expected...and since i was able to assist in the delivery by catching him with the dr. and then placing him on my wife... i was well aware of his temperature as well as texture of the skin.

after the doctor's confusing and fear based examination we were asked if we wanted several other tests to be performed. since our boy possessed normal reflexes, had healthy muscular tone, skin color was normal (actually red from the heat lamp), we declined the optional tests that were recommended by this doctor ( i will update the accurate name later) because we did not trust her. she questioned us repeatedly on why we did not want the test and gave her informed answers knowing of the risks and benefits.... after all, both my wife and i are health care practitioners, and had done our research on the proposed tests. since there was no real indication to perform the "recommended" we declined. this doctor was so aggressive we wanted to leave the hospital immediately. we did not feel safe.

we were next transferred to the postpartum room where we encountered another warm and compassionate nurse who tended to our baby... who also said she heard no murmur.... only to be attacked by another pediatrician who wanted to do more invasive testing involved in the newborn screening. we declined the test which requires a slicing of the heel and milking of blood to assess for possible conditions. since my wife an i had already done our own blood work and had  blood work drawn while she was pregnant, that reveal zero genetic abnormalities.

we had two separate experiences... one with the ob/gyn and nurses involved in the actual birth and another one were we felt like we were in germany in the 1940's with aggressive and hostile doctors.

we wish we could share a more positive experience, but this was a huge stain on our experience. 

finally, to avoid this traumatizing situation, make sure your pediatrician has hospital privileges at ucla to examine your newborn or you will be subject to receiving an exam from the hospital pediatrician who may scare the heck out of you by saying something is wrong with your child. if your pediatrician does not have privileges, then make sure you find a trusted md that can come to the hospital. that's the best advice i can give you.

designated cancer center in florida makes me wonder what their standards are. i'm alive in spite of moffitt, not because of them. i'm 33 years old and at 32 was diagnosed with stage iv renal cell carcinoma, which spread to my lungs. i was initially told treatment was basically pointless-death sentence blah blah by st. anthony's hospital in st. pete, but felt somewhat reassured that almighty moffitt was just across the bay. based on my outside urologist's recommendation, he said go to cleveland clinic or memorial sloan kettering, don't settle. i did just that, had a successful surgery to remove kidney and large tumor and saw an rcc specialist in cleveland. i was able to establish care at moffitt and begin immunotherapy for my lungs. my gu doctor, jingsong zhang and his office were an absolute trainwreck, nearly brought me to tears each visit with their incompetence. unorganized, unpleasant and just plain unhelpful at every turn. dr. zhang barely speaks english, refused to even go over scans and smirks if you ask him questions, like he's insulted that you try to participate in your care. his office routinely does not call back (number goes straight to vm and is unmanned). i've gotten calls back two and three days later and they did not answer messages online either. they were nasty to me on the phone when i spent all day trying to get through to them bc i was having ses from my infusion. the waiting room is a conveyor belt of sick people who get shoved in and out asap. if you need anything from the office (paperwork, tumor slides, you name it....you will not get it without forceful persistence). i dropped that team and opted to go to the mip location with dr. richard levine. he is very kind and responsive and his staff is the same. he readily admits he isn't a specialist, but he's been great-he defers to my specialist when applicable and has even called me on the weekend. i am now consulting with dr mayer fishman at tgh (who spent 20 years at moffitt-he's amazing...he must've seen the writing on the wall with their continued decay and got out of dodge...oh and shady dealing with china that's coming out). you will have to dig in and guide your care at moffitt if you want to get anything from them, you will get chewed up if you aren't active in your care. none of my absentee care team in the gu clinic offered me any assistance with my cobra coverage and now i'm getting booted off of it because i didn't file a simple extension that surely an experienced set of professionals would passingly mention. go to md anderson, utsw, dana farber, msk, city of hope, beth israel if you have the means to travel. moffitt is not all it's cracked up to be. they deal in quantity of patients fleeced not quality of care and there's nothing "comprehensive" about them. good luck.

my adult son recently had 2 stays at this facility. the reason i went back was because the drs on staff were wonderful. however my sons care was so below the standard of care. no one rolls patients for days. a man was falling out of bed and a nurse replied "not my patient". my sons condition was deteriorating twice. i was told by the receptionist he would have to wait days to receive a stat test he needed instead of just doing the transport he needed. when i was about to take him myself he hot a transport and had a very serious emergency surgery with a high mortality rate. thank god on high he intervened. there are some great nurses here but alot of sloppy neglect. you must self advocate here!!

nothing has changed here. same old bullshit treatment. zero stars for this place would still be an exaggeration of less than stellar service. poor service leaves you wondering why these people are always providing mediocre service. at the time of checking in, the lobby was empty, we asked about wait times and they said 11 minutes. what a sad lie that turned into.

we were kept at the er from 2pm to 8:30 pm, waiting to see the doctor. it's the  flu season and the looming fears of the deadly corona virus means every one with a slight symptom, is camped at the hospitals.

understandable why the doc is taking longer than usual. but 5 hours for a flu season is a joke! but telling someone with a sick relative that they don't look sick is a joke.

my issue is why a patient is kept waiting in a hospital room, no one took their vitals and after all that time the charge nurse has the caucasity to ask me if am ok with leaving with a hospital visit note? for what? for whom? am only answerable to the ones i brought in  to seek  treatment. i don't care to explain to anyone else. my family's wellbeing is my priority, every thing else is irrelevant.

what good does  a sick note do to any of us if we don't get the help we came for?

then the doctor prescribes enough antibiotic to kill a herd of cattle for a little child. wow the devil must be the administrator here. 

go anywhere else  but here.

a solid 0-stars.  at best it's a glorified urgent care clinic, at worst you're paying exorbitant hospital prices for excessively sub-par care.

they managed to mishandle an irreplaceable lab sample of mine, resulting in its disposal and subsequent cancellation of my lab test.  they didn't even contact me to let me know of this error.  i had to call in and ask for results--only to get nonchalantly told that it was cancelled.

them doing this has resulted in me still not having the answers i need, even after seeing multiple other doctors.  those labs were absolutely necessary and their half-hearted, semi-apology with the offer to do a retest unfortunately won't cut it in this case.  and i'd have to be pretty dumb to give that another go...

i was charged $300 for a medication they administered improperly, likely rendering it useless.  my referral to a specialist was also useless; to a doctor who exclusively does hospital rounds, not an out-patient office. for being so empty, everything was extremely disorganized. 

i did contact 301-557-6495--the same number they reply with to yelp complaints.  the woman told me she put in a dispute for all charges. a few weeks later i received a letter from her, basically writing off their error, "i apologize were were not able to successfully test...", and saying that the care i received was "appropriate". i disagree. if you ruin the one thing i came in for, it's highly inappropriate and certainly not worth $1,400.  you couldn't even pay me $1,400 to go there again to receive the same incompetent care.

their wait time was minimal and the waiting room was empty.  there's a reason for this but i didn't get the memo in time. seriously, go anywhere but here.  i never thought i'd have to yelp emergency rooms prior to going, but you live and you learn!

i cant rate this because there is no "0" this is by far the worst hospital ever, do not go there!! they will give you medicine and tell you to go home without any further search. we literately had to rush to shady grove hospital to get the correct treatment! thank you shady grove for getting us the appropriate help!!!!

this hospital was good to us for the time  we spent in bakersfield. i personally stayed in this hospital for 1  night for an emergency.  husband had good experiences here. thank you adventist!

if you find yourself at adventist's health be proactive and ask to see a dr. in your network. they have several out of network providers but don't tell you before being seen. weeks later you receive a bill for the physician for over $1,000 when you have full coverage insurance.

my doctor only delivers at san joaquin, and i honestly had a great experience in the maternity area, all nurses are kind and rooms were nice and clean. there is however a blonde lady who checks you in, in the maternity area, both times i checked into labor and delivery she was training someone, well yeah i didn't catch her name but she's rude. my boyfriend and i didn't like her attitude. she's not friendly at all and seems annoyed of her job. i always walk into places with my nicest attitude because i like being treated the same way i treat people, so i don't understand her ugly attitude and i'm glad it wasn't just my pregnancy hormones judging her lol cause my family members and boyfriend also noticed her attitude. when you are pregnant and in pain the last thing you wanna deal with is people who have ugly attitudes.

i recently had my first ever surgery here, and despite my nervousness, it went well because of the great care i received.  the whole process, from the pre-op appointment over the phone to the post-op care instructions and check out, was smooth and organized.  the staff and healthcare providers i interacted with were friendly and responsive to my needs, which my family and i really appreciated.  the only reason i'm giving four  stars now is because i had a really horrible experience at the er here a few years ago which left me without help and with huge medical bills at a time when i didn't have health insurance.  however this recent experience being admitted to the main hospital was vastly different and infinitely better.

awesome care i received in the er. thanks for getting me back to health!  the rapid medical evaluation has me on the correct path for my 3 week old cough in less than 30 minutes. there was constant consideration for my health from the moment i walked in and tell them and i left. nobody wants to be sick, but if you are and need to get back on the road, bakersfield adventist hospital should be your first choice

had my second surgery here and the staff and experience was wonderful. the check in process was very smooth, surgery went well with good pain relief in recovery. everyone explained things well and i had all the resources i needed for home.
