review:
my doctors are rock solid, i have zero complaints about my doctors. my complaint is for clerical. billing services / clerical are a joke. i have to file taxes, and as a disabled person, i have spent a lot of money with kaiser.  i have attempted to get copies of all out of pocket expenses for calendar 2019, and have received the run around at every turn. i have received incomplete information on my co pays, i still havent received pharmacy bills, and i have been re directed for premium bills. i have been attempting to collect this information since 12.30.19, and it is now 1.22.20. i filed grievances today. what is the response time on a grievance you ask? 30 days. i spend $720 a month on kaiser. that is $23.67 per day 365 days a year. kaiser has regularly tried to refer me back to the website which is strong in some ways, and very weak in others. if i go buy a printer, i could print out my co pays. i cant download and save it like people do in 2020, but i could print it if i went and bought a printer. they cant just print in the office for me. they sent me incomplete bills, they couldnt send me anything that just shows out of pocket. the website does not provide my out of pocket prescription payments even if i went and bought a printer. they failed to send me a copy of pharmacy records. the website does not provide payments made for my premiums over the year. they failed to send me a copy of the premiums i paid, and went on to tell me i need to contact a different department by phone. i filled out all of the paperwork, and explained clearly what was needed in the office on 12.30.19. when kaiser ca sales people sold me this plan, they told me that my records from kaiser hawaii to kaiser california would transfer seamlessly. they do not. i needed to fill in all of my new doctors on the info i was told they would have. i needed to get my kaiser medical records from hawaii, and give them to my california doctors so they could have my medical records. that is purely for medical records, and making sure my new doctors would have a list of ailments.  what does that mean for billing records? that means i need to go through all the same run around with kaiser hawaii since i moved to ca halfway through the year. if you are moving state to state, and you are considering sticking with kaiser for the convenience of record transfer, and the kp.org website, dont bother. their systems are not connected regardless of what they tell you at the point of sale. i am giving serious consideration to dropping kaiser at my next open enrollment. there are far cheaper options, and the whole benefit of kaiser to me was supposed to be convenience. here is what i have asked kaiser ca member services for, and cant seem to get:
1. complete neat statement of out of pocket expenses for co/pays
2: complete neat statement of out of pocket expenses for pharmacy
3: complete neat statement of out of pocket expenses for premium dues. 
i am literally asking for basic receipts, and they have terrible response time/turnaround. by the time you find out they have failed to provide information and you let them know, you need to start over at step 1. good doctors, garbage clerical system (not the people, the system), misleading sales department. i really wish i would have put all charges on one credit card so i could get my own receipts without relying on kaiser to give me a couple simple printouts. everybody i have spoken to at member services and billing was very polite, and incapable of  providing me with receipts due to the system. why cant i just look up, and save a file of this basic info on the website they so proudly use as a selling point?  what a mess.

 i am looking at the responses to the negative reviews from other customers. i have noticed that they are generic responses stating that the review will be discussed, but i dont see any that show kaiser taking any actual action. my problem is ongoing. any response that doesnt show them taking immediate action, and eludes to discussions with senior staff members is really just an example of the run around and ineffectiveness i am explaining.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Fremont Medical Center and Offices

review:

i tend to have a cheery disposition even though i'm the one in pain, i mean it's not their fault. however today's visit i am not at all pleased with the rn at the front desk in the er. and on martin luther king day. i expect more especially since her tag says she too is a veteran! 

i actually like the new (new to me policy) that you have to wait at the other side of the walk in doors for veterans privacy. what i am having a problem with is her disposition. she is just rude. i understand firm. i agree that you need to be especially when you don't know the kinds of people you will be engaging. however you also need to have some sort of caring bedside manner about yourself. she had none of that displayed. very disappointing. 

i also would like to complain about the neverending construction. seems odd. and really an inconvenience 

that's my complaint on it. seems odd. 

other than that my experiences are typically as i stated, good. and as hospitals go, va hospitals, this is a good one. with caring doctors even though it's a teaching facility. you of course find a few not so delicious apples in the bunch but that's everywhere. 


4 out of 5 ain't bad at the end of the day.

review:
i took my son here today from spring, north of houston. he is a veteran with some disability. he was told by a recording on the phone that the walk-in legal help workshop was from 2 to 5.  i dropped him off at the er entrance which is where he was told to go. by the time i found a place to park he called me saying he could not be seen and that they changed the hours but did not bother to change the recording.   there is no way to call and speak to a person.  the woman on the desk told him he had to be there before 12 to get help and was unconcerned that the times had changed but not the recording.  this is no way to treat anyone and especially not a veteran. my son was already depressed and now feels worse. i plan to search until i can find the proper place to lodge a complaint. 
and the parking situation is ridiculous. all but a few entrances and exits are blocked off with posts. god forbid they have a situation where people need to leave in a hurry because they will be out of luck.

review:
my husband went to the er for cellulitis in the face, yesterday morning. they placed him in a 23 hour observation to give iv antibiotics. by late afternoon, he started asking the nurses to tell the doctor his swelling spread to his jaw and neck. repeatedly he asked to see a doctor or to please let the doctor  know. the nurses kept telling him there is no doctor available after hours and  over night when you're an observation patient. he asked when do the doctors do rounds, and was told 7 am. however he wasn't seen until 4 pm today. once seen, they were "suddenly" alarmed at how much more he swelled  up and finally got more aggressive with his treatment. i call bullshit that there's no doctor available in the evenings or night for observation patients. what are they going to do, observe him suffocate to death as the swelling closes off his airway because there's no doctor??  you mean to tell me if his blood pressure should suddenly be 220/130, "after hours" there's no doctor to notify?? 
on top of all this, i tried to visit him today with our kids and they said i can't bring the kids up. i can't leave them in the waiting room. i can't have them stay in the lobby, unsupervised. they can't watch them for 15 minutes so that i can drop off my husbands toiletries and personal stuff. they can't bring the bag up to him for me. they can't have a transport person or volunteer bring the bag up to him for me. all they know what to do is put up walls for me at every turn and offered absolutely no solutions to my dilemma. they have no idea how to treat the hunan spirit or how to help alleviate stress of loved ones! 
at this point, if anything happens to my poor husband because of macneal-layola, someone will pay-even if it's after hours!! i am beyond  angry and disappointed.

a group of uncaring, ignorant nurses and doctors yes there are good ones but it can't make up for the lack of ignorant nurses unless they just don't care.  would give zero stars !    do not have a loved one in here without watching what meds there given , if they have been given right medications , if there pulse drops etc they have no respect for the elderly !   
so sad.

never a patient only a visitor of patients..i visited patients here..was not one myself so i can only comment on my personal observations.  i would never come here voluntarily because of how filthy and small the rooms are. it is apparent they cram 2 beds into what should be a single room...probably did that during renovation. very noisy.. no peace..i could never sleep there unless they knocked me unconscious. lovely fixtures in bathroom however who cares about the asthetics when the garbage cans are overflowing with soiled adult diapers. the patient i was visiting bed was right next to bathroom...probably 3 feet between bed and bathroom..shared with the other patient. i saw and smelled diapers on bathroom floor and a garbage can filled. the patient i was visiting was not using diapers so the nurse removed them from the other patient, walked by my friends bed to the bathroom and tossed it on the floor. gross. unhealthy. infectious  .the other can was filled with fast food garbage from the night before from the other patients visitors. it is obvious they do not clean very often, leave biohazard waste around for hours but the lobby gets alot of attention and cleaning, they would get 5 stars for that. one patient i visited had the wrong name on the door and inside the room. according to the family they had been asking the nurses to put the correct name up for days. they felt obligated to stand guard over their loved one to ensure they were not getting the wrong medication meant for the person whos name was there. i recently checked the ranking for this hospital on us news and world report...pretty mediocre to poor ranking. beware...there are much better hospitals in the area.

atrium health is not only involved in illegal billing practices, but they also provided me with the worst health care i have received in my entire life. as a pharmacy student i had surgery done by an orthocarolina physician who then held me overnight at atrium so that i could receive iv pain medications for the extensive trauma needed on the physician's end to correct my labrum, rotator cuff, and biceps tendon damage.  i never received any iv pain meds for my 8-10/10 pain throughout the night (no i am not an opioid seeker, i just had a major surgery and these people are clueless).  not only did they not give me any iv pain meds, but they also directly told me "no" when i questioned the night staff as to why my orders were not filled.  so apparently it is within hospital policy to leave a post-surgery patient in the most severe pain of their life, deny iv pain medication orders from the surgeon, and then charge them for an overnight stay, after  failing to deliver anything close to decent care  they also ran normal saline on me all night as a maintenance fluids, this is not a maintenance fluid.  d5 + 1/2 ns + 20-40 meq of kcl is a maintenance fluid.  unfortunately, their incompetent staff did not know this, and ended up raising my serum na so high i ended up with a massive headache from the pressure difference between my brain and the rest of my body's sodium concentration.  to make matters even worse, they gave me iv cefazolin all night.  there is absolutely no indication for iv cefazolin once a healthy, person leaves the or....but i got billed for that too.  atrium health 100% fumbled the ball once my care was transitioned to them, and then pursued illegal billing actions against me, in attempt to circumvent financial assistance law's put in place by the obama administration with irs tax code 501(r).  prior to my surgery on 7/5/17 i spoke with anne wingate about my expected surgical costs.  the surgery cost over $69,000, and my expected out of pocket expense was $4,200+.  at that time i could not make a down payment that they requested, and i asked for financial assistance.  somehow from that date forward there is no note or any record of me calling until 5/31/18 (my verizon records show otherwise).  may 31 is my birthday, and i called atrium health to once again, ask for financial assistance on my 28th birthday because these clowns had been busting my balls that hard and for that long.  they then finally sent me a financial assistance packet, but it was 8 months post surgery.  i did not meet their 6 month paperwork deadline, they claimed, and my financial assistance was denied and i was once again, turned over to collections.  however,  this is 100% in violation of irs statute 501(r) that applies to 503(c) non-profit (tax-exempt) hospitals.  it is illegal to deny a patient access to financial assistance paperwork and then pursue extreme collections actions against them.  i highly suggest that nobody ever pursue any type of care through atrium health.  this place is in absolute shambles, and i am telling you this as someone who experienced it first hand and is now a medical professional.  these people are absolute clowns, they have 0 care about their patient's best interests and they will do unethical and illegal things to force you into payment!
usually you get rude rns but i swear, from triage to getting seen to discharge, the nurses were sweet. thank you!

was forced to carry a dead embryo inside me for almost 3 weeks (until i later miscarried naturally) because the women's health clinic on the 4th floor didn't want to do anything about it.

this place treated my  navy dad with so much respect! can't say enough about the oncology department!

this is such a difficult review to write.  for the better part of the last 40 years i have received medical care on base.  it has been some of the best medical care a person could receive, and i have been grateful for that thoughtful and thorough care.    
after coming out to california to care for my mother, i had to change to david grant medical center and clinics at travis afb.  my recent experience there has been poor.  i booked an appointment for repeated high blood pressure readings at home, after a fall.  my blood pressure was high in the clinic.  the clinic appointment itself went well.  i was sent to get labs, period.  the lab was closed.  i came back for labs when they were open and waited 1 hour 45 minutes before i was called to the desk to do the initial check-in.  by that time, i was too late for one of the tests.  
a week later i received a phone call from the clinic staff asking me if my urinary tract infection symptoms were better.  what?  i explained i came in for high blood pressure.  the nurse asked me, why then, did i have a urine test done?  what?  probably because the doctor ordered it?  i explained my blood pressure readings were still high.  she hung up.
over two weeks later, i receive a call from another clinic staff.  she tells me a np looked at my labs and would like to start me on a cholesterol medication because my cardiac risk factor is high, and i needed more labs.  yes, you read that right.  my blood pressure is still high (200/110), i have received nothing for that at all, but they want to know if i wouldn't mind taking a "statin" for my elevated cardiac risk factor.  i explained that i came in for high blood pressure.  she explained the np looked at my labs and due to my labs i have an elevated cardiac risk and taking the "statin" will lower it and take me out of that risk category.  what?????????

leaving the hospital is where my experience falls short. i have received multiple phone calls and had my follow up procedure rescheduled three times due to dr. vittal's office making scheduling mistakes. the my health one portal is only useful if you need to access and read information from your visits. you cannot contact anyone directly from the hospital. i tried calling dr. mckeen's office numerous times and kept getting a voicemail saying their mailbox is full and cannot receive messages. i tried emailing him directly and did not receive a response until one week later. the lack of communication has been inconvenient, as i needed paperwork processed for fmla and short term disability in a short amount of time.

overall, the hospital, doctors, and staff are outstanding when you are a patient. unfortunately, i feel they do not care as much after you are discharged from the hospital.

my mother returned to the 3rd floor from icu.  she requires several machines due to her illness.  again they put her in the smallest room with not enough plugs to hook up her machines.  the nurses here are mostly traveling nurses because of the high turnover her.  i was told nurses leave here to work at stanford because this hospital is all about profit and less about care.  there are some wonderful nurses, assistants, doctors & other staff but the profit bureaucracy, and some terrible staff over shadowed the good

the er here is the best! but if you get checked in esp in the cardio dept the place is dirty....dirty....dirty. you have to share a room and the rooms are forken small. lights on all the time and everyone talks loud. so if you need to get rest? forken forget about it. the best nurse is paul. very communicative, knowledge and awesome bedside manner.

the only things to look forward to is the hospital food which is delicious.

my mom was in er  early on the dec. 27, 2019. after lots of test, dr. mc kenn came out and talked to me what problems my mom had, i burst out to tear , scare that she won't survive if she go through all the surgery to take care of her issues .
i have been patient and trusted all the doctors and nurses of this hospital for 25 years, why not this time for my mom   who's 84 years. had multiple colon surgery. very week and fragile!
exactly my trust is right.  she had triple successful surgery in two days! very happy with all the doctors , nurses and staffs! 
love and respect them to death! thank you all

this review is for the er and it's absolutely the best place if you ever need to take a kid to the er. i've had the unfortunate need to do that 3 times in the past 6 months & this place has been fantastic. the nurses are amazingly polite & empathetic, they give you the time to make choices & have a doctor take a look if needed. they expedite wait time for kids, so we never had to wait long. getting stitches is never fun, but they certainly help make it bearable. they also gave our kid a plush doggie toy :). keep up the good work & we're grateful for your service.

i don't know where should i start. i have delivered my first baby at good sam october 2019. hospital is good at every aspect clean rooms, amazing staff, great doctors, good food every day, easy parking for patients and guests etc. i can't thank enough to all the nursing staff who helped me through the whole baby delivery process. they made everything easy for me and they care for each patient a lot. really appreciate all of them and they indeed are doing one of the best jobs in the world. i would highly recommend this place to my friends and family and to anyone who is still doubtful of this place. good sam i will be back for my second baby in future :)

this so called doctor is not really a doctor, a doctor doesn't tell my mother who has chest pain and heart pain, that, " you can't really feel your heart tightening, it's like an organ, do you feel your liver and kidneys, or any other organ in your body? how do you feel your heart tightening?" he said to my mom. he let my mother out of the hospital within 30 minutes, he requested x-trays and told my brother that her lungs are perfectly clear, after my brother mentioned to him that they can't be clear because she's been coughing for a month badly, he repeated and said "her lungs are perfectly fine", after a couple of days, my mother was going through the same pain, she went back to good sam and a different doctor treated her which was very nice, he did an x-tray and listened to my moms lungs, he immediately knew that she was diagnosed with bronchitis and prescribed her a couple of medications. this doctor also thought my mom came in for pain medicine, and she didn't ask for any at all! this is totally unfair, he shouldn't be a doctor, doctors are supposed to help patients from their heart not because they get paid! so rude and disrespectful towards his patients, everybody be aware of him when you go to good sam!!! his name is "dr. rhys daper"

i brought my friend into the er today for severe abdominal pain from a surgery 3 weeks prior . you are confronted by a security guard  rough around the edges kind of scary . then my friend and i taken into a room and a male rn takes my friends blood pressure and not very personable . the doctor she had in the er was really nice . my friend never got a room , only a bed in the hallway for 4 hours . her male rn nurse complained  the whole time about his health issues . we waited for hours to get blood drawn and finally a nurse came with no personal
skills and very cold . i know it's very stressful in the er and they are probably over worked but as a health care professional that's your job and you should never forget why you went into this profession . be compassionate , loving, and kind. patients are scared and hurting they need to feel safe . my friend did not feel safe but scared . i followed through with the personnel because i know how patients should be treated .

i tried giving this hospital so many chances especially because my son was born there and spent 41 days in their nicu. after tonight this will probably be the last time i ever bring him to this hospital. every time i bring him in they make me feel like a helicopter mom which i feel is not fair and i feel like they try getting rid of you as fast as possible! my child was born premature so every time he gets a cough or a rash i'm concerned and their is nothing wrong with that! tonight i brought him in because he has a rash from an allergic reaction to medicine. while we were at home he was crying uncontrollably and he turned clammy and very cold i took his temp and it was oddly low (which apparently is inaccurate because i didn't put a thermometer in my kids butt). i got scared to see my baby's temperature low and seeing him all cold and clammy! i'm a nervous person as it is and well i obviously don't want anything to happen to my son! i just felt like they took the whole reason i took him in today as a joke! there was a person who asked what was wrong with him as we were walking into the room they were putting him in and the person who checked him in said that it was because his temperature was low but that she took it and he was fine and then that person answered then why they bring him in this nasty tone and she replied it's because he has a new rash on his rash which i thought was super rude and insensitive like is it bad that i want to double check on my child well being? but there's never anything wrong with him when they see him. ever. then they start saying remarks like weren't you here the other day like yeah ok first off all we don't go all the time why do they have to make me feel i'm being over bearing or something. but what if i was to take him everyday it shouldn't matter their still getting paid so what's the problem? i'm just super upset after tonight. you pay them thousands of dollars for 10 min of their time.

i have some mix feelings here. my wife got life flighted to st. luke's on a friday. she had bad kidneys and they wanted to do a biopsy. so they told her she wasnt going to eat or drink anything until after the biopsy tomorrow.  the next day (which was a saturday) around noon (been waiting all morning for the procedure) they finally told her "we're going to do the biopsy on sunday, sorry for starving you, you can go ahead and eat again, but dont eat after midnight". then sunday came around and late in the day, they told her again sorry for starving you, i guess we'll do the procedure tuesday. my wife asked is she could go home then, and come back for the procedure, they told her it's best to wait here because her bp was kinda high and they want to monitor her (ok, understanable), so my wife asked if she could get dialysis already since her kidneys are bad and she probably needs her blood cleaned out, which is another reason for the high bp. they told her better to wait after the procedure, because they'll do the dialysis right after.  tuesday came, she gets the biopsy done, but they send her back to her room. we asked if she was getting dialysis treatment yet, and the nurses didn't know. later in the evening the doctor visited and was surprised she didnt get started on dialysis.  he said sorry and maybe they're busy that's why. he then said tomorrow (wednesday) they'll get the catheter on her chest/shoulder and start the first dialysis treatment. so now, its wednesday,  we asked the nurse if they knew what's going on, they had no idea. said they'll check it out. came back an hour or so later and said they still dont know because it doesn't show on her chart about dialysis.  so now, the wife is going on 14hrs of no food and taking her anger out on me! smdh!! it seems like communication is not good  between nurses, doctors, cna's, staffs..etc. or maybe they just dont care that much, i dont know. 
anyway, the mix feelings is because there are some nurses that do stay up on things. and then, there are some that dont give a flying fudge, just here to get make a paycheck. meds would be late for hours, they probably forgot about it then remembered. some of the things that's funnily annoying is when they ask "anything i can do for you? anything you need?" and when you requested it "ok! no problem,  i'll be get it right away, i'll be back". then hours go by and we both say "they forgot again! press that nurse button". the main thing i want to point out is their lack of communication, lack of work ethics (for some nurses), i mean at least try right? well, we're all humans and nobody is perfect.  i better go back and comfort the wife because she looks hangry!
p.s. i guess i'll update when she gets dialysis treatment.
the rooms are really old and beat up and the dead flies in the light fixtures just made everything even worse.

i have been experiencing billing problems with saint lukes. i see a cardiologist at their st. luke's idaho cardiology associates in meridian, idaho. i have had 5 visit since april of last year. each time i see a different provider. (i don't care for that.) the last two times the providers they had me see weren't covered by my insurance. they know who my carrier is. the first out of service provider is actually contracted to provide service in nampa but not meridian. saint lukes won't correct that problem and wants me to pay the bill. the second provider they had me see wasn't contracted to provide service at any of their locations even though he was shown as a st lukes health care partner. i contacted their billing department and the vice president of the billing cycle with no luck. be very aware of the providers you see. double check with your insurance before hand to verify coverage. saint lukes will not help you to correct deficiencies within their system

the worst hospital!! horrible rude ass nurses that don't know what the fuck they're doing. nurse abby and nurse assistant michelle felt bothered when we arrived late afternoon. we felt like an incovenience to them. nurse abby said it herself in her thick heavy accent "nobody sent me a report this is ridiculous". they can't even tell you what the medications are for. nurse chika just hands you a cup with 10 pills and says with her thick heavy accent "most of them are for blood pressure". got mad at my brother for asking her why so many pills. told him who was he to question her. we we're kicked out on nye by a "nurse supervisor" by the name lola, very ghetto btw and unprofessional. told us "uhh this too many kids up in hea yall got 60 seconds to get up outta hea.the day before my loved one got discharged nurse elizabeth poked an iv canula on the hand and caused my loved one excrutiating pain. the line was even leaking blood!! but tried to clean it and kept tugging on it causing more pain. im not a dr, but nurse elizabeth doesn't know how to poke!! all she said was "im gonna poke you huhhhhh" sounded like an indian ritual. not the way you help a patient brace themselves before a poke. nurse supervisor chuck comes in and dismisses the pain my loved one was in. said he would document the request for removal of iv. this place is a fucking joke. do your research before accepting your loved one to be transitioned here. i read so many bad reviews online/social media and dind't think it would be that  bad. these people are here for a paycheck, they give two shits about the patient. no wonder locations have been shutting down. i pray to god this location is next. this hospital is a fucking joke

i went to this er on monday . and i have nothing negative to say about any of it. i got in a room within 10 minutes after getting checked in up front . they found out why i was in so much pain and also told me a few other things that i didn't know was also affecting my health . so i give them 5 and the pa i saw that afternoon amy she was awesome and very sweet and caring and she also personally called me and told me about another concern . so i thank them all so much for getting me back on the right track!!

from my first interaction with the reception area,to the person who wheeled me out the door, i received kind,warm,caring and professional attention.
the past reputation of this hospital caused me to hesitate to utilize its services over the years. recently my doctor, who is associate with hospital, felt i needed a procedure done and i acquiesced to have it at emerson.
each and every nurse greeted me with professionalism and empathy. when i expressed my anxiety the anesthesiologist and pre-op nurses assuage my fears with their reassurance and gentle words. each medical intervention the nurses needed to do they attended with explanation and skilled interpersonal interaction.
post surgical care also surpassed my expectations. they treated each patient as if each was the most important person there.
i sensed these nurses enjoy their job and enjoy working with each other and the feeling trickles down to the patients and makes it a much more pleasant experience.
they answered all my questions with smiles on their faces and kindness in their  heart.
when i called a few days later about a few concerns,i received the same amount of caring and friendliness, which impressed me.

review: had a good experience this time. thanks to the expresscare staff for expediting my visit so that i could make it to the pharmacy before they closed. the desk staff, nurse, and np were all efficient in addressing my immediate needs.

after a severe fall i was never checked for a concussion, nor were any x-rays taken. seems since bennington has become an over dose city that is the only way to get any kind of knowledgeable help is to od.

amazing hospital, amazing staff

sat in the emergency room over 7 hours with my daughter who had a fever. her private doctor sent us (we were not a walk-in). right away they told me it was a virus. but it took them 7 hours to get a doctor, do the bloodwork, put in the saline, while all around us the emergency room emptied out. i guess if you're not truly an emergency you sit and wait and wait (but there's no one else here!) i can't help but feel like i am being suckered. if she wasn't sick when we came out, she'll probably be sick by the time we leave.

it's a small hospital i'm told, only 275 beds. not sure what kind of a heart hospital it is but the emergency room is run like a one-room schoolhouse.  northwell is just 10 minutes away. i'd go there.

my mom was brought to st. francis after having intermittent chest and left arm pain despite her ekg coming back clear. she did not have to wait long from coming in by ambulance to start receiving care. immediately her information was taken as well as her vitals. within 5 minutes, she was in a room in the er. once in a room, her blood was drawn and she was kept informed about what the status was. she was very hungry(and the cafeteria was closed) and a nurse brought her a sandwich. she was admitted and within a few hours was in a room(much better than if we had gone to northwell).

once in a room, her nurse took her information and explained how things would go. a nurse came a few hours later to draw blood and get more detailed information. all of the nursing staff(as well as the pca's) were excellent and call button time response was excellent. the night nurses(which is when i was there) were all excellent. asking if i needed anything. the communication between me and the nurses was excellent. the board was always up-to-date with your nurse and pca's names as well as if you were having a procedure that day when you could have your next dose of pain meds as well as your estimated discharge date. 

for a hospital, the food was very good(even having a guest tray for $15). to get your food, you dial 5555 and order from the menu. that is nice because the food only comes when you are hungry(during meal hours) and doesn't just show up when you could be sleeping or not want it. if you miss a meal, they will call you to see if you want to order food. if you haven't ordered dinner, they will call before the end of dinner(6:30) to see if you want anything.

a sister came to visit my mom(when i wasn't there). she asked if my mom had any visitors and my mom felt had she said no, she would have stayed and spent some time with her.

south bay cardiology in west islip is a part of saint francis. their incompetence is surpassed only by their greed. don't use these "doctors" under any circumstances. their only mission is to bankrupt you.

avoid this hospital at all cost.  they are extremely disorganized. my father went for chest pain and their incompetence was evident immediately.  no doctors to be found.  the place ya run by pas.  cardiologist saw him hours later. mind you he was taken by ambulance for chest pain.  we can't even get our medical records from them. avoid at all cost especially for heart related issues.  don't buy that they are a heeled hospital.  it's all marketing.

review:
my dad is staying a the hospital due to a post op infection from a partial knee surgery. he went in to an emergency surgery on 1/1 and they plan to keep him at the hospital until 1/6 (the long stay is due to growing the infection to find the the type, ensuring the infection is flushed out of him and making sure that the antibiotics are working and that he is infection free for a minimum of 48 hours.

for the most part, we are very impressed with the experience. the post-surgery rooms are large with big windows and large couches. even when our whole family is here (5 guests), the room doesn't feel crowded. nearly all of the doctors, nurses, other staff have been very pleasant and helpful. the downstairs area (main entrance and hallways surrounding it) is really nice and does not feel like a hospital - it looks like a downtown area and has street names. 

the biggest complaint so the food here. none of it is good. prices are fair in the cafe ($1 for a small tea or coffee), but the actually meals are pretty bad. even to my dad, who was heavily medicated, hated the food.

the interior looks like i'm inside a mall.  

besides the clinic and medical aspect, there's a pharmacy, kitchen studio, gift shop and restaurant.  i saw a guy wearing his scrubs and playing live in a grand piano.  this hospital makes you feel comfortable. nice people working.   

always have our blood work done.  fast results online.

i worked at the main henry ford hospital campus on west grand boulevard in the late 1970s, and back then it was a great place to work, and a better than average place for patient care. the west bloomfield hospital today is a uniformly excellent place for patient care, at least in my experience. i've been in several times for colonoscopies over the past twenty-five years, as well as tests from cardiology, gastrointestinology, and urology, and on each visit i was treated with great respect and consideration by both medical and administrative staff. the atmosphere is pleasant, more like an upscale mall than a hospital, parking isn't too bad, and waiting areas are generally pleasant.

don't believe the hype. this is only a good looking hospital in west bloomfield, otherwise the quality of care is horrendous.

please, learn from my mistake. if you find yourself in an ambulance with an emt asking you which hospital to go to, under no circumstances say "king's county". say no to this place like your life depends on it. 

my particular horror story happened on a saturday morning when i began feeling a crippling, agonizing and debilitating pain in my abdomen, getting worse and worse. unable to move and barely able to stay conscious, i called 911 and an ambulance took me to the nearest hospital -- king's county. 

i was wheeled into the er on a gurney, crying and screaming in agony. after several minutes, someone asked for my insurance card. thinking that i was about to die, i cried and used profanity to plead for help. she said she didn't like my language and simply walked away.

i lay there, crying in agony and fearful that i was on death's door. i thrashed on my gurney, pleading for help. a full hour went by as i cried and pleaded for help, while the staff all around completely ignored me. i listened through my pain as they gossiped, engaged in long discussions about what they would have for lunch, and as they answered phones from people in distress and then joked about how "stupid" the callers were. after an hour a doctor happened to walk by. i reached out for him, pleading for help. he took one look at me and shouted at the staff that i should be a priority patient. 

i lay in the lobby for another 20 minutes, feet away from the open door in the middle of winter. 

finally i was wheeled into the hospital by a staff member who slammed my gurney into each and every door and wall, furthering the worst agony i had ever experienced. he ignored me, stopping to have a casual chat with another staffer about the upcoming super bowl. he then wheeled me into the middle of a busy hallway in the er, locked the wheels of the gurney, and left me there. for the next half hour, countless people bumped into me as my cries for help went unanswered. after vomiting several times, the pain became so unbearable that i lost consciousness. 

i woke up to a woman asking for my insurance again. i begged her for help, and she just walked away. 30 minutes later a friendly doctor (the only positive part of this experience) briefly examined me in the hallway (where privacy was nonexistent) and said they needed to run tests. after an endless wait, a horrendously mean nurse withdrew 5 vials of blood from my arm (i was later told this was a mistake and they only needed 2, so the others were disposed of). she hooked me up to an iv, left a bunch of literal garbage (wrappers and packaging from needles, etc) on top of me, and left. for 2 hours, no one would acknowledge my presence as i cried in pain. my questions went unanswered. it had been hours since i had anything to drink or gone to the bathroom, and with an empty iv bag connected to my arm, i was literally trapped on the bed, unable to move. 

i asked everyone who walked past (or rather, everyone who bumped into me) but i was ignored. occasionally, a nurse or staff member would walk by and treat me with about as much respect as they would give a stray animal. the staff here have no business dealing with patients, let alone other human beings. interacting with them was undoubtedly the single most dehumanizing experience of my entire life. 

after hours of this agony, of being ignored, of being literally denied the ability the use the bathroom or access to water, i told a staff member that i was on the verge of calling the police to report that i was being held captive against my will and tortured. this got their attention. the doctor came back, surprised that no one had spoken to me, surprised that i had been tied to this bed for so long, and very surprised that the nurse dumped her garbage on top of my lap. she ordered more tests and unhooked my iv. i waited 17 minutes to use the only available bathroom, peed into a cup, and held onto the urine for another 30 minutes until someone took it. after another endless wait, she came back to say she thought i had a kidney stone and suggesting i get a ct scan. well i finally got that scan, but they didn't bother to walk me back to my bed so i got lost, wandering the sprawling hospital halls... 

after a full day of being abused, abandoned, restrained, ignored, and borderline tortured, i wad diagnosed with a kidney stone, given a prescription to pick up from a pharmacy that had already closed, and sent on my way. look, no er is a fun place, and i understand that this one is working under exceptionally difficult circumstances out of their control. but there is simply no justification for what i experienced. i once visited a hospital in an impoverished, rural community in china, and the people there were treated with infinitely more respect and dignity. king's county er resembles a hospital from a post-apocalyptic zombie movie. but in a world without zombies, there is simply no excuse. shame on them. shame! you've been warned.

i was extremely septic and not doing good! i had sharp stomach pains on my right side and my stomach was swollen even though i hadn't been able to keep anything down. i was running a high fever and getting crazy chills for the entire previous week! i walked in christmas eve, when i checked in they took me back in a decent amount of time and put me in those curtain rooms. i was shivering from my fever and they didn't offer me a blanket. i finally got a blanket from the nurse doing my ultrasound! then the mri guy then gave me some warm blankets, after noticing my shivers. i hadn't eaten or drank anything all day cuz i threw it all up. i asked for ice chips and the dr cleared it. i ask 4 different people if i could have ice chips and they said they would get me some and i never saw them again! i hardly saw the nurse in charge of me and he's one of the one that i repeatedly ask for ice chips! i finally got ice chips when my husband came back from getting kids settled with family. i finally got ice chips. it took me 4 hours to get ice chips and shortly after that they gave me my diagnosis and said i was severely septic and that i would be staying the night. i stayed in that same curtain room for over 3 more hours. finally, the nurse in charge of giving me a potassium drip in my iv had just started her rounds and noticed how long i had been in the "fast track" area and found me a temporary room which was right next to the bathroom! hallelujah! i finally got a room a bit later. i got in my room and i was shivering so bad that i had my room temperature set for 85+ degrees. i told them that i had a fever but if it was 99.9% or lower they wouldn't give me anything! i would fall back to sleep to a extremely high fever that 1 time got up to 103. after getting fever meds i asked the head nurse if she could turn down the heater in my room because i knew i was going to get really hot once my fever was gone! she said she would and i did my best to fall asleep. when i woke up about an hour later i was soaked from head to toe in sweat! i then realize she didn't even touch the thermostat and i had to fix it myself! i had to change my clothes and they didn't bother to remake my bed! the daytime nurses noticed my room didn't have a phone or a menu at all. the day nurses took good care of me! i had to stay another night and that night at 12:50am i was shivering really bad and i told the nurse i was running a fever. missy who was the assistant nurse came in and checked my temperature, i was at 100.76. she said she would go get some tylenol for me and before leaving said that i couldn't have both of my blankets on because i was going to boil my brain by being to warm! i protested that was cold and couldn't possibly get rid of a blanket. i was noticeably cold because my teeth wouldn't stop chattering! despite my protests she took my top blanket off and said i could keep the sheet! i was shocked at her barbaric treatment and as soon as she left i pulled the blanket back on. i noted the time and incident. i dosed off while waiting only to wake up 40 min later and she never came back! i hit the call button and the head nurse came in i told her i was running a fever and the other nurse said she would get me something and all of a sudden the other nurse charges in the room trying to cover her butt because she didn't note it in my file that i had a fever and also failed to mention it to anyone including the head nurse. then proceeded to ask her private questions about other patients in front of me. the head nurse was noticeably upset about her negligence and lack of professionalism! even more upset when i told her about the blanket issue and how long i had been waiting! she made sure to check on me the rest of the night and keeping me comfortable i'm glad to say i was actually able to rest for a couple of hours at a time which wasn't happening before. the rest of my stay which i was luckily uneventful! i was released that afternoon. i'd watched christmas story 48,000 marathon and finally got to go home the day after christmas! i still wasn't feeling good and my white blood cell count was still extremely high. but i was safe enough to finish resting and antibiotics at home! i told my husband i don't care if i'm "supposed" to leave i can't stay one more night here and if it got bad again i'd pick a better place to be a patient in! it reminded me a lot of the lengthy hospital stay i had at the old mesa lutheran 36 years ago! the look and feel....oh and the food! yuck it was awful! my son stayed at cardon children's last year and their food is delicious gourmet and freshly cooked! i thought all hospitals were with the times but unfortunately i stand corrected! i'm hoping to put this nightmare behind me and not see the inside of another hospital(especially this one!) ever again!

i am not impressed with this hospital at all. i had my baby a year ago and had recieved prenatal monitoring here. i am still getting bills from them. i had requested and itemized printout of services rendered as well as payment recieved months ago. i haven't heard back so i thought we were paid off. then recently we get another bill and i have no idea what it is for. recently i have been very depressed and had asked the billing department to call my husband regarding all financial issues. guess what they called me today. i currently am at the point where i would rather die than seek any medical care. please listen yo your patients.

this review is for the er. i went in because i had the most excruciating stabbing headache. i had surgery here a week ago and my discharge papers said to go back to this hospital if i had complications. i went back, the two front girls that were signing me in were too busy talking to each other. then once i was called in the guy taking my vitals, older, really tall man, white hair, was rude! he literally made me feel bad for going to er for just a headache. he then got a text message and took this phone out in front of me, stopped doing his job and just started texting ! i can't imagine what they do when patients aren't around if that's how he acted. i was like hmm maybe it's just the people in the front that were off. nope then once i went in, the nurse( don't remember her name but blonde, and had a really bad orange tan) asked me my pain range, i said 10, she then said seriously 10, like the worst? i said yes this is the worst headache in my life!!!! i can barely open my eyes, or walk, why would i come in here for something non emergency. she then said okay i'll give you some medicine for the headache? i asked if she will do any testing or ct scan, she said no it's way too much radiation for something non emergency. so what does it take?????  me to flatline????? anyways, i ended up checking out because i heard her go back and tell the other nurses " i have a headache too" and they all laughed. wow just wow: i then asked to be discharged, i didn't tell them why because i already felt like a laughing stock. i never imagined going to seek care and feeling like crud because of people who's job is to care and help.!!! they literally talked about a patient in front of others! i should've read the reviews before i came in!!! anaheim global fix your staff to have some bedside manner !!! listen to your patients and reviews!!!! never coming here again!!! wouldn't even bring my worst enemy here !!!

nurses were turning around and gossiping about patients with mental health disorders security guards standing around not doing anything front desk staff was absolutely deplorable i am definitely filing a medical with the medical board of the state of california on this hospital

this review is for the er, specifically for the nurse named malinory or something like that from last nights shift. you shouldn't become a nurse for money, you should do it because you love helping and caring for people who are in pain and need. i've never felt so ignored by a nurse in my life then last night. why do i have to ask to go to the restroom 3 times before i could go? and when asked where it was she replied "where it is". does it look like i know where the room i was put it  is at and where the restroom is from there? very very rude nurse. acted like she didn't know anything when i asked. after waiting and waiting and nothing, i asked to be released. it took more then 30 mins after asking her to just release me so she could come with the clipboard and make me sign. i was reading and she kept saying sign here and i told her i'm reading what i'm signing. she just stood there then. why did i have to be flagging her down every 5 mins to come give me the paperwork. she would acknowledge me with just a nod when she saw me out of bed and keep sitting down. she told me i would see the dr. before leaving but that never happened. she just kept me there to ignore me more. wasted hours here. never again going to this hospital or recommending this hospital to anyone. if you want medical attention don't waste your time here.

this review is specifically for l&d. i was visiting a family member who was going into labor at night time. there were a couple of older nurses who were extremely unprofessional and lazy. just standing around gossiping. at some point during the night, one fell asleep at the desk and another came back from outside reeking of cigarettes. there are pregnant mothers and newborns around, come on.. management needs to do something about these unprofessional nurses.

this hospital has helped a loved one more than words can imagine. they saved his life on many occasions.  many thanks to the lady i met there who is by far superior in nursing betty on 6b and hannah.  many thanks especially to housekeeping they have who is simply the best on floor 4b when our loved one was down there.
dr. jalal was so helpful, and dr. joseph o'gorman,  do.
words cannot express gratitude in this condition.

i would rather die than go back to the emergency room here. not one bad experience but two! er staff has no compassion of patience, the blankets are always dirty. they need to fire everyone and start fresh

good medical care, probably the worst customer service in the industry. we were making regular payments on a successful procedure performed at memorial, but they turned us over to a collection agency anyway. they will be several months sending out a bill and then if you don't pay it off immediately they turn you over to a collection agency. when my father was ill they actually wanted a quarter of a million dollar lump sum payment upfront. there is no defending their business practices

it's a shame this is the only hospital in carthage. not happy with it at all. will drive to freeman in joplin from now on. i had a massive blood blot in my leg, couldn't walk, couldn't bend it. they gave me a shot to start blood thinning and a percocet that did nothing for pain. if i go to an er it's because i cant take it any longer. i hate hospitals and will likely just stay home next time. i guess addicts are making drs so scared to treat patients they'll send ya back out in the same condition you arrived. makes it pointless to even go to a dr anymore. when ask why not was given for pain he said the dea told him they'd rather 1000 people od on heroin than one person on pain meds. people aren't dying from prescribed pain meds. they're dying from meds not prescribed and fentanyl. but that's the american way, make everyone pay the price because the dea cant stop the bad stuff so they stop it all.

this er is absolutely rude. they are not helpful at all. there is an employee by the name of kent who is probably the rudest person i have ever encountered. i called to complain on him and nothing. of course he is protected. i will not send my people back to this mercy until he is gone. poor care, they don't even know their own policies and they have no idea about the hipaa laws. not a clue. but trust me, kent knows everything! he refuses to send information even with a release signed. i was talked to like i was a child and hung up on. deal with someone else when you go to the er. he is horrible to deal with.

these people don't even deserve the 1-star i have to give them! my child who is in lubbock going to school at tech went to this emergency room twice in one week with gastric distress. the 1st time they threw antibiotics at her but in the same sentence told her she just had a virus. the 2nd time (one week later) she returned with the same symptoms but they were much much worse. the dr. entered her room with a finance person and stated 'this is not an emergency' and he wouldn't treat her until she handed over her credit card and paid $200. the dr. gave her more bogus meds. 12 hours later she was admitted to umc for five days!! so much for not being an emergency. 

and to come at a 21 year old kid demanding money who is very sick and has great insurance that does not require a co-pay is a jerk move. save yourself and go somewhere else. i'm so angry i want to scratch all their eyes out.

the wait time to get admitted is horrendous. we waited 6 hours to get a room.  the volunteers, nurses, & dr's are extremely nice, however, some of the security guards are extremely rude and can't even say hello or crack a smile, which is unacceptable. the rooms do not have blackout curtains, so if your child is used to sleeping in the dark, good luck as it is a challenge and naps are impossible in these rooms. definitely prefer going to the cm in op, ks.

veterans beware !!!

i am a veteran  and prisma health or whatever they are calling themselves today does not honor veterans.

i've had three procedures done by prisma health referred by the veterans health admin and each time prisma has tried to bill me when the va was clearly responsible for the charges. once i received a bill a year later after the procedure was performed. each time i've had to prove to them that the va was responsible for the bill when my procedure was  approved and prisma notified by the va before any appointment was even set up. the accounting dept of prisma has no clue or maybe they do, maybe this is normal procedure to only scam and try to get more money from patients. i would not be surprised if billing was at both ends. surprise billing and ignoring the va seems to be the norm at prisma health. this hospital is just a huge corporate profit enterprise who does not care about patients.

transitioning from the portland va medical center to the washington, dc center has been an overwhelmingly frustrating experience, to say the least. from the constant sexual harassment to unprofessional demeanors demonstrated by staff members, i am appalled by the negative culture/climate illustrated. the portland va has a separate campus for the women's health clinic, which serves as an invaluable option for female vets. at the dc center, one must pass the gauntlet of inappropriate comments, and the like, before reaching a poorly structured (and arguably, abysmal) women's health clinic. 

my physician input incorrect referrals that i was forced to track down by physically visiting various clinics. adding injury to insult, secure messaging requests via myhealthevet were not honored within a timely manner (less than 48 hours). receiving a radiology report regarding a health issue with a note to "wait until our next visit," which is greater than 3 weeks out, is unacceptable and clinically questionable. as a retired air force flight nurse, i am greatly disappointed with this situation.

i haven't utilized valet services since encountering a belligerent employee during an initial visit and the majority of the employees within the hospital that i have encountered are either too busy or unconcerned regarding the toxic climate. 

stay as far away from the dc va as humanly possible, or request a community care referral asap. you have rights, and you've earned the right to decent healthcare. get what you need and stay the heck away from this horrific medical facility!

i have found the medical care provided for my dad to be very good at the va hospital in dc..   the optical shop by entrance is manned by a woman named rasjawn with a big negative attitude.  she is rude to the veterans.  
with so many people wanting a job and wanting to serve veterans, why would you allow a habitual chip on shoulder type to work there.  so many good changes, dintarr the good with a few bad apples

review:
i wasn't going to write a review. but i wanted to tell you guys regarding my experience at icu eden medical center.

my father was hit by a car. was admitted for severe brain trauma. i'm thankful that eden took my father in and that the neuro / trauma doctors did the surgery to release the pressure from his brain. the specialist doctors were awesome. there was a few nurses that were wonderful in taking care of my father. but some of them would make really bold remarks. yes, i do know my father is in a coma and might never wake up. but the way one of the nurses said it was not a good. they would make comments when they thought me or my siblings were asleep "i heard that we done everything and there's nothing more we can do" that to me sounds like you are giving up on my father and even if you done everything you keep on trying. the nurses who cared and they didn't treat my father like "i'm just doing this because is my job" would ask me how my father was. what would he be doing right now? what were his days like? i work in the medical field. but this was just disappointed. we already have mix emotions and to top it off with the remarks some of the nurses would make. it was totally uncalled for. 

also dr. ghandi would talk to us about if it was her "very spiritual" and if my father knew in the state he probably wouldn't want to live this way. i fell like she wanted us to take my dad off the ventilator. i hope am wrong. but either way it was to soon to have that conversation. it was barely a week and half from the severe brain injury and she wanted to have this conversations. 

thank you to the case manager. they were very helpful. help us with work letters and if we approve or deny certain things. they also help us in transferring my father as soon my father was okay to be transferred. 
the security staff were friendly.

review:
awful service! 
we are still waiting and we've been here for 3 hour and the waiting room is so empty; so there is no reason for this wait time. do not come here.

if you have a choice, avoid this hospital until they resolve their patient drop off and pick off bottleneck due to their on-going construction. the system they have in place is an embarrassment - either stage additional satellite parking locations, shuttles, valet stations - whatever it takes to remove the congestion on reservoir rd. just a horrible, horrible experience before you even set foot on the property. and today the parking attendants are only accepting cash because their credit card system is down. what a joke. avoid this hospital.

how can i say georgetown hospital has gone down! do not ever go to this hospital for an emergency.  i repeat...don't do it to yourself or a loved one. i spent over 8 hours in the emergency room.  i could have traveled to at least 8 different hospitals during my wait.

how does a hospital allow a patient to sit in the emergency room for over eight hours after telling the triage nurse that their symptoms include a head spinning, and periodic sharp pain in the chest, leg, arm, and neck?  in the meantime at least 5 people that arrived after me with what appeared to be common cold/flu symptoms were sent back for treatment.  the last time i checked cold symptoms were not considered an emergency.  

what type of triage is this? hell, what type of hospital emergency room is this? if an experienced doctor is not available to diagnose and treat patients with diverse illnesses, staff could have at least communicated this to me so i could have chosen another hospital.  

also, i need to know why in the world are staff taking vitals, blood, and urine right smack in the middle of the er waiting room next to the registration desk. talk about no privacy and just down right inconsiderate.  i just cannot with this hospital at this point.

now lets get to the lackluster registration staff including the nurses at the front desk.  please train your staff to be empathetic and show at least the slightest bit of concern for patients.  please remember that me and my  insurance are paying good  hard earned money for my er visit which in turn is paying your wages.

get it together right now georgetown hospital! we can not wait for future renovations just to see the basics achieved.  your name should be changed from medstar to medbelowpar!

this hospital kept us in the waiting room throwing up and very ill. even after i was seen, they put me back in the waiting room and did not take care of us with a needle in their patients arm still. i do not recommend it at all  and they do not care about their patients.

if i could give this place 0 stars i would. i left work early after waiting 2.5 months to obtain an appointment with the doctor i had researched online. upon arrival, the gentleman at the front desk told me that i was not in the system for an appointment and the doctor i was supposed to see was not there. mind you this is after 6 or so received confirmations.  he told me to have a seat to see what could be done  10 minutes. 20 minutes pass. i finally come up and he tells me there's nothing that can be done and i'll have to come back. i said that that was not an option and he went back to meet with the team. a lady then comes out and grabs me... no new patient forms or anything as everyone else was completing and starting conducting what she called an "interview" on a random paper she grabbed of her desk.  i have never seen anything like it. she then told me to go back and wait and the patient manager grabbed me back into this office to tell me that no one will see me today and they were going to ask me these questions anyway that they wrote on a random paper that anyone can see and that because i was in for a regular check up as a new patient it was not urgent which they outlined on the paper. then she wanted to set me up to come back. i will not be coming back here or seeing their doctors. how unfortunate.... i just wanted to make sure i was healthy.  do not go here. what a waste of time.

this is for one recent excruciating experience, although i've seen gu perform better in happier days.  a loved one recently tripped and fell down a flight of stairs and hurt her elbow, and we just went in to confirm whether it was a fracture, a break, stage iii pancreatic, or just something to put some tiger balm on and rest up.  after an hour+ in the rather slow-traffic waiting room filling out some pretty scintillating paperwork, we were ushered by the qualified powers that be into an area resembling a world war i field clinic and sequestered behind some flimsy curtain for at least two hours while these brainiacs sped around looking at various (others patients') charts, provided zero updates unless proactively solicited, and barely made eye contact with us even though they were obviously over-staffed and under-patiented.  we got one personal visit from the head cheese who then went on to bigger and better things (perhaps a head cold for the gent over behind curtain 5a) and couldn't be bothered to convey to us what, in what, after a likely three hundred years of experience in this practice, she could've told us in about 20 minutes). meantime, the purple scrubbed worker bees were busily buzzing around alternately looking at various charts on various computer screens and, um, checking their latest like, coat of nail polish.  (how many gals who just graduated with a pa license from strayer online does it take to manage an er full of, say, 5-7 patients?  15-20, apparently.  three to four illustrious worker bees for each patient lucky enough to end up at this underwhelming facility - not a bad ratio, in theory, but practice falls short, believe you me.)  no bedside manner (the key, glaring deficiency), sparing smiles, more or less basic command of verbal communication but nothing to write home about.  thankfully the news was good, but we would have appreciated it a couple of hours earlier.  and, hey, i'm not a medical operations specialist or anything, but perhaps an emergency room operation can optimize efficiency and effectiveness by clearing easy cases out sooner rather than later?  disappointing experience.  we'll opt for gwu, sibley or the effing minute clinic at pentagon city mall the next time around.

i can't say enough good things about dr eric anderson of pulmonology and dr. margolis and the thoracic surgery team.  the best nurses on c4-1 ever we're lou, stephanie, and erin.  they made sure to communicate with my mom what was going on and took the extra time with her when she needed it.  communication included things like, i am busy right now, can you give me an hour and i will walk with you.  the reason i gave two stars is for the communication between the depts, the nurses and the doctors as well as the parking.  the doctors would tell my mom one thing and not communicate it to the rest of the staff.  prime example my mom was to be ready to go by noon on the day of discharge and she was no where near ready.  getting medicine when she needed it to was another pain in the neck.  parking sucked! i found out that there is a pass for people who have family members who are staying for an extended time three days before shelby mom was discharged.  and this is after almost two weeks.  do you know how much money that is?!?!  not one word from the nurses, the parking staff or anyone who saw me on an almost daily basis.  as for the er, wonderful care from the start.  from liz who took us in to the nurses.  i know from other reviews that the er got a hard knock, but please remember, as much as it sucks being in pain, it is an er and they triage

harlem hospital is the worst hospital.  unprofessionalism is rampant at this so-called hospital.  tried to call to cancel an appointment. each time i call, there is always a busy signal.  typical ghetto hospital!
excellent care!!  beautiful setting.  the staff is just the best here and the facility is warm and welcoming.

the best of the best. my doctor here was wonderful, staff were wonderful, security was always helpful with questions, and they had tons of information desks, maps, and wow the food options were not just plentiful but good. i always find it a tad chuckle worthy when you go to a hospital and all they are serving is unhealthy food in the cafeteria. like... huh??
northwestern talks and walks with the same intention. yes, there is unhealthy food, but the plethora of options of fantastic healthy food is just praiseworthy. this location is so nice sometimes i would work remote from their lobby when i was in the area. 
also! they just announced they are putting 78 million into an emergency department expansion to cut down on wait times. 

exceptional, and that's just the facts

have been debating leaving a review on here but i see others have had a similar experience so here goes...

many years ago i went to the er here because of a debilitating headache that came on suddenly. despite that fact (and the fact that i told the attending doctor that i had a family history of cerebral aneurysms) the doctor literally treated me like i was a crackhead chasing a high, even asking me if i ever used cocaine before prescribing some ibuprofen. not sure if this hospital just has issues with treating "certain people" but i went to another hospital that not only treated me decently, actually ran tests to make sure that what i had wasn't life-threatening just based on my family history. i don't ask for much, but being treated like a human being is at the top of my list. not only will i never go here again under any circumstance i won't recommend it, either.

nmh is such a comfortable place for a hospital stay in downtown chicago. it's clean without feeling "too sterile" and the artistic installations throughout the building evoke a sense of home. there are about a dozen restaurants on the 2nd floor at reasonable prices. thank you to our amazing surgical team led by dr. gregory dumanian! we loved our 12th floor nurses including, alyssa, ro and lindsay. the pre-op nurses and pcts were also all-stars and the 12th floor chef monica made a delicious dinner and husband for my husband who has a ton of food allergies. 

pro tips:
- all ride shares can be accessed in the gelter pavilion by the arrivals entrance
- the walgreens pharmacy on the 2nd floor has everything you need for an unexpected overnight stay

top quality medical care. 
i came back here for hip replacement surgery instead of getting it done in my home state of louisiana.  (no duh)!!
they are meticulous,  super professional,  polite, knowledgeable.
i can't say enough. 
if your insurance allows it, i recommend 
northwestern without reservation.

this the second time i had the unfortunate experience of bringing my wife to northwestern emergency room. 
average wait time is between 6 to 7 hours. 
i came in at 11am and was not admitted until 3am the following day. 
my wife had an acute condition and was told by her primary go to northwestern er, but we still waited.
there should be an acute er for individuals with acute conditions and then another er for the individuals that have strain/sprains and head colds.
after the second er experience i changed my medical group to doctors out of university of chicago. much better and professional experience. and actually it is a much higher ranked hospital. 
also the gate keepers gals at northwestern er are rude and insensitive.

very unprofessional. i actually took myself out of their program due to very poor communication. if you have a terminal illness you would think they would at least contact you about results? think again. you have to call, write, beg for a call and usually get someone who has no clue and will 'send your questions on to the people who know'. then never get a response....again.

the only time you hear from them is when they schedule you for another vastly expensive procedure or test. and even then its just a mychart notice. 

they have some good nurses onsite when getting something done but it ends there.

but all they care about is cramming scans, exams, procedures down your throat without giving any more information. it is chaotic, a keystone cop act. left and right hand have no clue what the other is doing. transplant team rep? keeps making promises that never come through. 

team social worker? unbelievable at best. abrasive, condescending and useless. even she said transplant was not an option but i needed to keep coming back for tests and scans? not even a doctor and making prognosis?

each doctor gives different information.they keep swapping people around and never tell you. 

transplant team nurse is haughty and unfeeling at best. i have a friend who underwent a transplant 4 years back who had the same issues! they get mad at you for asking for information, but never remedy the issue.

her reply when i said i wanted out of the program? "ok. it's done.". nothing else!  lol

it is beyond ridiculous. looking at the top transplant hospitals in the usa they cannot even make the top 15, what does that tell you?

it's all about the money. we refuse to give you the exact prognosis but just keep spending a couple hundred thousand on useless tests and procedure we know will not work or give more information. they know those things will not fix anything but they can grab tons of cash from insurance either way.

i ended up moving my entire transplant plan to another hospital. now i can get real updates, no 'i don't know" garbage, and real information i can use to plan for future possible events. after talking to 5 different doctors from 5 different sites they were concerned i needed better treatment. not to mention a doctor in my own family and some nurses as well.

wouldn't recommend this place for anyone with transplant needs.

shout out to dr. mark agulnik in heme/oncology and his fabulous team!!! my wife is under his care and she has been so well cared for. northwestern is a world class sarcoma center. we are so lucky and grateful to have been directed to northwestern!!!

i have been going for 3 years. procedures, surgeries and inpatient stays. 
this is not a place to go to be cared for. they do not listen to you. it is disconnected patient care. all about money and procedures,get you in and out. have an issue good luck. you are on your own. 
i often referred to it as prison care. meaning, i felt like a prisoner without support of anyone. i had to be hospitalized after surgeries my heart was stressed afib. 
they scared me into getting on a medication that i would need to be inpatient to get on. 4-5 days. the 4th day i was so over medicated my b/p 90/40 hr 40s i pleaded with them to lower the dose. it's too high. not comfortable taking it. 
they did not listen. 
the next day.  i was to be discharged, i was told i need to stay another day and medication needs to be lowered. 
prison care. locked down in the system for another day and night. knowing, i was unheard. did they care? no. after, i was so upset.  stating, i begged no one listened. one dr said i would of listened to you. ok sure. i don't believe you. 
i have many more just like this i'm going to continue to share so others do know we have choices. northwestern is not the best. and patients do not come first. 
rush
loyola
lutheran general 
and more other hospitals in chicago area. 
if we continue to give this hospital business
