this review is regarding the in-patient general hospitalization-not the er which is where our visit started. since i am usually a positive person, i'll start with the positive:
     every single staff member from the receptionist to the triage nurse to the er nurse to the er dr's to the transporters were so incredibly sweet and attentive. the er entrance is tiny and overwhelmed with people. inside is the same way. so in spite of the terrible design, lack of space, and the overwhelming number of patients the er has, everyone handled themselves with such grace and treated the patients with such care. as stressed as their er employees must be by the sheer volume of cases they handle daily/nightly, everyone we met seemed to keep a great attitude and a calm demeanor. 

now, to the in-patient part,  wow! was this the same hospital?! that was my thought. in reading through previous yelp reviews, my family & i experienced the exact same discharge issues as others have. this is highly disturbing and worrisome. there needs to be a state investigation into their practices because i am sure that some would not hold up to the state law. i am going to actually file a complaint with the hospital and medical board. the main issues:
-incorrect diagnosis/follow up instructions on discharge paperwork. paperwork completed incorrectly/altered to make it look like the patient is ready to go home. in fact the nurse's & dr's attitudes made it terribly clear that they wanted my family member out asap so they could make space for their afternoon admits.
-both nurse and dr completely ignored my repeated statements that my family member's current health problems developed only following a fall and that this was actually what motivated the er to admit this person in the first place! what did the dr say, "he'll get a walker and a diaper. he's going home" in response to my request that the specialist that was called in the a.m. be fully informed of the symptoms my family member was experiencing. yes, my family member was released unable to get out of bed, unable to walk without assistance, & with additional concerning medical issues. we were told to wait for home hospital to call us in 24-48 hours. thank god that my family member has family who can step up and do the caregiving needed. imagine the person released who has not any family and is not able to lift themselves out of bed and cannot walk??!

-what happened when i asked them to correct their paperwork so we could use the paperwork as instructed? the case manager/nurse waved me off and told me i would have to request complete medical records downstairs. it was my first experience having to go in search of papers showing the correct diagnosis and follow up recommendations! 

-nurse gave incorrect instructions on otc meds dr prescribed. thank god again that i carefully read the discharge papers to find out that the med did not need to be taken as the nurse stated!!

-nurse was visibly stressed, wanted her lunch break before p.m. admits (stated this) & in a hurry with discharge paperwork so she ended throwing med bottles at my family member's feet as she attempted to correctly document the medication. at one point she was kind enough to ask, "did i hit you?" she kept having to come back because she couldn't get the meds written down despite having been given a list and the actual bottles. 

-nurse never put orders in for food for my family member after his emergency surgery was cancelled at 9am. my family member received no breakfast and no lunch. by 3pm, i finally requested lunch for him! 

-we were told we'd be talking with a social worker/case manager. that person never came and when i went to ask, a person shrugged and said they were a case manager but would not be talking to us. we were again told just go home and wait for a call from home hospital in 24-48 hours then waved off. 

if you or your family member want a hospital who makes mistakes, doesn't listen correctly to patients, & discharges people in such a haphazard and unorganized manner (i mean even the nurse's assistant forgot to dress my family member before leaving for the day and the stressed nurse made this clear to us!! i had to ask for my family member to be dressed!), then this may be the hospital for you. they are clearly looking at profit over patient care but it's to the point where you may be released in a worse state than in which you arrived and you may even be given incorrect instructions and reports. you may be, in some ways, worse off than before you were admitted. having strong family support is a must in case you need to come here. otherwise, steer clear for your health's sake.

i was at the hospital for five hours coughing really bad and the hospital e/r was some what kinda busy and i understood that and the staff in the lobby didn't do anything to make sure i was okay or needed anything. so five hours later the e/r rn came and got me and asked me if i was okay? i was like no ma'am i am not okay i am coughing really bad, shaking, not feeling well she took me to my e/r room then took my temperature and then left me then i went for a x ray then went back to my room and the technician came in basically left me there not asking me anything if i needed anything. only person who was doing there job was the rn "register nurse" and no one else could have careless most of them were complaining how busy it was.

overall this place is a good hospital but needs to keep up with the patients who come in to the hospital who are sick and needs to be seen. also don''t let the patients here how the staff talk towards "how busy they are and so on"

i gave birth to my 3rd child here at sutter davis birthing center. i preregistered so when i came in my delivery room was ready. this was a big concern for me because my last birth very fast and i want able to make it to the room and instead i had my first son in the checkin room. for my 3rd delivery i planned a water birth but when i got to the hospital this time my contractions where so close meaning that there wasn't enough time to get to tub filled. even though i didn't get to have a water birth like i planned i did have my son natural and the experience was amazing thanks to lois, kathy and sandy. addition to them are the wonderful nursing staff, techs, ped doctors, lactation consultants, midwives. i appreciate their thoroughness, kindness and professionalism.  they made my for day stay feel like a vacation. with their help i was able to transition into breastfeeding postpartum care and study for an upcoming exam.

the e.r.  staff is kind and they really care about their patients. they are all efficient and they made me very comfortable during my visit. it was not busy when i arrived and i was only there for two hours. i felt safe at this location. there were two police officers parked outside. i will come back if i have another emergency.

irecently had knee surgery at menorah medical center the staff and everyone involved in my care was absolutely amazing i have had many other procedures in my past and this is by far the best hospital i've ever stayed at.
medical errors, disinterested doctors, some mediocre nursing, yes menorah has it all.  unless you have a minor medical problem you are likely to fare better at a major medical center.

my father in 2013 was there twice the first time was ok he had a bag and did not need personal care. the second time was a horror. i walked in he was nude laying in his waste door closed. i know the knew his room was right outside the nurse's break room and the respiratory tech was to come at 6:30 each day and i got there at 6:45. they said he was released to go to rehab on thursday. i got a call from the rehab place that he had pneumonia saturday morning and needed to go to the hospital at 8 am when i got there at 9. they said he was septic and would not make it through the day. he was dead less than 48 hours after they said he was well enough to leave. must go every day. do not be fooled by the floors for transplant patients ask to see other floors.

my mother in the hospital, i called the front desk to transfer my call to her room the person answered the phone insist that no one was there by that name. the security desk on the previous day didn't have a problem finding her name in the system. the call center/ receptionist didn't know her job!! and she was rude!! incompetent as hell!

i was unexpectedly admitted for a couple days following an outpatient procedure. everyone - the nurses, aides, dietary staff, hospitalist, lab techs, and specialists - were top-notch! i was not expecting to be hospitalized, but fort hamilton hospital - kettering health network far exceeded my expectations! friendly, helpful, knowledgable, and professional staff throughout this facility.
fac_name: Fort Hamilton Hospital - Kettering Health Network

review:
i have never experienced such an incredible experience. this is the most wonderful team you will ever encounter, this place is truly a gem. if you are looking for a way to birth your way, have midwives that are all actual nurses but are the jack of all trades and still have all the security of a hospital and emergency care this is the perfect combination. from the moment i called, the whole team took my situation seriously and got me in quick for induction. they were so loving and kind! dr. blake was incredible. he was patient and efficient and allowed me to push for 2+ hours to deliver a higher risk baby that very well couldve had to be a c-section baby at any other hospital but thanks to him and his team and a lot of hard work, he came out safely and beautifully.  they truly fought for me and my baby and treated us like we were top priority from the very first phone call. they did an amazing job at delivering our baby boy and handled everyone of my concerns with so much ease. dr. blake and his team truly care about us moms, they are their biggest advocate. i cannot reccomend this place enough. we truly felt like family. 

 plus, what hospital let's their patients sleep while the incredible nurses tend and rock baby outside in the hallway? (just an extra little perk;) ) 


also, we werent kept any extra time and didnt have a ton of interruptions from random county services like bigger facilities and the food was awesome, best authntic mexican breakfast burritos!

a dear friend of ours was scheduled here for an outpatient exploratory surgery (he is 93) that's scary all by itself. 
the nurses are exceptional "nan" in outpatient went way above making "whitey" feel safe. she not only explained everything that was going to happen to him, but she stayed with him during most of the procedure...... she also took care of his very nervous family (us). the doctors decided to do more testing and to keep him overnight.....twice 
once he was admitted who should show up in his room but "nan" to make sure he was ok. 
sorry to say the testing did not go so well, one outpatient surgery turned into 3 full days.....our dear "whitey" was not prepared for this so as you can image he was not happy.

he is home now still waiting on test results we will see!
not like it's too much of a choice since i had pneumonia, but was definitely one of the better hospital experiences..

this is the worst hospital in the  valley. mom was admitted this morning and will have to spend the night. we are at room #423, a room for pysc patients! the reason they gave us is because the hospital is so full and this is the only room they have. i'm telling you if  you are not psycho, this room will make you one! the bathroom has a faucet that will make you ask wtf! there is no trash can in the room, no hand soap, no hygiene stuff that you will see in a regular hospital. you have to ask and wait for everything you need. the tv has been on and off since this afternoon, have called maintenance 4 times now and you can only leave a message. it is already night time and how can you expect to sleep with this tv turning on and off. even the cnas, nurses, rts who came in to our room are bothered by this, so what can u expect from us who are staying here for 24 hours? this is just so unacceptable. i hope that this will be a 24 hour ordeal, otherwise, we will check out even without doctor's order. i swear never never to come back to this ho

my dad came into imc in with low oxygen and congestive heart failure.  we have been thrilled with the quality of care here in every way!  it seems like he has made a full recovery in a short time!
we love the team work the nurses demonstrate- they help each patient not just their own whenever needed.  we had the best nurses and cna's anywhere!  despite uncomfortable  and embarrassing situations all the nurses especially christina always made my dad feel comfortable.  they even treated me well while i was with my dad.

in las vegas for a business expo. stepped off a curb and lost balance fell and injured wrist. this was 7 pm. next morning wrist was swollen and painful. called front desk and they recommended spring valley emer. they accepted medicare. the wait was short. they did x-ray and put in a splint. the people were super nice and efficient. i would recommend them highly.

3 minutes ago-edit
i would give this hospital zero stars if yelp allowed for it. i was admitted while traveling in las vegas in 2018 for emergency care around a pre-existing medical condition. i am very grateful the hospital was able to stabilize me and ultimately allow me to travel home. however, what came next was a saga around billing issues that is still ongoing. the hospital initially billed my out of state insurance an amount so egregious ($19,000 +) that insurance initially denied the majority of the claim. 

instead of negotiating a settlement with the insurance provider - as the hospital customer service department initially told me they would do - the hospital attempted to "balance bill" me over $18,000 for the cost of emergency care. after months of protracted mediation between the hospital and my insurance provider, i was able to get insurance to pay an additional $16,500 to spring valley as a settlement in the matter. at this point i thought the situation was resolved.

unfortunately, i was wrong, as several months later spring valley started trying to "balance bill" me again for an additional $1,924 they claim to still be owed. 

after dealing with the deceptive, hostile billing customer service department that represents the hospital for nearly a year when trying to negotiate a settlement in this case, i attempted to contact the hospital directly about this issue through the "contact us" form on the website several months ago - to no reply. instead, i've continued to get harassing mailers from them threatening collections against me on this latest bill. at this point i am working through additional legal options to remedy this latest issue with the hospital.

i am not one to publicly post negative reviews of businesses in my day-to-day life, especially hospitals as they are an essential service for many of us. however, given the awful experience i have had with this hospital after interacting with it, i thought it was important to share my story as a caution for others who might find themselves in a similar situation down the line.

spring valley hospital located near the west 215, easy access from rainbow exit or drop down from tropicana to rainbow, easy to find, lots of  food options nearby, plus a cafeteria/restaurant inside has both hot food and other options 24/7. 
lovely facility, lovely people, easy access in and out very friendly. one note at 9pm they lock the main entrance so you have to walk thru emergency to get inside. 
quiet and what i might call a boutique hospital. known for their ability to treat brain trauma with one of the best acute rehabilitation units available on the third floor. 
icu rooms are large with sleeping chairs, they are happy to give blankets, pillows, water, caring for the support family as well as patient. huge shout out to calista, rowena, in icu, they have the spirit of florence nightengale and mother teresa bringing such a love, kindness and generosity of compassion into the room. 
then there's sonya, grittel, winn, & michelle in the intermediary care unit, with a standup routine that brought humor and joy into the room. ladies i salute you, you are each fabulous and we as the family are soooooooooo very grateful!!!
thank you...may god bless you, utterly

if i could give  no stars i would. absolutely the worst hospital i have ever been to. arrived at 7:00am with my significant other who has a heart condition as he was having chest pains and leaving with no answers at all, except to call his cardiologist and have more test done with him. how do you know he needs to see a cardiologist? you have ran no test to know if it was his heart. handing a patient an aspirin and making them sit in a cubical for almost 12 hours is not a diagnosis. barely had an exam of just taking vitals every 4 hours. i don't understand the healthcare in the state of nevada. there is truly no patient care. that's a bill i will shred when it arrives in the mail.

if i could give this place 0 stars i would. allows homeless people to camp out in their lobby at night. at least tell them to go clean up they stink! the place is dirty, trash in the "triage" room if that's what you want to call it. the front desk person got up and left when we were trying to check in. didn't even to offer us help. was here friday morning and the doctor on call did absolutely nothing to treat my arm. told me it was just a scratch, go home and call some doctor for a follow up. ahh he didn't even clean the cut, no tetanus shot or blood draw either, nothing. today my entire arm and hand are swollen, with some bruising and it hurts!  band aids and ibruprofin don't fix everything people!! what an incompetent doctor.

thank you for your swift care and professionalism for taking care of one of my family members who was emitted in last night. i spoke with ashley (nurse) last night and she was extremely professional and caring when i was concerned for my brother's care as there was no family present during his emergency visit. thank you!

spent 5 days there. the day nurse was exceptional -- a real nurse, very attentive and great bedside manner. a few pointers for this hospital:  (1) when a patient is admitted, ask them how they would like to be addressed (i.e., first name, mrs., miss, etc) put that on their chart and make employees aware of it.  just because we are older does not mean you can call us "honey" and "sweetie." it is insulting and your  facility is a nursing home!  secondly, patients are there for one reason -- they are sick. congregating of employees for conversation, either work or pleasure is not appreciated! keep the conversations down and the personal ones out of the area period!  this would not be my first choice if hospitalization is needed in the future.

if minus stars was available they would get minus.this hospital is the worst in the valley but they are all bad,look up there rating in the bottom of the u.s. they absolutely killed my wife only 62 yrs old went in with complication of cancer they refused to transfer her to another hospital she got pnuemonia in hospital and died, horrible doctors who would not listen and wanted to protect the money coming in, than being more concerned for patient than money !!!!!people wake up you have the worst hospitals in the country and just as bad of doctor, city of 2.5million people not one hospital rated more than1 star out of 5 stars the lower 20%nation wide. wake wake up las vegas

the fine service and good food and comfort of this hospital all comes to an end when you walk out the door having paid $208,000 for two night stay november 1 and 2, 2019.  the accounting department is terrible.  i was (am) in need of the itemized pricing on my final bill for a hip replacement.  i have made 3 calls to billing (with substantial wait time) and written two emails to the ceo.  all have been with zero results.  when hip number two needs to be done it certainly will be at a different hospital.
now my grandfather is dead and they don't have a morge,and they need that bed for a patient and now me and my family have go to las vegas from florida

truthfully worst emergency center ever! if i am dying i will not be going here! the triage rooms are horrible, they leave the doors wide open, employees walk in and out of your room to grab water and to walk through the room to the front, 3 different employees did it with in a 30 minute time period. the doctor i saw was super unclear and i told him i might have the flu & he said we didn't need to test for the flu and didnt notify me that we were doing chest xray's till the xray guy came in! the front desk staff is so unorganized and all over the place, they can't handle fast paced environments. usually going into a hospital i feel a sense of relief because i know i am being taken care of and in the hospital i felt the complete opposite. seriously i would not recommend going here, i am not pleased with there treatment at all or there employees!

had a surgery procedure done in the outpatient wing. from the time i walked in till i was wheeled out it was relaxing fun personality and jennifer who was my nurse was beyond perfect. i thank the staff who did my surgery with up most professional integrity. great experience considering my situation.

we have been to the er twice in the past year with our kiddos. both times they were awesome!! one was with a severe case of chicken pox and once with a dislocated thumb. we were seen quickly and the care was wonderful. makes you so grateful for medical professionals who take their jobs seriously and are so professional, skilled, kind and thorough.

i was born at mercy hospital, my kids were both born here, my sister works here and my mom has worked here as a nurse for over 30 years. this is my preferred hospital. they have a great commitment to excellence and caring for the patient and i trust them with metaled, my family, and my kids. that says a lot and it's gets all that needs to be said. great organization with good doctors and top notch nurses

i had a good experience at this er. 
i came in on a thursday at around 1pm with really awful pains in my chest and upper left shoulder/back and there was no one else in the waiting room. i immediately got checked in by the initial info. taker and looked at by the first nurse who checked my basic markers like blood pressure, temperature, reason for coming in, etc. he told me to take a seat and that they'd call me in "if they had room". which was a little worrisome, but i actually only waited for about 15 minutes or so before i got called in. 
i was taken to a private room by one nurse, met by another, and got changed into a robe, and started the process for my specific issue. the nurse we met in there was really rushing (the other nurse even pointed it out) - not even leaving the room to let me change into the robe - just holding it up and telling me to take off my clothes behind it - and asking me questions super quickly without even waiting for my response. i'm thinking and hoping that she just had something urgent to get to, because it was a little unnecessary, but nothing terribly awful. i took my time and made sure to get all my answers out before moving on. the other nurse was very kind asking if i wanted a warm blanket, etc. they were out the door in about 5 min after i got in. it took around 45 min or so before the dr. came in. 
he was really great. dr. mccall is his name. great bedside manner: calm, kind, allowed me to ask all of my questions and say all that i wanted to say. he took the time to thoroughly explain the results of the tests the nurses took, going into more detail about how to read it and what certain markers would and could mean, etc. he did a physical examination, as well, and explained everything as he went. explaining why i was probably feeling the way that i felt and what would cause it. i didn't feel rushed with him, and i felt like a person.

i was in and out of the building in about 2 hours!
and, parking is in a parking garage next door that was free (gate was open and there were no tickets) the day that i went.

i will have to see how billing goes, but in-person care was pretty good and thankfully much better than other reviewers' on here.
fac_name: PeaceHealth Sacred Heart Medical Center University District

review: went in early in the morning, was seen by erik poyourow, md. he was condescending, practically sneering. i hadn't been to an er in over 10 years so it's not like i was overusing services. he managed to insult my gender and age in one statement. "mocking" best describes his attitude. i got in to see real doctors later that day, who did an xray, found a kidney stone. apparently they can exist and cause the symptoms i had without  intense pain. those providers were surprised erik had not done imaging. if he had tried harder to diagnose my problem and less trying to impress the nurses with his cleverness i might have gotten some help. $250 to be basically laughed at. i'm a provider also and he was just unprofessional. i'll be going to mckenzie-willamette in the future if i have to. get some cmes in ethics, doc. the nurses were nice.
fac_name: PeaceHealth Sacred Heart Medical Center University District

review: my dad is here now and has been for at least 4 days and he feels the staff on the second floor have been "excellent."  no complaints at all  great job second floor staff from gary in room 227!!
this is the worst emergency room i've ever been to, i've had the worst experience here in my life please do yourself a face and go somewhere else

took my girl here because she was having heart problems and we waited about 4 - 5 hours and they werent busy. staff full of lazy people that dont know how to do their job. by the time they saw us, my girlfriend didnt even feel the symptoms of what she was feeling anymore. never coming back again and if you have an emergency i suggest you dont come here. if i could give this place no stars i would.

can anyone explain to me how a 5 minute office visit at pmc  can result in 2 bills - one from the physician and another from pmc noted as a "facility charge" for $287.0!!!!! the physician bill was $100, for which we paid the specialist copay of $60.00. my husband went in, had blood pressure taken, got weighed, and spoke to the physician for no more than 5 minutes. i am told that since the hospital owns the physician practice, they can charge a "facility fee". what, exactly, is this fee for? he waited an hour past his appointment time for a 5 minute appointment, and was essentially billed $387.00 total. what for???? the fee is over twice as much as the doctor charged. how is this justifiable?

my family and i are disappointment that the blue spruce on the 2nd floor main entrance is not decorated for christmas!  here's an idea. have the volunteer department decorate so the patients entering and leaving can have some cheer.

my husband had open heart surgery. there were quite a lot of complications , this was jan2. he drive 51/2 hours to have all his pre op work done! includes his blood type and the lab must cross type his blood ! they missed that . surgery started 2 hours late! no one told us because  they did not cross type his blood dr.thurber and his team were amazing , admission and nurses there were great. we had to sit in a filthy waiting  room with a garbage can full of dirty diapers . katlin and anleigh were the only nurses that were compassionate and ivan you need cue on ethics !
in the  icu that we should have not stayed in the entire 5 days because a room wasn't available.

my father was admitted to this hospital a week ago due to a serious infection. he's been ill for a couple decades.  when my mom called to come quickly because he was fading and we needed to make end of life decisions, i became so touched by the compassionate and caring nursing staff.  the doctors were never rushing, stopped and listened, and answered questions. any time we needed a nurse, i'd pop my head out in the hall and someone would come. we were never left or ignored. 

as he neared the end, nursing staff would come by and see us and check on us, and leave us as we had to make those decisions.  no one rushed us or made us feel like we weren't doing the right thing.  i was especially moved by the expressions of faith by each staff person. it was incredibly comforting.  

i'd like to especially thank chris, sam, marylou, belle, dora, sarah and most of all june. dear kind june who made those final moments so peaceful.  it's been a hard week, but i'd recommend the care and compassion of this hospital from the security guards and front desk, housekeeping, gift shop, cafeteria staff, respiratory techs, but most of all the doctors and nurses who cared for my dad.

the physical therapy group at this facility, gina came to my room the second day. i was standing with a jersey type dress on (could see my panty line) she hit me on the incision of my back. her reason she said for doing that was  checking to see if you had your brace on. this was the first improper behavior, my 1st room was not a private room as my insurance paid for. they had an admit in the middle of the night and begged me to allow her to stay. the next morning they moved me to 111, this room appeared hadn't been occupied in a very long time. there was blood on the floor in the bathroom, dust about 3 layers deep, no phone " it was being disenfected according to their ceo ty". then when i was ready to take a shower it was determined that the shower didn't work! the nurse and tech on duty left out my room and didn't return. therefore i called the ceo on his cell. he had the nursing supervisors who took me to the community shower then, found me a room with a working shower. however this bed didn't include features necessary for comfort. at 4 am as tech instructed by nurse on duty (who knew i'm an insomniac) had her to bring me ice! then that nurse cane back in my room at 4:15 am to take pictures of my insidious under the excuse had to be done in this day. this pic could have waited until 6 am when they come in for meds/vitals. there were more issues while i was inpatient but, i'm just including in my grievance that i'm filing with my insurance.
i
would like to add that barry the coordinator did an excellent job ensuring that i received the additional day's necessary to receive adequate therapy 

additionally i'd like to compliment elaine (physical therapist) as she did a good job with physical therapy in a professional caring manner.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Arlington

review: i had to rush to deaconess with a very elevated blood pressure and tingling in my face. i was advised to get there immediately. upon checking in i was set in the waiting room for over two hours before someone evaluated me. thank god it wasn't a stroke. i wouldn't advise going there with an emergency.

i was treated in the er for an ongoing health issue that i have, then i was discharged. the problems started when i was told that medicaid would cover a cab home for me. so i sat in the lobby and waited... and waited, and waited, and waited... when i asked the staff what was going on, they just shrugged. when i asked if there was someplace i could at least lie down, as it was getting very late, they pointed indifferently to some chairs that were only large enough for a toddler. they clearly couldn't have cared less. one person told me that people had been known to wait all night for cabs. if they had told me that at 7:30 p.m., when i was discharged, i could have taken a bus home. but instead, i received a courtesy ride from the police, after 2:00 a.m., having never seen any sign of a cab. then i was too exhausted to go to work in the morning, so i lost a day's pay.

when i filed a grievance about this, i received a form letter in response, which was far from satisfactory in my opinion. in fact i think it's downright insulting. but when i took issue with it, i just received the form letter again. i think in the end i got the same letter a total of 3 times. impersonal much, bch? i even wrote a letter to the hospital director, which was completely ignored. they don't even acknowledge how totally unprofessional they are, much less try to make it right. and they claim to care. what a joke!

in the course of my occasional emergency visits, i have been treated incredibly rudely at times (why am i not surprised?), and have also found false information in my records twice. the first time it happened, they wouldn't even let me leave a message for the er doctor, who had said i had borderline personality disorder. i have nothing even resembling that. what kind of hospital won't even let a person speak to the doctor who attended them (and then put false information in the record)? the second time, they called asking me where the latest b.s. info. had come from, as if i'm supposed to know. i got it from them.

i so wish bch wasn't the nearest hospital to me. i may have to move.

my concern discussed in this review is financial in that i have twice been admitted for "observation" while under the impression i was being admitted as a patient ; being a patient means insurance covers as you would expect per your policy. the insurance coverage  is vastly different under the two admissions and it is very expensive to be in the hospital under "observation" . you feel like a usual patient but you are not. the second time i was to be admitted for  a very serious condition i asked the er nurse specifically " now is this admission as a regular patient because last time i was "observed" and the insurance does not pay the same. he went over to the computer , pulled up my records and promised me "you are admitted as a regular patient". after many nuclear tests, mri etc i was told i needed cath lab , possible stents etc. clearly admission was necessary. but insurance office dropped into my room and told me that after two days i would be admitted and no longer just being "observed" i don't call all of the test i was given just an "observation". yet,  all the tests , etc were under "observation" status so usual insurance coverage would not apply. 
it is dishonest and almost like bait switching in commercial advertising to tell someone they are in one status -a patient- when they are not.
 er docs can admit you under whatever terms they like and , clearly, you may not even know your status. since asking specifically gave me a false answer, i do not feel i can trust boulder community hospital for seeking care. this does not even address how i was treated by the er doctors who were abrupt, insulting, dismissive when i was both frightened and very ill.

ok, i know this is an odd review of a hospital, but specifically, this is for the cafeteria! this hospital does not serve hospital food! they serve real food at low low prices! today was their mardi gras celebration menu, and all the food was cooked in house and off-the-hook! crab cakes, crabby patty sandwiches, pan fried shrimp, gumbo, blackened chicken, deep-fried pastry, oven roasted cheese grits, roasted vegetables, bread pudding with rum sauce... the list doesn't end! and this may be a celebration day, but the food here is this good every day! the kitchen staff is totally on top of the quality and delivers friendly service with a smile. better still, the cafeteria is open to the public! you don't have to be a patient to enjoy this amazing food, so don't go shooting yourself in the foot. check out the jackson general hospital cafeteria in ripley, west virginia!

i was sent to this hospital while visiting my new pcp. i was having chest pains, and sure enough, it was acute pancreatitis. my 5th time having this and i'm not a drinker. so we assume its a medication causing this aggravating pain. now to figure which one of the many...? anywho, i can't go on and, on how 12 green made me feel like i was vip.  i loved my stay, although i was in pain, every nurse, doctor, clerk, maintenance man-made you smile because they enjoyed their part in providing you the best possible care. the food was delicious although i was on a restricted diet. kudos to the kitchen. this hospital caters to their patients' rehabilitation with the greatest care.

the worst experience ever. my son broke his arm and we took him to er, after 2 hours waiting with a 6 years old and after complaining they call us. a week after we came back to check his cast and the same 2 hours waiting and after i complained the doctor came and wasn't very nice. after 2 weeks we went back to remove the cast and again, they did not have our appointment, they were late and not friendly. i understand as a children's hospital they have been treatment much worse cases than a broken arm however this is not an excuse to not have a good treatment. when it is time to charge, nicklaus children's hospital knows how to send you a very high bill and when you call to understand about you bill they tell you to leave a message. horrible service and care.

i have an elderly godfather who has been in and out of the hospital for the last few years.  last week he went in by ambulance and was released several hours later too weak to get up.  the next day he was back in by ambulance and he requested that he receive no further treatment but wished to enter hospice.  the hospital kept trying to do blood work and x-rays despite this request.  the er doc spoke with us and insisted he could make him better.  he would be in the hospital another 5 or 6 days and probably get out for a few and be back but he would have time.  my godfather stated repeatedly he'd had a good life and enough time already but wished to die and have no further treatment.  we repeated this scenario several times.  we were visited by hospice and told he would be moved in the afternoon.  he waited from 9 am until 4 in the afternoon for transport.  from the time it was determined he would go to hospice the er offered no more care.  he remained in the hospital bed with an empty iv attached, on bloody sheets.  no amount of pleading on my part got him any comfort until he reached the hospice center in aldie where he lived only 24 hours.  i can't say enough good things about capital caring.  the horror of the day was the treatment in the er with the insistence that they could prop him up for a few more days and then ignore him from that point on.  they could have removed the iv from his arm, cleaned up the bed and allowed him some comfort but that is not what transpired at all and i am sorry he had to spend one of his last two days in that situation.

i wasn't a patient here, but my step-son was.   they helped us every step of the way, even with insurance issues.    the parent education was excellent.   i was impressed with the knowledge and warmth of all of the counselors i met.   aa principles are an integral part of their treatment plan, though they are free to admit that it is only one of many approaches to sobriety.  they also offer outpatient treatment and sobriety coaching to create a smooth transition to the community.    

having said all that, the relapse rate for addiction is very high, especially amongst teenagers, and fairbanks does see quite a number of repeat visits.   that is more a function of the disease than the rehab facility.   

i would highly recommend this rehab facility for anyone dealing with alcoholism and/or addiction.

most people complain about hospitals but they do not take the time to educate them selves on the financial programs that exist. not everyone will have their bill 100 percent eliminated, but will see huge bill reduction with payment plans. the hospital makes it easy to apply by including the application along with the bill.

my wife's delivery was fully covered minus our co-pay by kaiser in october at cmh.

i was able to articulate to him that i had wanted to see the results of my bloodwork before further testing.  i have been in the er many times in my life for various issues including gastric related ones, and i have never had anyone order extensive imaging before even examining me.  this clinic ordered an x-ray and ct scan, in addition to a urine sample, blood panel, and other tests,  before anyone had even examined me!! i had no unusual symptoms of any kind and in all my er experiences, the imaging comes when something shows up in bloodwork or due to symptoms noted in the exam with the doctor.  they claimed they needed imaging to see if it was appendicitis or other internal organ issue.  yet no one had even palpated my  abdomen to check for localized tenderness.  so i felt like this was a racket and i had every right to request to be seen, examined, and to know if any results in my tests indicated the need for imaging.  they had already swooped in and x-rayed my lungs and i didn't even have a cough or any symptoms remotely related.  

i was there because i needed intravenous fluids and anti-nausea meds so i could rehydrate and take tylenol, get my fever down, and be well enough to drive the next day.  i was of course willing to be examined and appreciated them looking for signs of something other than food poisoning or the flu, but this was excessive and i had every right to question them and to want to talk to the doctor about why the hell a ct scan was being ordered before anyone had talked to me.

anyway, this place is awful.

we showed up in this emergency room in june 2019 when my son was badly scalded on his legs and stomach while camping at folsom lake.  we don't even have sutter insurance, but kaiser; this just happened to be the closest er. the waiting room was overflowing when we arrived at about 9:00 pm, but we were triaged within just a few minutes and admitted right after that (my son was in a bad way).  kat, the charge nurse on duty that night, was awesome; she was a calming, knowledgeable presence, and she immediately started a course of treatment.  within two hours of our arrival, the staff had stabilized my son, gotten him admitted to the burn ward at shriner's hospital in sac (also awesome), and arranged for an ambulance to shuttle him down the hill.

review: on wednesday night i was at church when i began to experience severe chest pain, being an emt and a high level cardiac patient i made the choice to go to the er. when i arrived at the er (chi st. joseph, bryan) the visit started out as good as it could, my ekg was abnormal along with labs. i was rushed directly to an er room. doctor conrad and doctor tuckerton were the two doctors in the er at the time and thank god. issues started when it was time to start an iv. i know i am a very hard stick so i told the nurse to get the ultra sound, despite that 14 sticks later still no iv access. the nurses were doing what they could, but due to hospital staffing no one qualified to complete advanced iv procedures was working. finally, doctor tuckerton established it, during the testing i was told i was being admitted, but no beds were available so i might be in er all night, i was being kept very medicated and comfortable so no problem. finally, i was told that due to labs i was being taken to icu, again okay. this is where the part starts that results in a one-star review. again amazing nurses, but the doctor! i made the extra 15 mile run to this hospital due to my now former cardiologist, doctor marc schwartz being on staff. the first issue came with initial admitting orders; it took him over three hours to enter them. when the nurse went to get pain medication for me due to severe chest pain, surprise no orders for it. as a reminder my history includes five heart attacks, 6 stents, a quadruple bypass, 3 strokes, and afib. oh and i am 42.  i had not been given anything tor pain control for now going on 8 hours, when the cardiologist doctor marc schwartz was asked for the orders from the rn he said pain control was not his problem and walked off, thankfully the icu doctor took care of it. several hours later the pain control issue came up again. the previous order was a onetime only order, again doctor schwartz would not take care of it and relayed the message i would just have to deal with the pain. at this time my blood pressure was 179/99 and my pulse was back up to 140 due to the pain. once again the icu doctor fixed the issue. now for the crown jewel. doctor schwartz comes into announce that the severe chest pain and symptoms are due to the plumbing around my heart being very bad. we know it's bad, but something has to be done. i am on every medication i can be to manage the symptoms. he made it clear he does not know what to do and until the heart muscle starts to show damage he is not interested in any invasive procedures, his answer is, i will have to live with the pain and associated symptoms for now, playing the er round trip game, his attitude is why i will start going to the hospitals in the woodlands. his lack of empathy and his attitude are my deciding factors in filing a formal complaint with the hospital and the state of texas. i strongly encourage everyone, if you have an issue with a hospital or doctor, speak out! speaking out advocates for other patients and helps protect them and until enough people speak out against a doctor of facility a change will not happen!
fac_name: CHI St. Joseph Regional Health Care Center

review:
came here to meet my friend for lunch at the cafe.  there was a variety of food but we went to the grill for burgers and fries. didn't get to check out other parts of the hospital. there was a hand sanitizer and a box of masks by the entrance in case anyone needs it. 
the bathroom was clean and stocked with toilet papers. i parked in the scurlock tower garage and it was $7 for up to 3 hours. not terrible in tmc.

writing a yelp review for a hospital seems silly since your review will likely depend on how your visit went and your diagnosis, but here i am. methodist is an excellent hospital in the greatest medical center in the country, and that's that on that. the complex is expansive and offers everything you need, plus more - an imaging center in the same building as a bank and jewelry store? sure, why not. i have only encountered friendly staff here and there are plenty of information desks scattered around to help you navigate the numerous towers. valet and self parking are offered and a fairly reasonable rate when you consider you have to pay to park anywhere in the med center these days.
no wonder united healthcare dumped you and was trying to get you to adjust pricing. ultrasound at methodist $1,240. exact same ultrasound elsewhere $120, yes 10 times as much as methodist.  #thievery

i'm giving them a 2 because i got out alive!  never go to the emergency medicine stand alone houston methodist clinic on voss road.  i came in dry heaving with chills and stomach cramps as symptoms i know to be moving into an adrenal crises.  i was too sick to talk and told them i live with addison's disease and they needed to talk to my medic alert team.  they refused to call the number on my medic alert bracelet!  then they took more than 40 minutes when standard protocol is 15 minutes to get me my emergency stress dose via iv.  they didn't even know if they had the drug!  the rn didn't even tell me when the emergency stress dose was put in my vein and refused to ask the doctor to give me the only anti nausea drug that works for me.  it was a horrible experience with zero management of my juvenile diabetes and at discharge they insisted i take the hotel garbage can with me that still had my stomach bile in it!  go to a full service er and not houston methodist when you have an emergency!   i did a review with their quality control patient services department and they stated i didn't require acute diabetes management, which i know from other similar emergencies with juvenile diabetes and addison's i absolutely required close management of both diseases.  incompetent doctor on the day of and no endocrine doctors on the review team, so how could they have the knowledge to judge what happened to me and what i required.   they couldn't.   this location moved like sloughs when i required emergency care!!'

my stepfather was admitted via the emergency room last weekend and spent four nights as an inpatient. he and my mother and i were treated wonderfully by so many people there. he was given the thorough and expert workup that he has been needing for months but could not get in his small town. everyone treated us kindly. as we try to find places in the hospital, hospital staff were constantly stopping to ask if they could help. and when we asked for something, the attitude of staff was to see if they could make it happen rather than two be annoyed with us if we wanted to do something differently. for example, i was standing in the hall outside my stepfather's door to give him privacy and to be available when needed. instead of telling me to move out of the way and go to the lounge, a staff member offered to go find me a chair. that kindness was so precious because of all the fear and pain we were going through. our hospitalist, dr. patel, investigated everything and answered all of our questions patiently. we left the hospital with confidence in the diagnoses that were given and the diagnoses that were ruled out. 
the only service that did not serve us very well was psychiatry. this was far short of the level of care we received by the other specialties.
i've been sitting in emergency room for 4.5 hours with zero sign of being checked. unacceptable!

i was told by the eisenhower er doctor that the coronavirus is a bunch of hype. he asked me why my doctor didn't see me. i told him i didn't know why. he told me my doctor didn't know how to take care of sick people. i told him i called my doctor's office and they advised me to go to the er. he rolled his eyes and made me very uncomfortable.  they  left me in the examination room for an hour and a half.  gave me a test for influenza and it was negative and they sent me home. i have already lost a week's work.

i wish i could give a negative stars for this hospital. i took a recent trip here and waited 7 and a half hours!!!! it felt like i was being tortured! (urgent care advised me to come to er by the way.)absolutely despicable wait time! just pure insanity and unreal. not to mention the beyond filthy waiting area that never once was cleaned by anyone in the 7 and half grueling hours i waited to see a doctor. i was so disgusted with this place and the service and the aesthetics of the hospital. there was only one friendly nurse on staff, all the others looked miserable and over worked. this place really needs to make some changes.

this place i have no words 6 hours i waited it took an hour just to get check in... the guy who check mee in was rude as all hell!!!! my blood pressure was high and he didn't even seem to be considered about it 160/109 high for me being on medication for it, the place was dirty water bottles empty food wrappers dirty tissues and face masks all over the place honestly i wasn't even seen because i just couldn't sit their anymore. i was and still in pain and not feeling well if i wanted to feel like crap  i could do that in the comfort of my own home and not  this death trap that could care less about any person.... this whole place is a joke

this is the worst emergency room i have ever been to and i've been to many. they have very sick people just laying all over the place in the waiting room. we have been here for nine hours and still haven't seen a doctor yet. there's a baby that needs stitches after splitting her lip open and they just have her still in the waiting room laying here. this is absolutely unacceptable!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

very disappointed!! i was at the er a few days ago with pain and high fever. worse service!! the staff do not communicate with each other !! every person stepped in to the room asked me the same questions! the nurse ( bsn rn ) not even helped me to get dress. i couldn't walk and i was in so much pain.. but she hesitate to get me a wheel chair .. i had to drag myself out of er... very bad experience !!! after i fully gain my health , i will be going directly to the hospital and file a complaint .

this place is very poorly administered. we waited 5 hours before by brother's bleeding foot was looked at. we waited another 4 hours to get bandages and discharge. this is the worst emergency department i have ever seen. i wish there was some type of oversight on how they run this place

i came in with my father who has dementia but it had reached a whole new level which i know is from a uti having been through this many times.

 it took them 6 hours to do 3 tests. including 5 different nurses trying to draw blood. it has been a miserable experience with ridiculous delays. i am now going on hour 7 and still sitting in the emergency room. there wasn't even that many people in the waiting room. we have had 3 different nurses. they are all nice enough but aren't doing enough to help him.  this place is the worst. next time i'm driving him to loma linda.  i left to go to the cafeteria to get something to eat because i was starving and when i came back i found my dad roaming the hallways barefoot in his hospital gown. they decided to do a urine test on him and actually handed me the container and told me to collect the urine. are you kidding me? a daughter should never have to do that with her father even though i have done it before but never asked by a nurse. beware.....

absolutely the worst you will ever find anywhere! my 5-year old son was brought in on an ambulance with his skull exposed and they made him wait three hours behind people with sniffles, who had time to bring their novels while they waited. while he was passing out from blood loss, they offered him a coloring book. are you kidding me?! i also had another bad experience with this er. they are the worst!!!! i can't say enough! the absolute worst!!!!

if i could give 0 stars i would. worst hospital i've ever been too. i waited 5 1/2 hour in the lobby. i then got a room, waited 3 more hours before i was seen by a doctor, it's like they forgot about me. then the doctor spent 5 minutes with me, examined my shoulder which is the problem. wouldn't give me any pain medicine even though i was crying my eyes out from all of the pain. she gave me a fucking motrin. like okay. thanks. then gave me a x ray, didn't even tell me the results, i had to ask the nurse. said i probably hurt my rotator cuff and i need an mri but i have to see a primary doctor for that. i told her i have no insurance except for the emergency medical. where i live, there is only one medical office in the whole valley. she still wouldn't give  me one. sent me home in a sling with a advil prescription and that's it. i was there for 10 hours!! worst experience of my life. who knew doctors could be so bad and rude. i'm back again the next day hoping i can get some answers about my pain, etc hoping for an mri. we will see. the nurse i had last  night checked me in and she basically told me to just leave. 



update: after going back today, i was done in less than 4 hours so that's way better than yesterday. i had an amazing doctor this time who helped me and explained everything about my shoulder and what actually was wrong with it. she gave me better medicine and a few shots that are really helping so tonight was definitely better. still mad about yesterday though.

i was admitted to eisenhower er (by ambulance) on monday, 1/27/2020 due to a fall.  my head was bleeding.  i want to thank all those nurses and three doctors who cared for me.  and, i do mean cared for me.  sure, i was there for seven hours, but that's how long it took to stop the bleeding, get a ct scan, staple the wound and observe me.

sitting in the er with my husband who is experiencing heart blockage symptoms. we have been here for three and a half hours and of that time we have been waiting for three hours and twenty five minutes. it seems as though the several employees here have nothing better to do than talk and laugh. it's like they're having a big party while we sit and wait and wait and wait...very frustrating!

on january 3 (2020), a friday, i was in this er for twelve (12) hours. while eisenhower is commonly referred to by residents here as "the best" or the "best place to go" in an emergency, i will say this facility appears to be ill-equipped to handle a lot of people at once. by "a lot of people" i mean approximately 80-100, which was my rough count in the er waiting area.  when i finally got to go behind the scenes to an exam room, i learned from two nurses that there was only one (1) er doctor on duty that entire evening. this fact is unacceptable. i respect the fact that er medicine is often the first or only place some of our population go for healthcare treatment, and we have to work to improve chances that more people will obtain regular health insurance and go to a doctor for an annual checkup. but a highly advanced and professionally prepared medical facility should be planning for reality, and that reality is that the eisenhower er is overrun with people and the staff cannot adequately keep apace with the demand. i only hope there is no major disaster in our future, because then this hospital will be totally helpless to face the demand on its resources.

this hospital was detrimental in my father's health and basically killed him. he entered healthy and just needed help from geriatrics with medication side effects but they instead administered heavy duty psych drugs. dr scharma in the geri psych unit would not listen to me when i said my father has never been in a psych unit and was in a delirium from other medication. he administered new meds, more
meds, anti psychotics and the staff put my dad in restraints. my father was unable to talk, feed himself or speak after that. i had to hold a meeting with this incompetent doctor and the staff and demand all meds be stopped immediately. my father had no clinical
diagnosis for these meds. they made him so sick he ended up having heart problems and in a delirium for weeks. 

eventually he went into respiratory failure. he was trapped in bridgeport hospital for two months straight. he lost his bed at his long term care facility (he was only 74) and due to psych notes he could not get rehabilitation anywhere. but my father did not have psych issues. he had blood poisoning from his co2 build up from the respiratory failure his stay in psych did to him and from being bed ridden so long. bridgeport did no tests for this!! they let him stay in a room without tests being done as if he was fine. yale new haven ran the tests and  saw what was happening. he suffered immensely from bridgeport hospital , the staff was incompetent, un-empathetic and dr scharma is not fit to care for the elderly or anyone that needs  close attention. didnt matter that i was the healthcare proxy and knew my fathers entire medical history. my father needlessly suffered and went back and forth in and out of hospitals for months after bridgeport. 

he died december 2019, unable to ever get back to  
his baseline , and only with suffering propelled by the terrible two months of mistreatment in bridgeport hospital. i saw my father the first day he arrived at bridgeport and i saw him during and i saw him after. he went into a hospital that made  him worse than before and ultimately propelled him to death. 

no response from patient relations. i will be taking legal action. keep your family out of here.

this is the worst medical facility anyone can attend.  my wife has been there over a week.  they can not agree on a treatment plan.  never volunteer to be treated at this useless facility.  they should have their accreditation revoke. how can i send a reply. there is no link.  patient is in room 348a.

serious safety concerns. i tried following chain of command to resolve issues and it is near impossible to get leadership to talk let alone take ownership for their mistakes. staff doesn't wash hands and staff didn't check basic safety items like a name and date of birth when giving medications. multiple doctors with poor bedside manner. after surgery the surgeon never came out to let the family know the patient was out of surgery. 
 we observed the surgeon talk to other families and let them know their family member was out of surgery. we found out our family member was out of surgery when we saw our family member wheeled down the hallway to go back to their room. within an hour of  reaching the floor our family member was unstable and neededd to  be transferred to critical care.  so many other  safety concerns about dmc.
horrible horrible  hospital er is so bad my mom has been waiting for 3 almost 4 hours and still waiting for a doctor to see her and she's been in severe pain and still hasn't been seen

my husband and i were there on new year's eve. he had an aggressive infection and in a lot  of pain . the er staff took care of him immediately,  
with just a few questions from him and they knew exactly what to do to ease his pain and took great care with much empathy and kindness on their part . i cannot praise them enough. thank you with all my heart to the er people.

my aunt has been diagnosed with kidney cancer and the staff at doctors medical center have been very supportive and understanding of our feelings. the nurses and neurologists have been so informative and honest. the hospital as a whole is clean and quiet for the patients. the care has been so great everyone is helpful, patient, and very attentive to our needs. i want to send a special thank you to rebecca and brad in the e. r.  they were so respectful of our privacy and genuinely concerned for us and treated us like we were friends for awhile.  we can't thank them enough.
they literally saved my life and the care i received was fantastic. medical staff  could not have been any better.

i recently broke my hip and when i arrived by ambulance i was made to wait in a hallway for quite awhile amid police and people in handcuffs before being taken to a room for evaluation.  while in incredible pain, i was largely ignored, and finally taken to surgery after 26 hours, with the explanation that i was an "add on".  following surgery, patient care was minimal.  when i'd ring for a nurse during the night to help me get to the bathroom, i sometimes waited 10-15 minutes.  i was often told that they were understaffed, and rarely saw a nurse between 10pm and 7am.  the food was awful, and there seemed to be a disconnect between the hospitalist and my surgeon.  on the day i was to go home, they ordered my walker from the wrong company, causing me to wait an additional 6+ hours before i finally borrowed a walker from a friend and went home at 6pm.  no one ever informed my primary care physician of what had happened, and i was given little discharge information (like whether i could shower) - all in all a very disappointing experience.

in april, my dad suffered from a blood clot in his spine leaving him paralyzed from the chest down. my dad needed acute spinal rehabilitation after the hospital and deserved/ needed to be around people who really cared for him and his mental well-being. 

we were recommended kessler inpatient rehab for various reasons. this rehab is over an hour away for my family and i but due to past experiences at rehab facilities we needed my dad to get the best care possible. 

the first day my dad was admitted, an aid came in and insisted because he's obese and it would be too much work to constantly clean him so he needed an adult diaper. my dad was visibly upset and the aid made multiple remarks regarding his weight and how he was "too large" for her to do anything alone. my dad already felt like a burden, lost his meaning for life, and has had the hardest few years of his life. i have no tolerance for anyone bullying him but before i could say anything, one of the physical therapists, barbara, stepped into the room, heard what was being said and took care of the situation instantly. she filed a complaint with the head nurse and alerted her peers of what happened. she assured me no one, including my dad, deserves to be treated that way for any reason. 

after the first day, i felt like my dad was in good hands and the following months everyone at kessler would prove me right. 
i was fortunate enough to be able to visit my dad almost everyday but the days i or someone in my family couldn't visit, we felt safe knowing my dad was in good care. 

a special thank you to my dad's nurses and doctors, especially donna and alan. thank you to his physical therapists, barbara and tori, that kept us updated with his progress and worked with us to help him psychologically. 

after kessler, my dad had to go to a subacute rehab and we were happy he was closer to home but the staff and overall care was pathetic. my dad ended up in the hospital because of the lack of care and sadly he lost a lot of confidence, hope, and will to progress that the staff at kessler built. 

i wish my dad's insurance allowed him to stay at kessler longer. the disabled and their family deserve the level of care they provided.

i would recommend this specific kessler over and over and over again.

absolute the worst hospital on the planet! they have no cooth..terrible bed side manners and no clue what's going on. staff was very rude and made me feel worse than when i arrived. if you dare say anything about it...you will end up on suicide watch ...they enjoy degrading patients and showing their power. do yourself a solid and go elsewhere..spent 6 hours in er...my alarms went off..no one came. i hit the nurse button...no one came. they dont care!!  this is the absolute worst hospital on the planet!!!!!

avoid this hospital's ct scan dept.  i accompanied a syrian refugee yesterday to get a ct scan. they had gone on their own before two weeks earlier and were told that the procedure was not authorized. his letter said to go to his doctor's office in the main hospital by 9:45am.  we did and were told we weren't supposed to be there, to go to the boyer bldg. we did, logged in, waited, saw the intake clerk and were told the procedure was not authorized. i indicated that was unacceptable because we had been told to come for it. the clerk went away, came back, and said it was okay, to go to the ct scan waiting area. a staff member took out paperwork.  we waited over two hours before i let them know we seemed to be overlooked. i was told our appointment was for 3pm. how is that possible, to have a doctor's appointment to evaluate the results at 10am and have the scan being evaluated at 3pm? again they relented and took the patient next. we then went back to the doctor to get the results of the scan. there i spoke to the patient relations mgr and his boss to get them to not put others through the same thing in the future. it is so stupid, incompetent, and bureaucratic it is almost hard to describe. the hospital botched the appointment telling us to go to the doctor first, not having the authorization, and not spotting or letting us know the appointment was at 3pm, and this was the second time the refuge had been told there that the procedure was not authorized.  it was authorized, at least once and most likely the earlier time also when he was told to go home (after a difficult trip to the hospital).

it's mind boggling how disorganized the place is.  somebody should be fired.

minus stars better describes this hospital. after my daughter aged out of a children's hospital, we were sent to this cesspool. i think she would have received better care from the corner crackhead. besides the one nurse who helped me change my daughter, the night nurse (male) the night before she died and the day nurse, the day she died, no one seems to know the meaning of care, compassion or review:
i anonymously donated a kidney in january of 2019. the process was smooth until right after surgery. communication was lost and no one, because of the anonymity of the donation process, could tell my wife where i was. at one time, telling my wife i wasn't at banner. then, there was a three hour wait to get me a room! in this whole process i wasn't a vip...i will get to this issue later. the nursing staff was horrible. i am a medic, so i do understand the issues of working on a ward and the short staffing problems. i also have seen nurse burnout, but there are patients who love to complain about anything and everything - that is not me. i was a military medic for a decade and know there are things we can do in medical to help. i've also seen people on medical wards that can't make it in the ed, icu or any other specialty and show up on medical wards. my pain management was the worse i've ever seen, and i was in enough pain to regret donating. i didn't sleep for 48 hours because of the incredible pain i was in.
dr. harland assured me that he - because he was opening me up inches from my umbilical hernia, that he would fix that. i had an incision there, but it seems nothing was done/fixed. surprise!  
to spit in my face, i was recently sent an anesthesiology bill from the hospital! donners are not supposed to be billed for donating! hello! i've been told that this is "common"! your assured that this will not happen prior to donation. so, my issue is this - kidney recipients use their insurance, so they are the vip. i've ran into two other anonymous donners and they echo my feelings of the process..." thanks for the kidney, bye, bye". i can't prove that they "skimped" on my care, pain meds, etc., but i went home with less pain meds from the kidney transplant, than the meds i got months earlier from a tendon reattachment. thankfully i only used three days' worth and had leftovers. i don't know if the recipient received vip care - i will never know, but i can only hope she (i know it was a 30ish female) is doing well and did received great care - i did not. 
while the shortage of donners that is needed grows, i wish they could incentivize people to donate. no, not monetarily, but by insisting doctor, nurses and the process of donation makes you feel like a vip. i don't need someone fawning over me, but if i felt like a patient that was doing a good thing through exceptional care, i would have appreciated my donation more. if i were you - i would go to the pain/travel of donating in phoenix and stay away from banner umc.

review:
i delivered my baby here at lakewood ranch medical center. we had an absolute excellent experience from start to finish. i went into labor on new year's day and was really nervous that care would be subpar on a holiday. but contrary to my hesitations, the care was top-notch. all of the nurses and the staff couldn't have done any more for us. 

everything was exceptionally clean and to my knowledge, all the billing was done appropriately. they really took excellent care of me and my baby here.

er staff is exceptional. coming to the er countless times with aging parents and younger family members, for major problems to minor cuts and bug bites, service has always been very fast, competent,  and efficent. 

the hospital pcu has provided our family outstanding care. the staff on this floor involves family members in the care process whenever they can. nurses and doctors quickly attend to patient needs and, importantly, are sympathetic to patient well-being.

patient records are keyed into the computer system, as patient interaction occurs, and is easily accessible to all staff. at shift changes, the incoming and outgoing nurses discuss history of patient in front of the family and patient, bringing everyone up-to-date on progress. 

the hospital encourages families or patient to write a recommendation honoring a favorite staff member at the completion of their stay. one staff member then is selected monthly to be recognized for their performance. great idea! but how do you select one when each and every staff member performs their assigned duties to perfection?

menu choices are very appealing and arrive at patient's desired time - fresh and hot! the room is cleaned daily and patients are thoroughly hygiened by nursing staff. this hospital is a cheerful place.

tldr: with the exception of my assigned psychiatrist, the staff was kind caring and skilled. however, the psychiatrist was so arrogant and disinterested as to render the rest of the facilities treatment resources inaccessible to the average person confined to the facility. therefore, all the good of the facility is more than erased by the psychiatrist.

with the help of skilled psychiatrists and therapists, i have been managed my illness. however, it is not always smoothing and i had a flair-up that necessitated hospitalization. i would have liked to go to sharp mesa vista (smv) where their intensive outpatient program had been so helpful, but was sent to api as they had the first bed available. 

there, they assigned dr sam etchie as my psychiatrist. instead of doing anything for my treatment, he was was hindrance that he put me at greater risk. dr. sam etchie's failed to do any sort of mental health work-up on me. he failed to follow-up when api didn't get my medication dosage correct from the e.r. instead he cut me off cold turkey from a lifesaving medication; a medication that must be ramped up and down. he failed to establish and or drive a treatment plan.

instead, etchie leaves created and driving any sort of treatment is left to the patient. since most patients do not have the knowledge or motivation or coherence to do this. as a result, even with all the other wonderful staff and resources, the place is just a state mandated, insurance funded, revolving door for the untreated. if you want any real treatment, (1) you must be motivated to seek it, (2) you must know what to ask for, (3) you must know be coherent enough to ask for it, and (4) you must have a support on the outside to provide help. most of the patients fall short in one or more of these areas, making the place no help to most. if they would clean house on their psychiatrists, i believe the facility could provide so much help.

review:
my mom was admitted here on christmas eve with a shattered femur and needed emergency surgery.  for start to finish the whidbey health medical staff was absolutely wonderful.  their caring, attentive staff helped ease a horrific situation.  i was so happy the surgeon was able to take my mom's complicated case.  the private room made it easier for my mom to recover as there was a sofa bed i could sleep on in her room. having a family member with my mom 24/7 could let my mom relax and focus on getting better.  my only complaint/suggestion is not to get a room right next to the exit.  when people would go in and out the doors at night, it would wake my mom up. however, i will say our cna put a sign on the door asking people to use the other door.  they also brought us a fan for some white noise. 

all the staff here seem happy and act friendly and that is a good indicator that management takes good care of them.  i want to make sure i give everyone credit for the care of my mother to admissions, er, doctors/surgeons, x-ray tech, lab tech, mri, physical therapist, social services/discharge, nutritionist/kitchen, and housekeeping.  but the biggest shoutout needs to go to the nurses.  the nursing staff at whmc rocks!

the hospital is sneaky when they bill insurance.  for outpatient hip ultrasounds they bill the insurance two separate76885 codes.  one is for the provider fee, and the other is a facility fee.  why charge a facility fee for outpatient services?  hospitals are becoming more and more sneaky in billing, and patients have to become aware and fight back.
