review:
be very wary and second guess everything they tell you. i felt like i was studying for medical school having to constantly review the care my late spouse was receiving.

it really started to sink in about three years ago. my spouse was misdiagnosed as just a urinary tract infection by a physician's assistant at the kaiser pasadena urgent care, in may 2017, and ended up at kaiser sunset emergency room,and was finally diagnosed with an enlarged prostate. this should have been reported to the medical board then.

he met a urologist at that er, and agreed to start seeing him at his regular medical practice. it was confirmed a few months later, that he actually had prostate cancer. he was being treated with a watch and wait, very passive lupron injection treatment. this went along well until it finally dawned on me that the injections he was being given weren't doing anything for him. i didn't realize his urologist wasn't treating the cancer. i had to request a referral to the oncology department in december 2018. by then sadly the cancer had spread. the oncologist told me he wished he'd been seen sooner. and even made a comment about the notorious lack of aggressive treatment by that particular urologist.

the cancer treatment was starting to go well for a few weeks. and then an early morning er visit for a heart issue revealed an enlarged left ventricle, and the blood thinner, coumadin, was prescribed.

my spouse was supposedly being monitored by kaiser sunset for the blood thinner level and they'd call weekly, and tell him the dosage he should take of the coumadin.

my spouse was at his primary care doctor in pasadena in february 2019, when he suffered another heart issue and was rushed by ambulance to huntington memorial. that room was clean and staff was attentive. kaiser sent a nurse and ambulance to remove him from huntington and took him to kaiser sunset.

i went to see him at kaiser and some strange male nurse was attending to him. the nurse also kept hiding behind the curtain. the nurse refused to acknowledge me and it became clear that this nurse had some kind of mental problem so i had to go to the head nurse and have another nurse assigned. the second nurse said i was right to report the other nurse. apparently weird nurse had other run-ins. second nurse very professional so i didn't pursue any further.

it was a sad state of affairs that caused my spouse to end up at the urgent care in pasadena again, which will be another yelp review.

my spouse had run out of his pain medication. his primary care doctor, wrote the prescription and noted on the bottle to take up to 4 times a day as needed for pain. i called the doctor's office several times to refill the prescription starting on saturday 03/02/19. for some reason the primary care doctor's office ignored my spouse and was acting strangely and not renewing the prescription. i was told i would have to bring the patient in to urgent care since the doctor had no appointments. 

at the urgent care on monday 3/4,/19, the doctor was saying why were you taking so much of the pain meds? i then told him that was how it was prescribed, up to 4 times daily on the bottle. so basically he was saying don't follow the prescription directions. my spouse was supposed to know to take less than what his primary doctor said. again requiring second guessing his doctor.

my spouse got a small prescription of the pain meds, a laxative and an antibiotic from the urgent care. 

antibiotics interfere with blood thinners but he was assured that the monitoring by kaiser sunset would catch any issues.

he went to get his blood level checked after an appointment at kaiser sunset 03/07/19.

the evening of 03/07/19 he was called by the kaiser sunset inr clinic and told not to take anymore coumadin. he told that person he'd already taken the dosage that evening and asked specifically what needed to be done? 

kaiser sunset told him to come back monday. never telling how dangerously high the blood thinner level was and with no sense of urgency.

he ended up going to huntington memorial in pasadena by ambulance with a massive bleed the next day, friday, march 8.  i was told his blood was so thin he could have died merely sneezing. 

he never regained consciousness. he died monday march 11. the same day he was told to go back to kaiser.

the hospital is recently new.  the facility is immaculate.  the staff is personable and many are very compassionate.  the food trays are excellent and have a good variety.  guest trays are reasonably priced.  a pullout bed is available for spouses or caregivers to stay overnight.  parking is a bit of a challenge due to the number of people being served.  usually, the doctors are tops. however, i doubt that i will ever go there for care in the future.  they are clearly understaffed.  

example #1:   my wife has a bladder problem.   she had just come out of knee replacement surgery.  about 3 hours later, she wet the bed because the nurse or aide did not answer the call in a reasonable time.  other calls were made.  my wife told me that she laid in her own urine from 7:00 pm to nearly 7:00 am.  it appears that the night shift may have had too much to do.

example #2:  one of the doctors decided that she was getting too much pain medication.  without contacting the surgeon who prescribed it, the doctor adjusted (reduced) the medicine to fit his wishes.   my wife subsequently complained of severe pain.  after over an hour of intense pain (she said the pain was a 12 on a scale of 1 to 10) she was finally told that a nurse would be in in about 20 minutes.  prior to that she had also called because she was wet again.  it was about an hour and a half before she received additional pain medication and about two hours of laying in her own urine again before they came and took her to the bathroom.

example #3  while i was taking my wife's suitcase to the car, the discharge papers were being given to my wife without my presence even though i would be the caretaker for the next few weeks.    when we got home and i started reviewing the information, the names of the  drugs on the paperwork didn't even match those on the pill bottles, and the amounts were duplicated.  i literally had to write down the scripts of ten different bottles and their bottle directions so i would know what and when to give.  

example #4:  as stated above, pain did not seem to be an issue for the staff.  upon discharge, my wife was taken to my car in a wheel chair.  as soon as she was pushed to the car, the attendant left.  my wife was in so much pain and so stiff from the bandages and surgery that she was nearly unable to get into the car.  we had to have her scoot herself along the back seat with me on the other side of the back seat helping to pull her in before we could even get the doors closed...all this without anyone from the hospital staff helping.  i almost took her to back to the hospital to be readmitted as she was in so much pain that it appeared that i would not be able to  accommodate her needs.  it was about four hours later after giving her the drugs that should have been administered in  the hospital that my wife was finally relieved of much of her pain.

i started by saying that the staff is compassionate.  when someone finally did come to my wife's aid, they were very kind and willing to assist.  so was the staff guilty of  incompetence?  doubtful?  lack of staffing?  likely.
one more note.  after my wife had laid in urine for an hour and a half without assistance, i arrived in the hospital and went into the hallway to solicit help since the pager on the bed was soliciting no response.  two women (nurses or nurses aids) were sitting together talking to one another right outside of my wife's room.  one did tell me that she would get a nurse, and she also helped take my wife to the restroom and clean the bed.  but why did it take an advocate to get help?

review:
this was my first experience at this hospital, and  i was there for a normal annual physical.  the doctor and her nurse were great, the wait was about 30mins from my appointment, but clinics usually have that kind of wait time.  what made my experience 1 star and don't want to ever return to this hospital was the lab!

1. the phlebotomist that took my blood was not very nice.  she was chatting with her coworkers about wanting to get off work while she was drawing my blood.
2. she mislabeled my sample bottle!  it was labeled with a completely different name and birthdate.  so if you do labs at this hospital, make sure you check to make sure their labeling has your name on it.  had i not checked, my sample would have turned into somebody else's, and who knows which will be mine.  on top of that, when i approached her about mislabeling and i will need a new label, she just snatched the sample from me, didn't say a word, and made an angry face at me as if it was my fault for checking.  i asked her if my other samples she took had correct labeling, she retorted back "yeah, what, do you want to check those samples too?"  she didn't even apologize for putting the wrong labeling.  it was a horrible experience.  i have never been to a lab as messy as this and as rude as this place!

4.  and someone throughout the process misspelled my name.

so if you decide to go to this hospital because there's no other choice, be ready for very rude people, and remember to double check their sample labeling when they take blood or urine from you.  i understand that this is a huge, busy hospital, but i have been to ut southwestern/texas presbyterian hospitals before, and they were never messy like this place!

review:
for the insane cost of this "private" facility, you'll end up in a whole world of hurt.

a close family member ("cc") was involved with this program for a little over 2.5 years. after "graduating," cc then relocated and continued in outpatient therapy with the same psychiatrist. a few months ago, we terminated treatment with this provider. we finally realized that the provider was squirrely at best and only sought to make messes for cc that he would have no part in cleaning up.

prior to entering treatment, cc was on zero medications, had zero hospitalization, and zero history of drug abuse. cc was in school full time, working part time, active in our church community, and generally managing. following a traumatic life event, we voluntarily chose to have cc enter the retreat on the recommendation of our home psychologist.

after a series of:
-tms (junk science),
-ect (victorian, invasive shock therapy),
-2 years worth of toxic medication trials, and
-1.5 years of outpatient group therapy
-relocating cc several states away to continue treatment,
we are at a massive loss emotionally and financially.

the retreat psychiatrist (who led our family member's care) had far too much faith in his own capabilities. he had a deceptively closed-minded focus on his personal field of study, which we know now, doesn't really help with the functional treatment of complex trauma. we didn't get to choose cc's providers, but knowing what we know now, we never would have chosen this path for them.

you practically need a phd in psychiatric practice to understand how this program works. we were very blindsided to learn that the arcane psychoanalysis was the foundation for the retreat's programming. they tout dbt, but it's two sessions per week, which are confusing and disorganized at best.

the treatment team routinely exercised poor judgement in assessing the dynamics of cc's complicated trauma background, which continued throughout the entire course of care. they essentially allowed cc's biological parents (and main payors) to dictate the care and treatment strategies used, which resulted in a series of misdiagnoses.

it's a rampant issue in healthcare, but the providers are wholly protected by the system from bearing any consequence for their "firm suggestions." they put the onus on the patients and their families to be the ultimate deciders, but it really became a toxic cycle of the blind leading the blind. we didn't feel like we had a choice at any point if we wanted cc to get on a path to recovery.

think of sinking an average year's salary for a 3-week-long diagnostic workup by a supposed "team of experts." a mix of art therapists and social workers will work with your psychiatrist to strong arm the patient into a desire to "get better" and then coerce the family into refinancing their home to get the recommended weeks to months of extended care at over $2000 per day. this includes an intensive regimen of loosey-goosey therapy groups, bizarre binders full of self-help jargon, and patient-guided group therapy. they are trying to be progressive, but it's a classic case of poor administrative controls and defaulting into letting the inmates run the asylum. it honestly feels like some of the providers get a kick out making things messy and watching us drown while we try to clean up catastrophe after catastrophe. they just smile at us and placate us with politicized psychiatric jargon.

once we pursued outside consultation, we realized we'd been completely, wholly, massively duped by these supposed "experts" and gamed by a very unregulated rehabilitation system. unless medication management and positive talk therapy are the $200,000+ boost you need, these people constantly come up short.

after all is said and done, we were dealing with an entirely different medical and psychiatric picture than the providers were willing to treat or even investigate. hundreds of thousands of dollars later, and hundreds of hours of travel, family therapy, and the many years cc devoted to their own therapy, we have very little to show for it.

we are left with immeasurable pain and suffering, a heap of debt, and a solid education in the toxic dysfunction of the behavioral health system.

this is in reference to the outpatient intensive therapy day program. i was really at a low when i entered into this program. prior to entering i was very afraid. after being there for some time it felt safe. the staff members are very helpful and resourceful. they are willing to assist in whatever your need may be at the time. it may be a little uneasy on your first few days because you have to get to know people and be comfortable enough to want to share your story. you are never forced to do anything. this is a very intensive program. i suggest if you are not ready to do the work to help you heal this is not the program for you. the program teaches numerous skills that can aid in getting a grip on your mental illness. on the outside you may feel like an outcast. this is one place you can come and not be obligated to wear a mask. meaning you can be yourself. you have the opportunities to listen to others story. you also have the opportunity to share your story. you receive plenty of advice and suggestions. there is a daily schedule. first meeting with your nurse to discuss the daily questionnaire you must complete each morning. next you move on to a class with your social worker. once that is completed you continue with 4 more daily classes. the day starts at 8:30 am and ends at 3:20 pm. the program is monday thru friday. if you are truly ready to learn more about your illness and are ready to apply learned skills this program may be for you. i appreciate what is being taught there and look forward to using the learned skills to make coping with my illness easier.

review:
sitting at work one fine day, when sudden pain in my chest, hard to breathe, sweating, dizzy... yup, major cardiac event. dr. guru khalsa was and is an amazing physician, with an excellent bedside manner and a good, keen head on his shoulders. he made a good call on the diagnosis and subsequent surgery, and i'm here to write another epic review.

the nursing staff at chomp is beyond compare. in all the years i've lived here and visited this facility, i have never had need to say anything but the absolute best about these dedicated, hard working  linchpins of medical support. always cheerful, always going the extra mile, always doing way more than one could possibly imagine to make a difficult situation as easy and pleasant as possible. really, i could go in for days about the stellar care from the nursing staff here. just beyond compare in every possible way, in every department.

doctors are very much a personality based, subjective judgement. in my experience here, 99% of these hard working folks are exemplary across the board. they always seem to have all the time you need to understand where you were, why you got where you are, and the best possible way forward.

i'm not saying all this great stuff just because i'm feeling euphoric over having my life saved. these folks are the absolute best i've encountered anywhere.

of course, every rainbow has a shadow (not literally, but...) and at chomp you will find that all that excellent, high end care comes with a supremely high end price. they say good health is priceless, and chomp billing takes that to the extreme. still, what's your life worth? 

i happen to be lucky enough that i feel i have a really great life. so i'll pay that price, and be grateful that i'm around to pay.

review:
took my husband back to chomp er this evening.  while the triage nurse, registration and the er tech who takes vitals are fantastic!  they know us by sight!  on the other hand, the er doctor, dr. collins, is a joke.  

we experienced some horrible care by this doctor over the past couple of months.  my husband has several bulging discs in his neck and bone spurs which are pressing on the nerves in his neck for which i've taken him to chomp for help.  

so this evening, i took my husband to the er, like i said, and dr. collins came into the exam room, even after we said we wanted another doctor.  he went on to say that he was the only doctor back in express care.  wrong!!!  dr. ellison was there and so was the physician's assistant.  dr. collins then said "well what are we supposed to do for you tonight?"  i explained that my husband was experiencing some urological problems and could they be caused by the bulging discs in his neck that are pressing on some nerves. dr. collins said "the mri didn't really show any significant problems".  he needs to go back to school and learn how to read. 

we then asked him to try and contact the neurologist and he blatantly lied and said that this doctor didn't have privileges at chomp.  wrong again!!  according to the neurologist's profile on the hospital website, it clearly states that he has privileges at chomp. 

i then asked dr. collins about a recent discharge summary and he said that he never did these reports.  well, i located it in relay health portal and showed it to him.  i won't go into what it said for privacy reasons.  he read it and said that he stands by what he said.  one thing it did state was that my husband was trying to take out his iv.  my husband isn't stupid enough to do this.

chomp has this program called edie which stands for emergency department information exchange.  according to an er nurse, this is something that automatically tracks the number of er visits you've had in a short period of time.  well, if you're a senior citizen without a primary care doctor, what the h**l are you supposed to do when you're in pain, can't swallow or pee?  they don't tell you about this program and even the people in the administration that i talked to, didn't know anything about it.  

we left when it was clear that nothing was going to be done.  after we got home, i pulled out the after visit summary and under reason for visit, dr. collins put down neck pain.  wrong again!  we went in for a urological problem.

the er tech didn't even clean up the room that we were in.  i saw a bottle of a numbing medicine that's injected on the tray along with what looked like bandaging strips.  i did take pictures but i won't post them. i'm keeping them to show the administration when i talk to them tomorrow.

i won't be taking my husband back to the er anytime soon with the exception of a life-threatening condition.  i'll drive over to natividad if i can.

came to this kaiser panorama city pharmacy for an emergency medication written by my pcp. thankfully, i looked at my member benefits and it said no charge for this medication. however, when i went to check out i was informed by the pharm tech that i need to pay retail price for it because she said it's not emergency and that routine medications are consider emergency. uhh, no sweetie, when the medication has the word "emergency" on it, it's considered emergency and medication you take every day to prevent something is not considered emergency. kaiser really need to look at education when hiring their pharmacy tech. anyways i told her to bill it to me. she said she can't do that. she finally had to ask someone else. thankfully a pharmacist who understand kaiser's policy, acknowledged that i can be billed. so when i got my bill, i was able to dispute it and got the charge removed because i quoted from the member handbook including detailed information on exclusion and inclusion and kp acknowledged it was an error. so takeaways from my experience are:

1. know your member's rights. you have the rights to the latest copy of your member handbook/member benefits. make sure you ask for it with information on all the inclusion and exclusions. it's alot of pages but read it so you can be informed of what's covered. ask for a translation in your language if you prefer (it's part of your rights).

2. if you question the cost of something and you're a kp member, ask them to bill you so you can dispute it.

3. if kaiser charges you for something that is a covered benefit, it's considered fraud. file an grievance and/or appeal with them first. if it doesn't get resolve or address within 30 days, you should notify dhcs (for medi-cal), cms (for medicare), and/or dmhc in general so an investigation can be opened. let these organizations know as well if you see quality related issues. if they get fined, they lose fundings and accreditation.

be your own advocate and know what are your rights as a patient!

a few days prior to discharge, the facility delivers transition instructions to family members and caretakers to educate and ensure sustained improvement!!!!!

review: coming to the hospital as a child was always fantastic. when i officially "became an adult" with not the greatest insurance the care changed and i never felt the same care. my father has also had multiple surgeries that have never seemed to go right because we are always back "having it fixed." i guess it's like everywhere you go though, it depends on the people helping you and how much they care.

so. we were told to be here at 8:30 this morning. upon arrival, they took us back and let us sit for 3 hours in a room before the doctor came for pre-op consultation . he didn't even know what exactly was supposed to be done . he had to call his office to find out what he was doing. 
while waiting in the waiting room, they called me into a room so the doctor could tell me how the surgery went. i sat in there for an hour waiting until i finally just left and went back to the waiting room. 
the workers were talking loudly about how this was the worst job they have ever had . says a lot about the hospital. i wouldn't come here again if my life depended on it!

went in tonight for my significant other to get checked out for back/knee pain due to a car accident he was in earlier in the day. everyone on staff were so  efficient, caring, and made sure you felt welcome along with having everything you needed. of course it was a saturday night so we weren't in and out but you have to know that going into an er regardless i feel like. our nurse connor (redish hair, white scrubs) was seriously the nicest, most respectful, and kindest nurse we have ever encountered. he definitely made the visit less stressful & more welcoming. thank you connor. and the rest of the staff for taking care of my significant other tonight. you guys are very appreciated.

dr. pritchett was great- very professional, knowledgeable & kind. nurses were wonderful too! check-in was terrible. was sent wrong address for appointment, check in ipad lost battery, medical assistant called my baby girl a mister, was unable to use digital insurance card, and there was no smiles from anyone at front desk. as long as you can make it through the office door everything is awesome!

i checked in at the emergency room at south shore hospital at 2pm. its 715pm now and still waiting. 3 other patients waiting with me. nobody can give answer as to what the delay is. and why aren't they passing out face masks to these patients who are coughing up their lungs? just spray the flu virus all over the hospital why don't you? i should have made the trip to hammond st. margaret or south suburban. never coming back to ssh ever again except to visit someone i may know

came in with a broken wrist. i was seen within 15 minutes. all the staff was incredibly informative and friendly. dr. seefeld set my wrist and did an incredible job! i went home to boston and the surgeon at tufts said it was some of the best work they've seen. would absolutely recommend!

i have always received good care through east jeff.er.about 12 years ago my son was given an antibiotic by a male nurse before a spinal tap caused him to spend a week in children's hospital. what do you expect from a male nurse who's busy flirting instead of doing his job.

i recently took my mother to the er.  as a former healthcare executive with responsibility for multiple facilities across the u.s., i was incredibly disappointed with the facility.  the ramp to the enter the er is filthy and extremely patient unfriendly.  one patient registration kiosk woefully inadequate.  if i were the administrator i would be ashamed of how patients are greeted and taken through their care.  the staff were fine and i feel sorry for what they have to contend with facility wise.  to say that this is an incredibly inadequate facility would be an understatement!

horrible emergency room...they do not communicate ur chart symptoms and medication u r on to dr.when u get in a room  r shd i say behind a curtain decided by 6..r he just didnt read them ..he was rude..nurse was great..hospital er was filthy..i was given injections then bp and heart rate sky rocketed with no dr ..r nurse in site..bp beeper stayed on..blood pressure and heart kept rising i honestly thought i was about to hv a heart attact had to send my husband to find nurse ..they didnt even know i was on bp meds r didnt read chart.i thought i wasnt coming out of there alive...this er use to b a lot better it has hone downhill bad..really bad...will not go bk there ever i am changing all ej connected drs to oshner drs..and i always pay my bill's on time but they harass u to death even when u do...so goodbye ejgh...poorly run..oh and time b4 that they only had 1 non working bp cuff in er and laughed about it....sad.....

i arrived with a pain in the belly at 7pm i gave up and i was although at 10:30 without being attended!  really horrible hospital trash care at the reception grumpy people!  dirty bathroom!  it's worth driving 30 min and going on cha revere!

do not bother to go here if you have an emergency. the er and staff are the absolute worst. you're more likely to die waiting, than getting any sort of decent human interaction. no one cares about you, they see you as just work. and clearly they hate their jobs. the wait is ridiculous. not worth your time. go anywhere but here, no matter how urgent your case is.

mile bluff medical clinic massage
incredible first time experience. i've had many a massage in the big cities and this was by far the best!  first christmas my husband gave me a gift certificate for a 60 minute massage. natasha was outstanding. very excellent personality and strong firm hands. worked whole body and focused on my stressed points. room was warm comforting and peaceful. i feel like a million bucks

thank you

went to this "hospital" for blood work. it looks like a hospital from the outside but inside there is one woman at the "emergency" entrance receiving everyone, many people just didn't wait and entered the hospital without checking in, i wandered down the halls and found the lab and rang the bell, no answer. then i waited in line and tried not to hear  while patients had to explain why they needed medical attention in public. shameful. 

and even though the computer 
generated ordered were from another uchealth  hospital i was told it needed a signature from a doctor. i said really? it must be in the computer system.  she left and went into another room and came back and said yes we can't give you the test. 

ok......you mean there are people back therewhile people wait on line for the emergency department and they are waiting behind me while we figure out a clerical problem.

so i just leave, no problem, it's routine blood test. 

i thank god i wasn't there for anything serious.

i was visiting my family from out of state and had severe back pain for 4 days. i know my body and knew something had to be wrong as i couldn't even move anymore. i visited this location at 5am. i was the only person in there so the snarky comments from the nurse and doctor about "being an emergency facility" numerous times was obviously a big turn off and they rushed me out with a "you should visit your primary". once again.. i'm from out of state so i don't have a primary nearby. i told them i didn't want pain meds, i just wanted to understand the cause of pain so that i could address as necessary. i'm not a pain pill girl... they prescribed me some extra strength tylenol and pain patches. i asked the nurse if he knew where i could fill the prescription nearby and he said "we aren't a pharmacy". clearly that's not what i was asking... i was just from out of state and was hoping with his knowledge of the area he could recommend a 24 hour pharmacy to help. i don't go to the doctor often, but this might be a great example of why.. incredibly dismissive and disappointing. now that i read reviews, i'm looking forward to dealing with the billing side next. do yourself a favor.. pick a different hospital. i wish i would have researched this place first. after all of that, i ended up at the grocery store with icy hot and lots of tears until i could fill my prescription.

january 2018 after stroke i entered mercy rehab hospital in full panic mode.  as a non resident of st louis previous to stroke, i was very lucky to have been sent to this rehab hospital.  jill will always be remembered as the most compassionate and clinical therapist along with ot and speech therapists. without jill's guidance and tenacity i have no idea how i would have known what strength and what grit i possessed!  she led me and i followed her to believing that i could "do it".  and i have progressed to another tenacious and dedicated physical therapist, kristen pierce, at peak sport and spine, who also led me and i followed her to believe i can live independently 2 years later. i would never have made this progress without the fantastic two women mentioned above.  wishing them both love, health and happiness...and love from peggy

my husband went to pinnacle urgent care for a swollen, red ankle.
doctor diagnosed him with cellulitis, and he admitted him.
during my husband's five day admission, the care he received was good.

when he was discharged, he didn't receive any after care instructions.
they gave him a light  compression stocking  to wear. i asked the nurse if the sock had to be removed when he went to bed  . she said: patients sleep with the soon on here.

well, that was the wrong answer. he was home for 2 days, & when he removed the stocking, his shin/ankle was so much worse. we went to community hospital, where he again was admitted for another five days!

he lost 3 weeks of pay, because he had to keep his leg elevated 90% of the time..

if he got accurate discharge instructions, he wouldn't of been hospitalized a second time, not to mention all the additional hospital/doctor bills.

i went to pinnacle to have a venogram.  i had no idea this hospital even existed.  i'm so glad i do now!  most places i have been are so overcrowded and the wait time is unbelievable.  everyone there really has it together.  i was totally impressed!  3 nurses to one patient....what?  it was insane!   great job pinnnacle you made a very scary procedures a piece of a cake.

i was having strong pains in my back on the lower left side and thought it might be kidney stones. i went to the er and they were very friendly and efficient.  they did all the necessary tests and found nothing and said it was probably a muscle pull.  i was in and out of there within 2 hours.
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center Hinsdale

review: we arrived at 10:50pm after my 73 yr old mom had a severe head injury from a fall with blood streaming down her face.  we explained she fell and saw stars and had a deep cut and may have cracked her skull. 55 minutes and we are in the waiting room with people with colds and fevers going ahead of us. we asked for a sterile towel as the bleeding was not controlled and the front desk representative pulled one from the drawer next to him! ugh.  isn't er supposed to be a place to sort out injuries by severity? this place should be reported.
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center Hinsdale

review: my son has been admitted with rsv.  the care has been excellent so far.  the doctors and nurses have been extremely attentive and informative.  they have answered all my questions and then some.
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center Hinsdale

review:
the parking does not have enough space. i visited oncology in november of last year and the building for that department is okay, the room is descent.
i visited a loved one who had cancer and his bed had no sheet, no pillow, no blanket and both of his socks had holes. he was mainly lying down on a mattress and it was winter.
a nurse, particularly with the name of kim in oncology seemed unknowledgeable about how to deal with cancer patient and their changed behavior. i believe that medical staff like her should be trained on how to handle the emotional trauma of cancer patients to have better understanding of their behavior.  i never had any good impression in this hospital since i was hospitalized here in 2000 once and never wanted to be back. i just had to visit a loved one who unfortunately was hospitalized and passed in this hospital in less than 3 weeks of hospitalization and was very disappointed to see his bed condition and experienced an inefficient nurse with the name kim. i believe that nurses should be trained on emotional behavior of patients particularly cancer patients to have better understanding. or it maybe that they already are, but was just unfortunate to get an inefficient one for my loved one.

this place is a joke. receptionist not very friendly and seems like providing the minimum of professional customer service is the norm. very silo orientated department. if you are stuck using this hospital i feel for you. if you have a choice do yourself a favor and and go somewhere else , i'm sure you will receive better treatment. sorry for interrupting you while you gossip about your cousin with your co worker miss receptionist. 
on the bright side there was martha in the ct department that went above and beyond to help out. i wish our appointment was in her department. great job martha and thank you.

this review is for their massage services.   the massage area is located in the women's center on the first floor.   the ambiance of the massage area is very calm.  i had trudy as the masseuse and she was fantastic.   she's very nice and the massage was very thorough asking me what areas i wanted to focus on.  oh and the massage table is heated so that was a bonus.  i'll definitely be going back.

i went to the washington hospital er this weekend, and i would not recommend it. i told them i was having chest pain, which can be serious, but it did not seem to register with the customer service rep, for they went on about their business as usual, in a very slow pace, seeing a patient who had arrived after me before me. they also did not ask me to fill out a medical history form, while i was in the waiting room, which is problematic. what if i fainted in the er, who would have told them my relevant medical history? anyways, when i met the er nurse, who was taking my information, i told them all the medicine i took. but on the discharge sheet, i noticed, she had forgotten to put down one of the meds i mentioned. the er doctor gave me a tylenol (and when i refused, because the aspirins i took were having an effect) he gave me toradol shot (which is an even stronger pain killer). i am really concerned by the lack of proper procedure in this er. this er needs to be fixed or shut down.

i have always had issues with this hospital whether it's incredibly long waits, doctors who don't care enough, or rude staff there is always some sort problem arising. this trip has by far been the worst though.
rushed to the emergency room around 4pm with my 2 year old boy having a sudden onset fever from the same day. having a heart defect, my main concern for him is always a heart infection and so he is usually first priority. 
stood by the wait sign for 15 minutes before anyone acknowledged my son and i. the attendant at the window didn't say a word to us initially and didn't even ask for a moment before she asked for id and reason for visit. once checked in he went to get his vitals taken and his temperature read at 102.4. a dose of motrin and two and a half hours later his fever finally broke so i got up to ask the nurse if i could just go pick up some motrin and monitor at home since i wasn't sure how much longer it would take. she informed me there was a still a great deal of people ahead of him so she agreed that it seemed like a good course of action for me to take seeing as this was his only symptom.
find myself back 2 1/2 hours later because the fever is back, he has thrown  up and now has chills. am still currently sitting in the waiting room with the only progress being that now they are doing a flu swab. but still have no idea how long until we get seen, if we even get seen by a doctor. the nurse who took my son's vitals and temp was pretty rude. they genuinely do not care about taking care of you as a patient and most of the times i  have come here have been a waste of time since i get little to no answers. have been coming here for two years  and nothing improves here so it is a big disappointment.
fac_name: Dwight D Eisenhower Army Medical Center

lets rate the emergency room today.
i went to the emergency room for a searing 9/10 hip pain, in tears and hysterical. i wasn't really aware of my surroundings but i did have my family with me. the only thing that helped was pacing, then laying in fetal and pacing again. they put me in a room, i paced out front of it crying quietly. then a nurse at the desk told me they preferred me stay in my room. i pleaded to her hysterically that it was the only thing that helped. she rolled her eyes at me so i kept on pacing. i was in front of my room, it's not like i was freaking out walking the hospital- i don't even believe i was sobbing loudly. 
when the x-ray team arrived they were so ginger and careful and understood me. however, they found nothing. not a darn thing. so i'm here. no answers, being told i'm fine, as i experience what feels like some on twisting a pitchfork in my hip and pulling my quad muscle from my femur and knee. pleasant yes? 
at this point my husband left me with my teen son to go get our other children from school.
a woman whom ,i'm assuming was a doctor, later appeared. and at this point i was in the phase of fetal rocking. she asked me to feel around on this lump on my hip. does this hurt? no. she pushed with moderate force on my hip, triggering a dull ache, i started to cry. she proceeds to tell me i have a lipoma, a fatty tumor, that doesn't really cause pain. then she disappeared after telling me they'll get a referral started and get me discharged. that's really all i could comprehend.
i started to pace again trying to relieve the agonizing pain from the area. i think i placed myself in the floor  sobbing. now thinking back was probably the grossest thing i could have done. a lady appeared, not a doctor. she began to tell me something about orthopedic and scheduling. i told her i didn't understand what she was asking. she asked me if i could schedule a visit. i told her i didn't know. she proceeded to say dates and times and i simply could not hear her over the pain. my son handed me my phone while i lay on the floor and i opened it. i clicked on some apps, i forgot what i was looking for. i asked again what i was doing. she told me dates. i couldn't for the life of me figure out what i was supposed to do so i started to cry again. she said something and left. i now realize that she was trying to schedule me an orthopedic and follow up appointment.
i started to pace, the fetal phase was no longer working, back to the hysteria walking phase. it had been 2 hours of hell. pure hell. someone showed up, a nurse i believe. she handed me some papers and told me to stick to my appointments and to go through the doors to the right. my son grabbed my items and i lead me down the hall. suddenly we were outside. i suddenly realized- they discharged me. i kept to my pacing and fetal on the bench. since my husband left to get my other children, my son and i stayed outside with no way home. turned away by the hospital, no relief from my living hell and no way home. 
this is lake norman emergency.

02/16-17/2020 - diabetes type i patient arrived at 2:30pm in emergency for elevated blood sugar and vomiting. after 2hr wait, the medical staff informed the patient at 4pm that he will be moved to icu.

then, sudden silence and everyone exits the room with the male nurse sharing; "we will have a nurse come to disconnect the iv". not more than five minutes later the patient is disconnected, he traveled the distance to his regular physician, treated and is doing well.

world-class care at a small regional hospital? who would have guessed, but it's 100% true. 

i'm an internal medicine physician (m.d; board-certified)
visiting from los angeles and was finishing dinner at a restaurant in boca with my 85 year-old dad on a saturday evening when he suddenly collapsed to the left and was having a stroke in front of my eyes. 

rushed him to boca regional medical center where they were already on high alert (we called ahead) and they implemented their "stroke alert" protocol with all hands on deck. 

on arrival, the (terrific) nurses whisked him directly from the front door to the head doc in the er (david leeman, md), he did a quick but thorough neurological assessment while dad was still in a hospital-provided wheelchair and sent him immediately to the ct scanner for a sophisticated brain perfusion scan. mind you, this all took no more than 6 minutes from er door to ct scanner (!).

ct scan showed no major blockages (thank g_d), but did show a small area that had subtly narrowed blood vessels and wasn't getting enough blood/oxygen to dad's brain for a short time. thus, the stroke symptoms at the restaurant. 

here's the best/mind-blowing part: within minutes, they had dad back from his ct scan and into one of the er's "critical care" beds, wheeled a two-way video monitor to dad's bedside and a top cleveland clinic neurologist-stroke specialist appeared live on screen and she did a remote bedside teleconsult (freshly-done ct brain perfusion scan on her computer) and chatted with/"examined" dad on the spot. 

she determined that dad had a "tia" (mini-stroke") but did not need (effective but sometimes dangerous) clot-busting drug treatment. after a team of (incredibly kind/efficient/competent) nurses took a detailed medical history, drew blood and did an ekg, they wheeled dad directly to the new marcus neuroscience inpatient unit of the hospital, where another team of great nurses attended to dad, gave him his evening meds and got him properly tucked in for the night. 

bottom line: from initial stroke symptoms to er admission to completed ct scan and expert consult/diagnosis to monitored inpatient bed, the whole process took less than 90 minutes. as stated above, world class care! 

grateful and impressed beyond words. if you need emergency care in boca, there's no better place to go

my mom came in with the fire department through er in cardiac distress.  she has advanced heart failure and wears a pacemaker.

about 2 hours later we were in a room. i asked who her doctor would be. no one was sure. two residents were roaming around.  i grabbed them and took them into a quiet room on the floor to explain mom's condition.  of course, they told me i wasn't a doctor so i should let them figure out what was wrong with mom. we waited until 7a the next morning. dr. foster spent 5 minutes with mom. he is an internist, not a cardiologist. the rest of the day we waited for an echo cardiogram or some diagnostics to be done to asses her condition. it never happened.

the nurses couldn't do much, since there is no doctor on the floor (no doctor on the floor) and nurses advised that internists are only available by phone and only in case of an emergency.

my mother was dry heaving, unable to swallow, short of breath at rest (all signs of late stage heart failure) and completely unattended to except by helpless nurses.  i called my brother-in-law in pittsburgh who is a well known gerontologist and read the blood results to him.  he was appalled that there hadn't been a cardiologist in to see her, nor one assigned to her. 

i asked mom's nurse dinesha to contact the two young residents who i had learned were on duty in admitting.  she called them at least 3 times over a period of 4 hours.  finally they arrived. they asked me the same questions over and over and over again. i was losing hope and patience.  i told them i wanted a cardiac consult now.

my mom was nothing more than a school project for them. one was a junior resident, dr. awadallah, the other a senior. said they would order an echo cardiogram and assured me the cardiologist would see mom in the morning. they kept telling me, "none of this is in our control." i believe them.

finally, the patient in the room next door had to be moved to icu. the icu dr came up to our floor.  he was the only doctor i'd ever encountered outside of the residents. i asked if he was a cardiologist and one of the nurses asked me, "why do you want to know?" while a compassionate nurse named ernie, quietly told me, "yes, dr. louis is a cardiologist."

my mom was dry heaving and had extreme and advancing dyspnea (breathing distress), heart palpitations, dizziness, halos around her vision, tremors, and high anxiety. all i could do was stroke her hair and watch her gasp for air.

a kind young male nurse and a super nasty female nurse reluctantly gave us oxygen, while saying, "but she doesn't need it."  as soon as the oxygen was placed, mom felt slightly better, but still shaking, dry heaving, unable to swallow, get out of bed on her own, to toilet and generally feeling very sick.

so as of this morning, she hasn't been seen nor has the echo been read.  there is no one to talk with to help relieve the immediate distress let alone discuss a prognosis.

we have now called mom's cardiologist who does not have admitting privileges in this hospital.(boca regional is simply where the fire department took us.)

our cardiologist is currently searching for an available colleague with privileges at boca regional to intervene.  mom calls me just now to tell the her roomate is still screaming and she can't take any more.

my mother was at lifecare in dallas on record crossing during october and november 2019. i made my decision to place her there after speaking with a person that showed me around the facility and was very helpful and kind. the problem is the people in management and administration are not the ones caring for your loved ones on a day to day basis....the people that are taking care of them are low paid and low skilled employees. some were nice but many were not. the day before my mom was discharged to the hospital for a procedure, her credit card was stolen from her purse, which she always kept beside her. my mom was unable to speak and communicate....i found out about the card had been stolen when she received an email alert from her credit card provider. the person that stole the card made multiple charges that totaled over 2k at various liquor stores, clothng stores, grocery stores, gas stations and more. they had a full on shopping spree including lunch at on the border. the continued using the card for a period of 7 days and through the day after my mom passed away. i have filed police report and the problem is there are no cameras in the rooms only in the hallways. so what happens in the room cannot be seen and when your loved one cannot communicate, well the staff can steal and mistreat and there's little that can be done about it. i caution you to not use this facility and to thouroughly check any facility you are considering.

i got a call from 262-help saying that my friend had called in that she was concerned for my safety and wanted me to get evaluated. i was given two options. 1. drive to a local er and get evaluated or 2. have a screener come out and evaluate you. i was not suicidal, just having thoughts such as "this is getting hard, and i don't want to be here" i shared about my past suicide attempt and the screener became very concerned. the crisis worker came back in the room, handed the cops a paper, and said "you are being involuntarily committed". confused and surprised i said, "if you want me to go to the hospital i will go voluntarily to tvh where my insurance covers". she told me no. she said they already explained to me that i could have taken myself voluntarily to the hospital and if they come out and screen, i am automatically involuntary. i was not explained this and the screener dismissed that i was not fully informed of my rights in the situation. 
i talked to an er doc who agreed that i was not suicidal but saw that i needed additional resources outside of the hospital. the morning came and a nurse came in and said "we'll get you up to the unit soon". a social worker came and told me i was being admitted to an involuntary unit. no one offered me voluntary papers. when i asked why i was involuntary i was told "you are a healthcare professional you know how to get yourself out of here". transport came and brought me to the unit. the whole time transport was taking me to the unit she was cursing and laughing with security like i didn't even exist. i asked her to stop and not one time did she even acknowledge my existence. i got the to unit bg. i already knew the reputation this unit had because i work in healthcare. it is the most violent adult psychiatric unit in this hospital and houses the most severe psychiatric patients. i got there and was told to strip, bend and cough, and was put in a gown, showed my room and left alone without any questions answered. 
the doctor came to visit me. she immediately realized i did not belong on the unit and said she would have me discharged by the end of the day all she needed was collateral. i asked the nurse for something to eat. lunch came up without any food that they would allow me to eat because i was gluten free. once again they called for a tray. hours later dinner came. no food came again for me. at this point i had not eaten in their care for over 24 hours. 
my social worker was behind the desk. i tried calmly explaining what was going on and she walked away. frustrated i started crying then panicking. she walked back. i said "why do i need to cry in order to talk to you and have my basic needs met". she rolled her eyes and looked behind her shoulders hoping to get answers from someone else. she continued to dismiss me. i said "at the hospital i work at when someone makes a mistake, even if it isn't ours, we apologize." to which she responded with an eye roll "i'm sorry but," cutting her off i said "when you say but after a statement you negate what you just said" she walked away and an on call psychiatrist walked over to me and told me to get away from the glass and go eat dinner... to which i burst into more tears a tech yelled "call a dr. strong". realizing what a doctor strong was i tried to contain my anxiety attack and tell them, i'm not yelling, i'm not violent, i'm having a conversation about my needs not being met (while having an anxiety attack), you have no right to inject me with ativan against my will. so they didn't call the dr. strong my social worker also told me at this time i would not be discharging and did not give me a reason. over a full 24 hours after the last time the hospital fed me i finally got a piece of chicken and rice. the chicken was inedible, i still at it.
i woke up the next morning to my psychiatrist saying that since i hadn't been seeing a therapist in the past month that i would need to stay at least another day. we planned for discharge the next day. realizing i was going to stay i approached the nurse about a problem. a patient i had brought in a week (i'm an emt) earlier was on the unit and he remembered me. he sexually harassed me when i was on the ambulance and this didn't change while i was on the unit. i told the nurse i was uncomfortable and that i do not want to be on the same unit as him. the nurse told me to stay in my room until one of us discharges. because yes not leaving my room is the best solution. this patient continued to harass me and even sexually assaulted me. i didn't even bother to tell staff because it was obvious, they didn't care about my wellbeing. 
i was ready to leave. and they tried to keep me even though i was never suicidal.while i was here they messed up the dosages of my medication and took me off some of my medications. i went through active withdrawals while in the hospital. my depression got worse because i went off of my medication. i went to nbmc having a hard time and i left in a crisis

i came to the hospital back in june after i had diagnostic laparoscopy & endometriosis surgery.  i brought all my paperwork and surgery paperwork because i was having more extreme pain than usual, had a feeling i had some sort of ruptured cyst or maybe and infection.  i was greeted by this male sexist mysoginstic doctor and basically threw me out after he saw me, because he remembered me from a couple years ago because i have chronic pain. he said i was drug seeking (i am clean asf... i don't have anything in my system not even tobacco) and said i was here for the drugs. then security escorted me out, and at the time i was falling over from the pain & he loudly said "look she is walking and acting for attention." i was trying to show him my endometriosis & surgery paperwork but he was gaslighting me & saying i was forged & illegally downloaded my own paperwork wtf? is this how you treat chronic pain patients like junkies? my obgyn (the one who gave me surgery and my paperwork) she told me to come on & even get admitted for observation because i could have had a severe infection or ovarian torsion (could require emergency surgery) i did not only come in for pain but i was irregularly spotting and it was very concerning but, he didn't care & he didn't even want to check me out but just threw me out along with condescending security guards. i came home crying and just wanted to die of embarrassment because my pain as real and justified, and my paperwork is not freaking forged, stop gaslighting female patients! my mom called up the hospital and got ahold of the doctor and he kept gaslighting her saying that i was trying to start a fight which i was in so much pain i was doubled up screaming begging someone to believe me but he didn't, i have no violent history at all. he even told me that all females are overdramatic hypochondriacs!  my mom got into a screaming match with him because of how appalling his behavior was. if you stop caring about helping patients, as a doctor please quit your job. my mom got ahold of patient rights and they never got back with her. they kept snowing her and saying that they would get this resolved but they never did. stop treating pain patients like junkies! we didn't choose this life, i'm sorry you get drug addicts, but you know not all of us are &  not treating pain patients is barbaric. our health care is a human right not some sort of torture method. less than 1% of pain patients abuse their medication. #opioidhysteria 

 male doctors need to not practice medicine on females if they are just going to gaslight us, & saying that were overdramatic or we shouldn't be in pain because we can pop out babies. disgusting mysoginstic behavior!

review:
i hate going to the hospital or any appointment that's health-related, but after switching to kaiser from premera, i've only had pleasant experiences so far at kaiser and the capitol hill location was no different.

located on 15th avenue in capitol hill, it was easy to find and was accessible by public transit, as the bus stop is literally right in front of the hospital.  and though the campus is large, there was a map to show where all the different buildings and departments were, so i had no trouble at all finding where my appointment was. 

after checking into my appointment i was seen by dr. woo who could not have been friendlier.  again, i really dread going to health appointments, but dr. woo made my experience stress-free.  after she examined me she said she would give me a call the next day around the late afternoon, saying she was working a night shift.  i'll be honest with you.  i didn't expect her to call the following day because when i was on premera, they never called when they said they were gonna call.  but dr. woo proved me wrong.  she called the following day, gave me further instruction and let me know what was to happen next.  she even had my lab results transferred over to the bellevue location, knowing that's where i live and prefer to go, so she hooked me up with a doctor there for further help.  if i lived in seattle i would choose dr. woo as my primary care doctor.

i have been treated at kaiser permanente's urgent care a handful of times now spanning a 2-year period. i am just genuinely amused at how professional and polite the people working there are. every individual i have come into contact with at kaiser permanente had been extremely kind, patient, caring and informative - which are really important when you are already feeling unwell. so, if anything ever happens to me, kp will always be my top choice, because i am rest assured knowing that i am in good hands. thank you

oddly enough, this place is growing on me and i'm pretty vested. only updating to 3 stars because my entire staff hates them still and begs me to move the plan. i have not because i am now happy with the service.

i'm not sure what some of the negative reviewers were expecting, but it certainly makes me want to tell you about my outstanding treatment here at their urgent care unit on november 30, 2019.  i came in at a little after 7 am after a terrible night of chills, fever, nausea and occasional sharp abdominal pain.  it was the pain that lead me to believe i had something other than the flu.  although my kaiser permanente plan is in california, i was taken right in with no excessive paperwork and placed in a private room where my treatment team of physician's assistant jamie and rn kat went immediately to work making me comfortable and beginning the diagnostic process.  i was quickly told that my symptoms sounded like a classic kidney stone.  after drawing blood, taking a urine sample and eventually a cat scan, it turned out to be a large (11mm) stone, just as jamie suspected.  because i was just visiting seattle and needed to get back to my california home where i could have the stone treated by kaiser there, they provided iv pain relief, nausea relief and ibuprofen along with written prescriptions to ease my pain during travel.  but most of all they made me feel like they really cared about me!  there were other nurses and assistants involved whose names i didn't get and everybody was just terrific.  sure, i came in at a time when they weren't especially busy, but i received 5 star treatment and i'm sure this team gives the same to all their patients.  thank you jamie, kat and the whole team.  and by the way, my flight home was uneventful and pain free later that afternoon.

going in you have to understand that you're on legal hold. they can't just see you and then let you go right away and not everyone gets that. you can't have your phone except to write down phone numbers. then you have to use their cordless phones. the food is decent but nothing special. most of the people who work there are nice and they care but there's always some grouchy person on night shift. honestly, for being a locked ward, it's pretty decent overall.

review: minimal care should be the mission statement for this facility. i am so disappointed at the care given to my mother in law. she went in with flu, pneumonia, and sepsis. after dumping 2500cc of iv fluid into her, they had to give her lasix to remove the extra fluid. no i and o (measure in and out of fluid) with this issue. no breathing treatment unless she asked. she was too sick to ask. no cough medicine given although she would cough to the point of gagging. nurses couldn't get out of the room fast enough ( and she is a nice, pleasant lady)! iv antibodies given only every 48 hours instead of the normal 24 hours for that specific drug (i understand this is a doctor's order issue). no excuses for this lack of care. i have been a nurse for over 20 years and did my training at this hospital. it is not what it used to be.

currently on my second visit here to the er for the same severe chrons flare up. i have been here since 11 am. i have not received any food or liquids for the nursing staff since my initial iv at 1:30 pm. i've paged numerous times and i get, "we will check on that." they never come back. i'm not sure why i am being ignored but the staff has not been attentive or compassionate at all. they also gave me tylenol for the pain which is absolutely absurd as i can find that at home and if that was the solution i would not be here.

i'm hoping the hospitalist sees this during my stay.

review: worst hospital ever ! my mom is currently in the odu and has been here over 48 hours. the nurses have barely come in to check on her, just been sedating her all night. they keep telling us "the soecialist will be in shortly". for the past 5 hours ! no update. the worst part is they keep promising ya stuff, like they're going to move her  into a better room, then no one comes back for hours, and when we ask, they say "we'll find out for you" and never come back again. and when we ask again two hours later , they look frustrated with us. just find us some answers ! worst  service ever.

review: had my gall bladder removed and the nurses and doctors took wonderful care of me. very professional and caring. i will definitely recommend this hospital to everyone. nurses were amazing and paid wonderful attention to me.

review: horrible emergency room. from the minute you walk in you are greeted with extremely rude and moody staff behind the glass. they give you attitude and roll their eyes at you. first time i sat in the waiting area with half my face paralyzed and droopy in extreme pain and waited 2 hours before being seen to have my vitals taken. in the second waiting area i waited 5 hours standing up because there was nowhere to sit. i never even got called back to be seen. i eventually left and had to be treated at a different emergency room where i was taken seriously. and jcl calls themselves a "primary stroke facility" what a joke. second visit was today high fever, cough, chest pain when breathing in and coughing, shortness of breath. the minute i walked in the lady at the front rolled her eyes. i asked her how long is the wait as i could see the whole waiting area was full. she said long obviously with an attitude, i didn't even bother i walked away and went to go get treated at a different hospital. this is disgusting this place needs to shut down. i wonder how many people die in their facility because of their lack of care. they need a new er system. they are extremely unprofessional and i will make sure justice is made to all of us who were in a true emergency and got taken as a joke.

review: stopped to see a friend of mine that had surgery.  the information desk said he was not in the hospital. stopped by the switchboard operator and they said he was not in the hospital. when i called the hospital the switchboard operator connected me to his room. someone needs to have a talk with their employees on how to do there jobs! i am glad it was not my parents that i was looking for!!!

should not even deserve a star. i was given joseph p monley as my er doctor yesterday. i came in with concerning abdominal symptoms. told me it could be kidney stones. i thought to myself, "i do not have the kind of symptoms for kidney stones. i would know if i did." 

he ran a bunch of tests. everything came back negative. white blood cell count was high though. they said it could be some sort of infection.

discharge time. he said it was definitely kidney stones. either i passed one or i was about to pass one.

what about all the symptoms i told him? he ran crazy tests (pelvic exam + ultrasound) for an absolute misdiagnosis.

i still do not know what is wrong with me. they said to follow up with the auburn medical clinic if i am still having symptoms so i will be visiting somewhere else tomorrow.

as a student of auburn university, i have already missed over a week of classes this semester. they would not even give me a doctor's note for friday when i was experiencing too much pain to move.

i will not be coming back here. go to an urgent care. these people are crazy!
it doesn't make no sense how long you have to wait in the emergency room 2hr in waiting room and you was the third person in the waiting area and another 45 minutes before the doctor comes

i am laying in this horrible nightmare of a hospital observation room. i came monday. what i thought was a boil come under my left armpit sunday march 2, 2020. i had never experienced this before. after i was initially there i didn't stay in the emergency waiting room but a couple of hours arriving at 10:15 am. they took me in a like "urgent care". they did do proper test and diagnosed me with cellulitis. that was the beginning of my nightmare here. following day they kept antibiotics, and iv solution. they treat you like your in a serious bad area of a 3rd. world country. this cellulitis has gotten so bad they came in this morning said they were fixing to come lance it. this was 9:45 am at 3:50 pm they finally came in and lanced it. i have been laying in a bed since monday tonight it's 9:50 pm on wednesday night. the night shift does care more about you. i ask to walk to the bathroom to use the bathroom no bathroom's in the room. i have not bathed since sunday.  i have told them i stink. the nurse on duty tonight i told her i have been asking for some clean ups to wipe myself i have been sweating, no way to wash. she did say "oh no", they haven't given you anything. i said i ask they say ok and never come back. tonight i was staring i said what can i do to get some food? she said "oh no", no one have given you a menu? i said no i brought a bottle of water and have filled it up with tap water.  i am breaking down i have not been in a hospital like this situation in 15 years and i could not complain. i am dirty, hot, beg to go to the restroom, beg for  something  for pain. i stay in pain more so than don't they give 5mg norco when i ask about every 4 hours i get about every 5.  i have cried am in pain have a hugh packing i prob my arm with a thin plastic pillow, blood, all kinds of solutions on my bed they have not given a clean sheet, pillow case for this thin plastic pillow. i am checking myself out of here in the morning. i have never in my entire life had this type of neglect in health care, neglect in helping me, this reminds me of them abusive nursing homes that totally neglect the patients. i am so dirty i stink. i am hot. i beg and i hear ok and it continues. only good i can say this night nurse and a couple ppl and this night physicians assistant have been much better than the day crew.  this has been very stressful very concerning for me. i would never put myself in this bad situation again.

review: are the people who work here/answer the phone always so fucking rude and difficult? it's quite shocking how terrible the staff can be at this facility. especially around the holidays, when we are trying to check up on our loved ones who are under your care and supervision. it's disgusting and disgraceful. i can hardly get ahold of my family member, because the nurses are always too busy to help me get in touch with them. "i don't have time to help you." really? i'm at a loss of words.

this hospital has been consistent in substandard service and care.  it is much faster and safer to drive to any of the bakersfield hospitals than sit in the waiting room at drmc.  they don't do certain scans on weekends they have no neonatal intensive care unit and the wait times are atrocious even when the er is empty.  i don't say this blindly or based off of one experience.  i say this from repeatedly going to this hospital throughout the years and repeatedly receiving the same care.  hopefully adventist health (who officially acquired the hospital recently) can turn the hospital around.

my loved one died while receiving care at this hospital. i wish i would be able to have a glowing review on the quality of care here, but it is quite the opposite. it is a very regretful environment for someone to be in, there is constant noise and patients are given no time to rest, but either are repeatedly getting woken up throughout the day or being blatantly ignored (there is no in between). they have chairs and basically that's about it if you decide to spend the night visiting your loved one. also, they cannot adequately provide care because they seem to be underfunded, and lack a lot of the resources their bakersfield counterparts have. i believe the worst part is seeing a loved one suffer and endure such hardship and be helpless. i believe they were neglected on multiple occasions and complications rose from the incompetency of the staff..   rather than get better their health deteriorated and eventually they passed (couldn't even make it to a month here, mind you they were transferred back due to the stability and improvement of their health). i hope and pray that if you are ever in pain you go to the hospital immediately. but please under whatever circumstance do not come here and don't let your loved one be hospitalized here! i hope you are able to learn from this terrible mistake and my words will serve you some use...
horrible. takes hours just to get in. if could get 0 stars i would. couldn't wait any longer. rather just suffer at home in comfort.

i dont even know where to begin to describe the lack of care and compassion that exists with this place. emergency room operator , jamie and the "hospital supervisor " were uncaring and providing false information to me about reproductive health care. i was advised to get a morning after pill after explaining that i was already pregnant! this place should be closed and not allowed to open until they educate and train their staff. extremely discouraging and hurtful experience.

no stars!!! horrible experience with outpatient surgery and on top of it they are trying to charge me $16,800 for a procedure they didn't even perform. this place needs to be shut down. if you value your health and finances keep driving!

my wife was in the hospital for four days waiting for procedure. they had her using a toilet by her bed which was fine when it she was in her own room. they decided to move her into a joint room were she did not feel safe. they didn't care when the concern came up, if a curtain couldn't protect her then there wasn't anything they could do. never come to this hospital if safety is a concern!!!!

dr. gergory douglas has almost completely stitched up my vagina during the perineal repair process. i had a third degree perineal tear after i delivered my baby at the birthing center. dr. douglas had given me unnecessary stitches where he went beyond the perineum and placed extra stitches that significantly closed my vaginal opening.
i experienced constant pain and pulling after the repair and felt that something wrong was done to my body. after one week of suffering i went to another doctor who examined me and confirmed that the repair did not look right. she recommended a second evaluation in four weeks when i stop bleeding and heal completely after birth. when i returned in four weeks she confirmed that i was stitched too tightly. she apologized for all medical professionals and looked sorry that this had happened to me.
i felt betrayed and completely devastated. the way dr. douglas did the repair left me with constant pain and made it physically impossible to have sex.  
about two months later i saw yet another doctor. this doctor eventually did a surgery where she cut the vaginal opening back again. i was told that there was 1.5 centimeters of stitched together tissue, which means 3 centimeters of total tissue length.
i am surprised to see positive reviews for dr. douglas. i assume that he can be different... somehow choosing who would be victims of his unprofessional conduct and his gross negligence.
i saw dr. douglas two times - right before i went into active labor and after birth when he came in to place stitches. during both visits he was unprofessional. he never explained any procedures he was going to do. when he did my vaginal exam he would just dip his gloved hand into gel and come up waiting for me to pull off the sheet and spread my legs. he would not let me know what he was going to do. instead he acted like i had to guess his intentions and looked irritated when i hesitated or questioned what was going on. when my husband questioned dr. douglas' recommendation to fast forward my labor, he said that my husband was micromanaging me, though my husband was simply trying to help and advocated for me.
my husband and i did not want to argue with him. all we wanted was to welcome our baby into this world with love and peace. it is outrageous to me that people like dr. douglas are allowed to practice and mistreat women in their most vulnerable state.
in the hospital i had a number of nurses taking care of me. sarah, cara, and dawn deserve a separate review because they all were angels.
i hope my review will raise the awareness and warn future mothers-to-be of dr. douglas' actions and conduct so that they may not suffer at the hands of his unprofessionalism.

i would honestly give zero stars if possible.  no compassion, unskilled staff, horrible facilities.  they believe in just drugging their patients into comas and let em just lay around.  got told they were transferring me to ucd cause they couldn't handle the procedure then just continuously drugged me to the point i couldn't even move.  hell hole, do not go here

methodist hospital is a product of living in california so i understand a lot but at the same time i feel that there is a strong lack of empathy in this place. my fiance had to visit 3 times in 24 hours because he could not breathe due to asthma. the two previous times they sent him home because his oxygen levels were "ok" (about 94). but the third time, after being told to go home and "stop having so much anxiety" 6 or so hours later i had to call an ambulance because he was unable to drive and was really struggling to try and push through. this third time, the shifts had changed and he was admitted for a few days. they gave him treatments, though often late, and he did recover so i do really appreciate that he is still around today because of that. there were some during his stay with medication which were worrisome but either way he is breathing now. 

a few weeks later, after a heavy dose of antibiotics i got my second kidney stone. i came to the er in terrible pain, and it was a long process but they did give me prescriptions to take home, and while i was their my pain wasn't strong enough for me personally to need medication. i went again about a week later for what i though was another kidney stone. this time while i was waiting in the waiting room for what felt like hours, i went through what i thought was the worst pain in my life, and then by the time i was seen the pain was mostly gone. i got a ct scan and the kidney stone was confirmed to be there, though too small to treat with anything but flomax. i declined pain meds because i had leftover from the first visit.  

one week after that, i feel the actual worst pain in my life and take one of the last pills left of my pain medication, which offered me little relief. i go to the er again. i give a urine sample that wasn't moved from the bin until 2 hours of me waiting there. i know the sample testing takes at least an hour. they sent me out in the waiting room for 3 more hours, and in those three i could do nothing but cry from the pain and wait. i called my fiance over who helped to get a nurses attention. when he asked if he could talk to the doctor she said "we don't make calls like that". he brought me my very last pain pill so i declined when she said she could ask about something for the pain.  when i was finally seen again, i was discharged, and was to be sent home with ibuprofen. i immediately responded saying this is not going to be enough for the pain. the pa came out and prescribed me a less stronger medication but told me she couldn't prescribe me the pain meds i had because she had to watch  what i was taking. i get there is a drug epidemic here in sacramento, but a kidney stone is extremely painful and when i had my first one in my much smaller home town, they immediately got me a room and medicated me with what i needed. experiences like the one i had at methodist er make me miss home badly. 

i don't want to name any names because i know it is hard to make a living here and i know that the attitudes of these doctors and nurses are swayed by the many drug addicts that come in to get a fix. 
i know it is too busy to get a room but i find it astounding that they moved me out into the waiting room with a kidney stone. i'm not coming back here for my next emergency visit, though i don't think there is a hospital in sacramento i can go to that will give me the care i need.
