i learned a big lesson and so i am sharing my experience so others aren't as naive as i was.  i was referred to the physical therapy group within presbyterian hospital dallas by my internist after having repeat back issues. i had to check in with hospital services, which should have been  a red flag since hospital charges are often much more than a private practice. i had a 1 hour evaluation where i was told i needed to work on my core muscles. i was encouraged to sign up for 1-2 sessions per week. i signed up for two per week, so i had one 1-hour evaluation and five 45 minute sessions.

i really liked the physical therapist. she was wonderful to work with. but if i had known the bill would be $3237 for these six sessions, i would have gone elsewhere. the bill was submitted to insurance, which was then  adjusted to their agreed upon price. i have to pay 100% out of pocket until i reach my deductible, so my 100% was $1578. that's $263 per session. i realize that the evaluation should cost more, but the five individual sessions included 5-10 minutes on an exercise bike -- something i could have done at home prior to arrival. this is such an insane amount for what was delivered in return and i'm no better than i was when i first walked into the place. i could have purchased at least a year's worth of exercise classes that focused on building my core instead.  

i sent an email to texas health voicing my frustration with not being told up front what my cost would be, but i haven't heard a word back, so i'm going to share my experience and hope others learn from my mistake. i'm guessing they don't care because i have to pay regardless and they're not going to do anything about it.  so... be forewarned... unless you have excellent health insurance coverage or medicare that will cover a certain number of visits, this is not the place to go for physical therapy. there are private practice physical therapists who charge much less so you can get more sessions for your money.

i am paying it down over 12 months, but it's the equivalent of having a car payment again and i really didn't need this expense right now. in addition to still having back issues i came here to address, i now have a huge amount of stress trying to figure out how i can come up with these monthly payments. lesson learned.

i'm giving 2 stars only because i liked my physical therapist.

if i could give a rating in the negatives i would.  i'm appalled at how poorly my daughter was treated after we raised concerns over the opening of her incision after having a c-section.  we pointed out that the incision was actively bleeding after she had been closed up.  while it continued to bleed the nurse kept saying that it was old blood but kept changing the dressing, i kept count of how many times the dressing was changed.  after several hours and changes the nurse came back with an adhesive tape that was 3 inches wide and 8 inches, i had to reminded them that she is severely allergic to adhesives.  when the nurse left she left my daughter's incision site open so we took the opportunity to look and we were able to see that her incision had in fact come open, when the nurse returned we requested they inform the attending physician.  at this time they told us that they would not be able to do so because they never have one available on the floor, in turn we suggested they inform her physician of the issue and they told us they couldn't disturb him after hours.  i suggested that i could take her to the er so a qualified surgeon could close the incision and we were told that the er would refuse to provide the necessary services and help my daughter.  we were left frustrated and worried for her medical safety.  the nurse left and came back with surgical tape to address the problem, when we questioned her surgical skill and qualifications, because you could see my daughter's thin layer of fat and muscle tissue.   
after we consulted with a friend of the family who is a plastic surgeon i continued to press the nurses to get a surgeon to sew her up because of the possibilities of infection, it still took another hour until a doctor came and closed the incision.  i'm concerned that if my daughter who is well educated and economically well to do individual had to endure such a horrible experience, what would a less fortunate patient have to suffer or die because they may not be aware of their rights.

as a any years as ive lived where i do, up and down the stairs,  yesterday i somehow fell down entire flight. i still don't know how but there was no stopping me. finding myself alive at the bottom i tried to think and get my bearings before trying to stand. 
anyway, i got up, gingerly climbed up and waited a very short while before realizing that i needed to get to a hospital. the closest is lawrence general. i was afraid to take an ambulance because in doing so i would be entering the hospital all alone. also no ride back home... so i called a nearby friend who came right away.

i must state that - yes, i've had better experiences at other hospitals. but this one at lawrence general was very good. i believe i got good care in regards to what was wrong with me. the hospital was clean and anyone i interacted with were very professional. now all i need to do is get better....

had horrible pain in my stomach and lower back that increased throughout the day. had not engaged in any physical activity and was concerned that could possibly have some form of an infection or possibly my appendix . went to the er at putnam hospital. waited for over 2 hours despite the increasing pain and barely an ability to walk. after 2+ hours was ultimately brought to a room where i was left laying on a gurney for over 1 hour (so 3 hours + from when i first arrived at facility). was never triaged by a nurse or doctor to determine whether something more significant was going on which may have required more immediate assistance, was given no medicine and no medical attention and/or care. was not even given a pillow to lay on to try to help make me more comfortable. my husband complained and inquired for help with my increasing pain numerous times and was basically told that it was too bad i was in pain and we just had to wait. he was told that his repeated requests weren't "going to make the doctor see me any faster." a nurse practitioner...lorie gauthier...entered my room and when i expressed my frustration about being left for so long and in tears with increasing pain, she walked in and out and told me too bad, she wasn't going to "deal with me" and "i could wait for a doctor to come and see me when he had the time." at that point i left and my husband drove me to another hospital 25 minutes away...northern westchester hospital...where i was greeted with a wheel chair and received immediate care and support. i was at nwh for 3 hours start to finish including tests and medications provided...and this was the length of time i was at putnam hospital just waiting to be seen in the er.

despite its proximity to my home and being the closet place to access care i will never step foot in that disgusting, backwards, deplorable hospital again. northern westchester hospital exemplified what proper medical care should be and god willing in the event of an emergency i will be able to make it the 25 minutes to be seen there for care.

stay away!  we spent 7 hours yesterday at this facility, 4 hours in the waiting room and 3 hours in the er room.  this place is more like a medical providers office.  the staff is cold and unsympathetic to the pain and discomforts of the patients that have come in to see them for help. during our time there was a stroke victim came in and was left in the waiting room for 3.5 hours before being seen, a young man with, what i suspect was a broken ankle (swollen and discoloring quickly) was put in a wheel chair that was placed by the sliding door that remained open throughout his 3 hours before being seen (it was 51 degree outside). the young man sat there shivering and covering his face with his hoodie in an effort to stay warm. he had shorts on and sat directly within eyesight of the registration desk. the room was very uncomfortable hard chairs, food crumbs and half drunk coffee cups with a tv that remained off. when it was your turn, you knew it as well as everyone else.  the medical providers would remain behind the reception desk yelling your name out and if you didn't appear within a few seconds, another yelling out of your name would be called out.  most of the times that patients in the waiting room would respond by stating, "she's coming" as we did for the stroke victim who's daughter moved her slowly in her wheelchair or we would call out the person's name as the room was a long narrow curve that some from the back cannot hear the yelling's from behind the desk.  when we got to the back, my husband who was experiencing severe abdominal pain was brought to a room with a chair, not a bed. due to this he remained in a uncomfortable state. the pa that attended to him was very nice, this is my only compliment to this place - we liked her a lot. she was genuine, caring and friendly.  the chatter of the rn's in this facility was horrible. they spoke of birthday parties out loud, almost yelling to one another. they spoke loudly behind the drapes to the patients of their diagnosis. there was no respect for patient privacy here. after my husbands cat scan was done we were told we needed to move to the waiting room.  i immediately stated, "are you kidding me? he's finally in a comfortable state laying down after 4 hours in your waiting room." she stated as my husband got out of the bed slowly and with much difficult, "we need the bed".  at no time did she even offer assistance while he struggled to get up. in addition we still didn't even have the results of the cat scan and when i asked how long that would be she said "it could be hours".   it made no sense to me. when we got my husbands diagnosis the lady said, "its just a piece of fat, you can go home".  i felt like stating and per the previous pa, its a piece of fat that has been advised needs surgery asap or it could become a blockage, but i hesitated to be as cold and rude as her.  there was so much that happen at this place yesterday, but these are the ones that i have the time to write down.  please take your loved ones somewhere else. i know their response will be to send an email to their patient care team as they have in all their other negative reviews.  my response for them now is, "how about making changes, instead of the same generic response you have given so many already."  i told my husband, while we were there waiting for the results, "if you need surgery it will not be here" and "if i ever need an ambulance or care, do not ever take me here."

today... was the cherry on top of this disaster of a cake! went to memorial central for an arthrogram of my wrist with an mri. i was told a doctor would be doing an injection of dye into my wrist before the mri...but no. a very shaky, nervous rpa shows up and fumbles around just long enough for me to tell her to stop the procedure. first she didn't use enough lidocaine to numb the area; second, she put the injection needle in...it fell over when she let go of it...so the needle moved! then before rechecking the needle placement with fluoroscopy...she decided to try to go ahead and inject the dye until i asked her "are you going to recheck the needle placement?"....so she did. it was completely in the wrong spot! so she decided to start pushing the needle in (without using the fluoroscopy viewing) and when she hit a nerve in my wrist and i jumped, she yanked the needle out! then she said i guess i will give you more lidocaine... i said nope we are done. the argument in the us against nationalized healthcare is that one will lose the quality of care in the us. it's no accident the argument has now been people in insurance will not have  jobs; places like this make the quality argument weak. nowhere is the emphasis on care  on display here. if you have a choice don't come here. it's dismal indeed.

my wife waited for three days to get transferred here. was told the surgery would happen monday. now it's going to be thursday. maybe. or maybe not. maybe they will just keep her there forever.

i was skeptical about coming here. i have a 5 month old. my child couldn't breathe because my child was coughing and turned blue. they did not even stick me in a triage room. it was awful. you put unvaccinated babies in an adult waiting room  with the general population? i hope osha or whatever nj has to regulate hospitals wakes up. someone will die due to the advanced negligence of this hospital. if i ever get shot in nj, drive me to kings county brooklyn. you have a better shot of surviving than to go here. 

once my child was in the pediatric er, the nurse was good. they send in a resident. it took forever to see the doctor. she was ehhh. no bedside manner. i felt like i was wasting her time being there. like mom shamed. my doctor was sick. she doesn't have a backup. she said take baby to er. so i complied. next time i'll drive to nyc. i understand there are tons of respiratory infections but they wouldn't even swab my under 6 month old baby for rsv. can't wait for the bill. i am absolutely calling the patient advocate team to complain. they claimed it was crowded. come to ny and you'll see crowded. healthcare in nj is subpar. hackensack meridan is so much better. no sense of urgency at this hospital. i'm glad the nurse came out and got me and brought us in. she was empathetic. no one else gave 2 shits. i should have called 911.

having had previous, unavoidable experiences with robert wood's emergency room, it was with a mixture of trepidation and dread that i found myself once more walking through the emergency room entrance. previously, my father had often been a patient there due to a long battle with cancer which necessitated several trips to this particular emergency room.  at that time i had never before experienced such a complete disregard for basic patient care in an emergency room setting.
so when my elderly mother was transported there after a very serious fall this past week i was shocked as to how little has changed. this was a monday afternoon however you would have thought it was new year's eve - the waiting room was a war zone. at least forty people were cramped inside - patients were sitting on the floor - vomit was on the floors, in the bathrooms and even in front of the entrance! several heavily armed policeman stood looking menacingly at every person checking in. my mother was already in the er so i was waiting in line to check in. not knowing what her status was i was understandably anxious to get back to see her. however, i had to wait in line with patients that were checking in. as hipaa does not appear to be something that this hospital is familiar with, i was privy to most of these patients entire medical history. this was unavoidable as the receptionist loudly repeated it back to the patient, in front of all of us standing there. i became even more outraged when it became evident that most of the patients there were using the emergency room for their primary care - issues included stomach aches, slight fevers, colds, headaches, etc. - which were non emergencies and could have been dealt with at a pcp appointment. 
upon finally getting my "clearance" to go back to the emergency room (i had to have my id scanned - was told that weapons and/or drugs are not allowed - i felt like saying that the brooks brothers topcoat i was wearing does not have inner pockets large enough to hold a glock and meth just to be snarky however with two police officers glaring at me i felt it more prudent to just hold my tongue and press on).
once back in the emergency room i was disappointed to see that although the interior had been updated their view on quality of care remained the same. when my father was there he and several other patients were lined up on guerneys in the hallway for hours - one visit my father was in the hallway for 7 hours!
i arrived to find the same scene - row after row of patients lined up on stretchers against the walls. i found my elderly mother next to the nurses station covered in blood from severe facial lacerations. and then the wait began ..... one hour no nurse/no doctor; two hours the same; three hours the same. i was given a wash basin so i could wash the blood off my mom's face and hands. 
as this hospital once again has no conception of hipaa i found out from the team of doctors and nurses hovering over the patient in front of us that he came in with what he thought was chest pains - however he said it could have been indigestion from the two double cheeseburgers he ate. the young woman behind use was going through chemotherapy and was severally ill - once again staff went through her medical history for all to hear. 
i am generally a very patient person. i cannot begin to understand the stress that the staff in these settings are put under. however after 4 hours without a nurse or doctor even having the courtesy to stop and just apologize for the delay my patience was at an end. i stopped the nearest nurse and demanded that my mother be seen.
well amazingly enough a neurology intern and two nurses appeared out of thin air. they said it was busy but they would follow up and try to get my mother out of the hallway and into one of the er bays.
after 2 more hours she was finally moved to a semi private bay.
my niece who is a nurse practitioner arrived and thankfully took charge. the remainder of my mom's stay went relatively smoothly due to my niece's non stop advocacy.
however my niece was appalled by the condition of the facility. the bathrooms were filled with feces and urine, she found hypodermic needles in the elevator, the puddles of vomit in front of the entrance to the er remained there all day. 
in closing, avoid this emergency room at all costs! my mother will now be going to princeton medical center - a new facility that is clean with top flight staff where patients are treated as human beings and not objects of inconvenience.
also as an aside, during our "stay" in the er we kept noticing police and detectives running up and down the hallways - evidently there had been a "drive by shooting" in which 3 people were shot. individuals associated with the event were attempting to gain access to the er which had security on hyper alert. not the type of environment that i would want to expose any of my family members to again.

i love this emergency room. so huge and so busy. everyone works so hard. i came in one busy day and a team of doctors seen me and diagnosed me. they said i only had 6 months to live. after 6 months i couldn't afford the bills anymore so they gave me another 6 months to pay. how nice. 

thank you kaiser er.

had to come here this last week with a family member who got hurt at work.  occupational medicine staff was extremely nice and helpful. they sent us to the er to help get member fixed (great service in er, but could've been a lot cleaner) and then off to another building for a prescription.  as the weather was nice, going back and forth to different buildings was doable, but would be a nightmare when the weather is bad. we got a bit tired in the end. plus, the maps to find your way are few and far between and hard to find, so its hit or miss to figure out where the heck you are. we ended up resorting to the 'map view' on our cell phone and that made trekking back and forth easier.

the worst thing i can say about here--and its well known--is parking. the lot is full to the brim and good luck finding a spot. kaiser could have the place covered in 10 story garages, and parking would still be hit or miss.  security roams constantly to make you move your car and i basically ended up dropping my family member at the building he needed, then circling the lot constantly until he called me to come pick him up. that's pretty much the only downfall here.

parking sucks!!! it literally took me 30 minutes to find a parking spot. i'm so glad i actually got there early enough to waste all of that time. we made it to our appointment with 3 minutes to spare. get there early. expect to spend a good amount of time trying to find a parking spot. we were there on a wednesday at 2:00. (just an fyi). other than that, the hospital was great, staff was great.

by far the most degrading emergency room visit i've had. they literally leave you lying in a chair on the side of a hallway. there's no care for patient dignity. when asked if i was waiting for a room to open up, they said "no. sorry. we've just been really busy. and we're just waiting for your test results"
the lack of diversity amongst the e.r. staff was discouraging.
when you remind them that you've been there for hours they tell you they've seen people there for days.
"atleast you have a recliner to sit on" -kaiser staff
they had such an amazing staff. unfortunately i had to stay at the hospital for five days , but each and every nurse/doctor that helped me was very informative and helped me with all my needs .

juliet is the amazing nurse that was taking care of my husband in icu a26 west. rm 19. she kept us entertained. super nice and took a realllly good care. if you or family member ever get admitted there in icu ask for her. also mike who helped him walk, he truly cares for his patients. just great staff and shout out to amy she was awesome. these are rockstars of kaiser.

the doctor blake montana legit sucks. it's like he doesn't even know what he's talking about. he just comes up with some random solution about what he thinks might be the problem. just sucks to wait here for hours on end and for a doctor to talk to you for two seconds and not know for sure if it's one thing or the other and to follow up with your primary care doctor. like come on people if you don't like your job then quit. he doesn't know anything about customer privacy, he's screaming at my sister about what she thinks might be wrong with her and he says how "he and his coworkers all had a laugh" about her symptoms. what the hell is that? horrible er. wow, i'm amazed.

my wife just delivered at the roseville eureka location.  holy smokes it was a crazy experience. this was our first child.  we are and we're complete rookies.  

my wife was in labor for four days.  the doctor broke her water to help hurry the process along.  after 20 hours they brought her in for a c-section.  i was freaked out.  being a rookie in this area i also didn't realize how serious this procedure is/was. anyways, my wife had some minor complications and our baby landed in nicu.  needless to say i was a hot mess.  i've never felt more helpless in my life.  

if your in the same situation i recommend this location.  the nurses are literally solders.  they each have there own stories, and in almost all cases have been through something similar or more substantial.  i learned so much from all these amazing people.  i really appreciate them.

the ladies in nicu were also the best.  i feel like i owe them more than a co-pay.  they were upfront about our situation, but also reassuring.  i learned how to clean diapers, feed, hold the baby properly, and burp from tera and janelle.  i love them both.  words cannot illustrate how grateful i am to both of you.  

i'n the end everyone made it out healthy:)

they take good care of me! they are good about preventative medicine, promote diet, exercise and healthy lifestyle. my doctor is good listener and very knowledgeable. good parking and convenient location.

very disappointed with the services here. my husband was seen here friday and sunday for severe stomach pains. both visits the doctor did not provide any testing on his stomach. next time, we will go to sutter roseville.

beware of christopher romberg!!!!! wow i have never been so disgusted by the lack of "bed side manner" or attitude from a doctor. i'm severely concerned for anyone who has to been seen by him. he walked into the appointment for my mother and immediately stated - "i have 20 minutes so let's do this" in the rudest way possible. from that point on the appointment was extremely uncomfortable. he seemed as though he didn't want anything to do with the appointment he was very rude asking the questions and acted as though the answers to the questions were not adequate enough for him. he then gave a bs response to the pain in my mother's stomach advising that he will just give her numbing shots instead of getting down to the root of the problem. it feels as though he didn't care about fixing the actual problem just scratching the surface enough to say he did his job.... not. i then said to him that i understand he may be over worked from a large caseload or something along those lines but this is 10 years of pain hes trying to brush off like it was nothing. he then became extremely hostile and stood up towering over my mother and i with his voice raised and said that i was attacking him and that he's done with this appointment and he'll just assign us another doctor. i am blown away. we paid a $55 copay for 15 minutes of a half ass dr being rude and making us feel extremely uncomfortable. i am disgusted.
the doctors have been great here. the parking is not great but you'll usally find a spot but further out. overall the staff have been great and i'm happy with the service here.

i live in rocky river, ohio in the single family homes near westgate shopping center. there is a metro health express care in one of the office buildings with a sign that says "walk ins welcome." the sign gives a phone number. i often walk to westgate and saw the sign. i called and made an appointment. i paid a $10.00 insurance co-pay. a couple of weeks latter i received a $150.00 bill for "out patient hospital services." i called my insurance company and they told me to talk to metro health, good luck trying to get a hold of someone. i've used this same insurance at other urgent care centers and have only paid $10.00. i called the number on the bill and spoke to "ronnie." i nicely asked to speak to a supervisor. i was then sent to the voice mail for a supervisor named "tonya." my phone call was never returned. my credit score is above 800 so i decided to pay the bill even though i don't agree with it.

review:
last night my mother passed away. the nurses became more professional after speaking to the house supervisor. that's what it took. i wonder what it would have been like if we hadn't. but why did it take that?

 also, we were robbed of our last opportunity to speak with her because they sent us home citing visiting hours on her final lucid day without a breathing tube. we begged her to stay and she enjoyed turning us away with a great big smile on her face. i'm sure they knew how little time she had left and likely knew she would be intubated soon. 

i believe they had that tube in there wrong, as her tongue looked necrotic, and yet they called it a "blood blister" and tried to moisturize it away. i call it a horrific nightmare from hell. thankfully by that point she was no longer truly present to experience that. 

as we removed life support measures, we had hoped once that infernal breathing tube was out that she might speak, but it was too late. that nurse is evil incarnate. don't allow your critically ill loved ones and family members to suffer this way. 

if i had an open fracture on my leg and they were the last hospital on earth i'd fix that leg myself without painkiller rather than go there. what a nightmare. way to go for adding unnecessary insult to injury and traumatizing people. my mother was a sweet, loving, gentle person, who had suffered trauma after trauma her whole life. i'm outraged and appalled at this place and will never forget or forgive the misery and pain they caused us.

the saddest part is that we will never see the report the house supervisor will file. and the 3 bully nurses are still working there.

i had a scheduled appointment for a ct scan i arrived approximately 10 minutes early after registration we sat and waited over 30 minutes to be called back. we were the only people in the waiting room. we were not given any explanation to the delay. i do not recommend this for outpatient procedures. go to north oaks you get much faster service. the staff gave me the impression that they didn't really want to be there the customer service was very poor

this place is just wrong. if we could leave we would. i'm amazed they are in business. two teen girls sitting in the break room waiting to be processed. murder shows on the tv... i ask for the remote to change it. they can't find it.

worst administrative staff/practices i have ever witnessed, and not just in the health care industry. the dublin location is even worse than the east location! 

there was only one individual on staff there that didn't make me feel like i was interrupting them or bothering them. the staff didn't have answers to any of my questions, so all they said was to call the phone number. but no one answers the phone or returns messages. i was going here for medication management for about a year and i think i actually had someone answer my phone call one time. and they said they were transferring me to someone who could answer my questions, but i ended up being transferred to a desk in the east location. when i called back, the woman who had transferred me the first time told me she didn't know what i was talking about but that was the right number. then she interrupted me mid-sentence and said she couldn't help me and transferred me to the same line again.

and god forbid life happens and you need to cancel or reschedule a medication management appointment! i had to taper down my meds on my own because no one would call me back about rescheduling or answer when i called again and again. after 3 weeks, i finally had to drive all the way out there and talk to someone in person. i explained the situation and told them that someone needed to see me, today. and the woman at the front desk told me no one needs to do anything. completely unprofessional and rude. she had no empathy and took no responsibility for their bad business practices or horrible treatment of their patients. 

oh and if you do end up going there, you'll probably get a bunch of random bills in the mail for money you don't owe them.

i have been telling every person i know in the central ohio area not to go to this place. i don't want them to go through the crap i was put through when i had to deal with this business.

one thing that i really cannot stand, especially those who work in the healthcare field, are individuals who exhibit characteristics of pure laziness.

when a dear family member had to be admitted to the hospital and had to stay for a few days, the whole experience was just so frustrating and disgusting.  the doctors, their interns/residents, the pas, and the physical therapists were incompetent, uninformative, and unclear.  appointment times were never kept - times were changed constantly, and i know that there can be last-minute emergencies, but there was a lack of communication and absolutely no regards to the patient's time.

the nurses were always always always on their cell phones and preferred surfing on the internet at the nurse's station, without making the timely or occasional rounds and never answering calls for assistance (pain management, refill on water, etc.).  it was to the point where i had to ask where the cup, ice, and water were so that we could do it ourselves.

i just wish that those who live in the proximity of this hospital are able to relocate to an area that feeds into a more trustworthy and a reputable one or have the opportunity to divert being admitted to a different hospital if arriving by an emergency transportation.  i know it's not realistic, but my heart really goes out to anyone who has to experience lutheran. 

i cannot believe this healthcare system has the audacity to have the word 'advocate' in their name.  i can only imagine what happens to the patients who may not be fortunate in having a family member be readily available, who are willing to be supportive throughout an ordeal, and/or have someone who can be an advocate on their behalf for their best interests.  

not surprisingly, we were all ecstatic to have our family member discharged to finally go home.

please avoid this hospital at all costs if you're able to!

review: i have no idea what other people experienced that made them give this place a bad rating. probably entitled and impatient. i've been here for 5 days now. i've  experienced nothing but great service. all the nurses and doctors have been great. my room is cleaned every day, they supply me with extra food if i just ask, bring me in as many pillows and blankets i want. it is cold here, but at night it helps me to sleep deeper. the meals are better than any other hospital i've been to. i just had baked chicken breast, mashed potatoes, zucchini, squash, a roll, seasoning package, water and juice, and banana pudding. every meal is nice and healthy. you can also substitute if you don't eat one meat they'll bring you another. you don't eat pork? cool! would you like fish, or chicken, maybe a burger or quesadillas?! the nurses check on you every hour, will answer any question you have if they know. the food delivery people tell you whats for breakfast, lunch, and dinner and if that sounds good. every time has been absolutely...the place is clean... the only thing i would say could be upgraded was the er room while waiting because it's small. but my hospital stay has been nothing below amazing. oh by the way it's a 24 hour visitation hospital. the surgeon was awesome, my doctor was informant, and listened to my concerns and answered my questions, the emts that transport are nice and cool. they also supply a whiteboard that has a direct number to your nurse on that shift and the number to your doctor... really?!!! i've never seen or heard of that before! awesome! if you have anything to say negative about the hospital or the staff it's probably because you just have an ugly and negative personality or they are stressed and having a rough day and aren't being perfect people like 'you want' so your little feelings got hurt, like a child's. regardless, i recommend this hospital. any questions please feel free to ask.

review:
i am currently staying at the east tower fountain valley. i want to start off by thanking the nursing staff, and east tower staff, as they have been great. 

as far as my experience with my current situation, it has been less than ideal. 

i was transferred here last wednesday @ 6am from hoag. i didn't start my care until 30 hours later, thursday. i brought with me multiple mri copies from the previous 24 hours at hoag/ private mri facility. not only were these discs lost, (2 separate times), but i was told they were uploaded to my patient portal. unfortunately this wasn't true because my doctor told me they were never uploaded. the discs were eventually recovered. this caused the 30 hour delay, as confirmation of mri results were needed to help expedite my care.

this minor frustration was easily overlooked, until i received a biopsy on my l4 spine, on thursday afternoon, the following day. the next 4 days have included doctors telling me the results aren't ready, or the doctors not coming by at all. until today, monday, my doctor finally informed me the hospital lost my biopsy cultures. 

my doctor was very upset as well because the last 4 days i was told we are waiting for the biopsy results to start my specific antibiotic care plan. well now they lost the biopsy cultures and since the biopsy was on my spine my doctor doesn't feel comfortable ordering another. instead, he says we will just treat the problem with pathology results.

so my bone cultures are lost. i've been recovering in the east tower. my mri discs were lost. (since recovered) and i still don't have an update from my case manager, regarding my outpatient care plan. 

again, the nursing staff have been extremely kind. (5 star for the nurses in east tower)

but, i am beyond disappointed with this current experience. a week in the hospital, with minimal progress. 

i will update accordingly.


- since i posted my review i was contacted by hospital administration and nurse lead. both were extremely kind and understanding of my situation. they are doing their best to resolve this situation so it doesn't happen in the future. again, i appreciate the nurses and staff during this stay. also, dr goldstein, did an excellent job of communicating directly. thank you fountain valley for helping remedy this situation, as all we can do is move forward!

review:
i had 2 procedures done via the cath lab within two months.  the first was outpatient and the second inpatient.  
the intake at fvh was fast and efficient. 
the nurses and my primary cardiologist, dr. donohue, were wonderful during the first procedure.  two of the nurses hugged me goodbye when i left.
fast forward two months and i'm back in the cath lab and the same nurses gave me a warm welcome, hugged me hello and remembered my name.  :-)  they were professional and made me feel at ease.
this procedure was held in an awesome o.r. with huge screens and beautiful equipment.  all of the staff preparing me were kind and reassured me that i was in good hands and not to worry.  dr. warrier performed my procedure and then i was taken to "the tower", a 3 story building behind the actual hospital, for recovery.  
my roommate was an elderly woman (who must've been deaf) as she had the tv at the loudest volume up to midnight.  i should have complained, but i didn't.
i had to lay flat for 6 hours beginning at 4:00pm. my lower back was on fire within two hours because of no support.  i finally requested some pain meds @ 8:30pm, the nurse called the doctor and was given the okay.  
the two nurses who took care of me in the tower were fine.  

one thing, though.  i asked the second nurse for directions for my neighbor who was picking me up.  she didn't know the address, the street or how to tell him to get to us.  i found that a bit odd.

all in all, it was good for what it was.

(he was seen by a geneva practitioner and released, stating it was just a gastrointestinal bug) they went to geneva, the boy died under their care. he had peritonitis.

so this marks the first time i've "updated" a yelp review. while scca would in theory top the list of places i'd most want to upgrade to a higher rating, its scheduling department's ongoing incompetence once again caused enough stress and inconvenience today to warrant this downgrade to just one star.

quite frankly, i'd give the scheduling department (at least the one i'm stuck dealing with) zero stars if given the option. in my 10+ years as a patient, i've communicated with almost as many schedulers -- and perhaps one or two of them have been good at their jobs.

the one working when i first started treatment was so bad that after i once vented about her on a support board, a local person pm'd me to ask if i was talking about s***; she knew exactly who i was referring to (even though i didn't name names), and said the lady was notorious for her poor communication skills.

well, at this point, i actually miss that ten-years-ago scheduler. at least she never flat-out lied to me -- unlike the one two years ago who said it was ok when i questioned why my routine ct scan wasn't scheduled (see previous review), only for me to find out several weeks later, on the day i received the results for my bone scan, that yes, i did also need the ct scan (which i then had to have at the last minute, and wait an extra day to get results for -- as if regular "scanxiety" isn't bad enough without being made worse by lazy schedulers who can't be bothered to follow up on valid patient concerns).

after that 2018 incident, you'd best believe that i let scca know how i felt about it. i was then given some empty promise by patient relations that it "wouldn't happen again", they'd "communicate better", blah blah. because i'm a forgiving person, i thanked them and decided to let it go. 

i still have to initiate setting up all my appointments, despite always being told that the schedulers will "contact me" (and i'm actually ok with scheduling things myself; i do so on a regular basis with my gp's office, which has a specific portal for this, but apparently scca isn't yet that advanced. but why bother claiming that the schedulers will "contact me"?). still, things were more or less fine, until december of 2019.

that's when i contacted my onc's current scheduler to set up my every-three-months lupron injection, which i knew was due in january. she responded within a reasonable time frame, and told me that the shot was scheduled for 1/4.

right away, i noticed that this seemed too early; it's been made very clear to me over the years that these shots should be given every 12 weeks (though there is about a week's worth of flexibility; it doesn't have to be 100% exact).

but my most recent injection occurred on october 21st; and it shouldn't take a rocket scientist to see that 10/21 to 1/4 = not 12 weeks. it should take about 30 seconds to actually make the effort to count (or check a calendar, for crying out loud) and see that officially it's only 10 weeks and 5 days.

i emailed the scheduler with my concern. i pointed out that it seemed too early. i gave her the specific date of 10/21 as my last injection, so she had that information handy.

two days later, she replied; she mentioned the week's flexibility and said (and i quote; see attached) "it is okay for you to receive on 1/4". 

i knew it still wasn't quite even 11 weeks; and i certainly hadn't forgotten the incident two years ago. however, i decided to give this person -- who, after all, is paid to be thorough and accurate, and not make mistakes -- the benefit of the doubt and not question her further. i mean, i shouldn't need to be in a position where i'm asking "are you suuuure?" each time a member of my so-called "care team" relays a message to me. especially not after i'd handed this person her own error on a silver platter by pointing out the early date, and given her ample time and opportunity to follow up on and fix the error if needed.

fast-forward to today, january 4th. 

i don't blame scca for running behind, and for waiting until 20 minutes after my scheduled appointment to send me back to a room. i do, however, question why they waited until after i'd been sent back and had my vitals taken, to inform me that they couldn't actually give me the injection today... 

because it was too early. 

livid doesn't begin to cover how i felt after hearing this.

while lazy and irresponsible of them, i'll forgive scca for not bothering to call, or at least tell me when i checked in, that i wouldn't get the shot today; at least the infusion nurse who gave me the news seemed genuinely regretful, and made a visible (and appreciated) effort to help.

there is no excuse, though, to be flat-out lied to and misinformed again by a scheduler who can't be bothered to do her job. 

it's infuriating. it's ridiculous. and scca's patients deserve better.

i'll close with a line from my first review -- in short: i'd suggest looking elsewhere for treatment.

as you can tell if you look at how often i write reviews, i am extremely selective in my assessments. to cause me to write a review means you either hit a home run, or you struck out. unfortunately it's the latter with the emergency room of this hospital. we live within walking distance, and have lived in the community for 20 years +. in that time, we've used the hospital or the er just once or twice.  in other words, we're healthy, use regular doctors to meet our basic health needs, and are not the type of people who run to the er for a paper cut. additionally, we have truly excellent insurance supplied by our employers. 

with that as background, we visited the er at 1 am this week. my husband had been flat on his back with the flu/cold since returning from texas about 10 days ago. he was running a fever, coughing frequently, hadn't been able to eat, and was having trouble breathing. when we checked in we explained his symptoms and told them several times he'd been in international airports since coronavirus was starting to be talked about. when the er doctor sat down, he asked my husband "what's going on?" my husband very reasonably responded to that question by saying "i think i have the flu." the doctor shot back "i'll make the diagnosis." that sums up our experience in the er. they were generally detached, rude, and acted like we were bothering them by being there. the one exception was the truly friendly guy with the portable machine he rolled around to get a bit more info from patients such as religious preference. but the nurses and the doctor were awful. they didn't follow up with us about my husband being in houston airport (where the coronavirus was found), and when he complained about being lightheaded they initially ignored him and then reluctantly offered a wheelchair. they also debated between themselves as to whether they should offer an inhaler. once concluded, one trotted off to find the doctor. the other disappeared without telling us anything. a third employee sat staring at his phone, tapping away, and never said a word to us or looked our way even though we were perhaps 3 feet from him. i was standing the entire time and none offered me a chair.

as a community member, i don't feel los robles provided even minimally acceptable service. i looked on their website for a place to lodge complaints but there isn't one. interesting. additionally, there are more "1" ratings of this hospital on this site than "5" ratings. i'm not surprised by that.  i'm sure there will be an insipid follow up comment from jasmin o. saying "thank you for your comment, sorry we didn't meet your expectations" or something noncommittal like that. the fact that the hospital offers the same canned response to every poor review indicates to me that there is a lack of true caring.

everyone has bad days at work, i get that. but in certain industries, that can be dangerous. you don't want ticked off air traffic controllers, lackadaisical nuclear energy plant operators, or medical staff who lack compassion and don't really want to help patients. i expected more out of the er. we won't return; we'll go to an urgent care spot if needed in the future. which is too bad since los robles loses a future chance to over bill our very generous insurance company.

bottom line, i don't recommend anyone willingly going to this hospital's er based on our experience this week.

so i minused one star..the recovery room i was put in was awe fully small. they had completed renovations and i got a tour of a spacious room and a smaller room but overall i'm thinking okay i won't mind. merp, pump the brakes right there! so i ended up getting the smaller room. is it because i am 5'2.5 lol not quite at 5'3 so i didn't get the room next door that i could see was clearly available during my entire stay!?? yes i know i'm supposed to be sleeping when my child sleeps, but i can't help but look outside.. i cannot tell you how many times we bumped babies rolling bed into my bed when going in and out of the room for vital checks and what not. it was like everyone in the room freeze, you're taking my air, everyone suck it in, i need space! 

i don't want to get into the nitty gritty with my c-section experience but let me give you the vague explanation. second time mom here, first experience at kapiolani. i only needed to be shot once for the spinal, (this doctor didn't miss 4 times, like queens hospital!), i was awake and there was a huge group of students watching (not my choice, seriously like 10 of them and one main intern assigned to me), recovery went well and i was walking like a champ!! the overall process and procedure went even smoother and painless than i had anticipated 
, tyj! keeping in mind, every birth experience is different. i'm just very grateful that the team working on my delivery was top notch! don't retire just yet, i'm probably not done lol 

i love love loved my celebration dinner! that was a unique experience. my doctor offered me the decision to leave earlier but i scheduled my dinner on the last day so hubby and i could enjoy it together, i wasn't going to miss it! it was amazing! they take baby for an hour or two in the nursery, killed me so i never let him go, your choice. we had sparkling cider, prime rib, and everything else on the menu that i chose!

i could preorder all of my meals and pick specifically what i wanted for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. with a full medical team on standby and meals cooked, i was pampered lol. what was the rush? jk! 

kudos to lauren, who prepped me for my c-section. she was the sweetest and so very thoughtful! i had a bracelet i could not take off. other doctors were going to do it but she took initiative and took care of it. she went into my or and prepped the tools and came back in time. a true gem and hard worker! and my doctor dr.dillon who performed my procedure of course! also to the sweet ladies in my recovery room. i had completed a survey upon leaving the hospital, been called for another survey, and replied to countless email surveys. one is enough, thank you very much. so here is my last hoorah and review until my next experience.

my son has special needs, and we've been coming to the audiology department for 10+ years for hearing tests, hearing aide molds, hearing aides, in addition to numerous special surgeries.  everything from the checkin process before surgery early in the morning is helpful, organized and welcoming.  nurses in pre- and post-op are attentive, kind and knowledgeable.  this is home to pediatric specialists that are well-versed in their fields.  the parking is much improved with the new parking garage.

gave birth to all my kids here after a bad experience at tripler with my oldest i made sure i wasnt going to go back there. my younger children were born here, and i love the spirit of aloha that flows in this place. thank you kapiolani!

a good hospital overall, but be careful!  

my wife gave birth here in 2012.  when we arrived at around 1am, my wife was experiencing significant labor pains.  the triage staff didn't believe that she was in labor and refused to admit her.  they asked if she wanted a shot of morphine and we told them we thought she needed to be admitted but if it would help.  they basically said that it wouldn't help if she was in labor.  i said that we weren't doctors and asked for their medical advice.  they suggested that they try the shot to see if it worked and kept pushing the decision back to us.  we had no idea what to do, my wife was screaming, and we wanted the medical professionals to make a recommendation and stand by it.  it felt like nobody was willing to take accountability for the recommendation, but they also weren't willing to admit her.  ultimately, we let them give her the shot.

in giving it to her, they must have hit a nerve or caused some other permanent damage because that spot is sensive to this day and causes my wife significant pain whenever it is touched.

the frustrating part is that they were wrong, the morphine did nothing for her labor pains because she was indeed in active labor.  by the time they finally admitted her at 7:30a she was very dialated, they had to immediately give her the epidural, and our daughter was born only 4.5 hours later.

the delivery experience was great (largely do to the ob we had been working with as well as the nurse assigned) and we ultimately came back to deliver our son 4 years later.  i have also been impressed with the er docs there.  

that said, the pain my wife experiences due to the labor triage staff's negligence seems as though it will be permanent.  for that reason alone, because they needlessly and permanently insured her, i can only give this hospital one star.

hawaii's statute of limitations has likely run on this.  we had no idea that the damage would be permanent and little understanding at the time of how to handle it.  at this point, i feel that my only recourse is to recommend that others use caution and speak to an attorney immediately if you or one of your loved ones is injured by this hospital.

went to see my nephew after being flown from maui in the nicu. the new diamondhead tower is beautiful & the security to get into the nicu is 10*stars ...the nurses were very sweet & helpful in educating my cousin on the different type of nipples to use for preemie baby & various car seats available & do & don't a with a preemie.

truly, almost everyone provided the sharp experience and you could tell the employees who really enjoyed their job versus the employees that view their job as just a paycheck. perception is everything. i actually took down names of those i found were the epitome of the "sharp experience" and those who need a little sprinkle of the "sharp experience" back into their lives.

i will start with the good. check in process was good. the er staff were quick with triaging and with getting labs/xrays/ekgs done before you even go to the room to be seen by the dr. we waited a long time , more than a couple of hours to be seen-but it was ok because we had heard the code being called overhead so i knew someone needed all the help they could get. cambria was my moms er nurse. she was awesome and always kept my mom and i up to date. she was personable and i really appreciated it. another shout out needs to go out to luv who is another er rn that was helping with my mom's iv. i thank you for your hospitality. 

there are 2 individuals that rubbed me the wrong way in how they approached my mother-they are the ones to why this review is 4 stars versus 5. i really wanted to mark this review as 2 stars but i didn't want to downplay the services of the employees that were really awesome.  one was a healthcare partner by the name of april and the other is kandra or kendra from the pharmacy. everyone but these 2 employees were friendly, others came and introduced themselves to my mother and i. april came in, no introduction. she just stated matter of factly that she was there to do an ekg. no smile, nothing. not sure if she worked a long day, however, that's not an excuse to be the way she was. kandra or kendra (her badge was flipped and could not see her name)from pharmacy...she was just plain rude and condescending. she came to ask my mother what meds she was on...mind you my mom had a list and by the time kandra showed up-my mom had shown 3 other people including dr.shipley the list of the 4 meds she is on. kandra came off as being annoyed or irritated that my mom didn't know her meds by heart. my mom told kandra that she had given the list to dr. shipley and kandra retorted "the problem is the dr.'s don't always document it. so you don't know the names? the doses?" and just kept asking the same questions using the same tone while staring up at the ceiling. hmmm...ok. how is this our monkey? that's not our problem that they don't always document it. what a way to throw another staff member under the bus. she was short when talking to my mom and honestly my mom and i were happy to see this employee leave the room. for my mom to sit there and say "what's wrong with her?" speaks volumes. some people need empathy training and she is one of them. they need to put themselves in the patients' shoes. guaranteed if kandra/kendra had brought her mother into this er and was approached by a employee who acted just like her-she would be upset too. she acted like she hated her job. that was my perception. so cold in her responses, no smile, just not sympathetic and makes me question why she is in healthcare to begin with. she was rude and cold, plain and simple. maybe it was a long day? maybe she had seen a million patients that day? should that matter? no, it shouldn't.

back to the good. my mom was admitted onto 6 south. theresa (her pm rn), luz (pm aide) and joe p.(am rn)-i have nothing but the greatest things to say about these employees. hardworking, personable, helpful, always smiling, always keeping us updated, you guys have no idea how much i appreciated you and i know my mom appreciated you all just as much. i could tell all 3 of these employees love their job and love helping their patients. please make sure these 3 individuals get the recognition that they so deserve. sharp is lucky to have them on their team and we were really fortunate to have them taking care of my mom. 

also jay r. and christine f. in interventional radiology deserve recognition. they were phenomenal in their explanations. i loved how christine was practicing her mandarin with my mom. it's personal touches like this that makes me love sharp. 

she stayed one night. i finally convinced her to switch to sharp and tomorrow i'll be calling to find her a primary care physician with sharp rees stealy.

i hate this place with a passion!!! 
even with insurance, they continue to bill me for little stuff without even double checking if what they're doing is covered by my insurance. 

i went in to the er for chest pain and even with insurance, i've paid over $1000 already on little b.s. things they didn't even need to do. left the er with no meds or anything... just a "take it easy"

how can you truly rate a hospital? based off of skill of drs/surgeons/np/nurses/cnas? of quality of care? quality of food(which we all know who have been in a hospital for any extended time can be atrocious)? how about all of the above!

i was admitted on 11/7 for a major surgery. not simple by any means and i am glad and blessed that this was the hospital i went to. aortic valve replacement which entails open heart surgery is scary enough to hear, but the team here at sharp memorial along with my surgeon dr. adamson put my fears to rest. from the initial consultation with him and going over what was to occur i felt at ease along with my girlfriend. even making jokes with me to relax me and calm my nerves just showed the bedside manner was well above par.

the complex is large and if you have multiple appointments in different buildings as i did. just ask the nurse assisting you to request a shuttle and they will get you to were you need to go. instead of moving your car over and over and dealing with the parking.

depending on what you're in for will dictate what floor/building you will be placed in. post op recovery icu is 2nd floor of main building and god bless if that's what you're in for.

nursing staff along with the np(nurse practitioner, don't call them a dr even if they're right there) have some of the most gentle care i've experienced from any hospital. i've bee. to other sharps and i can wholeheartedly say this hospital takes the prize. from providing you with as much information as possible to assist you in your recovery to ensuring you help is merely a call away by providing you with their direct number(they're given a cell phone at work so they can be reached by you or the nurses station if needed urgently) these ladies and gentleman embody care. my hats off to floor 6 (cardiac recover) for all the outstanding service and care they provided me. i honestly don't think i would have been recovering as well as i am without their support and care.

food is still none the less hospital food but i was able to speak with the chef in charge and here their plans for the coming year. adopting a comprehensive plan to ensure that the food quality and nutritional value are in keeping with the care provided at the hospital. a one of a kind program that already has made staples in improving the quality of the food and nutritional value(small steps so far such as switching from iceberg lettuce to green leaf lettuce and such). my hats off to them for improving this overlooked aspect in hospitals. the ordering system is fantastic how they take your meal order ahead of time to not interfere with your recovery and to ensure that you designated meal with restrictions if any get to you on time. i lived how each .real came with a nutritional overview letting you k ow nutrients, calories, etc in your meal. loved that!

radiology/radiologist as i had to deal with frequently were friendly and helpful. whether they had to assist me in my room or take me down to get mris(be aware, its always the coldest part of the building because they do have to keep those machines cool or they can burnout so ask for bra blanket if you need it). the transport team who assisted you getting from location to location or helping you leave in the end were always kind, helpful and made sure you knew you were always welcomed back.... hopefully not soon though.

all in all if i could rate this hospital a 11 or higher i would! excellent is the only word i can come up with to describe the care provided by the staff at sharp memorial. my hats off to all the staff that help in the recovery of the many patients who walk through their doors and the supporting staff behind the scenes.

cannot say enough nice things about this hospital!! youngest daughter ended up visiting the er when she became very ill. for the severs hours before i was able yo get to her she said everyone was very nice, caring and warm. when i gig to the er i saw it firsthand from the nurses to the doctor to the technicians. she was admitted to outpatient observation and received excellent card and attention. even during shift changes it was not chaotic as had been my experience at other hospitals. also like the concept of this unit. you're not technically admitted to the hospital so the rates are s big lower. when dud was discharged the process was smooth and efficient...no waiting an hour for a transport to the pick up area! also like they treat family members gently and provide in and out privileges in the parking as well as discounts in the cafeteria.

professional, kind, understanding. the best experience in an er ever! was in and out in just over an hour, including xrays. everyone spoke english and were easy to understand!

i would like to highly recommend sharp hospital to everyone. two nurses especially made our hospital stay amazingly comforting and healthy. tim and jasmine are rns on the seventh floor and they deserve a gold medal. not only are their clinical skills top notch, they both had the most compassionate heard and conversations that i have ever seen. our whole experience was salubrious.

nurses, doctors were extremely professional and helpful. i'm someone that suffers from a few chronic ailments and they've always been there to help me. only issue i had is with two of the entry level staff members in the er department that were not well trained and most likely new. due to myself having focal seizures and other issues in the past i've been required to have a medical alert dog with me at all times. the rules are that you are not to separate this dog from the handler (myself) and this dog is also protected by federal law for access. in addition, this dog can hold its bladder/etc for over 15 hours if necessary. so a clerk telling me "we can't take your dog out for you" is a bit disrespectful and ignorant. so everything else rates a+ i'd start with educating your plebotomists and medical assistants for check in in regards to the laws in regards to service dogs. i understand it cost more money to train a service dog then to onboard a staff member at your hospital but we're not trying to compare anything here now are we.

we live in las vegas but it was necessary for us to have a surgical procedure performed in san diego at sharp memorial. from the time we walked in the door, our experience exceeded all expectations.  the staff was helpful, friendly, and professional.  the hospital was beautiful with a clean, uplifting, inviting atmosphere.  everyone from the cafe employee to the rn was so kind and very professional.  we especially appreciate chris, michelle, carol, bethel, albert, and brandon (rns, recovery, transport), and of course, our anesthesiologist and dr. dente.  the care we received was excellent.  everything was according to schedule, and throughout the whole experience, the staff took great care of us; extremely attentive, positive, reassuring, available, and happy to assist.  everyone seemed very happy to work there; no one seemed stressed, overwhelmed, or grumpy (we know hospitals can be very  high-stress environments with heavy workloads).  the procedure went quickly, smoothly, and was successful.  we are grateful for the excellent care we received at sharp memorial, and we will never forget your kindness.

i do want to mention that mckay-dee is a beautiful hospital and a bit more updated with larger rooms but my experience at ogden regional was far superior. my room might have been smaller but all of the nurses, doctors and staff i encountered were kind and professional. my room was clean at all times and everyone was constantly checking on me and baby. i had an awful experience with my epidural at the other hospital so that was my main concern here. ashley assured me that the guy administering the epidural that day was fantastic and everything would be ok. she was right i couldn't believe how smoothly everything went. the entire staff treated me like i was important and not another number to them and that really made a difference for me. i feel very vulnerable during the recovery time and to be treated with care and respect is huge. i actually teared up multiple times because i was so happy to have such a better experience here and vowed to leave a positive review. i'm a bit late leaving that review but i remembered! if given the choice now i'd select ogden regional to deliver at!

wow, i wish i had seen these other reviews before sending my mother here. her (our) experiences were a nightmare - with the list of grievances almost too long to list. she went to chcc following a bout with pneumonia. we selected chcc because i live in wyckoff, it was convenient and we thought it had a decent reputation. what a mistake. the aides and nurses don't work together and have a very "not my area" lack of responsibility. my mom was in the rehab center for over a week before she received her first shower. the bogus explanation was she was a two person assist and couldn't be put into the shower - really? she had been in a prior rehab center, we have seen the shower seats and the lifts used for immobile patients. the bottom line was understaffing of the aides and laziness on the part of staff.

there is also a lack of accountability and lack of oversight by administration. my mother was finally given a shower and had her hair washed after my insistence to speak to the head nurse and whomever ran the facility. even after complaining many of the same problems continued.  she wasn't washed again for another week after the first complaint.

my mom is immobile and incontinent. she too had issues with infrequent changing and dirty diapers. i had taken mom for a wheelchair ride one day and she told me she needed to go to the bathroom. we went back to the room, and i rang the call button. when the aide came in, she told me mom required two people to get her on the toilet so i should just let her dirty the diaper and then she would change it - is this someone's perverse definition of patient dignity? 
she's also been prone to urinary infections so we are careful to make sure she isn't sitting in a wet diaper. we were told, when we asked about frequency of changing, they have super absorbent diapers so we shouldn't worry.  how about just changing her more frequently? why was that not an option?

then there was the day my mother spilled water at lunch all over her floor - again we called the call button. first we were told maintenance was out of lunch and they would come later.  four hours and 5 or 6 calls later, the water was still there. it was not cleaned up until one nurse saw i was about to lose it - and she brought towels and cleaned it up herself. i regret i didn't take her name as she was the only person we encountered who acted like they cared.

the food can be ok but only if you carefully select from the menu - if you leave it up to regular choices, beware. we mistakenly ordered a tuna sandwich one day - it was disgusting. there were two pieces of white bread, a smear of tuna fish that was thinner than the amount of butter most people put on toast and that was it - no lettuce, no tomato, nothing nutritious about it. their idea of a good diet is interesting - again if you order a protein, a salad and some vegetables you have a chance at a decent meal, but beware if you aren't diligent about your loved ones food. my mother's roommate had to eat sandwiches because of an injury, she told her daughter one day she would rather not eat than to eat another one of those sandwiches.

bottom line - if my mother needs to go to rehab again, i can tell you where we won't go.

review:
choose your hospital wisely:

i went to holy cross for a knee replacement.  the doctor was great and replacement doing good. however, when i came home i was on pain meds with tylenol.  doctors told me i most likely acquired a gram negative ecoli infection from the urinary catheter. the infection then grew into my blood and i became sepsis. after a week in another hospital and sent home with a mid line iv for antibiotics. i recovered after three weeks. i called holy cross hospital infectious department to let them know.  well i received no concern, no caring, and an excuse that i only had the catheter for one day. they also said, in order to pick up this infection in the hospital i would have had to have the catheter two days.  so not a very educated answer.  infections are acquired through direct contact and time exposure plays no role. 

copied from the internet:

causes
bacteria are normally found throughout the body including on the skin and in the intestines. when kept in balance, bacteria can help the body work normally. however, an imbalance of the bacteria or passing of bacteria to areas where there are no bacteria, can lead to an infection. an infection will develop if large amounts of bacteria are present, the bacteria are aggressive, or the immune system is weakened.

common ways for bacteria to pass to vulnerable parts of the body include:

use of medical devices that pass into the body, such as iv or urinary catheters
open wounds
contact with someone who has or has been exposed to gram-negative bacteria
risk factors
hospitalization is the most common risk factor for gram-negative bacterial infections. the longer the stay in the hospital, the higher the risk of infection.

other factors that increase the risk of a bacterial infection include:

recent surgery
use of urinary catheter
war wounds
dialysis for kidney disease , which includes regular use of iv lines or catheters
mechanical ventilator use
weakened immune system

with my experience it doesn't matter how good the doctor is.  if the hospital is a sick hospital, even the most mild surgery could cause sickness or even death. do your research.

the absolute worst experience i've ever gone through. took my mother to the er  after her doctor said it would be easier and faster to get blood work, ct scan, mri and urine work done. my mom was in severe pain, so much she could barely walk. she had vertigo, tinnitus and was shaking. she had "flu" symptoms earlier that week but that was not the point of the visit, her pain and unbalance was. we waited around an hour to get a room, then we had to wait even more for a nurse to come and take a urine sample. we got into the room at almost 3, she was finally given tylenol at 4:30 for her severe pain. we didn't see the doctor until 5:30, after waiting hours. the doctor said my mom was okay to go home, without any blood work or exams. someone who is crying in bed, unable to handle the pain is okay to go home??? the doctor lacked any sort of humanity or empathy. i obviously felt insulted that nothing was done to help my mom apart from 1000mg of tylenol (which can be bought at any store) so i asked why she was in so much pain, why she was so dizzy she couldn't walk alone and why they didn't do any blood work. the doctor looked me in the face and said she didn't need it, that she needed to go home and rest. we were just another bed that needed to be empty for the next number to come in. i had to hunt down a nurse to get discharged, she said they were going to give mom a dose of vertigo medicine before she left. they weren't even going to send her medicine to go home. i was told that ct scans and mri were not done there, and that my mom would have to have an actual reason to them. urine culture was not sent to lab to find out if there was an infection, because that would take 48 hours and that wasn't needed. belittled and abused are not enough to describe this disgusting experience. all they're good for is over charging people for terrible service. if you go to a hospital you expect to be getting the best service possible, but instead here you leave just as bad as you came in and mentally drained. go anywhere else. the er doctors are inhuman.

this massive one stop kaiser under construction  and stadium parking makes for a fun time. said no one ever. parking here is no bueno. and i came on a holiday. if you are really sick the last thing you want is to have to walk. if you come on a day other than christmas parking will be 10 times worse. however, if it is raining i promise you won't get wet. whoever designed the walking bridges did a good job
 
urgent care is a lengthy process if any sort of lab/x ray/mri is required. expect to spend 3-4 hours here during your visit. with a change in shift or a rotation it can be even longer.

the mister got sick on the way to christmas dinner so we made our way to one of the few facilities that had urgent care. it had been at least 20 years that i visited this location.

care team was nice. however we got mixed in the shuffle when the doc we saw went off duty during our visit. which meant the nurse practitioner took over, which meant a new dr was also overseeing her recommendation. it took 2 hours after test results were sent to my phone before seeing the new provider.

pharmacy took only 10 minutes for a handful of meds and devices and a huge chunk of change.

i do prefer the garden grove urgent care because i feel it's easier to navigate.

review:
well, i went to urgent care on a sunday evening and they determined that i several bones in my foot were broken.  i had an appt they following morning with orthopaedics to determine the best course of action.  my appt was with sunil dinker mehta dpm, dpm who advised i would be in a cast for 6 weeks.  (oh joy!).  

i asked if i could get a wheelchair out to the pick-up area as i wasn't very good on the crutches. i was advised that the voluntears with the wheelchairs can only take people to their appts, not pick them up afterwards.  (how odd is that, go figure)

of course, i read all my paperwork and saw the following:  
if you're told to keep your cast or splint on, tape a sheet of plastic to cover it when you bathe. or ask your doctor about products that can help keep a cast or splint dry. water under the cast or splint can cause your skin to itch and hurt.

it would have been helpful of they just told me that cvs sells a product that is designed to keep your cast dry when you shower.  

oh well, see you in 6 weeks.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review:
i went into urgent care because getting an appointment with my regular physician would take a month and an available physician would be a week!

but with urgent care, i got my piece of mind and all i needed was aleve and a heat pad for my aching lumbar muscles.

i felt the staff who helped me were kind and the facility is clean. they supply hand-sanitizers everywhere and face mask, if you want extra protection from airborne illnesses. 

abundant amount of parking if you don't mind walking. the facility is huge!

review: what a racket. this place not only gets worse with each damn visit. they overbook appointments to a point it's a nightmare finding parking.  i suppose there is no way to coordinate visits at the hundreds of services at this massive location. being forced to choose between treatment and safety is not fun. everybody looks lost. lost and upset. the parking garage is dog eat dog today. what's worse is, having to drive so far only to be late to an appointment due to lack of parking places, circling endlessly in this maze of equally lost folks seeking care. i had a great care giver set up closer to home, and you could park within half a mile of the door. kaiser could not allow that level of convenience and moved my healthcare to a different county into this maze of confusion. i'm still not getting all the care my primary doctor recommends, i just can't drive an hour for a ten minute visit and then have to walk an unknown distance to make things easier for kaiser. i was almost hit twice by distracted drivers on my last visit here. walking with a cane just makes one a better target it seems. walking through a dark parking structure, dodging drivers who just came in from the bright sunlit day, is not the thrill it was when i was much younger.

pee in a cup and hold on to it for an additional 1 hour. this was back & forth 2+ times. once i got back to the emergency room, i was told to sit in a chair...this was for 6+ hours even when i told them my tailbone was hurting from the car accident. the nurse said "you could just stand there and wait." i couldn't sit i was standing up the entire time because i was in so much pain. there was a bed ready for a girl who just had a busted lip. they let out the chair for other patients into a bed form and that is what i requested, because my tail bone was so uncomfortable that was the real review:
so, i have long had a mixed relationship with kaiser but the latest update to how they conduct medical care really is just awful. i am giving them a 2 but i am seriously considering updating to a 1 after i have some additional time to think about this.

so some prescriptions as all hmo kaiser will not cover. that is fine. not fun but i get it. in those cases kaiser has been willing to allow the doctor to prescribe the medication and then i can go to a pharmacy like costco to get it filled where it is cheaper then going to kaiser.
