review: per kaiser staff member... #nofacemasksisgoodforbusiness!!!  i went in today, to request medical records, and found there were no protective face masks to be found anywhere. i stepped into the urgent care office, and begged for one, only to be told only those signing in could have one. i then stopped at the info counter, and one of the 2 ladies there felt sorry for me - so she retrieved [a mask] for me from the cabinet, under the desk. an older man stepped up a few minutes later, and asked the other lady [an old lady in her 70's - let's call her ru**] told him they did not have any at all. i turned to her and said, "yes, you do!" she informed me quite rudely that there were none in stock. i shot back with "open the cabinet right behind you. you do have masks!] she still refused to give the man one. i then said to her, loud enough for everyone in the immediate area to hear, "so, kaiser is now  refusing to provide protective masks, so that healthy people who come into the hospital will end up getting sick?!!! her response was a very matter-of-fact and smug, "no face masks is good fo business!!!" she repeated this twice!!... and, additionally, stated that kaiser had instructed all its' employees not to provide masks to anyone that asked for one, period!" i could not believe what she had just openly admitted to! i immediately reported her... & hopefully that heartless sorry excuse for a human being gets reprimanded, if not fired!  the flu season is back...& w/a vengeance! so if you aren't sick, avoid kaiser altogether if possible! if you must go, especially to their indoor pharmacy, bring your own face mask and a can of lysol, or run the risk of coming down with something serious shortly thereafter!!!  of course, compared to the extremely bad medical care my husband and daughter have suffered at the hands of kaiser's supposed "specialists"  over the past 6 months and counting, this latest kaiser "facemasks" debacle is nothing at all!

review: here's the good: the main pharmacy in the med center is awesome. the techs & pharmacists i've encountered are smart, efficient, and thank god have a great sense of humor. pretty much the same with northside. the lab: i've had great techs and really fast, efficient service. this is the organizational best here. my husband has not fared as well. he's allergic to plastic tape and every time that's what's been used to adhere his bandage. he's an adult, can walk, talk, see. obviously he can't think because he never  says anything!! oh well! the not good: follow up for problems, assessment of problems, primary care at the lowest possible level for the masses. it does not matter if the lowest possible action or treatment is not effective. it does not matter if you are willing to pay cash for legacy medicine that has proven to be effective and with which you've been stable for over 50 years. it does not matter if an inhaler for asthma is not effective despite correct use. there will not be any evaluation or consideration of alternative evaluations or intervention. you will not be evaluated for the possibility of eosinophilic generated asthma or asthma triggered by leukotrienes. apparently in the land of kp, albuterol is the only existing rescue inhaler in the universe. does not matter if it doesn't work. use the steroid inhaler & if the rescue doesn't work, well if you die, it's cheaper. family member with adult onset t2 diabetes? well if your glucose has been stable at 90-100 and your a1c at 5, they'll stop your effective meds, watch your glucose climb to 400+ then put you on 80-100 units of nph insulin and continue to enable out of control t2dm. no return to effective treatment-that's not how we do it now. my colleague is a nationally recognized advanced practice cde rn. she is appalled by the lack of current accepted practice management. so in these areas, kp fails. we will return to ucla & cedars-sinai during next open enrollment. my family member's life depends on it. but for well-person routine care & immunizations kp is great & convenient. perhaps a more forward-thinking pcp would also be better.

review:
this is in regards to emergency room dr. kenneth hoppens.


dr.hoppens has 0 bedside manner. i went in for a panic attack before i self harmed because my medication wasn't filled and i also had a busted lip. he worried about my previous self harm scars and my current medication list instead of what i was there for. he treated me like an er hopper looking for narcotics when i just wanted a shot not a prescription to calm me. this was after he also seen all of my surgical scars. this is also the doctor who sent me home the night i tried to overdose and end my life. he needs to be removed from emergency medicine.

i am not sure how to put this into words representative of the lasting emotional trauma they caused me, my girlfriend, and anyone else who received the same treatment; but i will do my best in articulating a proper review for this soulless place. 

stormont vail is yet another culprit in the ongoing "cesarean section epidemic" attempting to push them on anyone they can, regardless of a clean bill of health each time they run tests. if your tests do not meet the average with pinpoint accuracy, they will shame you into receiving a c-section.  

i am sad to say that shaming is the perfect descriptor for what they do to someone who questions why they are demanding you get a c-section. if the shaming does not work, well then they turn to directly strong arming you. they will berate you, and put you in such an uncomfortable position that you will suffer emotional distress. some of the doctors will even overstep their bounds and directly threaten you if you bring facts contrary to their beliefs. do not let them fool you. 

if every one of your health tests are borderline average, do not let them deceive you. my son was scheduled to be born a week after the c-section they coerced my girlfriend to get. he was born unable to take in the appropriate amount of oxygen, and for exactly a week i watched him suffer. 

i say my son suffered for a week, and the key point here is that was when his natural birth was meant to be, a week after the scheduled c-section. pure coincidence he left the nicu on his scheduled natural birth date? i'll leave that to the scientists who know better than shyster doctors. i can only present the data i have at hand. 

prospective families, do not under any circumstance let them sway you. unless they say specifically that your case is imminently life threatening (they may do that anyways, hence why i say overstepping their bounds), do not give in to the duress.  

in closing: the nursing staff is overworked and undervalued. their ability to be cordial is limited by this. nonetheless most of them were absolutely terrible at their jobs, and had atrocious bedside manner; often they would forget about you and become irate at even the slightest reminder. communication between the multiple wards is also nearly nonexistent, leaving you to run middleman for them.
this hospital is awful. not helpful at all, they all just stand around and talk. sat there for five hours waiting for tests results. never coming back here again.

9 hours after bringing a family member in for severe abdominal pain and a spiking fever, we've yet to see a doctor or have access to an actual er bed. waiting in the main lobby. this is round 2 since a month ago, made a similar trip with a non-diagnosis. note primary care doc ordered some tests and sent us immediately to the er. needless to say, i'm not impressed. the lack of communication and unhelpful information from front desk staff is 0 stars. and the waiting room is virtually empty. i'll never come here again.

update: i've been asked to call patient experience team, and will do so!

if you ask for the nurse name to file complaint, they stop responding to you, lies on you too, for them. the doctors band in w them, so if the staff get upset the doctors will lie too, on medical notes, to discharge you, then block your access to another hospital, like the next level down, an acute care hospital. they work to get you restricted from these rehab places, even having insurance thatll cover it.

review: i went for inpatient electric shock therapy so i had to stay on the behavior award... called ahead of time to see if i could bring a blanket and book, was told that would be fine, nothing about it having to be a soft bound book and then they wouldn't let me take my blanket... i had a horrible first night, i was sat in a room by a tech who was not very nice to anyone, and as fake as could be. i don't remember her name but she has a piercing on her cheek. she said she'd give me a tour of the floor but instead left me in that room for 35 minutes then came and got me and just took me to my room. it was very cold in there and all i had was the regular top blanket and a sheet and since they have to do bed checks every 15 minutes when someone come in at ask for a blanket and they would always say that they would come back with one i didn't get one until the next day!i felt like in a place where i needed comfort, there wasn't anywhere to look for it... after i have been crying all morning finally a nurse had approached me, penny. and she said that i could have my blanket if they washed it which was fine with me i didn't care so i had my husband bring it at visiting hours. and i asked if they could put it with the next load of laundry but instead i didn't get it till 530am the next day! i thought this whole process could have been a lot easier on me if things were told up front to me over the phone. there's some really great workers there though i have to say and some really nice people that do work there! i did get a voice my complaints to the guy running the floor. it seems like you have to figure out by yourself though how to get your hygiene products and your clothes because nobody will tell you, you have to ask. but i guess that is such as life with every place you go there's some good employees and some bad!

the hospital is generally average for what the do, but we have billing problems the last two years off and on.  they billed us 9 months in arrears.  i have gone to settle other billings directly with the finance dept. head and she wasn't able to find the invoices we received in the mail in their records. they have billed for a procedure that was a redo because the first one was done by a newby and had to be done again but at no charge as per the payment desk and doctors.  they are trying to get payment from the insurance company for it, but blue cross is disputing it as they should  call this what you may.  if this was just once, we would understand an error but this is ongoing.  we have used this hospital for fifteen or so years without many problems.  something has changed, so now we will go to another hospital that is actually closer now. we always pay our bills either at the time of service or within 15 days.

i asked for a first appointment and said that it had to be before a specific date. weather cancelled that appointment which, it turns out, i wasn't even scheduled for. i was apparently scheduled for a date during my trip the whole time. when i got back from the trip i was told i was a no-show and told i could never come back! this didn't happen at this exact location but it is a st. luke's policy so that is who i am writing the review about!

worst hospital ever. their staff has changed to huge jerks. no compassion. no care. no friendly staff. no bedside manner. doctors don't care whether you live or die. or whether you're happy or crying or screaming in pain.
great place to work. mountainview has great benefits as well as competitive pay. i've been at mv for 4 years now and look forward to many more.

i went to er with mysterious symptoms. the staff and doctor was thorough, friendly & professional. various tests were preformed to eliminate probable conditions. i felt that i was in good hands. since we were traveling from out of state, the doctor gave me copies of some tests to share with our family doctor. he made recommendations in changing some of my medications. even though my situation was not an "emergency", i appreciate their care & concern. thank you very much!

i arrived at mclaren hospital in an ambulance from war memorial hospital and admitted to a double room in the cardiac unit.  i was scared, talking a mile a minute, while gasping for breath.  the hospitalists, the nurses and nurse practitioners, the ultrasound tech, the cardiologists - all were professional, caring, willing to listen.  one fellow who delivered food, made me laugh and relax.  the hospital also had color-coded uniforms so that you could tell whether it was a phlebotomist or a nursing assistant or a medical doctor coming in to your room. even my roommates (4, over the course of 7 nights) were interesting and non-intrusive.  i was very pleasantly surprised that this relatively small community hospital gave me such good care.

the nurses were very nice and gave some wonderful tlc but the hospital as a whole is terrible. just entering the hospital is a death trap (construction everywhere). when released, i was told to go to admissions on the first floor. another nightmare with a woman who has definitely been doing her job far too long. rude and dismissive. barked orders at me, never looked up from her computer. of course there aren't many options in the area but if you can avoid this house of horrors, do so.

mclaren's billing:

my husband had a stroke december 2019. he was rushed to mclaren northern michigan hospital in petoskey. frankly, i felt my head was in a fog most of the time and i was just so glad he came out of it alive. he had rehab done locally in january and had to have a follow-up with the neurologist february 3rd. doctor said that they cannot find a reason for my husband having a stroke and he needed to have a loop recorder placed inside his chest to see if he has a-fib.  february 7th he has that put in.  today (february 26) i am sitting at my desk paying $1,300 in co-pays for the things he had done - i admit it is a bit steep for us but praising god my husband is still alive. however, as i was paying by phone with mclaren, they let me know that there was a bill for $11,000.00 coming down the pike that wasn't covered by bcbs. it was the loop recorder. they called and asked for a pre-authorization for the loop to be placed in and was told by bcbs that they didn't one - no mention that it wasn't a covered benefit; the doctor's office didn't ask and bcbs didn't offer them the information. how does two retired people on social security suppose to pay for their mistake because each one blames the other for not getting the information and we are stuck with the bill? 

paying on these bills are equally as hard because all you get from mclaren's is the dollar amount - you really have no idea what you are paying on (it isn't itemized). also, when paying online through your bank, you have to input each bill into your system as each bill has its own unique account number. so you may have a dozen bills (like we have) and each one has its own account number - very time-consuming having to pay online.

i would like to describe my dissatisfaction with the services at the entrance tonight. i am extremely upset at the way i was treated by the security that expressed his name: brian diaz. 

tomorrow will be exactly a week since my dad was admitted. unfortunately i found myself caught at work for two days and hadn't gone to visit so i decided to drive out to la puente to pick up a favorite meal for my dad upon his request. we spoke on the phone earlier before i headed out and agreed i would be "in and out" since it was late and i knew visiting hrs were over. i have visited 5 times prior after hours for about 15 min since i don't get out of work till late usually. all the other securities on post were very nice and understanding. i also called the nurses station and made sure it was ok beforehand. they ok my quick visit and i never received a rude reply from anyone until today. 

the security made me feel unwelcome the moment i walked in through the er. he rudely said "why are you here if you know visiting hours are over?" after i had already stated i was just dropping off a hot meal for my dad. also, he seemed very unexperienced since he asked what department i was heading to after i had already stated the room number and who i was there to see. he replied with " are you here for the labor department?" i said "for my dad?" as i frowned, this conversation was not going as i expected. i just simply said i'd call the nurses station to see if it was fine and they quickly connected me and said 10 minutes would be ok. i came back inside and he was already speaking to someone on his walkie. he proceeded to tell me that i was only allowed 10 minutes and i should be back not a minute later like i was a child. he scolded me and ignored anything else i had to say. he assumed i knew were the room was and just opened to door in the hospital through the er room were we were. he repeated to say i better be back or he'd send for me! never did he showed any costumer service skills and instead treated me disgustingly. 

i then walked in to the room where my father was and he saw how upset i was, i couldn't hide it. i told him i'd be here for a couple minutes now i was scared to be in longer. after 7 minutes passed i told him i was gonna go speak to his nurse to get an exact patient update and next day doctor's order. we are actually expecting his discharge pretty soon so i needed to know. as i approached the nurses station i saw a security guard coming towards the hall where i had come out of. diaz had already send another guard to come find me. i could hear him saying "what room is she in?" ten minutes had not even gone by. i tried to ignore him as i spoke to the nurses and told them how uncomfortable i was. i said "look that security i think is here to come get me". the nurses looked over at him, one laughed said "you could stay here 15 minutes if you want. don't worry," she said. they other nurse said "they are just doing his job." i said i understand but this doesn't feel right. i walked down the hall to speak private about my dad to the nurse. then i left and i was leaving i saw a missed call form my dad. i walked back into the room and found my dad very upset and he expressed to me he could hear the security loudly in the hallway and then told me he wasn't hungry anymore. now that broke my heart. my father wasn't able to enjoy my nice gesture. so i left and promised i'd be back the next morning. 

my night was clearly ruined. i would of been happy to have to 10 peaceful minute to see him.

for years i always expressed my pleasant visits to the er and wonderful experiences to others for the times i have visited and gave labor here. regardless of the negative comments people always have of greater el monte hospital, i always assure everyone that never have i ever had a bad experience from any staff. let me be clear that i have been to almost all the departments in this hospital for the years i have lived in el monte, 25 yrs and counting to be exact. everyone has been wonderful, why ruin it tonight? 

i find it concerning that i was treated as i was tonight. this cannot be tolerated. no patient nor visitor should have a low rated experience. i rate that mean security guard 0 stars but i can still rate everyone else 5 stars. my rating averages out to a 3 star because of this, very upsetting!

don't come to this emergency room. don't know about the hospital itself, but the er is definitely not where you want to take your loved ones.

twice this place has not handled our cases properly. twice it has been potentially life threatening and we've been sent on our merry fucking way like nothing was wrong. we've only come back because it's so much closer than any other hospital to us, but i think from now on we'll take our chances in going further out for help.

yesterday morning around 5 am my husband and i came in due to a major ear infection he had that started with jaw bone pain and slowly spread to his ear. they took a look at his ear for two minutes, said it was just an outer ear infection and sent him out with a prescription and said if it persisted to check in with his gp. this morning the pain became much worse. we went to an er in arcadia, and thankfully the nurses listened to him when asking when and where the pain started and suggested some tests. turns out the infection had spread to his bone and could spread to his brain. what kind of er are you guys running at this establishment? the staff didn't even want him time to read over the paperwork they were making him sign before discharging him, just telling him to sign it. he had to insist he wanted to know what he was signing for the nurse to quit pushing him to sign it right away and snatch it back. they weren't particularly busy at that hour, why can't my husband read what he's signing?

last year, my husband had an allergic reaction to his anti-psychotics medication he was taking and had seen on the label to go to the er if he developed any negative reactions to it. they said he was having nothing more than a panic attack and we walked out when the only thing they said they could do is let him ride it out. went to another hospital to be sure, and sure enough they diagnosed the allergy which could have pretty drastic repercussions if not rectified and took care of him and prescribed him something different.

maybe you should ensure your er staff pays better attention to the patients who roll through. you might actually save more lives that way.

i brought in my son to be evaluated and i received excellent care during our er visit. thank you to er staff especially monica for the excellent care provided. she was was amazing. lin did an amazing job while doing xrays and was so considerate and gentle with my son's arm that was in pain. dr tran was very kind and patient. he explained everything and updated me with results. jennifer provided  us with discharge teaching and was so wonderful. excellent care we received. i highly recommend.

our son was forced to come here two years ago from whittier presbyterian. this is the worst hospital i've ever been to in my life. it was like being in a third world. everything was outdated, and disgustingly dirty. staff and doctors were completely rude.  at one point they needed him taken to a room for blood tests and i found alot of dried old  blood spatter on the walls and i took my son out and complained and the staff made excuses for it. at the end of our stay the woman in charge of pediatrics pulled me aside and tried to convince me not to leave a bad review or complain. she had been quite rude and condescending to me the entire time because i made it known how unprofessional and hideous everything was about that place. if i could leave a -100 star review i would.

wow very impressed with the care my uncle mario carvajal received after he was admitted on 11/24/19, staff here attended to his needs promptly and ran the proper test to determine his condition according to his chief of complaint and rule out any suspicious of his illness. my uncle was treated very assertively.  last but not least they called a few days later to follow up on his care!!! excellent service!!! 

thank you,

lorena c

hello yesterday at 7:45pm after visiting with my aunt carmen figueroa i had went to the lobby to wait on my access ride. the app on my phone had told me i had a 5 minute wait. while i was waiting on my ride the security guard at the front desk came up to me and ask who i was waiting for. i told him that i was waiting for my access ride. he then told me that i was more than welcome to wait in the emergency room or to go outside and wait. i then told him that i couldn't wait in the emergency room because my ride wouldn't know where i was and that access always picks me up in front. he then told me well i can't have you here anymore and that he was closing for the night and that i would need to go outside and wait. i then told him but it's cold outside and he said well you can't wait here anymore. i then told him fine but if i get sick i am blaming you. that security guard was very rude to me he knows for a fact that it is against the law to throw a handicapped woman in a wheelchair in the freezing cold outside to wait for her ride i think there should be something done he should not be working there

i brought my daughter in yesterday for a shoulder injury. we were registered and seen quickly. then it seemed we were there for hours and felt like we were forgotten about.  me and my girlfriend were nervous and waiting impatiently. we decided to go somewhere else. claudia came and explained the process of a transfer and why it could take a while. she explained how the insurance worked. dr. kingsley was also very concerned and attentive. he explained why my daughter needed to be transferred. we decided to stay. great job dr. kingsley and  claudia.

definitely was scared to come for surgery here after i read the reviews. 

i went to orthopedic institute of the west first. the dr works there and does surgeries at this hospital. dr kaplan. 

surgery went well. got a hip replacement but when i woke up i couldn't move my toes or foot. i got a foot drop. still not sure how it happened. from touching the nerves to much, the nerve block shot, cause he stretched my foot, we don't know. 

also when i woke up and they brought me to the room the machines were beeping and no one came to check, this freaked me out. also the blood pressure cable got unhooked which is why it was beeping i found out. the other beeping was for fluids. they don't really check on you so make sure someone is with you. 

the breakfast was good. they usually called me to make an order or you can call the kitchen for breakfast lunch and dinner. 

physical therapy came twice a day which i was excited for so i can move and not be bored. 

the hospital can use some remodeling, especially the bathrooms cause you can barely go with the walker inside.

my mother went in for abdominal pain and they took good care of her while they found out what it was. their gi specialists and radiologists actually show great care for their patients. it felt like a while we waited to get the results (about a day), but they caught precancer and made sure that a few more tests were done to ensure that it wasn't more serious. we appreciated it a great deal. nurses came as soon as they were called and made us feel comfortable and some of them had a great sense of humor which made us all feel a lot better considering.

this is the worst hospital i have ever been to in my entire life. do not come here. we have been waiting behind 2 i repeat 2 people in the waiting room for 3 hours. unreal. again, the worst hospital i have ever experienced.

update: our past experience at this er has been worse than bad, but we went in a couple days ago and for the most part it was improved! the pa who cared for my husband, dana, was exceptional! she was friendly but very professional. the rn, teca, was also great. we felt like they actually cared about their patients! gold star for both of them! however, the triage nurse (didn't get her name but tall with short blonde hair) was the exact opposite. the triage in the er was not busy but she acted like she was angry we were even there. my husband is hard of hearing, so when she would ask him a question and he couldn't hear, she would practically shout the question again in a very condescending manner. super unprofessional! if we hadn't already checked in, we would have left to go to another er, just based on her actions alone. thank goodness for dana and teca! they are the best!

i went to immanuel's er with 104 temp, raging head ache and black urine. what this terrible hospital did is test for flu and staff. results were negative but i was severely ill. they sent me away with no further tests, i was clearly in bad shape, thank god i went to methodist the next day after going to my personal physician recognizing i was in trouble. i was diagnosed with legionaries disease and rushed to the icu. after a 10 day stay began to recover. very blessed!
    now what really upset me is a cover up stating i declined care. that is someone covering their a$$. maybe they were busy, i don't know. why would i decline care when i was so sick? all i asked was some help on a bill for treatment i did not receive. crappy care and a middle figure is basically what i received.
    i recommend any other hospital, both myself and my family will never trust this hospital for care again!

i've had good & bad experiences at the va hospital in columbia sc. i've been a part of the va health care system since 1985. i have to admit it's gotta much better than, when i had a emergency trip for my asthma issues and sat in the waiting area to be initially scene 
(six hours!)  but in a brighter note, i was scene in the private community and told a spot on my neck wasn't anything to worry about,  the va doctor at least had the sence to had the spot biopsy... turned out to be a basil cell skin cancer,  surgery was great!! no problems since. (with dermatology) 

  now let's talk about my current primary care doctor.....time to retire!!  
the doctor listens to my chest and says
"sounds like you have some wheezing....
he hadn't even looked at my chart before i arrived....to see i have copd/severe asthma. 

later that week i received in the mail,  a notice for surgery,  scheduled without my knowledge or permission....
again,  its time to think about someone putting in the retirement paperwork..33+ years 
 & someone called & gave me a chewing out!!
the caller looked at the wrong date...
piss poor quality of personal if you ask me 

lastly,  its fracking stupid, before i leave (every) appointment,  we set up a follow up appointment, then a few days later,  reminder in the mail, a week before the appointment,  post card reminder, phone calls to remind you 
text messages..... i've missed 1 (one) appointment by their records in
fac_name: WM Jennings Bryan Dorn VA Medical Center

review:
check the demographics of this place before you seek treatment. like many va hospitals, this one is broken. 

i received a phone call from a dr. stephanie curry at dorn. i've never been seen by this doctor in my life. this lady sounded aggressive, and was quick to anger when i asked her a question. i thought i had just got a call from one of the homies. sounds familiar? needless to say, i wrote the hospital director, dr. omura about her behavior. i would not recommend dr curry. she did not treat me like a customer. i don't think the type of attitude she displayed would be tolerated in private practice. people don't want to spend their money to be treated rudely. 

the va does not profit from their patients like a private hospital, but i can assure you that the va expects a return on investment (roi). veterans do carry "vote dollars." i suggest veterans utilize the choice program and see just how well you are treated at a private facility. as well as the effectiveness of your medical care. 

just ask yourself this one question about the va. "why does the housekeeping officer make more money than a doctor at the va? still want to go there for treatment? oh, and the housekeeping officer only needs a high school diploma. shocking!

this is why trump gave the va his immediate attention once elected. he initiated the "mission act of 2018." that means that veterans now have the extended choice program and can get their care with a private doctor within the va pay network. 

veterans, if you do chose this hospital, always please be sure to take a family member with you; it keeps staff honest. and don't lower your standards just because the standards are low at this hospital.
fac_name: WM Jennings Bryan Dorn VA Medical Center

review: they're always polite and helpful. the medical staff are awesome. when given the opportunity, i've always come here for tests and treatment.

i took my brother-in-law to the r.h. emergency room about 1 am. there were only about 4 people waiting. he is crippled with polio and permanently in a wheel chair and covered by medicaid. they got his billing info and we sat for 11/2 hours. we gave up and left. medicaid notified us that r.h. had billed them for over a thousand dollars for absolutely nothing.

i have 2 cataract surgeries here. first o all the staff is terrific. very pleasant and helpful. my first surgery was terrific. the nurses are more than nicce, down to tthe way they speak to u to the warm blanketts and the juice and crackers  dr.nguyen is a genius! forgive me for any misspelling my eyes are still adjusting from yesterday's surgery. a nurse just called to check on me which reminded me to post. they get you inal qnd out but  you feel important

i had two outpatient eye surgeries in 2014 and everything was fine.  i recently had a two-day in-patient knee replacement and i was seriously disappointed.   everything was fine with the surgery as before but the in-patient stay was horrific.   it was like staying in a stripped-down cheap motel 6.  the staffing was limited.  they encouraged you to have someone spend the night with you post surgery.  there were strangers roaming the hallways and patients were in single rooms.  it was scary.  the only persons i saw the first night were male attendants who helped me to the bathroom.  there is no in-house food service.  it is all brought in on trays like airplane service.  meals were microwaved and you are given flimsy plastic silverware that broke when you used it.  the day following surgery, no one came to check on me until 10 a.m.  the nurse?came in and i asked when breakfast was coming and she informed me that breakfast was over and there was no food.  eventually, a man came in in a white coat and pulled two small cereal boxes from his pocket and announced "breakfast is here!"  no bowl, milk or silverware.  they don't keep any juice, crackers, yogurt or jello for post-surgical patients who might come out of anesthesia with a queasy stomach.   there were no
amenities nor creature comforts like a carafe of ice water in your room, a towel or facecloth to wash up.   there was a bed, tray table and chair in the room and lousy tv service.  it was a cold, spare, soul less place.

the physical therapists were two older teens who helped me walk across the hall once and then showed me how to push a walmart bag back and forth while i sat in a chair.  i was never given a discharge meeting and was told ten minutes before i was picked up that an ambulance was coming to transfer me.  it was friday and they do not want to staff over the weekends so everyone was supposed to leave by noon.  i believe the kids might have been summer employees as it was summertime.

this is a doctor-owned facility and it is truly bare bones and they are pinching every last penny there.  the only good thing was the nurse who started my iv got it on the first try and it was painless.  kudos to her!  i would never go there again as an inpatient.  it was too barebones for me and scary at night if you were alone.  i think the out-patient surgery staff is good but the inpatient staff needs a lot of training and employees.

i started going to bsw because my insurance changed. i was trying to pick a doctor. i had to make a quick visit for a illness and i was paired with sarah yeakley demuth, pa. she is now my pcp. she has the best bedside manner. she takes the time to listen to any concerns and explains everything in detail. she searches for solutions to my problems with me. she is the best health care provider i have ever visited.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Emergency Medical Center - Cedar Park

review: came here for an er visit. they gave me fluids and i waited for about an hour before they said they couldn't serve me because the computers and thus equipment was down. i was transferred to an actual hospital for the duration of my care. i just received a bill for both hospitals despite the fact that it was their fault their equipment was down. a decent doctor would not have charged $400 for fluids when they knew i'd have to be transferred. safe to say i will not be recommending anyone to go here.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Emergency Medical Center - Cedar Park

review:
i just got out of here today and please stay away. while here i heard many staff making fun of the patients laughing and calling them "crazy". one girl with schizophrenia in here with me overheard them and was extremely hurt and cried to me about it and told me how they made her feel even worse about herself. this made me feel awful because this girl had so much horrible trauma in her life and that is why she was this way. these staff are lucky enough to not have gone through the things she has been through and should not be judging her.

the staff is just rude period. anytime you ask them for anything in the inpatient unit they just roll their eyes at you and act like you are such an inconvenience to them. sometimes they won't even get up and just ignore you. also a guy in there when i was in there kept seizing and every time we told them he was seizing they just rolled their eyes and laughed. i really wish i was making this up but i'm not... 

they are also soooo disorganized in order to get out of there you have to keep pushing and pushing them to get things rolling. they will never do anything without you having to ask them 10 times. they will try and keep you in here to make more money. also my mom and boyfriend were calling them and they just kept hanging up on them every time they called.

the inpatient unit literally was like a prison. the beds were uncomfortable, bathroom doors don't shut, etc. the breakfast is completely inedible every morning and i was left starving until lunch every day because of it. 

after getting out of here i felt worse than i did when i went in. please stay away.

went to the ear nose throat doctor across the street and was told to walk into financial services at tanner to get a quote on a possible procedure i might need. walk in and was told they couldn't do that, and was given a number to call. i call the number and the gentleman on the phone was baffled why they gave that number cause he just does scheduling. this hospital is trash. save your time/money/energy.

in the past week i have found myself in this emergency room 3 times. this place during basic admission seems to have no idea how to get the process moving along. as a result, every trip is a minimum of a 2 hour wait. on top of that, once you get to the back to be seen, they're just trying to get rid of you asap....after making you wait an hour after each person pokes their head in the room. i have a 92 year old grandma that couldn't be seen in over 5 hours while her muscle spasms were causing shortness of breath. if you have to go to an emergency source for healthcare i strongly recommend that you find one of the many local outside sources instead of this sad excuse for a hospital or you may not even live to regret coming here.

my mother in law has been in and out of the hospital for months with heart and lung issues.  the caretakers at huntington hospital are kind and compassionate.

she's been in the er, icu, and general rooming.  all the folks make a difference in the experience.  the facilities are nice and well kept.

my family and i will visit the café on the first floor.  they have quality food that tastes good and fairly reasonable prices.

extremely disappointed with how little informed the staff is, i've been jerked around on the phone for more than an hr. no one knows who i should speak with ?  don't you guys have my medical records? no one has the patience or heart to explain anything! they just want to transfer your call to another line that either won't answer or will hang up on me! looks like i'll have to come down there myself broken foot and all. this is ridiculous! if you have a choice, choose to go to another hospital, huntington hospital will only give you grief. 
*the nurses & doctors working the er are pretty nice, but the people behind the desks are useless!

i have a long history with the hospital, from family members, to my own admissions, to having friends work here, hmh and i go back a long way. it's a good hospital with good people and good care. i am not a very patient person and asking me to wait in a hospital for any reason is like nails on a chalkboard, but that has nothing to do with the staff or structure of the establishment, it's just me. 

the cafeteria has great food! 

the gift shop has a good selection and the lobby on the main floor is gorgeous. 

there is a starbucks inside, which makes things very convenient.

huntington hospital, the service is really attentive, clean and tidy, and the language translation. joseph y. li, director of obstetrics and gynecology, is also very friendly. i had a good boy there in may 2018 and the nurses in the inpatient department were very nice.  thank you very much.

unfortunately, it is with a heavy heart that i write this review. me, myself being a registered nurse. healthcare has to do better to provide a better patient experience for the money that we dish out for health insurance. 
i arrived at huntington er front desk clerk very friendly, i then went in to have my daughter triaged. i believe the nurse was hannah, she was wonderful. she interacted with my daughter very appropriate, her kindness kept my daughter mind off her symptoms. we were asked to go back to waiting room. finally, went in to be seen by md (3 chairs) in the corner with a curtain. i totally felt like i was having alterations done on some clothing. we were asked to return to waiting room. transporter arrived to walk us to ct, nice experience. we were placed back in waiting room for another hour, nurses did come around to offer blankets (very nice). after sitting for an hour, i asked front desk how much longer to go to back, they told me not much  longer. finally, we were called to go to back. however, we were placed in a cold interior waiting room. i had to ask for blankets. pa arriived  gave me results, informed me  that paperwork would be ready in a minute. nurse/ billing arrived 20 minutes to take me to a room that had a bed. i refused vs, i was just ready to sign out. however, billing clerk now wants to gather information after i have been waiting all that time. she said she needed address, then needed to run the insurance now. why wait till the very end, to start process??? i just handed insurance card and license to clerk and told her i would come back for them later. i was sooooo upset, i have been waiting alll that time, i'm sure someone could have obtain billing information. we have to do better. just a terrible experience.

was misdiagnosed and had dealt with the worst customer service ever. had severe stomach pain and so i went. i didn't have insurance so of course they treated me like a loser. the lady that deals with billing and insurance actually had the nerve to say " we won't treat you any different"... well darn i hope not. this is why private insurance needs to go away. people still matter and their issues are still important just because they can't afford the high prices for insurance.

took my mom here for a broken arm- she fell and needed to go to the er. the er staff seemed to be uninterested in helping my mom, particularly the rn staff made us feel like we were in the way (it was nye so i suppose they were busy) but we never felt like we were being cared for. i continually had to clean my moms bed and bathroom because the care staff was always too preoccupied for the 6 days my mom spent at huntington. next time i need to go to the er in pasadena ill just drive to dtla rather than waste time at this disorganised organisation

make sure when you are in this that you have all staff document everything. they lie on medical records. this hospital was in a class action law suit a couple years back for using dirty tools and patients dying if septic shock. be careful

as much as it pains me to give huntington hospital a low rating (because i adore and will no doubt give l&d, postpartum and nicu nurses a 5 star rating) the billing department is the total opposite. i have given birth july 2019, pre registered and gave all information they need before the scheduled csection yet still @ january 2020 my hospital bill hasn't been settled. not because of our lack of trying to get it settled (mind you, we even spoke with billing department supervisor to get our bill settled at one point) but its due to their incompetency. they tell us one thing but will do another. i do understand the billing process, and we are trying to expedite process by calling both insurance i have to help them. if any administrator will get a hold of this, i am in need of your help and will want to contact you about this matter.

er visit in just under 4 hours on a sunday afternoon.  3 hours and 50 minutes to get an xray. not sure how other ers compare speed wise, but the staff was friendly and gave me a face mask to help me avoid catching the seasonal flu virus many of the patients had.

this was my second labor and delivery at huntington hospital, however, this review is strictly for my l&d nurse, suzanna a. because she deserves the utmost recognition. although i had a good experience the first time giving birth in 2018 at huntington, this time was incomparable due to her care. she went above and beyond and exceeded all my expectations. she really took exceptional care of me, guided me, educated me on the induction process and never really left my side during labor. always asked me if i needed anything or how i was feeling (i wasn't feeling so great towards the end). when baby was born she reassured me everything was ok as we were experiencing a little bit of a complication after delivery. she made a worlds difference and i feel very lucky to have had her by my side when welcoming our second child into this world. this is the standard that huntington hospital should hold for all their nurses and she definitely lived up to it. i can't thank her enough!

i had the absolute best care from the nurses in every level of my visit. from the high risk maternity, icu and after care. the doctors also did everything they could to make me better. i wish i could see every single one of them again just to hug them and say thank you. i am so grateful. i thought i was not gonna leave there. and then maria stepped on. so, maria, hillary, bonnie, sona and medina.. that's just the beginning. i have a list of at least 20 nurses. it was hard to get them all. thank you all!!!! i am truly grateful for their care and work ethics.

my wife had an out patient procedure yesterday at huntington hospital. she is a cancer survivor so the lead up to the procedure was a time of anxiety for her. 

i must say that her anxiety was relieved by the attention from staff and the health care professionals that we interacted with in the 4 hours we were there. from adrian in the admitting office to the nurse, kaley, who attended to and prepared my wife for the procedure and to angela who tended to her recovery needs, we were thoroughly satisfied and pleased with the care and attention provided to us. 

we were equally impressed with the volunteers, alice and maria, who wheeled her to the main lobby for discharge. these two volunteers were happy and may have contributed to my wife enrolling as a volunteer herself at this hospital. 

our sincere appreciation goes out to the management and staff of this hospital for providing a most positive experience for us. my wife was 100% satisfied and grateful for the customer services provided to her at a very stressful moment. 

thank you all.

this hospital is phenomenal. i delivered my first son here and now have been in the hospital for almost a week with complications during my second pregnancy. everyone from the welcome desk and security to the on-call ob and nursing staff are just incredible. they are patient, kind, responsive, non-judgemental and go above and beyond. in fact, i used to live closer to this hospital and now come here all the way from sherman oaks because i trust the staff and it feels clean and safe here.

my wife was extremely sick so we went to the emergency room. waited over 2.5 hours and still never saw a doctor. there were people in the emergency room that were  actually leaving. after 3 hours we  chose to do the same. worst service in an emergency room i've ever had

i am in the waiting room in the emergency room right now and there are 2 women behind the desk at check in, just gossiping and and being rude and short to people. date 12/21/2019 at 4:50pm. we arrived at 4 and since then i have witnessed them being so rude to the patients and one patient even asked to speak to the supervisor and has not yet been able to speak with anyone they are just making her wait! this is the lost terrible patient care i have ever seen, the los angeles county hospital has better hospitality than this hospital does. i hope my grandmother gets moved to kaiser  her nurse is terrible as well do not want her to stay here.

huntington hospital saved my father's life...he was sent from a nearby nursing home after he stopped eating and drinking...his abdomen was swollen as if he were pregnant...he had been constipated due to pain killers given to him at the nursing home after he sustained a broken knee.  the team of doctors all talked to me very kindly and said they had never seen anything like this in their lives...one doctor actually put his hand up my dad's intestine and pulled out an 8 cm ball of dry poo....he was able to go for the next two days....this hospital is excellent at saving lives...it is excellent in geriatrics...

as the court appointed conservator for my (now deceased client), i was shocked to learn that the morgue at hmh is closed on sundays. this is absurd - my client died on a saturday evening. i contacted the mortuary requesting that they pick up her body - not possible on sunday. how is this possible - this is dreadful for loved ones whose religion requires immediate burial - is xenophobia or budgeting allowing this to continue?

huntington hospital has the worst billing practice and billing department of any hospital i've worked with in the past 20 years. expect them to lose your billing information or bill, pretend to submit your bill to insurance without doing so, screw up your billing insurance processing, give your insurance the run around, lie about submitting the bill to your insurance multiple times, lie to you about the status of your bill in the billing process, act rudely and condescending to you when you call in about the bill. i've been struggling and fighting with huntington hospital's billing department for 6+ months about submitting my hospital bill to insurance so i can pay it using fsa, its already january and the fsa cutoff is almost up. just got off my 20th call between the hospital and insurance, billing submission to insurance is still not resolved.

i had a baby at huntington hospital 7 months ago. i was excited to deliver there because it's such a beautiful hospital ( at least outside and the lobby lol) and people speak so highly of it.

my experience with overlook started with labor & delivery. i was scheduled to be induced on a tuesday. i had been warned ahead of time that since i was an elective induction, i could be bumped if other medically necessary inductions or women in active labor came in that same day, which obviously i understood. however, the communication with labor & delivery that day was horrible. they kept asking me to call back every two hours to check in to see if they had a bed for me. when we would call them, it would take 10 minutes to get someone on the phone who could provide an update and then we find out in the afternoon that my doctor didn't even know i was on the schedule for an induction that day. i didn't get induced until the following day and i do have to say, once we were actually there, the nursing staff was great.

then i get moved to the mother baby unit, which was the most horrible experience. the first issue was that it was amazon rainforest hot in there the entire stay. we spoke with various staff members including engineering about lowering the temperature only to be told that the unit was already on their winter setting and nothing could be done about the temperature. however, for about 3 hours in the middle of the day, there was actually antarctic cold air that blew out of the heat/ac unit, which contradicted the fact that the unit was already on the winter setting. the cold air was a welcome temperature change given how hot it was in there the majority of the time, but even cheap motels have better climate control. 

the experience with the techs was horrible as well. the amount of times they came in to take my blood pressure, take blood, etc. was absurd and never coordinated with other tests being performed so someone was walking into my room to do something to me or my baby what seemed like 100 times a day at all hours of the day and night. while i know that this is somewhat just the way it is when you stay at a hospital, they typically weren't even nice about it, it was like we were just a job they had to do and move on to the next one.

here are two specific horrible tech experiences. 2 techs came in to help me get out of bed 12 hours after my surgery. obviously i struggled to get out of bed and they were essentially nasty to me about the fact that i was slow. i then asked if i had to get up to go to the bathroom again should i call for them or was i pretty much on my own to do it. seeing how unhelpful they were i figured this would be the case and sure enough, they told me i was on my own. 

another morning, it was about 4 am. myself, my baby, and my husband were all sleeping, which was pretty obvious considering the lights in our room were out. a tech walks in, turns all the lights on, and proceeds to stick me with a needle to take blood right as i woke up to see her doing so. again, if this was something that absolutely had to be done at that time, she could have at least been more considerate in warning us that she was going to be turning on the lights and taking blood instead of just storming in and waking us all up and not even telling me why you are there before sticking me. 

and i have to mention that since overlook is baby friendly, the baby is with you 24/7. so after having major surgery, you need to care for your baby, and then they come into your room 100 times a day so i probably slept for 5 minutes the entire stay. 

after having so many medical staff in and out of the room every day, the cafeteria staff also asked you to fill out the menus and then if you didn't get to it when they wanted it done, they were nasty to you about that. but then after meals were brought, the dirty trays would sit in the room for hours to the point where we would stick it outside the door just to get it out of the room. 

then the day of check out, they say to be ready to leave by noon, which we were more than happy to do since we couldn't wait to get out of there. but instead of having an actual discharge procedure and having our paperwork ready to go, we had to call the nurses station twice before the paperwork was brought to us and it was definitely after 12 and then the person at the nurse's station was nasty to my husband after we had to call a second time to see what the status of the paperwork was. all the while they make you pay for parking. my husband had to make a few runs home for some things and each time they made him pay. tens of thousands of dollars for a hospital stay and they nickel and dime you on the parking. oh but don't worry they validate you so you only pay 2$ instead of 7$. all in all my husband paid close to 16$ extra for parking in their overcrowded and dirty lot.

needless to say, this stay was miserable and i'd rather go through another actual c section surgery than have to stay another few days in the mother baby unit. the only reason i even gave two stars is because the majority of the nurses were good.

review:
i cannot believe that i am giving this hospital a one star, considering that i was born here in 1995. 

long story short, i brought my mom to the er here back in october because she was experiencing pelvic pain. the entrance is horrible... they make handicapped people and sick people pass through a metal detector, without acknowledging the illness that they are experiencing. the security guard made me pass through the metal detector three times and when she saw that i was upset,, she goes: "sir, sir let me scan you once more. i said to her, you already scanned me three times, my mom needs to see a doctor. she starts scanning near my belt/crotch area and i told her to back off, so i pushed my mom in the wheel chair over to the er.

the admissions office is full of miserable, negative people who appear to be angry all the time. i asked this one woman if i could show her our health insurance care and she goes: that's fine, honey. bring it back later. so an hour or so later, my mom gets her own bed in the er and tells me to go show them our insurance, before they send a huge bill to our house. i went back and the same lady who attended us began to scold me. she asked me why i did not register my mom with an admissions staff member inside. i told her that i was not aware that i had to do that. she goes, your mom will be charged $40k for services at the er today. i asked why? if we have insurance. it does not make sense. so i had to speak with one of their co workers who was nice enough to help me, but at the same time, had a disgusted face attitude as if she wanted to throw me into space.

now the er....  there were a few decent human beings working in there but there were two idiots working there that made me question: how the hell did you get a job here?
the first nurse who attended us, questioned why i was helping my mom walk into her room, if she has movement in her legs. i tell him, they took our wheelchair and she is a lot of pelvic pain, which is affecting her ability to walk normally. didn't bother to hold the door or help us and responded with an "oh".

the next nurse that helped me mom comes in: ma'am, when was the last you have seen a gynecologist? she responds 15 years ago, i had a hysterectomy done and i had both ovaries removed, due to fibroids in this hospital. she goes, you have an ovary and the ct shows that you have a 4cm mass on the ovary. we were really upset about what they found, but my biggest concern was that they did not bother to admit her, nor run a biopsy to determine if it was cancerous or not. she just said: take your mom to her pcp, they will help you out. i go, your not going to help her? she's in pain and you're not going to administer any morphine or pain killer? or prescribe pain meds? she says... no, it's not our specialty. ask your pcp to refer her to a gynecologist/oncologist. 

honestly, this hospital visit was horrible in so many ways, but it's like why do people get treated like a commodity in a hospital? i feel like patients are seen as an object of waste, rather than as a human being that needs all the attention and care that they deserve. what's more sickening is that private health insurances pay these hospitals to provide health services to patients, but many people will take advantage of that money and not help their patients.

my mom unfortunately has cancer but we know deep down that she will be healed by the lord. miracles do happen and no one deserves to receive medical negligence like my mom did from this dump. beware of medical negligence/medical malpractices. they account for 250,000 deaths each year. no one deserves to die this way. 

never will we ever set foot in this hospital.

came here after going around in circles chasing urgent care facilities that were open new years day.  my wrist was swollen and i was in a lot of pain after a terrible fall at heavenly.  my boyfriend (firefighter) stopped into the closest fire station to ask where i should go.  they sent us to renown.  so glad they did.  they entire staff was kind and fast. holy cow!   i was in and out in less than an hour with a terrible sprain and this is including x-rays and seeing the doctor.  he had such a pleasant demeanor and bedside manor.  the nurse grace was amazing as well. i hope i never have to visit an er on another ski trip.... if i do i hope they can compete with the amazing staff at this er!  thank you!

if i could give this so-called hospital a 0 i would. absolutely the worst doctor i have ever seen. i will never go back again! the doctor flat said. i don't know and would not ask for help!! after a 5 day stay nothing but our gp found it!!

i had my first kidney stone experience ever and was in so much pain i decided to call the ambulance to help take me straight to the emergency. worst mistake of my life...
3:00pm: the austin ems ambulance is a joke taking more than 30 minutes to arrive to pick me up, two heavy built male medical ems staff took me into the vehicle and started interviewing and collecting my information, taking their sweet time parking at one place not driving me to the hospital for another 30 minutes. i have to beg for pain meds and they gave a shot for it but poorly directed the needle causing me unbearable pain i literally scream from so much pain!
4:30pm: the ambulance arrived at st david's south austin er walk-in, to my surprise i did not immediately get to see the doctor but had to wait in line to be checked in! omg, the torturous wait and the unbearable pain. i asked if i can have a bed to wait, no, sitting hurts me so much i cried the whole time waiting...
5:30pm: i had to go the bathroom and they called my name finally but i was in too much in pain to run out so i crawled out slowly and they told me i have to wait again because they skipped me! why did they not check the bathroom???
5:50pm: they called my name i thought i was finally saved, but a nurse took me inside a chair just to collect my insurance info and gave me a name tag, then sent me back out to wait some more. i begged for more pain meds as the old pain meds worn out, no, they cannot give me any meds until i see a doctor...at this time i'm heavily considering laying on the floor due to so much pain. i threw up 3 times in the bathroom and was heavily dehydrated, i begged a nurse for some water, he said he will go get me some, he never came back...i had to drink some water from the bathroom sink to stay alive. i continued crying in pain waiting and no tears came out since i'm so dehydrated....
6:50pm: they called my name again i thought i was finally saved again, but this time they took me to a chair to put iv on me to draw my blood and get urine test only. the nurse lady was so incompetent she had to poke me twice to find my vein, the first time she was probing with the large needle giving me excruciating pain while watching how incompetent she was. she continued to probe me the second time i felt like i should just die already, blood splatters everywhere and i saw old blood stain under the chair...still refused to give me water but agreed to give me pain meds finally. i beg for a bed, no, they have no bed available and i have to continue to wait in the waiting area. i got fever chills after all the blood drawn and beg for a blanket, no, they can't give me blanket to prevent contamination...no water, no blankets, no ability to lay down, no time frame to see doctor, constant excruciating pain, i was ready to just die...
7:30pm: finally got a bed, right out in the hallway with a number on the hallway wall. still not allow me to drink any water, a new nurse came to take more blood samples from me, poking and probing at my small veins at multiple places half jokingly complained my vein was so tiny (i'm so dehydrated of course my vein is tiny!!!). gave me ct scans, and concluded i got kidney stone...
10:00pm: gave me some prescription drugs, made me signed a bunch of forms to pay medical bills when it comes and dismissed me...

i've never been treated so badly in my life! 5.5 hours of torture! austin ems and this er sees me as nothing but a number and an object to poke at and probe without feelings...gravely disappointed at the american health system, and to say we are fully prepared for covid19, what a joke!
fac_name: St David's South Austin Medical Center

review: if your professional staff had looked at the chest x ray that you charged for you might have spotted the lung cancer.  thanks again st david's!   you guys are the ............. of the medical profession.  think "creative billing."
fac_name: St David's South Austin Medical Center

review: when i first moved here, i had heard mixed things about st. david's. however, after spending over a week there, there truly aren't enough yelp reviews to ever match my gratification for st. david's hospital. last year, st. david's literally saved my life. i had a bad case of pneumonia and ended up in icu after my heart went into an episode that would've been fatal, had it not been for their fast response and prompt care. i ended up needing emergency heart surgery and was beyond terrified. however, the staff is absolutely incredible and you could not ask for doctors who are more compassionate, knowledgeable, and caring for their patients. they definitely eased my anxiety about everything. the surgery went amazing and i can't believe it's almost been a year since this all went down. despite the anxiety and pain surrounding my time there, they did everything possible to ensure that i was taken care of and as comfortable as could be. the nurses even bought me a blanket and coloring book from the gift shop, as i awaited surgery. the food wasn't bad either. st. david's is a gift from god and every time i drive by, i just thank my lucky stars that i was fortunate enough to have been there when i was. it's no wonder why people fly in from all over the country to get the same surgery that i did. i'm a firm believer that things happen for a reason and after undergoing the most horrific experience of my life, i'm beyond grateful to know that st. david's was there for me through it all. there's not a day that goes by that i don't give thanks for st. david's. so, if you're ever in town or know anyone who needs an amazing hospital, st. david's is your place. thank you, thank you, thank you!
fac_name: St David's South Austin Medical Center

review: what a terrible experience in their er. i bring my mother for emergency since her insurance covers that hospital permanently, but this is the awful experience that we would never forget. i can't believe that there is the er without any hospital personnel to check in in registration since that person is on break, and they have a security personnel to fill into the position. we are told to wait if that is not that emergency. seriously? the funny part is that even the security personnel who sat there told me that it is not right and encouraged me to contact the customer service to file the complaint. my mother is extremely angry, ask to get in immediately and contacted the customer service to ask for additional service with her injured eye. that's how i can explain how bad they are. no way!

my mother was in this hospital for a week, and it was the worst experience we've ever had at a hospital.  she started in the er and was eventually admitted to the icu.  overall, there was no sense of urgency among the staff.  when she threw up blood in the er, i seemed to be the only one to react.  the aide took a long time to clean her up because she was too busy laughing and talking with another aide.  the nurse took even longer to evaluate her because "he was so busy."

in the icu, no one responded to the nurse's bell, we had to go to the nurse station every time to have someone address concerns for my mom.  even then it was a long wait for someone to come to the room.  the medical staff was so unprofessional.  i saw an aide and maintenance worker play fighting and wrestling in the hallway outside of my mom's room. the staff openly and loudly talked negatively about patients, visitors and their own coworkers in the middle of the hallway.  

my mom is bed bound and cannot go to the bathroom on her own.  one evening, i got there and found her soaked in urine.  it took over an hour for an aide to come change her after going to the nurse station multiple times to ask for assistance.  when the aide came, she started to change my mom without closing the door or pulling the privacy curtain.  my mom's bed was closest to the door.  i asked her to give my mother some privacy as people were walking back and forth in the hall. she shrugged her shoulders and said "it's mostly employees in the hallway."  i told her that's irrelevant and closed the door myself. 

the doctors did not return my calls when i left messages asking for an update on my mother.  the only time i spoke to them was when they were calling for consent to do a procedure and only then i was able to ask about her condition.  i work during the day so by the time i went to see her in the evening, i was met with nurses who couldn't tell me  much about her ongoing treatment plan.  i was not made aware of her discharge either, i got a call from the nursing home one morning saying that she was back in their facility.

waited over 2 hours. my medical condition was serious and i almost died.  they refused to update my correct name. they had "no beds" but could have moved me to ob or taken blood while waiting.  they don't care and aren't professional.

with  the deepest appreciation  i wanna thank each and everyone one of you for coming to a busy doctors rescue. dr singh your sharpness and diagnostic skills and delivery deserve an emmy. the traveling nurse, lisa i believe you made me laugh the entire time while not being able to breath that well. the  triage nurse, damn you work fast but very caring! and last the  the security guard for recognizing my urgency at 3 am. man you deserve a metal. ok....i believe my point is taken...i picked up my meds, returned and finished seeing my patients  and successfully heading home. to my family. my appreciation to you all! dr. j

salinas valley memorial hospital is an old hospital that has become much to small for a city the size of salinas.
the waiting area in the emergency department is a very small area cramped with chairs and numerous people waiting to be seen. as i sat there waiting i felt as if i was in a third world facility. i was surrounded by non english speakers many of which had numerous children with them. the waiting area is also dirty and not very comfortable.
after having my vitals taken i was then brought back into the hallways near the emergency department. i was triaged in the hallway and told to wait on a shitty cheap folding chair until a room became available.
the first emergency department room i was placed in already had another patient with her family in the room. the only thing seperating us was the flimsy curtain.
this patient and her family were obnoxious and loud laughing and making alot of noise. i finally blew up and told them to shut the fuck up. after me yelling i was then removed and placed in a private room.
the staff at this hospital are terrific some of the finest i have experienced. however my reasons for this 2 star rating has to do with the dirty waiting area and then being placed in a hallway on a cheap folding chair while waiting for an available room.
it is pretty pathetic.
what's more disturbing is the fact that this old hospital is to small as well as being outdated to handle the large city population of the salinas valley.

people are kinda rude

but the place is pretty nice though compared to other hospitals

i went to check in the er. there were a few people there and the clerk didn't ask why i needed to be seen.   he was security. he took my name and told me to sit down. i am two days past surgery and my in call doc thinks it might be blood clot. it appeared everyone else was here for cold /flu but you wouldn't know because security was doing the check in. unbelievable

my ophthalmologist told me to stop by an er asap while i was traveling home due to some eye issues i was having. i'm two hours from home and have been in the er for nearly three hours. doctor said that ophthalmologist left for the day and to come back the next day. i would have been much better off driving home to my local hospital. im not sure how much longer i will sit here before they release me. they say i might have a tear in my retina. nothing conclusive. i'm sitting in a room with six other patients who are waiting to be released. one man said that he has sat in this room for three hours before. they have checked my vitals twice. technician said he has no idea when i will be released. this was a waste of time as well as a waste of my er copay. it seems that this hospital al can't handle the patient load.

facility was definitely outdated, but all will change for the better as the new hospital is nearly complete.

fast, thorough and clean er. medical professionals were kind and caring. a  student doctor who spoke to me, asked great questions and although i hadn't mentioned a genetic issue i should have considered, he keyed into a potential issue that my dad has had for 30 years and likely i may have. i will need further testing to confirm, but am relieved to have an avenue to pursue. the physician also felt what i was experiencing was what the student had concluded. greatly relieved after my er visit.

excellent hospital experience super attentive staff they all seem authentically care about patients my mom was very confused she is 87 years old the doctor took time out to call me in florida and discuss the entire case and the situation where my dad with me so i can explain it to my mom excellent service real professionals here from the people who clean the room to the doctors they all have a smile on their face and know what they're doing all the equipment and machinery is top-notch very clean hospital would recommend to anyone

just recently found out apparently our daughter was not covered even though we we told she was. we paid copayments as expected and never thought about anything else. until we just got a bill saying the first visit was $40+ plus a $300+ for a new patient! $2,000 for a mri and multiple $200+ fees for reading the results!

we still don't know what is wrong with our daughter but cannot afford to come back here! we trusted all was covered since our dr referred us and the ladies at check in advised our insurance was accepted. 

the people are super great but unfortunately we are one of the patients that are just "business" for them.  so while i applaud them for being a childrens hospital i advise you to watch your billing nothing is what you are told. we had given 5 stars here and referred friends here now i have to follow up and make sure they are not in the same situation.
sick babies shouldn't have to wait 5 hours in the er before being seen. inexcusable!

we had only been to the er once three years ago, and being the only ones there, we were happy with everything. now, i rushed there with a patient having stroke symptoms. we were taken right in. the professionalism was astounding. not having  much medical knowledge, i couldn't have been happier with the triage, questions asked of us, and the communication between the doctors and nurses to us. up on the floors the staff again were great. they were busy with us and educated us. nighttime was noisy and the patient was checked often. the meals were quite good. hillcrest has two buildings. in the older one the rooms are very small. there is barely space for a chair. the bathroom is large. in the newer building the rooms are large with room for a visitor or two. elevators have letters and signs to help visitors get around, but it is confusing for newcomers. there is a lot of walking to get to offices and patient rooms. be patient. wear walking shoes. take reading material.

i spent several days here with my grandfather in the icu. the rns here are entitled and seem completely unapologetic to their patients problems. 
our cna was very sweet and took the utmost care of us. the doctors did well at explaining the issues and updating us when possible. the reason i can only muster of a 2 star review is by just how terrible my family was treated by the rns. the hospital itself is beautiful and modern and parking is a breeze. these rns need to come back down to earth though.

doctors in the emergency department are horrible - constant misdiagnoses, as has been my experience on multiple visits over the years. if you have to go there, good luck. the nurses and technicians however, are lovely.

i was taken to er and then admitted for surgery. i was there for 4 days. i was very pleased with all of the staff, nurses and doctors. they were all very courteous and well trained to attend to all my needs...not just medical. 
omg!! the food was fantastic! i would definitely recommend them.
this is the worst hospital i've been been too!!! lack or urgency and poor communication. don't come here unless your on your death bed. because you will be before your see.

this place is crooked as heck. double charged me. double charged. got 7 different bills for one stay. all charging me for the same thing advent charged me for.  took advantage of someone that was on pain medication. took me from an out patient without telling me . did test without consent. 
i was turned down for financial help.
