have called 14 times asking for them to take us off there mailing list and still getting them 41 mailing have been sent back. bunch of crooks. they should run for office.

new to this insurance. saw a family practioner and had blood work done.  saw an orthopedic and had x- rays done. they also scheduled an mri and made sure it was authorized under my plan which is advent health. as a matter of fact, all these services were done under advent health. you would think that billing would fall under an advent health central location. after all they want your copay, deductible or coinsurance before you have any services. not so. they call it precheck when they call you to get you to pay for your service instead of pre pay. i had a deductible to meet and paid it. the payment took care of my deductible except for 92 cents. well the radiology department has not sent the bill to be processed. so in the mean time all the other bills have been sent and processed under the deductible. will now have a credit and who knows how much because they haven't sent the bill to process. they would not see me unless i paid and they don't even know how much i owe. now all the billing will be going to the deductible until the radiology bill processes. it's hard enough to keep track of everything especially when you are sick. very wrong and messed up billing system. the patient gets taken advantage of financially here. so messed up and wrong!

thank you for correct diagnosis of my sister, your time and attention to get needs are truly appreciated and will never be forgotten. i'm grateful for the blood work done and the assessment turned out to be sleep deprivation. sending a huge hug to the doctor that treated nh67700.

re: dr. ken thompson  

november the 26th, my family decided it was over due that i see a doctor.  after breaking my shoulder last year, i never wanted to go to an emergency room again. 

i was not at home in ovilla, texas, but at my lake home in oklahoma. i do not have a physician here. after being sick with a horrific stomach virus for 7 straight days, i was miserable. 

upon arrival at the emergency room, i ran inside like a wrecking ball to continue my illness. thank you jesus, for er nurse rebecca and dr. thompson. i was so sick the whole time they patiently attended to me. they never stopped being attentive to me as i profusely apologized for my sick stomach. 

i had dehydrated with a virus that last from 9 to 10 days. i was finally on the down side, but could not keep nothing on my stomach. 

after an iv and meds, i finally felt better. i should of gone to a doctor sooner. i just kept thinking it was a 24 hour bug that kept on lingering. 

kudos to dr. thompson, you made me feel comfortable during my illness. i am so grateful to him and nurse rebecca. 

i was good as new on thanksgiving!  thank you both, including the warm staff at registration. 

i definitely would return!

review:

security came out and help me roll her in.

one nurse or receptionist, not sure of her position, ran out to help a very young, crying boy wheel his mother who had a broken foot into the er.

unfortunately i cannot rate this place less than 1 star. this was the absolute worst experience i've ever had at a hospital. i had done something to my jaw last night and couldn't really move it because it felt so loose... my face swole up and my lips were numb. i was freaking terrified because a. i hate hospitals... and b. i'm a hypochondriac. 
so i walked in, wasn't greeted. explained my situation to a nurse who was genuinely nice... then the biggest piece of human waste walked in. i wish i remembered her name. she basically interrogated me for 30 mins about information that didn't effing matter considering i was almost passing out every 2 minutes. it was obvious i was out of it and i got 0 concern from her. 
during this interview, the nurse kept telling me to talk louder (dude my jaw??) and was the most condescending person, acting like i was some inferior adolescent child. she had me sit in a chair asking me all this stuff and i'm like hey can we do this after? i was obviously concerned. i literally said "i'm about to pass out i feel very numb. my vision is blurred.. i have earaches" and she would just ignore me and continue.

for example: 111 county road 1111 houston, tx

and when i was leaving i followed her because i assumed she would show me out and she turned around and was like "do you need something?" 
moral of the story: screw this place

i went to sinai grace hospital to see a very sick friend and the staff was terrible, but the most horrible thing about the visit was the fact that a dying patient dinner request for orange juice was not available because  the hospital did not have orange juice (really)! 
the hospital only had water available for the patient (really)  imagine if this was your family member or friend.
this is a hospital that you never want to go to ever! 
oh, i forgot about the metal detector that you have to go through like at the airport.

i wouldn't bring stuffed animals to this hospital to have their plastic eyes glued on.  nearly 7 years after my initial review and they still don't have their $hit together. my father recently visited the er due to elevated bp.  personnel bickered about availability of equipment to perform an ekg and he observed someone actually hide a machine. he became disgusted and left without being evaluated.

respect the medical profession enought to consider that human beings are coming here for compassionate care, and they represent more than an invoice!!

please do not go to this hospital,  my loved one went there with extreme back pain and was waiting for 6 hours before he had his mri and just to be sent home and told nothing was wrong, he went back 3 times in pain and the lady at the front desk said you are back again, how rude, its not like somebody wants to come back three times for the same issues that wasn't addressed the first time, he ended up having a herniated disk and had to have an operation, i felt so bad for him and i begged him to go to another hospital but unfortunately he didn't want to start the procedure over because of the pain and time, the surgeon did a great job on his back but he ended up going back again for the same issue a year later with excruciating pain with the same run around before getting the help he needed.  you would think a repeat patient would at least get decent treatment.  without patients the hospital wouldn't make money so please treat your patients with respect and dignity.

my dad went and was given the run a round and i told him to go to a better hospital and he did and they were able to help him and found out he had congestive heart failure and the other hospital treated him respectfully and there was no going back and forth, here it is 3 years later and he is doing great.

oh also my nephew went there with meningitis and they treated him like a dog he ended up running out of the hospital in his gown, he ended up in emergency at a different hospital and they told him if he was one minute later he would of died.  how can this hospital continue to operate!!!  i'm calling labor relations today 1-2-2020.

something needs to be done with this hospital either fire the front desk workers, retrain them on how to give excellent customer service, send the doctors back to college or just close the whole damn hospital down!!!.   i mean this from the heart.

i myself went to sinai grace emergency january 8 2020 what i noticed was that the room's in the er doesn't have call buttons for the patient so i asked a nurse why she said that they removed them because of the mentally ill patients ok that's a dangerous move what about the patients that's not mentally ill people what happened if a patient or myself really need a nurse and we don't have a call button this hospital really needs to off people better quality care. another thing is that i want to complain about is that i had an iv put in my arm my arm was swollen and painful so i asked the nurse could she take the iv out for me she told me that she had to check on another patient and she will be back she never came back so what i did was pulled the damm iv out myself so i went across the hallway to use the bathroom the same nurse asked me did someone remove the iv i didn't respond to her but i close the door in her face lord behold this unprofessional skank call me a crazy bitch that's right this nurse her name was latasha i didn't respond but i recognized her voice this is a bad hospital no respect bad nurses and so forth there has to be some changes at this place i've heard nothing but negative things over the years about this dark hell hole of a place.

this review is for the information desk at 75 francis st main lobby. i was having trouble finding the office location of a new physician. so, i went to the information desk. i asked the woman if she could please tell me where the dr's office was located. she replies, "let's start with your name." not knowing why, i told her my name. she types in my first name and then asks me for last name again. what the hell??

i tell her to forget it and walk away. why the hell does she need to type in my name???? try answering the simple question!! don't make this more difficult than this is. and why does my name need to be captured? what was to have been done with that info?

this is just towards their emergency room:

our family has had kaiser for years. we live in west la and they have a pediatric urgent care which is great. we were on vacation at disneyland for a week and my son got a very painful ear infection. this was the closest kaiser. we made our way in only to find out that not only do they not have a pediatric urgent care, but they don't have an urgent care at all here. so we took our son into the emergency room. it was more than a two hour way while there was barely a handful of people in the waiting room. the staff has no sympathy or sense of urgency. i could not imagine how they'd handle a real emergency situation. more than a two hour wait with a screaming child and we finally make our way inside. the doctor comes out to look at him for less than a minute and then offers us a flu shot. get out of here! a flu shot? my son is in pain and needs antibiotics and pain reliever! the entire process dragged and they left a lot to be desired. this kaiser, unfortunately, sucks. don't know how else to say it. keep driving to another location if you're able to. even with traffic and a wait time, they will still take care of you faster elsewhere.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Orange County - Anaheim Medical Center

review:
kp anaheim is probably the busiest kp facility i have visited to-date. they have an information booth to answer general questions and a huge lobby with plenty of chairs. the layout of medical building 2 is a bit confusing. there aren't a lot of signs so ask for help like i did if you are not familiar with its layout. care provided by staff here is as good as i received at other kaiser facilities. no complaints.

parking can be challenging. there is a multilevel parking structure but it is pretty full as i found out today. 

beware phone signals (at&t) is rather weak inside the building. i had to walk out to make a call. i couldn't receive texts while inside either.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Orange County - Anaheim Medical Center

review:
so i went to the er around 8:30pm and stood in line. i was the only one in line and the intake nurse just sat there typing on her computer. she was obviously busy but didn't even acknowledge me. then when she did call me to her, i told her that i was sent by a kaiser doctor to the er and it was prearranged. the er doctor (dr. ly) and my primary care doctor had already spoken to each over the phone. i told her my diagnosis was on my chart with my medical record number. she ignored what i said and just said you have to get on the scale. i told her that there are other patients standing here and their family members. there is no privacy. i don't want to talk in front of other patients nor do i want them see my weight and listen to my medical diagnosis. she began yelling at me saying i don't know what is your problem is. i can't give you medicine unless i weigh you in front of all these people. then she proceeded to get up and move the scale by another nurse which was still by other patients and said to me it's in kilograms so i don't know why you are so worried that other people hear or see your number. by then i was utterly embarrassed and taken aback that kaiser had such an unprofessional woman/ nurse talking to patients this way. i would complain to the head of er but i have a feeling it will fall on deaf ears. my purpose in writing this review is to inform you of the quality of care given at this facility especially at the er. avoid this place. kaiser customer service has fallen! it's like a run of the mill county hospital.

update: 3/11/18
the er department totally redeemed themselves on today's visit. from the time i entered the er, i was treated with the upmost respect. the intake nurse was kind and genuinely attentive. i was updated every 10 minutes as to what was going with my case, x-rays etcetera. i was in and out within an hour!!! yes, thank you kaiser. my care was seamless. everyone did a fantastic job including the x-ray technician. 5 stars!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Orange County - Anaheim Medical Center

review: i have been admitted to this beautiful hospital many times. the hospital is always spotless and used state of the art medical equipment. the nurses, lab technicians, respiratory therapists, and all of the other supporting staff were all very knowledgeable and caring.  98% of the drs took the time to talk to me and explain treatments etc. because i'm admitted so often, many of the nurses are like family. i really like this hospital very much. #kaiserpermenente
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Orange County - Anaheim Medical Center

review:
i took my roommate to the er on christmas eve, she was experiencing a crone attack ( she was in severe pain and vomiting violently ) 1st the tech saw her right away took her vitals says they are okay? okay? she's bent over wrenching and he valuate her vitals are fine? 
she continues to wretch they ignore her. 

now i is see a patient in a wheel chair and her foot is bleeding  onto the floor. their is only a security  guard at a podium positioned in front of doors. no hospital staff. 

i worked in hospitals and currently a cancer patient and have been in & out of er's the last 2 years ( not kaiser ) and never have i seen a security guard in charge of  checking in patients, making decisions who is seen and who has staff respond to waiting patients and updating status of patients in waiting. 

i even spoke with him and expressed concern that she was worsening and could we see a staff?

review: my mother has been having some dementia type issues and had a short stay at linden oaks in january. at that time dr. chandra changed her medication which really helped. 10 months later, my mother is very confused again to the point she's not even sure where she is sometimes in her own home. i called linden oaks the night before i planned to take my mother in and described what was happening and was told to bring her in the next morning. i took my very confused mother there and we went through the evaluation only to be told the doctor they consulted with was refusing her admission. i got very irate and asked how they could send someone so confused (and hallucinating) back to her home alone, as i said she could walk out some night like she did once before and their response was 'but she hasn't yet'. it's nice to know that linden oaks feels being extremely confused, hallucinatory and even overdosing ones self, not a life-threatening or safety risk!!  they wasted our time for nothing and they dont even tell you which useless dr denied her admittance. i will definitely hold linden oaks personally responsible for anything that happens to her in the meantime before another doctor can see her. i don't know how those people live with themselves. i would give them zero stars if i could. so keep in mind if you ever decide to take a loved one there, even if it's not the case, apparently you have to say they're going to hurt themselves or someone else or tell them they've done something to put themselves at huge risk. it's sad that obviously people have to sometimes embellish to get the help they need. their parameters are a joke!!! and yes my mother does have a caregiver but no one can watch someone every single moment. they could have got her stabilized in a few days and then referred her to a psychiatrist. but they offered zero help instead. total fail!!
fac_name: Linden Oaks Behavioral Health - Main Campus

review:
i think this hospital and service got better, thanks a few years ago. there is only one draw back is their reconstruction. the project is lasting too long and i heard that it would take a few more years. 
another inconvenient is sharing with me my mom's situation. i know its the policy of the hospital not to disclose anything, but suggesting to come in person its ridiculous, especially when i am 2 hours away.
otherwise the staff and nurses are great.

i was 35 weeks and 5 days pregnant when i visited this hospital.
i was at home when i felt intense pain in my lower uterus. i didn't know what it was but i knew for sure it 1.) was not labor because it was an isolated spot and not my entire uterus and 2.) wasn't normal because it felt like a chainsaw or a fire inside me, like i was being ripped apart from the inside.
this hospital is a half mile away from my house so it was convenient to come here. the nurses in l&d were extremely sweet and tried their best to console me even though i was screaming my head off. i was hooked up to monitors but not an ultrasound so all they saw was contractions but didn't see what was going on inside me. they assumed i was in early labor, when i actually wasn't (but they did not find that out until after my delivery 5 hours later, so i 100% don't blame them for thinking i was). they administered 3 shots of some safe drug to slow down labor but it didn't make a difference (again, because i wasn't in labor) so they admitted me to a delivery room. i was offered an epidural and didn't hesitate to scream yes.
the epidural changed everything and now i was a happy camper. the delivery doctor, dr. renan, came in to tell me gently "we might might have to do a c section, because the baby's heart rate is dropping with each contraction, but we might not, we will see what the ultrasound reveals." i was hoping that wasn't true at all, as a c section delivering a preemie was not at all in my vision. i waved it off and said ok whatever. the us revealed my placenta was almost 80% detached (this is called a placental abruption) so he kindly told me he would "try to speed up my labor to get this baby out naturally". he was about to leave the room when my water broke all on it's own on the bed. it was 10% water and 90% bright red blood. with a smile on his face (to calm me down) he said in a sweet, caring tone, "ok, your placenta is detached, we are doing an emergency c section, it will be ok!" i began bawling and saying i didn't want that but the nurses told me it needed to happen. (i later found out 3 hours postpartum that i was actually 5 minutes from death at that moment, but they didn't want to act frantic to scare me more, which i really appreciate!!) 
within minutes i was in the or and they were cutting me open. fortunately i felt nothing. i kept looking at my husband telling him i was scared i would feel pain and then suddenly i heard my daughter squeak and the other surgeon said "baby is out". i hadn't even felt it! crazy! after they gave her oxygen and saved her life, they brought her to my face so i could kiss her and tell her i loved her. we locked eyes. she was perfect. my husband then followed her to the nicu while i was stitched up. 
first of all - my incision is amazing!!! i'm 12 days pp as i type this and i'm completely out of pain, and the scar is like 5 or 6 inches and so thin it's not even noticeable. it's still a little bruised but as soon as those go away i'm 100% confident no one will ever know i had abdominal surgery this summer when i'm in a bikini. i couldn't be more grateful to dr. renan for acting quickly and professionally to save our lives, and at the same time make it a cosmetic procedure to ensure i'd still have a slamming body afterwards. then there was the nurse who stayed with me in the recovery room for 2 hours after the surgery. she talked to me like we were best friends and made sure i was emotionally stable until my husband came back. she didn't leave me for a second. i felt so safe with her. her name was lilley.

nicu:  the nurses are friendly, answer all questions, are extremely respectful to parent wishes, informative, & amazing with preemie babies. i love all of them. especially lily & christine
my daughter was there for 7 days. during her stay i only left for several hours at a time to sleep in my own hospital room. once i was discharged i spent the next 3 nights on the couch in her room so i could bf her. they just let you sleep in your baby's room there! it's amazing! 
like i said, they respect parent wishes - i said no bath for 2 days, they obliged. i said no pacifiers, they said ok. i said bf only, they never gave her formula.

every day i was there i was visited by a lactation consultant to help me feed her. every other day a social worker came in to talk to me about my feelings like a therapist. i had an extremely traumatic week having an unexpected delivery, a c section, and a nicu baby. i was traumatized by the situation - not by anyone who helped me and my daughter. in fact, the only reason i'm not currently cookoo insane right now is because of how everyone treated me. everyone was so gentle, so sweet, so informative and respectful.... i'm just over the moon appreciative for everything they all did for me. i can never pay them back.

in the past i would have given mercy one-star on a good day. i have had several bad experiences and was not too keen on the place.
that has changed. i have been diagnosed with stage 4 colon cancer that has spread and is basically terminal. after being off chemo for several months i began to experience some issues and thought i was blocked. i went to the er, referred from the cancer center and with some trepidation, on a friday morning, 9ish.
i was the only person in the waiting room so my wait time was obviously short (5 minutes). i was taken back and put in a room by a very pleasant young lady who then tool my blood pressure, temperature & blood oxygen. she left, saying someone would be with me shortly. within 5 minutes i had a nurse in my room discussing my symptoms. she was very pleasant and put me at ease. after completing her assessment she informed me the doctor would be with me shortly and left. 
within 10 minutes i had the most pleasant er doctor i have ever encountered at mercy, wade fox, do (and a bunch of other letters). from the moment he walked into the room he had me smiling. he discussed what was going on with me, but we also talked about books/movies and he totally took my mind off my pain and at one point actually had me laughing! my husband was totally amazed as he had had several visits to mercy in the past as well that were not favorable.
after fluids, meds and a few tests it was determined i was not blocked, but close. i had to see my oncologist and resume chemotherapy.
the thing that impressed me the most was the fact that the er doctor, wade fox, actually called me at home to check on me and see if i was ok. amazing!
i do not have private insurance, i am on medicare. i was treated with dignity and respect and i commend the er staff. by the time i was discharged almost every room was full and there were quite a few people in the waiting room as well, but my level of service never changed from the start.
one thing i have discovered: your attitude can affect your level of care. no one wants to go out of their way to help a mean person. please and thank you go a long way. just saying...

i could go back years about the horrible things that have happened here.  a nurse tried to give me a bed bath - with the door open - and when i objected, she told me to shut up.  i almost died during my pacemaker implant.  my husband had cirrhosis not related to alcohol abuse.  the floor charge nurse stood outside his room loudly talking about "these lousy drunks abuse their bodies for years then show up here expecting us to help them."  i'm not sure which offended me more - her complete and utter lack of compassion or the absence of medical knowledge because many things can and do cause liver damage besides booze.  the next oops by mercy was the analysis of of the mri's of my husband's knee after his knee replacement.  it said, "no obvious change from previous study."  apparently that big new titanium knee doesn't constitute a 'change' at mercy.  

more recently, my husband was taken there by ambulance after experiencing severe chest pains and weakness.  one of their employees began throwing a fit outside his room in the er because, "why do we have to deal with these veterans?  why doesn't the va spend them someplace else??"  she was the first person in a long time to make him feel ashamed of serving his country.  this attitude to me is especially disturbing because the va recently closed their er and all patients are told to go to the mercy er.  veterans who experience this type of outright anti-veteran bias are likely to leave and not get medical care.  her attitude will likely kill someone if it hasn't already.  in addition to being a disabled veteran, he has ample health insurance so we can seek medical care anywhere.  sadly, the remainder of the visit was bad.  the pa who saw him sent him home with a diagnosis of 'stable angina'.  you know it's going to be wrong when the guy who gives you the diagnosis can't pronounce 'angina'.  to mercy er - here's a common sense tip from a layman - the angina is not stable when the patient is popping nitro like candy and not getting any relief.  it should come as no surprise that he was admitted to icu at sacred heart riverbend a couple days later and had open heart surgery.  this time i skipped the ambulance and drove him myself.  we also know two other men who went to mercy with classic heart symptoms (nausea, shortness of breath, dizzy, left arm pain) who were told they were ok and sent home.  they both died.  

after the open heart surgery he went to mercy for heart surgery rehab.  most of that went well but their dietician is horrible.  she abused my husband terribly about the supplements he had been told to take by his specialists after his liver transplant.  he told her he's been told to take them by the transplant team but that didn't stop her.  she'd tell him every chance she got that he was going to die of cancer because of a vitamin.  he finally refused to see her anymore because she upset him.  dear dietician - practice your bedside manner.  yelling at a patient and telling him he's going to die is probably not your best choice when dealing with a heart patient.  

if you can, do like we do and seek help at either sacred heart riverbend in springfield or ohsu in portland.  if it's important or involves breaking skin, we avoid mercy like the plague.

my review is specifically for my labor and delivery experience. i was having my first child, so needless to say i was nervous and had no idea what to expect. my labor and delivery nurses were marina and madison and they were phenomenal!!!! they made my labor and delivery experience so positive and memorable for myself, my husband and our families. they were so attentive and on the ball with everything! they were both so friendly and made me feel comfortable immediately. marina was very encouraging and she made sure i was constantly being preoccupied and not concentrating on contractions, which was awesome and very needed! i am so happy that i had these 2 to bring my son into the world and i couldn't have asked for a better experience! all thanks to marina and madison

i was directed by my child's pediatrician to head directly to onslow memorial hospital's er because they suspected a ruptured appendix and they even called ahead to warn them we were heading in and get the surgeon on call ready. we sat 7 and a half hours in the er before we saw a doctor and even longer before we saw a surgical team who wanted to get my child in the or within 20 min and we would be "delaying care" if we didn't get my child to the or immediately, plus my child was not stable enough to have been transferred. we subsequently agreed to have the or team take him into emergency surgery and spent many days in that horrid place with sub par care before i had my child transferred out to continue care and get stable and home. i wouldn't even have given them one star if not for the surgical team nurses and the anesthesiologist. do not go to onslow memorial hospital if you can make the drive to wilmington or greenville for your care.

i brought my daughter and myself in because we thought we may have caught the flu. we were out of town during christmas. so we got in and immediately experienced one of the most awful experiences from rude female nurses. i was asked if i took drugs several times and responded no each time. i am sick so i do look rough but no need to ask me 5 times if i am a drug addict!. my 4 year old daughter the whole time hearing this and the rude nurse saying we "should have" gotten the flu shot. they kept pushing the flu shot on us and we just don't do the flu shot for our own reasons. my family does not do flu shots but we do vaccinate other shots. so then the test was said to be 50% accurate. do you know how much money we spent to come to the er!? the nurse said i waited to long to come in treating me like a crap mom not knowing we were traveling out of town. then she demanded i take my daughter today to her her pediatrician to get her flu shot which if she had any sense she would know they dont give you the flu shot if you are already sick. so we met some of the most arrogant and prideful staff who obviously are more concerned with being right or thinking they are right than patient care and empathy! we will drive to the base hospital next time and will not come back here to the er.

this is more for my doctors office than the  hospital.  i will include the hospital. my doctor is dr. amy buchanan and she is the bomb!!!!!!   atomic!  bomb. com. have been seeing her for over ten years and no matter what my issue is she is there  to make it a non issue. she makes sure that i am  a part of the process. she teaches me as she diagnoses me. love that about her. 

the hospital i is blah.  needs better signage bit overall it's there for the community. i wish they would add pediatric dentistry.

my 76 year old father was admitted here for gallbladder surgery suddenly and we were worried because we weren't familiar with the hospital as my family had just moved nearby. naturally i was worried reading some of the negative reviews but we had a pleasant experience. the or room might be different than er but staff and nurses were very friendly and accommodating! the surgeon himself came out to let us know of a successful surgery and he was very vibrant and nice as well. clean facility, could use more light and maybe some decor in lobby waiting areas but all in all a good experience!!

do not have any surgical procedures performed at this hospital! my husband underwent wrong site surgery at this hospital. i gained copies of all his records - proving that the surgeon admitted he did not perform the correct procedure. i filed a grievance with the medical board and was basically told "too bad - pay all the bills anyway." terrible hospital. incompetent staff. stay away.

* my grievance was filed through patient relations, which is the only way to file a grievance. i am unsure why the hospital responded to my review by asking me to contact patient relations again. further proof of their ineptitude. just trying to show the public that they are "helping" but it is no help at all.

horrible service! er nurse ivette was really rude! i do not like going to hospitals unless necessary. i have been sick for two weeks now. my primary doctor called me today and per cdc regulations she was told i should go to the er and get tests done. i followed her instructions and headed to gotlieb. i didn't expect them to test me for coronavirus. because obviously they need to rule everything else out first..... the nurse insisted that she didn't understand why my doctor would sent me there and said they couldn't do much for me. not just was she not careful when doing my swaps but she has a nasty attitude the whole time, acting like i was a bother. after waiting a while a provider came in to my room and i explained how rude her nurse had been and that i did not appreciate how harsh she did my swabs and the things she said. she apologized for the nurses attitude and insisted it was good that i went and that they would do the tests necessary. she left and the next person that visited me was the same nurse with her smirk face on to discharge me. they couldn't do anything for me and i should follow up with my primary health provider. she is a rude person and obviously in the wrong profession. also i understand that there is a lot going on with the whole virus thing but all i want is to go back to work!!!! and i need to do everything i'm asked to go back to work... our health system is failing and we need better service not this crappy hospital . next time i'll just go elsewhere never again

i'd suggest this hospital it's a really good hospital i went here for an emergency  and they got me in right away and was able to go home the next hour they are fast with doing things and the correct way i've always been going to this hospital they are good
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center GlenOaks

review:
spend one day with us is their motto ...try spend 3 ...unorganized and everything takes forever... dr and team fail to return calls ...would love to  back great lakes (old ccs)...one division is unaware of the others workings

weekend appt. given to us - limited security, no valet, no help at main desk

unfortunately had to go to their ed last week. never wanted to go but it's the only game in town. i have a kidney transplant and really need to be seen right away because of being immune deficient. took vitals then nurse left saying she'd be right back. yeah, after an hour. i had to sleep there overnight and found out they were admitting me. did the paperwork while i was sleeping and didn't tell me until morning. could never get anyone to ans the call button. don't go there unless necessary

i was a patient in the er thursday  3/5/20. i had been sick for almost 4 weeks. i went to urgent care  x2,  my family physician 1. meds didn't work. from the moment i arrived the staff were professional and helpful. from the registration rep, to the triage nurse the ed nurse. lab tech , radiology tech all were very caring and helpful. dr benevides was excellent.  my diagnosis was confirmed and i am feeling so much better. thank you !

i had to go to er at chapman for a obstruction in my stomach and the nurse was rude and when i was grimacing in pain, she stated " settle down!"

             this is by far the worst organization i have ever dealt with. i had received a bill for $3100.00 6 months after discharge, they hit me up for $2000 while i was in my hospital bed already! i called the billing department to get my bill audited because the codes were excessively over charged. code 74176 avg cost $488, chapman billed me $4878 and code 74250 avg cost $123, chapman charged me $1132. i had some legitimate concerns and just wanted to make sure this was correct. i talked to george employee #je6 and ask him to look into the charges to make sure they are correct. he told me they will have the bill audited and get back to me and not to do anything until they do, i specifically ask him if this will go to collections and he responded:" no we will contact you when the audit is done".

       i waited and sure enough, got a letter from collections wanting their money. i called chapman immediately and spoke with a woman who told me there is nothing they can do the debt is now in collections. they have now ruined my 800+ fico score and are the most dishonest organization i have ever dealt with, not to mention their hospital and employees are subbar to below average. i could over hear staff complaining of other staff all night long with vulgar language...etc. i strongly advise anyone to avoid this hospital at all costs!

called the number that responded to my post. i explained my story and gave details the representative said he would look into it and call me back for sure. no response or explanation 6 months later!! pathetic customer service and this place is a joke!!

thank you all so much! along with the paraamedics and firefighters. knowing your are there is a blessing  and comforting. amanda you were amazing! i'm sorry she's the only name i remember but dr. b too! and everyone else there last night! thank you for keeping me alive. i wish everyone could appreciate the work you do, you're all the best and the world needs to know!

they don't keep you very long but last time i was there with flu symptoms the doctor came in told me they will perfo tests and i never saw him again the nurse came in with the results and send me to the pharmacy if it wasn't for me to ask what was that i had i will never knew i had bronchitis...  that was very disappointing  we as patients need to know what we have hog long we will be under medication, if is contagious etc. i felt they treat me like an other number.

avoid this for profit disaster of a hospital at all costs! it has been rates as one of the top 100 hospitals in the us with the most negative patient ratings (center of medicare and medicaid). the routinely get cited for inappropriate readmissions. i went to the emergency for severe back and hip pain. they did x-rays and an mri and 'found nothing'. a few days later i passed out at the mall and was taken by ambulance to hoag hospital in newport beach. horrified when they told me the pain i was experiencing was from kidney cancer. i was admitted to hoag that evening and had my kidney removed two days later. finished treatment and am doing well. global should be shut down.

my dad was in for a procedure and had extensive bleeding afterward.  the bleeding started in recovery after the surgeon had left.  nurses called and we had dad kept over night for observation.    i needed to have a cbc because dad is anemic as was still losing blood.   they agreed to the cbc but it was scheduled for morning.  when i said i needed it done stat because of his anemia he might have needed a transfusion before morning.  side note:  dad is 89, rebuilding strength in anyone is hard but more difficult with his age.  the cbc was ordered and they checked it every 4 hours!  by 8 pm the bleeding subsided and i was comfortable leaving my dad in the competent hands of the nursing staff.  dr. malhortra and nursing staff patricia, mark and lori were amazing.    i love hoag hospitals and was really not expecting much being "stuck" at chapman.  this is a staff that was amazing.  totally exceeded my expectations.
thank you.

this review is in regards to a scheduled surgery. everyone here was extremely nice and professional. things were done lightning fast and there was a process for everything and things went smoothly. 

i don't want to get into specifics, but basically, think on all the horror stories and complaints people have about kaiser and then realize that this hospital run by scripps this is the complete opposite.

great care but reporting a problem. these dividers have fallen over in patient rooms. they do not work. needs mdr report. please do so. i will follow up. also it does not work, so get manufacturer to take it back.

this review is for the labor and delivery wing. i would just love to thank everyone for making me feel as comfortable as possible even though nothing went to plan they kept me informed on possibilities and options that were available for me in the end i delivered a very happy and healthy little boy and that is all i could have asked for
had surgery in  november and everyone made me feel so safe in a scary  time of uncertainty!

spent 4 hrs in er with epic migraine. dr austin kinney was no help at all. 
he ordered iv meds but the little girls i mean really little girls 23 to 25 yrs 
used me like a pin cushion and were unable to administered an iv. after 3 tries one of them blew my vein. 
2 hrs later my head is still pounding. dr austin did nothing about it but change the order to tylenol and benadryl and ativan for nausea witch is all i took. make sure you stay away from dr austin he'll offer you tylenol while you're giving birth. i left after 4 hrs with even worst than when i came in 
never thought that was going to happen. a dr that ignores your pain is not

contracts out to 3rd party providers without patient notification. both coastline er phy med grp and encinitas hospitalist associates billing departments (tsc a/r solutions) state that they are part of scripps memorial hospital.   

this misrepresentation has caused billing delays and confusion as their billing is not done through the scripps medical hospital encinitas.  these 3rd party providers tag the patient's credit record with collection accounts for payments and circumvent the scripps memorial hospital billing process.  

both the 3rd party providers and scripps memorial hospital billing representatives state that they are "sorry" that this happens, but are unable to resolve the billing gap crisis.  the patient is left to "figure it out" on their own.

as for the patient experience, the staff ranges from expert to novice.  they saved my life, but forgot to put the bed rails up...

i'm new to san diego county and i went to another scripps facility in oceanside but this was my first time in encinitas. it is much larger than oceanside and a little difficult to navigate at first. there are several different buildings so make sure to have your building number and suite number available. there is limited parking outside of the building so i would recommend saving yourself the trouble and heading right to the parking garage. it's free to park and fairly close to everything. i was able to check in, easily. they told me to be there 15 minutes ahead of time but i'm not sure why they said that because it took me two seconds to sign in. i was there, now much earlier than i needed to be. i figured i would get some work done while i was waiting. except, the wi-fi barely works and there's no service so i stood outside for a while and did my work until i was called in. i met with dr. langley who's absolutely amazing! he was a great listener and gave me great insight while answering all of my questions. great doctor and staff. i will definitely come back here again and recommend it to my fellow yelpers.

this place sucks! stupid nurses and overworked doctors. i hate this generation medical field professionals. went in to get fixed and sat for hours. the democrats of california can suck me balls. they have completely screwed everything up for the everyday tax payer!  #recallnewsome

manish champaneria, md and the staff at this hospital were great! the nurses were very caring and made sure that i was taken care of and were very helpful. my 1 night stay was great. my surgery went well. if you're ever looking for or need a great plastic surgeon this is your guy.
scripps is best to go to if you need to be seen by a qualified doctor.

last week i suffered a heart attack and was taken by ambulance to scripps. from the moment i arrived in the emergency room, and then later to the icu, the care i received was truly exceptional. the empathy and professionalism on display by everyone was heartwarming and put my wife and i at ease. i have some special accolades for a few of the many who treated me. in the emergency room james was our first contact and kept us thoroughly informed and was reassuring of my upcoming procedures. in the icu the nurses in charge of my care over the next few days were angels. lora, emily and irene provided excellent care while keeping my spirits up and had me laughing in what would normally be a very dire time. last, but certainly not least is the care i received from dr. bulibek and his cardiac team before and after my stent procedure. they enabled me to go home sooner than anticipated and to share what would be a very meaningful thanksgiving with my family.

the nurses here are extremely rude(particularly karol) . i came to visit my wife after work and was told that i need to leave after 15 minutes. my wife non stop complained about all their services the short time we were allowed to see each otherand ended up checking herself out against dr advice. do yourself or your loved one the favor of brining them to st. cloud or maple grove.

if you are seriously sick,,motor vehicle accident, have been shot or stabbed this hospital has very competent surgeons, doctors and staff trained to handle the most extreme. you can't get better care  anywhere than at sjgh. now i if you're not seriously sick or in critical condition then the care is much different, long waits are in store for you and possibly no bed available for awhile. so they're an excellent hospital for the very sick but they do not have enough staff or beds to roll out the red carpet for people who don't need to be seen at a hospital setting.

really unsanitary, they put me in a room that was really dirty right after i had a baby, they moved us to the icn where women are trying to fight off infections and babies are taken care of, they do take care of the baby but for mom they're just letting them get infections and not giving good care, when asking for something you have to keep asking the staff because they don't like to actually work, when asking questions about the bathroom that the women have to share you just get attitude, i'm never coming back, lodi memorial is 100x better and cleaner and the staff has actually respect for the people who go through there doors, this place fucking sucks and absolutely never making the mistake to put my life and my babies life in there hands.

awful er department. i was taken by ambulance for feeling dizzy and confused. while i was on the ambulance they established that my blood sugar was incredibly low. when we got to the hospital, one of the emts said i needed some orange juice or something to raise my blood sugar. they told him to put me in the lobby and they'll get to me. i was taken back and asked the basic questions but was asked multiple times if i used drugs. i told them no repeatedly and explained that my blood sugar is low and if they could please get me some juice. to which they replied are you sure you don't use drugs? i was so angry. i was asked 3 times if i was a drug user when i was obviously showing signs of hypoglycemia. my husband arrived at the hospital shortly after i did and they would not let him back to give me some orange juice. they would have let me go into a diabetic coma because they were just assuming i was a drug addict. there people need better education and to listen to their patients better!

my sister just had a baby and everything was perfect until we got to the postpartum room aka the towers the delivery and labor room was nice and there was great service, they moved us about 1 hour after the baby arrived without informing us that we would be moving so soon they put us in a room with 2 other mothers the room was way too hot but the worst part about this room was the rn dr.balvir she kicked me out the room to sleep with the squirrels in the streets lying saying she would get in trouble with her supervisor after i already been there all day and the day before that i spoke to the supervisor and she didn't even know the rule she had to go look but what's funny is i came back in the morning and that night we had a different rn and she said nothing to me about leaving that dr.balvir is just a horrible old fart retire  already!!!!

dear kathleen in the family birthing center, 

you are an absolute angel. you made my entire labor and delivery experience absolutely amazing. i feel so blessed that god chose you to be a part of my support team. seriously, thank you from the bottom of my heart. i could not have done it without you. 

the nurses in recovery were also wonderful and very helpful and supportive! thank you all so much!

renae and rose are lactation consultants and if it weren't for them, i would've given up breastfeeding a long time ago! thank you for all of your help and advice!

we loved how friendly the nurses are and how you get the same nurses taking care of you (they are on a longer shift than the nurses at kaiser). the medical staff is very competent and you get a lot of attention, plus the rooms are clean and comfortable. we really enjoyed our short stay there.

zero stars!
i never leave bad reviews but this one is worth the read. this was the worst experience i've ever had with any hospital. especially finding out what i just did. we went in about 12:15 for my 4 month old. the waiting room wasn't completely filled, but it was a lot of people. they seen us in triage, took babies temperature, swabbed nose for influenza and all those things. first red flag, that i honestly didn't trip off of at the time because my baby was screaming her head off, was he didn't even tell me what her temperature was. we went and sat down like they told us to. we were there for a little over 2 hours, and not even exaggerating, my baby cried the whole time, minus the 10 minute nap she was able to get. around 2:20am i went and asked for an update, and possibly a time for my child to be seen. i had my 4 year old and 4 month old in this place for hours now, and if we aren't going to be seen i may as well take them home and deal with it there. the check in person, who i thought was a nurse, told me she wasn't and called the nurse . the nurse came out and i asked him was he the nurse that i was supposed to talk to, and he replied "no, i'm the triage nurse". then the lady called his name and told him he is the nurse that i needed to talk to. i expressed my concerns & he told me that it's up to me, they are completely full. at that point i got irritated because it makes no sense. i understand that everyone in there needs to be seen, but i had the youngest baby in the waiting room, no nurses or any one for that matter was coming out checking on any of us or giving us updates. literally just letting us all sit. when i went to even ask for an update  i had to look through windows to even see the woman sitting there. here we are now sitting at stanford urgent care (great service by the way) and come to find out, my baby has rsv and the flu! this is where my review kicks in. it was a bad experience but i wasn't even going to say anything, just not go back. they swabbed her nose for the flu and said the results come back in 1 hour. we didn't hear anything! although we left, they had all of our contact info! when those results came back positive, i would think they would reach out being that she 4 fuckin months old. i wouldn't recommend this place at all. i work at a hospital! i understand we get busy, but they honestly did not care & it showed!
i been going here for almost 15 years and they have the best stuff. everyone is super friendly and the doctors are great and caring. i appreciate everyone here and salute them for the great work.

what a rip off . went in for 2 hr not feeling good . charged me over 7000 . hospitals should not have blank check . to charge what ever they want . not i am worried to go to er again because off the amount they charge .

i brought my 16 year old son here today after 6 days of fever (flu diagnosis at urgent care and upper respiratory infection diagnosis at his doctors office just yesterday). unfortunately, he was a lot worse this morning and his doctor doesn't see patients on friday. we signed in and they immediately ordered a chest x-ray and blood work and had us go back to the waiting room. after being called back for the blood work, they sent us back to wait for the x-ray. about 10 minutes later, my son said everything was "going black" and he felt so sick, and he became gray in color, shaking, and clammy. i wanted to run for help but i couldn't leave him sitting there because he felt like he was passing out. i asked a woman sitting nearby to please ask the security guard to get help. he immediately went for help while another patient yelled for a doctor. the nurse came right out and brought him back to a room, he was shaking, so out of it, and so gray in color...he was going into shock, and needed to lie down. thankfully the charge nurse (i found our later her name is gerri) rushed in and had him in a gown and on the bed so quickly, all the while telling him what she was doing, telling him she knows he doesn't feel well, and reassuring both of us that she was going to start an iv and get him feeling better. she was amazing! kind, compassionate, and incredibly efficient. i honestly felt that he would be ok as soon as she took over. it was a bit of a blur after that, but gerri and his other nurse who took care of him for the majority of the time we were there (joyce) brought warm blankets, reassured him, was made us feel like our son was getting the care he needed. joyce  was very kind and caring also, and checked in with us often, even calling multiple times to find out the status of the chest x-ray. we found out later that this was their busiest day in years, and gerri and joyce both took the time to make sure our son felt safe and well cared for, and made me as a mom feel so much better. i can't thank these 2 nurses enough for taking such good care of my son. they both deserve 5 stars, the only reason i put 4 is because the first nurse didn't handle the situation well and showed no compassion, and very little competence. maybe she was having a bad day...maybe she's seem this too many times...but for my son and myself, this was a terrifying experience. i feel so grateful that gerri stepped in and took control of the situation, and handled it with such empathy, professionalism, and efficiency. thank you, gerri and joyce!

i broke my ankle in 3 places when i was downtown and i feel very lucky that i was taken to mercy in the ambulance. 

i got fast treatment in the er, which enabled me to only have one surgery for my ankle instead of two, which was a definite possibility. they set my ankle quickly and took very good care of me.

the 5th and 11th floor nursing staff also took good care of me on the nights before and after my surgery. everyone was very nice and made sure i had the best care possible.

the anesthesia team did an amazing job! i have always been very sick any time i've been under anesthesia (throwing up for 3 days typically) and thanks to the team at mercy, i threw up a little bit once the first time i was able to walk to the bathroom after surgery. that is an amazing improvement.

surgery seemed to go well, though i'm still not at the point where i'm able to put any pressure on my ankle.

i wish i had been told more clearly how long i'd need to be on crutches with absolutely no weight on my bad ankle. since it was in a boot immediately, i didn't realize it would be over 6 weeks before i could even put pressure on it with crutches. due to the pain i have just when i drive on bumpy roads, i understand this, but i had no idea how massive the surgery was, so having it explained to me in the hospital (rather than being told 2 weeks and then told 4 weeks at my first follow-up appointment) would have been very nice. i'd never broken a bone before. i didn't know how much the boot protected the ankle, but it seemed similar to the immobilizer situation i'd had with knee surgeries. it would have been nice to know right away and be able to rearrange more of my life, but generally everyone took very good care of me.

my 85 year old mom was transported to this hospital after taking a serious fall.  the treatment in the emergency department was horrible, the nurses were cold spirited, nonchalant and slow to respond.  we waited for 10 -15 minutes for a bed pan.  can you imagine an 85 year old being forced to almost urinate in the bed. we waited 3 hours for a room, not because there wasn't one available; because the departments were not communicating to get it done.   after being admitted to the 7th floor, the nurses were friendlier and more eager to help.  my intent was to leave an up to par review.  but, there are too many small details that are overlooked. the therapist is running late, the meal plan is limited, the nurse leaves the unclean bed pans in the bathroom on top of the toilet or near the sink, very unsanitary.  not the worst hospital in the world, but they are lacking the feeling of "going the extra mile." the hospital needs a new administrator or a new form of leadership that is willing to implement systems that will eliminate bad review.

back at the hospital with my mom. this time the 12th floor.  the emergency room visit was way better than 8 months ago.  the service was fast and the support staff was friendly.  we are now on the 12th floor and it's on to a bad experience.  my mom hasn't been bathed in 2 days. thank goodness my mom is not as sick as she was 8 months ago.

i like this building. they have free park, a beautiful chapel inside, staffs are nice and helpful. i just don't like the fact sometimes i have to wait longer than expected but in general this hospital is pretty good for out patient.

well i have been in three different hospitals this last week visiting patients. mercy has been the most impressive of the three. from the parking lot worker, explaining how to get into the hospital to the medical staff who offered to show us where the starbucks was (in addition to telling us) -hands down very customer/patient/visitor oriented. not sure if it was because it was christmas eve or what but their genuine kindness and helpfulness sure got my attention.  the gift shop was by far the superior of the three hospitals as well, with such a lovely selection and a great christmas discount!  well done mercy, well done !  ps. this is my first time reviewing a hospital too.

they don't seem to care about patients. during a recent visit one of my family members was left out in the hallway for an extended period of time.  he also overheard the nurses basically admitting that they do not offer sufficient care due to the fact he comes in often. he suffers from seizures. it is absolutely ridiculous.

review:
i cannot day enough amazing things about my experience as a first time mother delivering at this hospital. every single nurse and staff member we had the pleasure of helping us was extremely helpful, patient and so professional. 

a few names stand out, for starters amanda was the nurse that help deliver our baby boy she is just so amazing at what she does and definitely made my labor so much easier than i thought it was going to be in every way. we cannot thank her enough. 

yamila was one of the nurses we had in our recovery room. we unfortunately had to stay a few nights extra due to some tests the baby and i needed done so we had quite a few different nurses but yamila stood out because she really took the time to explain so much to me about my pain and how to ease it. i know she got the end part of our stay so she needed a little extra patiences with me and she was amazing with that. 

kristen is the director of the maternity and labor dept and she went in everyday into our room to make sure our stay was going great and anything we needed she made she to get for us. her energy was just so happy and positive and it's exactly what we needed during our stay.

debbie was the lactation consultant during our stay. she made the impossible happen and helped me latch my baby for breastfeeding. i was so tired and overwhelmed during this stay and didn't think this breastfeeding thing was going to happen for me but she helped so much with that and all the questions i had. 

and last but not least, our baby boy tested high for jaundice so we had to stay yet another night because he needed treatment at nicu and samatha was definitely a nurse i will never forget. she was so helpful and made everything possible to inform us of what was going on, let us interact with him as much as possible while he was getting treated, gave us so much advise, walked us out, help us first timers sit him properly in his car seat, just completely went above and beyond and was simply amazing! she definitely made that experience less painful.

overall a great experience. and i would definitely recommend giving birth here.

my nurse told me some patients order door dash or another food delivery service. that's what i ended up doing, but that is so sad! 

this hospital is so close to my house but i will not be coming here again. i'd rather drive to sunmerland and go to the hospital out there.

wow... i have never been to such a friendly and fast emergency room! dee at intake was amazing so bright and peppy and really made us feel at ease. the rest of the rn's that treated us were just as exceptional. 

keep doing what you guys do :)

took husband to er.  bloodwork, ekg, urinanalysis, etc.  decided to keep him.  he was there for 3 days, no shower, they kept losing him, when i called to talk to him, every single time i was transferred from pilar to post and back to pillar.  went to visit him the next day and was told visiting hours were only from 5 - 6.  since we live so far away, and i cannot drive at night very well, i opted to come back to the house.  called when i got home to try to let husband know why i would not be there for visitation.............again, pilar to post, he's back in the er, he's on the 4th floor, you don't have his patient number so you cant talk to him.  most asinine bs i have ever encountered with a hospital.  the only time the doctor saw him was in the er, yet numerous ekgs were done, and absolutely no explanation.  no information was given to the family.  they finally gave him the paperwork for the "patient number" at 9pm on saturday night.  sunday morning i get a report that he was no longer at the hospital.  once again i call and get the answer "he's back in the er and there are no phones back there".  my reply "please tell him to call his wife"............guess what?  no message was ever given to him.    he called and asked me to please come and pick him up, because they were doing absolutely nothing but have him sleep in a recliner.   picked him up, "discharge papers" were a joke, paperwork with "patient number" was given 2 days afterwards.  paper for area he was in clearly stated visitation from 3:30 to 5pm...............so, please tell me why i was told 5 -6?  i wouldn't take my dog to trident.  the best i can say about this experience is the hospital is severely lacking in getting information to the patient and family, and the total incompetence is beyond the pale.  unbelievable that the hospital cares this little about patients, but you can bet dollars to donuts they will send that bill out, and it won't get lost.

i was admitted to antelope valley hospital as a trauma patient early last month after a terrible head on collision. initially the trauma nurses were great until the ct scan. a woman who was in the ct scan room asked the man who was wheeling me in if he asked if i may be pregnant. "that's not my question to ask" is what he said. then she asked me directly if there was a chance that i could be pregnant and i said yes. after that the entire staff seemed extremely annoyed, and didn't end up even administering a pregnancy test before the ct scan. although this was very upsetting i wasn't in the state of mind to bring any more concern on the matter.

they then put me in the emergency room and eventually came in to tell me i had a fractured l5 vertebrae, and fractured fibula on my left leg. i knew something was wrong with my right foot but they insisted that nothing showed up in the ct scan. they ordered a cam boot for my left leg then tried to put it on the right instead. a common theme in my 5 days here was that i had to inform almost every staff member of my own injuries and i wasn't even confident that they had diagnosed everything properly.

i had two mris done because i kept complaining about my foot. it wasn't until the 4th day that they found 2 fractures in my right foot. this was extremely upsetting after a ct scan and x-rays on my feet, and the doctors kept promising that i would go home the next day after day 2.

i spent the first night and second day in the critical care unit, which most of the nurses there were extremely attentive, i believe angela was the name of the rn i had during the day and she was great. once they moved me out of critical care the second night, it all went extremely downhill.

the remaining 3 days consisted of an average wait of 30-45 minutes for any nurse to assist after i pushed the button (especially during the night time) and a lot of rough handling when transporting me anywhere. keep in mind i have a fractured spine vertebrae and (soon to realize) three total leg/foot fractures between my two legs so i could not do more than roll on to my side, let alone sit up/stand/walk. this is incredibly disappointing beings how i am only in my 20s and someone who would seriously need help could possibly not have their call answered in a timely manner.

the two other nurses that stood out to me were stephenie (rn) and sherri (nt). sherri, who was very nice and talkative, unfortunately spent entirely too long speaking with patients about her personal life. she was the one i had the biggest problem with answering my calls. after 45 minutes, i sent my husband to find her, then 30 minutes later she came back in a rush and told me i just needed to be patient. i'm sorry but waiting over an hour for a bed pan because i can't walk myself to the restroom is ridiculous. this seemed like a common theme before shift change that the wait times would get longer and longer.

stephenie on the other hand, was the best nurse i had. she answered my calls promptly (usually within 5 minutes),was very informative, gave me a lot of supplies and products to maintain my hygiene, and helped clean my tables often. she was very nice and offered a lot of emotional support as well as she was my nurse on day 4 and i was ready to get the f out of that place.

all in all, if you are not a trauma patient, please go elsewhere. that is the only reason i had to go here and although i am grateful for the staff members that truly helped, i wish that my experience was different.
