where do i begin?
i cannot put into words how much arrowhead helped me. i randomly called them in the middle of the night right before christmas. i had never attempted to seek help for my alcoholism which had been getting dangerously worse for the past 90 days-ish prior to making that phone call. the first thing i have to say is that they answered the phone on the very first ring ( and have continued to maintain that wonderful protocol every time i've called since). i spoke to an angel, her name is lisa. she listened so patiently, she told me to come in, she said i could come right then... i was worried because i had no insurance at all and zero money to pay. she said " it doesn't matter, you come now". she offered to get me a cab ride. luckily i had a ride. i arrived and was greeted by lisa. she was just as amazing in person as she was in the phone. she treated me like family. i was admitted to this center. this saved my life!!!!! i stayed from 12/24/19 through 12/30/19. each and every one of the staff there are exactly where they belong. i've never seen a medical facility where the staff exceeded my expectations at such a level that i am left speechless til this very day. i am writing this under a ' pen name' but i hope the staff and patients i met during this beautiful experience know who i am. i wanna say this to anyone who is so alone and suffering. don't hesitate. go to arrowhead. please.. it will save your life . i am clean and sober. i'm enrolled and attending their intensive outpatient program right now. it's great. regina is a real treat. i love them all. the staff at arrowhead coordinated all my medicaid applications , and took care of all my post discharge care. i now have medical insurance, rides through net plus ( free rides to all medical appointments) and i am so very happy. i'm alive in the best way. oh, and i must give a huge shout out to the chef. i forgot his name, but he's a very tall buff guy who created the best meals ever. i love this place. i hope someone reads this review and takes my advice. i want people who feel so hopeless to feel like i do now. i feel amazing.

3.5 stars would be appropriate. i rounded up in this instance. 

november 6th of 2019 i was at home and started to feel off, next thing i knew i was throwing up blood by the bucketful. my friend called 911 and they take me down to fmh - now i can't speak too much negative about this stay as i died twice and was brought back by this facility and there very talented staff. 
i was airlifted to a much larger hospital in the harbor university of maryland i stayed for 3 months and then was transferred back to fmh. they worked with me everyday for pt and taught me how to walk again. the majority of the staff are great and really care about you as a individual not just another patient. the food brings you the true definition of " hospital food " and the only thing with bubbles to drink is ginger ale. i don't drink pop but after months of drinking water and juice, a soda pop is amazingly refreshing. 
now before i jump into the facility i will say that they are in the middle of remodeling. 
the facility leaves something to be desired. it is a older hospital and they are due for a update. almost daily something had to be fixed in my room. i was hooked up to a machine so i couldn't use the bathroom but for some reason they had to work on it regularly. the paint is chipping and my hospital bed would move around almost like it was possessed. 
i am not from maryland and i only came here to work for a two year contract but i am forced to stay here because the transplant center here is the best in the nation and my local doctors urged me to stay here in frederick as they can't offer what the hospitals in maryland can. 
they lost a star because a lot of the beginner nurses ( they call them techs i think ) can barely speak english. their communication skills are lacking in a major way. i promise you that ins would have a field day there. 
slot of the younger staff - 35 and under are straight aces. i cannot put into words how good they are and how committed to fixing you and making sure your comfortable they are. that to me is extremely important. 
all in all i recommend this facility and their doctors. just bring your own drinks and download a translation app on your phone. 
get well soon!!

i've been to fmh several times, over the last six months, and everyone has been wonderful. the doctors, nurses, and security staff are very courteous, and caring, and the hospital itself is well maintained, and clean.

i suffer from kidney stones, so i'm unfortunately able to comment on many area hospitals, and to compare their levels of care. fmh is among the very best, for both emergency care and planned surgeries.

fantastic surgery experience. 
actually, the best experience i've ever had. the doctors and nurses were marvelously attentive! i did not want a nurse anesthetist so i requested a md anesthesiologist and they paged dr. o'fallon board certified anesthesiologist for me. he was a great listener as i told him about being frightened from waking up in terror in the middle of a past surgery with a different anesthesiologist! this guy made sure i did not wake up & was not nauseous when i did wake up. 'the vein whisperer nurse', 'angie' fab - got the iv port in painlessly the first time.

i have to write a letter to the hospital administrators this week i was so impressed.

 before surgery, while waiting, i got a heated air blanket, warm socks, leg compression massage boots, cable tv, the works! they even gave me hot coffee which i was craving and graham crackers right after surgery! and get this...the nurse told me if the coffee was no good (because she didn't know how long ago it was brewed as she just came on shift), she would be happy to brew me another pot ! huh? this is unbelievable. after hearing this i was going to pass out. not from the surgery , but because of the amazing caring and attentive service! are you sure this hospital isn't actually a 5 star royal caribbean cruise ship?

i felt like i was in a spa! i always had a nurse assigned to me from check -in to recovery. they were never more than 12 feet away and they did not leave me alone.

 even the valet parker at the surgery check-in door is unbelievable. very professional. she took the car & let us know the service is free. huh? (did i hear free)??? yes. and even gave instructions how to call up to get your car delivered when you're ready -even gave instructions to have it delivered if after hours - assuring you it was a 24-hour service so not to worry.

if you have to go to a hospital for surgery, this one is highly recommended.

worst hospital i have been to in a long time if you value you period don't go here and if you have to go be praying to jesus at all times cause you will need his protection.if you are admitted to the fourth floor ever just check yourself out and go home you will have a better chance there because some of the staff on this floor are nasty and poorly trained.fifth floor is better but still don't let down your guard listen well, take good notes and ask lots of questions.

unfortunately this past many weeks we had a dear relative who was admitted to barlow after leaving cedars-sinai hospital. this is where our horror starts. understaffed, filthy, dark and depressing, on top of being ancient. had we not had round the clock  sitters, our aunt would have died. she had three different roommates and i am positive they all passed. most were comatose and had no visitors. one incident amongst many will always be etched in my mind. my aunt was given stool softeners daily. well that produced non-stop diarrhea. i would call repeatedly for help to clean her up, and no help came. well i walked out of the room in search of someone in the empty halls. i was approached by nurse supervisor lisa kelly who on every visit reminded me the importance of wearing the yellow paper gown. i asked her why my aunt was sitting in her own feces for a half hour when nurse kelly never came to help. the cna's were great but there was never enough of them around. i was told there was two cna's for an entire floor of patients on the weekends. my aunt had no physical therapy other than one walk around the desk and back to bed. during holidays which lasted four days, no physical activity at all! thankfully we found a sub acute location and within 24 hours our aunt was walking talking and blossoming. in the future i would never even bring a dog to this location. my next contact will be with medicare and the state medical board.

this is a horrible place with a horrible staff. they do not attend the patients with respect nor when they are asked too. recently my mother could not speak, we then thought of getting her a wipe board and marker so she can communicate with us. she had told us that a nurse there pulled my mother's hair and they did not clean her, making her have a rash. the staff there does not attend her needs until one of our family members reaches out to them, then they will still take an hour to help out. i would not recommend this hospital for anyone.

i just delivered my daughter recently at this hospital. let me just say that the experience was amazing. from the second i arrived to the er, to getting discharged from the hospital. the l&d nurses made my labor experience phenomenal, being a first time mom i did not know what to expect, but everybody came together to made the process as stress free and memorable as possible. casey was our nurse during that time and she was exceptional!! dr. steele from complete women's care center delivered my daughter and she was also fantastic. the nurses in the postpartum room were also very sweet and helpful during my healing process especially helping me out with baby when we needed it. i also may add that the food served at this hospital is delicious. :) best experience ever!

let me just say how offended i am at the manner i and my family was treated. i went on saturday to the er because i was in severe pain and  had no fetal movement. besides being treated like i was overreacting. the staff did not care to accommodate me. the ultrasound tech lindsey briggs not sure in spelling of last name was extremely rude. i had my mother and aunt with me and was translating to them what i was asking her. she was really irritated by it and started making sounds and purposely applying pressure on my ribs to get me to be quite even tho i told her it was hurting. i asked her if i could see my baby or at least listen to the heartbeat and she was like for what. i told her i hasn't had an ultrasound since october and just wanted to see my baby. she purposely moved the screen and didn't even give me a picture like the discharge nurse told me she should of. not only that but neither the doctor told me if my baby was fine he was more upset that i didn't allow them to do the catheter and walked out of my room. i am highly considering finding a new place to deliver and will be telling my friends about the treatment here. i still don't know anything about my baby not even told if the heartbeat was good. now i'm scrambling to find a place to make an appointment before christmas to see if my baby is fine. these past few days have been a nightmare not knowing anything about my baby.

rocked it for me today in the er!!   thank you thank you.  

professional, prioritized others before me, the right thing to do!  my issues were small but many. took away pain, referral made.  great team great place
i would give a  full 5 stars but getting your meds takes forever. other than that pretty good people, especially their dental staff!

yesterday morning i walked in to the er (palmetto hospital) told the receptionist i was having stroke symptoms.. slurred speech... numbness in the face... 
she told me to have a seat with a disgusting attitude ... didn't pay no mind to me or any of the information i had just provided her.

we ended up leaving palmetto drove to memorial west and as soon as i told them my symptoms they screamed out stroke alert on the pa system and rushed me in and had 10 doctors in my face asking me questions.. even the staff were shocked they had me take seat instead of rushing me in after they knew i could've been having a stroke 
i am disgusted 

turns out i have a very large aneurysm.

this hospital needs to be shut down. you will die before the will attend you

en este hospital es la más mala atención q he visto en mi vida lo peor q he visto los médicos no vienen esto no se le puede llamar hospital es increíble el pulmónologo de la paciente se llama rene gonzales y lo llaman y nunca viene se preocupa muy poco por sus pacientes  tenía q cambiarle algo para la respiración llevaba dos días ahogándose  y no podía comer y lo llamaban y nunca vino me ayudó otro médico esto es increíble la paciente se llama idalia guerras gracias dr rené gonzales por preocuparse tan poco por pacientes

avoid this hospital. terrible treatment of patients and family members. no compassion, not a caring person that we could find. family member dies and you don't even get a chair to sit on. belongings go missing and you get the "i didn't work that day" excuse. unexceptable treatment. avoid avoid avoid

this hospital offers disabled person free parking if they validated the parking ticket, i took the parking permit, ticket and my mother's drivers license to get validated and was told my mother who is the person disable had to climb a hill from patient outcare to main lobby because it was policy. the person responsible for that policy should be fired, is or comes pretty close to a violation of americans with disability act.

you'll die before you get attended. do not go to this place i mean it   worst hospital. the nurses look like like they didn't even study they don't know anything so unprofessional the doctors are rude. i was literally in so much pain and the nurse taking her time doing nothing but talking with the other nurses. doctor for the kids area is just horrible omg if i could fire him id fire him. soon as i said id be doing a review he said talk about the nurses but not about me say good about me lmaooooo no he didn't.

my boyfriend went into the er last night because his nose was so swollen he can't sleep or breathe and the doctors and nurses where so rude. they made him wait 2 hours, and didn't even look at his nose. just because it's not a sickness doesn't not mean it's not important!
fac_name: Willamette Valley Medical Center & Cancer Center

review:
life happens... emergencies happen... there are six hospitals closer to me than davis hospital. wait... you have davis hospital three stars and you pass up six hospitals to go here?  sometimes.  the labor and delivery is exceptional and worth five stars in itself.  surgical wing, outpatient surgery, and nursing staff all deserve one star.  the nurses are unprofessional and check their phones, bad mouth their boss to patients, and have the worst bedside manners.  the nurses do not follow orders put in by the doctors and do not communicate with other nurses.

the cafeteria is worse the elementary cafeteria 15 years ago.

just want to say how much we appreciate this hospital's icu department.  especially nurse lisa & the other wonderful nurse that was there  recently for the whole family . they kept us informed as to how my best friend was doing. super caring and kind. unfortunately our friend passed away but we were glad as to how tender and loving they were with the whole family and friends that gathered there during this super difficult time for all of us. ( especially her daughter  & granddaughters :( 
from the bottom of our hearts thank you. nurse lisa   we love you!!!

i had an emergency while away on vacation and visited the er. certain staff members at intake were very nice, however i was horribly upset by the lack of privacy at this facility. i was told very personal, hard news in the emergency department with the door wide open with other patients listening and watching. as a health care professional myself, this is truly upsetting and insensitive, not to mention violates privacy laws. that along with the fact we waited hours for our results after testing, and the cleanliness of the area was lacking,  as they constantly shuffled sick patients in areas we were placed in. overall, the least i could've asked for was a closed door when receiving awful news.

coronavirus is less deadly than this hospital. piss poor service. i have a preexisting back injury and had to go in because i could not deal with the pain anymore. the nurses are garbage. they rush you out and state all your business in front of everybody. that is a privacy policy violation. i have to get a second opinion and a lawyer now because they can't do their job.

here we are in tahoe again, but unfortunately this time i had some significant chest pain that made me consider going to the er. we arrived here not knowing what to expect, but i am completely blown away. this was by far the most pleasant, professional, and efficient visit to a hospital that i've had in my entire life. the entire team working tonight was phenomenal and took great care of me while giving me peace of mind. i could not have been anymore pleased with the treatment i received.
great surgical experience. the entire surgery staff from before and after surgery, nurses, aids, doctors and nurse anesthesiologists were just amazing. thanks mason!
fac_name: Mason General Hospital & Family of Clinics

review: the nurses are not very well organized here, they seem to work against one another instead of helping one another. please don't use palliative care here unless you are ready to die. they push you into kindred hospice and the first dose of medication they give you puts you unresponsive, so you won't be talking, eating or drinking anymore, so you won't last long like this. i asked the palliative care doctor why this happened to my sister and her response was when your in hospice facility it's very aggressive! i don't care for piedmont athens regional hospital because of this. the hospice facility is on the oncology floor, please beware of this place.

i can't speak for the hospital as a whole but the labor and delivery unit is amazing. i delivered my son at tmca in august 2018 and had a wonderful experience. 

it was shortly after midnight when i went into active labor so i had to go through the er as it was after hours. the er staff that initially checked me in was friendly and calm. as a first time mom, i was a little panicked walking in, but they instantly reassured me that i was in the right place. 

the actual l&d wing was clean, cozy, and was staffed with (mostly) friendly staff. the anesthesiologist who did my epidural was quick and painless. the mom and baby side of the wing was just as fantastic. 

my only "hiccup" was after the fact when i received a bill for a miscoded error. but it was quickly resolved

all-in-all, i highly recommend tcma for all expectant mothers.

this place was the right place at the right time. after a 4 1/2 month injury that persisted since my wife's discharge from a different hospital. the comparison between the two was night and day. 
the aurora medical center staff were very friendly, informative, and helpful. there was never a time  that we felt like my wife's needs were  not attended to. as for the general atmosphere, the place was clean, modern, and in good repair.
thanks for a good experience with your health facility.

i came in having a history of kidney stones and uti and kidney infections. of course it was christmas eve eve, and low and behold my physician treating me treated me like an actual human and found the stones i both of my kidneys. 

i spent the night puking and wishing for gods mercy, but being in agony while it's bear years eve, well yeah. dr kalen abbott, he has very little bedside manor and said that there was no history of stones in my prior imaging. the nurse said there was a 4mm stone in my left kidney. 

but alas. i do have the report. unfortunate hospital staff. nurse who took care of me looked like she hadn't washed her hair in ages and the paramedic accused me of being in underwear because i was wearing white shorts. really great stay.

this is supposed to be a top notch mental health facility. my experience today tells me it's anything but that. after waiting 4 hours for help in the er it took me telling them we were leaving to get a room. this is a perfect example of mental health being treated as completely and totally unimportant. if the health professionals treat it this way it's no wonder the rest of the world does. after getting the room we continued to wait for an hour. at that point we left worse then we started because of this places total lack of concern. medical center of aurora should take all mention of mental health care off the website. they clearly don't give a rats ass.

terrible triage. zero communication for the first two hours we were there as far as how serious the situation was and what we should  watch for or do. totally dishonest about wait times. not caring or helpful with advice when we took our toddler there last week. the money grab at  the end was insulting. very discouraging example of the broken healthcare system.

had to come in this past weekend and go to the er! actually went twice to get my follow up bloodwork done. i had dr. smith and he was absolutely wonderful with my case. my nurse erica made me feel so much better since the er wouldn't let my husband come back due to not knowing anyone to watch our kids. she got my iv i'm on her first try because my veins are stubborn and blow easily. theo was my tech and he got my iv on the first time, but as soon as they went to get my blood it blew as always. erica was so gentle and through with my care and explaining everything to me. 

when i went the second time to get my follow up bloodwork i have nurse kevin who did my blood and got it the first time and luckily he got my blood before it blew. (my left arm clearly doesn't like needles) i have a couple of different nurses and people who took care of me and checked on me brian, kaitlyn and i think kelsi. they were all so nice and helpful through this experience. 

overall doctor smith and nurse erica were my favorite and everyone was so nice and helpful. my experience due to what was happening wasn't easy so i thank you to the nurse and dr. smith who had to talk to me before i was discharged saturday and monday.

the er doctor i saw was extremely aggressive and literally yelled at me for both my anxiety and my physiological orthostatic issues. he badgered me almost like a cross examination in a courtroom about the possibility of pregnancy and my sex life. just run a test lol, why are you screaming at me? i told him i couldn't be pregnant because i was celibate (my husband is away), and he ridiculed me for my 'sad life' and gave me creepy looks. it was beyond insensitive. another doctor made insulting remarks about my face, strongly implying i was less homely with my glasses on, and looked like 'two different people'. again, super weird and gross and inappropriate to say the least. it actually really upset me and any kind of stress is really bad for my condition. 

some of the nurses here are really nice, and a med student spent a lot of time with me, giving advice about my condition, even though he didn't have to. i wish he had been my doctor!!! he was so caring and attentive. the younger people here seemed much less jaded i guess and treated me like a human being. 

the room i had was great, very private, pretty decent food, and a lot of television options.

i had a scary finding on my echocardiogram that has even to this day not been explained to me, no matter who i contact.

had a test done here outside the er and the doctor was on his phone the entire time and he too was not very nice overall.

i did appreciate the discretion when chest tests were done. not once was i exposed, so that was nice. but some of the doctors here really need to take some sensitivity training, especially when dealing with nervous female patients. the way three of them spoke to me (but especially the gruff er doc) was quite shocking. it should go without saying that remarking on a patient's personal life and appearance is wildly inappropriate and unacceptable.

this hospital had terrible reviews which gave me high anxiety when i found out i would be delivering my child there. i had a great experience from when i was admitted into labor & delivery all the way to last day i left the hospital. my baby needed to stay a few extra days in the nursery for uv light treatment and all the staff was great, friendly & knowledgeable and i felt comfortable leaving my baby in their care. the labor & delivery nurses were my favorite nurses i've ever encountered in my life so a huge special shout out to them! and anyone who is nervous to deliver here because of bad reviews i hope this eases your mind.

this is the worse hosp around to go to as they  the staff  many of them are nasty and talk down to you, but without you would have no job or pay check.  some of them could care less and others go out of their  way to see your needs are met. my husband was in there and waited and waited for a pillow and i went and found one as they were ignoring the request saying they had to get one from somewhere as they don't have pillow on the unit and i got chewed out for finding one. the medicines were messed up and from one dr to another  we weren't told they changed their minds and ordered something else . the communication is very lacking.then on discharge they send us to outpatient pharmacy knowing they are closed on christmas day. we had togo back the next day to get the meds and didn't get what they told us he would get. he talks to the dr who called our home and yet still ordered the wrong medicine, after it was explained to him. they just don't pay attention. to what your telling them. they are going to do it their way regardless of your concerns that this does not work .as you have tried it and it didn't help you at all. i cant even see why this hosp is still open. finally before he left the supervisor was called into all of this mess, and she was nice and tried to get it all straight.there needs to be one plan of action not each dr doing there own thing and ordering things you don't even know about and its your care.

i was admitted to this facility on february 2, 2020. i was admitted via the er after arriving by ambulance. this hospital was not my first choice after having been a patient in june, 2019 with a uti and symptoms of a cerebral stroke. i was not really lucid upon admission but shortly after being taken to a room a hospitalist approached to give me grief about having complained about the hospital in june. he said, "why are you here after complaining about your care here?" i told him that this was not my first choice due to insurance restrictions so i was brought by ambulance!" it is not the responsibility of a hospitalist (physician) to chastise a patient who is ill for previous complaints about the hospital. a week following the june admission i was admitted to another hospital. 

i was not prepared to tell him this month that after the june, 2019 admission several physicians told me not to go back to mckee if i needed further medical care. i wrote a letter to the ceo of mckee this month. no reply has been received. the rating for this hospital of 2.5 stars on this site is an indication of patient satisfaction. i list my satisfaction level at 1 star.

a negative rating is not an option; therefore i have no choice but to give the lowest available rating.  i am an r.n. who wishes to take the bls course at mckee. the course is in 4 days.  i have left at least 6 messages on the answering machine of t. berq.... who is over the program.  she has not responded to my very polite messages. pure rudeness.  so i then tried calling the administration - also no one there to take a call. i shudder to think what being an inpatient would subject one to.  ?no reponse, no care?

my daughter and son-in-law are expecting and we came to see dr. gregory root in obstetrics and gynecology. the hospital is quite big. there's a gift shop by the elevators and a cafe on the first level. we too the elevator up to the 2nd floor, then to suite 240a. the lobby was beautiful and very roomy. the lady checking us in was nice and polite. it wasn't much of a wait at all and we were called back. they guided us to a small room and took my daughter's information. dr. root came in and made us feel very comfortable and at ease. not only was he professional but he added jokes to make us laugh..we were immediately confident in our choice as him being the doctor. he also gave us a list of vitamins to take and an app on our phone to track the baby. he does ultra sounds with each appointment and gave us 3 so we can each have one. the baby is 11 weeks and 5 days along. can't wait to come back and watch the growth of my newest grandbaby!!

my daughter went in sick and did not have any insurance. the emergency room staff, dr. hemal patel, leah and others were kind and caring. i could not be happier with the treatment they gave to my 27 year old daughter. thank you, hannibal regional.

i gave birth here in december, and every part of my experience was great. the ob appointments, classes, and tour beforehand all helped prepare us for the big day. the staff in l&d was incredibly attentive and helpful, as well as the staff in the postpartum floor. all of our needs were met well! the food was good and i could order whenever i was hungry. the room was very clean and comfortable. 

i fell the week before giving birth and had to go to the er on thanksgiving. i ended up with a broken elbow. the er check-in staff was good, and the doctor, nurses, and x-ray tech were helpful and efficient. this was our second visit to mcd er in a year, and while we hope to not have to return, we are confident in the care we received.

after spending months in the sicu fighting cancer, my husband passed away several months ago at med city dallas. i've started this review so many times i can't count, but i was so mentally drained, i kept pausing it. i wish i could say my beautiful husband got the best care. instead, we were hit by the harsh reality of complete disrespect and disregard for human suffering. patients don't normally stay in the sicu for long time, so the nurses can wear smiles for few days. we were there for months and got to see their real faces.

it started with me finding countless bruises, head bumps, blue skin indentations, scratches, bloody marks, skin tears, tube lids and saline syringes under my husband embedded in his skin. i kept finding him with wounded neck bent in such a way he was grimacing in pain, no one bothered to check and help. i was finding him lying with dirty face/ears/eyes, lips chapped covered with white pasty layer, chest covered with sticky residue from the electrodes, no one cared to wash it off, room dirty, feeding bags hanging over 24 hours, floor dusty, stained with dry formula, the list goes on. i kept complaining and they hated me for it. 

i took a lot of photos and involved patients advocate crystal crawford. those photos shocked everyone we know, yet crystal kept saying "when i'm there, they are so nice with him..."...like i was lying. it was useless. so i contacted the sicu director mark sanders. to justify their mess the nurses decided to gang up and roll it all on me. yes, i did raise my voice when confronted them, i was mentally and physically exhausted spending 8-10 hours with my husband, i was grieving. what was their excuse for yelling, calling me names, slamming doors, drawers, kicking me out of the room and badmouthing me? mark sanders was no help either, even called to tell me that nurses feelings were hurt and that "their tears were real". and my tears? they need to suck it up, it's icu, people are suffering. it was my loved one who was dying, not theirs! mark sanders offered to move us to a different unit, but after that he just vanished. i then contacted chief nursing officer joy sully. i left her voicemails, messages with her assistant, even a handwritten letter for her at the front desk pleading to move us to different icu, away from poisonous atmosphere, to give us peace. but she too ignored it. they didn't want to bother with the dying man. 

our last weeks in the sicu was a nightmare. every day was a different nurse, "fragile" them couldn't handle demanding wife for 3 shifts in the row. i made them face every neglect and they couldn't stand me for it. once they sent a nurse w. from the night shift. that nurse did a number on my husband. she left him lying in feces for hours, didn't check as often as she was supposed to and that created more skin erosion, she was so reckless that his peg tube popped out of his stomach, and finally from her rough "handling" his neck started to heavily bleed again. at that point i lost it! the other nurse k. said she didn't like my "tone" and left. my husband was in a horrendous condition and i was supposed to bow and whisper? the manager rachel rushed in to yell at me and defend her nurses of course. it was like spanish inquisition. "we are going to call security" became their signature dish. instead of me sitting and comforting my husband, i was on high alert non-stop and he had to witness me fighting neglect for months. besides physical pain and cancer, he was going through emotional agony watching me stand against the tsunami alone. 

on the day of my husband's passing we had a day shift nurse emily g. whenever she was our nurse she was always sweet, patient and caring. day shift sicu is the reason i will never use medical city dallas,i rather die in the streets. same goes for all our friends, family, colleagues, neighbors, their friends and families, it's spreading like wildfire, everyone is blown away. my husband was my life, my air, my light. half of me died when my love took his last breath, the other half of me is crippled. i will remember every nurse till i stop breathing and i know i will meet them all at the gates of hell one day.

so disappointed in the hospital and competency.  perhaps they have a large legal department, if not they should. while treatment was ok, they got so many thing's wrong, over medicated,  repeatedly miscommunicated amongs own staff and frankly didn't care after discharge.  pathetic.

they are racist, didn't care about my pain at all, didn't show me any attention. i get to my room put in this raggedy ass nightgown they gave me with one arm cut off, then some nurse cones in and tells me i have to leave this room cause it was reserved for somebody else, just for her to come back 30 seconds later and two me to stay and i requested a new gown and no one brought it. i sat in that room for over an hour in a half waiting all while everybody white was getting treated and they were cracking jokes and all this good stuff. no one came to church if i was okay no one offered me water or a blanket. the fat ass white nurse they gave me didn't even look me in my eyes. so after i sat in that cold as room for 2 hours finally the doctor comes and say where going to give you antibiotics then you can leave. then the fat ass nurse they gave me brings my medicine and i swear you would swear this fat bitch had so much shit to do how fast she was trying to get out off my room. the er wasn't even busy when i went to go pee this fat bitch was just sitting at her desk. like really bitch you couldn't come check on me. i just feel like i didn't receive the proper care i deserved and they didn't take my pain issues seriously. i left the hospital feeling worse then when i came in. they only catered to the white people and i'm saying this because i was the only black person in there and they didn't do shit for me. i hate this hospital i will never in my life go back there racist and i just can't believe how i was treated in there last night. they might as well put a whites only sign at the front door. and there bathrooms were fucking filthy!! trifling ass racist ass hospital i do not recommend if your black!!

went visit family @ this hospital for the first time on a sunday and found that this small looking hospital has huge lessons for all other hospitals to learn from.

its very neat, clean and organized. reception was friendly and helpful. signs are clear and easy to follow to find your way. perhaps its small and not too complicated to begin with but the experience was a positive one.

waiting area was again, neat, clean and even magazines are stacked in an organized way. that's pretty good. some one is definitely spending time and effort taking care of the facility!

restroom... well not surprised, neat, clean and organized. during the time we waited there, cleaning crew came by again.

rn assigned to care for our family was great as well. very positive person, caring and she definitely in the right profession! thank you!

simply put, positive organization from too down. great team overseeing this hospital!

had to take a family member here for an emergency blood transfusion due to cancer. 

the nurse, amber, was awesome and got the iv in the first time! (they usually have to poke several times). 

the room was private, had space and chairs for all family members. 

highly recommended if you are sick and want fast, excellent medical care!

i almost forgot the lvn who was failing at finding a vein tried to put a used needle back in my arm. so she stuck me didn't find a vein pulled the needle all the way out and tried to stick me again. wtf. who ever works in hr should be fired immediately before they hire another unprofessional lvn.

x ray department.   unprofessional.  insurance  info was sent over to the xray department from my doctor.  they performed the xray.  a month later i get a bill.  they never bothered to communicate effectively with my doctor who sent them my insurance  info.  now im doing their job getting my insurance involved.  some lazy people kill it for the whole business.

i originally came in because two nurses and doctor who saw my burn told me to come in because of the symptoms i was complaining of. so i waited in the lobby for 4 hours. the woman who's child fell down and may have a concussion had to wait as well the same amount of time as me. in fact the people that this hospital saw seemed perfectly healthy. i do not know what the priorities this hospital has as far as what patients go first. honestly this is the worst hospital. they did not do anything to help me, and in fact told me i would be fine. my doctor who saw the burn is the one who told me to go to er immediately. so they better hope it does not get infected because i will sue for malpractice. this hospital has a reputation in which i wish i would have known sooner. dont come here.

i wish i could give zero stars! thanks a lot yelp! anyways, came here at 10:30 with my sister-in-law on december 12th 2019. it was immediate dissatisfaction. i'm just going to give you a list of the issues we had.
1. the first nurse we had encountered was pushy and just seemed like she was over her day and taking it out on the patients. 
2. my sister-in-laws came to the hospital because of severe chest pain. when the pain suddenly came back i notified a passing nurse who looked at me and then told another nurse- who by the way never came to check on her (what if this has been serious???)
3. my sister-in-law asked more than a few times for a blanket because she was cold and it took over two hours for someone to actually accommodate her. 
4. i went looking for a nurse because she needed to use the restroom which required iv removal. while i was speaking to the nurse he was just looking at me dumbfounded and had totally disregarded me. instead he simply turned and tapped another nurse and walked away.

this is by far the worst er experience ever!!! i now understand why this hospital has such a horrible rating. 
here's a tip: hire people who actually enjoy caring for people and don't mind doing their job! you're providing a public service and if that bothers you so much maybe it's time to find a different career path! 

((( there was only two great people we encountered and that was an older nurse and a gentleman who did my sister-in-laws iv)))

do not take your family to this hospital because the doctors don't know what they are doing my dad was at this location for 5 day they were not able to find the issues they were guessing they finally send him home. he's not ok they told my mom he can go back to work tomorrow .he's can't walk on his own the nurses adriana and the other 2 nurses who speak spanish were nice to bad the reviews are only for the hospital.

mike riedinger, in the er took care of my 17 year old daughter's laceration to her hand he is heaven sent he knew what he was doing explain everything to me very professional very kind you can tell  he was very very busy there was a very high demand for him but the whole time he kept his composure  and his professionalism that night we arrive at 12:30 we seen him around 1:30 he was very attentive caring coach my daughter through the pain i really really appreciate what he did for us that will never forget that i know that is  his job but it meant the world to us  san g. hospital has always been a good experience

a delightful surgical experience.

pros - 
- my reservation was honored, on time, very punctual
- nurses, surgeon and anesthesiologist were all a delight to work with, despite my brutal honesty as to personal beverages of choice
- i checked in to have a troublesome gallbladder removed, and that's exactly what i got.

cons - 
- i didn't get to do the "count backwards from 100" thing with the anesthesia. i was simply told, "here's a little something to relax you." cosby style! i awoke suddenly three hours later, alone in a different room. 
- sent home with wholly inadequate pain meds after having been punctured in the abdomen several times - fortunately a phone call soon provided the good stuff.

i never wanted to believe all the negative feedback about newport hospital until i experienced horrific treatment from a nurse there. i had knee surgery today and she was the rudest nurse ever with the worst bedside manner. when i asked her to hand me my belongings so i could use my phone to inform my boyfriend i was ready to be discharged she started screaming at me to stay in my bed and refused to assist me. i was not attempting to get out of the bed, which is why i asked for her help. this was extremely upsetting to come out of surgery and be "taken care of" by someone so uncaring ,  unprofessional, and rude. i mentioned to her that i had a surgery at women and infants hospital last year and i had a wonderful service from the staff. she replied that i should go back to women and infant hospital! 
what a shame a newport hospital   registered nurse in the surgical department, treating patients so disrespectfully reflect on your institution so poorly.  it really hurts the reputation and insults all of the dedicated and compassionate care givers and other staff at newport hospital.
#thenurs

went in for a neck xray, i asked when i checked in, how much is it going to cost? told them i would pay cash if cheaper because i know my insurance is crappy. they said they would check and never got back with me on that. they sent me to the xray tech, took 3 xrays which took about 7 minutes. 
months later, i receive an $800 bill! ridiculous! i have paid $500 for a cat scan, and $300 for mammogram and ultrasound in san marcos. xrays should never cost that much. i have called to dispute the amount and no one seems to be able to tell me anything or get me to a person who knows about their billing. 
now they sent my bill to collections.....really?!! 
the hospital is really pretty but who cares when you are charged extremely high amounts for simple procedures.
i made a huge mistake by going to resolute!
i will stick with ctmc and advanced imagining in san marcos from now on. they tell you what the charges will be before you are even seen. isn't that what all medical facilities should do?

my mom has been to this hospital many times and we've always been pretty happy with it.  it is very nice and clean.  the staff is very friendly.  then recently she has had a few surgeries and i was surprised by how fast they discharged her.  she is 81 years old and i don't think discharging her before she is even fully out of the anesthesia is a good idea.  she could barely get out of bed.  this upset me.  then as i began to dig into some of her other medical issues, i realized they had messed up more than i thought.  she was extremely anemic and for each surgery they completely missed this.  that is standard preop.  i would not recommenced this hospital especially if you are elderly.

i had to come here for lab work and all went pretty well the first day. staff was nice and accommodating. i would give 4 stars just for that experience. however, fast forward to the next day when i had to bring in a sample. i was told to go to the er and drop it off and was never given any other instructions nor any paperwork. i called whilst on my way just to make sure this is in fact the place i drop it off at. the girl says, "well i don't have an answer for you so i have to find someone". super rude. very very unprofessional. she never came back on the line. so i just hung up and went to the er, as previously instructed. i get there and he girl is equally unhelpful and says well you don't have any paperwork. i proceed to tell her i wasn't provided any just told to write all information on the sample, which i did. if i didn't ask for a supervisor, i would have been sent home not knowing what to do with this sample and having to do it again! completely unhelpful. she proceeds to say i'm just the messenger ma'am. no accountability for any unhelpfulness. the supervisor was nice enough but the damage was already done. i'm very disappointed in my experience. it's sad that there is no customer service anymore. there is no empathy. i don't want someone taking care of me that i do not trust. change your staff. get better people to answer the phones. ugh

i've been to hospitals in south louisiana and houston. resolute has my vote. the facility is fairly new, the staff are courteous and professional. the interior is impeccably clean. while in pre-op, there was very little time when there wasn't a nurse present. all were very open and honest. i was admitted at my scheduled time, and the procedure took place almost as scheduled. try doing this in houston, good luck. the equipment in pre-op and where the surgery took place looked to be first class. everyone was kind, willing to answer questions, and very professional. it became more professional as showtime approached. these folks didn't leave a stone unturned. everything was recorded. i went under and woke 45 minutes later. never felt a thing. recovery took some time, but that happens to one that's sedated. all in all, i'll be back there again!. doctors and support staff were great.......... thanks for a pleasant experience.

the staff are not only grossly unprofessional but thieves as well. my brother had missing items from his "check-in" bag that were never logged in... of course, it was his fault for not verifying the checklist. when asked about the security tapes it took weeks to get a response and were then told they were already deleted... not to mention, they couldn't even identify what employees were working that night. 
this place should be condemned.

i'm a recent former patient at this wonderful hospital . staff are patient and merciful . ...always a smile on their faces dealing with me. ...i worked them hard too, and they showed me no frustration / anger. ...they were good to other patients too. .....the only issue i had at the time : is they temporarily lost my clothes, but a nice lady worker got them back several days later  . ....most hospitals lose clothes i know.  but everyone should be more careful next time.  ......i commend joyce for making my christmas merry by finding my clothes. ......anyways : besides that , one flaw. .this was the best hospital i've ever been in.  god bless.

a relative of mine stayed at this place and it was awful! no meds for 48 hours, he was not seen by a doctor for 2 days. staff at the front desk were unprofessional. some of the staff were nice and helpful. the director i think her name was katherine was awful and not helpful at all. they gave meds that made my relative even worse. this place is pure hell! i felt really bad for the patients. i am glad they seem to finally be closing the place down.
compassionate staff! great nurses and doctors! they're remodeling as well so the interior is much nicer!

where do i start? i took my elderly mom to the er and let's just say, next time we will go to boston! we waited 40 minutes in the waiting room, the triangle nurse, intake folks and ekg tech were really great. they were knowledgeable, helpful and kind. she was moved to a wheelchair in the hallway, and upgraded to a stretcher in said hallway (for the rest of the visit). there was already an elderly lady and her family in the same hallway. a nurse came over, took blood and started an iv. we never were told who my mom's nurse was? another nurse gave mom a warm blanket. the pa seemed irritated that my mom couldn't answer her questions quickly enough. i must have moved my chair 10 times so beds could move past. the kicker is some official (from administration maybe) would float around, not doing much. then they brought a patient in via ambulance and put him from the er stretcher into a chair in the hallway. the kind of hard plastic chair a visitor would use! he got medical care in the hallway too, the same as my mom. only she at least had her intake done in a room first. as for privacy or hippa in that hall? there was none! can i tell you all about that gentleman's name, address and medical history? yes of course, and of course i will not. he did eventually get put into a recliner (which a nurse loudly complained about having to move for him). the place was a zoo....we would have been better off in the waiting room until they had a bed! my cat gets more privacy and better care at the vet. and don't bother to hold a spot on the website. the lady at the desk told someone, "that doesn't work, i don't know why they have it". maybe i should take mom to the vet next time.... couldn't be any worse?

review: i use to work at cardinal hill for almost 13 years and i was able to see change take place so fast that it would keep your head spinning.  the worst change that ever happened to cardinal hill was being bought out by healthsouth/encompass with this brought a decline in the quality of care due to the emphasis no longer being about the patient and their goals but about the revenue.  at this time we lost most of our therapists that were experienced and had grown with cardinal hill.  when i was hired it was viewed as a preveliage to work at this prestigious facility and you were viewed as the best of the best therapist if you worked at cardinal hill because of their outstanding reputation but now their reputation is very poor according to the talk out in the community.  my neighbor choose cardinal hill after a fall because she knew i had worked there and the reputation they had for getting people back up and on their feet again, however the patient requested to leave early and stated she would not put her most valued pet in a facility like that. the management team is the only ones that are given credit for the hospitals progress when it is actually the doctors, nurses, and therapists that work their tails off in order for the hospital to grow and have a reputation for which is now subpar since the hospital was bought out by a for profit company.  management needs to change and so does the company that now owns cardinal hill in order for cardinal hill to regain their outstanding reputation.i personally would not want my family member brought to this rehab facility at this time.  i think i would choose another option like frazier before i would bring them to cardinal hill.
i was pleasantly surprised with the care here. i did have some issues with the case manager but the nurses, doctors and therapists are all very caring and knowledgeable.

i came to the er with my son and i. he was very sick and i was struggling with a lot of things as well. they have given medication to me and my son. and plans did change and my other kid had to get to school. the one thing is that a nurse came in here telling me that she had to bend rules, telling me that i lied to her, telling me i was putting my son at risk, and also telling me that i would get a dui. so this really bothered me because for one i have two kids and plans always change no matter what. so if northcrest does not contact me i will be making a youtube video with my over million subscribers. and you all will definitely regret it. when someone tells me i'm a bad mom or i'm putting my kid at risk just to get a snack. you messed up. and the rn's name is megan. the doctor and everyone else was so kind it was just the nurse that wasn't.

went to the er for kidney pain, haven't went to the doctors for anything since i needed shots for school so you know it was bad. got some type of iv medicine for the pain and a urine test showing blood in my urine. was told i had kidney stones. gave me a prescription for 10 pain killers and sent on my way 3 hours later. paid $100 there, a $600 bill that came a week later and then another $1100 dollar bill a few weeks after that. i had a 3 month gap in insurance thanks to changing back to my old employment so luckily they have a "$1000 discount" for uninsured people or i would've been even more angry. the $1000 dollar bill was for the "physician" that seen me, seems like they would include that with the first bill but i guess they think they lll just ease into stealing from you

worst hospital ever.  rare 1-star rating from me.  notice all the low ratings.  this is no coincidence.  

arrive at archbold in a honda and you will leave in a hearst.  well understaffed on the floors with incompetent people.  nurses loves to argue with you. morale must be low.  i had to against medical advice "ama" myself to capital medical in tallahasee to avoid my certain death at archbold.  the archbold doctor didn't want to remove my gall bladder.  too risky he said.   capital medical took care of my needs before certain death had i stayed in thomasville.   
archbold has a bad habit of putting false information in medical records to cover themselves.  nurses take 30 to 45 minutes to get your drugs to you.  they expect you to tell them when your drugs are due.  really?    if you call 30 minutes early they say it's not time.  then you call them at 4:00 for your meds and you are lucky to get them by 4:45 after 2 calls to the desk.    this is rampant at archbold.  no matter who is in the hospital, it is their norm.  that's what computers and clocks are for.  
they insisted my son raise his hospital window  shades during the day because it was "policy".   he wanted to sleep.  they still raised them out of spite.  then i lowered them. 
i've always been told to "stay ahead of the pain" by continued use of pain meds.  but no, if you are asleep they won't administer pain meds.  then you wake up in pain and it's 45 minutes before the meds get to your bedside.  now you are way behind the curve on pain.  it's because their "policy to not wake you for pain meds".   but wait, it's now 4 hours late and the nurse has five pills on her cup.  so they don't wake you for your other meds either.   that's because they won't wake you for any pills.  you could stay in a room and be dead for half a day if it wasn't for the blood pressure and temperature lpn coming around to wake you or check your pulse. 

like i said:  go to archbold in a honda and check out in a hearst.  just go to capital medical who is a for-profit hospital managed by hospitals of america.  they all a well oiled machine with exceptional protocol procedures and a paperless system that can't be beat.

once again this place is so unorangized been here for 2 hours for a 15 minute procedure. she was taken back for x-ray 40 minutes ago told would take 10-15 minutes. these people must take valium when they come to work. i do not think they have a clue how to schedule procedures. let you be 10 minutes late and they charge you for a missed appointment. this place is a joke.

majority of the time when you are sick you become inpatient and want to be seen immediately. it's not how the er works. high acuity patients come first. i've been in the er for several hours now but the nurses have been amazing. i can tell it's been a very hectic morning and afternoon for these hard working nurses but through the midst of all the chaos they have shown compassion for me constantly.


thank you clovis community nurses.

i like taking the healthquest seminars at the h . marcus radin conference room here at the clovis community medical center. parking in the parking structure is free, close enough to the conference room, the room is spacious and clean, the restrooms are clean . 

. so far i've taken three seminars here , one on skin cancer prevention , neurological diseases prevention and the cardiovascular disease prevention   all three seminars were interesting ,informative  and well put. the physicians were great speakers, it wasn't boring ,  one hour seminar  went fast. 

those seminars are free to the public in the community and i really appreciate it.  

commuunityhealthquest.org for more info.

we came to clovis community medical center today for a procedure my husband was having at the outpatient care center. i was impressed with the friendliness and professionalism of the staff at the hospital. the buildings have lots of natural light and are very well appointed. i had lunch at the everts bistro on the first floor. they serve gourmet sandwiches, wraps salads and fresh pastries. i was happily surprised that they also serve peet's coffee.  the quality of the food was excellent!  i chose a rice bowl with noodles instead of rice, asian vegetables and chicken. it was very tasty and good.  stop by and have something to eat. you will love it.

we came yesterday, people in the hallways, in a small room 2 patients with their blood work plus another patient with a different  situation.  i am not a nurse, doctor but i feel that i was in a different place,  overwhelmingly.  no privacy at all.    is any one checking the hospitals.   i saw yesterday elderly  , women, children in chairs and all over the place.  i understand  that they are building!!! but also in kaiser and downtown  community  hospital  is the same.  
while hospitals are gaining money from the heath insurance or they are together in this? no one seems to be paying attention  to this new way of service like third world country hospitals.
worst customer service ever! especially the medical record department. i will not deliver there again!

horrible service. horrible service as soon as you walk up to the door. if you don't like your job or want to be there then don't work at the hospital and also you should find staff that are actually helpful that don't act as though they don't even want to see you. so good luck to anyone who even walks in because the white, tall lady at the front doors of the emergency room, on today 2-12-2020, at 5:30 is rude and very unhelpful. so is the asian man at the front door standing with her also. everyone beware of them when you even walk up to the door. thanks for nothing clovis community. also, my mom has been waiting literally since 11 this morning and it's now 6 in the evening. clovis community is amazing at doing nothing and treating their patients like shit! 

also, i don't give any stars but i can't post this without giving a star
i did my surgery here, and the staff members was caring and amazing. they took care of me so much. i went back a week after discharge because my husband has caught the flu.

the clovis community out patient phlebotomist gilbert is the most amazing ever! he is gentle, kind, patient, and i never feel a thing when he draws blood from me. i drive all the way from kingsburg to see him. i am appreciating his presence in the phlebotomy dept and will be back to see him when i need to draw blood. thank you gilbert!

one dr. one. we have been sitting in the er since 11pm. it's now 5am. no test results. nothing. my grandmother fell and her arm is completely black. i ask the nurse why it has been taking so long. she says at night they have one dr. wtf. one dr. the waiting  room is packed and people that should be is psych strapped to beds in the hall screaming and yelling. and there is one dr to treat everyone. absolutely ridiculous. will never be coming here again. going on 6 hours for x-ray results. st agnes  may be a not so fancy place, but they get the job done.

clovis  out patient ob fluid check today - high risk pregnancy, not sure how relaxed i can be with the staff listening to cardi b, maybe a more neutral  station would be a bit more appropriate. the young lady  in training, mary was wonderful but i was not able to catch the other girls name who wasn't to friendly.

worst er to the doctor to the nurses to the staff! was not treated with respect, was not heard or listened too. so unprofessional. i will not be returning to this hospital ever again unless i had no choice and was brought here without my doing! so much to say but no words could express my visit in november of 2019 how horrible my visit was. very disappointing! zero stars! we need more people in the medical industry who truely cares about people!

went to l&d triage because of abdominal pain. the staff rns were very nice, but their fetal heartbeat equipment (which is apparently refurbished equipment) was crap. i'm already on edge because i'm in triage, but it was even worse when the nurse couldn't find the fetal heartbeat for several minutes because the monitor was crap. the nurse said that after having multiple monitors fail and multiple moms freak out about it, she brought up the concern to her management, but management was doing nothing.  i asked our regular doctor about what her thoughts were, re: the caliber of equipment at ccmc, and all she could say was "i don't want to lie to you, it's just ok." i'm now second guessing my decision to have my baby at ccmc because i don't trust that they maintain the best possible equipment.

this is by far the absolute worst hospital i've ever been to in my entire life. from the cleanliness of the bathrooms to the care. absolutely horrible. the first room they tried to put me didn't even have clean sheets on the bed. the second room only had clean sheets, there was blood splatters all over the room. the techs and nurses didn't wash their hands or use hand sanitizer in front of me. no one wore gloves but my sonogram tech. the dr. didn't even know what was going on with me. he tried to tell me i had a cyst on my kidney then later came back and said it was on my ovary. no one read their charts to even see what i came in for. 

i will be contacting hr about the cleanliness of the hospital

review:
i first saw dr. espinosa when i broke my shoulder, then again when i broke my wrist. i had no complaints. my trouble started when i asked him to refer me to a back dr. i had fallen & compressed disk in my back in 2008. my back was really started to hurt again in 2016 the compressed disk blew. dr. winston fong was that dr. he decided i needed a 360* surgery. that involved removing my lower spine & replacing it with a cage. he did that & it was great for less than a month. due to excruciating pain, he went back in & removed a bone spur??! since then my left leg/hip is almost 1-1/2" shorter!! when i mentioned it to fong he said "i do not know why, i did not work on you hip/leg. i only worked on your back." he then sent me to their cast dept. they fit me with a foam lift for my shoe. i missed 2 appts with his office so he fired me as a patient. this dr. fong is very pompous, egotistical, he couldn't admit he screwed up my back. he wouldn't 
even discuss it with me. 
i would never refer this so called surgeon to anybody. instead i would tell you to run from this dr. i'm not the only one he has screwed up for life with this surgery. the surgery was to severe for 1 collapsed disk. now i'm lopsided and in constant pain!!!! instead of trying to repair & help me, he denied any wrongdoing on his part he fired me.

review:
worst hospital ever. my father was brought in here by ambulance. he had no strength, shaking, and was mentally out of it. he was admitted. the next day my sister and i returned in the morning. we were told that no doctor was in his room yet. we left our names and numbers with the nurse as well as on the wipe off board in the room. we told the nurse to have a doctor call us.
 we returned mid afternoon to find our dad with all his meds in the iv bags empty and my dad was laying in soaking bed of urine. we called the nurses 3 times and nobody came. we tried to get an administrator at 4:30 on a saturday and could not get anybody in charge. the helpful lady at the front desk tried to get a hold of a number of people and there was nobody to assist.
stay away  from this hospital, you have been warned.
we were here from wisconsin and need to return home. what do i do with dad.
1 star because i can't give a negative.

the only positive things i can say about this place are that the intake people are super nice and the surgeon (bradley) managed not to kill me during my planned procedure. everything else about my experience at this hospital was terrible, and dont bother registering complaints with patient relations because they do absolutely nothing. no one ever bothered to follow up after i documented my complaints. i suspect the real job of patient relations is to gauge how many people are likely to sue the hospital at any given time. here are more details on my experience: i have more incisions than i was told i would need and the only explanation the dr gave was that it made it more convenient for him. the incisions are larger than necessary according to the manufacturer of the robot that was used for my surgery so they have taken much longer to heal. while the surgery went fine i am still have pain at the incision site two months later and stitches that should have been internal coming to the skin's surface. (i've sought a second option about this and we are managing it, but it boils down to the closure wasnt done well.) the idiot nurse anesthetist (kronour) chipped my tooth and the surgeon claims he told the head of the department and that someone would contact me about the resulting dental expense, and no one did. if  you need surgery and you want a team of medical professionals who have their act together, you will have to look elsewhere. the care here is what i would expect at a free clinic; not as a health insurance-carrying, on-time-bill-payer! just remember that the person with the lowest gpa in a graduating medical class is still called doctor...how scary is that.

salem hospital is the most incompetent hospital around. they missed a heart attack with one person. diagnosed indigestion in another person who had heart issue, my mom died in cardiac icu unit after she was allowed to get up and walk to the restroom alone. non of the doctors know what they are doing in my experience. my recommendation is go to silverton, stayton or ohsu. stay away from salem.

most medical facilities get a bad rap, because unlike a coffee shop or hot new bar, you're going there because you have to deal with some potentially serious medical procedure and not a latte or a beer. along with that is the complications of our healthcare system and the medical-industrial complex and a host of other issues. 

va in specific maybe even has more red tape given that it's a government-run facility. 

all issues considered, they still should hold themselves to some sort of higher standard than the complacency which runs rampant. they are still providing a service, a very important one that everyone will at some point need, and their employees are still getting paid and should be at the very least be able to provide a level of care and human decency--that doesn't change regardless of the budget. 

most of the staff i've had to deal with here, just doesn't seem to care at all about anyone. and i definitely understand it's just a job for them, that they aren't saints, but they are still providing a sort of costumer service, even if they aren't working for tips. 

while it is great that veterans have a place for free and reduced cost medical services, it's still sad that the men & women who served our country have to settle for such treatment. 

the medical system as a whole has issues that won't be taken care of with a simple fix, but if the right people are in charge and holding people accountable; i think they can all take steps toward improvement.

something that tosh has that other clinics typically don't have is an olympic-sized pool. this has been excellent for my spinal surgery recovery. there are options to see a therapist in the pool, and after "graduating" from the therapist sessions, there is an option for an independent program.  lance is the exercise specialist (he rocks!!), and he is able to provide additional exercises to complement the routine from the therapists. you pay a monthly fee for the independent program, and it has been a lifesaver for me!  there are both morning and evening hours available, which works well for my work schedule.

my only complaint is how much the pt services cost.  a pool session with a therapist cost me $300 for an hour (with insurance), which is completely unaffordable.  a few years back, someone in the office told me that i should look into other offices because tosh charges so much more.  (the exception is the independent pool program, which is very affordable).  just something to keep in mind if you have a high deductible plan.

i was a patient at harbor oaks hospital many times in the adolescent (pediatric) section. your personal freedom here is pretty much deprived, as it is in most places. you have limited access to your clothes, hygiene material, books, anything used to help or regulate yourself. try to bring pg books, they won't be hesitant to take away any 'graphic' material (non-gut-churning material such as stephen king is not allowed, neither are books on psychology/mental health, or books with tragedy (drug addiction, mental health crisis, suicide, etc) as it is assumed other patients will read your materials. if lucky, the nurses/behavioral techs will take pity on your situation and let you have some of your 'graphic' books and the like. 
anyway, harbor oaks. not the best hospital. treatment is less than mediocre or adequate. no interacting with the opposite sex, which i can understand, although they don't stop children from butting into a situation such as phone calls, a personal matter with the nurses/behavioral techs, or whatever. children, if not enough beds on their side, will be housed on the teen girls' side. not the best choice. they will put transgenders on whichever side their sex at birth is. no lgbt rights whatsoever yet they won't stop patients from telling you graphic details of their sexual assault/abuse. being abused is a horrible thing and to be dealing with that, and have someone whom you've first met tell you their graphic details of abuse, is not something i enjoyed, and i wouldn't expect anyone to enjoy this either. the interaction with the same sex is not monitored. 
the food is not terrible, although what they promise for dinner is the opposite you receive. for example, if they promise cookies/cake/brownies, you may get gelatin or something of that sort. 
the social worker, eva, is inadequate and treats her adolescent patients like they are children. there are groups 2-4 times a day, and you will be frequently bored, no matter what they tell you. there is rarely treatment that addresses destructive behaviors or any other disorder besides clinical depression/persistent depressive disorder. if that is your issue, go to this hospital. if you struggle with something more complex, such as childhood abuse, destructive behaviors, eating disorders, personality disorders, etcetera, spend your money someplace else. 
they'll dope you up to as far as 600 m.g, morphing you into a zombie. you get no say in your aftercare or treatment in general. 
the average stay here, from what i remember, is 5-9 days. sometimes longer, sometimes shorter. the shortest i saw someone stay was 3-4 days, the longest, 13. it depends on your behavior and why you're there in the first place. 
the psychiatrist, dr. sanjeev venkataraman, (dr. raman, for short) can be pretty empty and fail to explain why you need a certain medication or give you an estimate for your discharge date. like most treatment facilities, more often than not, you will gain weight. the staff and psychiatrists will not care; you will be punished for not eating. 
your discharge date will likely be on a weekday. the psychiatrists rarely work on weekends. 
the groups range from rec. therapy (walking/exercising mindlessly in the adult gym for about an hour, making bracelets), and others. i cannot recall, as they were unimportant then and still unimportant now as i fail to remember them or their contents. 
the majority of adolescents were there for suicidal ideation. i wouldn't recommend sending your adolescent child here for substance abuse, as i recall, you are unable to mention anything related to addiction whatsoever. send them to a therapist. teen rehabs are disgusting and used for clout.
i don't know if harbor oaks made me worse in terms of suicidal ideation and destructive behaviors, though i know because of this facility and others, i've gained weight. this has sent my self-esteem to an all-time low. 
there have been reports of child abuse throughout this facility. i never saw or heard of anything like that whilst i was there multiple times. only after it'd been months after i left the most recent time i'd been there did i hear about a young child being slammed to the floor and getting a concussion. 
visitation times are, from what i recall, 3-5 times a week. phone calls twice a day, ten minutes. parents choose your contact list. only immediate family. 
as i mentioned you get no say in your aftercare and will likely be sent to a new oakland face to face location. this program, in particular, is pretty gross and please advocate for your rights. tell your parents not to send you. 
try to talk to your child before sending them away. sending them to a treatment facility such as harbor oaks may make them worse. do your research, don't believe everything you hear.

it's weird to write a review about kaiser, but, here i go. 

i gave birth to our daughter at kaiser and really glad that i did! kaiser has an extremely low c-section rate and the kaiser in san jose has a bunch more midwives than the one in santa clara, which means that more of the deliveries are actually done by midwives, rather than obgyns. obgyns take care of the births that may have some complications. 

i ended up having a c-section (breech positioned baby!) and dr. sheila loanzon was awesome. it felt like my daughter was born, being surrounded by strong and kind women, and i wouldn't have asked for a better experience. i was part of their centering pregnancy group, which was led by sandy pineda, and while i didn't feel like i learned new information, it was a great way to build community. one of the other people who assisted the group, lex, made sure to be part of the c-section/delivery, and it was so relieving to have a familiar face from that group. 

the postpartum care nurses were pretty good, but i did have to call them rather than them check on me a ton. my recovery was great, and even though i wasn't keen on having a c-section, kaiser made the whole experience easy.
