i've had many procedures done at this hospital but had never had an overnight stay. my most recent procedure was my hysterectomy where dr. lewis schulman performed the procedure with the da vinci robot.  let me tell you folks my recovery was excellent the staff is outstanding, the nurses were caring and went above and beyond to make sure my recovery  went smoothly. i was extremely impressed with every person i encountered even the cleaning staff was respectful and courteous. this hospital was by far the best hospital ever! the food was delicious, if you have a stay ann's you get to eat the food eat the filet mignon, yes i said filet mignon cooked to perfection! my nurses were the very best they made sure i had plenty of ice packs to reduce my swelling and that my pain was managed around the clock! this hospital deserves an award for not only having the best staff but for having the most advanced technology available to patients!

after seeing the specialist at uab, he confirmed that i not only was misdiagnosed but did not even meet the criteria required to make the diagnosis. $1,500 out of pocket costs and there wasn't anything wrong with me. another lesson learned - always get a second opinion.

i ended up here a few months ago w/ severe abdominal cramping.  went to the er and had blood drawn and a "gi cocktail" given to me.  i was sent home an hour later w/ medical grade tums and nausea medicine.  told to follow up w/ a gi doctor the following week.  i was not relieved of any of the cramping. 2 hours later i had to be driven back to another er closer to work and was immediately given a ct scan which showed twisted bowels.  i then spent the next 4 days getting my bowels corrected and was discharged.  i called grandview to dispute the charges since the er doctor neglected to give proper care and literally put my life in danger sending me back home.  had he taken the necessary steps and requested a simple ct scan i would of been admitted immediately knowing the correct diagnosis and therefore getting it resolved.  grandview denied my request and i paid the bill anyways.  i do not recommend this hospital due to inadequate care, aka rushing me in and out without properly diagnosing the real issue.

i feel weird posting 5 stars because i have only completed a hospital tour as part of a childbirth class. however, i'm worried that after i deliver our baby, the last thing i'll be thinking about is reviewing the hospital on yelp so i'm going by the initial thoughts just based on the tour. the labor and delivery floor is beautiful. when you get off the elevator into the lobby it feels like you've walked into a day spa. the labor and delivery rooms are beautiful. there are 4 large rooms with windows and gorgeous tubs (with a shower head also) for mothers to labor in. there are several rooms that are just as large with a shower, no tub and other smaller rooms with a shower and no tub. the smaller rooms did not have a small pullout couch for dads to sleep on, but i think they had recliners. the postpartum floor (i think called maternity) was just a beautiful but the rooms are much smaller. i do feel that it's more important to have a larger, more comfortable room to labor in. the labor and delivery rooms have birthing balls, peanut balls, birthing bars, and crazy adjustable beds, along with tvs and music. i was told all the equipment is available in all the rooms. i am attaching photos because i tried to find pics online before our visit and couldn't. i did not snap any photos of the smaller room. they also have nitrous oxide available for pain management. hope this helps!

my dad had knee replacement surgery.  all was well in pre-op. everyone was kind and we got things moving quickly.  we put his belongings in a bad and the nurse put them in the locker.  after he was done, he spent about 2 hours in post-op before coming to his patient room. 
when he did arrive in his room, i noticed his belongings bag did not come with him. i asked the nurse if they could go back and get it, (we needed his phone).  after they got him settled in the room, we asked again if the belongings were coming.  they said they will call pre-op again.  about an hour later, still nothing.  i finally went to the post-op nursing station and asked him to call them again.  he did and nobody answered.  so, i had to walk down there on my own, go to the lockers and request someone to get my dad's things.  this was annoying.

great hospitality in hospital staff! will listen to your needs and very patient with you too. we had to take in our kiddo christmas morning because we didnt know what was going on with him. nurse staff brought him a lil stocking that made him smile. very thoughtful about the patient's guests that stay there too. highly recommend this hospital! very clean and calm environment.

so i called trying to reach a patient that was admitted yesterday and the woman that answered the phone couldn't find the patient in the system and she was very short with me and unpleasant. she acted like i was bothering her. i gave her the room number and last name and she still couldn't find the patient! i remembered the patient had a cell phone so i ended up calling the cell phone to reach the patient.  the patient did not move rooms at all so i don't know why the lady answering the phone can't do her job correctly! maybe they should hire someone who knows how to do their job correctly and pleasantly.

my son went there after being sick for over a month and had 3 other hospital stays during that time. this was the second visit to osu. the first time he was there for 48 hrs, this time it was the same. a previous hospital stay at another facility was for 9 days. no one has been able to diagnose the root cause of his illness, but other places have at least tried. osu has been unwilling to try to find the cause and has only treated the symptoms. for a teaching hospital one would think they would be interested in a perplexing case, but no, they are not. could it be because my son is disabled and lives on ssi and medicaid? makes me wonder. perhaps they will find the cause at this autopsy. he is failing, has lost 35 pds in 50 days, cannot care for himself, and i'm being told he's got acid reflux and will be fine to go home. standard of care, proper diagnosis, proper treatment of that diagnosis are all missing from this institution. they must get a lot of malpractice suits.

please don't go here, unless you want to die. this place is terrible and almost killed my husband. we went there three times when he was having major symptoms, and they basically told him not to come back because there was nothing wrong with him. the next day he was turning yellow so i took him straight to lvhn.  they diagnosed him with sepsis and he was going into septic shock. he also had c diff.  he had diarrhea the days we went into the er, and it was black. i told the nurse, but they refused to do a stool sample. 
my husband is alive today thanks to lvhn. absolutely no thanks to st. lukes.  again, don't come here or bring your family to this terrible place called a hospital.

i came down with the flu (which was super harsh this year) and visited the garfield er. everyone there was super friendly and accommodating. i was seen quickly and was well taken care of. my nurse marlin was amazing- very kind and attentive. although i was in a lot of pain and discomfort, the er team worked diligently to ensure i could attain a semblance of comfort under their care. 
i noticed a lot of people only leave reviews for hospitals when they have a very negative experience. the reality is, these hard-working people dedicate their lives to provide a service to help others heal. let's give them the love and recognition they greatly deserve!

review:
nothing in life is more irritating than when a billing dept. contacts you with a price that is significantly lower than the price presented to you from your healthcare insurance provider.  

prior to being rendering services at this location, i was contacted by billing and was presented with the amount of $738.72 as well as a request for payment.  mind you, this is before being rendered services; hence my insurance had not yet been billed.  aggravating, i know.

then, when i go check in, the same amount was listed in their system; and then after being rendered services, an estimate w/ that same amount was sent to me via usps; with a request for payment.  

meanwhile, i decided to go and check my claim through my healthcare insurance provider and i see an amount of $1,684 for the same services; as the amount of my deductible.  i call my insurance and inform them that i was presented with an amount that was less than 50% than the amount displayed on their portal; only to be told that that is the accurate amount that i will be responsible for.  so what happens next, you ask...

i file a grievance through my healthcare insurance and then contact the attorney general's office; even though i know deep down inside that not a damn thing is going to change what has happened.  i wait to hear back from either or; and below and behold i hear back from my healthcare insurance provider with the lame explanation of:  " in review of your grievance, i brought your case to the attention of a svh patient access operations director, who appreciated being made aware of your concern. the director stated that you were provided an estimate based off the cpt code that was going to be used during the procedure. the director stated that the estimate is subject to change if the provider in question uses a different service code (cpt code) or adds any services..."  

ok...let me start off by saying... that in the world of business, i have witnessed estimates being different by either 10-20%... and the differential is usually written on the estimate to let the customer know.  
in this case, the amount was over a 50% difference and nowhere was it listed that the amount could be significantly higher... also too, where it was an "estimate" then they truly had no flippin' business requesting payment in the first place.

seriously... the poor business displayed by the billing department is unbelievable and the fact that they can get away with, what other companies cannot, is repulsive.  i mean,  would you allow a company to bill you a price that is significantly higher than the price you were originally presented with?  would they not have to honor that lower price?

i thought so... 

so with all due respect, what makes this situation any different?  it may be the medical field, but it's still a business...and well the same rules should still have to apply... 

needless to say... i am not in the least bit impressed and if i have my way, i will be taking my medical needs elsewhere in the future.
fac_name: Saint Vincent Hospital At Worcester Medical Center

review: been here 3 days, had a severe infection, was suppose to be admitted through the er to have a drain tube placed in my kidney, got to er at 3pm, wasn't until 7pm i got a room because nobody knew anything of course, wasn't until 9pm i got my surgery and the dress were joking about how they had been there since 7am and were so tired and out of it that they forgot to push the button on the elevator, made me feel real safe knowing they were about to cut into my kidney! then finding a nurse or a dr is impossible, there are no doctors or nurses on the floor until after 7pm, only people before that are nurses aids and they can't do anything but check vitals. i literally laid in pain all day yesterday because nobody was around to give me pills until 7pm the dr finally ordered tordol. today i was suppose to be released and have a 1.5cm stone removed in iowa city tomorrow but had to cancel tomorrow because there was no doctor around today to release me... this place sucks, i'm walking out and will never ever be back!! 4 people have died here just in the 3 days i have been here and it's because there are no doctors or nurses around! they leave nurses aids in charge of everything!!

mercy's getting 5 stars cause of awesome  doctors & nurses that have helped me & my friend every time we go & the blood  draw station staff that say hello & ask how's things are and now & then tell a joke. my illness keeps me from doing a lot i get tired quick if i do to much at one time. but thanks to everyone at mercy hospital  the staff the coffee shop there & yes the cafeteria staff & the food they put out thank you for making our day brighter. godspeed god bless  merry christmas

so we when to the er because my dad had a heartattack  and they got everything done really fast and then when they took a x-ray it was correct but it took a little longer then they expected but they got everything tooken care of and the way to make it fast is calling the hospital before going then you'll be out of there in no time!!

my wife went to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain.  the doctor ran cardiac and lung tests and the doctor said everything was normal and she could go home. she then asked the doctor about the symptom she actually came in with - the abdominal pain. the doctor was reluctant to test further but at my wife's insistence he finally agreed to an ultrasound. sure enough they found gallstones.

they ran the same ultrasound tests and saw the same medical readings (gallstones, same size) . but instead of suggesting she wait, they put her into emergency surgery. 

afterward the lab results showed the gall bladder was infected and severely inflamed and life threatening.

if in orange county id recommend st. joseph's in orange psychiatric unit for adults and uci's in orange for adolescents. my stay in 2018's st.joseph's in orange was much more therapeutic and have successfully remained outside the hospital since then. i'd like to think college hospital is was the start of mental health wellness road. now i go to a support group once a week and have a great psychiatrist and therapist.l

it's been now one year since i stepped foot outside this hospital when i was placed on a hold for attempting suicide last year. it's bad enough living with what i tried to do and even worse remembering what happened to me while in the care of this hospital. i'd like to start off saying that i'm still not fully okay or better but i have been getting professional help (not what this place at all provides) each day gets better but some days are a struggle. i feel like it is extremely important to speak out about this so that no women, or man ever goes through what i did and can possibly save themselves from going here if you're needing help. on arrival i was terrified and in an extreme fragile state. i had no clothes and was given only a hospital gown that was open in the back. when i said i didn't feel comfortable being exposed like this in front of male patients, a male staff said to me "only the privileged are allowed clothing" after that i sat in a chair terrified and lost for a couple of hours until another staff noticed me and found a place to put me. the first room they put me in i was attacked by a female patient. i was moved to another room with other women but across the hall was a room full of men. once again i politely pleaded for clothing so i didnt feel exposed. i told another staff member i didn't feel safe sleeping or resting in any open room near grown men with nothing but a sheet covering me. the staff member said no and that nothing was going to happen to me and if so to just scream and they'd come running. i kept to myself the rest of the night, i pretty much stayed in the bed they gave me the whole time because i didn't feel comfortable walking around in a gown with nothing on underneath. while keeping to myself, sitting in bed, reading a self help book for guidance someone had entered the room. i didnt look up to see who it was because i was reading and was scared and to nervous to be social with anyone there. the person who had entered the room then walked straight up to my bed side, hovering over me. it was a man. he was clearly mentally ill but he towered over me. i'm 4'11 and he was at least 6'2. i froze and was terrified. the man exposed himself to me and grabbed my head, shoving me into his private area. he had one had gripping my jaw and his other hand on the back of my head. when he tried to shove me down on the bed i fought and screamed. i broke free and ran out of the room crying. i ran straight to the front office desk, i collapsed and broke down struggling to explain what had happened. none of the staff members were sympathetic or kind! one even said "oh that must have been (whoever the male patients name was) and thought you were (some other female patients name) which only made me come to the conclusion that this had happen before and they allowed it to happen. after hearing that i demanded to make a phone call and be released. i stated that i no longer felt safe and that i will not be staying in this unsafe environment. i told them to call 911 because i was sexually assaulted and if they didn't they were refusing my rights. they immediately got a psychiatric doctor to come talk to me. i explained all of this again to him, all my concerns and fears. he didn't listen to me at all. in fact he laughed at me and threatened me. he said "just because a man exposed himself to you does not mean you were sexually assaulted. he didn't put his fingers in you, he didn't enter you. if you do not calm down i will sign these papers and have you kept here for two more weeks." i cried my eyes out and he didn't care at all, all he did was sign me a paper for medication without even acknowledging i have a severe heart condition and some meds can literally kill me. i did as i was told. i was just one woman, already hurting from my personal issues but now feeling broken by people who were supposed to help me. i took whatever meds they gave me. i was hoping they made a mistake and id slip into unconsciousness and eventually die. everything was extremely fuzzy and i hardly remembered much after that, all i know is that the meds made me feel like a zombie for a couple days. i do however remember that they refused to feed me because i wouldn't leave my room. they demanded i eat in the same room as the men who sexually assaulted me.

i had hip replacement february 4, 2020 and have no complaints. i was treated with great care by all. friendly service, meds and treatment well explained, and thoughtful care by all!
thanks to all of you!

on 12/11/19 your front office staff was so incredibly cruel and unkind to my dad, i am shaking with anger. this obviously does not matter but i will never, ever in my life utilize this facility if ever needed in the future, and if i ever hear of your name in passing, i will be sure to pass along how disgusting your staff treats people.

i was a student at this facility, there to learn for nursing school. while i wasn't an admitted patient, i got to see the inner workings everything going on in the facility for many days and was so impressed. i had never been in a mental health facility before and felt like the staff cared so much, the patients seemed well taken care of and listened to, and the facility was very clean and all extra precautions were taken. the group therapies were touching and run by incredibly passionate people who care deeply about the patients. they are doing the best they can with how rough it is for most patients to be admitted there. i saw a lot of maintenance happening too. i stand behind all of their values and how they run this facility.

there are some small pros to this place, they generally keep you safe and some of the staff really does care, the groups are usually good and the therapists that run them are amazing. but everything else is so low quality. the food is made on the start of the week and then re-served every other day till it runs out, i was and still don't expect 5 star food but stale bread and cake and re-using food throughout the week is just, not good? do not expect 1 on 1 therapy cause you will not get it- period. you talk to a psychiatrist but they don't remember each patient, they are so overloaded with (up to 30)kids- they can't personalize treatment in anyway. they are extremely irresponsible with meds, there were kids who would not take their meds and hide them for later and they in no way tried to prevent this. the psychiatrists would also forget who you were, why you were there, what they are doing with meds, etc they took me off all my meds which is and was not ok in any way, they then told me and my mom that it was our fault i was off all my meds because we "refused" any medication which is not true. then there is the not so good staff, the staff who make side handed comments about patients and their parents in front of other patients, staff who have no mental health training or experience and think that telling hysterical patients to "calm down" and that "it gets better" or to just sedate them - is a cure. the staff who tell you they are "busy with other things" and that they can't help you because there are other - more important things - than your care. they want you in and out and expect 72+ hours to heal everything wrong with your mental state. i was there for 15 days, three days before i got released, i self harmed and was on a m5 and a one on one. they then, during my second family meeting, made me leave the room and told my mom that i was getting "to comfortable" and that i was "having a blast" on the unit- they also told them that our insurance is no longer covering my stay, this is where the nightmare really started. i talked to my social worker once she was done having that conversation and she went ahead and told me exactly what she made me leave the room for- that insurance isn't covering my stay and that i will need to be discharged asap- regardless of the fact that i just got off of a 1 on 1 and was still on a m5. they then called my mom the next day and with no advanced notice, told her that she needed to be there, that day, from 6-8. my mom has a job and could not do that so she just drove over right away. my mom called me and told me this was happening and so i asked staff for help to get my stuff ready and they told me that they needed to handle other patients, before they could handle me because i was "not a priority at the moment". then i answered honestly, told them i was still suicidal and that i was still depressed and they wrote a note on a paper saying that i agreed to staying safe and that i know how to get to a er if needed, instead of , i don't know, giving me proper care. then, the day after i get released, we get a call from insurance. stating that they found it medically necessary for me to stay in highlands and that they were willing to pay for it. so not only did they release me when i was of safety concern and when it was deemed medically necessary for me to stay, they lied to us about our insurance coverage and essentially told my parents that i was faking my symptoms to get to stay longer. we are getting a lawyer, this isn't even all of the things that happened there. this place is just generally not a good place to seek care and i would strongly recommend avoiding it. also: if you care about the person you are sending here, please be careful if they refer you to residential treatment. they attempted to send me to some of the most notoriously abusive and crappy places as soon as they could because they just wanted me gone.

this review is for the dental department!

va dental is much harder to qualify for than medical. if you're 100% disabled, then you're in there and it's free. such a blessing! 

cons: my only complaint is that i have to go to la jolla. there isn't a dental facility at the mission valley location, which sucks for people like me who live in otay (near aquatica). this can mean 1-1.5 hour commute in the morning. but again, it's free, so i'm definitely making the drive. 

i'm new to va dental (as of january 2020) and have had the absolute best experience so far. i called to set my initial intake appointment and they were booked out six months so my appointment would be in june 2020. i thought that was insane, but the truth is that people call in and cancel their appointments everyday. don't let this discourage you! let me explain...

i had a dental emergency and the front desk staff instructed me to come into their walk-in clinic that opens at 0800 i believe. she told me to check in at 0730 and i'd be the first seen. i did that and it turned out that i had an infection from a year old root canal. they put me on antibiotics and scheduled me with their top endodontist, dr. sulter!  i am such a baby when it comes to procedures, even shots! i literally l got sick before the appointment just getting nervous about it. dr. sulter and her assistant were fantastic! they have been there together for 10 years. they were extremely concerned about my comfort and did everything possible to ease my worries. they were extremely gentle too...i didn't feel the shots! i found out that i have extremely long roots that a previous dentist didn't clean correctly. she prescribed me a stronger antibiotic due to what she found and some yeast infection medicine due to the antibiotic side effects on me. this is the first dentist to do this for me!!

i had another tooth that was a bootcamp root canal that was never crowned and finally crack to the point of missing half the tooth. she took it upon herself to schedule me the following week to take care of it. she also referred and authorized me to see an amazing dentist out in town because i need a special procedure done on one tooth. i also told her about my front tooth that had been bothering me.  i cracked my tooth on deployment and the good ol navy dental covered it up with a yellow color while my teeth are extremely white. it's so embarrassing! she referred me to dr. henz, who personally called me the next day.

dr.  henz was able to schedule me in for my intake appointment first, which meant i didn't have to wait til june. when i tell you guys...the most thorough dental exam ever! her assistant was awesome too even though he's a vikings fan, go bears! in the same week, she scheduled me for impressions on one of my root canals for a crown. the other needs a crown lengthening procedure that they had to send me out in town for. i've already seen that dentist as well and will have the procedure done next week with a month of healing time. 

on the same day as my intake appointment, i went to the front desk to schedule a cleaning. they told me it wouldn't be til september (keep in mind, it's now january). what can i do? another lady  told her to wait because she was sure there was a cancellation in march. then another lady said she was cancelling an appointment that same day in about 30 minutes and asked if i'd like to take it....uhhh absolutely! the front desk staff are awesome and they really work together!

i got my teeth cleaned by oscar i believe and he did an amazing job. the best part about him, dr. sulter, and dr. henz is that they all walked me through the process and educated me about cleaning my teeth properly, recommended products, and gave tips on maintaining my wisdoms. i have all of my adult teeth and this is the only dental facility that didn't try to have me wisdoms removed due to possible "hygiene" problems or telling me i'd get crooked teeth, mine are straight! 

all of this happened during the month of january! if you be need to get in sooner, you can! you have to call up there though...cancellations happen all the time and the staff encourage you to call them and check.

don't be discouraged by someone's horror story of navy dental, the va has the latest technology and new or not,  their staff is educated!

love that some individuals that work here care about the veterans and thank them for all they do!

for disabled veteran's the vamc is a great choice as it is free based on your combined disability rating. what many veteran's do not know is that if you have over a 30% medical disability rating you qualify for "free" medical insurance through the va. i fall into this category and i have always been taken care of, but you have to be patient. this is such a busy medical center and san diego is a major hub for veterans that you often have to wait 3-4 weeks for any appointment made. did this reason i also pay for private medical insurance through my work. i find this to be very beneficial because my private health care provider can get my seen quickly and diagnosed. based on the diagnosis (cost of treatment) i schedule the my surgeries and procedures through them at no cost to myself. 

my suggestion for those who qualify for the free medical insurance is to get enrolled asap. it takes some time to get the process started and to get an established va health care primary provider so get to work! this coverage pays off, but be proactive and get enrolled prior to needing urgent medical attention. following the approval process and referral process can be very time consuming and annoying so if it is within your budget carry dual coverage (private). use the medical notes from your private provider to skip levels and expatiate the va medical process. 

overall i have to give the service a 4 star rating. i love that they take care of veterans and i have seen improvements every year.

advised her i could send her what was written as it did not make sense to me either.  which leads me to question who's chart were you looking at writing my child a rx.   by this time we were done it should not stress the family out dealing with a facility when you are just trying to get your child help.  it is abysmal how bad mental health care is in this society.  they were also supposed to have a person inn charge of helping them keep up with school work in the few hours they have per day to do that.  this position was vacant most of the time my child was there or if not vacant no one did help.  we are on the list of the dell iop.  hopefully this will be a better situation.  best wishes to all of you navigating a stressful situation.

not sure if i got lucky, if it's the er department in particular, or if the reviews here swing negative because--let's be honest--a lot of patients are in highly stressful and emotional situations when they write these, but i got good vibes from this place. 

in fact, i overheard some conversations between coworkers (my room was by some kinda reception desk), and from what i can deduce, it sounds like they have a healthy workplace culture where the staff is genuinely invested in the wellbeing of their colleagues + patients & quality of their work. 

a rare thing when modern western medicine is characterized by uncaring, clinical coldness.

keep doing what you do, er team!

p.s. regarding all these reviews about payment problems...the fault typically lies with your insurance and not the healthcare provider. over the past decade+, patients have been forced to shoulder more and more of the burden of healthcare bills because insurance companies are covering less and less. medical billing & collections is an ugggggly thing, and the heinous greed of for-profit insurance corps is to blame.

the mission er intake nurse is the worst. i'm not even sure if he has the credentials to make any medical decisions. he minimized the state my female family member was in, and not only got fussy with her when he asked in an annoyed tone if she "..saw her doctor, called her doctor, or went to urgent care first." he then accused her of not having treated her injury prior to coming to the er. we then asked another intake nurse who didn't have a chip on his shoulder if we should just go to urgent care, even after showing him her injury explaining the length of time it had been like that. he said yes, we should go to urgent care. 

we left and went to urgent care and the doctor was shocked at the injury and said we should have gone to the er. we explained that we were just there and they didn't think the injury was a big deal. now my family member is at saddleback with a major infection that is moving up her leg and on iv antibiotics, expecting to stay multiple days. 

great job mission er! 

thanks for minimizing her injury and compromising her health even more.

hello my name is jessica 
i honestly have a great experience been here for about 2 times , but when i came in for the er there was a lady that was really rude  but honestly jarri made up for it his such a amazing guy  and the rest doctors are great people just one advice get better people in the front , other that great amazing staffs

do not give birth at this hospital! i gave birth to my daughter at this hospital and at some point during her birth, her collar bone was broken! none of the doctors or nurses caught this! i was discharged from this hospital only 24 hours after giving birth. all doctors and nurses telling me she was completely fine. shortly after we were discharged i took my newborn to the er and they then told me her collar bone was broken. 

it's absolutely ridiculous that out of all the doctors and nurses that saw us during her birth and stay at this hospital that none of them caught this! their one job is to make sure my baby came into this world safely and they couldn't even do that! how could they just let us leave saying she was fine? my newborn daughter was neglected!!! numerous people dropped the ball here and it's not okay!

my mom and i came in because she is having horrible pain in her side. multiple people have gone after her even though she's been here the longest out of everyone. i decided to ask the nurse in this photo if she knew how much longer. (no attitude what so ever just want to make sure my mom is ok.) and this woman was just like i just got here so i don't know (in a very rude tone) and just gave me a bitchy stare until i walked away. literally all i was asking for was an estimate. that's it. i'm sorry your life sucks and you have to be rude, but thank god you brought a christmas headband because that's what really matters instead of helping people. (now they're talking bad about previous patients they had and how they don't care if they have a bad attitude.) this hospital is a joke.

my review is of a specific department at mission hospital, the pediatric intensive care unit (picu). my granddaughter was recently hospitalized with pneumonia. she has a number of ongoing medical issues that require specialized daily care, so she was kept in the picu for all 13 days of her stay.

i was very impressed by the caring and thorough care that my granddaughter received. the doctors, especially dr. goodman, and all of the picu nurses, were absolute professionals. this was a very trying time for our family, we were all sick to some degree (it's flu season) and it was a real challenge for us to be at the hospital 24/7. the nurses gave us so much moral support. respiratory therapists james and mike were excellent and provided much needed therapies multiple times day and night. 

this is not the first time my granddaughter has been hospitalized, she's spent way too much of her 6 years in hospitals. the care she received at mission picu was exemplary and our family thanks all the staff for their hard work, skill, and dedication.

my doctor sent me to mission hospital in mission viejo for a "stat" mri of my neck.

upon arrival at the mri desk a young lady wanted to know my appointment time. i told her i didn't have one as my doctors office contacted them and told them of his emergency request. they should have been expecting me but she said she had no info. then she blamed the doctors office for not contacting them properly.

i showed my paperwork to the lady. she said they were double booked with appointments and couldn't help me or see me as a patient and refused my dr's request for a "stat" mri.  ??? seriously? ?wow...
i don't care if they're double or triple booked i would think a "stat"request is a priority over routine appointments

she did call mission hospital at laguna beach and told me to go there and  maybe they could get me in. she faxed my paperwork to them at the laguna beach location so she was helpful in that respect.

i was at mission to celebrate the arrival of my sister in laws baby girl. 

the security in the ward was great, driver's license to get to the elevator, buzz door to get onto the ward. the rooms were good with that hospital look and smell and baby successfully popped out in time for me to have breakfast.

unfortunately, my husband is accident prone so we have had to visit here quite frequently. while some things during our visit were unpleasant (let's be honest that's to be expected) some of the staff did a wonderful job and really went out of their way to help us. i don't want to go into details because i don't want to get anyone in trouble for breaking the rules, but honestly these people really care about you. i think the negative reviews come from the fact that people don't think to review a hospital unless they have a negative experience. also, the people complaining about the wait please remember this is a trauma hospital. unfortunately, when you go to the hospital for a non life threatening issue you might have to wait while doctors save people's lives...wow shocking!

very unprofessional staff!my aunt got admitted into the hospital and they found out she had brain tumor. after the surgery, they lied to us saying the condition was benign and we shouldnt worry but after a few days, they decided to tell us it was a malignant condition and she only has a year to live. even when we demanded to talk to the doctor, they could not get us in contact with him and were wishy washy about anything they told us. they did not seem like they knew what they were doing! one of the nurses told us even the wrong location my aunt would be relocated to. multiple times they would tell us one thing but it would be something else. i do not trust anything that these nurses say!

went to mission hospital radiology to have a biopsy for my wife. had the pleasure of having dr kevin burns and his assistant, diane perform the procedure.  he was very knowledgeable, had an amazing bedside manner.  he would be my go to doctor for any radiology or vascular issues.

i have 1 complaint and 1 advice:

complaint: we received discharged papers despite vitals showing really high heart rate.

this is the worst hospital to ever be admitted to . beware!!! these people have no compassion, love or care nurses should have. worst bed side manner. unethical and should be shut down for insurance fraud. this place is a joke, they'll lie to you, steal from you, and treat loved ones awful.

it's to bad that i had to erase over half the review. but now that i haven't slept in a few nights i have no energy to write anymore.
hope we leave  tomorrow. i don't appreciate being made to feel worried to ask for anything, or worried abt pushing the button for help for my son. who wants to just get thru it and get out, he doesn't want to ask for anything.
what kind of caring for patient is that? we pay ins ppo pay deductibles, this hospital is going to be paid a huge amount of money for this stay billing our ins 
where u don't feel taken care of. or made to feel bad when asking questions abt medications which is your right on what's being given not given. my son is 21 what 21 year old actually wants to be in the hospital. none! 
i had all 3 sons in this hospital and it was a great experience.   
this is a lack of empathy, kind of your a pain in the ass care. if i where mission hospital i would have a meeting and look at your reviews because it's not looking good.

my elderly (90 y/o) mother fell and was taken by ambulance to mission hospital. after high blood pressure, a dislocated shoulder and a fall to the head they sent her home without my liking. i begged for a nurse to check up on her in her home after the sarcastic, well...we're not going to keep her because of high blood pressure. once the home health nurse visited her home, she said she was going to call an ambulance if i could not take her to the hospital for her "concerning" 220 bp. so back we went for another 7.5 hours.

work for mission hospital as a traveling nurse or tech would be a bad mistake some of the staff members abuse travelers and always like to put the blame on them as well i have been lied on twice there evening the  permit it staffed don't trust each other so if you choose to take a travel assignment at this hospital be very careful and i'm talking about the operating room if you are of color the look at you very carefully i have work there 3 times in the pass 10 to 15 years off and on as a traveler

the er is completely incompetent. my dementia grandmother spent all day (6am-7pm) at this place. they said they checked for uti and impaction. this was 2 weeks ago. they said nothing was wrong other than her dementia. they left her urine sample on the table the whole time. we even found a vial of someone else's blood on the floor! they refused to admit her and let her leave. we got her to virginia and yesterday she was admitted to a real hospital for uti and massive impaction. they said she's been that way for weeks. do not come to this horrible place. dr. calkins was very rude to my father and aunt. horrible place!!!

went for a routine ultra sound. they charged me $2900 almost 10 times the amount for an ultra sound anywhere else.  when i called to inquire, they simply said "it's all legal." doesn't seam to operate by the guiding principles of the parent organization st. joseph's.

we in santa fe, badly need a better hospital. 
unfortunately my husband had to use christus st. vicent twice.
it is worse than hospital in a third world country.
i couldn't ever imagine that usa would have such bad quality hospital!

review:
unfortunately, while visiting, had to take relative to emergency room. wheelchairs were conveniently located outside of the entrance doors and the check-in process was quick and efficient. we were quickly taken to a room. the emergency treatment area is smaller and felt very crowded but it does serve its purpose. it is loud however which is somewhat understandable. staff are excellent, patient, and professional. ended up having to admit relative to the hospital proper. the actual hospital wing is newer and the rooms are more spacious than most hospital rooms i have visited. 

pros: outstandingly patient and kind nurses and cnas, clean hospital rooms, nice gift shop, impressively helpful volunteer staff

cons: new chapel still under construction, elevators can be a little tricky to locate, limited cafeteria hours and vending machines are located in the cafeteria

after cutting my finger we went to the pv hospital for stiches.  i got to the front desk and the lady said they were running 6-7 hours out.  i said i just needed stiches and she said sorry but it is 6-7 hours.  i said what do you want me to do?  she said sorry i dont give medical advice.

i found an urgent care.  i was in and out in half hour?  great service.  paid in cash and it was reasonable.

bottom line, dont go to pv unless you are close to dead.  doctors dont know how to run a business.  glad urgent cares understands.

surprised at all the negative reviews. new to the area and had the worst pain from a kidney stone. emergency room staff was right on it took me right away, made me comfortable. doctor was very informative. bottom line, i felt well taken care of.

just spent the end of the holiday weekend in the er after my mother fell and dislocated/fractured her humerus (shoulder). after being there from about 9 pm until a little after 5 am, i can't say i would go back (as long the reason for another visit allowed time for an er a little further away). the triage worker and x-ray tech were wonderful and showed compassion, the md started off iffy but in the end was good and i hope i never have to get treated by shelby (rn). it took over four hours for xrays and for them to relocate my mother shoulder, which i understand is not always under their control depending on other patients coming in. it took another four hours for repeat xrays and discharge. we asked several times for pillows, water, views or a report of some kind of the fracture, and pain meds with either no help or a long wait. when shelby finally came to discharge my mother she told my mother that she could start taking things off. maybe something got to her about my mother letting people know that she is an obgyn, but that was not appropriate at all (especially for someone with only one functioning arm and iv still in). i can't say my experience that night will make me tell people to avoid the place altogether but i would consider other options if possible. i do know it is a hard job to have and am sure dignity health is doing the best job making sure enough staff are there on a saturday night.

***update*** i received a call and resolution to this situation. thank you, st. john's for acknowledging the error and correcting it! i hope that this does not occur to anyone else. 

on 11/11/2019, after having a poor reaction to an allergy test at a nearby clinic, i took my son to the waiting room of the er. i wanted to observe my son in the lobby and in the event he needed more care, have him admitted. we spent roughly 20 minutes in the lobby and left as my son did not warrant er level intervention. my son was never triaged, admitted, or provided medical treatment. on 1/7/2020, i received a call from bill collectors for over $623.00 for services and treatment. again, my son was never triaged, admitted, treated, or discharged from the er. he was never seen by a nurse, taken into an exam room, or provided medical care on 11/11/19. i was never provided a statement or bill. my insurance was never billed. they did not provide these things because services were never provided to my child. i have requested information on two separate occasions and have not been provided a statement with itemized information. st. john's pleasant valley falsified services and fraudulently billed for services that never occurred. a complaint has been filed and investigation into the matter is happening. they have done nothing to correct or resolve this matter. shame on this establishment!

i have been told by numerous phlebotomists and nurses that i have small veins and typically baby needles are used on me and to always pass this information along to whomever is treating me. although i told my rn he insisted on using an 18, this iv needle felt like it was scraping the inside of my vein.  when another nurse removed the iv when i was leaving the pain was terrible and the nurse said wow he used a large needle on you. i have never experienced a bruise like this in my life from an iv.  kudos to all the staff that cared for me so quickly.  the nurse who did this should learn to listen a bit more to their patients and admit that he may not know everything.

i recently delivered a baby in the new women's wing.  my experience with the labor, delivery, and recovery time there was excellent.  every single nurse & other employee i came into contact with during my stay was great.  i felt well taken care of, and it was definitely worth the drive for me to go there rather than the hospital that's closer to home.

just checking in. baby delivered here by relative. 
great service, clean hospital and good security. 
parking is free up front by the main entrance all day. check with the guard to help guide your visit..

today is day 14 of my husband in the hospital. the first eight were in icu followed by two days in the designated observation unit and the last two days in a regular hospital room. i was so pleasantly surprised with the staff as well as most of the rooms. let's start with the icu, i think the stand out starr would be heather. heather was there at night, was very good with my husband and clearly communicated anything i needed to know. there were other shining stars but heather really stood out. in the designated observation unit julie was the bomb! it was refreshing to find somebody who is thinking like i was, a big advocate for my husband. when my husband's procedure was moved from morning until evening she shared my concerns and got his procedure moved to the next morning. last stop, checking out tomorrow, is the brand new tower in a regular room. these rooms are absolutely gorgeous, every single one is private and the amenities are top notch including a big screen tv. jeanetta was the perfect nurse for my husband because she like my husband has a sense of humor, good at her job but knows how to lighten up the situation!  
i don't remember the names of the different respiratory staff who came to visit my husband but they all were really really good.  just really pleasant, seem to do their job well and if they saw me in the cafeteria or elsewhere in the hospital they either acknowledged that my husband was doing great or at least said hi. hospitalist dr. rana keep me well-informed as to his total care. finally, michael his nurse the last couple of days was amazing! very patient and was so willing to show us how to do the bolus feeding!

the medical surgical services dep. on tower 3 is the worst department i've encountered, my fiancé was admitted on 12-29-19 he has an infected gallbladder that needs immediate surgery we have been asking the nurses why is taking so long for him to have the surgery they kept on telling us there are not drs. available this morning when we finally spoke to a doctor this morning he said my fiancé was not even on the waiting list to be operated and in the records it was showing my fiancé was already discharged, how can that be?!! since they are still scanning his meds and fluids they are giving him. this is unacceptable!!!  my fiancé is still waiting......for surgery as we speak.

just a follow up on my recent post my fiancé got surgery at 11:00am and the only reason he got it done was because my mothers fiancé had to push the dr. to have the operation done sooner they wanted to operate him until 10:00pm today.

the new unit for labor & delivery at the hospital is outstanding: the rooms, service, nurses, respiratory therapists, anesthesiologists, lactation consultants etc. are very professional and very good in every way. i had my first baby at the cedars sinai and my second at the henry mayo. if i were to have a third child i wouldn't doubt to come here again. 
don't hesitate if you are considering, its awesome!

i wish i had the time to really explain my experience at henry mayo.  in july, i had a bad kidney infection and went against my gut instinct to go to cedars, and opted to go to henry mayo because it is closer.  i should have followed my gut instinct.  

their website said that the er had a five-minute wait.  

i was in the er for eight hours without a room, just stuck on a gurney in the hallway with no pain medicine (i was in excruciating pain), no care whatsoever, and had to be moved to another hallway at one point due to some loud and crazy criminal who was threatening patients (cops were everywhere).  it was a nightmare.

finally i was put into a room, and received pain medicine.  the nurses felt really bad for me, and that was appreciated.  the room was shared (unnecessary as they had many empty rooms) and my roommate wanted the room so hot i was dripping sweat.  the nurses called the room "the sauna" because it was so hot in there.  i begged them to turn down the temperature and every time they tried, she'd cry and beg them to turn it up because she was so cold (even with many blankets).  i am not a complainer, and not demanding in the slightest. she was very loud and very demanding.  so she won out.  they could have moved me into another room--that would have been great.  but no.  it was days of this...it was awful.  finally, i was ready to go home and because they didn't have the proper staff to release me (it was a friday and they are understaffed on the weekends), they wanted me to stay an extra 2.5 days because they would be back on monday.  

i could not deal with this for that long--besides, i did not want to overcharge my insurance company (that seemed like fraud to me), so i checked myself out ama.  they threatened that my insurance would not pay (this is blatantly not true).  they tried everything to scare me into staying.  my doctor even told me to go home.  they refused to talk to me once i signed on the dotted line, and would not even give me outprocessing papers.  i had to walk myself to my car.  fine with me.  the nurses were really pissed.  i found out later that they are audited based on number of amas, and they get dinged for each one.  i'm sorry for that, but maybe they should run a better business.

top all of that off with receiving a $1500 bill from the er doc--the doc i never saw.  turns out that, though the hospital is in my network, they hire out of network doctors for their er.  now i'm fighting with my insurance company, the doctor, and the hospital.  this is ridiculous.  this has happened to me before--getting an out of network doc in an er--and now i always ask if the doc is in my network.  if not, i won't see them and/or i'll go to another er.  i did this on this trip, and was told that he was in my network.  they lied.  he is not.  this is quite a racket, henry mayo--taking the people who need the care the most, who put their trust in you, and give them the bait-and-switch with out-of-network doctors who will bill as much as they want for their "care" (even if there is no care).

between the misleading information on their website for er wait times, the lack of care in the er, the hospital experience, ama experience, and final billing--this was a nightmare that i hope i can save you from.  skip it.  it's just not worth the convenience of "local".  

providence holy cross is not far from here--and it's a great hospital.  next time in the need of an er, i'll either go there or to cedars.  never again, henry mayo.

i used to love this hospital. 

i've came here many times and i've started to see a major decline in the patient care and overall demeanor of staff. 

today, i entered the er to meet keesha - the rn responsible for triage. i've never met someone who is so rude to everyone upon their arrival. 

a man entered with chest pains like he was having a heart attack and she treated him like gum on the sidewalk. his brother walked in concerned and asked if he needed a visitors pass and she yelled at him that his brother isn't even checked in yet and to go over there -- basically shoo fly, dont bother me. i noticed she was browsing the internet so it's understandable that she didn't want to be bothered. 

even though she heard me explain why i'm coming in, i sit down and she asks me so why did i come in?    so i repeat myself and then she proceeds to start arguing with me about why i'm there! 

i will absolutely not be returning...

admin staff, first impressions are key to maintaining a positive atmosphere
i've been there several times in the last two years due to lower back pain. they are always quick to treat me and the staff is very professional. glad i live close by.

just got home from going to the emergency room! i was in the er for 6+ hours and my nurses were so nice and attentive. there was a woman i think from kansas she was so kind and made me feel so safe. her partner (i'm sorry i forgot everyone's names) who also was very informative about the whole process and explained to me what was going on. the curly haired young 20s nurse who took me to get my cat scan she was so nice and funny. i can tell these people love their job and helping others. i felt so comfortable in their care. thank you for your service. 
this 1 star is for the billing service henry mayo uses msnllc this place is beyond shady. they directly billed me and didn't even contact my health insurance. also there's a catch. my bill is due in about a week and their customer service is unreachable. their phone systems have been down and i've been calling them everyday for the last week. and no one is willing to help me. other people have been having the same problem and henry mayo's billing department gave me the same number that didn't work. this is beyond crazy. i already notified the better business bureau about msn and i wasn't the first one that had issues with this company.

took my mother to the ed on thanksgiving night. i was sitting in the chair next to her bed and noticed there was dry blood on the railing that was not my mother's. thank god housekeeping had passed by and i asked her to clean it.

my father was in the emergency room due to a car accident and they provided such poor care... they were even sending him home with glass in hand from the windshield!!! so disappointed to see that they didn't even bother to clean his scraps and cuts. wish i could leave no stars!

i don't understand all these bad reviews. my husband had pneumonia, we went to the er. like everyone else, we waited. that is what happens, you have to wait everywhere you go. all of these reviews in my opinion are for people who go to the er for the sniffles. just my opinion, we were treated with respect, everyone was professional. yes we waited for the dr. but meanwhile my husband was getting tests, attention from nurses. we were never left alone for any amount of time or ignored. they help the sickest patients as it should be. our experience was a good one! the nurses and staff do talk with on another, they aren't robots. they are normal everyday people doing their job.

avoid this hospital, don't go here the staff are a bunch of morons, arrogant in their ignorance. i had a shift leader drag a gown across the floor and hand it to me and said," you can change clothes in the men's room." i looked at her and said you just dragged the thing across the floor of the entire length of the pre-op room and you expect me to put this own in the men's room. i am disabled and i have a cane i use, which should have been enough information for her to understand my plight, these clowns didn't have a gurney ready for me for 2 procedures i was having done, i changed my clothes in the men's room and then stood around in the preop until some asked why we were there as if a guy in a gown isn't signal enough that i am a patient. these people are either on drugs or in need of prozac, don't risk your life with the rude fools, the admissions reps are just as rude and don't get caught standing around anywhere they expect you to able to sit, something i can't do so instead of asking for a gurney they just yelled at me to go stand in the lobby. these people are imbeciles with a capital i this hospital needs to be shut down. these morons must be killing more people than they help. this is not a hospital it is placed where people go to get a paycheck and that is it, they don't earn a dime of it my procedures were for 1:30 at 15 minutes to 3 i was still on a gurney waiting to go into a closet sized procedure room. this hospital is old the rooms are small and not built for modern equipment hence there is no privacy and the people are just plain rude and ignorant, it takes three people to make one decision. who ever is funding this is wasting money, tear it down and fire these clowns they don't have a clue as to what the hell they are doing.

i just don't think people get how scarce mental health care is in texas. this place is a gem. it's a sanctuary. it's a place that i can thank time and time again for saving my life. not once did they mistreat me. i came there voluntarily after choosing to take my life and stopping myself from doing it. the counseling rooms just show you how violent some of their patients can be. there's scratch marks and scuffs. in fact while staying there a gentleman attempted to escape by breaking through a window. completely shattered the glass and caused lots of panic but even so the spirit was calm and the staff well trained did what they were supposed to do. the cafeteria really did an amazing job accommodating me. even after an unknown party threw a tray at the beverage counter destroying the soda fountain dispenser. turns out their marketing website isn't as fictional as they make it out to be. one thing i did learn loud and clear is if you offer something to a peer- a fellow patient- they'll take you up on it. this is a hospital. people in there aren't clowns. they aren't crazy people. they are people hurting and rock prarie behaviorial health are the right ones for the job.

my son had been teething, but was still acting like his normal happy, cant get him to stop moving self. saturday he was super lethargic and you could tell he wasn't feeling well. he had a cough that made him cry.  being out of town i went to the sutter lakeside hospital er. dr. hatfield came in and as soon as i told him he had been teething he determined then and there that was the reason my son wasn't feeling well. he did not listen to anything i had to say and barely examined him. checked his chest and said he was clear. i had to ask him to check his ears and thank god i asked because he wasn't going to and it turns out he had an ear infection. he did not want to give my son an antibiotic for his ear. luckily he gave me the prescription "hesitantly" and wrote on the prescription it was a "wait and see prescription", as well as wrote an email to my pediatrician about how he saw things. good thing i didn't trust him because on monday when i went in to see his pediatrician (after no improvement) we found out he had pneumonia. i would give zero stars if i could. 

oh and to top it off, during my visit a nurse came into the room while he was examining my son and  they had a conversation about what to give another patient who was in the er at the same time as us. 


do not go to sutter lakeside hospital er!

one of the worst hospitals i have been too in about 20 states. unbelievably dysfunctional staff that consistently violates patients rights and neglects the standard of care in the er department. i even brought this up over the phone and in writing to the patient relations staff. typically this department spanning most hospitals is the one that holds the many other departments accountable for their conduct and behavior in hopes for training. that's the scary part of the last line of defense doesn't value feedback or act on the many issues that run over this hospital then i'm afraid it is too far gone. beware many assistants with zero accredited training will often walk in and attempt to act as licensed medical providers but are nothing more than admin support. make sure you get a copy of your rights and hold them to not violating your rights. make them introduce themselves, state their names and positions. do not assume anything. please don't be like me if you have transportation  go anywhere else!! and please, if your going to respond with a generic response that is generated automatically, save your time . i expressed my concerns in writing and over the phone with no interest in bettering your hospital. how can you operate so egregiously?? how does the rogue staff that works there live with themselves?

on monday evening, december 30, 2019, i sustained a broken ankle injury and was taken to the er room of memorial community hospital in blair, ne.  i received fast, excellent care in the er from dr. jeremy lee and the nursing and x-ray staff.  my dislocated foot/ankle was realigned in the proper position, x-rays were taken, and i was put in a cast to transport me back to my home in kansas city.  
i appreciate the professional care and kind attitude of dr. lee and hospital staff.

review:
i'm new to the area and my past hospitals experiences have been at stanford or ucsf. my expectations are high on quality of care. i came to the er on a sunday evening and was pleasantly surprised by the fast admission and triage process.  during my initial tests another issue was found.  it was impressive how thorough they were and how they were able to bring in specialists on short notice.  i spend one night on the second floor  next night on the first floor.

the thing that stood out to me was that every single person i met from the guard at the gate, admissions, er doctors, hospitalist dr omogrosso, nursing team, to the janitor were personable, collaborative, helpful, and generally liked their job and people in general.  whatever the management team is doing to motivate their staff to work together and  show patients they are important is working. i spent one night on the top floor and the second night on the first floor.

this is regarding the er. i was incredibly disappointed with the care received. my little sister fainted while in the shower during her period. she had a small gash on her head-- because it was on her face we wanted to make sure there was no scarring and thus took her to the er. when we got there, they checked us in... and called us to the back for an ekg and blood work (excessive, yes, but it is the er). they took us back to the front, and called us back again for a chest x-ray. the np was walking by so we inquired as to why a chest x-ray was needed for someone who fainted (with known cause) after an ekg was already done.  the np proceeded to tell us that football players have fainted and died (completely irrelevant). i asked her if the ekg was normal, and her response was that there was syncope and we needed to find the cause of the syncope. then she asked my 18 yr old sister if she felt a vagal response. i looked up what syncope was on my phone- "fainting"? why is a medical professional using these terms when talking to patients? terrible bedside manner. my sister had to ask what she meant, and she still was unable to explain properly. i asked if my sister needed all these tests as she has been acting completely normal- she just has a cut on her forehead and i wasn't sure if it'd scar. np asked when the fall occured and i told her it was 10 am (this was about 11 hours later), and she responded she didn't realize. i asked if they would give my sister treatment without all these diagnostics tests and the np said that they would not! we felt stuck at that point, because the stitches needed to be done within a certain time frame. after all of this, we to the front and get called back again-they decided to finally take vitals/check the blood pressure of the girl who fainted! they also said they needed to take do a cat scan of her head! at this point, we refused treatment to the tech and said we needed to see an md/physician. the ct tech said okay and said we could go back out front. over an hour later, we were called back so more blood could be drawn; i asked if there was something wrong with the first draw, and was told no- they simply have to draw blood for the particular test over a period of six hours. we inquired as to why this was necessary and where the doctor was and why this was all needed for some stitches! the np came and said she was waiting on the cat scan results before she did stitches. we asked her who was ordering all these tests, and we absolutely refuse to have a cat scan. she said the doctor ordered them and we'd have to sign a waiver saying we decline treatment. we said we would like to see the doctor who is ordering these tests, because why is he/she doing so without even seeing the patient. she said she was ordering on behalf of the doctor. we proceeded to sternly say we need to see a doctor, and her response was, "well i see patients all the time by myself." we replied that was fine but we need to see a doctor. in the meantime, she went back to her office and we heard her talking to the doctor on speakerphone who said that we did not need to sign anything, but simply make sure it was noted in the chart. after some time we were put in a room, and then waited for the doctor. 
the poor doctor came in a while later and was very sweet. i was ready to just have my sister receive treatment and leave, but my mother said it was important to tell/ask about what happened because other patients need protection to. i then went into detail of everything happened, and said i felt the chest x-ray was completely unnecessary, i was appalled that the blood pressure of a patient who came in because she fainted was taken after having a chest x ray, and the bedside manner and advanced terminology of the np (kim tarver) was unacceptable. very surprisingly, the doctor agreed. she professionally stated she agreed that the chest xray was unnecessary and my sister did not need a cat scan. she said the blood pressure thing was an outlier, but still needed to be noted...and she stated the terminology used was a personnel issue. after all this, she used liquid stitches (liquid skin) on my sister. she's good to go now, but it was an incredibly painful, unnecessary process.
