i called multiple times to get a hold of someone there and finally, ivonne cardenas answered and told me you have been referred to another department and gave me pms (progressive management systems) phone number. what department is this, and she very rudely said uhh its pms department! they will talk to you and hung up on me. wow lady how about you do your job or get me someone who will help. she is not in the right work field. avoid this hospital!

having a strict policy for not allowing any member of the patient's family stay overnight is a nightmare, we can't trust and feel confident with your health service...ignoring patient's request and listening based on the present diagnosed is ridiculous...being a health service professional do kindly pay attention and listen to your patient's health history and take your outrageous pride somewhere...
the nicu drs and nurses are amazing as are the entire staff , they literally saved my granddaughters life ! we call them our angels !

i presented in the  er with nausea and severe chest pain. after a few hours i was diagnosed with pancreatitis and immediately admitted. 

doctors apparently didn't confer   they contradicted each  other and ordered  different meds. nurses had no idea what the orders were   a couple nurses made it very clear they didn't want to be working on the weekend   one almost handed me  another patient's medication. 
took way too long for a nurse to respond (sometimes 30+ minutes)

once it was determined i did not have pancreatitis, i was basically ignored.  room was never touched to be cleaned in three days!  no clean linen, offer of a clean gown, nothing.  when i asked to take  a shower, i was told to take one when i got home.  nursing management was sympathetic but this experience was absolutely horrible. 

i completed the lengthy survey they emailed. no response. no surprise. it doesn't appear anyone cares what happens in this hospital. 

there is no shortage of local hospitals. seek treatment  elsewhere!!

my daughter is pregnant for first time. took her to virtua voorhees hospital early morning. they keep her about 1 hr. tell her she is not in labor and go home. then 12 hrs later we go back because labor pains were at about 9 . plus she was bleeding . she is 2 cm 90% thin. again told to go home after them checking her for less then 1hr. they tell her since she is going natural best place for her to be is home to deliver. they were so unprofessional!!! got home with daughter had to turn around and go to another hospital, because she was bleeding bad and lot of pain. in the time we went jefferson in washington twp.she was 4 cm. they took great care of her, very caring,  and every professional. i will never recommend virtua hospital ever again to anyone. only reason  i put 1 star is because there was - stars!

i had a great experience here from jan 1 to feb 15 2018.   i had some medical issues as well as substantial rehab needs and i was treated well both by medical and rehab personnel.  i was taken from being entirely reconditioned after a month of septic shock, where i couldn't walk, sit up, or raise my arms, to being quite functional.  it included months of outpatient which was also excellent.  i am grateful to the fine staff at marianjoy.

my husband has been a patient at mj several times. the first time, mj was an independent facility. therapists and nursing staff were both wonderful; efficient, well-trained and competent, very caring, and seemingly happy in their positions. in 2018 northwestern bought the facility. the facility has become very "corporate." while the therapy is still top-notch, the staff has taken on a different attitude toward their patients and their jobs. they are no longer caring and friendly; those traits enhance the patient and family experience and speed the healing process - lack of those traits make the patient want to get out of there before they are actually ready. the nursing staff, particularly the night shift, are "businesslike" to the point of being rude. the medical staff is also poor, at best, in communicating with patients and family and seem incompetent in following the discharge orders of the hospital from which the patient came, even to the point of simply ignoring the medication orders without informing the ordering physician or the patient/family. 
i am so disappointed that a superior facility like marianjoy would "sell out" to the corporate world which is taking over so much of medicine today. i would still return to mj strictly for the therapy, but i am certainly not happy about the new atmosphere and i honestly don't know if i would blanketly recommend the facility as i once did. 
i find that outpatient therapy at a dupage medical group facility is as good if the patient is capable of doing op therapy.
of course, there are still several staff members who maintain the old fashioned bedside manner and at least try to go above and beyond in patient care, but even those seem to be "afraid of breaking corporate protocol."

i had out patient surgery and the staff was great! they were professional and friendly! everything went as discussed. i was released in the timeframe they told me. all precautions were taken and my surgeon did a great job on my gallbladder surgery! they even use robots as an extension of the doctors arms! i would use this facility again!

i have the same experience that many of the patients who already posted reviews on this medical center.
my husband came to the hospital for a gallbladder problem. it took three days to have surgery because the doctors were not reaching the same diagnosis.
general doctor, gastrointelogist and the surgeon wanted different things. it seems there is no communication among the doctors.
discharging was awful. they promised discharged in the morning and it was 2 pm and he was waiting in the room ready to go. it was until my husband started to walk out on his own that they rush the discharge.

currently at this hospital with my mother in the surgical portion of the hospital.

absolute worse experience ever...we have seen three doctors and they have completely different diagnosis.

one says no antibiotics are needed and the other orders antibiotics.

we ask to have the doctors talk to one another and they disappear and never come back.

we have been here since friday and continue to struggle to get any consistent answers. we ask to speak to someone who is able to help and we get a charge nurse who can't really help with our issues.

it is so disheartening to be here and not have any idea what is really going on and no one is here to help clear anything up.

if you have a choice...do not come here!

stephanie at medical records is very unprofessional and negligent. i have called several times and she never answers the phone. she does not care to call back. i don't know exactly what she is hired for is she's not there to assist patients.
i came in to the emergency because i have a stent put in not to long ago and have pain in my chest. to be safe i came to the er. i waited 6 hours with chest pain to have a bed. unreal!

this place literally has the worst er and the worst staffing.... my dad had a procedure done here but only resulted in his rectal abscess coming back. the second time they did the removal procedure they opened another which connect the original into one but with two different entry points. he decided to go to a different doctor and he basically said they f'd him up. i decide to take my friend here due to a psychiatric emergency and then took 3 hours just to get her in. she was so overwhelmed by the wait and the situation she wanted to leave but they wouldn't let her. another 5 hours go by and still nothing from a doctor and still a no for her to go home. we ask how long it will take for her to be seen and they mention they're unsure... if they're treating so important that she is unable to leave where is the help??? they even gave her a shot and asked the nurse what it was for and he said "mmm i don't know." i'm so over this place and if i could give it zero stars i would.

terrible service for high risk patients in their emergency department. physician's assistant that was on call with blonde hair on the evening of 12/23/2019 was not knowledgeable regarding mandatory protocols and was dismissive; almost cost my child's life. i walked out after several hours and went to choc. my child had pneumonia. i'm glad i followed my gut. we will never be going there again and we live in los alamitos.

i want to pay a compliment to los alamitos medical center. my husband was taken there via paramedics for excruciating, debilitating sciatica pain. they were the only local er open due to the flu season. during his stay marvin was his caring nurse who  helped him very attentively with such tender kindness and compassion. thank you dr sheih who started with the most effective pain treatment to give him quick relief. dr prince continued his care into the next shift of staff. what a kind person. a heroine of doctors who understands pain control. once he was stable and pain under control, she discharged my husband with a great medicine treatment plan for home, to sustain him until he sees his orthopedic md a few days later. this was a "10" on a 1-10 scale of giving kind care and pain relief to my precious husband. for this we are very grateful. thank you all involved.

telephone contact!
most of my doctors are at hup.  they are terrific.  but getting through to a person on the phone is impossible!  i left my briefcase after a visit yesterday and i have been trying for an hour to reach a person who could tell me if i left it there.  there were only 2 places i could have left it.  the only person i talked to eventually was in lost & found for the entire hospital!  i am going to have to drive down there and look for myself.
this is crazy.
fac_name: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania

review: very disappointed to say the least.. treated my son like he was just a number.. plan of treatment was the look of a football play on a piece of paper.  no heart, no empathy, no bedside manner..younger doctors walked around thinking they were god, above all.. as my son who was diagnosed with cancer lay in his bed, doctors came in to tell the patient in the next bed he only had days to live.. my son heard the conversation and was devastated.. why would you not have this conversation privately?! fortunately, my son received his remaining care at tower health in reading.. where patients matter, he was cared for like he was the only patient in the hospital.
fac_name: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania

review:
this was the absolute worst, most traumatic experience i've had in possibly my entire 32 years of life. i'm a nurse if that matters, but would never behave as poorly as the nurses who worked un upenn's er. i came to upenn hospital and waited 9.5 hours to be seen in the er for gallbladder pain and vomiting every two hours. i had to go through these visits three times (wait time was always around nine hours, no pain medication except tylenol was provided even once i was back in the er, and i was treated like a drug seeker. one nurse had the gall to tell me the hospital was out of morphine, which made me laugh because hospitals have many opiates at their disposal. let me mention that i had never gone to an er before in my life and gallbladder pain had me writhing on the ground moaning. one time i was put on a gurney in the hall with no call bell and was not checked on for 1.5 hours. one time i was put in a room, but no one had put pillows or blankets on the gurney and i had to use the call bell after waiting two hours for a nurse to finally see me for the first time. she mocked me for complaining about the wait and then i heard her at the nurse's station making fun of me. the third time was the same and the residents looked at my very obvious symptoms and suggested things like heartburn or a bowel blockage. come on, even i know the symptoms i presented with represented gallbladder pain. before going to upenn i saw the physician at the university of pennsylvania school health center and day one she knew i needed to have my gallbladder out. finally, my dad drove up from pittsburgh and he's a physician, so he was treated with a tiny bit of respect. instead of looking at my symptoms, the residents just did tests and because the tests were negative, they didn't trust their diagnostic skills to diagnose me as needing my gallbladder removed. eventually, i was so upset i went to penn presby and was admitted to an observation unit. unfortunately, no doctor trusted their diagnostic skills there either and after five days they told my dad, "well, we can just keep running tests...". my dad said absolutely not. they provided me with two pain pills for the six-hour drive home and i got my gallbladder removed in pittsburgh the next day. i had immediate relief. i was treated like a human being with kindness and sympathy, not like a drug seeker who was making up symptoms. one the gallbladder was out, the pain was immediately gone. i will absolutely never go to the penn health system again no recommend it to anyone. i will instead warn people about the poor treatment and inadequate care as well as the inability of any physician to properly diagnose me. if i stay in philadelphia, i will drive out to main line health lankenau or bryn mawr hospital. 
i want to point out i worked at chop next door and would have been fired if i was as lazy and mean as the nurses were at upenn (upenn and chop are not affiliated). i couldn't believe adults were treated like trash while we treated children and their parents with first-rate service. i cannot emphasize this enough if you want and accurate diagnosis, pain management, or kind treatment stay as far away from upenn health system as possible.
fac_name: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania

review: if you want inaccurate billing information and months of on-going aggravation requesting a corrected, confirmed adjustment in writing go here. this review is for the billing & patient relation department, not the physician. awful! it is now mid jan 2020 and i am still waiting on written confirmation of an itemized pdf adjustment for my records date of service june 2019 (i already have the general email). no matter how many times you call & leave messages, no one gets back to you. it is only a matter of luck if someone in patient relations actually picks up the phone, then you go in circles over & over with the same excuse of "this is what came from billing", & no updates are provided! emails are not responded to either. i work full time; running after incompetent staff should not turn into another full time job as i have been dealing with this nonsense for months. maybe this review will grab the attention of someone who is capable of closing out my issue. this place is unreal.
fac_name: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania

review:
usually our emergency visits aren't too bad. the past two times i have gone have been a sh*t show. the first time (for an asthma attack) i bring my daughter in, we stand in triage for about 15 minutes waiting for someone to even acknowledge us. finally the nurse says he'll be with us soon. there's nowhere to sign in, and the window to be seen is closed. after standing there for 15 minutes another couple comes in, mind you were still standing there waiting for someone to at least take her name, the couple walks right in front of us into the triage area after the nurse had told us he'll be with us shortly. they are seen right away....we walked out. 

the second time (for the flu) we were seeing right away, we put masks on as soon as we walked in the door. for courtesy of other patient's. she was taken back to fast track. everything was fine until after the doctor came in, ran some tests, then sat us in this large common area full of other sick people and not a single person was wearing a mask! the two children that were sitting next to us were both diagnosed with the flu, and the only reason why i knew that is because one of the nurses came out and said it in front of everybody! the lady across from us also had the flu! no mask! how are you going to sit all these people in a large common area knowing they have the flu but not requiring them to wear a mask and infect the elderly patients that are also sitting in that waiting room, knowing that their immune system's are compromised because of age!?! my daughter and i were the only ones wearing a mask and it's not because they asked us. it's because i made that choice. 

that whole system they have is completely ridiculous and needs to be redone. out of respect for other patients and their privacy. 

most of the time the doctors and nurses are great, just depends on when you go i suppose.

i will honestly never go into this hospital  for anything including a bandaid!  i have know for years the care here is no- care at all!  on 01/12/2020 at 330 pm i took my husband to the er as he was in severe pain and thought he might have cracked a rib . we were triaged quickly telling them he heard a pop when he  coughed and all needed info.
    they took him into one room, left us, came and took him into another room for who knows what reason. as he could barely move , this was  painful!  they got him quickly for ex-rays and then..... the wait began. 
   after some time they came and told us they had to send the ex-rays to st joe"s to be read and they had problems getting them! are you serious?? it was 330 in the afternoon and noone  could read ex-rays in the hospital. this is not little house on the prairie folks.
    so we wait, all the meanwhile my husband cannot stand straight, bend, lie down, sit down, kneel, etc without screaming in pain. never did one person come in and touch him- ask  questions, evaluate the area,  have him move his shirt, watch his motion. nothing! i mean zero! is it bruised? no one asked? where exactly is the pain? nope,  nothing  was asked! we told them in triage he heard a pop! 
   finally at about 630 they  came in and said , no broken bones, muscle spasm- ice it , flexerill, ibuprophen. i questioned them. they knew i was not buying it! i explained the pain was  unbearable and he could not  work.  they did not give him a work note either.
   the meds given gave him zero relief- none, nada, zero, zilch. he screamed all night. he could not get in the bed, lay down, lay back,  sleep.
     monday morning we went to his pa- c in tecumseh where in 5 minutes  he was told he most likely had a hairline fracture of his rib and they do not all show on ex-rays. she simply  touched his side, and looked and  did what a dr does in a painful injury. she gave him stronger meds , detailed instructions and  he is now resting  comfortably. 
   this er is  a joke! it is no wonder it is commonly called a bandaid station. they stand and chit chat, gossip about patients, read their texts and phones when one even told me when i asked him a ? and apologized for bothering him that he wasn't supposed to be using his phone anyhow!! seriously? when you need help, there is no feeling you will be helped here!  he screamed for 8 hours after this visit. i have a video of him. hire better people and pay them and they might care enough to work  but this "hospital "  is not and never will be a good hospital even if they are building a new one!!!! new building- same idiots.
  d. mueller , adrian, mi

this is for the er. unless you are truly on your deathbed, avoid this er if at all possible. i was convinced by staff of an urgent care to go to marin general er. i spent 7 hours there and they charged me more than $10,000, quite literally to sit in a bed and receive no attention. the doctor talked to me for possibly 2 minutes and they weren't present enough to assess what was wrong.  not a drop of medication was dispensed. they were severely understaffed and everyone was super stressed and short with the patients. i was worse when i left than when i went in. what a mistake!

my spinal surgery was a large event for me and a stay in a hospital something i did not look forward to, either. but, i felt adequately prepped and my family support group was there. they have been watching over me for months. surgery and post surgery i suppose was the usual; pain and reduced physical abilities. i felt secure with the nursing squads although all of them were so belabored with making tests and pushing computers (no more paper work!) around they seem rushed. all of them were kind and patient with me; some were actually emotionally helpful. nurses must have to like their work to keep smiling. the hospital food was excessive, very large portions for a small woman but well put together; good; no complaints certainly. and i had pt and preparation to make my next step...home.
 it's now been several weeks later that i was called by a survey company to give my ratings of the hospital services. during the questioning i was told i had been an outpatient! a large error, of course and it had to have come from the hospital accounts. i'm glad it was an mistake like that, book keeping instead of any other category of care. but, really, new construction complications granted; there's no excuse for hospitals to make mistakes. i have joined the ranks of those who say " i better keep out of there!". the old marin general will have a new face and more rooms and more advantages now. i hope it will not become, as we old folks used to say, "too big for its britches!".gp

i took a bad fall on my face and called marinhealth medical center urgent care (they advertise constantly on tv)...yet they told me they wouldn't attend to any cut on the face despite the fact it was under my chin.  i didn't want to spend the time, money or clog the emergency department with this non-life threatening emergency and ended up taking care of it myself and will now have a nice pitted scar thanks to marinhealth. i'm simply needed a few stitches but they wouldn't because they said on the face requires a plastic surgeon.  i wouldn't consider going here for anything quite frankly

kabir singh is a throwback to a time when doctors cared about their patients. in a county where callbacks can be anywhere from days to weeks, dr singh is a responsive, caring health provider. he is knowledgeable and professional in providing cardiovascular care. he is clear and concise in providing options and explanations. he has a wonderful personality and i can't recommend him enough.

let me say the worst place to work is in the evs department at this cherry hill location. not only is the management a joke but mila pillar is so unprofessional. i honestly feel like i was treated very unfairly by not only mila pillar but by john weir. i had a huge issue and instead of getting the solution from my supervisor and manager i was forced to quit & that was something i didn't want to do i love my job but we don't quit our jobs we quit the management. 



tiffany chavez
fac_name: Swedish Medical Center - Cherry Hill Campus

review:
i have just visited dr andrew eastman and stephanie arguelles licsw at the above  facility. i am beyond impressed. the hospital is clean, the staff courteous and dr eastman's assistant, amy, a treasure.
dr eastman took his time and demonstrated patience, kindness and utmost professionalism with me. i know i have found the right doctor.
ms arguelles is empathetic, intuitive and  professional. she is genuine and very easy to talk to; compassionate and very knowledgeable. 
i moved to seattle recently, am a two time cancer survivor and grieving the deaths of my husband and daughter. at last i have found the care i need. 
thank you. 
penrose anderson.

review: i was seeing dr chapman about my back and the horrified pain i was having. well i don't drive and live way south of swedish. the staff was rude. kept wanting me to come to all these different pre surgery appointments. one at a time. instead of helping me schedule for all the same day. they refused. i could not sit up due to the pain. traveling in a care was unbearable. they did not care. then i was told pick the date that was available or i would have to wait 4 months. i was already depressed due to the pain.  the day i would of had surgery the nurses went out on strike so my surgery would not of happened anyways. glad i switch to tacoma general and dr harris. i've had my surgery i'm doing great and on the road to recovery. he may of been the top dr in the nation but swedish is not and i won't be going back there.  so do yourself a favor and do not go to swedish.
fac_name: Swedish Medical Center - Cherry Hill Campus

review:
beautiful for a hospital. many friendly people working here. excellent cafeteria. and i need to give a huge shout out to labor and delivery! what a great team of nurses and staff in labor and delivery! kind patient and were very knowledgeable. big rooms, and the baby rooms in with the mom which i loved! 
the only odd thing was we saw an uncapped syringe in the parking structure. otherwise a beautiful hospital where the care is far above standard.

have always been a hoag fan.....but....went to er with severe lower back pain on 2/25/20 - pa attended, diagnosed as muscular despite the intense pain i was experiencing; reluctantly ok'd back x-ray, said no issues - gave me percocet, muscle relaxer, ibuprofen, steroid 5-day.....said no need for mri, even though we suggested.  something didn't seem right; went to my orthopod / spine doc for follow up....more x-rays, mri - severely herniated disc (so much for muscular)....considering choices - maybe surgery...hmmmm

so disappointed hoag......my daughter was born there and you did a great job, we have donated to hoag foundation......you are not what you used to be....

pros
hospital renovations inside & out.

hospital interior/exterior decor is upgraded.  

hospital uniforms upgraded.

staff in icu appeared to work as a team & 

icu staff seemed caring & professional. 

gift-shop has nice selection of gift items.


cons 

hospital beds & blankets need to be upgraded.
( mattresses / blankets linens need to be better quality)

patient food pantry generic & cheap.

icu porta-potty chairs need upgrades & prompt containment of feces.
( patient rooms in icu don't have restrooms? ) 

parking structure / lot automated facility is & process is complicated & inconvenient.

i just spent 2 nights at hoag newport beach.  the entire staff from the moment i walked in to the moment i was wheeled out, were amazing. everyone was super nice and helpful. i truly felt i was in the best hands and couldn't be more thankful to everyone who i had the pleasure of meeting.   i just wanted to mention, one of my wonderful nurses aureila.   i had a lot of great people around me,but she stood out. 

thank you hoag.  what a fabulous hospital.
i have had the bests experience here. moved here recently an needed a place to go for emergencies. i have been here 3 times and the staff if amazing. best customer care and focus on treatment.
shame on this hospital!!! no beds, people are waiting 2-3 hours for in lobby of the emergency room!!! such missed up medical!!!

second time i had surgery hoag facility and received a staph infection.
furthermore, when i went to their emergency room, after told by the er doctor that a pa(physician's assistant) told him to drain my knee, and sitting there for 3 hours with my wound wide open(despite there only being one other person in there. 6am sunday), i decided it was best to leave. 3 months later i received a bill from them stating my insurance company refused to pay because i failed to fill out a questionnaire . when i called the insurance company i was told not only that they paid it, but they paid it weeks before this bill was sent to me. i've attempted to call their billing office now 6 times, and still no return phone call.

they get one start and thats too much to give. every unfortunate time i've come here it's been well over 2-3 hour wait even if they are not busy. this is bull shit. i sliced my hand open with nerve damage and been sitting for over 3 hours. i've seen new patients come and go and i'm sitting here. i told them i've been waiting for 3 hours and they say it's a emergency room..  no shit idiot. i'm sitting here with hand cut wide open...

the worst experience i've ever had at a hospital all the nurses were for the most part pretty rude and incompetent in my opinion they kept forgetting to do what they said they were going to do we had to keep calling to remind them. one nurse forgot to tell the doctor my daughter had a fever which was very important for her to know. forgot to change her catheter which was full and needed to be changed also the nurse said she was gonna be right back to change her anabiotic medicine because she had a fever and she didn't come back for over an hour and a half and we  had to call and remind her.
my daughter gave birth on 1/20/2020 and the labor and delivery nurse tien was amazing! all the stafff was great but tien really stood out like a boss!

hoag is a despicable institution.  honestly.  they did an investigation and wouldn't you know, my claims of abuse and coercion were unfounded.  hoag has single handily helped to destroy my once beautiful life full of love and laughter, yet there is no accountability.
the nurses are amazing here. i'm pregnant with twins and they have taken such amazing care of me.

great care but. no bicycle racks! probably not the first thing you'd think you need at a hospital but if you're walking in for labs, etc  it could help. it took a bit of doing to find something i could lock my bike to without blocking wheelchair access.

please stay far and away from thjs hospital. i heard many have had a bad experience with their labor units but did not listen. they were all right. this hospital is probably ok given the view but the labor nurses? they just follow what the dr tells them even if that means breaking the honesty between her and the patient and her baby. extreme shadiness from one nurse and my dr who tried to rush the delivery in the most aggressive manner. shame on them all. how could they consider themselves doctors acting like that? isnt there an oath you take before becoming a nurse or dr??? thank god there are far better hospital staff than this unit. the mom and baby unit were amazing. the only issue is that our room had a plumbing problem and very unsanitary sink condition and not one care in the world from all. do not deliver here is my best advice to all the ladies out there.

love, love, this place. they took good care of me and my daughter. everyone is nice. i was hungry and it wasn't lunchtime; yet. my nurse  managed to bring me a snack and a drink. delivery staff was very helpful and my recovery time went smoothly. the view was beautiful; watching the sunset and sunrise gave us a sense of peace.

came in for an emergency miscarriage and had okay service with staff. i came in with nothing they gave me a cheap shampoo that was water alcohol that ruined my hair! they had absolutely no conditioner, no body wash, no mini deodorant! food was gross!!! surprised being they have a huge cafeteria and they rape in high billing costs!!!go to st. joseph they give you full set of toiletry needs, best nurses, best food!!! and cheaper billing cost! hoag is going downhill quickly! other hospitals have better premium care and quality services. do not be deceived by hospital by the beach! you're treated like cattle here, it's a complete zoo! they're focus is mass production in cheapest budget in a demon like popularity contest. all they care about is serving the rich on their tight budget! go to st. joseph where there is love for any walk of man, and less focus on budget of money money money. hoag is only for the rich period!!! former patient/former hoag staff who seen behind the scenes seeing people getting better treatment than people with disabilities. from staying here in 3 emergency situations as a victim! for being in the health industry they are cruel to domestic violence victims(the head nurse staff laughed in my face in 2016 about being strangled , and held hostage by an ex bf. mental health ptsd patient, assistant that sat at door and young trash guy in 2017 laughed about it being a mental health floor in front of us patients) and as being painful emotional miscarriage, not emotional after care support, no social worker, no emergency quality care. 3/3 horrifying overnight visits! i'm done giving chances! i will tell every person on earth how they run their circus act for the rich and have horrific manners and care as s community hospital!!!! do not give money to these devils!!!

i went to the er for a pelvic fracture sustained in a bike accident. everyone there was kind and attentive. the care i received was exceptional - all of the exams/labs/and assessments were timely and performed in such a way as to avoid causing me more pain than i was already experiencing. i was given immediate feedback on all test results and their relevance. a social worker set up all of my home care appointments and was incredibly helpful. i love hoag and highly recommend going there if you ever need emergency care.

i'm usually not the one to write negative reviews, but i'm writing this on behalf of future patients to forewarn them on what to expect. i'm saddened to say i was very disappointed in the lack of bedside manner and professionalism by the front desk receptionist in the imaging department. she was visibly overwhelmed and projected her frantic nature onto the patients checking in. not only did i observe her rude mannerisms to other patients including myself, but she gossiped with other coworkers about how annoyed and frustrated she was due to the amount of people checking in "all at once". it isn't fair to the patients who already have nerves about getting medical imaging to then deal with an employee of hoag who is dismissive, insensitive, unprofessional  and clearly unfit for handling a position at the hospital. upon checking in (without a greeting), she said name and insurance. i told her my insurance was in the system and she had responded immediately(without looking) that it was not. it was, because i was a rehabilitation patient for 2 and a half weeks at hoag, recovering from a near-death car accident that put me in a wheelchair. understand that you are working in a health care environment and you need to be trained as such. you are working with people who have suffered to some degree and you should be sympathetic and accommodating in making their experience as stress free as possible, not adding stress and anxiety to an already tense situation. i do not recommend going here.

i had a sleep deprived eeg scheduled for today at 9:30am. i'm new to the area and live in irvine. i show up to the hoag hospital in irvine only to find out i'm at the wrong hospital. who would have thought! they never told me the address when they confirmed the appointment and my doctor is in irvine. it was a complete nightmare. i have a 5 month old baby and a 3 year old plus we are all alone here in the us from canada for my  husbands work and i don't know all the hospitals in oc. i quickly call to let the newport hospital eeg department know i will be 1... not 5... but 1 minute late and she told me too bad! and empathy, no sympathy that i had zero sleep all night, a huge migraine, epilepsy, torn hip among many other issues hence the eeg and most cold heartedly tells me too bad! i am so angry! what horrible customer service. cedars sinai would never ever treat me this way and this is why i will continue to take the 1.5 hour drive in and the 3 hour trek home because they treat me with respect as a paying customer and understand their own mistakes. you guys never gave me the address! i had never been to your hospital before! thanks for ruining my day and for making my epilepsy journey so much harder.
great service, got registered and taken to my room quickly with no wait time upon my arrival.
great hospital but don't be late on any bill as this non profit send you to collections after 5 months from the first bill!?

december 27th 2019 was the happiest day of my life. my dear daughter was born. hoag is an amazing hospital i was dignosed with gd and their diabetes center gave me great support! the last weeks of my pregnancy i was refered to to nst (non stress testing) for my baby and the staff at fetal diagnostics was so welcoming and helpful. finally labor and delivery assisted me on 2 false alarms when i thought i was going into labor. they never made me feel incompetent even though  i clearly was not in labor. i am a first time mom and when finally the day came, they made my birthing experience wonderful. every step of the way i felt like i was treated like family. nurses and doctors were so warm and welcoming. my daughter was treated with so much care and attention. thank you so much hoag! i remember looking up reviews and would have loved for more people to truly express how this hospital is amazing! i truly appreciate all of the staff i wish i had names but forgot them. my ob was dr richard agnew i was one of the last deliveries for him he retired dec 31st he will be missed he was also so much help:) thank you.

hoag hospital has mis-diagnosed multiple times so far. they need to step up again and hire true doctors. it is really sad a hospital with this fame is so poor at proper diagnosis. me and family and colleague all tried this facility multiple times and they completely diagnosed wrong. all they did was trying to run tests and say things that wad not correct. very nice personnel though. i hope one day they be great again.

could your organization get any greedier or money hungry??? i had an ultrasound 8 days ago, i'm fully insured with ppo insurance. i have received two calls over the past 2 days asking me to call hoag's finance department. finally called back today to find out the billing department is calling me to tell me to expect the bill for the ultrasound in the mail and that it is hoag's policy to have all bills paid in full. when i asked when the bill was due i was told 30 days after i received the bill which would be, by my estimate, around 1/20/2020. i can't think of a more bizarre interaction with a healthcare system. how can hoag possibly be considered a nonprofit? no wonder you are losing business and out there begging for patients. since hoag is going to act like a for profit then it is time for this organization to start paying taxes!!!

i can not say enough about the emergency  room services in this hospital. it is just terrible. a few months ago my husband came in with all the symptoms of a heart attack, they made him wait outside and filled out some paper work. for about 5 to 10  minutes. in turns  out that in fact he had a heart attack!!! we all know that every minute counts when you are having one. 
today my mother, who does not speak english , came  in an ambulance due to possible stroke. she is in her 80's. i had to fight my way into her room, for about 30 minutes. she was by herself, unable to understand what was being asked, extremely nervous and none of the nurses seem to care,  they gave instructions of not letting any family member get in the room!!! as soon as i got in the room, they were able to clearly understand what happened to her, how she was feeling at the moment,  she needed the calmness and interpretation of her daughter. 
now i see why this emergency room seems to be always empty. 
ps. my husband had to be transferred to another hospital because they didn't have a cardiologist that could handle his case. my mother will probably have to be transferred too, no neurologist department here!!!!

hospital stays are not what we look forward to, but the staff at thph does their best to make you comfortable when you are the most uncomfortable. i spent three days there last week and really appreciate the nurses, pas, and doctors. i was admitted through the er and have high praise for their team as well. no matter the job, from admin to cleaning staff, everyone greeted me with a friendly smile, listened to me, and always asked if there was anything else they could do for me.

be very cautious about using this facility.  the care if fine, however, the billing will leave you extremely frustrated.  i visited the er and provided my license and insurance.  the hospital neglected to enter my address, and therefore never sent me a bill.  i finally was alerted that i had an outstanding charge when a collection agency contacted me.  after the hospital investigated and confirmed their error, they apologized and we arranged for a payment plan.  after finally being on a payment plan and making successful payments, i received another collection notice - the hospital was ignoring my payment plan - even after process a nov and dec payment from me in full.  basically they collected my in full payment and turned my account over anyway.  beware as this is unethical and i believe illegal when someone is making arranged payments in good faith.

this an utterly horrifying facility. 
an untrained and inexperienced social worker who clearly was newly "licensed" lied about what i said in an intake assessment. i had my lawyer attempt to get my paperwork under a hippa authorization release request and they admitted to shredding it. this is a complete violation of hippa.
i am in the process of attempting a lawsuit with my attorney.
do not go to this facility! i seriously urge you not to. it's dirty, unsafe, and filled with staff who lie to save their own behinds. seriously, if you or a loved one need mental health treatment, please go elsewhere. i urge you.
this place should be brought to light and shut down immediately.

i fell off a ladder doing a home improvement project barefoot and thought i broke my heel (#wearshoesonaladder). i didn't have time to shower and change clothes like i would have preferred-my wife loaded me up in the car as-is and drove me to medical city north hills. 

i found the entire experience to be exactly what i needed and hoped for- i got in quickly, had my pain controlled, was diagnosed accurately with a stone bruise (and thankfully not a fracture), and was discharged.  everyone was courteous and kind, the facility was clean, i got in and out quickly, and my care was very good.

this was not what i expected when seeing the yelp reviews being a "2 out of 5 star rating". i am grateful for the care i received and for having this hospital in my community right down the street.

i don't recommend falling off a ladder to experience  the er, but...they made a painful situation so much better for me and i appreciate they took great care of me when i needed them!!!!!!

i have been coming to this hospital since i was a teenager and every single visit i have ever had with them has always been horrible. their staff are not professional at all the doctors are not caring or almost not knowledgeable. the wait time is ridiculous i live right down the street from this hospital and i will go all the way to alliance harris methodist if we need to go to the er. my husband had a stomach virus and when we went there all they said was that he was dehydrated and just made it seem like he was just ridiculous for being there. when we went to alliance they kept my husband overnight and come to find out from a stool sample he had a bacteria growing in his stomach from food poisoning so therefore we now have a hospital bill that was unnecessary and a waste of time being there. you're better off going to urgent care and getting the same treatment because i don't think those doctors care enough to be in a emergency room setting. the weight and the rooms are so small cramped outdated and so uncomfortable for as long as they have everyone waiting there especially for labs it's ridiculous that they don't have it at least more comfortable. i hate literally hate this hospital it's the most horrible hospital ever.

i had a kidney stone today, the second worse pain i have ever had. what was the first? my first kidney stone. i have also had several broken bones, face reconstructed with titanium, and i have been shot. i know pain... i had to walk out of harris methodist downtown fort worth (literal assholes) twice before going to nrh er today... hm treated me like i had no insurance and no money. neither can be further from the truth. after still being in the triage area for almost 3 hours, i couldn't take it any longer, so i can to nrh er. they had me in a bed in 10 minutes, treated me with medicine within 30 minutes, and on my way in approximately an hour... all this while being attentive, compassionate, knowledgeable, and efficient. get this, they literally said to me that they didn't want to run up a needless bill... i will admit that i had a bad experience at this location once before but since it didn't have anything to do with compassion, i gave it another try and i was so glad i did today.

this is sad at the quality provided by most of the staff here. 

  there are few shining lights of care and hope here but overall the support staff really need to consider their roles here.
  examples: dietary restrictions provided by doctors and yet food is still delivered late and the wrong meal. then the replacement meal is later than the first. (incorrect lunch is corrected and almost arrives at dinner? really?)

  medical staff does not make the scheduled rounds. services staff does not seem to care or pay attention to details.

 the cafeteria should be a nice area yet all i tend to see are dirty tables wiped with dirty towels while security and cafe staff just lounge.

  the cafe is always cluttered it seems and the food prep stations should be better managed and controlled; you would think that a hospital would respect safety and quality standards to prevent germ contamination.
  are these sticking points detailed? yes. for many reasons.

review:
one sorry hospital in my opinion. i have insurance and they demanded a very large cash payment before they would perform a procedure. i asked about a payment plan and they basically told me i could apply for their credit card and wait to see if i would get approved before allowing payments. i am sure there are people that dont have money getting write offs but the person with insurance that wants to make payments is screwed. i am seriously considering changing from a great doctor just so i am not forced to use this facility as its the only one he practices in.
i might also add that i got a rude phone call reminder to be at my appt at such and such time. lady acted like she was put out to call.

review:
came in to have some blood taken for some tests. was promptly checked in and taken to the back waiting room where i proceeded to wait for over 90 minutes. the reason i know it was over 90 minutes was the lady next to me congratulated me on the time. seems she had been waiting as long. not sure of why it took so long, but there were people who came in after me that got in and out ahead of me. once inside the actual procedure lasted about three or four minutes. for the amount of people working there you would think it would have been a relatively short wait, but no.
inexcusable!
also was surprised at the dirty floors in the lab area.

this place is greedy and guilty of horrendous price gauging. my daughter visited the er a few months ago and we were left with the most ridiculously expensive er bill i've even seen for a simple visit. the total charges without insurance came to around $10,000. even after insurance paid their portion, we were left with $2500. others in our family have visited various ers for the exact same issue and the total price without insurance was between $2000-$3000, not $10,000. unless you'll die otherwise, go anywhere but here.

aurora behavioral health center has a very inviting website, yet it's not what it seems.
my friend checked in to detox from an alcohol binge and only needed to safely detox so went in to do an intake process. once she signed some paper work she was then removed most of her belongings only leaving her in jeans and a long sleeve shirt. 
she was brought up to her ward and was given very little direction aside from where her room was and where the schedule for the day was on the wall. because it was 5pm they provided no food for her because dinner had already taken place at 4:30.
during her first night she became concerned and spoke with the nurse about the chances of leaving and doing an intensive out patient program instead. they told her this isnt how it works and she would be there as long as the psychiatrist saw fit. 
she asked if there was any way to leave legally and the nurse reluctantly said that there was an option of an ama (against medical advice) but that they highly discouraged it and that her insurance probably wouldn't cover it and that she would still have to stay a mandatory 24 hours after signing it.  this is a way to deter you from leaving as there are several homeless addicts in the hospital as well.
this was only for detox from only alcohol, not even hard alcohol. she wasn't depressed, suicidal and only expressed that she had some anxiety.
she was finally able to call me the next day when they opened up the phones. this is when she told me the ward was really cold and uncomfortable, probably around  60-65 degrees.  the beds are were hard and had a sheet and a very thin blanket with a plastic pillow. she said it was almost impossible to stay warm considering she only had a shirt on. they gave her a hospital town to keep her extra warm.  the social room was also very uncomfortable, very hard furniture. pretty much the most uncomfortable setting she could have wanted for help.  the whole process is very systematic, you are treated as a prisoner, the only plus side is they give you drugs so you can sleep.
while she was there she met several people that had only gone in there to speak to a therapist or get counseling cause they felt depressed and they were stuck there over a week. constantly told they couldn't leave because the psychiatrist didn't feel that they were ready. these were people that didn't walk in even on medication!  they ended up prescribing my friends with three prescriptions when really she only wanted to safely detox from alcohol.
this is a scary process and if you dont have insurance they wont let you discharge without paying in full. this is why they keep you as long as possible.

just so people know. you shouldn't be discouraged to sign an ama is you feel like the treatment isn't helpful. you can also call the police to come get you if you want to leave.

i know people need help but this really wrecked my friend, not just for her but for her family.  she also mentioned there's no one on one therapy, they do group sessions that most people walk out of and they are directed by inexperienced social workers. most the time the more talkative patients take over the group and it ends up pointless.

i can't believe anyone would recommend this place for someone that isn't categorized as smi (severe mental issues).

mostly wonderful!
doctors are very knowledgeable and nurses are some of the best i've experienced. 
had problems with lack of communication within the hospital. i feel that the doctors, nurses, and other staff should improve by communicating more with each other. 
other than that small "hiccup", i would say this is the best choice for health care in wilkes, surry and somewhat yadkin county. 
overall a great experience!

review:
las encinas made a difficult psychiatric evaluation easier.
the food is good and the accommodations are okay for what they are. 3 beds per room but i had two nights by myself.
the nursing staff seems to really care.

please read:

i have been to las encinas few times...so i know how it was back then compared to how it was last year. never too late for a review though.

first: the nice pictures, the nice pictures , very clean, nice interior is from brier residential. not inpatient units either (detox or mental health unit)).  

few years ago,  both units were full., very clean, quite a few nurses, organized meetings for both units. we could go outside..get fresh air..there were puzzles, books. not to mention the cafeteria was open, and sunny (not 
half as it was last year). food, was great,

last year, it was a ghost town. downstairs unit was maybe one or 2 patients so they moved those patients from downstairs to detox unit. they closed the downstairs unit and it's nurses station. 

las encinas, the nurses and all the staff , all combined , was support 
system for what ever the reason for patients were there.

wish they would make some changes, if they haven't yet.
residential is great because they get money from insurance who people can afford to have expensive insurance plans.

bottom line: 

a)  the pictures are deceiving. it's residential brier. people with top notch insurance stay there and have money stay there.

 b)  maybe one group a day, if any...jeff gammy has a great meeting.  
back then we had morning check in group. also had aa panels that came entire day we were kept busy.

c)  having staff do your laundry? last year i was there for few days but that what i heard for this year.
so someone with ocd, like myself, have to let others handle my clothes..

d)  no activity what so ever, basically you spend time watching tv and day dream. if just around, looking like zombies.

e)  what happened to las encinas. i learned quite a bit with encouragement all day groups. 

f)  forgot this one:  back then( not my stay a year ago. few years ago, they would check our bags and suitcases inside the room. (right after in take) inside assigned rooms, so you wouldn't feel uncomfortable and more private.  las year they open your suitcase or bag inside the nurses station, and everyone on there (male workers) also watch. i felt so uncomfortable and with ocd i packed whole bunch. i'm sure all stuff looked at me thinking nut case!

all my recovery, med adjustment, i owe to las encinas.  i can't deal with change. i'd go back because it's familiar to me. 

jeff gammy knows recovery. some of the nurses were great

last years was not good. i hope they can make changes

worst staff ever! no one in this facility really gives a shit about the patients seeking care. you are treated worse than an inmate and forced to inhale feces that is never cleaned up. the nurses just lock themselves in their station and have no compassion for the patients having a hard time adjusting. the only good thing that came out of this place is knowing that this place is honestly worse than any image or thought of hell and i never want to end up in my dark thoughts again in hopes of never returning there again. las encinas is inhumane! shame on the staff for being so cruel. $1,500 to be tortured. dr. alikhan and all the social workers do not care about their patients.

i was in the day program due to mental illness. i was put in johnath group.  i was the only one that had a mental illness.  he didn't help me with my problems at all.  i left coming back worse then i started.

not a phone in sight.... just patients living in the moment....

in all seriousness though the nurses at this hospital took a few things from me. when i was checked in i was asked to sign a paper that was suppose to list all my possessions i came in with. the paper was blank and i was off an ambien so i didn't think much of it. when i was discharged i was missing my cigarette case that was full of gift cards (a few of them were unused with values of $100) , but since it wasn't listed with my items there was no way i could get it back. called them a few times and would get transferred back and forth between the wards for a few hours until i was told whoever handles the lost items had left for the day/ was on lunch. nurses also made me sign a release stating they would not return any of the ( legal and medical ) marijuana i had with me when i came in. hundreds of dollars worth of flower and cbd products gone just like that. i saw on the paper that it was optional, but was told i had to sign it or i wouldn't be able to get discharged. 

cassandra was my favorite nurse. only one who was gentle when waking us up for vitals and made sure she got all the smokers to come downstairs for cigarette breaks when they were happening.

nice hospital, but like others say you need an advocate for you on the outside or it's going to be tough to get discharged.

i have now had two horrible experiences with this facility. the first was with a family member several years ago when i did not think their psychologists were professional with follow up. the second experience was just recently with a client, who was not told the psychiatrist who saw her in an emergency situation was not covered by her insurance. the admissions staff was not particularly friendly or helpful either.

i had seen this place deteriorate over a period of 22 years.  it used to be a  place where one  could actually find help.  as an inpatient having access to the lovely grounds helped in the healing process in a very profound way.  we had various activities, like arts and crafts and swimming.  in  inpatient  they had gradually taken away many patient privileges, and made access to the grounds smaller and smaller until there was no access for us poor slobs at all.  if you are a wealthy addict, you can go to briar and have access to what all of us used to have access to.   the staff has become more callous, and downright cruel and manipulative. i personally got caught up in a really nasty  power struggle  and tons of gaslighting with some therapists there, and a more  vulnerable person would have been traumatized. i have watched the general state of mental health treatment rot over the years, and judging by these recent reviews, it has gotten much worse.  we seem to be slouching toward bedlam.  i was considering a return to las encinas iop after being away for 3 years.  i have tried other places that i felt were very unsafe, but these reviews have made me change my mind.  treating the mentally ill like criminals is never acceptable.  neither is gaslighting. it is abuse, and should be considered a human rights violation.   i guess i amjust going to  have to wait until conditions and  the rights of the mentally ill improve again before i seek any help.  i don't know when that will happen as these are very dark times.

oh god, she's so fat

ok lets be straight- i'm a big girl. i've struggled with my weight my whole life. 
i'm also narcoleptic, and have fought a battle with depression and anxiety since i was 10. are these things an issue? yep. do they define me and explain every issue without an obvious answer? no, they do not. 

unless, of course, i am an in-patient at abrazo central campus.

the first doctor i met was called "dr. d." the first thing to roll out of his mouth upon meeting me was "have you considered gastric bypass surgery?" no hello? the second thing was "are you diabetic?" diabetes was a natural first question, as i was there because neuropathy in my feet was spreading alarmingly fast up both my legs.

something to rule out for sure, but folks, i am not diabetic. 

not if abrazo staff pokes me every 6 hrs for 2 days, not if the dr orders 2 different blood tests, not if he adds insulin to my prn list while neglecting my actual prescriptions, not by the hair of my chinny chin chin! 
so whats next?

oh awesome, here comes the neurologist. a gallon or two of my blood was taken for testing, a spinal tap and mri were ordered. 

the spinal tap was, of course, terrifying. one of my symptoms was spontaneous involuntary muscle spasms and they wanted to put a giant needle in my spine that could paralyze me if i moved! 
i had a panic attack. i have already admitted that i have anxiety. but wouldn't you call that a reasonable fear? 

now, looking over the paperwork, i see references to my anxiety all over the place as a poor explanation for their failure to find the reason for the neuropathy

but back to the fat prejudice, as that is my theme.
 
when i was admitted, i was starving. i had spent hours in the er before being transferred to the hospital. i had only expected to spend a few hours at the er and for them to do whatever they do and send me home.
so i asked for a sandwich. 3 hours and multiple ignored requests passed between me and that sandwich. it was one of those little elementary school sized ones with one slice of mystery meat, a slice of cheese, and two pieces of bread cut in a diagonal. 

i ate it thankfully. an hour later, i was still hungry and asked if there was somewhere i could get some food. perhaps a vending machine? they put me off a couple more hours and served me fat shame with my second sandwich. 

then, when i was sitting up in bed in the middle of the night (as i do multiple times a night, part of the narcolepsy) the nurse walking by stopped and asked, "your not eating again, are you?" with a horrified expression on his face. 

time for the mri came, and the tech walked in, looked at me, and walked back out into the hall. he announced that i was too fat for the machine several times using different descriptors. he was ordered to try anyways. yep, i heard all of it. i'm sure the neighboring rooms did too. 

he left, and came back with the biggest wheelchair i have ever seen. 
i told him i had heard him in the hall, and he did look genuinely embarrassed and apologetic, so i dropped it.  it turns out that i did fit, but it was so snug that we decided it would be better to wait for a machine that was 70 inches rather than the one there that was 60. 

so yeah, he was pretty much right. 

but my complaint is about a complete and widespread attitude of prejudice and lack of tact because of my weight. 

i am also concerned about the fact that we, the patients, could hear everything the staff was saying to each other in the hallway. i can tell you exactly what was wrong with the people on either side of me and not because i was trying to listen. i think its unprofessional. 

i have a lot of other complaints too.... but i'll just leave it at that.

well, that and that my symptoms have not resolved, an explanation has not been found, and now i have a giant bill for labs that nobody bothered to interpret, and that i can only pray the insurance company will cover most of. 
the list is a few pages long. i may have been tested for bubonic plague, i haven't made it through the whole list yet.

if you are planning a visit to an abrazo er, do a quick check first. can you see your feet while standing up? 

if not, you might want to chose a different er.

one of the worst experiences of my life. from the moment of check-in with that nurse ratchet in the middle of the night. i'm still not sure what she thought she was presiding over. i guess i'm to blame as well. not knowing phoenix very well i asked to be taken to nearest er. i actually thought i was closer to st.joe. boy did i miss that by a few (& i don't mean miles) . there was one redeeming male nurse, he's about the only thing they had going for them. he was a good nurse.

 the guy at the front desk says that " mam stop yelling at me" i stated i'm not yelling i'm in  pain   and i apologized, continuing to cooperate w answering his questions. he says mam i told you to stop yelling and wheels me into another room and shuts the door- no explanation.

review: i had to get admitted for a blood transfusion. ryan and deziree on the 7th floor made my experience a great one. they are so nice, catered to my needs, made me not even think about how bad i felt. even ieshia from housekeeping was great and so warm. the whole staff in general was very helpful and so sweet.  for a hospital that is full and so busy they really did make me feel at home and catered to all my needs and requests.

my frustration with mh is to the point that if my doctor requires me to utilize their facilities, it's time to find another doctor. 

i have been trying to get mh to file a claim correctly for over a year. what a headache! i'm amazed by their incompetence.

thank you methodist houston for your professionalism and for not putting your patients through similar situations.

      the ct scan alone was about $3800, similar to in the following news story about another in-network ct scan bill ---) https://www.clarionledger.com/story/news/politics/2018/07/02/hospital-told-patient-insurance-pays-ct-scan-billed-him-3-800/740151002/

   i have had a gallbladder removal surgery at memorial hermann er for more like $3000 under similar insurance and my girlfriend's birth around $7000 and apparently no way to anticipate how high this bill would be.

unethical and fraudulent. i've advised him to report the hospital and doctor to the texas attorney general.

review:
i was admitted into the er and then the the cardiac unit last week and i have nothing but superlatives to say about my experience.  i have never experienced an entire staff of such compassionate staff of medical professionals in any other hospital. the main purpose of this review is to give recognition to the fine people who helped save my life (although the emts inside the port orchard skfd ambulance who transported me to harrison get the primary credit and thank you for the excellent care i received on the way to the hospital). in the er my utmost thanks to dr. schindler, who supervised my care when i was first wheeled into the er. i was barely conscious but i remember her telling me her name and taking charge. she immediately filled me with total confidence as she led the team that gave me my initial emergency care. i was also lucky to have an amazingly compassionate er nurse named maureen who came into my room to care for me and to comfort my family even though she was not my assigned er nurse. another er nurse named brett, who wheeled me out of the er and up to the cu had a great sense of humor which i greatly appreciated considering the experience i had just endured. 

i met and was cared for by a uniformly wonderful and compassionate cardiac nursing staff. their names are andrew, ashley, egar, kayla, janet, lauren and mandy. i love them all, they will all remain special to me. they were all incredible and very sweet. every nurse treated me with respect, compassion and dignity. some of the nurses gave me important medical information and advice, and with a couple we got into talking about food and cooking which was a real kick. i want to single out janet for the immense help she gave in getting me discharged quickly from the hospital and providing extensive post-care written information along with medical prescriptions for my post-care. she took the time to verbally explain everything although it was also in the written printouts in the discharge folder. this doesn't begin to describe what she did for me on my last day. my wife and i will always be grateful to her. but as i said, all the nurses who gave me care are the finest i have ever known. 

karen, who did my echocardiogram also deserves my thanks. she allowed me to see the sonogram in process and explained exactly what i was watching as well as telling me some interesting stories. 

a huge thank you goes out to dr. jason chung, the cardiologist who supervised my care. gotta use the word compassionate again in describing his manner. his care was extraordinary, he was on top of everything with my case which included multiple issues.  

lastly, i want to recognize ash, the person who wheeled me out of the hospital directly to where my wife had parked our car in the south parking lot. he showed both humor and (that word again) compassion and was very respectful, calling me sir with almost every sentence. i feel like i'm just a regular guy but he sure elevated my self-image. 

for me, five stars is just not high enough to rate these magnificent professionals. i will be eternally grateful to you all.

first, this place was great taking care of my grandmother in her end of life moments.  second, i was born here 41 years ago, so i have to give them props for that.

as i sit here today, i cannot believe the way i am watching people being talk to and how they just talked to me and one of my employees, who has pancreatitis from blocked bile duct.  ive never had it, but i think it probably sucks.  my employee is a very timid man in his mid 50s.  he is from guatemala and this process is terrifying for him.  the last month he has been complaining of stomach pains.  i told him, he needs to go to a doctor and it sounded like a gallbladder issue.  i wrote him a letter to give to a physician a month ago, in the letter explainrd that it sounded like a gallbladder thing.  so, he called in this morning and i said jose (not his name), you cant come back to work until you get a doctor's note.  so he finally went.  to be clear, this man is my family.  after being here for over 6 hours (not their fault, its busy) they said he needed to have surgery, from what i understand and he flew the coup.  the guy didnt know what was going on.  he called me and kind of explained what happened but through the language barrier, he thought he had something wrong with his stomach and wanted me to read the paper, which was a paper that said he left on his own accord against their recommendations.  i told him the paper doesnt say what the problem was.  he asked if i could call and figure out what was wrong with him.  i talked to a nurse, she couldnt give me much info, even with jose there, but i pulled from it, gall stones.

at the hospital, i explained, "hey, it sounds like he was scared and confused and he wanted to ask me for help.  i go to the dmv with this man.  i go to immigration in tukwilla to help when his paperwork gets messed up (he has been a legal resident for like 20 years).  even in these settings, he gets extremely nervous and cant communicate.  plus, people are mean as hell without knowing they are mean as hell.  even if you were speaking in broken spanish, under these circumstances, he wouldn't understand.  so the nurse was one of these people x10.  

she comes out, after the very nice front desk lady got her, in the most condescending manner.  "so, why did he leave!?!?"  mam, he is from a small town in guatemala and this scenario is extremely intimidating.  "excuse me, i work at a hospital, i treat people from other countries.  i dont need an education from you about that".  no, seriously, verbatim.  i let her know that she speaks to people terribly.  she then said to me, "well he said he left because you didnt believe him".  i have no idea wtf she was talking about with that.  then she looked at jose and said loudly, "why did you leave?!?!, now were going to have to check you in and put you through the whole process again.  you are going to have to get another iv and give more blood".  jose tried to answer but as expected, it made no sense, because the poor guy was so nervous his hands were visibly shaking.  i stopped her and said, "hold on, now youre sounding punitive.  why would they need to take more blood if they just took it".  she mumbled some more stuff and was equally rude.  she has long black hair and looks to be about 50.  another employee whinced nearby.  she was terrible.  just to be clear i can only imagine how difficult their job is, but there is no excuse.  

in the next 40 minutes i watched another nurse(?) come out and speak to a grown man like a parent would speak to a tired 4 year old "i dont know sir, thats your decision whether you come or go, but my beds are full and it will be a long wait".  she said it loudly so everyone focused on the man, again the tone was the bad part, if the same words were said in a nice quite way it would have been innocuous.

jose and were finally called in.  a new nurse with the same voice that sounds like shes an annoyed parent talking to a child so that everyone can hear.  "so watcha here for".  "well my friend...", i told her the story.  "okay, and so what can we do for ya", in this condescending tone.  at that point i just said, well hes got a blocked duct and pancreatitis, should he leave, or?

neglected would have been a step up from my first and only visit here. my back was bad enough i was unable to walk. it took a total of five people to get me out of the car and onto a gurney. i was wheeled back past the waiting room where i was just forgetting in the hallway for an hour.

particularly nice that it's easy to get to, you don't have to spend valuable time taking tours of the parking lot looking for a spot.  gps brings you to the front door, it's a breeze.

review:
i broke my ankle and went there on a recommendation. full disclosure, it was a friday morning (not a saturday night), but we were in and out in three hours, which went very quickly. staff was great, place is immaculate and now they have private rooms with televisions (a huge upgrade over the old er). 

one tiny complaint: i had to use the ladies room and the attendant didn't know how to transfer me from the wheel chair. i ended up hopping over the footrest. come on, i can't be the only one whose ever shown up immobile and had to pee.

one bigger complaint: my husband had to go back in to get my xrays on a disc after the orthopedist they recommended (and said they were on pascack's system) told me that they aren't, and wouldn't be able to read them unless we brought them. could i have been the first patient to go to the recommended orthopod after breaking a bone and showing up at the er?

mister's dad needed emergency back surgery on christmas eve and our experience at this hospital could not have been better. 

the surgery itself took about an hour and then they monitored him for 3 hours. after that he was ready to go home! not only was it quick, i feel like there was always a nurse coming in to check in on him or offer us something. 

i loved when our nurse said it was a super busy christmas eve night in the hospital. i barely saw anyone in the halls! any other hospital i've been to most of the time i'm in the hallway on a stretch because they don't have enough rooms. this place definitely took care of him and made every minute he was there as pleasant as possible. 

even though we were only there for a few hours, they offered us plenty of chairs and their nourishing room which had snacks and drinks. i mean really, it doesn't get better. it's way out of the way for me but if you're in this area this is the hospital to go to.

i am not a fan of emergency rooms however the nurses and doctors are so nice and accommodating the rooms are clean you get your own room with a tv.  the doctors explain everything and provide advice this  er is a hidden quiet gem.

my mom had to stay two nights here and i was so impressed with how well the care was during that time. everyone was friendly and you could tell they really cared. something that impressed my mom was how fast the response was to her "call nurse" button.
