this is the worst hospital i have ever been too. if i could give it 0 stars i would. this isn't the first time i've had a bad hospital trip here either. the nurses and doctors love to sit on their asses, when you ask them a question no one has an answer for you, but as they walk by 100 times no one says not one thing to you. they put their patients out in their hallways and let's not forget how disgustingly dirty it is here. i'm appalled, if you can bring a loved one or yourself to any other hospital make sure you do it. they would rather see their patients screaming  in pain instead of doing the right thing. this place fucking sucks.

it is just unbelievable our personal information has been breached once again this is like the third time this has happened to me. may i suggest better training of employees not to open suspicious e/mails vassar is a decent hospital but this is undoubtably complacent behavior on part of there staff and must be dealt with accordingly totally unacceptable.

my mom was about to leave the hospital and needed to go somewhere for a while longer until she could start breathing on her own without the machines. they gave me some recommendations for places closer to where i live so i did my due diligence and researched them. i narrowed it down to new england sinai and curahealth. my friend recommended new england sinai so i tried to set up a tour but it was like pulling teeth to get it arranged. i couldn't get calls returned and then when i finally set it up and showed up and no one knew i was coming so i sat there for 30 min so they could find someone to show me around. finally got my tour and i have to say it's really a nice facility but it was more of the same with the staff. they seemed overworked and rude and didn't want to be bothered. i'm from the south where being respectful and courteous to others is extremely important and these people really rubbed me the wrong way. so then i drove on over to curahealth without any appointment and walked in and asked the lady at the front desk for a tour. she thanked me for coming in and made a call and a minute later bridget came out and shook my hand with a smile (big points in my book) and took me on a tour. the facility is a little older and smaller than new englanf sinai but the staff was very friendly. eveyone was nice and answered my questions. so i made my decision and my mom was sent to curahealth a few days later. i have to say that i believe my mom got the best care there. i visited almost every day and was never turned away. i met all her nurses and respiratory people and everyone was always happy to answer my questions. i met the ceo greg who was a quiet guy and would never laugh at my jokes :( but he was always there for me. i even saw him on the floor helping his staff with patients a bunch of times. mom got better after a few weeks and we were a little sad when we had to leave but i still visit sometimes to say hi to everyone.

was to say;i had injured my foot to the point of immobility. i have made it to the end of the er drive ramp and then called for a wheelchair. i was told, could not send out a chair... thought it is a joke... wt? not one staffer offered assistance of any kind. do i want that to be working on me? thanks summerlin hosp e.r....  ya got no heart.
great hospital. nurses and doctors are very professional and caring . staff takes their time and patience to find out what's wrong with you. pediatric department is on point.

most people that write reviews, write negative ones... i however appreciate  the effort the  staff puts forth every  visit i've had or my  children have had with summerlin hospital. tests take time, and the nurse can't make them go any faster! so duhhhhh chill out people! thank you  for your continuous effort to provide good service here in vegas!

my mother was taken to this hospital because she fainted. they took blood from her to see what's wrong, the nurse didn't wear gloves nor wash her hands. later i told another nurse who was also in the room with us when it happened but she didn't see it. she told me to bring up my concerns next time i see it. there won't be a next time. i wouldnt let any of my closed ones  go back to this place. if you didn't read the reviews and was taken here because of emergency just beware they do this. the man in the ambulance caused a lot of pain to her when he stucked in the needle  in her veins while inside the ambulance too. it's just bad to get sick and have to hand over your life to people who don't care.

do not go here!! if i could give negative stars i would!  i never take the time to write reviews but as a new mother i feel this is absolutely necessary for other mothers. most of our staff were fantastic and this review has no reflection on them what so ever. my baby caught rsv virus at 3 weeks old. we were transported via ambulance to summerlin hospital. 

first issue: food! as a nursing mother i need food and nutrition and they completely dropped the ball  on this. i didn't receive dinner until 8pm the first night my baby was admitted. next day, i didn't receive dinner at all. i called to complained to nutritionist the next morning about it and  also complained about the fact i was never given a choice of what food i wanted either. the following day my food came extremely late and it was the wrong order. i called to complain once again and she told me she resent it and i didn't get my breakfast until 1115am! the day after that they messed up my breakfast order again!!! they said it "got lost" and they were "sorry" and again i received breakfast around 1045am! my baby was deathly ill and the last thing i should have to worry about is calling and hunting down food for myself as i'm nursing my sick baby. 

second issue: one of the nurses. my baby started having a coughing spell around 12pm one night and was turning red and actually chocking because he couldn't breathe. i called the nurse immediately. she turned his oxygen up a bit and left the room. our baby continued coughing uncontrollably to where my husband and i thought he was for sure going to stop breathing (because that happened the previous day). we voiced concerns with nurse and she insisted we just keep him propped up to help control chocking and coughing. we told her this was not okay and he needed help as he was literally
gasping for air. we asked for pediatrician. nurse told us they always do a big consultation with the group as pediatricians need sleep between shifts. can you believe that!!! our baby was literally beat red gasping for air and the nurse didn't want to contact the pediatrician because they were sleeping between shifts?!!!! my husband told her to get pediatrician on the phone now. she did. pediatrician advised nurse to crank my babies oxygen to 8 and about blew my babies nostrils out of his head which caused him to cry and become even more hysterical than he already was which led to even more difficulty breathing and even more chocking!!!! we yelled at nurse to get pediatrician again! pediatrician said she wasn't going to give him anything for his cough! respiratory lady came in and instantly said he needed to be on a different breathing machine and she transferred us to another room asap!!! if we didn't push and be stern with the nurse to wake the damn pediatrician up and make a stink about all of this who knows what would have happened to our baby! thank god for respiratory nurse! to top all of that nightmare off the same nurse put in his new oxygen tube in his nose backwards so it was shooting air up and out of his nose instead back into his nose!!

third issue: sewage gas leakage!! yes a sewage leakage in the middle of all of this! we woke up to a foul smell and my grandmother fanning out 


last issue: the last issue was the cleanliness. my room was absolutely disgusting and the janitor didn't come by for a full day to empty the trash and it was actually overflowing along with trash everywhere on the floor! the head nurse finally came in and took it out and even he was pissed about it! whatever you do don't go here! it's one thing dealing with a sick baby but it's another when you cant event trust the hospital to look after your sick baby!

i had to go to the er a couple of weeks ago due to a foreign object in my eye. the staff could not have been more caring or kind. dr. morgan came in to take care of the issue and she successfully found the object and was able to remove it. a male nurse david took good care of me and kept me posted on what would happen. both of these team members were complete professionals and i felt very comfortable in their hands. thank you!

because quest diagnostics's compromised my blood test results my kidney doctor rushed me to summerlin hospital er to redo my blood draw and while i was there an ultrasound and urine tests. from registration to the er staff i had a pleasant, quick and satisfying experience. clean, comfortable and efficient. thank you summerlin hospital er.. excellent experience!! ( and i hate hospitals)!!

the staff in labor and delivery were very attentive and nice. once i got moved to the postpartum area the disappointment of the treatment that i got went began.  they didn't check on me for hours and i had to constantly press the button for service. the nurses aren't really helpful or nice in this unit. worse hospital and experience ever!! i should've went to southern hills to give birth. the supervisor came to my room to ask how my stay was and i told her how miserable i was. she tried to make things right in the end but it was already too late since i was getting discharged later that day.

i want to say i give 5 stars to the staff, nurses and people coming to my room to take care of me. i am giving a lower rating for the following reasons: i went to the emergency with chest and jaw pain. they got me in right away..thank you. the took my blood did x rays, they were taking really great care of me. i was asked to check into the hospital and spend the night. this was on a sunday. i didnt see the cardiologist till the next day. he ordered a ct of my heart with contrast. i was there 3 nights before the test was done on the 4th day of my stay wed. why so long? i never had an answer for this. they tried to keep me an additional night and i demanded to see my test results. it was safe for me to check out so i did and stayed with my dad that night and flew back to california the next day. i never saw the cardiologist or got a phone call from him to talk with me about my high calcium score on my ct. basically i felt like they blew me off while trying to keep me there for as long as possible for a simple test that was 30 min. the nurses were great! thank you. very disappointed in the lack of communication. i started to feel like they were keeping me there to rack up the bill. not a great feeling when you are away from home.

absolute joke of a so-called pediatric er . they put up partitions, add a few toys with a child's room for triage, and call it a pediatric er.  my child injured her foot and it was suggested by our primary doctor to go her.  worst decision on my part.  when we first arrived, i asked to use a wheelchair for my young daughter that way hobbling.  the woman at the desk told me to leave it and just have her hobble or carry her because they needed it for someone who couldn't walk!!!  what was my daughter doing?  faking her injury?  i should have left then and there but with flu season rampant and new to the area, i had no idea where to go.  next, we were triaged and of course, the pediatric patient was even triaged in the special pediatric triage room, just thrown with all of the adults bleeding and coughing everywhere.  the x-ray process went smoothly but my daughter was never given a room to see the doctor.  nurse came out and suggested pain relief which took her 45 minutes to bring to my daughter.  dr. michael (who was not even a pediatric doctor) came out for all of 5 minutes to talk to us to tell us that her ankle wasn't broken but was sprained.  no time or care was given to my daughter at any point in time.  i had to beg to have my child's foot wrapped and given crutches because she was in so much pain. yes, sprains hurt too.  i have lived all over the country and have visited many ers with my children and this was by far the worst experience ever!  there were so many unhappy and uncaring employees that i encountered.  friendliness and kindness were non-existent and a child was involved.  pathetic!   if you are a parent that cares about your child, do not take your child here at all!! in fact, don't even send your worst enemy here.

had my second kiddo here and had a minor operation here as well. both times all employees had excellent bed-side manners and customer service. if this hospital is in network for you i would highly recommend choosing this one.

this is the absolute worst medical care imaginable.
no prioritization in their triage as to severity. someone with hand injury goes before a galstone patient about to pass out.  amazing, attitude, no compassion what so ever. for the smallest county with the highest per capita income, i would take my chances in a 3rd world country.
if you don't have an emergency and have hours, roll the dice, otherwise just take the drive to dallas

my daughter was sick and doc at northside said she must had a virus. she was discharged. children's hospital diagnosed her later with an uti and prescribed antibiotics.

northside charged me usd 2k for a wrong diagnose. now take your own conclusions...

i took my husband to their er two weeks ago for respiratory issues and possible pneumonia. he was seen to by a doctor before i could get my car parked. what followed was a hospital stay for nine days on their respiratory floor. 

we can't say enough good things about the quality of care, the compassion, the thoroughness, the attitude and the genuine sterling work ethic of all who work at northside cherokee. 

they were able to diagnose a secondary potential disease while testing my husband for pneumonia and probably have saved his life. 

beautiful, clean, friendly and professional. i hope you don't have to go, but it's the place to do if you must!

dont get me wrong i have a healthy son, im healthy and had some wonderful nurses but my birthing experience was horrible. i came in 6 cm dilated and had two lovely nurses. very chipper and understood you have to be quiet during contractions. (i had a natural birth, no pain relievers of any sort) my midwife knew me from my first birth and knew i labored fast so they moved me to the labor room. nice big room, very clean. as i was in transition i had fifty papers to sign obviously you can't go around that which i think is horrible because i have no clue what i signed. 9 cm,- in a lot of pain. 10 more nurses walk in all talking and laughing. pushing- tall nurse sounded like a drill sergeant in a mean tone telling me (along with everyone else) if i want this baby out i have to hold my legs when i said i couldn't do it because well i was in a uncomfortable position and had another nurse bending my leg backwards along the nurses still all chatting away here's drill sergeant still yelling at me. 9lb bab
somewhat hard to find but very efficient and clean once you get there. something of a drive from marietta, but professional service with little waiting.

i unfortunately had to put my mom here after a fall because she was on dialysis and couldn't walk well. the rehab here is good , and the dialysis treatment was fine . however, it is dark and dingy and looks more like a prison. the food was awful . we had to bring food every day . also ,the nurses are so overwhelmed that they on occasion yelled at her for asking for help. my mom begged to be taken out of there .
fac_name: ArchCare at Terence Cardinal Cooke Health Care Center

review:
warning: this is long and probably tmi but whatever!

this review is for the walk-in/urgent care clinic. i was told at the ward clinic the wait would be 45 minutes there so i called here and the receptionist said that she couldn't promise anything but at the moment there was only one patient and two doctors. i was in a bit of pain so decided to come here instead. 

i wasn't aware the main hospital had a walk-in clinic, but the receptionist at ward was very helpful in explaining where to find it, and that we should park in the main hospital garage.

so fyi, the walk-in clinic is in the strode building to the right as you're looking at the entrance from king street. my husband dropped me off at the patient dropoff area so that i could go to the clinic while he parked, and there were plentiful signs for the strode building. it's located just past the pharmacy, and you go through a walkway to get to it. 

the super helpful receptionist quickly took my info and immediately provided me with a cup for a urine sample. i provided it, and it took about 10-15 minutes before they called me back to see the doctor.

based on previous experience, i thought it was a kidney infection or kidney stone - but i wanted to rule out appendicitis because two of my sisters had to have surgery for it, one of them just a month ago.

after hearing my symptoms, dr. susie chun didn't think it was appendicitis and ordered an ultrasound to check my right kidney, where the pain was. we then went to radiology, which is in the main building, second floor. the receptionist and techs were also friendly and helpful there; btw it's super freezing in there, so they provide warm blankets in a metal heater at the back, against the wall. note: you open the heater by pulling on the right side of the door, not the left. watched a couple of people struggle to open it before realizing what side to open. also, for an ultrasound, you must have a full bladder. because i emptied mine to provide a sample at intake, i had to drink several cups and wait about 20 minutes before they could do the procedure.

after the ultrasound, we went back to the clinic, where dr. chun said it showed slight inflammation to my kidney. she didn't want to have me go straight to a ct scan since it involves radiation, but with the ultrasound results she thought it best to confirm with a ct scan. so i went back to radiology, where they were just as nice the second time, and did the procedure quickly.

back at the clinic again, and dr. chun confirmed the kidney stone, showing me the imaging of one in my kidney (wasn't causing the pain) and one in my ureter (that was the culprit). it wasn't large enough to require surgery so she prescribed a medication to help me pass that sucker and i could go home. all in all it took about three hours, but the pain had eased and i was so relieved,  i could be patient with all the tests. 

everyone at both clinics were so helpful and friendly, from the receptionists to the nurses to dr. chun. it was a fairly slow saturday so maybe that made for a better experience since no one was rushed dealing with a ton of patients, but i appreciated the warmth and care i received today. it made a very uncomfortable experience much easier to bear.

careful of this place. they cancel appointments without telling you. when you ask the supervisor why said she's not familiar with mychart. really?! my appointment was on mychart a couple of weeks ago. where did it go? someone cancelled it and it wasn't me. 

it's weird when you leave your last appointment with an appointment card of an appointment and somehow you find out that the appointment was cancelled by me before my last visit when i requested an earlier appointment. well why did the receptionist and the md himself say i already had a follow-up appointment scheduled in four months (the original appt).

even despite that it's the  staff's incompetence, they blame the patient instead and say the md (who's double-booked and covering for another provider on medical leave) who is doing me a favor by offering me appointments at times that don't work in my schedule. i purposely schedule my md appointments on the same day so i don't need to keep on taking vacation leave. so i had scheduled other md appointments purposely on the same day. i can't reschedule these appointment either as it is still with a specialist too. 

then i get the guilt trip that i should make the appointment time they gave me because they are accommodating me on the day i was supposed to have my original appointment...their mistake. if i don't take the appointment there is no such thing as a wait-list because i am already being accommodated so my next appointment which was supposed to be next week is now pushed back another six weeks. apparently my other doctors don't matter because they are doing me a favor by giving me an appointment. 

some people need to learn proper etiquette and customer service skills, especially the so-called supervisor tracy. never do you blame the patient for a mistake made by your staff...

the operator nikki was so helpful in helping me schedule an appt. for the soonest available pcp. i first called to originally schedule with dr. zachariah but due to his new patient appt being on a day i couldn't do she helped me by looking through a lot of the int med doctors schedules to see what she could get us sooner and low and behold she found an appt for dr. picket (don't know if i pronounced that correctly). for next week monday the 23rd. so thanks soo so much nikki (strath pbx operator)

just had a left hip replacement performed by dr maeda and his team. it went very well, was on time, and the post-op team were incredible. nurse dandy made sure i was comfortable while i was waiting for my overnight room, which was available almost immediately. tasha, jp and aileen, the nurses helping me recover after surgery were awesome. they made me feel at home and comfortable while staying overnight. mahalo straub, your service is outstanding!

lazy and uncaring staff. my friend obviously had something wrong with him. he lost partial vision all of a sudden. the er checked him out briefly, no tests, said make an appointment with a neurologist. well, he had a massive stroke (in addition to the one he must have had earlier that caused the partial vision loss) 4 weeks later, 3 days before his neurologist appointment, and he died. i hate straub. i will never go there or bring anyone there again.

this review is for the emergency room physician assistant.  she made rude unprofessional comments to me.  i refused a test and she forced me to take it and claimed that if she does it, i wont feel a thing...she lied.  if you can't feel empathy for patients that come in or listen to how they feel or respect their decisions on health care, why are you working in this field??  even the nurse made a comment to me about the physician assistant after she left the room.  the doctor and the nurse was very gentle and friendly.  i wouldn't recommend coming here.  i would recommend queens.

straub nurses can't get things done. i went to see a doctor. i told her that i need to change my address. i tried to update my address using mychart weeks ago and it didn't get changed. the nurse said "ok". then i went to get imaging. i called to have my imaging record. the lady tried to verify my address. it's wrong. we figured they still have my old address on file. she said i need to call admitting office to have my address changed. she tried to verify my pcp name, is wrong. so i called admitting office, the customer service representative, a lady who picked up the phone sounded irritated and was trying to rush me off the phone. she said "you just had an appointment today, the department nurse should have changed it." ok, i asked her can you change it for me? she said "ok". after i told her my new address, i then asked her to update my pcp name to this doctors name. she said "ok". weeks later i still didn't see my information get updated on mychart. now i have to sign up to paperless billing to make sure my bill don't get send to the old address. why it is so hard to get our record up to date?

if you want your loved one that cannot walk to lay on a pee soaked pad around 10:30 a.m., then this is the place for your loved one. shift changes should have already happened and morning checks for water, freshening up, breakfast and meds. better care at a veterinary clinic. i gave 1 star only because i had to give a rating to comment.

terrible place.  i went in with so much anxiety and couldn't fully control my body or emotions and all i hear in the background is them talking shit about me saying i'm a dumbass and other rude things. i was told i could put my clothes back on by one doctor after the ekg due to my anxiety getting worse with it off and another guy immediately said he didn't care how it made me feel i had to stay undressed. they seriously don't care about how your feeling. they get annoyed when patients come in and they openly talk and laugh at patients problems thinking no one is listening. if you don't like people. then don't work at a hospital where you have to help people get better.

went to the emergency room recently, the male nurse gary, couldn't have been more rude, distracted or just, well,,, who was my nurse? not that hospitals should be like fine dining, but the experience and communication was very lacking.  don't do tests on me and not tell me what your doing, and when i ask about it, do not give me any flip of your lip, gary, i am the patient. so yes reader, he was treating me like a piece of meat, not like a person. not my favorite experience.

don't get sick on the coast.  incompetence and you spend hours waiting and  the bedside manner of the doctors, nurses and support staff are severely lacking.  went to er with my wife.  they took an hour to see her and it wasn't a doctor then they put us back in waiting room,  and no communication from nurses or doctors on what's going on.....the medical community is getting paid far too much

the worst... nurses there are condescending and think they're better than others. not all nurses are bad but i don't recommend having a baby there. their moms program is ok but the nurses at the birthing center are so rude and just awful. the head nurse will ignore your concerns and will call dhs on you if you're a minority.  the worst nurses! exception of two or three... they made my first child experience incredibly difficult and made me cry.  i mean, i cry often but they made me depressed.

$12,047.26 bill for my husband's stress test!  they do not take cigna insurance and said nothing about that when my husband checked in with a cigna insurance card!  i think they should be obliged to disclose that to patients checking in with insurance that they do not accept!      cigna paid nothing, and it was not applied to my deductible or out-of-pocket.  since we had the procedure approved in advance, if we had gone elsewhere, it would have been a $40 co-pay.

i actually do not allow anyone to call an ambulance for me because i always get brought to landmark hospital. ok so needless to say i was dying and an ambulance was called and for the fifth time this year i was brought and admitted to landmark hospital. i was told i had inclusions blocking the circulation to foot and yes they focused on that and secondary my toe that turned black and gangrene. they discharged me and referred me back to my podiatrist that had initially referred to the hospital. i went home only top bre brought back with the usual double pnemonia i seem to catch from there 4 times already this year. this time the doctors decided to play with my pacemaker...at the time i haff no idea they w0llere doing it without the bio company that controls and tests it. it's called comprising the integrity of my pacemaker. thanks again landmark. nurses were wonderful. especially jenn and all the icu nurses.

i cannot say enough good things about this rehab hospital, they were just amazing. 

i was admitted here from the hospital to undergo physical therapy after a stroke left my right leg very weak and i had difficulty standing. jean the nurse who was there when i was admitted was so kind and understanding it truly made me feel better about being there. that said all of the nurses were amazing, very kind and knowledgeable; it was because of them my stay was so smooth. 

the program includes three hours of physical therapy per day which was intense but welcomed. the gym they have was huge and had everything from a car to all stations one would encounter outside the hospital. the therapists were all great, they would push you as far as you are willing but we're very sensitive to over exerting. 

probably less important the food was pretty good all things considered and the rooms were very nice. this is a top notch facility and one i wouldn't hesitate to recommend to anyone in need.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Desert Canyon

review: had my hernia repair surgery done at mercy hospital and i was impressed. professional and caring nurses, great surgeon and quick recovery. valet parking made it easy. everything seemed clean and organized.

i got really sick and had to be taken to mercy to get a couple blood transfusions the nurses are super nice the doctors were very understanding and everyone was very helpful in explaining things that i had questions about - the only big complaint i have is that the last time i was a there they lost my moms car keys the valet lost her keys he showed us a key ring with no car key and he said it was like that when he got them - needless to say my mom was pissed we hardly got any sleep so we both had boho for over 24 hours so all we wanted to do is go home and get some rest but we couldn't because he lots the keys so instead we had to sit and wait for my uncle to get home from work (he works in fredonia) so he could grab my moms extra key from my grandmas house (we live in north collins) and bring it all the way to mercy - it was honestly the worst 48 hours of my life - i haven't been back to mercy lately because i get iron infusions at a different place now - just watch out for the valet parking

let me start by saying this is the day after i was released from south bay hospital. i read all the positive and negative reviews so here goes my review; first er staff were great (go chad!!), as a female i had 2 male nurses who were highly professional. i was having chest pain and was admitted for observation. my room was ready rather quickly, i was totally impressed with the cleanliness of this hospital (kudos housekeeping!). everyone was pleasant and they responded quickly to my concerns/needs. i follow a keto diet and although the dietary didn't know what foods i could eat, they allowed me to pick off the menu (what hospital does that?!!). now to the actual medical care-dr. wise was thorough and she kept me informed as did the nursing staff on the floor (2nd floor). david my first day nurse (best!) and the nurse lead chonda (can't get over her attentiveness for running a whole floor!!!), trish (sorry if i mistake spelling) and amy both afternoon and night nurses were great as well! keira and michele (big shout out!!) available and responsible as med techs! the phlebotomy staff, ultrasound technician for my echogram (bettina i believe), xray staff (made me comfortable through providing that extra support), the personable transport staff, and thank you all for your care. although i may not have shown it, i was nervous and worried! i didn't know the hospital and am really happy and satisfied knowing that you exist! so, thank you all again for the exceptional care i was given!!

i have never been to a hospital where they let anyone wander in and not a single living soul asks where you are going or if you need help. hardly anyone is "working". they stare at you but the second you make eye contact, they look away and pretend they are on the phone. no one communicates with anyone. not a living soul at a front desk.

this hospital and the staff is super awesome!!!! the level of comfort and care that these healthcare professionals give is a1. i recommend this hospital. special thank u to dr. farivar and dr. berkeley for caring for my mom and the awesome cvicu nurses

b worst hospital ever terrible service they didn't give my sister the right treat she came here for coughing up blood but got an breathing treatment instead which had nothing to do with her purpose i am very disappointed and will not be returning to this hospital due to the service i have gotten ‼

this place is really bad, as everyone else has stated.  they kept me so drugged up that i have little recollection of being there.  they claimed i was an alcoholic and gave me detox drugs even though my bac was .00 and i hadn't touched a drink in over a month.  i told them not to give me detox drugs because i don't drink that much.  they did, and i hallucinated.

i have severe hypertension.  they gave me no bp meds.  my bp skyrocketed to the point that the pharmacist ran into my room in a panic, meds in hand.

my room was bad, but i felt horrible for the patients sleeping on the floor with only a blanket.

the attitude here is that patients are inmates and are the enemy.  jails are run like this, not a place that's supposed  to help people who need it.

geraldo rivera would have a field day here.  the state needs to check this place out and shut it down.

two days after i was finally unbaker acted, i flew out of florida to another state.  i would truly rather die than go back there.

horrible feel here. just came to visit my father who has dimentia. looks like he hasn't been given a bath or a shave in weeks. fruit flies all over room and visiting room temperature kept unreasonably cold for patients as well around food and coffee machines is disgusting. lobby dirty and staff not very warm at all. i'll be making formal complaint to state hotline and thank gos were transferring him monday to a wonderful facility in ny to live out his time with respect.  pathetic this place not held to minimum human standards.

horrible doctors, old and stuck in their ways. don't treat the patient just a diagnosis. i had a bad infection and dr was so conceited and rude, didn't hear my concerns. the hospital is nasty, old building and dirty. there is no cafeteria. your visitors have to leave hospital parking garage to get food, then just decide it's too much a hassle to re park.  i'll never come back to this hospital. do not recommend if you have infections

my mom was recently admitted to west oaks for almost a week, the front desk was pretty helpful answered all my questions about what was allowed in. the nurses were okay some were nice some seemed irritated when asked a question but i also only got to interact with 5 nurses in total. the unit my mom was being kept in felt bland and depressing but it is a mental health hospital so you can't really expect a luxury stay. just wish it was a more cheerful atmosphere. visiting my mom she never had any complaints, she said the food was fine and everyone was nice to her which was a plus. she said they also had groups i don't know if it's the same for children/teens but they kept a copy of their schedule on a whiteboard and from what i saw they were pretty occupied throughout the day. my only regret is not talking to her doctor or therapists. i'm only 22 so i didn't know what to do to help my mom, i thought that maybe getting to meet her doctor would shed some light on what i'm supposed to do, just wish they would've reached out and had family sessions with the doctor/therapist. i didn't find out i could talk to her doctor until the day before she was discharged. i did feel like they were quick to let her go though. 

would recommend scheduling a time to meet with them as soon as they're admitted.

i've seen the reviews for this place and i was very skeptical but most reviews were from patients and some just seemed extreme. if half the things these people were saying happened i'm almost 100% sure they'd have tons of lawsuits on them. 
the reviews about the food are irrational what else do you expect from a mental health facility? i'm sure their purpose is to make sure you're mentally stable not spoiled.
reviews about patients being abused? they have cameras everywhere if your child or loved one was hit or abused in any way it would be on camera. i do not know if there are cameras in the rooms but i'm sure there are.
lost items? i don't know if they did this a couple months ago but they make you write down everything you bring them and they keep record of it. they keep a slip and you keep a slip and it's all signed off by you and the front desk employee.

overall they did an okay job of making sure my mom was good to go home. if they would've consulted with me and informed me on what i'm supposed to do to help her i'm sure my mom wouldn't be going back to another mental health facility 4 days after being discharged.

by no means a bad place to send your loved one to just can't stress enough that if you could get a family session do it within a day or two of them being there. the doctor will tell you their progress and what their possible discharge day would be.

i spent 5hrs in the hall of the er after arriving by ambulance with a head injury & displaced spiral fracture of my arm. there were no beds available... so much for privacy & hippa. i laid there vomiting & in agonizing pain. i was bumped several times to the ct due to a stroke & gsw patient. i understood that. my c-spine was neither protected nor evaluated until near the end of my stay. when my arm was finally splinted 
for discharge, this was done in full view of the public while still wearing my partially cut off bloodied sweater & bra. i would have been embarrassed if i hadn't been in such pain. my traumatized knee was never evaluated except with a brief cursatory  exam over my jeans. 
i will add that the nurses were phenomenal given the conditions they have to work in. they were attentive, supportive and managed my pain with keeping frequent tabs on me. they offered apologies for the lack of privacy & for my suffering. applying the splint over my fracture was excruciating but done with as much gentleness as possible.
these are the hero's of the er. overworked, overwhelmed and no doubt unappreciated. this experience is a system failure. failure of proper funding for adequate space/beds & staff. these are the shades of socialized medicine  and your future too....think about that next time you vote to support your 1st responders, funding for your hospital, etc.

health grades
bryant toth md has helped jimmy, my baby brother, out so much. born with a cleft lip/palate, it was hard for my brother to be comfortable. feeding has its struggles. my family was constantly down. after a few surgeries by our amazing specialist, jimmy was back into a normal baby boy!

this review is not about the treatment, but about their arcane billing practices and lack of transparency. it's the typical scamerica hospital billing routine. one visit results in 4 bills. dr bill, radiologist bill, facility bill etc. there is no online billing where you can view all the charges and make sense of it. 

the particular frustration that prompted this review was i paid what i  was told was the full balance on 12/5, with the help of a cs rep. today i am receiving calls from the hospital that i need to call them right away for an overdue amount. 

i called and the rep who couldn't tell me anything other than i had an outstanding bill that was about to go delinquent.

i tried to address the issues with sutter twice, but their response was that they didn't know much about le or the le clinic or what the pts did, so there you go. i even asked if i could feel out a patient survey -- nope.

le pts are supposed to treat each patient as an individual. truly experienced and skilled pts know that the training they receive may need to be modified from one le patient to another. mine was incapable of adjusting her technique to meet the needs of my damaged body. she lacked the experience and was too inflexible to try anything else. although she had  been sent to the best le pt in town for additional training, this sutter le pt decided she knew more and refused to access this pt for help. this was a major mistake that meant my le was not improved under this sutter pt whatsoever. i ended up worse off. i'd like to hope that this pt would improve with time, but she'd have to adjust her attitude as part of that growth if she truly wants to meet the needs of her patients. le is a terrible health condition that drastically affects our quality of life. the last thing we need is a le pt that doesn't understand that the patient comes first, not their own ego.

the staff leaves a lot to be desired.  2 cna's in my wife's stepmom's room and just not very friendly at all.  and the cleaning after a patient was released in the same room was very shoddy.  i'm hoping i will never have to be placed here.

after going to first aid urgent care at 8.15am today, dr dautey looked at my husband and told us he needed to go to the er. i knew my husband would listen to the doctor. (i said he needed er last night, beside the point.)
off to verdugo hills er we go. parked right outside. we were in triage in 7 minutes of checking in, by 9.30am we were in a room. excellent care, lots of great drugs, plenty of attention given us, of course it's never fast enough when one is in pain. this er was busy. we appreciated the level of care given. 

thank you.

i was in the hospital in january with an emergency hip
replacement. i had an excellent experience on the 8 th floor during my 5 day stay . the staff was completely attentive at all times. i could not have been more impressed with this hospital staff. i highly recommend usc verdugo hospital. along with dr. stephan owens orthopedic physician. very best bedside manners as well as excellent doctor.

excellent service all the way around.  wife went for arthroscopic surgery on knee and it went smoothly.  nurse was attentive which is my #1 criterja.  prior to check out, they made sure she understood how to use crutches.  pleasant experience for an unpleasant experience.

i went to the er for severe pain. when i arrived i waited for 3 hours to see a doctor. when i left i got hit with a $6000 bill. when i look up fair market value for these services, they are around $1000. if you want to wait a long time, be overcharged. this is the hospital to go to. highly suggest avoiding it.

i'm providing an updated version of this review after my complaint was handled very well by the usc verdugo hills patient relations department.

after posting my initial review (which i wrote after several voice mails and calls to that department went unanswered), i received a call back from two different people, one person i'd been in touch with before and also the head of the department, who i'd left a message for. her name is angela. she was extremely kind, responsive and truly listened in a way that would have been great during my actual er visit. it sounded like angela really cares about the hospital and the people who work there, and felt bad that i didn't have a good experience at usc verdugo hills. she assured me that my complaints have been logged and shown to the new head of the er, and was able to amend a portion of my bill so i wasn't responsible for the full amount, both of which are very much appreciated.

even though my visit was bad and i'm still not sure if i would return to this hospital, i would encourage people who have a concern to contact the patient relations department. based on my experience, which is all i can speak to, they do listen and try to make things right. it's unfortunate that i had to deal with them in the first place, but as patients with complaints it's important that we advocate for ourselves so the hospital can hopefully learn from their mistakes. thanks angela!

my father in law had hip surgeryy  because he  broke his hip . he was transferred here  for recovery! worst ever! he git here sunday & today is  wednesday. he had to beg his nurses and drs for a shower. and he finally got one today! unfortunatkey the nurse at the time had a huge attitude.  his breakfast got cold because he had to shower! the air!!! ridiculous! he also  just now got an extra blanket..  he told the nurse he was cold . and the nurse replied "its not cold" like how u know??? these people need to be retrained on how to treat and talk to patients! especially the elderly!

i don't know of any other feeling that could match that which i felt when my doctor looked me in the eyes and said "you have cancer." my life quickly changed direction, to say the least - fortunately i was under the care of dr. rene sotelo, usc urology clinic, who was amazingly empathetic and calming as he explained the surgery procedure using robotics and reassuring me that i would be under his expert care - and i'm here to tell you, i was, he is amazing - i had what was referred to as "major surgery." my recovery has been very fast and little to no pain at all - i feel that dr sotelo saved my life. 

i also want to mention how professional, caring and very attentive everyone at the hospital was, in the entire process of my surgery, pre-surgery, day of the surgery and aftercare. 

in the hospital, recovering from the surgery - in walked catherine pradt and introduced herself as my "care coordinator." now i'm not a religious man, but i like to think of her as a gift from heaven. i was really taken care of - she completely took charge of my needs - presently in the hospital and my home health care needs. i didn't even know she had done that until i got home and received a call stating that a nurse will be arriving shortly to assess and assist me in my home and to make sure my medical needs were met. trust me, my family was very happy.

a few times some concerns came up regarding my recovery, and i would call or text catherine and she would respond straight away putting my fears to rest - she completely understood my recovery process and with clarity explaining and walking me through what my concerns were, establishing the appropriate next step in my "window of recovery." she was very calming and reassuring, so was the nurse, but it was catherine i relied on.  

i would recommend usc verdugo hills hospital, dr. sotelo and catherine to my family, friends and anyone who finds themselves in need of a hospital, expert doctor and a care coordinator.

my husband was scheduled for surgery at 12:30 pm and was told to arrive at 10:30 am.  after 5+ hours he was finally taken to surgery.  excuse for the delay was that one surgery went longer than anticipated and then instruments weren't ready for my husband's surgery.  omg doesn't this hospital have enough instruments?  can this be typical of a keck usc hospital?  i would never recommend this hospital to anyone.

we had an unfortunate incident that necessitated a visit just before  10 pm yesterday.  i was very surprised at how quickly they got us in - 10-15 minutes.  they triaged my husband and had him in a room in no time, receiving treatment.  they gave us medication to take home and we were on our way about an hour, hour and a half after arriving.  the doctor, nurse, insurance lady, er admitting lady, etc., were all super nice, helpful, and totally on their game.   the only thing that was really strange, that neither of  us has ever seen, is they made us pay our er copay right then and there.  i've never seen a hospital, with a well insured  patient, not just mail us a bill.  i mean, what would happen if i didn't have cash, credit cards or whatever, on me at that moment.   overall, it was a very positive experience.

this is without a doubt the best hospital i have ever been to. anytime i've come here the nurses and physicians have gone above and beyond in order to make sure that i'm okay and well taken care of. the compassion and empathy that they portray really shows no matter which provider it is. they even go out of their way to do things that aren't in their job descriptions such as offering snacks or drinks to make the patient more comfortable along with many other things. thank you for everything you guys do here when a person is feeling their lowest.

i fell when i tried to change the battery of my smoke detector. i'm 4'11". i landed on my left hip. i had hip surgery the next morning at huntington hospital. i was coming down with the flu at the same time so i was placed at verdugo hills hospital for rehabilitation post surgery because i needed to be in isolation to protect other patients. i am writing this to commend the dedication, the support, hard work and the love of the staff on the  8th floor. whenever i needed anything they were there for me. dr barry and dr ghandi answered my questions. the pts worked with me. and the nurses and cnas were so devoted to helping me feel  comfortable. and i needed help every couple hours. no one complained. and the place has the best fish tacos! i wish i had chosen to be a nurse. thank you verdugo hills. god bless you.

the emergency room seems very understaffed with doctors. it took over 4 hours for the doctor to finally come see us in our room and we were told there was only one doctor on staff in the er. i only gave this 3 stars because the staff are friendly.

on christmas afternoon my mother suddenly could not see out of one eye. after going to urgent care we were told to go to the er at usc verdugo hills hospital. the staff at verdugo was amazing especially dr tashman. urgent care scared my mother and told she might lose an eye which increased her blood pressure. after some examinations dr tashman assured us it did not appear as such but did suggest she see a specialist the next day for a follow-up. he called her insurance and gave the authorization for an emergency referral (she has hmo) and gave us his number in case there were any issues. due to the holidays she wasn't able to get seen until 2 days later but i as able to follow-up with dr tashman and make sure it was ok. he saved us a trip to usc county on xmas day and i was able to communicate with him until she was seen. even a couple days after he texted to see how she was doing. i was truly amazed on the level of service we received from dr tashman during the holidays. him and his staff work during holidays and the level of service was truly unexpected but truly appreciated. thank you dr. tashman and er staff!

this hospital is wonderful. i was worried with some of the comments but there is no need to be concerned.  the staff's number one goal is to make patients feel cared for and kept comfortable.  the nurses are top of the line and i have had several surgeries in several locations.  catherine, rowena, hazel and nazeli are the best.  they know their field and have great attitudes even when i was in pain and had discomfort from my surgery.  dr. nguyen and dr. eric are very skilled surgeons and excellent care givers.  the parking is free!  the food in the cafe is tasty.  if you have a choice of hospitals for urology surgery, go to verdugo hills usc hospital!

i just had my 5th surgery (3rd stay as inpatient) in four years at usc-vhh, and i can state unequivocally that this is an awesome facility.  it is well run from the moment my doctors' offices or i call to set up a procedure.  i am always treated with dignity, respect, caring and a sense that my well-being truly matters to them.  the facilities are impeccably clean, well staffed and my paperwork is always correct and timely done.  all staff, from intake clerk to surgical intake nurses to or nursing to recovery to floor nurses, therapists, cleaning crew, nutrition employees are unfailingly polite, competent and attentive. post-hospitalization care arranged by julie in ortho nursing is so well done - all i have to do is answer the phone!  billing is a breeze and handled well - my 6-day hospital stay ending 12/22/19 has already been billed and paid in full according to the contract between vhh and my insurance company.  i only have one criticism - which is that the onsite lab required for use by the patient 72 hours prior to surgery for cross-match does not have a contract with my insurer (2nd largest health insurer in usa), and although my deductible and out of pocket maximums have been met, i end up getting billed at a non-negotiated rate because i am required to use this lab.  this needs to be addressed by admin, please - completely unreasonable policy, in my opinion.  other than that one hiccup - everything was absolutely stellar.  michele m.

my review is based solely on the birthing center. i've been to the er dozens of times and it sucks- that's non surprise seeing all the reviews. but i want to review the birthing center.

worst er experience ever! do not let them fast track you in the er! this is a review of my er department experience. i had to be wheeled in with a wheelchair because i could not walk at all. i reported that i fell and had knee, back and hip pain. i feared i had broken something. i was in horrible pain and reported i was uncomfortable in a seated position. when the triage nurse said she was going to put me in "fast track", i thought that would be a good thing. it is not! turns out fast track is a minor emergency triage option. very appropriate for kids with ear infections, etc. but not for trauma!!! they wheeled me to a tiny hot waiting room where we waited for an hour and a half only to be directed to a room the size of a regular er room with 5 or 6 recliners separated by curtains. the room was tiny and also very hot. i told the nurse i could not sit in that chair, that i needed a bed. sitting in the wheelchair for as long as i had had caused my pain to increase a lot! they said they don't have a bed. sorry. i explained my pain and injury and they said that's all they have. so they put me in a torn up recliner(they were all torn up) that had a broken handle and didn't even recline. i was in tears by this point. the pa had another patient change seats with me because mine didn't recline. after a while of sitting in pain and crying the pa saw me, after she saw another kid with an ear infection. i happen to know every symptom and treatment for every other person in that room because, remember, only curtains separated the many chairs. another fun point, we got the chair directly beside a very dirty bathroom with no soap that apparently was the only one for the whole er department, because the traffic level was very high. my wife was constantly stepping out of the bathroom seekers way. imagine being examined by the pa while tons of little kids brushed past to get to the bathroom. of course they stopped and watched for a bit because they are kids and they don't understand how horribly inappropriate that is. the pa promised pain meds soon, but no one came. i was taken to the xray room with no pain meds and i cried and cried through the whole xray. my pain was at a 10 and i had to climb around on that hard cold xray table. well at least the table was cold after sitting in the 100 degree fast track waiting room and joke of an er room. they finally came with some meds. pills, no iv's here! no pillows for my knee to at least try to make me more comfortable. nothing. nothing but a bunch of kids with ear infections. 
we begged them to move us to a room. we asked 2 nurses and the pa and they all said, "i'll see what i can do". i bet you can guess what they did. nothing. there was a young man that also was in the fast track waiting room with us, and i saw the room across the hall from us empty and they put him in it because the recliners were all full. instead of moving me into the room and putting him in the recliner that he was apparently in line for too. are you kidding me!!?? 
look- i think that fast track deal has its place and is a good idea....for kids with ear infections!!!! not for a trauma patient in extreme pain. if i was mobile enough i would have left and gone somewhere else. but guess what? they took my wheelchair, so i couldn't go anywhere. not even to the bathroom. my wife had to help me hop to the bathroom when i couldn't wait any longer. i'll tell you this is the absolute worst er experience i have ever had in all of my 50 years. no bed, no iv, no pillow or blanket, no m.d. and no empathy either. unless you are bringing in a kid with an earache, do not let them put you in that "fast track" it is an absolute joke. in fairness, i had treatment at that er on a previous occasion and had a regular er room, and dr. jordan was wonderful. i was not so lucky this time. summary: i did not receive appropriate treatment for my specific need. i was ignored. the staff was rude.

***this is regarding the emergency room.***
from the beginning, the er doctors misevaluated my father's medical condition.  first doctor said, he had a small puka in his lung, that could be  why for his shortness of breath; it turned out to be a shadow that they mistaken it for on the x-ray.  second, another doctor or nurse said he might have an bleeding ulcer, cause blood was found in the stool; it turned out to be not as bad, just a tiny bit which could be residue from a recent bleeding ulcer.  third, another doctor said, he has a slight collasped lung, which could be the reason for shortness of breath.  all this caused a roller coaster of emotions for me because he was weak as it is. they said he was going to be moved upstairs in-house for few days, but we waited hours & hours, and still no move.  i finally asked the nurse, then got an overall negative answer that the er is so full & in-house there's no room, so he eventually was placed in an narrow hallway at the er for hours again.  he was supposed to be discharged at 3:30 pm. at the time it was around 11:15 am.

i hate saying that, but why all the medical reasoning and later re-track from it?!  in the end, he's the same as he came in.  it was a waste of time and money sending him there.

review:
this review is only for kaiser's mental health department, specifically dr. jessica bergstrom.

i have ptsd and was assigned to bergstrom because she is apparently a ptsd specialist. at my first appointment with her, she arrived 15 minutes late. therapy is only 50 minutes long, so i ended up having a very short 35 minute appointment due to her lack of professionalism and inability to arrive on time for scheduled appointments. any other doctor would understand that it was their fault that they were late and extend the appointment accordingly, but not bergstrom. she apparently doesn't understand accountability and responsibility.

the appointment itself wasn't great. she's a pretty cold and unfriendly person. she spent quite a bit of time complaining about how she doesn't like kaiser and she wanted to go on strike. i figured i would give her one more chance though, so i scheduled another appointment with her. again, she arrived late, only this time it was by 20 minutes. this time, she was completely offensive, texting someone on her phone and getting angry at me when i asked her to stop. she also seemed to have completely forgotten who i was and what my problems were; she gave me advice to "fix" my ptsd symptoms, even though the particular symptoms she was discussing weren't symptoms i had. when i tried to tell her that, she snapped at me, "do you even want to get better?!" then she ended the appointment. 10 minutes early. so this time, i ended up getting seen for 20 minutes.

i later called and requested a different therapist. i got told that my request would be sent to a manager and someone would call me back within 3 days. no one called. i called again and sent in a change of therapist request once more. again, same spiel but no call. i called again. no call back from the managers. instead, i get a call from bergstrom, asking me why i didn't want to see her anymore and what had she done wrong and can she schedule another appointment with me to find out why i'm switching? i was just completely horrified by how she was acting and also by kaiser, for letting her call me when the manager was supposed to. i can't believe how unprofessionally and immaturely this woman acts! and i can't believe that kaiser doesn't have the sense to let the managing therapist handle therapist switches so that patients can honestly explain what went wrong. the whole thing was a nightmare for me and ended up taking over a month to sort out, when it really only should have taken a few days. i really would not recommend jessica bergstrom to anyone who is looking for therapy at kaiser walnut creek. there are better options out there.

review: i went into the pharmacy this afternoon to pick up a couple of prescriptions that were called in earlier today. while there, i thought i might as well pick up two other prescriptions, which needed to be refilled. i asked the pharmacy tech to share with me my very small list of medications, as i couldn't remember the name of one of the prescriptions; yet he would not. instead, he asked me a series of questions: "who's the doctor? what's it for? is it (name of medicine)?," and i was forced to name my symptoms in public at the cashier ("it's for menopause.") after his failed attempts at determining the name of the medicine, he then referred me to the pharmacist who put me through the exact same routine. i asked the pharmacist for a list of my medications, and he wouldn't provide one either--written or orally. i was quite irritated at this point and told the pharmacist that the pharmacy tech asked me the very same questions. i said, "i feel like i'm being quizzed; i don't like that...i have a right to my healthcare information." however, he maintained the same stance as the tech, explaining that he couldn't give me a print out of my prescriptions because of hipaa (yet somehow it was okay to for me to share aloud my symptoms and diagnosis at the cashier?). i told him i am well aware of hipaa rules, as i'm a psychotherapist and deal with phi in my own job. after he finally called out the name of the medicine i couldn't remember, and i confirmed it, he agreed to fill the medication along with the others. by the way, i have gotten a list of meds before from cvs when i was not a kaiser member; it is not a hipaa violation. it's these kinds of experiences that make me consider changing my health insurance during my next enrollment period at work. kaiser continues to be a disappointment.

review:
my daughter was a patient on 6 south (surgical)  at oakwood/ beaumont hospital dearborn and i have never run into such a bunch of lazy, could care less nursing staff to the point of endangerment. as an rn myself i know my way around a hospital so i have a very good idea when something is very wrong  when i worked at oakwood back in the day we had double the amount of patients to take care of and we did this with efficiency, being well organized  helping each other, and taking great care of our patients. what i recently witnessed in the nursing care  at oakwood, dearborn, shocked me to my core ie; my daughter put the call light on because her iv bag ran dry and ²the ivac machine was  beeping, we waited and waited for someone to come but no one came, call light on again, no one showed up and 20 minutes pass, i glanced out in the hallway and their were 5 nursing personnel chit chatting and ignoring the call lights. i went up to a nurse aide and she blew me off. for instance with an iv going dry you only have so many minutes to get to the iv before a clot forms in the cannula and renders the iv site useless causing the patient more pain getting poked again for an iv site, there was blood backing up in the iv but no one came to check the beeping iv which is designed to be heard at the other end of the hall. these nurses have only 4  patients to take care of and they refuse to work as a team to help each other out with the attitude " it's not my patient"... this is dangerous, irresponsible, selfish thinking and will inevitably end up hurting a patient. on my way out i complained to the charge nurse mary who blew me off, there were 2 people sitting at the desk who could easily have answered the call light but chose to ignore it, which begs the question; if a patient is in imminent danger either from falling on the floor or develops an emergency of not feeling well and no one shows up to help!
this is a very scary place for a patient to be in and it shows the lack of commitment these nurses and aides have toward their patients which should be, "do no harm" by keeping them safe at all times instead of  an attitude "so what". i would give the level of care a big 0. horrible place!

it's my 1st 24 hours here and  physical therapist rebecca is head & shoulders above the rest.  she had me bending my knee three days after surgery and my first day here at rehab.  amazingly straight forward but kind, determined and sweet, focused and trust worthy. thank you! rn's &cna's should practice engagement with their patient, try actually looking at the patient and smiling. the room was clean coming in however there must be rules on who can pick up the trash on the floor etc.  because the same napkin is on the floor from yesterday moring. to wrap this up, each person should worked as a member of a good team, observe, analyze, be responsible and thorough .

2nd day besides the napkin still on the floor from yesterday, no housekeeping staff i guessed this morning would be the same lethargic staff as yesterday. no! wonderful abby/avelina showed up at 8:15am to provide me with pt and the first thing she did was 'pick up the trash on my floor" wow!! she even looked around for other debris and picked it up. wow! not only was she knowledgeable and attentive during our session and encouraged me to go further than i thought i could...she was real. thank you abby

a fabulous place! i loved the compassionate care that i received from everyone at this facility. a beautiful place to be in rehab. it's like a hotel.
the food was ok. not great but not horrible either. i would recommend this facility for anyone's rehabilitation needs. 10 out of 10!!!!

extremely rude and unintelligent parking attendants. explained to them that i was doing an uber drop off and helped a disabled person take their belongings to their room, they still charged me a parking fee.. even though i was there for about 10 minutes. i tried to slowly explain to them that i was simply helping someone get up to their room safely and didn't actually park my car, they looked at me with a blank stare and said i must pay the fee.

this is for the billing department not the hospital. i would give them 1 star but i dont want to be distrespectful to their hard working dedicated staff. the dr.s  and nurses are wonderful. the billing department sucks. after paying a bill over the phone, it went to collections, and started a huge marital fight. they have internal issues with their computer system that cause hiccups and malfunctions. even if you speak to a human and get a confirmation number: don't trust them with your credit history. their card reader has problems too. it even hiccupped when i paid my bill a second time. check your credit card statements after  your bill processes. i had received calls from their billing department after paying bills because they don't show up on everyone's system. then they would call for a bill that i never received in the mail. the women wouldn't identify themselves and requested my credit card. after speaking to their office manager, she assured me my account was in good standing. 
blood pressure alert! they want your visa statements to prove them wrong, not a fax loop from visa protecting your financial records.
speaking to the third party collections agency made me crack. they asked all kinds of personal questions you should never give over the phone to a stranger. they want everyone's birthdate and social security number, and they  write down everything you say  in an attempt to show that you are contradicting yourself. i finally told the man that we live in a democracy and people are innocent until proven guilty, and then i hung up on him. 
if swedish hires a third party to do their billing, they should rethink their business objective and re-evaluate this decision. 
will i go back to swedish? absolutely !
will i be more proactive with my bill? absolutley. 
and you should be too. i'm too old and grouchy to be lectured by some kid about my financial irresponsibility, who is young enough to be my child, and is probably still living at home with his mommy.
and guess what? it's still not over even though i called the collection agency and gave them proof of my payment. the card reader can still bounce and not reflect my payment again, and swedish billing only sends updates to their collection agency once a month. they can actually damage your credit history with this nonsense. why can't you call now, i asked swedish billing, and straighten this out? 
nope.. not done like that. they send a print out to the collection agency with a calmness and a smirk,  that a  teen uses on his mother when he reprimands her for talking too much because he's just tuned her out: like the old tv stations at 10 pm in the 60's. but because those old tv stations ended their broadcast with our nation's anthem; i always belt out my own version as well, to signify that we are truly done with this broadcast. it also pays to have had a mother who was an opera singer. oh for the love of pavarotti, i am enjoying this.
went to denver health for follow up because no follow up care was given after collapsing and being admitted

this hospital should give lessons on how ers and hospital care should be given! 

my son suffers from severe sciatic pain from being hit while riding his motorcycle last year. the weekend of january 17-1, he was in excruciating pain. on the 17th, i took him to littleton adventist hospital... what a joke. never going there again. they made him feel like he was a junkie, looking for pills.

the pain was still debilitating soon the morning of january 18th, i took him to a different er - same treatment. no pain help. just a lot of admonishing that taking prescription pain pills was tantamount to walking into a full blown addiction. seriously? they gave him nothing for his pain. 

on monday he saw his pain management dr. and was prescribed something for the pain. he couldn't walk, couldn't sit, couldn't lie down and by january 22nd, he was screaming in pain. i called an ambulance and said, "take him to swedish." 

the best decision ever. the staff was attentive. they cared that he was hurting. the came in often. tried different pain treatments and when one didn't work,  they tried another. he had a bad reaction to one medication, so they decided to admit him overnight. finally!! people who wanted to help! from the er doctors and nurses, to the hospital doctors and nurses, they listened to him. the morning after he was admitted, occupational and physical therapists came in to work with him. 

and the er doc finally gave him a medication that knocked the sciatic pain from an excruciating 11 to a manageable 4 or 5. he received an rx for more if needed, and never once made him feel bad for needing it. 

what a difference in the way he was treated here! 

this hospital, in my opinion, is the best in the denver area. they go out if their way to help. pain is a difficult condition to treat because of the potential for addiction, but with additional pain management, he won't need it for long. 

thank you, swedish hospital!

went to have my hysterectomy done and can not complaint. everyone, everyone at that facility  the amount of care, kindness, professionalism from everyone from the person richard who checked me in till the last nurse to wheeled me out sidney. i felt safe, loved, protected. awesome smart, professionals. thank you for treating me so well.

i forgot to add they violated hippa by giving out information over the phone to someone calling looking for me. i didn't authorize that and yess, i am still to this day appalled at this establishment. 


your name is ryan but also julie?!?!

shitty place. piss on the floors, nurses laughing that it still wasn't cleaned and had dried up on its own. another nurse, quinones, has a lot of negative things to say abt homeless people and i wrote a letter to the supervisor but nothing was done. shit smeared all over the toilet seat. terrible hygiene. they sent me home without one of my meds w a lil note telling my insurance doesn't cover that medication. i'm praying to god they don't charge me for that med they gave me while i was there. if they do i'm going to sue cus they shouldn't have given me a med my insurance didnt cover. 
shelby is the shittiest social worker. she didn't help me in the slightest. she told me for 26 days that she was looking into rehabs for me and the day of my discharge, she tells me my insurance isn't covering rehab. she had me stay more days, and on the 29th day they let me out and pulled that med shit. she also couldn't get me housing. she said she could only refer me to shelters. other patients had to refer me to places that i mentioned to her. i pretty much did her job. 
constantly understaffed. 
in the 29 days i was there, i saw three patients return to the facility so clearly they're not doing a good job.

groups are great. shout out to jackie.

visited my friend on the 2nd floor several times. place was clean, staff friendly and  helpful and food good. doctors listened and tried to help my friend and fallow up outpatient care was aranged for before release. we had experience with other hospital before and   this was by far a better facility for psychiatric  patients.

hospitals of all shapes and sizes are places of healing, rest, and recovery. it is thereby a gross oxymoron to call lakeview a hospital.

i realize that there are off days and that things happen. but to have the good care be the exception is a problem. now for story time. 

a family member of mine went in for emergency care and was admitted to this facility recently. tests were performed and a few good nurses gave care. them the fun began. my family member had limited use of the right side of their body and thereby unable to walk. needing a shower the aid just brought and dropped off a couple towels with hardly a word, afterward relating that because there was family present that they would assist. never assume in patient care! 

it came into question what insurance would cover and respect dropped. an ice queen of a case worker (really?!) left them in tears after delivering that they're insurance wouldn't cover rehab and that they were essentially screwed. no sympathy or alternatives given, just your screwed. they requested information be related to their pcp and this was completely disregarded. maybe you get better care if you pay cash up front. 

in the end we removed them from the facility (hospital in name only) with some practitioners saying please stay and others (like ice queen) saying don't let the door hit you where the lord split you.

had a knee replacement by whom i consider " the rockstar of implant". that would be dr. joshua hickman. highly advise. i had my knee done by a hack that retired. went to uofu nobody wanted to fix someone garbage. then i finally found dr. hickman. fixed it beautifully. unfortunately the place he originally planned wasn't in my insurance plan. so in order for it to be in my plan, it had to done at lakeview hospital. stayed one one day. with my insurance i paid 4000.00$, my insurance pays 90%. that means it cost 40,000.00$ for one day. nurses stop in maybe 2 times. didn't get any food. was able to retain a menu after i asked three times. pretty bad service for 40,000$

unless you just want to go to the er for fun and not real quality care, avoid this place. from the moment i walked in i was so disappointed. the triage nurse was short with me, sarcastic and flippant. my actual nurse, who i only saw once, didn't seem to communicate with the lpn in charge of my care. once the diagnosis, after no physical exam, was given, and i got teary eyes he says "oh come on, it could be so much worse". they are lazy, cold and just not invested in their work. i wouldn't recommend this er unless you're bleeding out your eyeballs and can't get anywhere else. even then...do better mountainstar.

i had heard nothing but good things about khh but was so disappointed when i recently had a heart cath and stent. grateful to the nurses and staff that  conducted themselves professionally. the bathroom that i shared with another woman wasn't very clean. i was given a package of wet wipes and told to clean myself following the procedure and 6 hours of bed rest. i've had 14 surgeries and this was my third heart cath. i've never  been asked to clean up all the  blood that remained  post surgery. i had one male nurse who talked at great length at nite about his ultra conservative political views...even after i suggested we i only talk about medical topics.

in respond to the review i left on behalf of dr. abdalla and mercy hospital.  dr. abdalla called me on the friday evening and i talked to his office on tuesday, had a appointment on thursday.  we (my husband and me) had a long visit in his office and he showed great concern about my health and gut.  i apricate all he did for the appointment and for me, we (dr. and i) have a game plan and i am looking forward to long relationship with him.  he has in my opinion turned out to be a really good dr.  
thank you

went in for three staples, left with twenty thousand dollar bill. i would have rather just died.

i'm pretty pleased with the 7th floor h of the building. i never realized how nice this hospital was. the emergency room is so terribly kept. you would think the whole hospital is like that.

bad service at 4floor 4c to 4 e, they don't know how to manage the time my wife have an appointment at 2:20 pm and it's 4:58pm still we are waiting to be served, someone has to solve this problem for the appointment every time we come here they made us to wait for 2 or 3 hour with appointment.they supposed give the right time appointment.

came in for a 2nd degree burn to my hand, waited in the er for 5+ hours before i was actually seated in a room. the lady that came in to make sure i was charged for this visit came in extremely fast, and approximately 1 hour later, finally an rn who came in did not introduce herself, showed no concern, did not perform the necessary focused assessment to my hand, rather she just asked my pain level & walked away. 1.5 hours into waiting in a shared room, no one has checked in & no vital signs of any kind were taken. the basic first aid was not even performed to my hand as i sat in the room watching my hand blister up. the lack of care provided shows the incompetency of the nurses & doctors at this hospital. it's sad to see the level of care being provided to patients at this point.

p.s. please be careful of the beds, i witnessed an er tech clear out a bed with no gloves, did not disinfect the bed with any cleaner, & overheard the nurses and techs speak loudly about another patient at the nurses station. so ridiculous the amount of infection control (or lack thereof) & hipaa violations just in one er visit. 

if you dont want to wait 5+ hours to be seen this is not the place for you.
