the only person manning the front desk was the security guard. so if you feel over dead or wanted to be discharged from the waiting room after five hours of waiting in pain good luck. two security guards. you have to go through a metal detector. more security than medical staff. alta bates corporate administration should be ashamed of the poor dismal quality they offer and have the nerve to charge people. berkeley does not have an a good neighborhood er. we pay so many taxes, high property costs and medical insurance costs to be ripped off and not given proper medical care. the administration does not care because this hospital is slated for closure. they are just staying afloat. don't go there. don't give them your hard earned money. if you don't have medi-cal and you don't have kiaser you are fucked in the berkeley, el cerrito and richmond area. maybe drive to walnut creek to john muir.

it made me really sad what terrible care this place gives working in health care myself. i can't believe i had to walk around and beg for an ice pack, the only really kind person was the ct technician and the nurse who finally cleaned my cuts after 4 hours of being sent in and out of rooms. i should've been more insistent on going home since i'm confident i could've taken better care of myself.

on my primary doc's advice, i went to this er. i got there are 11:30 a.m.
the staff all seems to think they are doing patients favors. and the staff is either vacuously blank or openly uncaring. i asked for a blanket and got a flannel sheet that did not warm me up; the nurse actually said "this place saves lives, blankets aren't important' so i asked her how much a patient paid to spend time in the hospital's bed without blankets and i asked her when did comforting a sick patient stop being part of health care?  when i asked for a sliding board so i could get out of my wheelchair and onto one of their beds, the same nurse told me her hospital didn't have sliding boards because they are out dated. then another nurse, a male one, came in with a sliding board that the hospital owns. when i asked for help putting my pants back on (i am paralyzed from waist down and cannot put on or take off pants), same nurse asked me "who usually does this?" 

when i became upset over multiple degradations and, good heavens, when i raised my voice in the room with a closed door and no call button, they threatened to label me as a mental case -- i swear this is true. they said if i didn't stop raising my voice (i only raised my voice to get help because the door was closed and i had no way to communicate) they would assign a security guard to me full time to keep an eye on me!

i finally exclaimed, too loudly for my keepers, that a hospital er is not a prison and just because i am crippled doesn't mean they have a right to do whatever they want (such as they insisted on keeping my door closed when i asked to have it open. . . all kinds of emotional stress could be related to a patient preferring an open door but, hey, alta bates berkeley is not about caring for people, just keeping their costs down -- they stop using blankets because they are not, as a real-life manager in sutter system said, 'cost effective'.  how much does this horror show charge for someone to be in that bed?  managerial cost-reductions are, it seems, literally costing trapped patients decent care.

i will die in my apartment before i ever go to this er again.

my mom came in by ambulance and as we are sitting here and i am writing this review, it has been 7 hours, tests done , results confirmed by the er doc and told we would be placed in a room in a few minutes. we have been waiting for transport from er to room now for 1.5 hours and she has has nothing to eat and she is a diabetic. some of the staff a very nice and caring, however i found that the people( ward clerks or whatever )sit at the nurses station , do just that. they just sit there. total waste of space. those are the positions that need to be eliminated, not people that really work or want to do a job.

i hate coming here. it's huge and there is terrible signage so i always get lost. anyway, they make you call kn advance of your appointment to pre register, i'm not sure what that does exactly as when you get there you then have to go to... you guessed it, registration. you sign your life away, no option to opt out of anything or they just won't treat you. then, once you hand in their fancy ipad and if you're lucky, you'll wait only 20 min for them to "activate" your account. if they have other people and are busy, your wait will be much longer. don't worry though, that was only the first waiting room. then you go to wherever you need to go, early morning admissions, imaging, whatever, and wait some more. i have been here three times, i will say imaging didn't take too long but the other times the wait was intense. 

basically, the docs and people seem good but the waits are crazy, the paperwork is ridiculous, and the bureaucracy of it all is nuts. if you can go elsewhere, do yourself a favor and do so!

it's a mixed bag here. i would generally say the service is either fine, or good -it's significantly better than the boston bi. you will generally get served somewhat quickly, usually without a long wait. if you show up early, it can actually speed up the service. so, if you are busy and just want to leave asap it's on  the quicker end of service. i wouldn't say it was fast tho'. it's just more timely, and the pace has less waiting, boredom , and time wasting. 

i wouldn't say anyone working there was rude or impolite. they check all the boxes as far as being polite to your face, speaking all of the expected choice phrases in order to not be considered rude. but, it feels very mechanical, coached, plastic, fake, hallow, superficial, and empty. they're not rude per se, and they  do and say all of the "correct" or "pc" things, so you can't accuse them of doing a bad  job. but, so much of it lacks warmth, bedside manner, and you don't actually feel cared about. it just isn't there. you can see the smiles, and hear the "customer service" tone of voice. but, it feels more like a drive through service at jiffy lube, and you are the car. you don't feel like a human person, but a thing that needs a checklist of things to be performed and spoken to you, then get out, but "have a nice day". 

i wouldn't say any of the personnel working there were bad or negligent people. but, they definitely do not have any wish to connect with anyone on an actual personal level. they only want it to seem this way on the surface. i noticed that if they were speaking in a manner that was meant to simulate trust building or relationship relatability, if you actually became candid and treated them as a person, and not submissive to dominant power dynamic of professional above the patient, they would often change the subject, give you a very extra big smile, and try to leave and send you on your way immediately, rather than actually forming a bond of personable trust. 

if you are having surgery, like i did here,  remember to address your fears if u have a special circumstance like if most people have a pair of 2 organs but you only have 1, and they removing giant growths from it, but they've already told you that if it bleeds, they must remove it. because they can totally forget. in my case i could've become castrated if they removed my ovary, because i only had 1 left. then i would've been thrust into menopause and my life would've shortened abruptly and thrust into rapid aging. 

this was very concerning  to me. i was having anxiety over this  for months. i also had other complications due to this issue, and the causes were unknown until  after the surgery. 

everything was a success. i'm fine now. 

but, it bothers me a lot that they felt very cold about this. i felt like just another machine on the assembly line, and not a person. the personal discussions i had with the professionals felt more like a puppet show of telling me things i was supposed to hear, to dupe me to believe everything was fine at the push of a button, or just speak  some specific words and everything was good,, then send me on my way like a drive through. 

but, since my circumstances were unique and complex, it shattered the customer service illusion that they cared, and it wasn't real trust or care. it was people going through the hum drum daily life of a career, and the semblance of a number of things on a resumé. 

it's bothered me a number of times. and i assumed i was  just picky, or overly sensitive, or worried i did something wrong. but, after having spoken with a recent recent professional that spoke too me as a person on the phone, actually cared about me, didn't rush me to hang up or leave, and didn't speak to me with cookie-cutter phrases from a scripted coached list of things to say, or boxes to check  off, i realized that the person i was talking to was a real person whom actually cared about the entire process, the care, the person. and they didn't just put all the burden on me, or pass the buck while "have a nice day"-ing me. 
so, i felt it validated my feelings of how i felt about this place. 

it has just been a long time since i'd experienced people being authentic, natural, and caring. i can feel what people feel. it's called empathy, and it's something the brain does. but when people are saying all the right things on a checklist customer service style and fakely smiling at me, it puts me off.  because i can't feel anything.... but i can feel the: 
oh no! she's trying to get to know me, bond with me, and relate! get out! send her on her way! smile and nod, and get out! 

it's not me being overly sensitive or picky, it's that my sensitivity of my empathy in my brain is functioning fine, and i'm actually picking up the mixed messages. hence my mixed feelings. 

i hope this information is at least useful and constructive.

just gave birth to my first baby 2 and a half weeks ago here. as a patient of dr. arora, i was scheduled for an induction and checked in bright and early. after being helped at the front desk with paperwork, i was directed to the labor and delivery department. once there, they got me all checked in and started me on fluids. not only did my nurse check on me, but i also had a few other people introduce themselves. i was impressed because one of the technicians heard it was my first child, and she took the time to walk me through what to expect for my induction there- i was incredibly grateful! 

throughout the remainder of my waiting time, the nurses were very attentive, ensured i was staying hydrated, and that baby and i were doing well. i could tell my daytime nurse was probably newer as she seemed a little timid and struggled to put my iv in, but the charge nurse was fantastic. amanda completely made it a 5 star experience for me. she was so personable, ready to answer my questions, gave me a laugh when i needed one, a shoulder to cry on when i needed that as well, and guided me with confidence through my choices.

the only negative experience i had was with the anesthesiologist who gave me my epidural. while i had never had one before, i had a feeling something was wrong when i felt her digging around in my back. my suspicions were confirmed when she told me, "this is a little tricky because of your scoliosis." i've never had scoliosis before. needless to say, the epidural didn't work, and i ended up having to take another medication for pain management because she wasn't able to come back to redo the epidural in a reasonable amount of time. thankfully, she eventually did come back about 2 hours later (in that time i went from 4cm dilated to 8cm), and then magically she got the epidural in quickly and with ease that time. so at least it worked eventually. 

once my little one was out, all of the nurses handled her and i with the best of care. i felt like a fish out of water as a first timer, but everyone was so patient with me and guided me through my recovery. i had multiple nurses help me with breastfeeding (little one didn't want to latch), and even got a helpful visit from their lactation consultant (who was so pleasant)! 

overall, while i have heard some stories about this hospital, i must admit i had the best experience there.

review:
i had my baby here 3 months ago.. i chose this hospital because i heard they are one of the best hospital for l&d around the area. when i went to the hospital because i was bleeding at 39 weeks they admitted me right away because i was already 5cm dilated. the l&d staff was very helpful. since this was my first pregnancy i didnt really know what to expect, but the nurses in l&d department were very attentive and very good at explaining things to me. my labor was for 18 hours. i was very exhausted and was very sleepy. when i was transferred to postpartum i thought it was very crowded. i had to share a room with another mother. i thought it was ok at first but comes night time, it was very stressful because when my baby is sleeping the other baby was crying and my baby wakes up. it was not a good set up especially for post partum because you will never get enough rest. my first nurse (her name is rowena and she is a filipina nurse) was really rude. she did not explain how the process works for cleaning after pregnancy. she did not even bother checking up on me. so i was just on my bed the whole day and had no idea what to do. i had a catheter on because of my 3rd degree laceration and when she pulled the catheter out she just pulled it right away without even telling me what to do after. then here comes the night shift nurse(her name is elaine) she asked me if i already changed my pads and if i am still bleeding heavily. i told her i dont know where i can change the pads and where can i get the pads. she was shocked that i havent changed my pads since morning that it might cause some infections. i told her that nobody told me anything and asked if the morning nurse didnt explain it to me
 i told her she didnt even bother checking on me and didnt really talk to me at all ( i was crying when i was telling her that..cause i felt neglected). she asked me to go with her in the bathroom and explain everything to me. she was one of the best nurse in that department. i asked her if she can ask her supervisor to check on the schedule the next day to make sure that i will not have that same nurse. they were very kind to change their schedule for me. 

the whole experience was good, but that one nurse reslly ruined everything for me. i hope nobody gets treated again the way that nurse (rowena) treated me.

if ever i get pregnant again. i will never go back here since it was really nightmare especially during my postpartum recovery.

we got referred here by my sons doctor. we were sent to the er and we were quickly in, my son had severe myositis due to a viral infection and was not able to walk. they brought a volunteer to us with a wheelchair and we were in a room within the hour with a bed for my son after them checking his vitals and symptoms in one of the triages. all the nurses were nice and extremely helpful. we stayed here 3 nights after also testing positive for coronavirus and other complications. they have someone bring the kids a tablet or bubbles to distract them while they get their blood drawn. 
dr. cooray was our doctor and he helped answer all my questions and concerns. the rns and staff was extremely attentive and they even brought my son toys, crayons and coloring worksheets and a tablet. the tv had plenty of kid movies and kept my little one entertained but he liked to watch netflix on the tablet instead. they brought a physical therapist for two days that we were there. they even had a playroom for the kids but unfortunately my son was quarantined due to his virus. they made sure we were well taken care off. today is week since we were discharged and i'm so happy to see my babyboy walking and jumping again! thank you millers children's hospital!

i did wish the surgeon had talked to me after my surgery. he talked to my husband, but i didn't get to see him or ask any questions once it was over.
the nurse i had at check out was...a bit incompetent. i loved literally everyone else i interacted with, at least a dozen people in the two hospitals and the 20 hours i spent there. 
but, my evening nurse was a mess. she didn't know how to use the equipment that gave me my medication. she was tapping all over the machine and eventually called in another nurse for help. together they still couldn't figure out how to get both bags going at once, so i only got the antibiotics, not the saline as well before checking out. she let a ton of air into the line, and told my husband it didn't matter, even though alicia had made sure to clear the line of any bubbles. she didn't know how to turn off the beeping, she didn't seem to know how to do anything. as we were checking out she didn't have any of the discharge care instructions printed. we asked for them, she couldn't figure out how to print them out, so eventually she just wrote a bunch of notes. it was all important stuff, like how much i am allowed to lift and how long before i can get into water! she would have just sent us home without it if we hadn't noticed it was missing and insisted on getting it. it was just sad. the rest of the visit was great, but she was the last person we interacted with and it was just frustrating.

took my mom here a month ahí because she had chest pain. she was left overnight in observation. waiting times for everything was excessive. her dinner never arrived so i had to buy it from the cafeteria. there were only 2 nurses to look after 5+ patients, these women are stretched too thin.

i went in for pre-op, was seen by initial associate and she said some someone would be with me shortly. i waited 45 minutes more, i peeped out the window heard assistance laughing, i walked over to the break room, and asked if i was done? the young gentleman came and said let me check yes you're done. i said did you forget me? he didn't say anything, but it was obvious he did. no apology nothing. i had to ask which way was the exit. 
disappointed.

leaving 1 star because i can't leave 0. 

i've been incorrectly billed 5 times in amounts 3-times higher than my payment arrangement. they say they cannot issue a refund as long as i have a balance on the account even though i've continued to make manual payments as well. 

this is the worst customer service i've ever experienced and it's just shady business practices.

i suggest looking into other healthcare providers in the austin area.

i visited the maternal fetal medicine clinic and was disturbed by the uncleanliness and overcrowding in the waiting room. chairs needed to be wiped down, there was a sick patient wearing a mask but was accompanied by three children and another adult. the waiting room is very small. the sick patient was not taken to another area. people were giving up seats to other arriving patients or waiting outside the clinic in the hall. also, several patients were taken  ahead of me even though they arrived very late for their appointments. we waited for nearly an hour to be called to the back. very unorganized and poorly managed. i was happy with the demeanor of the ultrasound tech who took care of us and the two minutes we spent with the doctor, she seemed nice.  the room we were taken to have the ultrasound was crammed with three chairs between the wall and patient bed. a third person definitely wouldn't be able to actually sit in the chair provided.
what's worse i woke up the following morning to a sore throat which progressed over the next couple of days into nasal congestion and a nasty cough that keeps me up at night.

if i could give the er at seton medical center a minus 1,000 review, i would.  i am celebrating 5 years of life after they almost killed me with a misdiagnosis of a ruptured appendix and sent me back to my hotel telling me that i had food poisoning.  after being in agony for 3 more days at my hotel, i went to the er at st. davids, was properly diagnosed, and was told that i could have died.  as a result of seton's gross incompetence, i developed massive infections, required major surgery, and spent an agonizing 3 weeks as an in-patient at st. davids. thank you seton medical er for costing me tens of thousands of dollars in medical bills after insurance, causing me a year of agonizing recovery which prevented me from working (losing a year of income), and leaving me with a life-changing chronic bowel condition that will never go away.  your incompetent staff almost killed me. your er should be shut down.

had surgery here because they were in network with my health insurance. it was the worst experience from start to finish. i was sedated for an hour and a half of additional time because some of their equipment broke during surgery/ they didn't have the proper tools the dr needed. due to the late finish i was admitted overnight ( was suppose to be out patient) where the bad experience continued. the staff didn't seem to know what they were doing and weren't helpful. they didn't give me food with meds that indicated "must be taken with food" so i became sick to my stomach. this was only some of what went on while i was there, but i will spare you all the details. it was a battle to get out of there even after my surgeon released me. this process took it took several more hours for no reason and resulted with me insisting to leave immediately. my recovery would have been much better if i simply just went home. i will never return to any seton facility again

wonderful hospital. came alone for surgery to treat my appendicitis which was a little nerve wracking since this was my first major operation ever. however, all the nurses and doctors were extremely friendly and welcoming. they quickly put my mind at ease, patiently answering all of my questions. my surgery was scheduled for noon but they were able to squeeze me in an hour early which meant i got to leave the hospital earlier than expected later that afternoon. overall, excellent quality of care.
fac_name: The Hospital At Westlake Medical Center

review: best hospital i have been in. everyone in this facility is efficient and friendly. they are so caring.  i will tell all my friends about this great hospital.
fac_name: The Hospital At Westlake Medical Center

review: going back in for my 4th spinal surgery tomorrow morning. the staff was wonderful and friendly and my neurosurgeon is right next door.  when my recovery at home gets painful and i'm hopeless, they always take my calls and give me the best advice possible. even if that advise takes me to a different facility.

they really are the worst. we had our baby there and they find any way to make you pay. our baby had minor jaundice. they had us rent a bilirubin bed and he was fine according to the labs after three days. we wanted to return it to avoid extra fees. the dr said it's not a big deal, just keep it over the weekend and return it then. now, six months later (!!) we are receiving bills for those extra days that we did not want or need. several hundred dollars. will have next baby delivered at timp.
incompetent and unprofessional staff. prescribed wrong medication after wanting nothing to do with the situation. no full exam. discriminatory behavior.

i would give zero stars if possible.  my son was in an accident and taken to intermountain medical center by ambulance.  he was complaining about his back and about his elbow, which was covered in blood, and he couldn't move it.  they said he did not need an x ray on his arm, and irrigated the wound, stitched him up, and sent him home.  once home, he was still in excruciating pain.  he went for an x-ray, and an mri and has two broken bones, torn ligaments, shifted cartilage, and received a lovely gift from this place as there was a piece of metal that fell into the wound when they cleaned him up, and stitched inside for safe keeping. for a level 1 trauma center, i am so shocked at the poor quality of care received.

i came this hospital for er on thus night!
all er stuff are so nice and very friendly ,unfortunately i had to have surgery and stayed 6 days

at hospital room, all nurses are so nice and very knowledgeable,
they are so much professional
especially the nurse  ms.navdeep muha,
she is the best nurse ii have ever see
every time i have a problem,she figure out and fix right away
also other nurse yolanda,she is really good take care of me,too 

and of course dr.chan,he is a great doctor and best surgeon 

i'm so happy i choose o'conners hospital,
if you have any problem,you need to come down to see them!

thank you for great service

oh my god, out of all the staff we've come across during my dying grandpa's stay here, there were only like 3 that were compassionate and actually doing their job right. one the worst doctors was dr. saha who was very cold hearted and rude. and there were 2 nurses whose names i didn't get but they would push her way through between my family members, not even acknowledging our presence as we just witnessed my grandpa die! the nerve of those b's! this low review is for the 3 of them. the rest of the staff provided 5 star care.

i had given birth to my daughter here via c-section in april of last year. i had the best staff/nurses care for me. many of them were traveling nurses though. they were attentive and made sure i was comfortable during my labor despite being in pain from contractions. also, at the time, they were transitioning into santa clara valley medical system. so, timing worked out perfectly for me because i had medi-cal at the time and i did not want to give birth to my daughter at valley medical hospital. yes, everything seemed out of date, but the hospitality my bf and i received in labor & delivery was amazing. i enjoyed my 5 day stay because it wasn't crowded or busy in comparison to kaiser's labor & delivery. idk how things will be here in the future due to their transition, but i would deliver my next baby here again.

i gave birth to my son here in 2013. all my needs were taken care of and i always felt like i was in good hands. my son was a healthy 22in 8lb baby and i couldn't be more grateful to this hospital for delivering him

even a star is a waste for this facility called hospital. 
they do what they do for themselves as a job. doctors, rns, therapists, and clinical staffs are all useless and helpless. please be a hospital for the patients not for yourselves or the bill. we are not the figures that you tests or source of your financial aids.

don't waste on your time and budget for posting those replies. 

do one round of visiting current patients will do a lot of those discussions that you want to do. if you really want to hear. don't pretend this facility is care for the people.

i had great experience delivering my baby here.  all the staff were nice and friendly.  most importantly they were helpful and attentive.  i wanted to thank hawa and huong for an outstanding job in taking care of me during my 5 days stay.  i have nothing bad to say about the staff other than receiving excellent service.

place is horrible. only guy actually helped me with advice that i was seeking for. i don't have any insurance or medical but simply for advise and no one helped me but one guy at the desk. i was ask for personal information & no treatment of any sort was occurred whatsoever for my situation, but kudos to him. this hospital is just sad, even bascom does a better job.

if i could give zero stars i would yesterday i took my daughter to the nearest hospital which was o'conner for an open head wound and when i got there the emergency room was empty no people what so ever they check her vitals weight they send us back out to wait again to get called while my daughters head is bleeding my 2 year old she was falling asleep they said it was fine will after an hour waiting the room was already full of patients they were getting seen before us another hour passed my daughter kept bleeding so we kept asking what's taking so long and they told " we take in people in fashionable order" what does that even well we ended up just leaving because they didnt seem to care we went regional medical hospital where the room was beyond packed no seats to sit but we got seen within 20 min i advise you not to take your child to o'conner hospital please if its urgent go somewhere else there staff was betond rude and careless

20 year-old student with asthma, severe chest pain and difficulty breathing made to wait in waiting room for three hours and told the earliest she would be seen would be three more hours. forced to seek treatment elsewhere at 4am. sad state of affairs when this is the medical care in this country. good luck if you have to go to this hospital.

i got admitted after been in the er for like two hours. in the time i spend in the er i got x-rays from my lungs an electrocardiogram to check my heart they took several samples of my blood also i was send to have an ultrasound done for both of my legs to check for blood clot. i really want to thank every single person in the er because they were all real nice patient and caring with me. once i got a room upstairs my whole experience during the two days i stayed was awesome no complaints all the nurses i saw were super nice and helpful. the food they provided me was unbelievable good the people from the kitchen also very nice everyone i talked to. overall the only complain i have has nothing to do with the hospital but with the roommate i got. omg i mean she was 93 years old and basically all she wanted and all she was there for was pain killers lol and she wasnt shy about it i had to put up with several tantrums she had screams whining arguments etc. at the same time it kept me entertained so there's that. back to the main reason i'm here all i can say it's that  o'connor hospital rocks and my whole experience there was awesome. i want to say thank you every single one there. next time i'm sick hopefully not soon i won't hesitate going back there again. i also have recommended to my whole family and friends to give it a try. thanks again you guys are all super stars. ‍‍
i came here to visit a friend in hospice.  i was so impressed with this hospital i moved from southern california to work here.

my grandmother spent 11/28-11/29 at o'connor hospital and what a disappointment it was. besides the obvious of the hospital being old and dirty the care she received from the nursing staff was not a positive experience. the nurses that admitted her to the 4th floor were good that night, as she was being wheeled into her room from the er the smell of marijuana smacked me across the face from before the time she even entered her room. (it smelled like her roommates were wiz khalifa and snoop dogg) the roommate had so many visitors they were sitting on the floor, took the chairs from our side, and were using the restrooms constantly that is intended for the patients use only. those evening nurses did eventually move my grandmother to another room after we expressed our concerns. the rest of the nurses seemed to be disinterested in patient care and more robotic focused on the computer more than the patient. thankfully my grandmother was discharged the following day and when she asked the nurse for her discharge paperwork the nurse responded coldly, "i will get to it later. there are sicker patients that i am taking care of." unfortunately, this is the hospital that my grandmother comes to as all her doctors are from och, but i pray that she will not have to have another hospital stay here again. there were many other issues that came up in her overnight stay, i would hope that even though o'connor is now a county hospital it would retain some of the compassion and patient-centered care that it had in the past.

had a really scary experience with an inattentive nurse named dominique on the med surg floor. on tuesday february 11th around shift change at 7pm, i was in room 641 recovering from an appendectomy procedure. i was in the restroom when my incision site began bleeding in excess. i hit the call light and sat for ten minutes waiting for my night nurse to come into the room, as my day nurse bryan had been dealing with a critical situation in another room. i was bleeding all over my gown and onto the floor, and my mother in law went into the hall to find my nurse, dominique. dominique told my mother in law that she hadn't read my chart yet and that i would have to wait. my mother in law was able to track down bryan, my day nurse, and he went into action right away. two surgical residents were in my room and they began working to stop the bleeding. they bandaged me up, and the residents said they would be back to check on me within two hours. during no time did dominique check on me or take my vitals signs. my husband happens to be a nurse, and because he was so worried for my well being he took my vitals every 15 minutes to make sure i was stable. around 9:15pm, i was 2 hours past due for pain medication and dominique was nowhere to be found. i hit the call light and the patient care technician came in to assist me with my bedpan and i asked if i could please have some tylenol as i hadn't received anything for pain for over 2 hours. while waiting for dominique to finally do her job, my mother (also a nurse) caught wind of what was happening and phoned the nursing desk. she was placed on hold for 7 minutes and never spoke with the charge nurse as she had requested. dominique finally appeared in my room with tylenol and berated my husband for "calling the front desk." her exact words were "sir, i understand that she's bleeding but there is no need to call the desk on me!" luckily my bleeding stopped on it's own, because i would have hated to become a critical situation in the care of this disinterested and negligent nurse. 

ascension, you have a very dangerous employee working for you. i am shocked and appalled by how horrible i was treated by this nurse. nothing about her is caring or safe; she does not deserve to be employed by such a reputable health institution. i hope you will do the right thing and end her employment with ascension. my mother, mother-in-law, my husband, and myself plan to take this up with the higher ups at the hospital. i hope you will do the right thing and reprimand this employee. 


if dominique is your nurse, request another one! she is dangerous!

i should have looked at the ratings here for this hospital before i chose to have my surgery there. the ratings are low and for good reason. uncaring staff and lazy for the most part. patient care was terrible, ignoring calls; be prepared to take care of yourself or bring a caregiver with you. patients can be heard down the halls screaming in pain and yelling for help, it was horrifying. some doctors are aware of the conditions and get on the staff and their patients get better treatment hence the few good reviews. some doctors even recommend you hire a nurse to stay with your loved one if you can afford it. 
staff lied to my insurance company about my care and services that never happened. i will be contacting my insurance company.

i have worked at three different psychiatric hospitals in the dallas metroplex and can say without reservation that garland behavioral hospital is the best. the staff really care about the patients and i have always been impressed by their competence and compassion. the facility is clean and well maintained. therapeutic groups are excellent. i would not hesitate to recommend this hospital to anyone who needed inpatient care.
this place is a nightmare! they do not separate people into categories so dangerous patients are mixed with people that are there that are suicidal. they treat patients like prisoners.

after taking antibiotics for what i thought was a uti, my symptoms just weren't going away. i couldn't sleep through the night, so i took myself the er in the middle of the night. my husband is deployed, so this was the first time i had to go to the er alone. let me tell you, that's scary. i brought a blanket, and a phone charger and i walked in, tears in my eyes. i had read the reviews before coming, since i'm brand new to the area and i was nervous. but i'm glad i came anyway, everyone was sooooo nice i felt so taken care of. the nurse at the front desk got me checked in quickly and brought me to my room. the nurses checked in on me frequently until the doctor came in. it was around midnight on a wednesday night, and it wasn't too busy. turns out i had a kidney stone! worst pain of my life, but the staff did a great job of making me comfortable. every single person i talked to that night made me feel less alone, and for that i am so so grateful.

if you care about the wellness of yourself and your loved ones, i'd advise that you stay clear of this hospital. i've had two relatives who needed to be transferred out of this hospital because we saw that they were not being given proper care. one of the many instances of neglect was not giving my father in law (who is both a diabetic and transplant patient) his antibiotics on three different occasions. when questioning the staff, i'm forced to hear a run around of answers.

after a week, he looked worse in the care of those at alameda hospital than he did prior to being taken there.

i, myself, had to be transferred to alta bates because of the amount of neglect i experienced after a gallbladder surgery (which included significant internal bleeding caused by mistakes made by the surgeon). because of their mistakes, i had to spend an additional week and a half in the hospital.

i plead with you.

if you care for your loved ones, do not bring them here.

boy has this place gone downhill. i'm sitting in the parking lot waiting for a family member to be seen in the er. it's been hours and no action. there were only two people in the waiting room when this started.  there has only been another few coming and going since.

there is now a security guard just inside the entry door who won't allow anyone to sit on one side of the room away from those who are coughing, etc.  he said it's because it is for check in. there was no one checking in! 

in the meantime, the receptionist was advising my family member what treatment would be needed, despite the fact no actual medical provider had seen or spoken with her yet.  

when she finally got into a freezing room, she had to don the gown and wait for an hour and counting.  she finally had to get dressed again to get warm.  

she has a previously diagnosed kidney stone-a huge one, and brought the imaging documents along to prevent the need for more costly tests or god forbid, another round of unnecessary x-rays.  this thing has kicked up with pain and bleeding. she just needs some symptom relief.  instead of processing her quickly, she's been put on ice (almost literally, due to the cold room and flimsy gown).

what has happened to caring in the medical field, and specifically, in this emergency room? 

shame on those front-line folks and administrators who have forgotten about people in favor of process.

i went to the er over the summer. the care was adequate. however, i am still dealing with the billing. i tried to get them to send the bill to my insurance. the hospital bill went in ok. when i got the doctor's bill, i sent it back with my insurance information. they never billed my insurance, and a couple of months later sent a "final notice". i took the notice to my insurance, but they couldn't pay from that, as it wasn't the actual bill. when my insurance called the medical group's payment processor, the medical group had my birthdate wrong, and would not release information to my insurance. today i got a call from a collection agency.

i will never go back because of their fraudulent billing practices.

i doubt the man who injected my neck with anesthesic today was even a doctor! i am in excruciating pain and from the beginning i told everyone who was working at the hospital that i don't want any pain killers. i got some sort of injection to numb the pain. i rested. i take a water pill, so i had to urinate many times while there. after i got up to go to the bathroom a third time after the injections, my neck was burning. the pain was worse! i couldn't even think or talk. the man said i was just fine when walking to the bathroom a moment ago...he added, "i don't know what happened in the bathroom." what happened? i peed and the pain that had abated for a moment when i was still returned with a vengeance. i have been to this horrid hospital three times and each time, i had to walk out of the er for lack of appropriate medical care. this hospital sucks!!! do not go there if you have a choice and you value your life!

i wish it were possible to give zero stars. this used to be a pretty decent hospital; occasionally there would be a minor issue but was generally a competent, reasonably fast service, the place has become a place of last resort. the utter lack of professionalism, patient-centered processes, and now much longer wait times has greatly diminished my view of alameda hospital. if you care about your health and being treated with basic respect, look elsewhere. i will not bother with the list of issues causing someone with serious, well-documented medical problems causing intense pain to leave, untreated after four hours. suffice it to say that i will never seek help here again when i am in town and shall be speaking with hospital administration about the situation. the bay area is far too tech-savvy and wealthy to present such poor choices for health care, especially in the east bay. alameda was the only patient-friendly hospital and now this is no longer an option.

i gave birth here on 1/3/20. the nurses and midwife was great! however i was not informed of a lot of things. like how to discharge and an issue with the birth certificate. this is my first child so there was a lot i didn't know. i was rushed out the hospital. i only came here cause i wanted to have a water birth, my son had other plans. i don't think i'll be giving birth here again.

i have unfortunately been here twice.  it is not my "hospital of choice".  however, this review is strictly on the emergency room treating an emergency.  both times i arrived and was immediately taken to triage for vitals.  i was treated with respect and compassion.   after being placed in a room (not a fancy or quiet room, but not just a triage curtain like some), i waited roughly 15 to 20 minutes before meeting my nurse and shortly thereafter being joined by a doctor.  both times, i was in immense pain and found relief via pain medication promptly.  both times, the nurses also had the iv in correctly within 1 or 2 pricks - which is quite an accomplishment with me!  the doctor did a great job involving my regular physician via their emergency office line.  the person who wheeled me out wasn't over friendly, but the rest of the staff really seemed to care, provided relief for my pain and stabilized my condition(s).  i received a survey the next day from the hospital asking for feedback, which is more than i can say about several of the general practices i have been to here in ga.  
i am happy that we have a local option for emergencies and at this time would feel completely comfortable taking myself or family back there if needed.  i understand others haven't been as fortunate with who helped them at this er, but i am grateful for the help i was given and hope they continue to provide care to others in a similar manner.   thank you wellstar at north fulton!

this is the worst hospital i have ever been to. the doctor basically told me he's there to keep people alive and your not dying. i told him my ear hurt really bad he didn't even look at it. i told him my throat hurt he didn't even look at it. the nurse swabbed my nose said i didn't have the flu. i left , these people are just horrible

my emergency room experience was horrendous.  rude check in nurse, extremely rude insurance/paperwork gathering lady.  i was placed in a separate room because i had the flu, and i totally understand that; i asked for some water and the lady at the desk who gathers insurance information was rude, had a nasty attitude and un-empathetic demeanor.  i assumed folks that work at a hospital would have a bit more empathy.  then i got a bill for $2000.. it's quite a paradox.

we took a family member here and needed a medical check before transporting to a rehab facility.  in this crisis mode, we were trying to determine where to transfer to.  we explained in great detail to the nurses that we would need dual diagnosis treatment.  a "peachford rep" was there and came to do an evaluation.  we were promised all kinds of things including individual and family therapy.  all of this was a lie.  do not let them advise on where to send your loved ones.    do your own research outside of their recommendations.  contact and get recommendations from aa or na members who have been through this.  they will be a lot more reliable and authentic than a company who just wants to bill your insurance.   the peachford experience was another joke amongst several lies and i will be doing a review on that also.

insane wait times despite waiting area. i'm absolutely appalled. my wife and i have been here with our 6 year old daughter waiting on 3 stitches  for a cut on her face for 5 hours and counting. the hospital is a ghost town based on multiple walks around the er space, aside from the dozens of nurses sitting around on their phones. clearly they are super understaffed on the doctor side while wildly overstaffed on the nurse side

i get that a 3 stitch cut is not priority but all the more reason to take the 5 minutes to address and free up the bed for someone who needs it more. meanwhile, we've now had to apply two 30 minute rounds of novacaine to my daughters face (per instruction from the nurses) since the effect of the first round wore off as we wait here. and i say we had to apply the novocaine because despite a bunch a dozen nurses mulling around they asked my wife and i to continue applying it for them. 

absolute joke

our children have been patients of dr. timothy buie, md. for many years. 
dr. buie is a very talented pediatric gastroenterologist (and harvard med school professor) and always gives exceptional care to our children.  he is always polite, extremely knowledgeable and is always happy to help and answer our questions.  highly recommend and well worth the drive.

this place sucks speaking on vendor terms the docks are always over crowded, endless construction, rude desk staff that rather be texting then helping, no one knew how to operate a pass machine, no one picks up the phone from the dock entrance god forbid if you ring the other line or some hood rat security guy will tell you try the button again and hang up not even attempt to help, confusing layout of the building feels like i'm in a bug hive. that's pretty much why this place sucks.

the doctors are great help . i just wanted to say that the au bon pain restaurant definitely needs a new staff because the people are rude, don't speak a lick of english and could care less about customer service . if the owner to this place for some reason sees this please for the life of me , fire your staff and start from scratch !!

my then 4 year old son was being treated for scoliosis by dr. michael glotzbecker at boston children's hospital - orthopedics.   due to my sons age and nature of his curve the md ordered a mri to rule out certain neurological conditions (chiari 1 malformation, tethered spine, etc) and said the procedure was i would be contacted if an abnormality was detected.  one full year later (after glotzbecker left for cleveland oh) my son's new physician reviewed his file and found that nobody had ever reviewed the mri and my son in fact did have a chiari 1 malformation causing a syrinx in his spine.   this should have been communicated immediately a year before and addressed surgically.  dr. glotzbecker's negligence and the failure of boston children's hospital to have proper procedures to ensure proper review and action was taken endangered my son's health and will have an unknown impact on the future outcome of his scoliosis.  i can not recommend dr. michael glotzbecker in any way as he was responsible and his failure is in my opinion negligent, and boston children's hospital also failed because they had an "unknown open loop" in their system... aka failure to ensure the mri was reviewed.   we went to boston children's hospital because they promote themselves as the top juvenile orthopedics hospital in america.  unfortunately in my experience they are simply living off their own self promotion not providing world class care.   they have also failed to take actual accountability for the issue and are treating it like an "oops" and imply that i should be thankful it wasn't worse.  tremendously disappointing.

do not go to this hospital unless you're unconscious and can't make the decision on your own.  they are completely incompetent.  they didn't even ask my daughter if she was allergic to any medication, and wrote on her chart that she has no known allergies.  she is deathly allergic to a particular medication.  she waited for 4 hours and never saw a doctor.  if you care about you or your loved one's well-being, stay away from tmh.

what a joke! our wait time of course was expected for the er but our treatment afterwards when we finally got a room, i mean we felt like we got forgotten constantly! my husband peed in a cup when we first got there then they didn't pick it up for two hours! this young doctor comes in to tell us to go home and take pain medicine when my husband is in severe pain. the medication they gave did nothing so we're we suppose to go home then come right back with the same issue?? i realize it's the er but when i asked to run another test the doctor sat down with us and urged us not to. yah you're just trying to free up the room at this point. like we really want to be here hanging out in the hospital so bad disappointed, annoyed, and very tired. we will go elsewhere for care when it's needed kadlec and it's not with you!

i would of given less stars if it wasn't for my nurse that did more for me after being discharged then the doctor did while a patient. this place literally told me i need more testing but not here. i only went here cause my mom was driving and can't see at night. i will not ever be back. i don't have insurance or money for this. i would rather die then go to an er for the most expensive shot of morphine ever. fix your system kadlec/providence before you kill someone. i wish providence would of never bought you. the woman working that night had to run the front desk while checking patience in. i hope you cut enough costs to line your pockets at the cost of hurting others. i loved your place when i had my baby 29yrs ago in everett sure gone to crap here. my mom worked for you for 20yrs in everett i loved you cause my mom was happy. you disgust me now. you're a hospital to help. start helping!!!!

worst hospital ever !!! glad to here that it's closing! my mom passed away here. the doctors never talked to me to tell me that she  dying . i was under the impression that she was dehydrated next thing i know some rude hospice doctor who showed absolutely no compassion to me and my family,basically said ,"look she'll be died in a couple of days". to this day i wonder how on a friday she's sitting up eating and a few day later she's died. i was never told she was hospice until  three days of her passing. she was taken to st. vincent on a friday the next week she passed away.. i'm still feeling some way on how you can be sitting up eating on a friday which i fed her to to totally shutting down.. the next week  even when i felt that the antibiotics that were given to her seemed to be much.

this review is part of my cousin needing to heal from the emotional and mental abuse she suffered at the hands of staff at riveredge hospital in forest park in the late 80's.  i am speaking on her behalf.

my cousin had some teenage depression.  she was admitted to riveredge as a teen.  no drugs, no drinking issues.  depression. 

my cousin told my aunt and uncle some things that were going on at this facility.  when the staff found out from my aunt and uncle whom were upset with what they found out was going on in that unit,  they said to my cousin "who do you think people are going to believe?  us or you.  look where you are."  the staff in a group session  then allowed another teen to berate my cousin in retaliation for my cousin complaining to her parents about some transgressions that transpired with this other teen on that unit/floor. 

when the staff could not find any diagnosis other than mild depression for my cousin that was a teenager at the time, they told her she suffered from, "narcistic personality disorder."  years later my cousin was told by a psychologist that as a  teenager any teen can be, " narcistic," in nature.  riveredge needed something to hold my cousin with for insurance purposes longer term.  something to diagnose her with for insurance purposes. 

it was common knowledge amongst the teenage patients that the only way anyone was, "cured,"  and released was either to lie and agree with what the staff members told them they were feeling or if the parent's insurance ran out.  the kids called it, "playing the therapy game." agree with the therapists on staff at riveredge or you will not be deemed to be making progress and released.   many kids knew they were stuck at this private hospital for great lengths of time due to mom or dad having great health coverage.

today,  despite being at riveredge hospital for a month, my cousin is a thriving individual.  she is a productive member of society that is happy and healthy in mind, body and spirit.  that is despite her stay at riveredge hospital as a teen for mild depression. 

 occasionally she still has  nightmares about her experience at riveredge hospital in forest park.  

i told my cousin i would write a review even though this  transpired in the mid-late 80's.   i did this for her as part of her healing process.  i am happy as her cousin and as her friend to do so.

please seek therapy elsewhere for your teen, child or for yourself.

i can see from more recent reviews of riveredge in forest park that it is still a pretty lousy place to experience therapy.

review:
the nurses at this hospital are excellent. they are quick to respond, competent, and kind. unfortunately, this antiquated medical center requires them to wait for doctor's "orders." if the nurses ran the hospital, im confident it would be the best in the city!

an iv was started, labs were drawn, history taken, ecg done,  throat looked at, i dont recall anyone having a stethoscope, but diagnosis of  dehydration made. liter of fluid infused by gravity in 30 minutes then sat for next 40 minutes alone. no idea how to get help if needed and couldnt talk or scream.
then a team, 3 nurses, paramedic, doctor and scribe came in. suddenly, the dehydration was critical, they started another iv ran 3 liters of fluid in with pressure bags and pumps, which actually took twice as long as gravity, and transferred to ccu simultaneously!  what do you think they were doing for the 40 minutes we just sat there after the first liter? 
the doctor in ccu started explaining diagnosis, but was called away to an emergency. he never came back. we saw a doctor each morning who was kind but ignored sore throat as dehydration, ignored stomach pain as hunger or gas, ordered tests and never gave results or explained plan of care. once said needed to drink more but order was npo! 
the nurses always asked, every time they left room if patient or family needed anything. they agreed every time to check on results and plan. sometimes they responded they weren't sure why there wasn't a plan yet, but agreed to check. 
when transferred to regular floor, we were told the doctor had 24 hrs to see patient and they started new meds per protocol. they offered to contact np. they returned stating np was at a rapid response and would try to return. its been 8 hours. i have no doubt the np was busy. there are rapid responses every hour and several code blues.
maybe if patients had a plan of care they wouldnt be dying for attention.

review: i will never darken the steps of this place again. if i was having a medical emergency, i would drive past here to get somewhere else. i know it's a hospital and it's rarely a pleasant or quick experience but this is beyond. my 80 year old mother has been in a wheelchair waiting for hours, being pulled back and forth from the waiting room to a crappy triage area. people are out in the waiting room with iv poles and moaning and such. five hours and there hasn't been one room opened?  it's been a total shitshow. not to mention the dr spent 75 seconds with her barking off a bunch of medical lingo to someone feverishly typing on a laptop. very disappointed. i'm furious.

recently i had eye surgery to replace a lens that was becoming cloudy from a cataract.  the surgery was performed by dr. richard pare, md.  i was awake during the procedure and experienced no pain at all.  dr. pare sliced out the lens contaminated by a cataract and inserted one that was designed to bring my vision from 20/100 to 20/20!!  i have been in the healthcare business for over 40 years and what makes northside hospital a winner is the attitude of the people there.  they all want to provide the best possible service to their patients.  i have been in some of the most famous hospitals in the usa ranging from the mayo clinic to the cleveland clinic and although both are fine hospitals, neither one's staff has the great attitude of northside!!!!

i had a horrible experience giving birth here. it was my third child and i pretty much had no choice; i had to be induced in this hospital. everything was perfectly fine  until i got out in a room. it was so hot and i guess the ac was out because there was only a room fan in the room. strange but it wasn't a big deal. then i look over and i'm sharing a room with another woman; i still did not make it a big deal. after i give birth, i got put into my room. i didn't feel anything at the beginning, but later on i guess my bladder was really full and i was in so much pain, literally crying. i asked the nurse if she can  please get me a bed pan because i was in severe pain i couldn't even get  up and she rudely said "i can't be doing that you need to get up and go use the bathroom yourself" i was in utter shock and disbelief. i was literally begging this woman to help me, my insurance was paying and that's the response i get? later on this really nice nurse came in and she was godsend. incredibly nice and  patient and understanding. i don't remember her name but i think she worked at pacific alliance hospital. she is an example  of how all nurses should be! i will never ever come back here.

i have been here many a times. it is a small hospital, and i feel well taken care of when i come. i have been to the er for myself and family members at least 10 times in the past  5 years and the staff is always friendly and always right there to help, even in the middle of the night. i had my appendix removed here and the doctors were great. i had my son here 2 years ago and we were the only ones there having a baby those few days. 4/5 nurses that were there for us were awesome. i give it 4 stars because i am not a big fan of how close the sick patients are to the new babies. the only thing separating the two wards is a nurses station.

oh yeah..they treat you really good ...then send you the "good bill" and mandate you to pay  up or "collections"...they chose their doctors  ..the ones that cost $1700.oo for 70 mins and you get a separate bill from that dr...
and you continue getting bills months later...there is no sympathy...no empathy ...pay up or collections...

i was transferred here from hoag, for a surgery and am so please with the care and service of all the people who work here. all the nurses have been amazing, responsive and very caring! i also have a service dog and everyone here has treated me and her with the utmost respect. 
from er to surgical to multiple days in the hospital- foothill regional med center is a very safe and cosy place to recover!
thank you all for taking care of me and putting me back to health!- ann

this is by far the best experience me and my wife have seen. we first went to a global medical.....well let's say i wouldn't even send trump there if giving a signed executive order staff is rude unprofessional, violated all kinds of codes and laws.

my wife transfered here to frmc and has the best care i've seen anywhere. foothill is top-notch. we been to several hospitals that treat you like rotten dogfood when they find out homeless and on cal-optima. 
not here at foothill. all the staff treated her like at some high-end private pay facility. asked if needed anything, if she was sleeping they'd let her sleep and informed me will be back appx 60- 90 minutes  for tests or blood. her dr....dr. boutros(soory if misspelled)was amazing & he greeted my wife, and then stuck out hand and gave a good man's handshake. he promised to give my amber the best care he could....which is exactly what she's recieving. i don't think the girlscouts have produced as many "brownie's buttons as this hospital and it's entire staff from the janitor (place is spotless) to the rns have earned. in my book this place should be listed as oc most friendly/professional medical facility of 2020.

just had my second surgery here and i have zero complaints about this place. the check in process was quick and a nurse came to get me shortly afterwards.

you're led to the back prep room where you change into a gown and fluids are administered. the prep nurses are great! the asian one, i wish i remembered her name, remembered me from my first surgery 7 months ago. you're asked a lot of questions while you wait for your doctor to arrive.  

doc arrives, goes over your surgery with you, and you're  about 15 minutes out. an operating room nurse wheels you into the surgery room. everything in there is super clean and the room is very bright. an anesthesiologist comes in, gives you a shot, and boom - you're out like a light and wake up in the recovery room.

the recovery room nurses were top notch and the cherry on top of an overall great experience, even though i had my hip replaced. david and blanca went above and beyond to make sure every need was taken care of while there. i really appreciated everything they did for me.

oh my god- this place is a nightmare. if you aren't forced here by insurance run like hell. the nursing staff is the worst, well except for one named kathy and an honerable mention for angela. the only time i sleep is when kathy gets assigned to my dad! it's a miracle if the other nurses even wash their hands and my dad doesn't even sleep because they are so disruptive and unprofessional. they know i'm a nurse practitioner and know what they are supposed to be doing and they don't even try for my benefit. kathy actually cares..seriously! she cares about the little things as well and not just giving meds. she has the experience that the others lack. i'm done with this. i'm taking names and writing the board about them. if you want to hurt someone call in sick. the staff =no stars! kathy ten stars !!! just hope to get her if you want your family member to wake up in the morning. period!!!

update post:

updating my review to 3 stars. they reached out to me, put a hold on the collection company and i paid the bill direct. just wish it was resolved differently from the beginning.


initial post:

i went to their er because of a small wound that was starting to get infected. did all the check in process showing my insurance id card, filled all paperwork etc.. after about 30 min waiting, the doctor shows up in the waiting room to take a look at the wound. at one point he used his pen to exam it ( in the waiting room! how professional!) a few minutes later they gave me some anti-biotics, a prescription and i was on my way home. the very next day i received a call from the billing dpt telling me that i had to pay a $300 copay for my visit. alright, no problem, i understand that, here is the $300 dollars. and i thought that was it as nobody ever contacted me again. now, 6 months after the fact, i just received a collection letter  from a collection company trying to bill me for another $169! are you guys kidding me?? no one ever calls me to let me know? send a letter, maybe?? no, you guys gave my information out to some third party collection company for just $169 dollars!! how am i supposed to know that this bill ever existed? and what  is this $169 for?? stay away!!!

huge thank you to dr. d thomas! i just visited foothill er today with my son and daughter (1&3) and he was so very awesome with them! considering everything going on with the coronavirus all of the staff were very nice and helpful and made my kids feel at ease. the rn carlos, i think is his name was so nice and gave my daughter a coloring pad! also, the woman nurse (unfortunately i didn't get her name) who i have met before, was just as wonderful as the first time from car seat advice to helping hold down a fussy baby. thank you guys so very much for helping my babies and putting my mind at ease!!! probably one of the best hospital visits i've ever had. thank you again!

-taylor parker

at a glance, i was not impressed with the er.  once my dad was transferred to his room, i was impressed by the hospitality of the staff.  there was an rn by the name of thomas that is attentive, and humorous, and his assistant michelle was caring and compassionate.  maggie (case manager) is awesome, she helped throughout the process and kept me informed the entire time.

unfortunately i had to check into their er last week and had a bad experience. the bed was dirty and the staff was not so friendly. to make matters worse when they took my blood the nurse brought a young trainee and she didn't know what she was doing because now my arm is bruised up. i can't believe they use er patients as their guinea pigs to practice on.

i never know that this hospital was here, and it's so close to my home but aside from that what a wonderful group of people. i have had excellent care dispute being a cal optima patient. my pacu nurse caroline was amazing and the or nurse an angel. what compassion and loving energy is in this hospital, i'll never go anywhere else!

my father was recently receiving care here in icu, and initially i wasn't pleased with the environment and comfort. the first night i stayed with him, and it was hard to sleep with the light always being left on and the lack of warmth (literally and figuratively). the second day the rn kathie was his nurse, and what a huge difference she made in creating a comfortable, caring, and relaxing environment turning the bright lighting off and making him feel more at ease. i was able to go home and get some rest knowing that he was in capable and compassionate hands. thank you kathie we are both so grateful for ending up having a positive experience at this hospital.

being a nurse, the last place you expect to find yourself on your day off is the hospital ed.   it happens !  on the brighter side , after suffering an injury that resulted in a knee and wrist fracture, i was so happy to be cared for by such a wonderful team.   the nurses , the doctors , and the case management team were awesome at foothill!    the injury was not so fun , but, i was great full for the care i received , thank you all of you !

it has been a year and a half since i was admitted as a inpatient at kennestone. it was 4 weeks after back surgery at emory. my right leg was 10 on the pain scale. because i was screaming so loudly, i was put in a small room to await whatever records they were able to get from emory. 

they finally gave me pain meds and admitted me to the oldest, smallest semi-private room in the hospital that did not have a chair. i was told it was too small for a chair. i have fibromyalgia and needed to get out of my bed often. also, the mattress was sagging, which hurt my back. i had two mattress/bed changes. 

after 4 days, i was treated for nothing!  a hospital affiliated physician of orthopedics was called in, but he refused to examine my leg because in his words, "i was still under the care of the emory spinal surgeon." 
lso i was sent home. 

it turned out that i needed a hip replacement, which i did have at emory several months later. no not at kennestone. 

the kicker is that wellstar is still billing me 1 1/2 years later. for doing nothing.

they have the best er in atlanta, bar none.

they are appalling bad at treating patients in the hospital itself.
y'all treated my grandmother like crap. nurses and doctors were completely disrespectful towards her. rather take the longer drive to northside cherokee than go here.

billing department is horrible they won't give you any information on who you can speak with in financial services. when u make a complaint with the human resources department the lady does nothing to help. supervisors don't talk to anyone there never available. er drs have different billing than the hospital.

mom had a heart attack.  despite clear indicators of this, we had to wait for hours before a a doctor would even look at her, and even longer for a cardiologist who could actually read the ekg.  despicable.

went to the er the other night with my mom in extreme pain from diverticulitis. we waited in the waiting room for over two hours, which is fine except the doctor gave her bad care. she finally got a room past midnight and complained of pain but didn't receive a single medication until 7am. when she asked why the nurse said she "forgot". after waiting there for over 10 hours she finally left only to discover the doctor forgot to put her written prescription in her checkout folder. i was under the assumption that doctors were supposed to go over the treatment upon release but we were handed a folder and said to leave. between the wait time and irresponsible doctors and nurses i don't plan on going back.
if you want the wrong side of the brain taken off this is the place to go. very poor medical staff.

we brought our 88 year old mother here to urgent care. from the moment we arrived, we were treated with care and respect. she spent an additional 3 days, and was placed in a postpartum room. again her treatment was exceptional.
hospitals are never easy, because emotions are high, the employees are always busy, and fear of the unknown that's ahead. the staff at loma linda made our mom's stay exceptional.
thank you all for making us all feel confident in our mom's treatment

i would like to commend efren, orthopedics surgery, who worked so hard rescheduling 3  appointments for me and my husband on same day. this will eliminate three different trips to loma linda medical center it will not only save time and fuel  but also exposure to potential corona virus. we cant be too careful right now.
next time i need to schedule an appointment i will ask for efren.
efren is very helpful, curtious, respectful and friendly. 
congratulations to loma linda for this employee.

i just had surgery here today. i just want to say this place is wonderful! the staff is sweet. the facility is extremely clean and i felt very informed prior to surgery. it was really nice talking with the nurses and laughing. i guess they got a kick out of me when i was coming out of my anesthesia. ‍‍‍ i would recommend this facility to anyone who is referred or has to have surgery here. kaiser partners with loma linda for surgery and i am glad they did.

so this is now a class action lawsuit. just got a letter in the mail that someone has started the process and they want information about the bill and the deceptive techniques used when you speak the billing service. i will keep updating as i find out more.

just being honest - i was pretty terrified to walk into the er because of the really frightening yelp reviews. however, my insurance sent me to this place and i only went when it got so painful i could barely walk. not kidding. the admitting rn took one look at my recent bloodwork copy i'd brought along, and told me immediately that i had what i was later diagnosed with: impressive! the overcrowding was an issue, but i still got a hall bed for awhile, and i got that pretty quickly; maybe because of my temperature? anyhow, i loved the employees- they were young but seemed genuinely joyful - especially ellie...her joy made my day. my overnight room had no toilet - which was rough while having a case of ulcerative colitis (diarrhea!) - but i'm younger and more mobile than most patients there, so i get it. not a real problem. the upstairs was like shangri la! just heavenly!!! felt like i had a rockstar room - but they are all like that! and the end lobby views were absolutely break taking!!! jesus brought me a heated sheet one night that was so comforting i nearly cried, one of the nurses was wonderful with lots of room cleaning, and i think the docs there actually saved my life. my biggest issue was the menu and the one dietician who went running away when i was crying over the soda and hard food that got served after my uc diagnosis- and all the sealed food they had to throw away after i requested they not bring it in the first place (runny gelatins and sugary icy desserts and such)...in their defense, the chicken with sauce  they served was restaurant quality, and they were just trying to help me gain weight with all the sugary things, i guess. overall, it was a beautiful amazing place. if my dietary concerns were addressed and if they'd responded to numerous calls and voicemails (re billing) that both my insurance co and i placed afterward...they'd get 5 stars for sure. definitely not perfect, but i've never in my life been to a more beautiful hospital...and i really loved almost all of the employees!

unprofessional, unorganized, miscommunication are the initial thoughts for the er. 9 hours later i can clearly define the horrible, cringe worthy experience here at the loma linda murrieta er. this department cannot get anything right and seem to enjoy the fact that they could not care less about it. i can deal with unprofessional behavior, having to draw blood twice and throwing their mouse and mouse pad in frustration with patience. but i draw the line at clearly not giving a shit while they sit in their dirt, grime, sticky and disgusting er environment. mean while hemet hospital has an amazing patience experience. everyone at the executive and the management level at loma linda should be embarrassed of this place.
amazing staff. amazing dr's. they were so patient and so informative about the care we are going to receive. i'm always so impressed with loma linda every single visit.

i went to the er this evening and was very appalled. there was a male nurse that was extremely rude for no reason. i was heading back with my mom and he stood up with attitude and said aggressively i can't be back there. he has no bedside manner and should not work in healthcare. even worse, later i saw him taking an elderly man back. the woman with the man said she needed to be with him to assist. he replied back to her with attitude, "why?!". even i understand some elderly need someone to speak on their behalf. this guy suffers from little man syndrome for sure. i will warn to avoid a little guy that might be hispanic or middle eastern. i did not get his name but he had a grey sweater with black on top.

the medical director of the ed dept. is not doing his/her job. this is the most terrible ed experience i have ever had. as my mother checked in vomiting, she asked the greeting nurse if she spoke spanish and the nurse responded with "no, but i do speak english". whoever chose this person to represent a hospital is completely lacking judgement skills when interviewing candidates for job openings. immediately after that nurses response, the people in the waiting room looked in disbelief of what they just had witnessed. once in the back, and still vomiting, the insurance person comes with her computer on wheels and starts asking her for her name and insurance information. like hellooooo, can you not see i'm trying to help my mom while she can barely catch her breath from all the nausea and vomiting and stomach pain she is having. we made it clear to her that we have insurance (and a really good one) but at the moment we could not provide her with the information other than what we know from the top of our heads which was her name, dob, and insurance company as our hands were full and i was concentrating on helping my mom. some people need to have the common sense to know when it is not a good time to ask for this kind of stuff. she just stood there watching my mom toss,turn, puke, and closing her eyes shut from stomach pain and still wanted the information. we finally very bluntly asked her to come back later. this ed needs better management and a few people replaced.

this hospital sucks.  my mother in law has been in the er hallway for 24 hours because of they cannot find a  room for here.  they don't want to transfer  her to a different facility because they will loose money so she will  remain in the hallway for good knows when.   don't come here.  the staff are unprofessional and clueless.  they almost a procedure twice because they  are  tooo busy with too many patients and not  enough room.

went to urgent care first since i dread er due to all the nightmare scenarios and urgent care said you need to go to er stat you have a tachycardia and 105 temp do you need us to call an ambulance? it's not that far i will drive. i get there and attempt to give the front desk the note only to be dismissed by emt sara and get yelled at in a lobby full of people that if i don't  take a seat she's going to get security to kick me out. fine i will call paramedics and have them take me where bees are available no problem i have a premium ppo. i guess she takes personal offense to it puts me in a tiny room in the back and dismisses my ailments as it's just the flu. then this god send of a nurse and doctor take extremely better care of me and diagnose me with strep. & tachycardia with a fever. they give me a cocktail of medication to make me feel better versus the advise of sara to just buy some tylenol or advil over the counter. not the reception i was expecting from a christian private organization that has its values posted everywhere for all to see. i shouldn't have to dread going to the er due to the chance encounter of an individual like this sara. hospital is okay just be cautious of this individual she might yell at you in public like you're a child not a consumer.

this is a terrible hospital. i am furious i will never come back here. come here if you want to be in pain and die. i cannot believe the service here. this is the worst hospital ever. everyone here is incompetent idiot. also, when you are hiring workers, hire people who can articulate a sentence at the least.
