va clinic, waiting , one hour and 45 minutes ti see doctor, real bad

took my husband into the er for terrible pain related to his ra. saw a staff pa, two written scripts for us to fill at an outside pharmacy.  total of @ 12 minutes medical and the rest waiting for billing and discharge.  billed the insurance for a level 3!  after calling and requesting a line by line billing, got a one line 'level 3'.  requested a review and response was billing was right. i reviewed coding and, even reaching, should have been a 2 at most. appealed in writing and still ignored. i'm giving another week and then i'll turn it over to the regulatory agency and the press to look into the overcoding practices of north suburban.

waited 2 hours just to be  seen and the another 2 hours for treatment and 30 minutes just to get discharged ridiculous and horrible service
we felt so well taken care of and cared for during our visit! nurses, doctors, front desk, even the room service and house keeping staff were warm and friendly. thank you :)
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco

review: this review is more so for the billing/records departments. my hospital stay was fantastic but i would caution anyone staying here to follow up with the hospital for any billing information. i gave birth in july and i am now receiving notices from other doctors and agencies (collections) claiming they have mailed me bills numerous times. come to find out this hospital inputted my address incorrectly into their system even after having a copy of my dl that had my most current address. terrible!! never once did i receive a phone call or email about any bills from the hospital. nor did i get any bills from my insurance company. i would think the hospital would try to reach out or check their records (where they made a copy of my dl) to ensure they had the correct address.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco

review: i had an abdominal surgery on december 2019 in this hospital. just right after my surgeries, the nurse rushed to release me from hospital without making sure that i couldn't pee.  i had to go to near by urgent care to release my urine and then went back to er of this hospital to put catheter on.  i shouldn't have suffered several tough days and shouldn't happen to any hospital for such a careless mistake.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco

review:
this hospital (doctors, nurses, chaplain and staff) saved my life! 

excellent medical knowledge, unbelievable bedside manner, and they also put an emphasis on god,  family and friends!  i love this place

i had trouble breathing. staff fixated on my heart, which i told them was not the issue. they admitted me. ran various tests. but would not give the blood test i requested and discharged me 24 hours unable to diagnose me and, quote "sometimes these things just happen." 24 hours later breathing difficulties even worse. go to a different hospital where they do actually listen. did requested blood test. scanned my chest. discovered multiple pulmonary emboli in both lungs. life threatening. get me on blood thinners immediately. i then receive bill for st. josephs. i call them up, make arrangements that they don't send me any more bills and i don't sue for malpractice. fast forward to this week. statute of limitations has passed on malpractice case. they issue a summons to appear in court for not paying bill. utter scum.

my family brought in my father into your emergency room at st. joseph's on thursday december 5th. he had weakness and pain in his legs which was causing him to be unable to walk with out 2+ people holding him up to move him around. we were given a room later on that night and they were observing him over night. on saturday they decided he needed surgery due to his gallbladder being inflamed, which they said is the reason that he is unable to walk and do stuff on his own. but a couple days passed and he just was becoming weaker as the days passed. he still needed 2+ people helping him out so the physical therapist told the case manager that he will need to go to a rehabilitation center until he gains his strength back. it is now december 11th and my father was discharged and admitted into sloan's lake rehabilitation center. my father was mistreated at this location and we made the decision to remove my father from this facility. we contacted st. joseph's hospital to let them know what happened and see if we can bring my father back until another rehab facility opens up. which we were told the next opening was on friday at the rehabilitation center in lakewood. which is the one we asked to be sent to in the first place since it's right by our home. but  the person we spoke to  said it was not their problem anymore and they can not help us anymore since we left the facility. we asked if we can get in contact with his doctor that was seeing him at the hospital and we were told that we can't have access to those records. they kept transferring us to other departments and they would pick up and hang up on us or no one would pick up. my father still cannot move on his own which is an unsafe not only for him but also for my family. & he is still  hallucinating and it keeps getting worse. i want to understand why this hospital does not want to help my father out. he is ill and they decided to discharge him way too soon in the first place and put him in the  hands of a facility that should not be up and running.  i thought as a physician you guys do no harm but all they caused is harm to my father's health. my father is not the same person that we brought into this hospital and i blame st. joseph's hospital for that.
thanks for the review sample, maybe you should just write mine for me, since i have little positive to pass along.

i delivered my second child here and had the best care. the maternity ward nurses were amazing. dr. lysy was the most uplifting obgyn i've ever had. i definitely recommend her if your expecting. she practices out of this hospital with prevea. buuut don't expect a 5 star meal for your a stay though, however it is decent quality. there's quite a few places that deliver food though, if your not diggin the cafeteria grub. i definitely recommend this  hospital

terrible experience. doctors used poor treatment practices, nurses and doctors alike practiced unethical standards of care-- nurse telling me that my foot wasn't broken and to simply walk on it without supports. i had a shattered heel bone. doctors and nurses discussing private client information in halls with and without patient, in the presence of other people. will avoid this hospital at all costs now, wentworth douglas and exeter hospitals both practice client-centered care and have higher standards of care than portsmouth.

the worst emergency room ever. the secretaries are from hell. my mom waited 12 hours because of these heartless human beings behind the desk!!! they ignored me like i wasn't even there!! cruel hearted bitches!!!

awful!! dangerous place!!  incompetent!  i went there after leaving the hospital due to multiple fractures thinking it would be good for rehab before going home.  however, we only lasted about 5 hours.  it took them 45 minutes to answer a call button.  if a person had fallen and busted their head they could be dead as long as it took them to respond!! there were other issues as well and we found them to be totally incompetent!!  such a shame!!
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Scottsdale

review:
i had to go to the er on sunday night. the sign said 8 minute wait time. well that only applied to the time to do the paperwork. 

i arrived around 5 and didn't see a doctor or receive any tests for over an hour and a half. i was in excruciating pain from a gallbladder attack and didn't even get any pain meds until about 9:00 even though i was told i was getting them several times. my sister had to go up and tell them again that i hadn't had them yet. 

this was after they had decided that i would need surgery and said that a surgeon would be out to talk to me in a few minutes.  i didn't see a surgeon until around 11:00 after they finally decided to admit me and get me out of the waiting room. i sat back in a recliner for what seemed like forever waiting for a room. i had to walk out to the desk to remind them that i was in there waiting for saline and whatever else they were supposed to get me when i went in there.

the next day he was transferred to med-surg 3rd floor, stella (daytime) as his nurse for the next 2 days. she likewise provided exceptional service, tending to all his/our needs in a very prompt manner. she consistently went above and beyond, not hesitating to call physicians and inpatient pharmacy to obtain orders, inquire about starting his new chemo meds, verifying home meds, etc.

assistants, the social worker, intake folks, my surgeon's assistant, the meal hostess, the nursing students, the chaplain, the physical therapists... every single one has been as though they were snapped up out of the best, funniest, most soulful, helpful and charming medical comedy/drama film ever made. now, i have to be brutally honest, i have been on some strong pain medicine, but nothing that has significantly altered my cognitive ability. unfortunately, it has caused me to forget some of the names of a few of the remarkably compassionate, funny, kind, competent medical professionals i have ever had the privilege to be cared for by. but it has truly been the nurses and nursing assistants who have saved me here. over the last nearly 4 years, i have lost the love of my life, two close friends, a cousin i grew up with and my dear little dog. i came here angry and tearful and hopeless. i actually expected to wake up from surgery missing a leg. so, here goes. the nurses...lizzy, young, funny, immensely caring. she stayed over after shift change when she'd been up for the whole night shift taking care of me, because i was scared and in pain. she stayed past her work day (night) until she was sure i was ok. mikell who was so compassionate and thoughtful that he made my bed into a cozy cocoon so i could sleep comfortably even though my leg was excruciatingly painful. loretta, who liked to pretend she was just a no nonsense health care worker, but helped me bathe and go to the bathroom and learn to safely get in and out of bed when i could barely move without pain and never once made me feel embarrassed or desperately dependent. martha, whose quiet, peaceful competence made me feel safe and as cared for as when i was a child...and my childhood through my adolescence and adulthood was plagued by illness and injury. and dina, a straight forward, no nonsense nurse who ended up not only caring for my physical well-being, but gave me the straight forward life advice i have needed to hear since i lost my husband and my relationship with my daughter and my  mind and my life on an extremely heartbreaking mother's day. and my last night nurse, mark, who anticipated my pain and my fear and my boredom and my anxiety and put me at such ease that i actually want to adopt him, except that he already has a great mom in the phillipines. there was virginia, who i barely remember because of the heavy pain meds and anxiety, but who i know took excellent care of me. and finally elizabeth, the nurse's assistant who didn't laugh at me when i asked who all my other caregivers had been while i was crying with sheer gratitude over the  incredible staff at grossmont hospital in la mesa, california. if i have missed someone, i am sincerely sorry, it is only because of the pain medication. so, there it is then. nuff said. kate  okay, it's been just 22 hours since i first posted this review. there are five more grossmont care givers i need to mention. 3 from the very beginning of my stay that i've only now remembered and two from the very end of my stay, whom i had not yet met when i first reviewed grossmont hospital. first, the lovely and extremely informative astrid, who hosted the total joint replacement class before the surgery. she answered all of my many questions regarding my knee replacement surgery and post-op care. she actually came to my hospital room before i was discharged to answer even more concerns i had post-op about how best to heal and get the healthy diet i need to heal quickly and properly. technically, her job was already completed even before i was admitted. thank you, astrid, for coming in to check on me when you simply heard through the grapevine that i had some questions about discharge and my post-op journey.

this by far the worst hospital i've ever encountered. i've been here admitted for 9 days with no end in site. the first 3 days neither myself or roommate were brought any food trays at all the entire day. we both went 3 days without eating. yes, management was called, so many supervisors and management came to our room in attempt to clear this all out. photos were taken for proof of the trays we were given when we managed to get one. today, day #9 a tray arrived with chicken pot pie as the dinner. literally there was 2 teaspoon fulls of food, again photos. it's not like we can go to the corner store to get a meal. last night i had to order out and have it delivered just to eat. so not only are we paying a hospital bill but have to pay to eat as well. i'd assume patients haven't been complaining and the staff have been getting away with this for so long it's becoming habit. there is no excuse for treating patients this way! many patients are very ill and are fighting for their lives, fighting to eat and keep your strength shouldn't be part of your recovery process. grossmont hospital should hang their heads in shame, i know upper management is aware of the problems as i've contacted them, i've also contacted hospital administrators.

i was in coastal harbor treatment center for 2 weeks, from 12.13.2019 to 12.27.2019. i was in the residential 2 east girls' unit for self-harm. i was supposed to stay for half a year, but my "treatment team" decided to release me after 2 weeks because i believe they thought i was violent or self-harmed but in fact, i was not. the reason i was sent there, according to my mom, was refusal to take my medication and because i had a "bad attitude". i have anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, tourette's syndrome, and adhd, but i am not physically aggressive and i have no history of self-harm, despite what my mother says (she says she stopped me from self-harming, when in fact i stopped her from self-harming)

when i was there, i had a very mediocre experience. 

when you first arrived, you were on "precautions" for up to 10 days, i was on it for about 9. this meant you could not do any fun activities like recreational therapy and you ate meals on the unit. you could also not have any pencils or pens. this is nearly also the case if you get what they called a "privilege freeze", where they gave you no privileges for 7 days, freeze was supposed to be for kids who were physically aggressive or self harmed but they instead gave them out because kids either talked to staff in a tone they didn't like or didn't get out of the shower quick enough. i got a freeze for talking to a staff member about a complaint i had with the program. said complaint was that we actually did nothing worthy of treatment. all we did was watch movies. i never went outside during my entire stay because they told me there was a "runaway risk". i also got threatened with freeze 2 times; one time because i didn't get out of the shower fast enough and the other time because i was looking at the lunch menu "too long" during visitation time in the cafeteria.

i was originally in the 2 west unit for physical aggression, but i was moved to 2 east my first day there.

i had a full-on breakdown because i was scared and in an unfamiliar environment. i asked for a time-out, which they were supposed to give, but instead one of the mhts there, who's name was ms. g, pulled me by the neck and hair.

i complained of feeling sick and feeling like i was about to barf. i had no appetite the first few days i was there, yet the staff laughed at me for barely eating anything. all the nurses gave me for my nausea was a pill that didn't even help. i actually did throw up, but the staff made me clean my puke up with a rag despite me feeling sick and dizzy.

i was put in solitary for 1 hour because i said "what?" to a mht when i did not understand something that they said. i had a full-on breakdown in that solitary room and the mht who sent me there, i believe her name was ms. acia (ay-see-uh), did not do anything but scroll through her phone for that hour.

in terms of communication, it was actually very good. you got a 10-minute long uncensored phone call every night. you were allowed to send mail. they had visitation in the cafeteria every day which lasted for about an hour and 30 minutes and it was uncensored and very nice.

we did barely any treatment or groups. we had a "goals group" every morning, the only therapy group i could go to was once every weekday. the kids did recreational therapy (rt) every weekday but only people off of freeze and precautions were able to go. we had bible studies once a week, but luckily that was optional. the only thing we did all day, outside of school, was watch movies. on one sunday we watched 9 movies (i counted!). you met with your therapist twice a week, once for individual session and once for a family session.

we could not have any personal effects in our room. only clothes and a bible. and despite being non-denominational, we were required to say a christian prayer every morning.

education was very good. mr. jeff was my teacher, he had a good sense of humor and was a cool guy. learning was on odysseyware at our own pace. overall i say the education quality was nice and it was in a way that i liked.
really bad memories from this place. definitely would not recommend it. not much therapy, felt more like a place of punishment rather than rehabilitation

my spouse recently had a cardiac catheterization here as well as several procedures in the past year. he has received world class care from people who seem very happy to work there and are proud of serving our veterans. i can't say enough good things about the staff and doctors as well as the beautiful new hospital. thank you for your exceptional service to veterans!

hospital is really nice and the people are very helpful but the cafeteria sucks very small nothing to choose from. i guess the management of saint vincents don't care for the guest and professionals to have a healthy meal.

an absolute horror show, travesty of medical care, and a lawsuit waiting to happen. 

my mom fell this week (fragile, dementia, history of stroke, and a hip replacement). i called 911 and on scene the paramedics asked which hospital we preferred- i chose mercy general as her pcp and records are all at dignity health. 

worst decision ever. 
how the hospital is run: 
a doctor saw my mom for a total of 1 minute at arrival and 30 seconds at exit. no supervision or accountability. lots of people here seemed "checked out" working in an untenable environment. 

medical assistants and one rn is on duty, one pa or doctor for what seemed to be 50 or more patients. there are lots of guys in green outfits doing, apparently, nothing that i noticed for the five hours we were there. my mom was parked on a gurney for the whole time in a busy hallway. people, patients, staff, gurneys, paramedics, security guards, and random people coming and going nonstop. 

she had imaging of her hip, elbow, and arm. there were good people doing the imaging. i repeated that her head hurt- mom chimed in- and then that was related to the doctor and a ct was ordered. too bad the doctor refused to talk to the patient and just felt  her bones for minute and didn't ask one question to her "patient" aka just a number.  props to the imaging team for maintaining a system and compassion for patients in a totally chaotic situation. 

she was offered a tylenol and glass of water. no updates on what was happening...i assumed a room would be provided eventually.  other patients parked in hallway, including a man and his wife- he begged to have someone help her use the restroom- for an hour. 

at about 8:30 pm the medical assistant popped by and said no broken bones, mom had to get up and prove she could walk before being released. i stepped in when mom got upright on the gurney and said she felt dizzy. 

medical assistant said she would have a chair behind mom as she walks. my dad was helping. honest to god, this was the plan. my mom fell, said she's dizzy, and they want her to walk in a busy hallway with people crashing around pell-mell. 

i spoke up loudly, said you need to get an orderly and she said, this is how we do it do you have a better suggestion? 

this could have been solved by having my mom move to a room- (literally across the hall an empty room with three hospital beds) for a safe environment for a trial run. 

we worked with situation at hand with me guarding the hall like a pit bull behind mom and blocking people and gurneys from coming through....and dad ready to catch mom. and then medical assistant tells mom to get back to 
the gurney after a successful trial run. mom has lymphedema and her swollen legs would be hitting metal. i said no get a wheelchair. then a guy in green shows up. apparently ready to catch mom if she falls. thanks, perfect timing. 

so, end of story- doctor comes by for 30 seconds to tell us no broken bones and runs off, totally masked  to protect herself from coronavirus. brava. medical assistant turned out to be a nice person and she stood by us while my dad got car. she was smart and empathetic once she was freed from caring for 50 people simultaneously with no tangible support. 

literally the worst er i have ever been in. train wreck, third world care. danger. no info. a few decent people trying to do their best in a disaster scene. never again. they should close their doors if they can't serve patients and provide a baseline of medical care. our east sac family has been born cared for. and died at mercy for three generations. sadly, switching care to sutter asap. 

every person who walks out of these doors should get a t-shirt that says, "i survived mercy er."

suggestion: hire some nuns to get this place shipshape. someone needs to be slapping a ruler.

well , 9 mos after the incident with my mother at santa cruz hospital , a very good friend was brought to the emergency dept. . his experience was much  like the june event. the staff and md's in the ed are a disgrace. little to no communication between staff and patient no warm blankets for my friend who had the chills, long wait time to see the md even though only 3 other rooms were occupied, the ct tech was having trouble with the machine while talking on her personal phone about her dogs and what shouldd be cooked for dinner that  night. it was rude, unprofessional and gave the patient high anxiety.  he was admitted after not seeing a hospitalist, or a gastroenterologist. needless to say, after many hours there , he walked out , after signing his ama release form.  this hospital gets a negative 3 stars  again . never ever will i , or members of my family and friends , pass through those hospital doors.

brought my 5 year old son here last week not because he was experiencing cold symptoms but because he had also started wheezing when breathing and also vomiting. he had no fever but the wheezing concerned me because he has never had any issues with breathing or any asthma related issues. 
all the staff that helped were wonderful and friendly. 
they gave him some breathing treatments which really helped with the wheezing. they also did chest x-rays and tested for flu and strep. tests came back negative and x-rays looked fine. doctor said his lungs were reacting to something, possible allergy or asthma related, so he prescribed an asthma pump and a couple medications for nausea and his chest. 
came in at 3am, left around 7:30am. 

now almost a week later, my son woke up at 3:30am with a 104 fever that wouldn't go down. brought him in at 7:30am, was brought in immediately which was surprising to me because usually they make us wait a bit. doctor originally was going to just test again for flu because my boyfriend recently tested positive for it, and give him a bunch of fluids because his heart rate was out the roof. they also did some blood work. while we were waiting for results, he started screaming, crying, and clutching his stomach. this went on for 30 minutes before they were able to give him motrin which helped with the pain and fever. at this point i believe his temp was 102, heart rate still above 150. he also started vomiting a lot. now this concerned the doctor more also because his blood work showed his white blood cell count was 24 and normally should be 8-10. she said that was showing that his body is trying to fight something off so something was wrong. because he was clutching the  right side of his stomach, they thought it was possibly his appendix so he went off for an ultrasound. they couldn't see his appendix because his bladder was full and he did not want to pee so the result was that the doctor thought he might've had appendicitis and we were transferred to hartford hospital because it's a dedicated children's hospital and if it was appendicitis, he would have to have surgery to remove his appendix. waterbury hospital does not have a pediatric department. 
we were transferred about noon and got to hartford hospital about 12:30. 
once there we were seen immediately by a bunch of staff. he got an ultrasound done and appendix looked normal. they did more x-rays on him and turns out he had pneumonia (they could see it in the x-rays and doctor says it explains his fever, and abdominal pain). they diagnosed him in about an hour and a half, and we were out by 3. 
so....he had pneumonia since the first er trip we took but instead he was diagnosed with asthma and this second trip was diagnosed with possible appendicitis scaring me to death! why couldn't they see the pneumonia when they did the x-rays the first time from the very beginning?! extremely frustrating!!

still, the staff that helped me during this time were all great, friendly, and treated my son very well. 
i took 1 star off because of the wait time that always seems to be a problem and another star because of the improper diagnoses, not once but twice. 
i should've known though because when i came here for myself awhile back, they tested me for strep and although it came back negative, i was still prescribed strep medication for whatever reason. unbelievable! 
anyways, if you're coming here for your children, know they do not have a pediatric department so either go to saint mary's or i highly recommend hartford's children emergency department, worth the longer drive trust me!!!!

the nurses and direct care staff at austin oaks are very caring and compassionate. they were kind to him, no matter how disregulated he became. they crafted a very unique program to address his special needs, even arranging for extra staff to insure safety.
the clinical director,  molly wang, was amazing. she really went out of her way to insure that our son would have the ongoing support he needed after his hospitalization.... meeting with us,  calling other providers, advocating for him to be able to stay long enough to stabilize. she was very approachable and supportive, and we truly felt like she was part of our team. our only concern was with the psychiatrist,  who made drastic changes to our son's medication regimen without talking to us (or his longterm psychiatrist, even though we'd signed a release). the med changes really exacerbated the problems that had brought him to the hospital in the first place. fortunately,  that psychiatrist is no longer with the inpatient division, and our son's doctors are working to get his medications back into the therapeutic range.
if you must seek out acute psychiatric care for your child, know that they will be well cared for at austin oaks.

the blake medical center has an in-house hospital rehab center located on the 2nd floor of blake hospital, a dedicated wing for rehab patients. my dad went there after an eleven-day hospitalization stay for a punctured lung and broken ribs. at age 96, he wanted to be at home rather than rehab, but as he began his rehab stay of 8 days, he realized this rigorous program was doing him a world of good! he came away from the experience more knowledgeable and stronger than ever!

if patients get approval from the nursing staff, they can ride the elevator to the courtyard with family! a little fresh air and green space is healthy for healing! the staff on the rehab floor is kind to the whole family and involves them in the healing process, whenever possible. 

nurses and doctors quickly attend to patients' needs and, importantly, are sympathetic and understanding to their well-being. my dad's rehab was a four-piece collaboration between nursing and doctor care, physical therapy, occupational therapy, and patient's desire to get better. dad's therapy was rigorous - 4 times a day. we could observe his therapy sessions, which we did a couple of times. the ot and pt gave us helpful hints to use at home. he gained great confidence and strength during his rehab stay!

menu choices are very appealing and arrive to the patient on time - fresh and hot! he enjoyed his meals very much, especially the chocolate cake and the carrot cake. 

this rehab hospital is outstanding in every way! the rehab program couldn't be any better!!!

while there i was given a prn anti-anxiety medication with known and severe possible interactions with my anti-depressants that could have caused significant medical issues. i was not given a suicide risk assessment until almost 48 hours later, despite the fact that it is required more frequently - the discharge paperwork was signed and dated before my only sra was completed.

because my service animal was not present with me, i had a full autistic meltdown due to violations of my personal space, was frequently touched in areas that have nerve damage and are very painful for me to be touched at, and engaged in self-harmful stimming because i was not alerted to what i was doing so i could stop. i ended up with multiple additional scars on my arms from scratching at my skin (something which i do without noticing when i am overstimulated or stressed). no nurse or provider noticed or did anything to stop it, or provide first aid after the fact.

the group sessions were a load of hot garbage. they primarily focused on things which patients had no way of implementing, such as significant dietary changes or exercising out of doors. additionally, a lot of the information was significantly out of date or incorrect, such as claiming that depression can be caused by caffeine (there is no known link between the two), or that all carbohydrates make depression worse ( refined carbohydrates, such as white bread and soda, have been linked to depression in post-menopausal women, but unrefined carbs are not, and there's no known link between unrefined carbs and depression when eaten in a balanced diet). ironically, a majority of meals offered were high in processed sugars and refined carbs - deep-fried shrimp and preserved peaches, fried chicken tenders, sugary cereals, etc. as a person who needs to eat a fairly strictly balanced diet due to physical health issues, it made my overall health worse as well.

there were exposed cords in several areas, and the staff handling medication dispensation didn't pay attention to allergies. i have an anaphylactic reaction to ibuprofen, and was offered... ibuprofen for pain caused by a severely sprained ankle. if i had been actively suicidal i not only could have killed myself in this hospital, but would have been actively aided by the staff, since they openly admitted to not having any epipens or albuterol inhalants on site when i pointed out that they offered a medication that could kill me.

despite purportedly being a "voluntary" admission, i was denied the ability to check myself out, which is considered a felony charge for false imprisonment. i was threatened repeatedly with violence by the "therapist" present during a twenty minute meeting, and he lacked any relevant knowledge on autism, trauma, and comorbid issues which affected previous treatments i have received. he attempted to switch my anti-depressant to lexapro, ignoring the information provided in my medical charts which clearly state that lexapro was not an effective medication for my depression and that it had severe side-effects on me.

i was discharged after 48 hours, with no changes to my medication, no useful resources, three open wounds, and new additional trauma to add to my pile from being sexually harassed, threatened repeatedly with violence, being forcibly taken from my medical equipment, and being strip-searched.

unfortunately i cannot directly sue prairie st. john's for this because they have a disclaimer present on intake paperwork which i was coerced into signing, again under threat of violence. this is the last place anyone who needs any form of help should be sent to. they are a disgrace to the mental health field, and they have no appropriate oversight or checks in place to prevent medical malpractice or abuse of patients.

review:

so, if you can just go elsewhere for your meds.

if this is a surgery, you'll first talk to a worker about finances. they have a federal assistance program which helps a lot even after insurance.

you wait in their lobby, then you're taken to the surgery waiting room. i was then called into the area with the bed and iv stuff. the nurse was super nice and you didn't even have to lift a finger! i hate getting ivs done, but the nurse was super accommodating and helped me feel less scared. during this time you're asked questions, the doctor come in and see you, they explain everything to you.

then you're wheeled off and into surgery!

this review is based on several visits to gsh.  

parking can be extremely difficult here at times during the day.  valet service is available but is frequently closed when the parking garage gets full.  i have had the best luck getting a parking spot in the early morning hours or after 8:00pm.

emergency room can have really long wait times periodically.  getting in there in the morning or after the evening rush seems to be the best way to avoid the long times. 

overall, i found the doctors, nurses and staff to be friendly and helpful.  

the rooms are very nice and well kept in the new part of the hospital (dally tower).  some of the older parts of the hospital are in serious need of renovation or replacement.  it can also be a challenge to find your way to some of the rooms located within the old portions of the hospital.  

overall cleanliness seems average.  i did notice the waiting room chairs looked well worn / stained in some areas of the hospital.  i also observed the hospital wheelchairs transporting patient after patient without anyone stopping to even wipe down the armrests once in a while.

this hospital caters to military active duty, family members and retirees and their dependents. it's a very big facility. the staff is really friendly. they have ambassadors that help guide you in case you're not sure where you're going or if you don't have the time to figure out where you are to get to your appointment on time. although, they're only there during regular hours. i think if you come after 6pm. it's basically just the specialty clinics and er that's open. it's essentially a ghost town so make sure you know exactly where you're going. i had to walk around the whole building trying to find the radiology/mri clinic. there's a self-serve check-in process in this specific clinic (sort of) and you have to call to make sure they know you're there. otherwise, you'll be waiting around and they're not going to come out unless you call them. 

i also came in here to get some blood drawn. the staff at the front desk weren't so helpful- kind of rude to be honest. they know people are waiting to get checked in but they're just sitting around lounging and chatting up with each other. 

they have a nice open area in the main entrance with a large staircase that takes you to the second floor. there's a grand piano by the lobby that sometimes gets played by one of the staff members. their pharmacy is huge but the wait is just as bad anywhere so be prepared if you're going to pick up your medications here. they also have a chapel and offer services to the staff and patients alike.

they have a dining area in the top floor where you can get decent lunch at a very low cost. there's also a starbucks and a small convenient store where you can get drinks and snacks and maybe pick up some last minute card, flowers or gifts. 

all in all - i think the staff could be better. maybe their supervisors/administrators can walk around more and see how their staff are treating the patients. have a better feedback system. i want to give them more stars because they cater to the military, but honestly, they could do better.

is the food good? not at all. are the staff always amazing? no, and some staff members were absolutely terrible. is the schedule sometimes annoying? yeah. but i couldn't possibly give it less than 5 stars because of the results.

i had an accident last year where i lost my fingertip, it got caught in a door that the wind blew shut which removed the tip from the base of the fingernail. i went to this hospital, it was around midnight, and i had to wait 3 hours to see the doctor although no one appeared to be there. it was extremely painful and psychologically traumatic, yet the staff didn't seem very caring, and it took around 2 hours to get a shot for the excruciating pain. the shot was something called hydromorphone, formulated to not get people "high".
if ever there was a time a person needs to be a little bit high, it's when you have had a fingertip torn off. i have no history of drug abuse, though i understand we are all suspects due to the drug problem.
3 hours after i got there, i was given a shot in my hand which finally relieved the pain, if briefly, so the doctor could look at it and clean it up. after that a wonderful nurse wrapped it, and showed me how to do so which turned out to be a real blessing, as it had turned out my insurance had been cancelled shortly before though i didn't know, and i was not able to see a doctor afterwards because of that.
the doctor came in again, and gave me 2 percocet pills to take home with me (that helped much more than the worthless shot) so i could have something to take before seeing a doctor the next day, though as i soon found out, due to a glitch in my insurance took 3 weeks for one to see me. thank god a friend had some kratom which she gave me, and between that and tylenol pills i was able to somewhat manage the pain.
we should not be punished because of the drug issue, especially with a chopped off fingertip, the pain issue should have been addressed better. 
the 2 stars i do give was for the very nice nurse who bandaged my finger and showed me how to do it and what materials i needed.
i don't understand why i had to wait hours though when no one was there.
if i have an emergency again, i will try to have it taken care of in olympia instead if possible.

i went to er and got triaged for allergic reaction and was sent back to waiting room. i was never seen by a doctor or called back into the room to get seen/treated. i took a benadryl prior to going to er and waited an hour and half and my symptoms got better, so i told the front that i was better and the triage nurse said it was okay for me to go since i felt better. i did not want to waste anyone's time since my symptoms had gone away. they still sent me a bill of $212. i spoke to someone at er and supervisor says that's how much they charge for being triaged and if i did see a doctor that would cost $1200 so $212 is nothing per person i spoke to. i work at kaiser and patient care is our number 1 priority. our providers at kaiser are affiliated with vhc, i told the providers i work with about what happened, and they agree that is not right. i referred my entire family and friends to vhc, and i even talk to my patients about how great vhc is. i am shocked and sad how money hungry vhc is. the staff who triaged me was not friendly either. i am not going to refer anyone to vhc anymore.

i've had to go to their emergency room for 15 years and the staff has always been knowledgeable and considerate.  i live in shirley and it is the closest hospital.  the only complaint that i have about those visits (bladder infections, migraines, or asthma attack) is once by ambulance with no way to get home.  i've used them for x-rays to avoid going over to leominster hospital.  still, every time i've been to nashoba late at night there are a lot of drug overdose cases that come in.  i didn't know that we had that much of a drug crises around here, but we do.  with all that going on they do their job.  i have no complaints about any other procedures, such as pt, medical records.  everyone is courteous.

so i found out the day after christmas that the baby that i'm pregnant with had no heartbeat.  while i tried to naturally induce the miscarriage my body wasn't cooperating and the thought of going to bed with a corpse inside of me was tearing me apart. so i called nashoba valley to ask if they had misoprostal available. i couldn't remember the name so i asked for the "abortion pill.   the woman on the phone, directly after telling her that i just learned that my baby was dead, responded to me in the absolute most condescending tone as if she was annoyed by my stupid question. "uuuuuh no..... those pills are for after you have sex. that won't do anything."       

that level of beside manner alone was enough for me.    i don't see myself ever walking in their if they are that inconsiderate and rude. after i explained to her that i was not looking for plan b but something to induce contractions so i could actually complete miscarrying she  suggested planned parenthood.      fine. however, she didn't handle that call right -at all-.
this hospital should be closed  all about the money  medicaid should review it drs are not qualified

i am incredibly disappointed in the "care" my husband is/isn't receiving. thank god i'm here through the night to take care of him and get him to the bathroom or he'd have been on his own, no vitals being taken, his fever spiked through the night to 104! i had to go find a nurse to tell them he was burning up. we've seen 3 different doctors, none of whom talked or communicated between them, i have to retell his heath history and current issues every time, to every person that comes in the room. his regular specialist still hasn't been contacted or consulted and i'm ready to just pack him up and walk out the front doors and drive to the university of utah. i earned a helluva paycheck here, and they'll want 6 months worth of my husbands paycheck for this unwelcome hospital stay. and just a side note i am not an asshole! i totally get nurses can be overworked and most of them are absolutely amazing, my point is, that has not been my experience at this hospital. one star  . and that star is only because i can make a badass pot of coffee or hot chocky due to the fact they provide a small galley kitchen for others like me taking care of their loved ones.. so.. ya. that's cool. but not cool enough to make up for poor care of my sick loved one. one star. do not recommend.

i would give zero stars if that were an option.  dr. agarwal is absolutely the most arrogant physician i've ever seen, and i have ulcerative colitis, and advanced stage primary sclerosing cholangitis, so i've seen a lot of doctors.  i've been told by my gastroenterologist that when i'm having a flare up, i need to go to the er to be checked out, as my disease can be fatal.  i've been made to feel like i'm a med seeker (addict), and i'm far from that!!!!  i received a letter from the higher ups in that hospital, and was basically told to pound sand.  i know i'm not the only person to give poor reviews to dr. agarwal, because i've seen another, and their story was like mine.  do not go to this hospital.  they don't care about their patients!!!

i just went to the er for migraine treatment. we pre registered online and when we arrived they brought me right in. they already had a quiet, dark room waiting for me. the nurse quietly put in my iv on the first stick, i barely felt it and he was so quick even though i am generally a hard stick for an iv and especially when i am dehydrated from throwing up. they got my fluids up and running before the doctor came in. i told him what actually works for my migraines and even though it's a new and fairly 
controversial treatment he immediately agreed to do it to get me help. 15 minutes later my infusion was running, the nurse and intake coordinator, and doctor were all very compassionate and cared about my well being. 
it was clean and quiet and a quick experience. in 25 years of horrible migraines and nightmare er visits this was by far the easiest most efficient hospital i've ever dealt with and i was in and out and very well treated in under 2.5 hours. i was impressed to say the very least. hopefully i won't have to go back again but if i do i know where i'd go,
fac_name: Ascension NE Wisconsin St. Elizabeth Hospital

review: got here around 11:20 am was brought back very fast but i'm still here at 4:06 pm waited 2 hrs for ultrasound now waiting for results. i had dr fisherman he was great but nurse didn't wear gloves to put my iv in or take blood and i'm a nursing student so i was just thinking everything she did wrong

one of the worst er experiences i've encountered.  the place is very disorganized and short staffed.  do your health a favor and go to real emergency room like virtua.  this place should be shut down.  i ended up walking out after waiting 4 hours in a bed to be treated or helped.  two days later they follow up with a phone call to talk about my experience.  all they could say, in a snarky tone no less, was "sorry for the wait."

i came to visit a family friend who had just been admitted and needed rehabilitation.  the place is beautiful.  it is very state of the art and the staff is welcoming, professional and attentive.  during my visit, the staff was always readily available to the patients and checked in every half hour or so.  

they provide a wide variety of activities for the patients which include music, trivia and arts and crafts which is a major plus because one can get board while recuperating without any capability of getting up and moving around by themselves.  also, the volunteers *huge shout to the volunteers* because not everyone is fortunate to have family, loved ones and friends to visit.  there were a group of them that went room to room to check on the patients.  

some actually came to collect the patients to get them out of their beds for a while.  a very crucial part of healing and rehabilitation is support from other caring individuals.  

this rehab facility is exemplary and the staff takes pride in providing care which is demonstrated in their bedside manner.  highly recommended facility.  i feel comfortable and confident that my family friend is getting the best care and that she will recover nicely.

this is specifically for the ct room. i've been to this location a couple of times and i can say that this is the worst location for nyp.
when i called to make an appointment last week, no one picked up. after repeated attempts throughout the day, some guy finally picked up and was extremely disorganized.  

it's a freaking maze here while the other locations are straight forward. had an appointment at 8am, after filling out the paperwork, they didn't provide the oral contrast until 9am, with the second serving at 10am. this whole time that i was waiting, they could've provided this. the ct scan took only a few minutes, yet i didn't leave until 12:30 pm. while the staff is friendly and in good spirits, this is an completely unacceptable wait time. i don't recommend this location at all.

while once trying to fly out of new york city to las vegas (don't ask), i cut my foot in a delta terminal at jfk. 

i was bleeding pretty bad. delta/jfk didn't have the proper emergency kit available (no offense to them -- this was ancient history -- way back in 2017). an american ambulance would of cost over $1000, so a cabbie kindly dropped me off here. 

aghast, i found myself lying on a stained mattress (think all body fluids) to simply be *prescribed* aleve and then charged bankrupting american emergency room fees with insurance. i would of been ok with brush-off service, because in all fairness, in true triage, i was not dying -- but wow someone obviously died on the mattress right before me that i was put on...it was horrifying to be placed on top of so many stains. it must of been more horrifying for the person before me. 

until it is 1863 again, i am not returning.

this review is for "advanced womens imaging" who could've resulted in me having a stillbirth! oh my god! 

i was referred to here by a list from a private ob who doesn't do sono's in office. i thought it made sense to come because i am delivering here. 85% of their patients are from the clinic across the street and yes expect to wait 3 hours at least from your appointment time, there werent even chairs they were so over booked and we had women who were over 30 something weeks pregnant standing. i had my first sonogram here at almost 13 weeks. both abdominal and transvaginal.

my ob doesn't order many sonograms, but i told him i'd feel comfortable having one once a month to be safe. he said sure and wrote a bunch of referrals at once. 3 weeks later i called to make an appointment. they tried telling me they'll make my 20 week anatomy.. no, i said- i have a referral for one before that. they were not understanding the clear  and thorough  referral and said they  can't help me. also they'll randomly ask in the middle of the phone call if you're pregnant right after asking your due date... wtf? 

well i trusted my gut. at 16 weeks i paid out of network for a high risk specialist instead. within minutes they detected multiple blood clots in the  placenta that have been forming since day 1,  beyond 5cm, almost 7! i am now on blood thinner shots everyday, and me- a 21yo, 135ib, healthy first time mom is high risk. they kept asking who did the first sonogram and how wasn't this seen? 

negligence. avoid. im now 18 weeks and so thankful i stopped coming here. im
so scared to deliver here now. the only person who's  "advanced" in this center is sydney the genetic counselor. she's an absolute peach, please see her if you're considering genetic testing. so kind and informative.

this hospital is amazing!!! the staff is friendly, attentive and available with advice and updates. it was really terrifying to have my mother hospitalized but they really did save her life and i'll always be grateful!!!

went because urgent care referred me due to abdominal pain.  i don't know why the fuck they didn't get around to asking my insurance for the money until november when i was there in august, but thanks for ruining my life, fuckers.  i was just starting to get on top of shit.  now there's this bill and you know what, i'm not just done with this shit, i'm done with this country.  next time i'll just die in the most inconvenient way possible (in public, loudly, making a scene) or go to a more civilized country and be a pain in the ass if i die from my appendix exploding on the way overseas.  get your fucking shit together.  also i had to bring my own blankets, and fuck those fluorescent lights.  people who are sick need sleep, not that shit.  also the wait time was stupid.

if you're hit by a car, be prepared to use bed pans and to receive zero help. but it gets better. 
if you're on medications, be prepared for medications that can cause serious interactions to be prescribed. out of concern for your liver, kidneys, and life, be prepared for no new medications to control the pain to be prescribed. 
prescription errors have occurred more than once during my visits to this hospital. 
on occasion, if your condition does not allow you to move, expect wait times up to 8 minutes to sit in your own urine and/or feces for someone to help you move the bedpan, after which, you have to figure out a way to clean yourself because an absorbent pad is placed under you without any concept of cleanliness. i asked the nurse if diaper rash was the goal. 
my primary care physician said at this point, at the rate their emergency room is declining, if i return here, he's expecting a call stating i passed away.

after she was sent home in excruciating pain, it was discovered that my mom had sepsis, so she was called back in. since then, she's had surgery with subsequent uncontrolled pain, been patronized and treated like a drug-seeker. even given valium thru her iv without her consent, probably because she was being a "nuisance" with all her excruciating pain noise.
the communication is poor, and despite loose-lipped promises, the treatment has not progressed toward something that actually works. 
in addition. nobody seems to be able to figure out what is going on with her, so they just want to send her to a nursing home, even though she is not stable. 
and where are all the doctors???

i am guilty of declaring that "no country quack doctor or quack hospital in these damn hills is ever going to get me to have surgery!"  well, i just spent three days recuperating from extensive knee surgery, where the doc reconstructed my acl ligament, fixed up my battered meniscus, and other needed improvements--no, i didn't get a bionic knee . . . yet.  every person i dealt, from dr. rogalski, to all the nurses, and everybody in physical therapy were top notch, out-of-this-world, exceptional people and professionals.  when it comes to the staff at this place, know right away that you will be taken care of in every way possible.  everybody explained all the details, kept watch on me, and worked with me, even though i was in miserable pain, and really not the wonderful, nice man i am.  they were not only professional, but every person was personable as well.  they say laughter is the best medicine, and if true, there is no better place to receive excellent, personal care.  i was constantly enjoying the presence of the staff at mark twain--especially the nurses.  now i ask myself, "why the hell did it take me so long to trust these people?"  i give the staff at dignity health's mark twain medical center 8 stars if possible.  when it comes to dignity health, the corporation that runs mark twain medical center, i have to give them 2 stars, maybe one.  corporate medicine has reached a new low--i mean, i have to laugh at dignity health because they have gone so low, truly, there is nothing to do but laugh . . .  they no longer serve their patients juice . . . you know, the little boxes of apple juice, or little cranberry juices, that remind you that you are in the hospital, are no longer . . . i guess in a desperate effort to save money, or to keep the staff engaged in serious work, the juices are no more.  i did raise a small fit, and i was assured that i would get my juice fix, if i asked.  they would have to go all the way to the kitchen though, but my request would be answered positively. again, that is how wonderful the staff is--it has little to do with the corporation running the place.  you want juice?  you best stop off at save mart and bring your own . . . i guess that the $27,000 hospital bill just isn't big enough to cover the costs of those nifty little juice packs . . . once again, corporate america takes a dump, a small one nonetheless, but it still smells, into the lap of the unaware american consumer.  i might add, that the little ice cream desserts, and the pudding cups as well, are no longer.  those little things are what keep me sane while i am in the hospital!  i quickly called a dear friend, who stopped at save mart, loaded up with the necessities to keep my visit sane, and she brought them to the hospital.  that made my stay worth it.  so . . . the staff gets five stars, the company gets a pathetic one star for being foolish.  i am certain that the person who made this new cost-saving discovery is some nerdy millenial, still living at home, who walks around pulling up their pants like they are now the big-wig of a corporation!  all i can say is, "i sure didn't see my bill decrease with that creature comfort of juice missing from my stay . . ."  it just goes to prove that corporations--even medical ones, are all about the penny-profit they can squeeze from each and every one of us.  what's next?  byos?  bring your own syringe? dignity health has no dignity, probably never did, but in 20 years from now, they will declare, "we were the first to do away with juice in hospitals!"  let's give them this win!  even corporate holes need to feel special at times . . .

this is an embarrassment to the healthcare community. 5 hours in the emergency room before any treatment began is completely unacceptable. this is a non-profit and teaching hospital which is not a bad unless you get what we have here, inefficiency and ineffectiveness. it's sad that the az dept of health services doesn't have a standard for er patient care that involves time to begin treatment. 
as many other reviews state, unless you are bleeding externally, you will wait in the er for as long as it will take you to drive to another facility where you'll inevitably receive better care.
since this is the only er in yuma you may be stuck going to it and if that is the case, call an ambulance as that is the only way you won't be waiting more than 2 hours for treatment to begin.

if you have the flu go ahead and go there but for anything serious please do find someplace else. go to phoenix or san diego.

this place is the biggest joke. it is staffed by walk in clinic dr.s. and any dr worth his shit never stays. unfortunately for yuma residents. other hospitals have tried to come here and somehow magically they go away....hmmmm.

plenty of winter visitor's are leaving here because of the poor health care. don't just take it from me.....read the reviews.
..."2 family members lost with no explanation"
..."worst care in 60 years"
....incompetent, incompetent incompetent!

yrmc, medical staff that can't make it elsewhere and the costs, well like i said read the reviews.

dr thomas shields (npi: 1760400873) in the er had to staple a simple head laceration after  sustaining an injury at the dunes... sloppy, non-sterile, didn't even clean the area before or after the 12 staples he rammed in.  then they take ct scans, multiple other xrays and tell me "...sorry but we don't have a radiologist to read your films....". this is a level four "trauma center"; patients need to know that if yuma regional medical center is a level 4, than siri and alexa would likely be better surgeons or er docs than this place has. to be clear... this in my personal opinion is nothing more than a overpriced primary care  clinic commonly found in mexico.

absolutely the worst. i came in on a saturday morning following a fall the previous day. the doctor came in and his first question was if i had been drinking. i told him i had the night before, but nothing that morning. he replied he'd been doing this for 20 years and he could smell it. after ordering x-rays, he told me someone would be in to clean the wound on my hand. the x-rays came back negative, but i'm not convinced they were read properly. the nurse had me wash my wound with soap and water. i asked if i should wrap my writs and she told me whatever i wanted to do. the doctor never returned. i asked for something for the pain. she promised tylenol, but never brought it. shameful!

absolutely the worse service ive ever experienced!! my daughter was very ill, vomiting blood, abdominal pain level of an 8 and the sat us in the waiting from from close to 5 hours, in the meantime, she still vomiting blood & severe abdominal pain! all the took was a ua & a basic cbc/cmp and back to the wating room. i know it gets busy but c'mon...they treated her like she came in for toe pain !! its sad that this is all yuma has for a hospital!

we visit every year and i have been to this walk-in clinic 3 times, most recently a couple of weeks ago. this is the worst and i'm an rn who knows how it should work. they advertise "walk-ins welcome but don't have the staff to accommodate them. people sit in the waiting room for hours coughing and spreading whatever. on my second visit, i saw a sweet female pa or arnp named jennifer who was very good, but when i went back the next week to say the abo i was on was making me very short of breath - omg - two hours just to get in back where i waited again behind a curtain listening to the staff joke and laugh and blah blah blah.  the black male pa was flirting with a nurse, discussing whether or not she should put her car in an upcoming car show or not and on and on....and on! guess what all you people sitting around the desk - we in the cubbys behind the curtains can hear you in spite of the stupid out-of-sync "ocean wave" tapes in each one. when the nurse came in for vitals i commented that they were very loud, she agreed and looked disgusted. when the pa finally came in, all he said was to stop the antibiotic i was on and "see."  i'd already done that! i asked if i shouldn't start something else because i'd only been on it for 3 days...again ""wait and see." i ended up going over to the foothills clinic on fortuna where i saw john smock and got another prescription and also sent my husband the next week where he got excellent care. don't waste your time at the foothills yrmc walk-in clinic...go across the highway to the foothills clinic instead.

what a great place to bring someone with heart issues. i had to bring my husband to the emergency room. he was having trouble breathing. first, they had valet services. this was such a blessing . once we arrived at the emergency room. i felt such a sense of relief knowing he was being checked out completely. with the most qualified, professional staff.

our family would like to thank the incredible staff at mease countryside. the care we received for our family member was beyond what we could have ever asked for. we would specifically like to thank the staff at the ccu for ensuring we were comfortable and that our family was informed and supported.

i had ct scan or xrays that determined my ab pain was from appendicitis.  during the service, i asked if the bill is for everything and they said yes.  then i receive a separate bill for the reading of the xrays!  i called mease and they say sorry we didn't tell you that there would be another charge for the reading of the xrays offsite!  i said the xrays were read right there within 20 minutes, that  is why i went to the emergency room. they apologized again and wiped their hands clean of their lies. thanks again mease countryside.

was scheduled for colonoscopy.   received an estimate of 4700 from hospital saying i was in insured called them gave my  insurance info 3 times.   they assured me that it was taken care of.   did my prep (which is not fun) went to register again at hospital and waited an hour for them to tell me that they don't take my insurance.   that i could pay them 5500 before procedure.  beware stay away!!!!!

i did a review a couple of year's ago and clobbered them.in the beginning of january i was taken here by ambulance---what a difference.the er was busy but ok the staff were friendly and attentive.  my room was clean and nice  the staff was very friendly and knew their stuff. the food was good. it was noisy only 1nite because of a new patient.  my feelings about this hospital have changed drastically

did you realize that you could be charged $6000 for having a baby there even with insurance but if you don't have insurance they'll charge you $2000 less?  that is what mease countryside is trying to do to us right now.  that they would charge through our insurance company $2000+ more than they would charge a person without insurance seems like insurance fraud on their end.  we've already tried discussing this with cynde in their billing department and they were no help at all.

i also forgot to mention nurse gabby. how rude she was, how she ignored me. laughed in my faced. turned around and spoke badly and mocked me to her co workers to get a laugh out of them , refused to get me food when i was here from 6pm-4am. how i had to scream to get a sandwich. i was just attacked in the street... choked out until i was unconscious and beat up. this is how you treat me nurse gabby?!?? patient relations will hear about it all tomorrow. your supervisor already did. 

edit: i went in at around 6pm. i just got discharged. it's now 5:23am. that's fxcking sick


disgusting. staff is rude. you can hear the nurses / doctors fighting with each other . they stack up patients right on top of each other. now as i'm typing this 2 nurses are fighting over the schedule , one nurse is mine and she was supposed to bring me food about 1.5 hours ago. after making an extremely loud outburst i was brought food within seconds. funny how that worked. when you ask how much longer they tell you "no time frame were busy" or just don't answer you at all. i asked a short haired african american with glasses where the bathroom was and she just looked at me like i was crazy. i asked her if i was maybe invisible ?!? she laughed in my face and then joked with the other "nurses" i found the bathroom on my own. i will never ever ever come her again. i would never send my worst enemy here . who is the director . there is so much malpractice going on . i experienced it myself, already called my lawyer and he is looking into it.  you call this a hospital ?!? this should be called a funeral home!!! before they get to you you will be dead !!!

i'd give this place 0 stars if possible. the wait times are ridiculous. they range in time from 3 to 5 hrs. i was just there 2 weeks ago for 5 hrs. also, they keep messing up the appointments. the call center & the medical staff give you different info. i once waited for abt 3 hrs for the doctor to just fill out my med form but it was 4:30 by then & i was told that the doctor was leaving & i had to return the next day just to pick up my form again. 

last time i went, i had 2 appointments. i had 1 at 9am which i was told was actually at 11am for some reason i don't know. the 2nd 1 was at 10. so, i went to the 10am apt 1st & waited 3hrs to see the med assistant.

for the other apt, i just needed to get a vaccine & bloodwork done for more med forms. even though i waited for 2hrs to see a doctor, i was told i'd have to come in another day for bloodwork. in total, i waited 5 hrs. i was there before 9:30am & i left at 2:30pm.

don't even bother with this hospital. just go to a doctor's office instead. its a nightmare in there.

i called the hospital twice for a doctor's note. they transferred me to 6 different depts & an invalid #. the 2nd time, i got transferred 3 times until they transferred me to ambulatory care where it was just voicemail & i had to hang up. so, i went in after work again to tell them i need a note. i was told a day later i'd have to pick up the note. they cant fax or email it as i requested. i was told i can come in during the weekend to pick it up. i went in today, sunday, & adult primary care is closed. apparently, they're only open weekdays said the guy at the front desk of the main entrance.

just don't go here. nothing is good about this place! 
spent 9 hours in the emergency room just to see a nurse!  and on top of that they give you a dirty bloody bed, have drunks smelling like crap next to you peeing on themselves, throwing up and acting like dumbasses. been to many other er's never seen something like this place! first and last time!!!!

unresponsibility, unprofessional ... just push patients go around for weeks, no official paper document about medical record, no direction, no take care ... i don't receive what i need. i really don't want to come here again. it waste of my money if i have to pay for this stuff

this is the worst hospital i've ever been to. my cousin was admitted and was only seen by the doctor after many hours. been in the e.r for two days because there was no bed and finally got a bed and when we got up there, it wasn't even ready. he was told that he will be getting surgery the next morning and not to eat anything after 12 am. but guess what, they left him hanging about the surgery and told us in the evening that he'll be getting the surgery next day. my cousin did not eat for 18 hours and they didn't even mention about the surgery postpone. i had to ask them for meal otherwise they were not going to give him at all. 
the staffs are rude and doesn't care about the patients at all.

wait time is ridiculously long even if you have an appointment i've been trying my hardest to get my appointment locations switched it sucks i have to come all the way here for a sonagram and then have to wait almost two hours to even get called. i mean this is really ridiculous i would not recommend this hospital it's extremely big and very easy to get lost, not many people around to help you find your way then when your waiting to get seen the people at the front desk act like they don't know that you've been waiting forever or maybe they just don't care i'm so fed up with this place!

needed to be seen quickly and went to the expresscare at elmhurst. it was a great experience - fast care and a friendly doctor who made me feel at ease (i'm usually incredibly squeamish when it comes to anything clinical!). thank you dr. rabinovich! marisol at the front desk made the process easy and made sure my regular primary care doctor was informed of my visit. highly recommend if you need to be seen fast and are looking for an easy process with good care.

fuck this place and all the staff that abused me when i was younger. they treat people with anxiety disorders like utter shit and force you into a piss smelled room and call you a liar. fuck this place i though i was going to die in there.

father in law was treated here, nurses and doctors were all great! thank you dr. kira xie and the nurses in 4a for taking such good care of him.  also thanks so much to the trauma team day and night team... you made sure everything go smoothly!

i've had my double jaw surgery done here. dr. montazem, dr. avi, dr. akbari, and dr. schiff did an amazing job. they took care of me and monitored my healing progress consistently. the nurses at the icu were very patient and attentive during my stay, and i can't thank them enough for their hardwork.

my dad was transferred to this hospital for their acute rehab. i was told by their medical team that they're the stroke center for this area. what a joke! neurologist were never involved. we never had a family meeting or discussion of dad's care plan & his medication regimen, and when i asked, dr im says i'm putting alot if stress on my dad & i had to be very patient as its a slow recovery. there's one nurse that touches our heart, his name is n jean joseph, he's so caring, gentle & thoughtful, he makes sure dad is clean & comfortable, he always assist w/ dad's transfer from bed to wheelchair even when he's not dad's nurse! he deserves a 5
the physical therapist & occupational therapist were all awesome, specially ate bernie (ot) & maria b (pt tech). maria b is so caring & helpful, she made our stay tolerable. ate bernie explains to us what & why she's doing certain exercises & how she's trying to activate/retrain the brain/muscles. 10 days later, some regional director, i think its dr nori, she came & basically saying  its time for dad to transfer to sub-acute rehab since he's not improving & insurance wont be paying if he continues to stay. my whole family takes turn staying w/ dad everyday, we never saw any medical team doing an assessment on dad. they came  looking at their papers & say, "ok, no change" then walk away, i have to ask questions very quickly & most if their answers are "i have to look at the chart or computer, i will update you later" 60% of the time they dont come back!!

the girl went through the list - name, birthday, address, emergency contact, etc. none of the information that they had on file was what i had filled out and we didn't recognize anything...

question #2: is it not protocol to ask the patients for their birthday and then the patient provides it? this girl was literally reading off what was on file, and each item we had no idea where that information was coming from. they had the wrong address, wrong birthday, we had never heard of the person that was the emergency contact. at no point during this initial confirmation of information did anyone ask him for his ssn, or i'm sure this would have been caught immediately. 

they took my boyfriend for a ct and he eventually returned. the doctor/pa returned to let us know that it didn't show any issues, that his gallbladder was contracted and nothing wrong with his pancreas (not shocking, ordered an expensive test for nothing without checking off all of the other things that it could be first). he would get us set up to be discharged. he also made some kind of comment that my boyfriend had been to the er back in 2015, which my boyfriend has never been there. 

while we continued to wait and i was holding my boyfriend's hand, at that point i noticed that the birthday on his wristband was incorrect. and that was when it clicked in my head that they 100% had some other patient's information and did not have the right patient.

review:
i am writing this review as my father began his treatment recently at kentfield after having a difficult time at a different ltac facility. i have nothing but good things to say about kentfield. we have seen a huge progress since bringing him here. the nurses, cna's are incredibly attentive to his needs and make sure he is comfortable, clean, and well taken care of.
the physician staff is caring and transparent. we had a great chance to talk to his attending and understand his plan of care. 
when it comes to the various therapies they offer, each member of therapy is very rigorous and focuses hard on getting a patient better. my father who is incredibly drowsy and incoherent is still attended to daily by his therapists who strive to keep him going. even if he is conked out the entire day they still spend the time with him trying to at least get him moving involuntarily so he does not develop sores or lose muscle mass. 

kentfield overall is an amazing place and very appropriate for someone with a brain injury. i am very confident as of now, they saved my father from negligence at his other ltac facility, and i hope over time we can see some recovery with their honest and sincere efforts.

jerome, an rn in the ed who took great care of my mom and answered all my questions and taught me information. 
dr. walker in the ed who showed me such kindness and thoroughly explained every procedure before and during to help me keep calm.
