i had bad bronchitis this winter and due to my asthma, i ended up in the er twice. if you've never been unable to breathe, it's absolutely terrifying. this is the closest hospital to my house and i thought i was going to die so i went here. mistake. 

the doctor was some young woman who told me i was just having a panic attack and refused to help me. i am an adult who has had asthma since i was 8. i know exactly when i am having an asthma attack. i had to drive myself to the next closest hospital to get help. the next hospital gave me a steroid shot and i was fine in 10 minutes. they were horrified. i could have died during that drive because my bronchioles were completely closing up. 

other things i saw the doctor do: 
-yell at a woman going through withdrawals just because she asked for anti-nausea meds
-ignore an old man for so long that he peed his pants and the only one who did anything was the male nurse.

one thing this doctor did do for me was inspire me to move near a better hospital so thanks for that, i guess. don't go here if you can avoid it. the ambulance will take you somewhere else if you ask.

the lobby was filled with homeless people sleeping in the er admission lobby.  staff are helpful and nice.  however, the doctor on duty didn't take the time to talk to speak to the patient prior to discharge.  the nurse just told us that the doctor is sending us home.  we had some questions and the nurse said that we can ask the new doctor that came to replace the other one.  but he was busy attending to another patient and we could not wait any longer.  so we left without proper discharge instructions from the emergency room doctor.

my mom has been battling cancer for the last 3 years and recently got pneumonia. her cancer drs are at cedars and coh (city of hope). unfortunately the ambalance brought her to the closest hospital so. this hospital is not equipped to deal with cancer patients/serious illnesses. after a week of my mom being in the hospital, she ended up in icu. 

the case managers are horrible! we needed my mom transferred to cedars. you need an accepting dr from the other hospital which we had but they had no beds. i dealt with daisy and eric and their compassion level is zero. most people might say things like i'm sorry for what you're going through, i can't imagine how hard this might be, or we are trying our best. any empathy would have been nice during this stressful time. i knew cedars or coh would be able to treat my mom better so i was trying to move her asap.    

also coh had a bed but soh never offered me one. it's really hard to get into another hospital so when a bed opened up they should have told me! i had to hire a patient advocate to get my mom to the coh even though they had a bed available a week before. the timing was crucial in getting my mom to the coh. also the drs couldn't decide if my mom had pneumonia or pneumonitis. the cat scan should've have confirmed this.                

once we got to the coh they told me she had both pneumonia and pneumonitis. also, they immediately did a bronchoscopy which soh never did. this was the only way to save my mom's life. it was really important to see what was growing in her lungs. like the 2 fungus, virus and bacterial infection so they know how to treat her. at soh it was nice dr. stacey gave me his cell # to address my concerns but why couldn't they figure out my mom had 5 infections. 

my friend asked soh if my mom could have an infection called c-diff because my mom was having continuous diarrhea. they told me they thought it was the ensures. the nurses couldn't even figure out my mom had one of the most common infections from all the anabiotic's. my friend who is a nurse had to tell them to test for it!  

cdiff it's highly contagious and puts us at risk for getting this infection. you're supposed to wear gloves, a gown, and a mask anytime you enter the room. we had been doing none of this.  

the worst thing about this hospital is some of the nurses. tonya in icu is not only rude but she's completely incompetent. i called and my mom's heartbeat was a fib with a heart rate of 171! your heart beat should be 60-100. they told me they were transferring her out of icu. i forced them to call a dr and he ordered medicine immediately and to stay in icu! also they had a device up her nose to monitor her continuous fever. when i called they told me my mom didn't have a fever. when i walked in her monitor said 96.1 but my mom felt super hot. she also had complained to her nurse lyn she was hot. any moron could've figured out my mom had a fever. we took her temperature by mouth and it was 104.5! i immediately called for a charge nurse. it took us hours to get her fever down. we needed a cooling blanket and a ice bath to bring the fever down. also my mom had diarrhea all over her. when i asked her nurse when is the last time she had been changed she said early that morning!

after my mom kept having diarrhea they put an anal probe in so it would catch all the diarrhea. they insisted this was necessary. once we got to coh they said those probes cause anal bleeding and should never be used. the nurses are just  lazy and don't want to do their job even if my mom has discomfort or risk an infection.   

for some reason at soh my mom had a continuous fever but the day she got to coh no fevers. i'm not quite sure what they were doing to her at so but i do know that they weren't conducting the proper treatments needed. keep in mind this is the icu, the best care she could have gotten! my mom arrived to coh not in icu and her level of care went up 10x. she has a respiratory therapist w/ 4 breathing treatments a day. someone to bathe her so she's clean at all times. a team to avoid bedsores/rashes. (in soh my mom had a starting bedsore and a rash from them not cleaning her butt)  

the day we came into coh she got her bronchoscopy, which they did not do at so. if they did they would've found out that she had a very serious life-threatening fungal infection that needs to be treated as early as possible. it grows very fast so if it's not caught early you can die. the only good thing about soh is the nurses (renee/allen/charles) which are not complete idiots like the rest of the hospital. 

i'm not writing a bad review because i'm angry my mom could die. i'm writing to warn others that this hospital really is bad. there's a reason why there are no beds at cedars or the coh. they don't have the experience or technology to treat illnesses and infections. the best advice i can give you is if you dont want them to kill your family member don't come here!

stay away from here!!! i had a horrible experience here at sherman oaks hospital. i have a heart condition and am due for surgery this month at usc. since i live in sherman oaks and couldn't make it to ucla, i was rushed in and could not breathe and my heart was palpitating so fast. i am very used to being in the er but it was my first time here and it was the worst er experience i've ever had. they took their time and did not show any sense of urgency whatsoever. they kept treating me like i was crazy. bad dirty looks, rolling eyes from the nurses. i'm young and don't look sick. but i have chronic health issues. when i told the doctor of my health issues he looked at me and said, "and you were diagnosed by a doctor with those issues?" - what kind of stupid question is that? are you fucking kidding me? and you call yourself a nurse??? - i am so disgusted with this place. how could you call yourselves doctors & nurses when you look down on people who are desperate for your care? how could you treat people this way? to you, you may be desensitized because you run into people who make choices to put themselves in the er, like taking drugs etc. but to us who have chronic health issues (yes even at a young age) this is our fucking reality! get a new profession if you lack empathy and a big heart because the way i was treated was horrible. i am so upset. shame on you all!!!! they gave me magnesium finally after i asked so many times. i wanted it to go in through iv to work faster but they said "it'll take too long and you'll be here all night" - oh so are you trying to get rid of me? what's in the best interest of the patient? and they gave me anxiety medication to "calm me down" which instead made me feel so much worse and lifeless like a rock. when the doctor came to discharge me, he told me - "wow it seems like you have a really great team of doctors up at usc." - like what did you think i was making it up this whole time???? yeah i have real doctors who care at usc. unfortunately i had to come to this shithole to be treated like a crazy person. this is by far the worst hospital i've ever been in. what a shame. our city deserves better. if you are a doctor or nurse reading this please don't treat people this way. not everyone who goes to the er is a drug addict or seeking attention. there are people with real issues who need help. such a shame

review:
this review is specifically for the day surgery center.

i was booked to have a minor procedure here and made the mistake of looking at the yelp reviews first, which had an average of two stars at the time. as a result, i was very nervous about my visit - but overall, my experience here ended up being very positive.

the check-in was quick and painless, the nurses in the prep room were charming and caring, the team in the or was confident and communicative; all in all, a good experience.

i'm not giving tbhc five stars because the other reviewers are correct in pointing out that the building is rather old and tired - in my brief visit, i encountered two doors that wouldn't close correctly, and there was some water leak damage on the hanging ceiling. none of that actually affected my experience as a patient, though, which was marked by professionalism overall.

again, i can only speak for day surgery, but my advice is not to avoid this place (as most other reviews have suggested). remember when reading these reviews that no one has a good time at any hospital.

i wish i could give 0 stars. was visiting family in ny when i was struck with a severe norovirus. if i was going to fly home, i needed to be able to stop vomiting. this was the closest er. here is a list of all of the horrible things about this hospital:

1) bathrooms are filthy, doors don't close, and there is no hot water (although at least there is soap)
2) man handcuffed to er bed being watched over by 2 nypd officers
3) people screaming for help (i.e. pain meds) nonstop 
4) slow, slow service
5) staff doesn't care. literally, no one here cares about you - from the second you walk in the door to the second you leave. 
6) staff isn't qualified - the intake nurse had to google how to spell "yesterday" and asked if my anxiety medicine was for asthma. my iv was put in by a medical student, who poked me in every possible hand and vein before finding one. i wasn't given lidocane before the iv went in. the iv came out, and fluid was leaking into my arm (which is incredibly painful) and i only got someone to remove it after asking no less than four times. 

go to any other hospital but this one.

just came by the hospital to schedule my 4th year rotations as a medical student. the staff was very kind and helpful and directed me to the appropriate personnel. they helped me schedule all my electives immediately. highly recommend!

the brooklyn hospital center is definitely worth reporting the negligence & the maltreatment shown to my 21 year old cousin as she gave birth to a still born tuesday afternoon. 

she came to the hospital on monday morning because she noticed her baby was completely inactive. the nurses tested for a heartbeat and ultimately concluded that the baby had passed in her womb. she was to begin the labor process. 

she waited 5 hours to be induced. as if the sounds of other women on the floor giving birth wasn't enough, the nurses would attend her jubilantly often laughing in her presence at a time where there was nothing to laugh about. 

finally during the labor process, we begged for her to receive an epidural. at this point, we were no longer a priority, as women who were expecting normal delivery received the utmost care. we had to settle on morphine, again hours after it was requested (my cousin was induced twice... you can imagine the pain). 

she finally gave birth to her still born. the nurses left her placenta out in the open for 2 hours before removing it from the delivery room and left behind the bloody blanket that was used to clean off the baby (as if this process wasn't traumatic enough). one nurse even came to the room congratulating her hours after delivery. was she not briefed about the situation?! did she not notice the symbol on the door?! here's the kicker, when it was time for my cousin to be discharged, she was denied the request for a wheel chair and was forced to leave walking out of the hospital on her own. she gave birth like a normal person yet we deny her the same courtesy?! 

a re-evaluation of the staff and their competence at this hospital is definitely needed.  this hospital is extremely lucky that we were in such grief that we did not think to take pictures or videos exposing them to the world.

when you walk into the ambulatory care center you walk into a 3rd world country. 

i was referred to brooklyn hospital by my surgeon at my request just bc it was close to home and what i needed was "a super simple process". that should be the case.

my only need was a medical clearance for a minor surgery that would require local anesthesia (i.e. numbing my ear for a procedure. my ear!). the clearance equates to less than a common physical.

after waiting in a loud, chaotic, asylum-resembling lobby for 40 minutes beyond my appointment time, i was taken into a room where 2 techs/nurses took my vitals. over the next 15 mins they argued which vitals were needed, how the scale worked, how to enter the details into the computer...and what they wanted for lunch (it was 9:45a). 

they moved me to another room...waited 20 more minutes and an intern/resident showed up...nice guy...but had no idea why i was there or what was needed. said he'd grab the doctor and i'd be done shortly. 

thirty minutes pass. i walk down the hall to track down someone...anyone...that can help. (random non-patient civilians freely wandering around the exam areas.) "the doctor is on her way". 

twenty minutes pass...the doctor arrives! however, she's only there to inform me that unless i make her my primary care physician and commit to using her in the future she will not provide the clearance i need. 

it's been 2 hours. i'm not making her my pcp. 

they don't reimburse my co-payment bc the 2-min conversation where she denied me her assistance "counts as a consultation". she never actually entered the room. she told me from the hallway.

folks, don't. just...don't.

(btw my surgery is not taking place at this hospital)

in the early fall of 2019, i was admitted to wellbridge hospital for a medicine change. during this difficult time, i witnessed a strong presentation by kaitlynn, the counselor who supervised the iop (intensive outpatient program. as she emphasized the value of attending the wellbridge iop group, i knew it was what i needed. two days after coming home, i began a ten-week program that met three times a week from 10 am to 2 pm. the wellbridge van drove me from my home in dallas to the iop in plano and then home each day. we had coffee and hot lunches. 

combined with my own hard work, kaitlynn was the key to my successful iop experience. she wisely taught and led us on a journey of self-discovery and compassion. like unpeeling an onion, we uncovered layers of ourselves that needed healing. because of the richness she brought, i didn't want to miss a day, even when i was tired. 

the iop group became like a family with kaitlynn as our leader. i felt safe to talk and be myself. in the spirit of confidentiality, i saw people begin to open, share their thoughts and ideas, and begin to make changes. we supported one another.

if you or your loved one is/will be a patient at wellbridge hospital, i encourage you to inquire about this important step in healing.

if i could give zero stars, i would. last october, i came down with intense flank pain, sweating, and nausea. it was a kidney stone. i knew because it was not my first kidney stone and those symptoms are hard to forget. my employer told me to leave work early and get medical care.

i tried an urgent care first, but they refused care because they didn't have imaging equipment to diagnose a kidney stone. i asked google for the closest hospital, because i was in too much pain to drive but had no one else to drive me so i needed to get there as soon as possible.

i checked in to ahmc emergency room at 12:30pm but was not attended to (other than a urine test) until 3:00pm despite being in so much pain that i was writhing and rocking, and had short/ragged breaths. and yes, i had taken pain relievers... 4 excedrin migraine, which did absolutely nothing for my pain.

once i got into a bed at 3:00pm, where i sat without treatment or fluids for another hour. finally, at 4:00pm, i was given toradol which relieved my pain for about 30 minutes, and 1 liter of saline. then, at 4:30pm, the doctor came to chat with me for about 30 seconds and tell me he thinks i'm an alcoholic because i have pancreatitis (a pathology which can also happen if you're in extreme duress, which i had been for 5 hours) and that he's holding me overnight.

i'm not in the habit of disobeying doctors' orders, so i allowed this and informed my employer immediately. no one on the hospital staff would tell me approximately how long i would be hospitalized, only that i would be going upstairs.

well, upstairs was even worse. i didn't get there until 6:15pm (nearly 2 hours after any pain relief had long-since disappeared), and an hour passed before i was even 'checked in'. around 10pm i was finally given pain medication, but they didn't bother to ask me what medications i respond to, just asked if i had any 'tolerance issues' (code for, "are you a drug addict"). well no, i'm not, but i am an advocate for myself when it comes to pain management and morphine, which they gave me, only causes chest pain and severe anxiety.

i immediately expressed this after the nurse gave me the morphine, because i felt the familiar symptoms, and he said, "oh, well give it some time."

i suffered for 6 more hours without seeing another person's face, although i could hear them talking just outside my room and ignoring my moaning/crying from the pain. the next time someone checked on me, it was 4am. i begged for something different, even the toradol that i was given downstairs because it worked. the nurse said he'd have to check with the doctor on call. i didn't see him again for hours and when he did come back he said the doctor refused the toradol because it's "bad for the kidney," all the while i've been given just 2l of fluid for the past 18 hours. hey, idiots, kidney stones don't spontaneously pass. you have to flush them with fluid.

i finally did get a norco at 10:30am, which meant that about 18 hours passed while i was in 11/10 levels of pain and completely unable to sleep or focus on anything else to take my mind off of the pain... and, once again, listening to nurses talk about other patients while they were right outside my door and had to have heard my cries. furthermore, they would not allow me to take any of my regular medications, which meant 1) no anxiety medication, 2) no sleep medication, and 3) no depression medication when i was still there the next morning.

i begged to be discharged, because they were doing nothing to treat my pain or the cause of my pain. and it still took until 5:30pm (seven hours after the norco) for me to actually be discharged so that i could drink water and pass the stone, which i did in a walgreens bathroom while waiting for the azo and diuretics they had prescribed.

a couple of months later, i got a bill that stated my insurance (which was a 10% coinsurance, mind you) covered all but $900. the original bill was over $18,000. there were fees on the list that looked completely fraudulent, like a $700 charge to assess pulmonary function. unless that was how much my pulse-ox cost, there is no reason i should have a charge for pulmonary assessment. and my 2 liters of saline? $298.

so there you have it -- 30 hours of my life wasted on lack of treatment, only to receive a $900 bill.

since this incident led to me losing my job because my boss felt like i had taken a "vacation" without warning, i didn't have the energy to fight the bill. i just paid it. but you should do anything you can to avoid this hospital like it's the actual plague. walk, take the bus or a taxi, or pay a random stranger to take you to another hospital because all you'll get here is people ignoring you and then asking for ungodly amounts of money for it.

review:
2 stars only because the awesome, underpaid staff is so stellar.  i want this hospital to be great....really i do.  have never stayed at sg but have had er visits for stitches for self and child. 

recently, i had a scary incident at home and called 911.  the wonderful paramedics were able to address it at home but were very forceful about my going to hosp to get checked out.  i told one of them i wanted to go to to suburban because that's my doc's hospital, but since i live so close to sg, they said that would be impossible.  i was told in the past by a much more assertive woman i know that if you push it, they will comply.  but i didn't.

the er nurses were incredible - angels. the docs were very nice and seemed knowledgeable.  they could have let me go home, but decided that i should stay overnight to be on the safe side.  i refused some meds-a shot to the gut. whaaaaaaaat?  no.  it was about 2 am at the time.  i could have walked out, but my husband and the docs, i decided, were right.  that's when things went downhill. 

the room i was assigned to was right next to nursing station.  so very noisy.  it was literally freezing in there.  not enough blankets to be comfortable.  the nurses were lovely but they kept coming in and out instead of doing what they intended to do the first time.  then they'd burst in, throw on that damned stark white overhead light and ask 25 questions that required cogent responses.  problem with this and probably most all hospitals is that cya and $ hold precedence over patients' health.  this is the *hospital policy*, not the employees' faults, but they lose good people because of it.  

finally a doc came in, said he would have let me go last night and kind of muttered about the fact that 2 short procedures would/could be done before i left.  but no one came to do them.  i waited for hours.  finally i found my nurse and said, "i'm leaving and will take responsibility for not having the procedures.  made an appt w/my doc and he'd take care of it. true, i did make the appt and he said he could do one of the procedures. he felt the other was not necessary.  

she summoned the the way overworked "hospitalist," who said i couldn't leave w/out the procedures.  she didn't mention the magic exit, which is to sign a release stating i didn't comply w/medical directives or whatever.  i said i "need to get out of here."  patients were ill all around me, coughing like they had the worst pneumonias, whooping coughs, etc.  i thought hospitals were very concerned with people catching infections while there and wanted them outta there asap, also $$$. i was going crazy.  finally had the 2 procedures.  then the waiting till i was told of the results and hopefully, released.  i tried to find my nurse, over and over and over.  finally found her and she said i'd have to sign the release. i said, "hey that's fine but *i* complied, i did the 2 tests. you guys haven't held up your side of the bargain...i should have had the results hours ago!"

she said the hospitalist had to sign the release! omg. she finally got ahold of her.  the woman looked like someone had dragged her behind their car.  she's young, very smart and competent, but they are killing her! i actually felt sorry for her, everyone was calling, approaching her, pulling at her.  that is *just* inhumane.  these cheap arse hospitals lining ceo's pockets with money and understaffing to keep it that way should be thrown in jail.....for life.  she was very nice, pulled up my results, signed my forms and i was so outta there!!!!!!  i could have cried, i was so frustrated and needed to get out of that place. 

this was disorganization at its worst.  the nurses were, overall, incredible.  but no matter how good you are, you can't do this job alone or be pressed this hard and retain your quality and/or your attitude!  i totally get that. 

at the *very* most, in the am, i should have had the two tests (15 min at most), gotten my results immediately and been sent on my way.  if they had needed the bed, magically, i prob wouldn't have *needed* the tests anymore. 

this place needs to get their act together and treat their employees right.  hire more people and get your procedures in place.  i realize there are  priorities among patient care, but a hospital or any health care facility, had to have have enough committed, serious people so that you can keep the process moving efficiently.

i've been with kaiser hmo for over 25 years.  over the years, i've had a love hate relationship with kaiser vallejo services.  frontline receptionists are inconsistent, they sometimes treat you well and sometimes neglect your needs.  kaiser advice nurse services are helpful and sometimes a waste of time. 

overall, general practitioners are ok.  specialist services are better.  our girls' pediatrician was a wonderful doctor who truly looked after each of them until he retired---kind, patient, and relationship-oriented.  

based on our family's collective health experiences, the quality of services vary by department.  
podiatry department is consistently helpful and supportive.  
dermatology department can learn basic care from podiatry.  
auditory services were special.  
cardiology care was excellent. 
pharmacy wait could be better.

empathy is key.  even if it's evident healthcare workers cannot fix a problem, a patient in need simply needs to see that he or she is heard and understood.

tip of kaiser: it's better for kaiser workers to err on the side of overflowing kindness than curt reprimand.  you will get better cooperation when you are kind to patients in need.

my doctor at kaiser vallejo is awesome. i've seen her for 15 years. she referred me to bariatrics back in 2005 because i was very challenged losing weight and was at 320 pounds. i went to the kaiser bariatric program in richmond ca, and yes, they make the patient go through all kinds of psychological tests and all kinds of classes so we can make an informed decision about whether or not to have weight-loss surgery. here's my warning for anyone thinking about having radical weight loss surgery. they'll teach you about not being able to take nsaids, drink alcohol, eat more than 5g of sugar, no time-release or extended-release medications, etc. the problem: you don't know what is yet to come. i developed osteoarthritis years later. what is the treatment for osteoarthritis? nsaids. unless you have ever had osteoarthritis, you don't have any clue how painful your life is going to be. the only pain-relieving alternative (legal and permitted by kaiser) is narcotic. percocet works really well on osteoarthritis pain. but it wears off after 3.5-4 hours. that means on really bad days you take 6 of them. a 30-day supply is 180 pills. 

kaiser used to provide 200, so there was always extra and refills were about every 4.5-5 weeks. then the government's war on opioids kicked in, and that overshadows patient needs. if someone is in pain, and has no other options for pain control, too bad so sad. sucks to be you. now kaiser limits to 90 tablets for 30 days. they wear off after 3 1/2 hours so that means more than half of the day is spent in pain. and there is no other option. i've complained all the way up the chain at kaiser to no avail. there is not another option and no fix. my recommendation to anyone considering bariatric surgery is fine out before you proceed what your options are if, 15-20 years down the road you've got arthritis that has you in pain most of the time.

all of that said this kaiser is awesome. i just wish they recognize that some patients are in real pain and are falling through the cracks and they need to find a way to address it.

this review is for the er department. this place is the worst.  i checked in with symptoms of short of breath (asthma attack) and chest pain and for the er nurses  these symptoms were not a real emergency.  there were only four patients ahead of me, everyone got seen and left and the receptionist kept on telling me that they were still waiting for a bed.  i sat there and waited for over 3 hours and still nothing. it was 5am and there were no patients waiting beside me and i was still waiting for a bed.  this was ridiculous, i ended up leaving without been seen.  same thing happened to my daughter couple of weeks ago and same situation not too many people waiting and she had to wait four hours and also was never seen by anyone.  i have been a kaiser member for over 40 years, but i think it's time  to reconsider renewing my health insurance next year.
the ladies that are the receptionists in the opthalmgy head neck department are so loud. they never stop talking and never talk at a reasonable volume. it is very annoying and disrespectful.

a friend of mine got stuck by a car.  ambulance came and drove him off to vallejo kaiser.  i must say the emergency security guard that takes you to see the patients is super slow.  my 88 year old mom can move faster than this security guard.

this place treats patients like paychecks at the best of times and animals at the worst of times. patients struggling with mental health need a safe, warm, and comfortable place to go in order to recover - this place is none of those. 

some examples:

- patients up in the middle of the night to another patient standing over them, staring at them
- nurses walking by patients clearly in the middle of an emotional breakdown -- never providing assistance 
- forcing new patients to wait to in process with no shoes, no jacket, and no information for hours. all of this in full view of other patients. 
- frequently berating patients. saying things such as, "shut your mouth," "you don't know anything," and "we'll see you next month" (sarcastically claiming they aren't healthy enough to stay out of the hospital)
- forcing a patient wait for 4 days just to get some chapstick 
- bathrooms with urine on the floor, graffiti on the walls, and looking like they haven't had a good cleaning in years

as for the "healthcare" quality, don't expect much there. in 8 days at the facility, don't expect to see a real doctor for more than 5 minutes -- total!

bottom line: a miserable place only concerned with imprisoning patients as long as possible in order to keep the cash flowing in.

how amazing!! clean and professional! my youngest son is here for surgery and they're amazing! the staff has left me speechless and without questions. he's six years old and i expect the highest of quality care for him as well as all of my children. they have met my expectations and some. i would bring him and my other children back here for all future procedures

most of these have to do with billing or personal disputes but my experience was legit. i'd been hiking and slipped breaking my ankle and knocking my head. when i arrived by ambulance they had an er room waiting for me. in less than 3 hours i'd had all the tests i needed and a plan. thanks to the fast acting and caring staff.

dr. ahmad here misdiagnosed my daughter when she was born.  this cost us an extra week in the hospital, a day and night in the nicu, and a lot of heartache - not to mention the tens of thousands they billed us for his mistake.  the whole time my wife and i were begging with him and the staff to let us take our girl home and that the same thing happened with our son and he was fine.  this smarty-pants doctor thought he knew our baby better than us and turned out he was flat out wrong.  so wrong that him and a good handful of staff were kissing our butts apologizing for what happened.  i understand it's an emotional time, but all the doctors at choc thought they knew better than us and wouldn't let us have a voice when it came to our daughter's well being.  in the end, they poked and prodded her and ripped her away from her mother, starved her for a day and night - all unnecessarily.  

mind you, dr. ahmad is the head of the neosurgical department.  the head.  tells you everything you need to know about choc.  do yourself a favor and deliver your baby elsewhere.  there's nothing worse in the world than watching your newborn baby be tortured unnecessarily - all so a smarty-pants doctor can look like a stud in front of his medical students.  sickening.

review: my 9 year old sister was transferred to choc from a local emergency room with signs of pericardial effusion that resulted in a 2 night stay. the nursing staff is amazing, the doctors on the other hand were not. besides guaranteeing the flu shot wouldn't cause any side effects- which is did, he also released my sister although she was having breathing issues still. 2 days later, her follow-up appointment at another facility, new x-rays were ordered and they found pneumonia. maybe take some time actually evaluating patients instead of being in such a rush. what a shame. also said she was good to go back to school the next day of her release. imagine sending a sick child with pneumonia around other kids?! thank goodness we kept her home.

my young retaliative was admitted to icu for a traumatic brain injury almost 7 weeks ago. there have been a whole host of medical mistakes from surgery to sub standard nursing care.
even though managers apologize and say they will "look into it" and make corrections on.....whatever the current issue is, just about every day there is a new, preventable issue that comes up.
to cover it over nurses make light of it or make up excuses.
no one is perfect but.....at least in the icu setting, one would expect a uniform, high level of nursing experience and care......not so much.
now out of icu and in "step down care" it seems he is getting just that....step down care.

this kid has enough on his plate just to recover and rehabilitate.  sutter memorial is not making this easy for him.

for whatever reason, this hospital seems to staff a mixed bag of both competent nurses, incompetent physician's assistants, and blatantly ignorant (or pocketed) doctors.

upon taking my roommate for symptoms which were confirmed to be identical to generalized anxiety disorder or a panic attack, they instead decided to first diagnose him with an infection after having him wait in the overfull waiting area of the er for 2 or 3 hours before taking him back for blood work, followed by another 2 hour wait after that. then, instead of listening, at all, they chose to treat him for a potential viral infection with nothing more than ibuprofen and acetaminophen, to be taken together (why they think he needed a cocktail of army candy and tylenol for what they assumed was a virus is beyond me) with absolutely nothing done to address his earlier presented symptoms of: racing heart, tingling in the arm and neck, cold sweat, etc

follow this up with today's visit, during which the physician determined that, without any medication of any sort, the signs of an infection (which, again, we weren't even there for. we were there for a panic attack) had gone away on their own in under 24 hours. i'm no doctor, but actual infections tend to last a minimum of 3 days in the human body, assuming they're from pathogens compatible with our biology (the more you know, people). how this physician acted following our combined repeated attempts to reiterate that we were there for my roommate's anxiety symptoms fell upon deaf or disregarding ears. they shuffled my roommate out the door, his mental state worsened visibly upon leaving the care section, and has only gotten worse since we've been away from the hospital, independent of stimuli.

why do people call this a terrible hospital? easy, they allow rampantly asinine doctors to order their nurses and staff to only treat patients they can make the most money on rather than holding to the hippocratic oath and treating all patients with the respect and care unto which they are due. was it because he has state health insurance? was it his appearance? was it because medical doctors think mental illnesses are a myth made up by psychologists to keep them from making money on misdiagnoses?

let's even step back and take a moment to relive that famous question everyone sees on job applications and medical paperwork alike: have you served in the us military?

roomie and i have both served, we both always say yes, and we always have to tell the nurses and doctors everything. we're required to by federal law.

take a moment to realize that this hospital and its leading staff (i'm looking at you, doctors, your nurses are angels and deserve better than you) do not care about you, they don't care about the next person, they don't even care about the people who served their country to protect this freedom we have to tear them down verbally without fear of reprisal. 

they. don't. care.

and, if you want more solid proof than that, just listen to your nurse next time you're there: "hope you feel better soon." not get better, just feel better. the point of us being there in the first place was my roommate not feeling okay and they made the problem worse by shuffling him out the door as quickly as they were legally permitted.

i won't ever recommend memorial to anyone! my husband took me in tonight after a lot of consideration, because i was in excruciating pain and i am also pregnant. my back is injured to the extent that i can't walk nor stand up straight. 
i sat in a wheelchair in extreme agony for over 3 hours. finally got called back and the nurse that took us back didn't have any empathy for the fact that i was crying from my level of pain at this point. when my husband asked if i could have tylenol while we waiting for the doctor, he said i had to wait for the doctor to see me. he never tried to ask the doctor or a pa if they could order me tylenol, we weren't asking for norco for crying out loud. 
after waiting yet another hour for the doctor or just anyone to come and check on me, we asked again for tylenol. again, same response and the same lack of care and at this point the pain had me curled up in the fetal position. 
finally, i looked at my husband and said "i rather be in pain and agony at home than to be doing it here and be ignored." we asked for a wheelchair so we could leave and when we were explaining to that same nurse that we were leaving he didn't even blink! he couldn't care less! he just said "oh ok, you can leave whenever you want." who treats a pregnant woman in this level of pain like that ?! 
you're supposed to be a patient care professional, yet you couldn't care any less about the patient in front of you in tears. when we asked to speak to someone they just tried to justify it all by saying that doctor's need breaks too and that there were people there who had been waiting upwards of 5 hours, like somehow that is acceptable. 
i have insurance, and my deductible when i go to the er isn't cheap, so do you think i would go there if it truly wasn't an emergency? memorial really needs to wisen up and get some better people working in their er. people with hearts and with the ability to actually listen and care. people aren't cattle. i won't ever be coming back to memorial and i suggest you also go elsewhere, give doctor's medical center a try first.

been here for over 6 hours, and still waiting. not sure what's going on but they need more help. you can tell they are over worked and getting annoyed with patients. i'm glad i have kaiser i would never want to come here. i rather chop my own leg off then come here.

my dad is a patient here for an unknown infection that made him light headed. he was admitted to sutter memorial of coffee road in mothe 29th of december. while the nurses and doctors have been attentive, don't get put on the 5th floor. here are my complaints:
1) no running hot water in the sinks or showers. the nurses station doesn't have hot water either.
2) if you are going to be seen by a specialist (infectious disease-dr. shwe in particular), make sure to get a time commitment. our dr. sharma promised to have this specialist by to see our dad. two of us waited over 4 hours only to be told by the nurse who had her on the phone "i'm too busy, maybe tomorrow" wtf? seriously??  dereliction of duty or poor doctor to doctor communication that doesn't get passed to the patient-i can't say but please be aware.
3) it helps to know the nurses by name. it seems they are a little more attentive to the weird requests like new bed sheets, ice for drinking water, and turning off the alarm for the iv drips when they go off.
4) in a two person room, be ready for little to no privacy as guests, different doctors, nurses, etc. make it tough for any kind of sleep.
5) the food? wow, not great. any meat served was tough, baked potatoes cold, and all vegetables served appeared boiled at best. not appetizing and i wouldn't give it to my dogs.

suggestions: 
when a nurse says "this is an old hospital and sometimes the 5th floor doesn't get hot water", fix it! 
steam your vegetables. opening up a large foodservice frozen bag and boiling it is just a waste.
on the call button/tv changer/bed controller devise, figure a way to silence one side so that every verbal request by your room mate doesn't transfer to the other speaker.
several machines in this particular room were non functioning. the machine taking the temperature did not work so the neighbors machine was borrowed that worked twice before it broke. we ended up with an old school thermometer to take his temperature. really, again, wtf?
when the 8th or 9th bag of different antibiotics pumped through in 2 days does not work, call the specialist sooner. it seems the cultures they took take "4-5 days" to grow to help determine what you have so instead of a rifle shot of cure, we got a shotgun blast of everything they had. the doctors tells us "it's a mystery, we'll try everything". good or bad, this room and treatments are not free.
they also wanted cat-scans of just about every organ in his body including mri's of his head. hard to say from a non medical perspective but again, these activities come with a huge price tag. 

a new addition: no ice on this floor. i have been traveling to the restaurant  twice a day to get my dad ice for his water. seriously?


this hospital was chosen because it is close to his home. if we ever have a similar issue, we will not return here and would prefer a better equipped hospital and larger staff of disease specialist like stanford or any other hospital for that matter.

this is one of the dirtiest hospitals i've been in! i can't believe it. my family was admitted and was in a room on the 3rd floor. every time i walked in and out i just could not believe that it was a hospital i was walking through filthy!!

my mom, sister and brother have been here for different surgeries and treatments and every single time they have had a terrible experience, i pay good money for their health care and i expect them to be treated well. misdiagnosed, over medicated, sent home with a untreated infection resulting in a longer stay at the hospital. when i've visited the staff is unpleasant and not comforting during these hard times.

my 90-year-old mom was at memorial hospital for a week. she was taken there by ambulance after a fall where she broke her hip. while there, they discovered she had a complication called rhabdomyolysis, which can lead to kidney failure, heart problems, or even death, if not treated. they postponed her hip surgery and moved her to the cardiac ward (because of her previous heart problems) until they got it under control, and then dr. cash (a wonderful orthopedic surgeon) performed the surgery. we were very impressed with the hospital and the people who worked there. the nurses and aids were caring and friendly, and we were really happy that the complication my mom had was quickly discovered and dealt with. the room she was in was very nice, spacious, and comfortable. the cafeteria is really good too. we would definitely recommend this hospital.

i am one such pregnant woman. i have an extremely anxious personality and am no getting no help from this practice. the main doctor who is assigned to me is never available to answer questions or concerns and i am always fobbed off to the physician's assistant, who also has no time or concern to help. i have seen the actual doctor exactly once in 33 weeks of pregnancy. i have seen the physician's assistant for every other appointment that is scheduled for the doctor and she is brusque and unfriendly. every concern i have is condescended and brushed off with a general air of "just deal with it." 

now i have anxiety to the point of not being able to function and no one will do a thing. i have called and insisted that i want to meet with the doctor and been flat out refused. i have requested medication and again been refused. i have been to the er with panic attacks for weeks and begged to just talk to a doctor to calm my fears of delivery and been told no.

the doctors in this practice don't care about the health of pregnant women and just show up to deliver and then disappear again. we are nothing but vessels for babies and not worth helping in their eyes.

if you have tricare, my advice to you if you're pregnant is to make sure you hang out near reno when's it close to your due date and then just go to the nearest hospital there. banner churchill is the worst thing to happen to pregnancy in fallon and no one cares to do anything about it.

i am an rn with a master's degree and was also an aprn for 10 years. having been a healthcare provider for many years, i am saddened to write a negative review of a hospital.

i was sent to the er by my primary doctor's office. when i arrived at ascension seton hays county er in kyle, the waiting room was not overly crowded, and it was evident some of the people were not patients but family members of patients. i was optimistic for a quick visit. 

i made sure to confirm that not only the hospital but all related to my care would be in-network with my medical insurance. i knew seton was in-network, but i did not want anyone involved in my care who was not in-network. i know seton has not been very good about this in the past.

after i was triaged, i was told to sit again in the waiting room. since i had to use the bathroom, i was directed to collect a sample. sitting in the waiting room holding a container of urine on my lap felt incredibly awkward. in fact, i was so embarrassed that for part of the time, i felt compelled to put it in my handbag. 

when i was called to the back, i was led to a stretcher in the hallway. that is where i remained throughout my care from assessment through treatment through discharge. 

way back in nursing school, i was taught to always introduce myself by name and role to each patient, for instance, "hi. i'm sandra, and i will be your nurse today." i consistently did this throughout my career regardless if i was wearing a name tag or id, and i strongly believe that every provider in healthcare should do the same, from technicians to nurses to physicians. during my visit at seton's er, some staff did introduce themselves to me such as ashley (the triage nurse) and the er doctor. however, there were others involved with my care who did not. 

from my place in the hallway, i had a front row seat to everything. the patient in the room next to my stretcher was obviously dying. family members sat next to and stood near my stretcher. i felt like i was intruding on their grief. as a caring person, i wanted to reach out and provide support, but i kept quiet since i really should not have even been aware of what was going on with them and the patient.

at another point, i heard a commotion going on behind the head of my stretcher. it was not particularly loud, but i heard security involved, and i felt frightened. i did not dare turn around to see what was going on, but i did watch as security walked a man in handcuffs down the hallway. i hope i had not been in any danger.

when my iv was removed, a band-aid was placed in my antecubital space where the iv had been located. shortly after, i noticed my arm felt wet and cold. i looked down and saw that i was bleeding profusely and that my beloved sweater was getting soaked with bright red. a nurse (well, i assume she was a nurse; she never introduced herself) brought over a bottle of hydrogen peroxide and a stack of gauze to remove the blood. she started the process pouring the peroxide on my sweater, but it would take a while to remove such a quantity of blood, so she left me with the supplies to continue working on it myself. finally, i got my sweater mostly clean, but i was left very wet and cold.

it was taking a long time to get final lab results, and then i learned that the lab had lost my specimen! how does that even happen? is the lab not in the same building? a mishap like that does not instill confidence. hopefully the lab does not also accidentally mix up samples or misread them or misreport them.

i spent almost 4 hours at ascension hays seton to have a few simple tests done (no imaging) and a medication administered (a push, not a slow drip). it was not like the er was chaotic. in fact, i watched many staff sitting behind the desk for much of my time there.

close to the time of my discharge, i was approached to sign a consent to treatment. it seemed quite late to be asking for that. i was feeling so frustrated by that point that i signed the various forms without reading anything. i was also told that with insurance i owed $*** just for walking into the er (the amount did not include tests, etc.). she wanted to collect money right there on the spot. i handed over my credit card, thinking this trip to was the biggest waste of money and time i could have imagined. i dread thinking about the remainder of my bill still yet to come.

every staff member i encountered was nice, and i appreciate them. still, i would not recommend ascension seton hays er in kyle. obviously, i strive and wish for good health and hope i never have to go to an emergency room again. however, if i do, i will first check into my other options before heading to seton.
