a lullaby plays every time a baby is born! (i personally know several cha obgyns and if you are looking to have a baby you are in amazing hands. my experience is surgery only !)

i honestly only came to cha for my surgeon. i wouldn't come otherwise for surgery. nothing against cha. but the nurse to patient ratio is enough to keep me away.

my mom was a patient at 6 north and it was horrible. i noticed many safety violations happening throughout stay on floor, as well as hippa violations, and negligence. management was no help, was promised "safety is #1 priority" by laurie bausk, nurse manager only to see patient safety disregarded repeatedly. 
there was a great and knowledgeable nurse there gina but she was outnumbered by bad nurses like krista who told my family "she may never be the same again and may end up in rehab for the rest of her life." thankfully she was wrong, as they were wrong about a lot of things during her stay. i also had a safety issue and asked if the nurse station would screen visitors and that we only wanted certain people to come in the room, i was told no. my mom was roomed near loud nurse station were patients were talked about poorly. the kitchen and housekeeping staff were more uplifting than the floor nurses. i won't even touch on the way we were treated and talked down to by internist megan b. callahan, md who misdiagnosed my mom and just wanted us to be happy they were wrong. she had a preconceived notion about us and it showed on everything she did. thankfully she was replaced by jeremy sylvan, md who knew his stuff and also cared about the people he treats. they were more concerned about which insurance was paying for the stay and were going to discharge her without treating the reason she was admitted. it made a scary experience worse.  1 month later and myself and my mother haven't heard from patient relations although we have contacted them numerous times, my emails have gone ignored. maybe the not caring about patients comes from the top? also finding our more bad things about my mothers care and treatment during stay. if im lucky i will get her in a new hospital system that cares about patients and knows what they are doing. my mother had no insurance at time it was pending if she did i believe she would have been treated a lot better.

the doctor was being a complete dick head. as soon as we got to the hospital he greets us at the ambulance and is genuinely concerned. i tell him what was going on with my mom(she has messed up her back, and her pain tolerance isn't high so she was in tears) and his attitude isn't the greatest, but i just brushed it off before maybe he was having a bad day. but what happened after we got in the room is very unnaceptable, and highly unprofessional. i hear him mumble to the nurse and i quote "let's see how full of shit she is about all this". i try to remain cool and not smack his shinny ass bald ass fucken head because talking to someone of higher power in the medical facility would be more professional. his name is joe leary, and we already asked if we can have another doctor but he was the only doc on shift tonight.

i went into the hospital er for abdominal pain and rectal bleeding today friday 2/1/2020 around 10pm.

waiting room had about 8 people; patients, friends, and family included. i had my vitals taken with in 15 minutes. one patient gave me the stink eye because i was called in just before them. the triage nurse that took my vials asked if i had a history of hemorrhoids, i said yes but 12 years ago after having my daughter but i had surgery to remove it and have not had an issue since.  i added that i had 4 bowl movements in the day and the started normal then turned into diarrhea with severe burning and bright red blood.  

she diagnosed me with a hemorrhoid and suggested that i take a laxative. 

then i waited two and a half hours. 

i went to the triage desk, no one to befound. i could smell chick-fil-a so i looked into the other bay windows where the triage nurse popped her head out. i asked how much longer, she said let me look. she had a two minute conversation with the other nurse about being short staffed. she then walked around the corner with a full mouth of food telling me it'll be another twenty minutes, maybe. then she went back to her meal. i left.

dr t newton advised to do chest x-rays without examining my son. he then said " what do you want me to do then".  me: "examine him like a doctor does; and tell me if his lungs are clear, as i am not a doctor", "my son has asthma". 

this seton is exactly the same as i remembered 15 years ago when my son was born, absolutely horrible care. was praying for improvement since it's so close and convenient. dr. t newton is sarcastic and just plain rude.

i arrived this afternoon right at 5pm. i had a blockage in my stomach called a good bolis. i was in a ton of pain. i was taken back to a room within 30 minutes. professional and caring nurses took very good care of me, very quickly! not to mention a doctor that made everything move fast. i had lab work, fluids for dehydration, x ray within an hour and was on my way to have an edg to remove the blockage. surgeon and staff in the or were just as amazing. i'm from fort worth and completely out of my comfort zone. they made me feel important and cared for! i can't thank them enough!! out of the hospital and back at my hotel within 3.5 hours.

excellent experience in the surgical center (cataract  surgery). everyone we encountered was friendly, helpful, and professional. many hospitals have programs to ensure that patients have a good experience, but this often  results  in inane checklists, canned questions, etc. but seton nw is getting it right. their people provide top quality care with excellent personal attention. well done!

you want to see one of the most tone-deaf hospital, visit this. sad. as soon my son was taken to er twice, they want to do every test possible. worse when the staff came and asked "have you signed up to give your organs?" my son had anxiety attack and this question only makes it worse. there is no commonsense here. they will ask a person in shock questions that will worsen the situation. most of their doctors are on contract. they will bill the heck out of you. i am trying to resolve the billing issue but no one is willing to talk. endless hold and then "sorry we cant speak to you" since my son is just above 18 years. they took co-pay and miraculously that is not taken out of the bill and their system doesn't track it. the same happened 4 months ago and after talking over a month they took it off. how much worse do you want to make the patients and their family? you want really bad then visit this place. the doctor and some nurses were fine.
sibley is a part of johns hopkins in dc right at the maryland border. has a rehab center too.

i'm not a big fan of hospitals but planning for my twins' birth, i knew it had to be at a hospital. 

i had a scheduled c section (at 38 weeks) prior to thanksgiving so i had to stay through the holiday. the labor and delivery department and postpartum department were all great! i believe sibley already has a good reputation for delivery and i feared going into labor before week 34 because then i would've had to go to gw or georgetown university... whichever one has the nicu. i'm so thankful for making it to term and being able to deliver here. 

i loved the team that worked with me ... even though different nurses had different ways of doing things. i recommend sibley for future mamas!

if the apple store and chick-fil-a had a baby who said "i want to be a hospital when i grow up," this would be that baby's dream fulfilled. 

it's the nicest and cleanest hospital i've ever been in with the nicest people. the er waiting room (sponsored by marriott according to the placard on the wall) had phone charging stations. the rooms in the back looked like something off of a medical drama. i was half expecting house to walk by. 

i have never had so many medical professionals treat me like i was the first sick person they'd ever encountered. 

"i'm so sorry you're not feeling well."
"i sincerely hope you feel better." 

i was laying on the bed outside the ct machine room when a random nurse passed by and asked me if i was cold and if i wanted him to bring me a warm blanket. i already had a blanket, but he brought me a piping hot one and folded it over me like my life depended on it. the only thing missing was "have a blessed day" and some waffle fries. 

everything was fast too. the last dc emergency room i visited left a lot to be desired...like medical care. after three hours of waiting for a bed and six hours of waiting for an ekg, i was asked to leave at 2 in the morning and come back the next day, so they could "free up some beds." 

not here. they literally called me back after 30 minutes, and still two nurses and a doctor repeatedly apologized for "the long wait." they did all my labs and even got a ct scan done in about two hours. when i was discharged, the doctor took her time explaining everything and repeatedly asked if i had any questions as if i was the only patient there. the nurse came in after her and did the same thing "just in case." 

little baby chick-fil-apple turned out to be a damn fine hospital.

the sweetest staff members ever. from the moment i walked in ... no one likes having to go to the er but when you do, you'd like to be accommodated and feel cared for or at least like your health is a priority, and they did nothing less than. above and beyond, service is immaculate. i came in with chills, high heart rate due to dehydration and horrible abdominal pain caused by food poison. my uber driver had recommended sibley memorial over the er i was initially going to, and i am so glad that he did. i highly recommend sibley hospital i wish i had gotten the names of all of the helpful nurses. thank you
wow! sibley is the best hospital i've ever been to. the hospital is extremely clean and the staff is out of this world phenomenal!
no wait. i came in at 8:30 and they admitted to see me at 8:15. the people are super nice and they actually know how to stitch. i avoided gw hospital, paid for an uber to come here, well worth it.

i waited for 9 hours in the er and wasn't seen until 1am by a doctor to address severe abdominal pain. very disorganized and no communication. there was no one available to answer questions. they did a blood test, urine test, ultrasound, and ct scan and provided me no updates on any of those and just proceeded to the next one. i would not recommend this hospital if you have a serious emergency that needs to be met immediately.

recently, i went to sibley memorial hospital with acute shortness of breath and received excellent, caring, courteous care! dr. louis piper, the attending physician, alison mackin, nurse, and yodit kassa, ultrasound tech, were all outstanding, friendly and did a great job of communicating what was going on and answering my questions. i was seen for an initial screening in a matter of about 10 minutes and, once they determined my symptoms didn't pose an immediate threat to life, i had to wait another half hour or so. in the end, i spent all day in the er getting lots of tests, which wasn't much fun, but the team did a great job of checking into the possible causes of my shortness of breath. my only complaint about the er is very minor: i was sent home after getting a single tablet of blood-thinners and a prescription for more--but i needed that prescription filled before the next morning. filling a prescription on a sunday evening is challenging and it would have been nice if they had been able to give me a one-day supply--but apparently hospital protocols don't allow that.
thank you, everybody at sibley. i'm so grateful!

this review is for the cafeteria only. i went down to get breakfast and they had food but no workers  to serve it to you (hot food behind glass). after waiting for 5 min and nobody willing to work or do there job i left. on my way out i saw the back door open and a group of workers hanging out in the back talking and laughing. i have no problem with that but when you have customers trying to get food you should take 2 min to do your job.

it used to be easy to schedule an appointment in the sibley imaging center.  today it took 40 minutes wait time, listening over and over to the message saying how busy everyone was.  then they offer to return your call if you want to leave a message, and promise to return the call within 24-48 hours.  are you supposed to sit at home and wait for their call? a silly offer.  clearly the staff is shorthanded, and hopkins is economizing.

the absolute worst bedside manner you can imagine!!! they will leave your loved one on the toilet for hours before returning and helping them back to bed. you can't ask questions due to the rude sarcastic answers you have to deal with besides the lack of urgency when it comes to patient relations. sad sad sad. i hope management can get these nurses the training they need to properly care for the patients and help their bedside manner. maybe next time they won't forget to take the iv out of my mother-in-law's arm before sending her home misdiagnosed? blood clots and kidney stones... i guess those are kind of like the same thing?

this is the nasty hospital i've seen. i honestly watch a pca by the name, kolby that works on the 4th floor take dirty sheets with bowel movement on them and through them on the floor. she didn't want to wash the patient bed off no type of disinfection was use. we ask her to clean the pillows and the bed please before putting them back on the bed. this so call care giving then started looking at us real nasty up and down rolling her eyes turning up her nose which she is ugly enough without doing that. looking like a dried up piece of meat! bowel was almost every where. she told the other nurse just rinse it off. we had to ask again for the bed and pillow to be disinfected and she replied we don't have any! after taking off the dirty sheets she reach for some clean sheets dragging them on the floor in the dirty sheets with the bowel movement on them and put them on the bed! i do have proof and can prove my every word! i have a video... a lot of patient has come in contact with c-diff while in the hospital and died from the bacterium and hp aka helicobacter pylori. read up on these bacterium! hospital are suppose to be clean and a care giving attitudes. this pca was ill-mannered, rude, ill-bred, nasty, uncivilized and this pca was acting just like a savage! are patient just a pay check and where are the good old doctor's and nurses???

hospital is an absolute piece of shit. staff was dismissive as i told them that i was literally going insane. i told them multiple times that i've been severely isolated and needed someone to talk to, only for me to feel like an annoyance. i explained that i was going insane and they told me it was just a chemical imbalance. i even allowed my mother to keep me company but they told her no anyway. i should've escaped by the emergency exit.

 after the visit, my mother told the nurses i was trying to kill myself only for them to play it off with a shrug and a grimace as if they couldn't do a damn thing about it.

dont bring your family here,the nurses have very bad actitud specially the night shift .the african american nurses will treat you like shit .can't wait to take my dad out off this shit hole!!!!! the night shift starts at 8pm and they already come with bad actitud they are lazy !!!!!many nurses don't speak english is hard to communicate with them !!!! you can heard people yelling for help and they just being ignored for hours!!!!! someone needs to come anonymously and watch your lazy workers!!!! watch them treating people like animals!!!! i'm taking my dad out of this place asap.

i'm the daughter of a patient who had a stroke. my mom came to this facility on a ventilator. dr. hourani was/is super amazing. dr. hourani got my mom of the vent in approximately one month. he is super amazing and very down to earth. he works with jocelyn she is the head of rt she is super amazing and i voiced my concerns to both of them and they helped me resolved them. i had my ups and down with this facility... in the sense that i don't play about mom. i want all t's crossed and i's dotted. emily, randall, christina and a host of other rn/lvn are super amazing. i appreciate the staff and dr's at kindred... kuddos to dr. hourani and his team!!!  i also forgot to say thank you to grace and daisy. when i complained they did their best to make everything better. at the end of the day.. no facility is perfect... however, when i voiced a concern is was addressed and dealt with. thank you

beware of over charges!!!
i received decent care but they charged me $158 for using a q-tip in my ear!
i don't mind paying for medical services rendered but this is ridiculous.

after getting the run around they would not reduce or remove the charge.

not from personal experience, but from being involved with someone who was a patient for 5 days, i don't know why the reviews are so poor.  my loved one really enjoyed the therapy groups, the therapists, and really liked his psychiatrist.  saying that, i also met with these people and they were very helpful and took their time to listen to my concerns.  it is a lockdown but everyone was very nice and respectful.  they encouraged follow up therapy, which he is motivated to continue given this experience.  also, my experience was solely with c ward.  i cannot speak to the rest.  four stars is only because i was not the patient.

i was there about 1 month ago, for about 5 days.  i found the staff was very caring and helpful.  my care was excellent, groups were good, food pretty good.  if i go down that mania path again, i would not mind going back.

if i can leave a 0 review i would but it doesn't let me. warning!!! do not bring your loved ones here!!!! i repeat do not bring them here. this was the worst place and i regret bringing my daughter here. i wish someone would of told me about this place before, but this place does not care about their patients, all they care about is trying to keep patients longer to make money from your insurance. they will lie to your face and make up stories to make your child stay longer. also they verbally assaulted my daughter by saying, "if you don't stop crying, we will have to medicate you" i was devastated to hear how they were treating my daughter and i was mostly upset at myself for not being able to do anything to help my daughter from these monsters. the sad part is that they do these types of things to all the kids that stay there and to their families. it's sad to know the nurses enter the medical field making an oath to supposly advocate for their patients but yet these nurses are doing the opposite. they are in it for the money and not for these poor children. i'm disgusted with this facility i don't understand why they're still open they should be shut down for ever!

from my experiences at aurora charter oak hospital i must profess that the groups, and support system is extremely great ! although some of the employees can be bullies i understand to a degree that i was a hard patient to deal with at the time but i experienced harassment from a tall american american employee that works in the all boys unit  he was creating conflict! i also experienced harassment from a women named natile

if i could give this place negative stars i would. i was held here against my will during a very difficult time in my life, and now besides having to deal with an astronomical bill that i cannot afford to pay, i also have to deal with the emotional and physical damage that i sustained while i was held here. i was treated like an animal from the minute i came through the door up until the minute i walked out. it was also very clear to me that even though i was there on a 72 hour hold, they never had any intentions of even considering letting me leave until i had been there at least 5 days. this place is a business that takes advantage of people who are in a tough place and are unable to resist. why is the typical time that people spend here 5-7 days? it's because they know that after they extend a 72 hour hold they have so many days that they can continue to hold you before you are able to have a court hearing, so they cash in on as many of those days as possible before they allow you to go. nothing that happens at this facility is done in the patients best interest. all this "hospital" has done for me is force me  to chose between buying food and paying off their bill, as well as give me recurring nightmares about the damaging treatment i received while i was there.

mishi (head o.r. nurse) and all intake and o.r. prep staff were amazing. the facilities were clean, staff pleasant and it was almost stress-free getting prepped for surgery. the anesthesiologist (dr. nyberg, md) and the vascular surgeon (dr. gonzalez, md) were personable and very clear about surgical procedures and how they could make the medical experience more comfortable based on specific needs (history of nausea, history of past procedures, etc...). 
staff were attentive, practiced, well-trained and respectful. as far as i can recall, i got wheeled into the surgery with a smile on my face:)
would recommend this hospital based on medical professionalism, cleanliness, location, upgraded equipment and patient care and contact.i couldn't have asked for better.

we had already previously toured the facility and really liked what we saw! clean and big rooms, friendly staff, and loved that their labor and delivery is completely separate from their emergency building! if you're planning on having your baby in the valley, please go here! we had a scheduled induction for 01/18 at night and i have to say, their staff took the best care of us from start to finish. after 24 hours of trying to induce my labor, i was actually sent home because my body just wasn't ready to give birth and the staff new isn't more comfortable at home. after being home for 3 hours, our baby boy changed his mind and we headed back to the hospital! it was a very long labor but thankfully all the nurses took such great care of us! always checking in on us and being super tentative, reminding us or meal times and making sure we got fed, made sure i got the medication i needed and wanted and when i wanted it, always offering a hand once baby boy was here, helping me through my first few days of postpartum, and making sure my all baby and my testing got done in a timely yet still respectful manner. i know it seems like a no brained than a hospital should already do these things but usually they're so busy and hectic that this just isn't the case. not with honorhealth osborn. if i could give them 10 stars, i would! as happy as i was to go home and start our "normal lives", i was sad to their their amazing staff.
the absolute best hospital in america! from the check in staff, to the nurses and doctors.

while on a casual evening walk christmas eve, admiring some nearby lighted landscape, i failed to see the gnarly, prickly, cactus as i reached out my hand to point to a holiday decoration.  in doing so, i pointed my finger directly into a cactus needle, which quickly imbedded itself under my fingernail and broke off in between my skin and nail.  not realizing at the time it had actually broke off inside, i thought it was just a puncture. as the pain continued, and my attempts at self-treatment to try and remove it failed, it was evident that i needed professional medical help. we called honorhealth scottsdale osborn about 10:00 pm christmas eve and they said come in. we were professionally and warmly greeted by the er staff and seen immediately. i cannot say enough great things about the professional medical staff here. the nurses, er admit, and er dr nichols, are the best. after numbing, and cutting my nail away from the skin to get that prickly cactus needle out from my nail bed, and a tetanus shot, rx for antibiotics, we were on our way just after midnight christmas morning. i am so thankful for the nurses and doctor who were on call this christmas night. they were all so kind and compassionate. i'm truly grateful for their time and commitment to being there for people like me. there were, indeed, emergencies far worse than my cactus catastrophe, but all the same courtesy and care for all.

my stepmother (a former nurse) fell and shattered her wrist while we were visiting scottsdale over thanksgiving from out of town.  from the time she arrived by ambulance to the er to the day she was discharged (3 days later), she receceived  excellent care at honorhealth - osborn, compassionate, professional, caring, and quality care.  absolutely everyone she encountered during her stay provided excellent care.  their kindness was very much appreciated. thank you to the er, dr. miller (the surgeon), and the entire staff on the 6th floor.

my son was admitted a week ago with a bacterial infection on his leg.  i give the er (both doctors and nurses, 5 stars).  the were fast, efficient, and i had complete confidence in them.  we were moved up to the 4th floor and, while i was comfortable with the nursing staff and the doctor we saw daily, i was pretty appalled at how filthy the room and general areas on that floor were.   on day two, i brought in my own lysol and rags to clean.  i had to ask for my son's bedding to be changed and then i was handed a stack of sheets to change it myself.  do hospitals no longer maintain a housekeeping staff?  this one certainly didn't appear to.  again, i was very happy with the medical staff, but considering we were fighting a bacterial infection of the skin, it was a miracle we didn't pick up something else while there.
horrible service. horrible people. no sense of urgency and people were not helpful in the slightest

had to do xrays for my 10 yo daughter and from walking in everyone was extremely friendly! there volunteers make sure to help direct you to where you need to be and the smell of fresh popcorn gets your mouth watery! 

they have a playground directly in front of the hospital to keep the kids busy. you can always appreciate a hospital that does not charge for parking!
fac_name: Texas Scottish Rite Hospital For Children

review:
dr horsepool at the charlie mitchell's clinic here at the valley childrens hospital is the most patient, kind , compassionate physician i've met in my life. i pretty much consider anybody who are kind and compassionate towards children on the autism spectrum to be the angels on earth. :) 

trust me , my son on the spectrum is fourteen now and we've encountered plenty of people who are unfortunately the opposite of the angels. one of the nurse practitioner, michelle is super sweet and awesome too. she understands kids with autism . she just gets it. she's patient and knows how to deal with their fears and anxiety. 

i'm so grateful for the charlie mitchell's clinic and their dedicated staff who tirelessly help make special needs children feel better . i'm also thankful to the social workers here who writes referrals for us so that my son is able to receive therapies he needs otherwise the school district won't offer. 

many many kisses and hugs to charlie mitchell's angels !!!

the pediatrician dept on the 1st floor of the charlie mitchell clinic....suck.

dont waste your time....find other doctors!

don't come here for anything at the er, each and every person we saw was rude! we waited for 4 hours, waiting room after waiting room and we get seen for 2 minutes. 

this place is a joke, never bringing my family to this circus ever again. 

save your self the time, go to a urgent care and if you need to come here - bring earplugs, face mask and patience.

valley children's hospital is amazing we don't regularly go here since my kids have a primary physician somewhere else. but when we get referred to them for certain things they have always been amazing and the staff is always super friendly. not to mention the cafeteria has great food
was told it was the best hospital but they were so unorganized the nurses were a joke never been so pissed in my life. sad that i had to keep asking for things to help my daughter with her 106 fever.

the er is the slowest er i have ever been too. my son had a deep facial wound when we came in. it was bleeding down his cheek. no one offered anything to help stop the blood. we waited 8 hours to get get back and they still weren't an any hurry to clean it. he screamed when the sutured his cut up. i don't think he was numb. horrible experience. in total it took 10 hours!!!

worst experience of my life , so my daughter was throwing up blood and bleeding from her nose as well as a fever  , we took her to childrens at 2:30 am and seemed like they didn't even care , we were there until 8:30am before we decided to leave.. i do not recommend this place for anyone unless you don't mind waiting 12 hours to be seen ..

waited 5 hours just to get in a hallway, the dr came and asked why i came and i said my daughter had been crying for a week straight and her cheeks have a really bad rash and his was reply was literally " oh my god" in the most sarcastic way possible, very unprofessional, didn't even check my baby out just said "i will get her some cream"

today i would like to discuss our experience at valley children's hospital. farrah garcia was discharged after a day and 7 hours with pneumonia, influenza, fluctuating fever, and chronic cough. as they were leaving the outpatient area to the parking lot,a wheelchair was not provided to my fatigue and sick child. the nurse ramon expected farrah to walk a far distance without any transport assistance. farrah's grandma was concerned and asked if there were any wheelchair's available. he said there were none available at the time. as farrah and her grandma walked through the hospital they saw three wheelchairs and they even witnessed a women who is expecting a child sitting on a wheelchair she eventually gave it to my daughter to use. also monday february 10,2020 11pm-7 am, i stayed the night with farrah in the hospital the nurse were rude didn't keep me informed about farrah's temperature & progression.
tuesday feb 11, 2020 around 12 pm my mom experience rudeness and unfriendliness from one of the nurses. we believe we experienced this type of behavior because of racism and discrimination.

if i could give this hospital a zero  stars i would. i took my boyfriend to the emergency room due extreme pain and swelling in his knee area. we were seen right away and wheeled to a room. where the medical assistant took vital vitals and a health history. from there the attending doctor order an x-ray of his knee . as we waited for the result the doctor never ordered any type of pain relief despite my boyfriend saying his pain was an 9 out of 10. also his nurse only come into his room at the every end to go over the discharge papers.

jackson hospital apparently has a policy that co-pays have to be paid two days in advance. really? it is highly unethical to require payment for services before they are rendered so much in advance! just before checking in would be much more appropriate! only hospital in area except defuniak springs (which is a mess) requiring this!

ok guys,  i'm here & ready to get my endoscopic procedure finally done.  today is the makeup endoscopic procedure that has been postponed for the past several weeks due to food being found in my stomach.  thus the catalyst for my stint on my liquid diet adventure,  hopefully real food is in my future very soon.  lol you know what....? i'm hungry.  
apparently,  yet again i have arrived way earlier than i ought to have.  lol yeah,  i was that kid!

ok, i'm prepped & ready to go....

ok guys,  i'm home and exhausted.  my mouth & throat apparently became banged up.  i will remain on a liquid/ soft diet for the foreseeable future until i see my new usc g.i specialist.

ok guys,  i have something that i left out of my review ending.  it was mentioned to me as i woke,  dr.van dam did not find any of the clusters that had been removed to have grown back.  he further explained that my stomach was swollen during my original procedure that removed my clusters of tumors so while he was cleaning up after my growths were removed nothing was noticed or found.  on this day,  he discovered a large tumor & subsequently took a biopsy and sent it to the lab.  i will be meeting with both van dam and my usc oncologist.  
so i have been somewhat out of sorts....
fac_name: Keck Medicine of USC - Keck Hospital of USC

review: keck usc hospital...specifically dr. daniel oakes of the ortho department....and his entire staff..is just the best!  a hip and total knee replacement for my wife in the last two years, a hip replacement for me just recently...i wouldn't consider going to anyone else.  his confidence in treateing a very high risk difficult case (my wife)....his calmness, personality...can't be beat.  the team of johh, addah, arpi, jessica and all of them...saying they are there for you 24/7 isn't just something they say...they mean it.great team, caring, compassionate, humorous, you feel like you and your problem is their only concern.  and then the nursing staff and support staff once you get to your room!  you just want to take them home and make them part of the family.  thank you dr. oakes and team oakes!!!   you're simply the best.
fac_name: Keck Medicine of USC - Keck Hospital of USC

review: best staff! best hospital i have ever been in. that's all i have to say nothing negative what so ever..
fac_name: Keck Medicine of USC - Keck Hospital of USC

review: i went to see dr dale rice for a sinus issue and surgery and was happy with him.  he was highly recommended to us by a friend.  he knows his stuff and is a nice person.  i am a fan of his non nonsense in and out style......
fac_name: Keck Medicine of USC - Keck Hospital of USC

review:
doctors who performed the extensive surgery on my father were exceptional.  my father was in surgery for almost 4-1/2 hours.  when the doctor emerged he told us that we would be able to see our father about 2 hours.  similar to others who have complained about the pager system and cleanliness, we waited and after 2 hours finally went to the desk in the gold lobby to ask status.  they informed us that indeed dad was in recovery because the room that had been assigned wasn't cleaned yet.  after 4 hours - same answer.  since we were here since 5:00 am this morning and it was now 13 hours later, the admissions nurse called us and asked if we'd like to visit my father by facetime?  are you serious?  worst after care ever.  clean the hospital and understand that waiting visitors who were already anxious about their loved ones getting through a major surgery don't want to visit their loved ones by facetime.

hard to believe this is the number 16 hospital in the us.  a strong letter headed to us news and world report to contradict.

paul rivera

review:
well, as if it could not get any more insane.  i received a call from a case manager for ortho-neuro january 03, 2020 informing me the doctor discharged my brother.  let me give you the highlights.
during the course of the lengthy stay, he began suffering from severe delirium.  yes, he would see a cat in the corner of the room.  confusion was the word thrown around.   so back to the day of discharge. the case manager asked me what time i would be there to pick him up.
well, guess what? when i showed up to pick him up, he was not ready and no one on the nursing staff knew he was discharged.  let me just jump ahead. they lost his clothes and shoes he was wearing when admitted.  they attempted to dress him without washing him and he urinated on the pants i took him to wear  home. they washed him. dressed him in his turtle neck, and a diaper. what happened to paper scrubs or something, it was freezing that day.  i asked had they removed any ivs they said yes.    i had to insist on discharge orders.  discharge orders!  it was friday so there was no way he would be visiting a primary for prescriptions. i had to demand certain prescriptions and i had no idea, but they did not include a blood thinner and he almost died of a pulmonary embolism during this stay.  i was so stressed out, i asked for him to be transported by ambulance, plus i was embarrassed to have patient transport services wheel him down to the front entrance in a turtle neck and diaper.  i was given a number to call about the lost items. it was about 5pm, i left to meet home pharmacy technician and be at home when the ambulance arrived.   he arrived at 8:30pm via ambulance. the ladies were wonderful. they pointed out that he was not wearing anything from the waist down. they had covered him. they allowed me time to obtain pj bottoms before they placed him in bed.  the next day when i was helping him with hygiene, guess what was still in his arm?   his iv line. i called home health nurse and she graciously came out to the house and removed it.  i am the sole caregiver for my deathly ill brother.  my nerves are shot.  i feel like i let my brother down. 
i haven't called about the clothes and shoes yet. it's all too much. of course i would be responsible for following up, not them.  i am too tired and emotionally overloaded to sue for negligence.  after the last review, the head of ortho-neuro called.  this time, i am not repeating anything they can read in this review.

stay away from here!!!!
place is a joke. they screw up my wife's surgical procedure the day before then you go back as your in so much pain you can't stand it and we have waited now for over 5 + hours? and everyone else gets preferenced? no updates or communication. if you dare ask your not treated like you matter at all and that your bothering them. staff's overworked and understaffed.

review: the absolute worst er. waiting time is ridiculous! you could pass away by the time they complete your stay. their system is so poor. 7 to infinity waiting is normal. my wife came  in  ambulance with shortness of breath to only sit in waiting area for 6 hrs. took cat scan and check x-ray and waited the rest of the day.

i had outpatient surgery here this week. what a rollercoaster 

i had to arrive at 530a for a 730a procedure. i haven't had surgery since i was a child, but that seemed fine. until we got there and they didn't start calling patients back until almost 545a! seemed a little unprofessional. 

the nurses and techs who helped prep me were fantastic. super sweet and talkative which really helped quell my nerves. the anesthesiologist also came in and he was fun to talk to. (i'd had a pre-op call with an anesthesia nurse the friday prior, which was also good.) different techs came in to do different prep tasks, then my surgeon came in just to chat through things one more time. he seemed to be in a bit of a rush which wasn't the case at my consultation, but it put me a little on edge again.

as soon as he left, it was like the green berets of rns came in and things were in motion extremely quickly. there was also a high school student from gpnhs in there?? they must have given me the happy juice before she came in because in retrospect that's freaking weird. anyway, very little chatting and then i was on my way to the or. 

there were tons of people in there which i assume is normal. but that hs student was in there too! (oh, what gpf money can buy!) i barely remember anything past moving to the operating table. it would have been nice for my surgeon to stop in again before i was asleep.

when i woke up in recovery all i could hear was a nurse telling me to breathe deeply, and telling me that my surgeon couldn't find my husband. nice wake-up call but whatever. i couldn't breathe well because i was in a lot of pain. her only response was "that's normal, you just had major surgery". whuh?? i get that i had to get the anesthesia out but the total disregard for my pain and comfort was really frustrating. it's also so bright in there. i had to ask for a towel to put over my eyes. that nurse and another were concerned about my oxygen levels at one point, but i literally couldn't breathe deeply. i was really sad that they couldn't give me any tips/tricks for taking better breaths, but just kept snapping at me.

i then went to my private recovery room. my husband came back (he was at home, which is just around the corner). from this point on i was still in a lot of pain and kept telling the nurse there. her only solution was to "go get the doctor so he could admit for pain management". giant eye roll. maybe you could just be patient and give me an hour to 1. wake up and 2. let the meds kick in? so rude. surgeon came in again to follow up on one issue that came up, but he was in a huge rush again. not that i needed him to stay by my bedside but it was literally like "went well. put ice on the incision. bye." 

the initial recovery room nurse went on break evidently, so then a nurse named nan (pretty sure. i was a little high still, lol) came in. she was great. finally someone who helped me breathe normally, and recommended that i sit up in a chair to help with both the breathing and the pain. nan was so wonderful. she took my vitals one more time.

then i decided just to get my butt home so i didn't have to deal with the rush there anymore. the initial recovery nurse came back and once my husband helped me
get dressed, she was stripping the bed before i even got all the way into the wheelchair. nice exit. see ya.

like i said, a rollercoaster. like anyplace i'm sure there are good and bad employees. at times this really felt like a factory, though, which was disheartening. i'm thankful all the people who took care of me did so, though, and i trust the doctors here immensely. the experience just leaves some desires.
awful. took them taking blood 5 times to figure out my potassium was1.2 which is critically low.

very cold towards people. all staff seems like they are on they are angry at customer for coming in. they make me feel like a burden. doctors there jump to conclusions and do not bother to offer basic care. staff doesnt seem to listen very well.

do not take an ailing person, who can't keep up with what the doctors are doing to them every second, to this rehab. my 81 year old father almost died at this facility. i was trying desperately to tell the doctor and nurse that something was very wrong with my father and that he had been very sick all night long and that he was almost incoherent when i arrived in the morning. noone would listen to me until he was bleeding all over their floor and 911 had to be called. if i hadn't been there when it happened noone would have even known until it was too late. i was trying desperately to get someone to listen to me that something was terribly wrong, yelling even, and they told me to calm down. i was right in the middle of trying to see how to remove him from the facility when he started bleeding out. when the doctor came in the room he didn't even know it was blood and said it was just poop. it was not, it was obviously a lot of blood spewing out of him. when the paramedics arrived they knew immediately it was blood. he had to be transferred to st. rose hospital with a bleeding ulcer. his pressure had dropped because he lost so much blood. 
one week later they actually called to see how he was doing since he went home!! the people didn't even know he had been rushed out of there by ambulance and was still in the hospital. i will be hiring a lawyer. 
avoid this rehab if you care about your loved one. i wish i had known.

(i've talked with them about this) want to be there, want to help veterans. five stars.

(so happy they got a starbucks on the main floor.)

it took a while (they were super busy), but my husband was treated with compassion and thoroughness in the er.  after blood work and a ct scan, he was diagnosed with diverticulitis. he was sent home with meds from the hospital pharmacy to get him through until we could get to our pharmacy. it's definitely an improvement having the blood draw, etc., in triage before being seen by a doctor.  the doctor then had an idea of what may be coming their way.

my rating is based on the fact that this level 3 hospital is the primary facility serving the capital city of washington state.  until i entered the emergency room in mid november, i had only seen patients being treated in hallways on television shows.  i had never dreamed i would be one of those or that i would hear physicians breaking hipaa laws next to me so carelessly as they went over patient's medical history after confirming their 1st and surnames and continuing with incredibly personal information i would love to forget.
turns out the night i spent in that hallway, i was joined with about 40 others seeking medical care and this was what my physician called a "normal night" - not a crisis event.  has thurston county and our state never heard of crisis planning?  god help us if this area does ever need our medical facilities to step up when they can't handle a normal evening.  and shame on providence for not going to the state years ago and begging for a competitor to step into this region.  while medicine is about science; healthcare is about relationships and providence has failed in their relationship with the people who live in this area.  it's time for uw, swedish, chi or any caring nonprofit organization from outside wa to come here.  preferably to north lacey/dupont.  think about the future.  work with the nisqually tribe. plan a healthy relationship.  it's not brain surgery.
once you get passed the emergency room and are admitted, it's a very good hospital. last time we went there, they had updated the triage process and was quite fast getting people in and out.

nothing wrong with the doctors or anything, but the communication to representatives in the billing/financial aid department is the absolute worst. my bill was sent to collections because representatives constantly told me over the phone that my bill was covered or that my financial aid was being processed for another bill... then i got a notice in the mail saying my account had been collected. it's obvious sentara does not live up fully to their "pay what you can/as you go" message/motto because i spent almost over a year with this bull crap and got a collection notice for my account during the christmas holiday season. merry christmas to me right? lol. you all have some major work to do because of course i'm considering going somewhere else for my health needs now because of this absolute nonsense. a person with incredibly heavy anxiety should not have to deal with this. but you all want your money paid in full up front... yet say you stand for different. the billing department cares more about money than a patient's health, it's obvious.

review: i have had kaiser medical insurance coverage for quite a few years.  during that time, i have come across both good and bad doctors.  because the overall care and convenience kaiser provided in the past was fairly good i never considered switching to another health insurer.  however, in the past 3 years i have seen the quality of medical care and their doctors' concerns for their patients deteriorate.  six weeks ago, i accompanied my neighbor as she visited the kaiser hospital emergency room 3 times during a 48 hour period of time.  she was suffering with severe abdominal pain and swelling but did not have a fever.  the first 2 times the er doctors sent her home without offering any help because the abdominal cat scan did not show anything.  the er doctors totally ignored the fact that she was in a lot of pain, unable to eat, and also had a distended stomach.  as a result, she contacted the people in management at the hospital.  they told her that they would call the er department and for her to return to the emergency room immediately.  this time, under pressure from management, the er doctors consulted with a specialist.  although nothing showed up in the ultrasound or cat scan, the specialist figured out that she had an intestinal blockage.  as a result, they pumped out a huge amount of bile that had pooled in her stomach.  she had to spend the next 6 days in the hospital for additional treatment and testing.  during that time, they also discovered that she was bleeding internally.

been a cardiac patient for 20 years & moved to delray recently.
this week, i had the worst angina attack i have ever had. after my nitro tabs, no more chest pain, but i didn't feel right & my wife took me to this er.

day 1  emergency room
the main er dr. i saw, was dressed like she was attending a tennis match & was chewing gum with an open mouth, very unprofessional. her assistants were very professional.
i had not eaten all day & asked for a sandwich after being there about 5 hours. i was told 1 would be coming, but we waited. we all were joking that i was going to order a pizza.
an armed guard then wheeled in a wheelchair loaded with pizzas. i asked if he brought enough for everybody & was basically told stfu. very unprofessional. 
i saw an intern & she said i could eat. the nurses said no i can't. a male nurse (half my size) took a step towards me & raised his fist, like he was going to punch me. the 2 lead nurses made him back down, luckily for him. he was aggressive towards other er patients as well.
i was admitted for "chest pains" that i did not have.

day 2 cardiac telemetry unit
after being admitted to the cardiac telemetry area, the nurses were all amazing, each & every one of them. they care about their patients.
however, they were the only highlight of this journey.
an echo was ordered. they said they wanted to do a cta later in that day. as the echo started, i was told the cta would immediately follow. my wife was waiting in my room for a 20 minute test. after the echo was completed, (tech was great), i waited 20 minutes for a transport that never arrived. the echo tech wheeled me to the ct room for the cta.
i was prepped & put on the table, waiting 20 minutes for a nurse qualified to inject the contrast required for the test. none showed, but an emergency was brought in & i was removed from the room & waited in the hallway for another 30 minutes. i was then returned to my room. a little while later, i was brought back to the ct room & had the test. because of the delays, no results would be available until morning.

day 3 
after finally getting the results, the dr stated "the imaging indicated a 53% blockage, but we say it is 70%, so you need to go to the cath lab."
a cath was scheduled. the transporters came  & told me to remove everything except the gown. 
when i came out of the bathroom, they were both gone, as was my wife. wtf?
my wife returned in a minute, telling me they were called away for an "emergency in room xyz". my wife followed them to the nurses station, where they were just chatting. she also looked into room xyz & there were no medical people in the room.
it seemed the dr performing the procedure had not arrived yet.

their delays are causing me to spend more nights here. i am getting angry & have still not eaten today.

i demanded to see the head nurse. she showed up an hour later, with an attitude of "this is a hospital, we do what we want, how we want & when we want".
during this lovely heated discussion, the transport arrives & said something to the extent of "if you are not ready in 2 minutes, it will need to be rescheduled", raising my bp even more. my response was heard throughout the wing, "you need to learn some bedside manners, dude". 
he then transported me to the lab & he understood my frustrations after he heard about the numerous delays. we got along fine after that.
the test finished, people were really nice throughout.
because of the delays, i needed to spend yet another night.

mind you, the most nights i ever spent in a hospital for any of my heart attacks was 2 nights. now, with angina, i am spending 3 nights. huh????

day 4 cardiac step down
9am, they tell me i will be leaving today, just waiting for cardiologist & admitting doctors. the cardiologist's intern (really nice) came in before 11 and gave me a 1 minute rundown, not enough time for me to process what he was saying.
now, just waiting for the resident, who was another doctor that looked like she was out shopping, not attending patients in a hospital.
at 3pm, we were still waiting. i still have an iv connection in my arm & a heart monitor on. her intern finally shows up (much nicer than she is) & tells me i am being released. he also said that i can remove the heart monitor. i removed the monitor & got dressed. where are my new, expensive sandals? they were in my bag when i left the telemetry unit. not any more.
the nurse comes in & asks why i removed the monitor & i told her. she scolded me, but i understood why. again, the floor nurses were all great. the nurse removed my iv connection & off i went.

this hospital's great nurses are handcuffed by administration's greed.
the 2nd star is for the nurses.

it seems this hospital intentionally delays tests, to force patients to spend more nights. 
btw.... i have had angina throughout my cardiac history. i was never hospitalized for it
this hospital experience proves again, that...
healthcare in the usa, is not about health or care, only profit.

worst experience ever!!! horrible care, horrible hospital!! tried talking to administration they didn't care!! go anywhere but here!! nurses don't answer call buttons, no coverage at front nurses desk, my mom has severe pneumonia and has gone hours without breathing treatments as ordered, no p/t for days even though ordered, certain meds were supposed to be ordered and were not for 12 hours, a sonogram was ordered to rule out blood clots in her legs and when she was sent down to ultrasound and the orders apparently read to perform a sonogram on her arm, luckily my mom was coherent and corrected them. in a community where elderly people are often confused during a terrible illness, a hospital should be on top of their care, not making mistakes and excuses.  i spoke with the nurse leader she assured me she would look into the issues and correct them yet nothing changed.  not even water or clean cups to be found, aide's not knowing their patient assignments, nurses and aides claiming their batteries are dead in their phones so always unreachable for assistance. meds given 2 1/2 hours after when the are due. i think this hospital should be reported to the state. i am considering moving my sick mom to a safer hospital that can tend to her  needs. i can be reached via email at srosen9934@aol.com for any advocate who would like to reach out. i'm am truly appalled!!

i went to the atlanta va medical center to check on my eligibility for medical coverage yesterday and to update my information in the va system.  this is a big facility, with multiple parking structures.  this was my first time visiting this va med center.

parking was available in the rear parking structure, which is very large.  i wasn't exactly sure where to walk because there wasn't any signage instructing visitors to the main departments and which levels they're on.  i'm glad there was an information station with a live person just inside the second level med center entrance from the parking structure.  i asked directions to the eligibility department, and the woman there gave detailed and very accurate instructions.

i easily found the department, but, again, with no signage, i wasn't sure exactly where to go.  there was one very unhelpful man at the counter, and he asked what i needed.  i told him what i was there for, then took out some forms that i had already filled out.  he was too lazy to review my forms, and, thankfully, a very helpful woman, stephanie, saw what was happening, so she came over to me.  the lazy man (just on the other side of the counter) leaned back and told stephanie to find out what i needed.  stephanie physically walked around from behind the counter, came over to my side and asked me questions.  she quickly determined what i needed, so she led me to her desk, away from the department lobby, where she quickly reviewed my paperwork and then got an approval signature from her supervisor, who was also nice.  i was out of there with the eligibility approval that i needed, all within 30 minutes!

overall, i'm please with the assistance that i received from the three helpful va med center employees.  if i should have to visit this facility in the future, i hope to continue to have assistance from helpful employees.

pardon me... while i  figuratively, and thankfully, not literally, burst into flames in the atlanta va medical center!   this cautionary tale began with my arrival in the va medical center er around 11:00 in the morning and not leaving until 8:00pm.  it's no big secret and everyone pretty much knows that if you're going to take that leap of faith and go to the er, you better be mentally prepared to wait a long-time.  however, in this ominous pressure cooker of never ending calamity,  i was missed-placed, overlooked and abandoned for 3 full hours.  a staff nurse called me from the er waiting area and sat me in the back room of the er where i spent  3 lonely hours sitting in one chair  and staring at another.  the only thing that kept me from kicking in those latte colored walls was the reason i was there and the excruciating pain in my ankle.  i was holding tight to my last 3 drops of sanity.

while i'm not one to bash the va, i don't always want to lower my expectations when i walk through their doors either.  i understand that they are probably understaffed and overworked, like the rest of us but that can't be the excuse for poor service.  while there are several different ways i could end this review, i'm going to remember those physician assistants and nurses who stood proud and tried their best to make it right with me.  i'll remember those who apologized and personally took charge of the situation and made sure that i was treated like something other than a number.  and finally, a big shout out and thank you to the nurse who applied my splint, took me to the pharmacy to pick up medication and pushed the wheelchair to my car in the parking garage.

i'll always expect better of all va medical centers, but until further notice...

yes this facility like most va medical center is overwhelmed with veterans. for my experience here so far i think a four star rating is more appropriate. like most hospitals, there are isolated and unfortunate incidents that take place. the staff that served me are very caring and professional staff. the nurses went out of their way to make sure i understood why they asked me their questions and i understood my health concerns and what to expect. 

the pharmacy tech personally came and explained why it will be a longer wait for my meds. 

also, the doctor saw me in a reasonable amount of time and came 3 times so far to make sure i'm being taken care of. so if it's warranted, i will update my review but i think the staff here truly do their best to care for everyone.

my father went in for a torn bicep and shoulder. he has been getting the run around from the atlanta va for two weeks. very rude. finally he went to the er because his arm was such a problem. went in at 5 pm and left at 4:30 am after not receiving any aid. this is not how people who served the country should be treated. the people at this location were extremely rude and did not care at all about the people who came in. this place needs a complete overhaul.

unfortunate, but i had to update my review from years ago. not sure if its due to renovations or time of year (middle of winter, so a lot of sick folks coming in) but i recently had a family member make an emergency visit and the entire visit was just an epic disaster. my family member was admitted to the er and couldn't get a bed for close to 24 hours. the er had my family member hanging out in a hallway the entire time. granted, it was not a life or death emergency, but does it take almost 24 hours to actually find a bed/room for someone? once said family member was in their room, it was just a cluster in terms of what was going to happen next in terms of tests and what not. apparently nothing had the ability to be scheduled and it was just waiting around for days only to find out 5 minutes beforehand that said family member was being taken away for testing. i get that the hospital is busy but jeez, you have to provide the family with some type of schedule or heads up? then it was deemed that the family member needed to go to lij for a test and it was another sit and wait for a few more days for 'a bed to open up' only to find out once my family member was there, it seemed like there were plenty of beds to be had at the floor the family member was moved to. not to mention, lij just seemed to have there ish in order way more than north shore and was cleaner.

review:
we had a less than favorable experience a few days ago at the lcom er. the er was a mess and seemed no better than what i'd expect harbor general to be like. we have very little experience in an er setting so maybe my expectations are unrealistic.

for starters, the was place filthy. the sheet on the triage nurse's intake bed was dirty.  people, we're in the middle of the corona virus problem! that thing should be changed after every patient. just so you know, i went back the next day almost 24 hours later to get some paperwork and that same dirty sheet was still on there with the same identifiable dirty shoe marks and stains. at the time of admittance, i was happy my husband was even being seen so i didn't make a fuss. in hindsight, i should have said something. 

most important however, was the lack of care he received by the attending physician dr. lu. he was impersonal and spoke very condescendingly to us. my husband was treated on a bed in the hallway the entire time hooked up to a heart a portable heart monitor!  here's a person with a heart condition and skyrocketing blood pressure, dizziness and whose been vomiting.  no blood work done, urine taken but not evaluated, and no fluids given.  and yes, i do feel entitled to decent care - i'm going to pay my bill! 

i think the main problem is too many people in our community use the er like a doctor's office with common ailments because they can't be turned away for lack of insurance or ability to pay. the staff are like robots with the barrage of problems that walk through the door. 

i'm sharing my experience because we are concerned at the level of healthcare available to us in our community during an emergency situation. is what we experienced an isolated event or is this the norm at our community er?

besides couple regular check ups, this was my very first actual experience with both the er and inpatient care. fortunately, it wasn't for me. unfortunately, it was for my mom. then again, super fortunate that everything was more than i could hope for her. 

long story short, i had to take my mom to arlington memorial er after having been to md arlington er just right before. there wasn't anything wrong with md arlington, but per my mom's doctor recommendation, based on which specialty doctors they had on staff that night vs arlington memorial. needless to say, it was a very long friday night of emotional rollercoaster.

when we arrived at tham er, i immediately told the front desk my mom's symptoms and how we were told by her doctor to come here, in less than a min after filling out the 1, possibly 2 page document, they took my mom in right away, started running several different tests on her. she was seen by a doctor, x-ray technician, a nurse, all within 20mins. 

it took them a little longer after that to do a few more tests, go over the findings, and complete administering her to inpatient, before they could move her upstairs to settle in. never been to any inpatient room before, i was quite surprised to see how nice and spacious her room is. besides all the necessary medical equipments, it comes fully equipped with 2 sinks, private bathroom with shower, a couch, 32in tv, and a closet. honestly, i wouldn't mind having to spend a week or 2 here.

i never gotten a chance to meet her doctors since i could only stay with my mom at night, and all doctors do their rounds during day time. however, her nurse, annie, was excellent, extremely helpful, and informative. not only did she attend all of my mom's needs during her night shift, she was very informative and patient with all of our questions.

just like most hospital, it could be a bit confusing to navigate around. luckily, they have a lot of signs to tell you what is what and which direction to go, also, they have an information desk with volunteers that would be more than happy to walk with you to where you need to go. there are also 2 big garages that provide plenty of free parking for your convenient.

all in all, our experience was much more than i could hope for. it definitely wasn't a good thing we had to come to the hospital, but i'm glad we came to tham!

i spent several hours in the er a few months ago and for the most part, had a great experience in the hospital itself.  the radiology tech and the nurse who tended to me in my room were excellent and made me feel well cared for.  

this hospital's billing department, however, would get negative stars if i could give them.  even though lbh is in network with my insurance, and even though my explanation of benefits explains that no further charges are to be billed to me after my copay, i still received a $12,000 bill for my stay.  the issue has not been resolved for over a month of my insurance company assuring me i do not owe the money and three different answers from people at lower bucks' billing department.  i've been told they only need a few days to adjust my claim and told my insurance company has rejected the claim (which made my insurance rep laugh when i called them and place a call on my behalf, which still did not resolve the issue).  i've been told it would be resolved in a couple of days, then told to give it two weeks, then told they don't know when it will be resolved, so this outrageous $12k bill that my insurance lists as non-billable is just hanging over my head.

was 302 earlier this month. i had a psychotic episode, so please believe me when i say i needed inpatient admission.   during the initial 120 hr stay, i was told that there would be a hearing on the 5th day and that the hospital was going to recommend a 303 and keep me for 20 more days.  when i almost broke down, i was told that it was standard practice and that the court would make the final decision.  was told i would have a public defender to represent me.  to prepare, i made sure i took my meds, attended each group therapy session (where i told my story umpteen times to the same  therapists and fellow patients) practiced good hygiene, basically anything that i could possibly do to prove that i was compliant and would remain compliant if disharged.  the 5th day came, and the psychiatrist called me out of a therapy session, and introduced me to the attorney appointed for me.  when the word "hearing" is used it is common knowledge that you go to either a court house (or other venue where a judge of some level conducts legal proceedings) and that your attorney will brief you as to what to say and when to say it.  its also good when the attorney is on your side, hence the word defense.  this was not the case.  the attorney told me on the spot that he was going with the hospital's recommendation of a 303 with a maximum of 20 days.  i felt sick.  i asked "what about the hearing?"  he told me "there is no actual hearing.  i just submit a recommendation to a judge.  but that doesnt mean you will be here all 20 days.  thats just the maximum".  he then said goodbye and both he and the psychiatrist walked away.  i was overwhelmed with anxiety and could not return to the group.  i went to my room and cried for hours.  nothing else was said.  anytime i had questions, they were met with a terse "just keep going to group and take ur meds and we'll see what happens"  i actually, by chance, found out from another patient what the real story was.  they base your discharge date on how well your insurance pays, and if you are being discharged to a recovery house or some sort of residence. i was being discharged to my wife, that was the plan.    all i could do was be compliant, don't give anyone a hard time, and they might shave some time off.  well, the fact that i am writing this means that im out.  7 days shy of my max.  i think my insurance questioned them and they relented.  the psychiatrist i saw shaved my medication regiment to her own form, and had nothing positive to say to me.  i think its also telling that even though she saw me every single day since my admission, she did not see me today.  not to even finalize discharge instructions.  they keep you cooped up, not allowed outside (even though i was told that sleeping late everyday when at home robbed me of vitamin d and fresh air, lol)  like i said, about the meds, the dr. cut down my night meds and i couldnt get a full night sleep with people popping in and out of your room at night (even though all patients are on candid camera) the food was half decent and they did have 3 times a day where you could get a snack, so if your meal was gross, you wouldnt starve.  unfortuneatly, things were tightened down this past week because the state was doing an inspection.  i dont blame the nurses or the techs.  i blame the program.  if i ever suffered another crisis, i would ask to be taken to horsham house.  atleast you can smoke/go outside.

wow! i am amazed by the turn around of this hospital! my boyfriend had a scheduled heart procedure with dr. kiningsberg, the staff was welcoming and organized throughout the whole visit! the front desk entrance were nice and happy, the insurance people were calm and reassuring, the nurses for pre-op were comforting and detailed oriented, the doctors were informative and successful, the recovery nurse ria was so sweet and reassuring while taking care of chris. the rn nurses alexa and paulette were great, very informative and caring.  the nurse  director joe came in a checked on us and ask how the service of his nurses was, and we can see the amazing work he has done with the team! there is not one bad thing i had to say about this visit! i was pleasantly surprised! i will definitely be making the longer drive to come back here! highly recommend!

the food choices were actually vegetarian friendly and really tasty for a hospital. and the elder brit volunteer by the name of jean calmed everyone in the pre-op waiting area. chatting with her really put my mind at ease, she was so lovely.

of course i can't do a review without a few minor gripes though. 1. this campus is huge and very intimidating at first. once you've gone a few times, it's much easier to navigate. the food court and gift shop are a really nice touch. 2. the parking sucks! if you're just there for a short visit, your best bet is to just go with the valet at the main entrance. save yourself the aggravation! if you're having a surgery they do give you a parking pass...but good luck getting to the parking garage. not really user friendly. 3. my surgery was delayed by 5 hours due to an emergency surgery that was squeezed in right before mine. that really messed up everyone's day, but way she goes! 

overall, now i have a better idea of what to expect should there be a next time. i will continue my relationship with uh hospitals as long as i live in northeast ohio. they really are top notch. (alot more compassionate than cleveland clinic).

i had a 50/50 experience here. i've unfortunately been in and out of what is now called "ascension" the last few days, having emergency surgery and extreme post surgery pain. while i experienced some great and quick care from some of the nurses, doctors and surgeons i also had very poor experiences with other "professionals" that i was getting "care" under that honestly leave's me baffled, disgusted and angry. the people at the er desk and the initial intake were good as well as registration. no complaints there at all. the first rn i had, mark, was great as well. very caring and helpful. the rest of the team that i was under that night was timely and great too, from the doctor to the surgeon and his entire team. i wish i could remember the doctors name but i fail to as i was in a lot of pain and hadn't got much sleep the previous night due to waking up from the pain. the surgeon was brett larsen. him and his team were absolutely great. the second visit i had just last night/this morning wasn't so pleasant. the first rn i had, stephen, was also great. very helpful and caring along with the handful of doctors that came to check my mysterious pain out. but after he had left i seemed to get every rude out of line nurse on the block and the timing of care started to lag. i felt and still completely feel they were entirely insensitive, blatantly rude, complaining to a patient who was in immense pain, poor in explaining any details of what was going on and things i should know, and on a grumpy power trip?  unbelievable and completely unprofessional. i eventually decided to leave a little earlier than i wanted to because i was entirely fed up with the way i was being treated and handled all in all. even the woman who did my ct scan was rude. the last doctor i had was great thank god. she was totally aware and understanding of my frustrations and was so helpful and comforting. if not for the handful of actual caring professionals i would write off ascension genesys as a place totally unfit for ill people to receive quality care and treatment. granted i still find that questionable and won't be going back there if ever needed in the future. with all of this said i also want to say that i do realize and understand that it is a very tough profession as my mother has been in the medical field her entire working career but even aside of that i feel i'm intelligent and aware enough of the many different challenges and stressor's they often have to deal with probably on the daily but regardless, if you can't treat an honest, cooperative, young patient who is  in serious pain with basic manners and decency then you have absolutely no damn business being in the field of which you care take of people. the last nurse i had was argumentative and i honestly feel she was oddly enough trying to power trip over me in our last couple interactions. she had the nerve to try and tell me what i did or didn't experience and how i felt. i am going back to collect my medical records and to speak with whomever this should concern. if you've read this entire rave thanks for hanging until the end and a big thank you to the professional's who did their job well. i hope everyone's experiences were/are better than mine.

doctors don't listen to folks in the instance of determining a patient who has panic disorder or anxiety. i've been admitted to this hospital 5 times this year for various issues and was almost immediately bucketed into a 'non-emergency' or what i would refer to as a 'lower-tier' case even when trying to explain to a doctor what is going on; it never mattered because in my case, i have a history of panic disorder & anxiety.   

this is beyond frustrating and given the cost of 'doing business' at this establishment and the hyper-inflated self published "reviews" about various wings of the hospital i.e the cardiology/cardiac departments various awards and recognition's as well as the marketing dollars kaweah delta's pr firm dumps into crafting a would-be 'medical mecca' - one would expect that the services rendered here would be top tier and sadly, they are not. 

respectfully, i would not recommend this hospital to anyone i actually cared about. especially not other friends or family members who may suffer from panic-related mental disorders as they would likely be quickly shuffled out the door regardless of whether or not something else is actually occurring or not.

the general accommodations available for people here are excessively underwhelming. if you're not being carted in via ambulance you can expect to sit and wait for hours in the waiting area to then be shuffled into a tiny 'intake' area where you are forced to sit in a micro-cubical style room where you're then stuck basically sitting in the person next to you's lap being further exposed to god knows viral/bacterial contaminates, general illnesses, and mental breakdowns. all the while you're bound to receive looks of malcontent and disgust from the medical staff as not a single one (in my experience) looked as though they wanted to be working at this particular hospital. 

once arriving in intake you're then destined to sit there for another 30-45 minutes while you wait for a doctor to acknowledge your existence. while waiting you can expect a nurse or cna to come by and have you sign a few documents and acknowledge that the hospital is going to sodomize your wallet in exchange for 'quality' bottom of the barrel care.

after you've survived the waiting game and the intake gauntlet it is then up to the doctors' discretion as to whether or not you're actually going to be admitted i.e transferred to a room where you can expect to wait another 1-2 hours minimum before a 'provider' comes in to further assess your financial fortitude in making you fully aware of the excessive charges you are about to receive for seeking medical assessment and care.

in 4/5 of my visits to this hospital in the last 8 months, i spent about 4-5 hours (minimum) waiting to receive at most 20 minutes of face time with an actual doctor who then would dismiss me based on my pre-existing conditions.

tl:dr - i'd strongly recommend and encourage everyone to seek emergency medical care from other establishments in other cities, especially if you suffer from any form of mental disorder.

i had to come here recently because i got really sick! i was really nauseous and felt like i was going to pass out. i came late at night, and fortunately i was checked in quickly. 

i was surprised at the cleanliness of the environment and the friendliness of the staff. i was pretty scared that something was going on with my heart because my dad has heart problems.. a nurse named kyle (guy with a short, cool beard) made me feel a lot better. he was really friendly and he was definitely knowledgeable! i kept asking a lot of questions because i was nervous but he was happy to answer me without hesitation. 

i was discharged within what i felt a reasonable amount of time and the doctor gave me a good cardiologist to see later. def recommend coming here if you're nearby! hopefully you get kyle!

review:

the rooms themselves were very nice and were cleaned everyday. all of the daytime nurses were very available and knowledgeable and the doctors took great care of me. 

the only two things i can complain about is one the food is absolutely terrible. i don't expect much from hospital food but if i'm being honest theirs is boardering on inedible. the other thing is the night shift nurses really don't compare to the day. while none of them were terrible they were far less helpful and knowledgeable than the day shift. i had one nurse at night that i just clashed with but beyond that they were just okay in comparison to the day shift that i think was amazing.

overall this hospital lives upto it's great reputation, i hope to never have to go back but if i do the care they give us top!
