review:
https://www.romper.com/p/the-failure-of-baby-friendly-initiatives-19374870

i've considered taking this post down, but i can't. it's been 5 months since my baby was born, but i still feel like my baby and i were not taken care of properly. this article helps explain what i experienced.

st. rose, i really think you should consider not being a baby friendly hospital, or at the very least having a more hands-on policy for mothers who have a c-section surgery. looking back, i really struggled breastfeeding after a major abdominal surgery because i couldn't sit up all the way... and to me that sounds like common sense. i could barely move and i struggled to walk. my baby lost weight, and i was recovering from a major surgery. anyone with common sense would've given me a bottle of formula so i could rest and recover. i'm not sure why a trained nurse didn't see my baby lost 10% of her weight and was dehydrated. she needed  something to eat, but i was pushed to only breastfeed. someone dropped the ball here. i hope this doesn't happen to any mother again. please review your processes to protect your moms and babies.

this hospital claims to be a "baby friendly hospital", but it doesn't seem like they really care about my baby at all. i ended up having a c-section, and i have been trying to breast feed on schedule, but my baby lost over a pound because i'm not producing enough milk. the doctor told me i need to supplement my baby's feeding with formula. which is so devastating to hear because i really want to breast feed her and i have been trying so hard to make sure i'm doing it right. so today when we are about to be released to go home, i asked them for some formula to get us through the next feeding...  the nurse and the charge nurse refused to give me even one bottle. the charge nurse had the audacity to shame me by asking me if i'm even breast feeding! i've been doing everything i can to feed my baby. my milk simply hasn't come in yet. she kept telling us that my nurse was correct to follow hospital policy, and there is nothing she can do for us. my husband tried to reason with the charge nurse, and she didn't want to talk to him. she just kept saying, "can i just talk to her (me)." i also tried to reason with her by telling her how concerned i am for my baby's weight loss, and that i'm not asking for a box of formula, just enough to get us through the next feeding so we can settle in at home and my husband can go to the store to buy some. her response was, "just to make you happy i'll give you one bottle, but just so you know it's against our baby friendly policy". her attitude, condescending tone, and over all mom-shaming really breaks my heart. i'm a first time mom who needed an emergency c-section. i am devastated that my baby lost weight, and here i have these nurses making me feel bad that i haven't been able to produce enough milk to nourish my baby. they don't want to give me formula to help my baby, and made me feel like i'm begging for one bottle of formula just to get me through one feeding. all the other nurses have been over the moon, but to see that management can't make a reasonable call on giving a struggling mom some formula and that hospital policy is more important than the health of my baby is unbelievable. i cannot believe how a "baby friendly" hospital won't actually help my baby. i'm devastated and heart

review:
i was in-patient at healthsouth for 11 days and it was one of the most wonderful facilities/"hospitals" i've ever been in.  the entire staff is fantastic.  they were a life changer for me.  by the time i was being discharged, i didn't want to go home! dr. savitz, dr. lee, dr. hakim are fantastic doctors along with any i may have forgotten! not one bad experience.  i really loved the staff too.  my nurses, allison, cindy, rabia and the rest (i'm sorry, i had made a list of all their names so i'm so sorry i forgot!) we're all some of the best nurses around! the best supporting staff, ot (gayle) a trainee was great, along with her trainer (i forgot her name but she was sweet and extremely knowledgeable.  i have to say i had most of my pt with amy (and others who were great as well) and she is one of the best, most skilled physical therapists i've ever had the pleasure of being a patient of.  i miss her! who says that about their physical therapist?! she really is a gift from up on high to anyone that becomes her patient.  she is such a great therapist, but just just a very bright woman.  she wasn't just god at the physical therapy part, but she is great at working with people and just so clever at finding ways to figure out things that may be difficult for someone with any injury.  
       for me, my left ankle was painful and stiff coming down the stairs.  i was always told and respectively, with a bad leg you only use the good one the stairs, so i would always lead with the good leg.  when i got better, i had a stiff ankle that wouldn't elevate and vice-versa coming down the stairs.  i would come down on my good leg and have to essentially do a small hop as my left ankle wouldn't flex enough and would in fact snap (painfully) as a result of my injury.  so she taught me (for example, one of the many great things she did teach me) to lead with the good going up the stairs and when coming down, whether on crutches or even with just my legs, using the railings to lead with that ankle, then come down on my "good leg" which makes it much easier for me.  
      i've had many complications from a complete broken leg, where i've needed a im rod, locking screws, a plate with 4 more screws.....all of which, except the 4 locking screws for the im rod, will be with me forever.  i would have had to suffer with that forever if not for amy i.'s help, teachings and training.  she was so conscientious of how i was feeling mentally, physically and emotionally that even she could see when i was not feeling well as i'd almost get the spins (which seems to be an inner ear problem that i am now getting help with as an outpatient that i wouldn't have known.)
barbara, my case manager was fantastic.  joan jackson was a staff member who also deserves a shout out.
i honestly never saw anything as what was described in some other negative reviews.  everyone was attentive, prompt, efficient and friendly.  been twice.  the second time i had a choice and i chose to go here.  nobody i know likes going to physical rehab, but this was the place for me.

review:
this place needs to be closed down! communication with family is horrible, my father in law went in for depression, they never picked up how confused he was. they never had him shower or wash for the week he was there. they told us, they would go over his discharge plan when we picked him up, he was sitting in a wheel chair with his bags packed. they also said someone would call with follow up care, he already had appointments made that he didn't know about and changes to his medications. 
i know it is very hard to find good mental health facilities, but he was 78 years old! communication with family goes a long way!

if you are able to commute and don't mind 30 minutes of driving, i highly reccommend this hospital. i had my best birthing experience here, and every time i go to the er i'm out within 3 to 4 hours. hospital is super clean and quiet. get triaged right away and in some cases placed into a room with in minutes. i rather wait in a clean quiet hospital for 3-4 hours then a local dirty, filled with sick people and crazies for over 3-4 hours.

this will be my second encounter with this er. my first was with my father-in-law. that was 4 years ago and now here i sit with my husband for his hypertension. i understand that this is a tricky thing to treat. 

i just wish practicing doctors had a more appealing bedsmanner. i also wish that insurance would allow doctors to do their job in a more practical way. which might allow for things to move smoothly. 

our service was and wait time was fairly quick because of what we came in for. however my husband left completely dissatisfied and with the exact same medication and with his bp 168/101  how do you leave a hospital like that? 

is that not an emergency? do you not need to alter your meds? i think so? my goodness? i cannot recall the service that we got for my father-in-law but it wasn't stellar. i just knew we were in the area and we needed to go now! and this was the closest now place.

my boyfriend  and i went to the er the  beginning of july 2019.  we were at home and he went to having a seizure, then wet himself. i took him to this hospital because it was the closest one to us. dropped him off at the emergency drop off no one person came out to help me to get him in a wheel chair. took him to the front desk and went back to the car to go park. as soon as i got in  they were already giving him attitude because he was not responding. they took an hour and a half to get us back to a room and that was because i was complaining. the guy was watching something on youtube, the other person was face timing her son. we finally got to the back and of course he started complaining about his head hurts. the nurse was trying to talk to him but he was in and out of sleep. he was trying to talk but wasn't getting far. so i was speaking for him letting her know what happened, he started shaking and wet himself, hours before. after an hour or so in the room i get up to go use the restroom. wasn't gone for more then 3-4 minutes. i get back to the room and the nurse tell me were discharging him because he's no incorporating. he tells her please giving me something for my head and i'll talk. he stated to her that something popped in my head. she also said the dr came in 3/4 time and tried to talk to him bs!!! i was in the room the whole time but left to use the rr. then she prescribe allergy medication!! wtf.  he told her give me a few minutes to so i can get myself together, then  she say ill give you 5 minutes because we need the room. i told her you cant discharge without getting seen by the dr. i told her i want to see another dr and she says you will have to start the whole process all over again as in go back outside and wait for another dr. we went home and he started getting worse i took him the hermann memorial woodland and with in 30 min they did blood work and a scan of his head. he had a brain aneurysm and they informed me that life flight will be here in 12 minutes to take him to the medical center. sure enough life flight was there. you guys send people home to die and she  profiled him because he wanted something for his head.will never go back to this place and will let everyone know about this sorry excuse of a hospital.

bon secours just bought this hospital. i think this is a good move considering that it can't get much worse.

there is a doctor here who performs a knee replacement surgery--from what i hear, he's excellent. this is the primary reason people choose this hospital.

if you're actually sick, having an emergency, go to obici in suffolk. yeah, i know you'll have to drive, but your safety and wellness are worth it.

had a great experience at clark regional medical center! got me right in and the nursing staff took great care of me! did an mri and got right to the problem. doctor was friendly and knowledgeable! feel much better! thank you!

knew someone who went in for extreme pain in her neck. they didn't run any tests and just assumed it was a strained neck. the didn't offer any help and were extremely rude to her. they claimed they sent a prescription for muscle relaxers for her to a cvs but when she got there she discovered that they never sent her prescription. she is still in lots of pain and struggles to do basic things without feeling it.

several people in the family including myself have been in uci hospital saved my grandsons life after a near fatal accident. as well as me, when i had septic shock and restored my hearing and knee replacement for my wife after a fall down some stairs. 

i highly recommend uci to everyone. 
the doctor's, nurses, technicians are world class. 
there are many names that i would like to say thank you to dr. alessio pigazzi, dr. david so, dr. brian smith & dr. hamid djalilian

is zero stars even an option? i would first like to say that if you are coming here for an elective surgery, joint replacement or others, do not come here, run as far as you can. 

my grandmother was scheduled 12/18/19 @7am for a total knee replacement, preop, or & pacu were awesome.

once she was admitted to the ortho floor (3rd floor) we were welcomed by the nursing manager, daniel bernstein, my grandmother is rolled into the corner of the hallway where we wait hours for her to get into a clean room. the hallway was "equipped" with a call light (silver desk bell), a pulseox monitor that was not being monitored at the nurses station because she is in the hallway, a privacy curtain that did not cover or provide any privacy and the list goes on (all pictured below). this not just a privacy concern but a real safety concern. the cords from the bed and all the machines she was hooked up too were crisscrossing along the floor where my handicapped grandfather almost fell! i asked for my concerns to be escalated when daniel said "we escalate this all the time", just blowing me off, noooo daniel i want to speak to someone else regarding this issue, so here i am writing this review as i wait. 

according to the academy of medsurg nursing: the practice of admitting patients to hallway beds while they await appropriate room assignments is patently unsafe and should never be used.

patients must be provided adequate space, privacy, comfort, and safety at all times. hallway beds do not provide clinicians with bedside access to equipment, such as oxygen, suction, and call lights, needed for safe provision of care. patients are at greater risk for falls and other adverse events if they cannot access a call light or be monitored appropriately by nurses.

she wanted the lights to be off, the thermostat adjusted, non of which can be done because this is a hallway. it was no surprise that my grandmother would be admitted to the hospital following her surgery so why was the hospital so poorly prepared? they have signs plastered every where saying "a quiet environment is a healing environment", well when you are in a hallway you can't just close the door. you are exposed to the chaos of the unit, the chemicals from house keeping, the constant call lights & phones ringing.

my last concern is for the nursing staff. how do you expect your nurses to provide adequate care if they can't even get to the patients bed. "your safety and health is our main concern", well then get patients out of the hallways then, safety is not a concern, money is. value money over patient safety, satisfaction & health.

you need to really ask how this is safe, how can you provide care to a patient in the hall, what if an emergency occurs then what? how about fire code violation? hipaa? i'm sure joint commission would love this....

but i will end this on a good note, our charge nurse hoang & primary nurse laura are the only good thing about this place. way to go hoang & laura. you are both worth 10 stars!

i came here to the er 5 hours ago with chest pain, heart palpitations and sky-high blood pressure. i was seen immediately and had an abnormal ekg and then a chest x-ray and blood work followed. that was 4.5 hours ago. no updates- nothing. everyone else that arrived at the same time as me have come and gone but i've received no update.

my mom died at 55 of a heart attack and since my ekg was abnormal, i'd assume there would be more of an urgency.

this place has a culture of undertrained and pissed off people who don't have too much concern on patient health and safety.

i'll be switching my insurance to kaiser and using the va in the meantime. yes, the va gives better service than uci medical.

i came here with my wife. i got here at 12am so we're do i start  it's pretty dirty not clean . i understand it's emergency room n it's very busy. but they took seven hours and out time here we saw two strokes or seizures they leave people in th er waiting room to long

" i have to add here, that this is the explanation that one of the staff gave me, i am not even sure it was correct, because before that she said "we are charging you because your insurance didn't pay their part for another statement until december, and now we are charging you the interest". if this is true, can you imagine? they charge you arm and leg for a simple visit, then you pay the bill and then you have to pay interest too?

crazy , crazy amount of charges. they charged 3 times the amount of other medical clinic for some simple tests. i was seen by a resident, oversaw by a doctor, and got charged by both. then another charge for visiting the lab, then multiple charges for lab test. all were at 3 , 4 times the amount of other labs.

nightmare experience going to uci er sunday, 2/23/20, with a dislocated shoulder.  dr matonis was the resident doctor.  they would not give me a mask saying i was not contagious. the box of masks was empty.  i got a real bad cold/cough at uci a month ago from the rn that was wearing a mask because he was sick with a cold.  i was sick that very night we left uci.  i had not gone anywhere else so knew i got it from that rn wearing the mask.   that is why i wanted a mask - to prevent getting sick again.  but, they would not give me one.  
i asked the doctor if she ever had put a shoulder back in the socket and was told she had done it many times and that every week someone comes in with a shoulder dislocated.  i soon found out she had no idea what to do and wondered if i was her first patient.  she had to ask the attending doctor how to put in lidocane. the attending doctor was instructing her.  when she was twisting my arm up and all around she kept asking the attending doctor if she was doing it right.  after 10 minutes of no luck and pain i told her i wanted an ortho doctor called in.   i told her an ortho doctor could do it.  i see on tv all the time where doctors put the shoulder back in the joint in a minute.  she refused to call out to the ortho doctor on-call and said they now have to try weights.  the tech tried to put weights around my elbow.  it caused a lot of elbow pain, so he then tried around my wrist.  extreme pain on my wrist.  i told him why don't you attach to my upper arm since that is closer to the dislocation.  he went out and  created the device to wrap around my upper arm and that worked.  that tech did a great job.  i wondered if they do this all the time how come no one knew how to relocate my shoulder and they would not call-out to an experienced doctor that would know what to do.  
the doctor also had another set of x-rays to see if after all her twisting it was now in the socket.  i told her it was not and that i did not want all the extra radiation when i knew it was still out.  she said radiation was low.   results showed shoulder was not in the socket.  i also told her those weights are not going to work and i want an ortho doctor.  she said we need to go in order and weights is the next step.   as the weights were hanging from my arm dr matonis told me to yell out when the shoulder goes back in the joint.  i told her i did not know it was out to begin with so how an i suppose to know when it goes back in.  she said i will know which is ridiculous because after they finally got my shoulder back in the joint the pain was still the same.  she kept telling me it would feel better.  it is now a week later and i still could not tell you if my shoulder is in the joint.  the pain in the middle of the upper arm is exactly the same.    
when the weights did not work she asked me if i wanted her to try again to force my arm in the joint.  i told her again i want an ortho doctor.  she said after weights the next step is to put me under in the trauma room.  i said what makes you think you can to it when i'm asleep, if you can't do it when i'm awake.  she said my arm will be easier to manipulate.  i again told her to try.  another male resident was pushing on the back of my shoulder as hard as he could.  his hard pushing would have hurt if he did that on any part of my body.  meanwhile, she was twisting my arm trying to get it in the socket.  the uci ladies (two) that would alternate sitting in the room across from my room (watching the patient in that room) kept turning their chairs around so they could watch.  they stared as if watching tv.  it was so rude! ! the doctors - resident, attending, rn, never thought to close my door a little so i could have privacy. 
after pushing/pulling, weights, pushing/pulling, she said we now should put you under. i again told her i want an ortho doctor and that an ortho doctor could have resolved this a long time ago.  she again told me she could do this. she said she was having such a hard time getting my shoulder back in because i waited so long to come in (i came in 5 hours after the fall).  this is a typical response from a woman that cannot get the job done and so blame their lack of expertise on the patient.  while waiting for a trauma room i asked the rn about getting an ortho doctor.  he said he did call-out.  dr matonis never told me that.  the trauma room was finally available.  it did not look to me like anyone was in any of the trauma rooms to begin with.  she told the tech to put a mask on me, but he told her is was not needed, since i had the nose tube. she then told others in the room that they will learn a lot when the ortho doctor comes.  after it was over the tech told me ortho, dr choi, was there and assisted.  dr matonis never told me anything.  never saw her after.  they wrapped  shoulder stabilizer around my bra under my clothes.  my belly showed. no one helped.  now x-rays show a possible fracture which did not show in 1st set.

review: i'm truly surprised why anyone would or could give this place anything other than 5 stars. it's easy to drive to, (yes there is construction but it's clear where you need to park), the staff is unbelievably competent and kind (from reception to the surgeons to the discharge nurses), the facility is clean, discharge instructions are clear, and the food is good. the waiting area is incredible - you get to watch the status of whomever you are there with at the hospital. i was there for major surgery and i felt calm, informed and most of all cared for the entire time. also leading up to the surgery the phone calls for registration and billing we're professional and easy. this place is  5 stars all the way.

avoid elective imaging here.  go to a different imaging center when you make an appointment for a ct, mri, or bone scan.  the radiology dept at this inova location is immature, lies, gossip, and talks about patients in front of other patients.  scans are not done accurately.  lead radiology technicians lack ethics and engage in name calling of patients.

our little guy had his first er visit last night and i am so pleased with his care i had to write a review. specifically to give kudos to katie who was not our assigned pediatric er nurse but was someone our toddler latched onto. katie sat with him and played with him off and on for the four hours we were in the hospital which really made his experience (and ours) a lot less stressful. the entire staff was amazing but katie was particularly great. the only reason why i'm giving it four instead of five stars was the wait time. we were there for four hours just for a vital check and a ct scan. this did seem to be a particularly busy day for ct scans and i am sure preference was given to those in more traumatic situations than ours but for the little guy, the wait was rough. the radiology team was fantastic as well. thank you again for making our first er visit a lot less traumatic

this was the worst hospital stay!!!! go somewhere else!!!

they literally forgot about me for over 24 hours!!! they also misdiagnosed me, which was brutal. the whole stay was awful. the iv in my hand left a scar and was extremely painful damaging my vein. i kept asking them for extra blankets, which they refused me due to my fever until it turned out....the air conditioning knob was installed incorrectly so when it said it was off, it was actually on high! i had 104.3 fever with high a/c on me and 1 hospital blanket. ridiculous! if my friend hadn't gotten me balloons we would have never been able to prove it. when they forgot about me, they didn't do any vital checks, didn't feed me, and i even ran out of toilet paper/extras, to which i had to call the nurse button from the bathroom - humiliating. there was also no remote for the tv in my room so i had to stand up and walk over to the tv with my iv bag every time i wanted to turn it on/off, volume up/down, or change the channel. really ridiculous. also, they don't have full time doctors on staff here. they have doctors from other professions come in, so i had a doctor, who was technically a sleep doctor, that would only come in after 11pm (when i finally got to sleep and was getting some rest), and then he was gone within the half hour. i learned this because when he misdiagnosed me, and i called the front desk to ask questions (within 10 minutes), they told me he was already gone and couldn't talk to me about it the next day, which i said was unacceptable. i'm lucky i made it through my stay there. my first hospital stay and it was absolutely the worst. the staff is bad, the doctors are bad, the facilities are somehow even worse. go somewhere else!!!

i've been a cancer patient since 2012. after brain radiation in december, my brain became swollen and i lost use of my left side, sort of like a stroke. i spent 12 hours in 2 different ers before being admitted on nye at 11:30 pm. dr. wong added a medication to my chart that i was not taking and, in fact, hadn't been discussed with me. he indicated i needed an "acute neuro rehab" but i learned after 8 days that i'd been passed over by every rehab, due to said medication. i was shipped off to a rank, nasty nursing home where i got no rehab and was physically assaulted by a nurse, only after calling the head of case management to have the medication removed from my chart. all your medical records are available electronically to other facilities. 

after that nightmare, and my leg continuing to atrophy, i returned to dr. wong's office mid january for readmission. this time i was smart enough to bring a witness. the doctor made specific representations that he made a mistake putting that medication in my chart and assured me he knew an oncologist at ri hospital where i could get both the acute neuro rehab and the medication he wanted me to start. so i went back in, 2 weeks later no placement and i was offered another nursing home, meanwhile my left leg was completely atrophied. i went home to get nursing, ot, and pt. dr. wong clearly misrepresented his ability to place me and i had to force myself out. 

after getting services at home, i was still falling and injuring myself. dr. wong dumped my care on dr. meghan shea because he knew he royally messed up. she also assured me she would get me the help i needed if i was readmitted. after spending 19 hours in the er, i was placed on the wrong floor and then moved. once again, no appropriate placement was found after staying days and days on end. i now have anxiety attacks, which i never had before. i was shipped off to another nursing home, where i was promised physical therapy on my useless left leg. the place was set up only for elderly patients, the "physical therapy" was less than i'd done at home and the one bike had 4-5 people waiting to use it at any given time!

i have so much more negative things to say about my three stays in 3 months, pt made a false report, patient services and case management were useless and i never got the orthopedic consult i'd been asking for since january. dr. wong's fellow assured me with appropriate therapy, i'd be on my feet in a month. it's now been 5 months and i'm still on a walker and unable to do almost anything. yet, they billed a fortune to insurance for virtually no care and allowing my leg to atrophy to the point it still doesn't work over the course of 3 hospitalizations.

review: took my 5 year old son to the emergency room after he fell and hit his head.  after waiting for a while, i realized he was fine and told them i was leaving, they insisted they look at him.  took his vitals and said to come back if he vomited in the next 4 hours.  they spent all of 10 minutes with him and that is being generous......i just got a bill for $1350!  that is more than brain surgery costs for 10 minutes.  completely out of line.  unless i'm on the verge of death, i won't be returning here ever!!! i will update this review if my bill is prorated within reason.  the two previous emergency room visits i've taken my son to phoenix children's hospital, i happily paid each bill which was over $1000 a piece but had a ct scan on one visit and breathing treatment on another.  i understand paying more for going to the emergency room but $1350 is so far from fair pricing that i can't even possibly think it is anything other than a complete and total ripoff!!!!

review: i just had my second surgery within a year here with both requiring stays (nov. 17, 2018 & oct. 17, 2019).  both experiences with the pre surgery staff were great.  they did an awesome job at communicating with me, preparing me and making sure i was as comfortable as could be, checking on me frequently. they all had a sense of humor which really goes a long way in stressful situations such as a pending surgery. the pre surgery staff get 5 stars however since this is an overall review i must detract a star for the hospital staff that care for you once you are assigned a room, for both visit experiences.  the level of communication (information), concern, responsiveness to needs and compassion was quite noticeably less than the pre surgery staff.  if restroom was needed and you placed the call light on, they would respond to turn it off yet i waited 40 minutes to use the restroom.  when one is dependent on others for the most basic items, this simply causes stress, agitation, and anxiety which isn't good for any recovery process.  there were no warm and fuzzy feelings as experienced with the pre surgery staff.  my only recommendation is to remind staff that they chose the field to assist others and assistance comes in many forms other than physical assistance.  overall, you have a great facility and would recommend your facility to family and friends.  good job!
fac_name: HonorHealth Scottsdale Thompson Peak Medical Center

this is long but bare with me. this place stereotypes people with mental health history. this is strictly for their er doctors and er intake nurses (some). i have past heart problems which were corrected in high school. i was feeling close to the same way the first time i had my heart episode and went to the er in mid november. i went in for heart palpitations, shortness of breath, extreme lethargic about to pass out feeling, and weakness. when i was taken to the er by my boyfriend, because who wants to call an ambulance on their lunch break in their work parking garage and drawl that kind of attention to themselves, when i got there, the intake nurses literally did not fucking care i existed as a human. it took the nurses or security guards who help wheel people in and out to tell them to open the door and let me in. the er intake nurse didn't give rats a$$ that i couldn't breath well, didn't pay attention to my boyfriend who was literally handing her an emergency card i keep in my wallet of all my allergies and medical history. my boyfriend told them my symptoms, they didn't even think about hooking me up to a ekg until i was in the er exam room, which if i can remember correctly was about 15 to 20 minutes after i arrived. the nurses were ok that day and the nurse who put my iv in kept moving it because she couldn't get the blood out...ok we'll go somewhere else?! so much pain while feeling like i could pass out. 

next the doctor comes in. talks about my symptoms, some history, so on. the moment i mentioned i was on an anti depressant with past history of anxiety, it switched his questions. it went from asking about how i was feeling physically to asking me if i was stressed, or sad, or anxious...so on with the other related questions. look, doc, i know the difference between heart problems and an anxiety attack, this is not an anxiety attack. so instead of ordering more tests he gives me an anti anxiety med, and let's me chill out for an hour or so. of course a anxiety med like xanax is going to chill me out and slow down my heart and breathing. been on them before in high school and anyone who has a friend in their residency at a top tier hospital can tell you, "yea that med is going to make your heart slow down and relax any symptoms." never once consulted a on staff cardiologist or offering to wait to have one come down because of my past history. given my previous heart problem, if anyone remotely understands the heart knows that things can come back and not in the same way as before!!! after this i was discharged and told if i have any more symptoms to come back. 

the next day and a half i slept, no joke, 18 hours out of a 24 hour day. i could still feel heart beats skip, still had shortness of breath just doing small things like going up stairs or even getting up to go to the bathroom. i didn't want to eat or even talk. so after a day and a half of not feeling like a functioning person, i went back.

this time the intake nurses took me seriously, hooked me up to ekg right away, and got an iv in me right away. this doctor took me seriously and ordered a ct with contrast to check for blood clots and did a few blood pressure tests based on laying and standing. everything came back normal. the moment i knew she looked at the most recent visit, started the, "are you sure you're not anxious," questions came out. in my head i'm thinking, "are you flipping kidding me?! does no one take me seriously?!" the one thing i will never forget the doctor saying to me is, " if you are feeling bad and don't get answers the first time, you shouldn't come back to the er. go see the doctors we referred you to the first time." i'm sorry what!????! i was literally doing what the discharge papers said. it's not my problem ( well kinda is if i die from not well examined heart issue) if you didn't exhaust all your resources to help or passed me along because you gave up. i started to cry. the only person who gave me hope was the nurse. she literally ask me, "do you feel safe to go home?" i flat out started crying, and said no. and told her i would never return here for any emergency. i told her i rather drive to a further hospital and die on the way, than come to this hospital again. she took that seriously and comforted me. i was discharged sent home waiting to see a cardiologist 2 weeks later. 

that cardiologist was pissed no one consulted a cardiologist on staff. i got an eco, heart monitor for a week, and a stress test, i have a problem with my sinus node and will need to have surgery. something that could have been solved and found in that moment if someone didn't profile me as a depressed anxious person!!! 

seriously, tell your doctors to stop stereotyping people with mental health problems. stop thinking that someone with a valid history of cardiac problems and a mental health past is just making it up and is just "anxious."

if you have to go here for an emergency make sure someone comes with you otherwise you won't get any attention or care if you need it. i went to the emergency room via ambulance due to severe vomiting diarrhea and non stop shaking. within seconds of getting there i had an episode and was basically laying in crap. i kept yelling out for help and not only did no one do anything no one even stopped to ask what was wrong. when my wife got there i got better care but only because she was tracking them down all the time.  there was one nurse or aid, not sure which, at the end that was very caring and nice. she was the standard that all staff should meet. oh and the cat scan tech was very good. but on the other hand i actually had one aid that kept trying to get me to walk to the bathroom. really, i had severe diarrhea and when it hit it hit and i was exhausted from dozens of times of crapping and vomiting and you want me to walk to the bathroom so you don't have to clean up. i get it but after you see what the patient is going through stop asking. i finally had to tell her if you make me try to walk to the bathroom you will wind up with crap on the floor instead of the bed because i can't control it. she finally stopped asking. i get it... all the jobs are hard, but there is such a difference in care when compared to other hospitals so the low level of care is not just because the job is hard. if you look at past reviews there is a history of poor care here and everyone knows it. everyone i talked to said why did you go there. well, if you have a choice don't go here.

this is for aspire hospital in conroe. call me crazy, but i believe medical institutions should be transparent about the amount patients are responsible for paying out of pocket. i also believe medical staff should be polite and helpful to each and every patient. i went here for imaging. i made sure to check what my out of pocket would be before arriving. once i arrived i was told i would be billed separately by the radiologist in addition to what they would be charging me. instead of helping me find out what additional costs i would incur, the lady at the front desk made me feel like i was being difficult when i stated i would like to call my insurance to ensure the radiologist was in network. she was rude and unprofessional. when my insurance wasn't able to tell me an exact amount but that the radiologist was in network i decided to go ahead with the imaging. the unprofessional front desk clerk decided to ask if i found out how much i would pay. when i told her they couldn't give me an exact amount she smiled and condescendingly said "i'm sorry". her response was immature and rude. she was unwilling to lift a finger to help me find out what my out of pocket would be to the radiologist. she kept saying it would be an insignificant amount of money. what does that me? what's insignificant to you? how is that helpful in any way? it's a shame she couldn't just be understanding and polite because the radiology technician was wonderful. the two stars are for her! but never going back to this place. i'll give my money to a healthcare organization that staffs their front office with friendly and helpful people!

sad to see such low ratings, but not uncommon for a rehab to be rated low, not everyone is gonna get it, not everyone is going to make it.. 

sierra tucson played a vital roll in my shift from a drug addicted and emotionally damaged person into a functional loving and caring individual. there were some humps in the road along the way but st gave me the resources to recover. namely  doctor moyer. she was an amazing influence on my life and provided me with the gift of compassion. i cannot say enough good things about her, i'd fly to tucson to meet with her again.

other highlights: amazing food, drinks, and coffee. super nice nurses and behavioral therapists. a ton of different therapeutic modalities. absolutely beautiful campus and natural environment.   lodging is great, each room has a private bathroom. i had my own room for 22 out of 30 days which was great, had to spend the last week with a super noisy snorer but i can deal with that.

the family week program is another phenomenal resource for the patient and their family. my wife and father both enjoyed it and learned a lot.

this was not my first rehab  experience but it was certainly my best. thank you sierra tucson!

only a month ago they changed their policy to not allow service animals in violation of ada access requirements. the call buttons aren't within reach of the beds and they think a scooter replaces a service animal when a scooter can't come help you off the ground if you fall when walking. completely unreasonable accommodation. so they avoid doing the work of educating people to leave service animals alone in their policies and instead violate the sacred bond between service animals and their handlers increasing the emotional and financial burden on their patients to an unreasonable degree. overall the staff is kind and caring and even supportive of service animals. the risk management department is trying use the cover up of saying that it's important  to break the bond between handler and service animal for you own good because it's an external dependency, like they haven't read the expensive research on how healing animals are for trauma and anxiety. but they'll bring in horses and dogs for therapy time. completely backwards and against most of the documentation that supports healing for ptsd, just cause it feels too challenging for them to do the work. one person there was rejected only hours before her arrival for her service animal and had to find last minute emergency accommodations with a stranger for her animal. horrible.

to top it off they lost my phone for 45 mins when i had a scheduled call for the sale of my house to pay their bill. they don't secure the items they won't let you keep with you in the 'holding tank' prior to moving you to 'residential'. there's a locker room with coded lockers that are never locked and the whole staff has access to, so your stuff is not safe.

there are amazing people here that this isn't a job and they are willing to go the extra mile to help you when their systems and process dictates stupid decisions. i feel bad for the nurses because they see us the most and are given the least advocacy power. maybe if they listened to their nurses they would have less problems figuring out what their patient's need. the body work people are phenomenal. they have a nurse with a doctorate who demands to be called dr. padilla, don't let them assign you to her, she's arrogant, condescending, and considers having a motorcycle a suicide attempt. i heard dr. pritchard doesn't even believe in the extreme dissociation and amnesia that can happen with severe ptsd. if you for some strange reason chose to come here make sure you know how to advocate for yourself. the patient advocates are 12 step sponsors with no accreditation.

sierra tucson changed my life. the month that i spent there helped me learn so much about mental health as well as many different coping skills. the staff are very knowledgeable and know what they are taking about. i felt the treatment was individualized for each patient depending on their needs. the scenery is beautiful, the food was great and there were so many different treatment types and modalities offered. 10/10 would go back.

on the advice of a trusted professional, we sent our 19 year old son to sierra tucson(st) in november 2019.  we asked the intake coordinator to explain the many negative reviews and her response was that they take some very tough cases, so they don't always end well.  that was an understatement!  our son was there for four days and on the day they moved him to the "lodge", he ended up bolting from the property and was picked up by a local sheriff to be taken to another facility for observation.  although not the outcome we wanted, we could understand it.  what we couldn't understand was that st never returned our many calls for the next 36 hours, nor called the other facility to coordinate next steps.  the next communication we got was from the outside facility to let us know that our son was not welcome back at st and was being driven to a homeless shelter in phoenix without a phone, any of his belongings, or id.  fortunately, we were able to intercept the driver to get him to a hotel and eventually home, roughly 2,500 miles away.  it took two days for st to get his passport to him so he could fly.  and then after a week of asking about his medications, they emailed us to tell us they'd been destroyed.  in the days he was there, they added medications for diagnoses he doesn't have and mentioned him living in the wrong state. i do believe dr chhatwal was reading the wrong patient chart when she called. we've sadly become very familiar with mental health/substance abuse facilities but never felt the need to write a review/warning. just ask yourself why none of the staff members or providers are listed with any contact info.  it's a fortress.

sierra tucson is one of the few programs in the country that is willing to treat very complex mental health disorders in a dignified residential campus. (instead of a psych unit or hospital based environment) some of the disorders treated include personality disorders. the people who take the time to write these dramatic negative reviews were most likely not ready to get well-parents and the family systems included. the state with it's stringent protocols would not have just granted sierra tucson clearance to build and open a new 40,000 square foot inpatient program if these reviews had merit. sure some people have valid concerns-no program is perfect- but please consider the source and make your decision about serious medical conditions like mental health disorders with your therapist or treating physician. reviews are great for planning a trip and shopping for things like computers and gadgets , not for deciding on medical care. anyone can write them and just because a program has no reviews or mainly good reviews -is no indication that it is a good program. anyone can ask their buddy to give a 5 star review. think about it. please don't make decisions about life threatening chronic illnesses using yelp! sierra tucson changed my life for the better in every possible way. i was ready to change and worked very hard while there. it is sad to see some of these reviews as it keeps some people from receiving the best treatment in the country for mental health.  sierra tucson treats thousands of people every year for over 35 years. please consider the source and partner with your medical provider to make these very important decisions.

how does one begin to rate a mental hospital? this place literally saved my life. every single person from staff to doctors and everyone in between was wonderful. these people are doing mental health care right. if they don't care then they're doing a hell of a job pretending.

no one likes to visit the emergency room during the holidays.
the wait time in the emergency room on friday january 3,2020 was unreal.
the registration desk clerk was really helpful.
i wish each patient could get a wait time buzzer, while waiting in the emergency room. 
this is the only hospital in tennessee, were patients are their priority in the health care system.

after sitting here from 11:30pm to almost 6am, i'm ready to take my daughter and leave. she has been so sick... literally crying in pain and shaking. she has crohns and may have a blockage. we will now have to leave and go find another hospital. i keep getting told we are the next one up. for the last 4 hours, we are the next ones up. what a bunch of crock. first time bringing her here and last time. we came all the way from sevierville. the surgeons at this hospital are great - my husband has had all his surgeries and i highly recommend the actual hospital, but stay far away from this er! i only gave 2 stars because they did do an ekg when we first got here. other than that, 1 star.
